# File Summary

## Purpose
This file contains a packed representation of the entire repository's contents.
It is designed to be easily consumable by AI systems for analysis, code review,

## File: .github/workflows/pages.yml
````yaml
 1: name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
 2: 
 3: on:
 4:   push:
 5:     branches: [master]
 6:   workflow_dispatch:
 7: 
 8: permissions:
 9:   contents: read
10:   pages: write
11:   id-token: write
12: 
13: concurrency:
14:   group: pages
15:   cancel-in-progress: true
16: 
17: jobs:
18:   build:
19:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
20:     steps:
21:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
22: 
23:       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
24:         with:
25:           targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
26: 
27:       - uses: taiki-e/install-action@wasm-pack
28: 
29:       # The main engine (`/`) generates chunks in the browser, so it needs
30:       # nothing but static files. `wasm-pack` output is checked in for local
31:       # convenience, but Pages always deploys a fresh build from source.
32:       - name: Build wasm front end
33:         run: wasm-pack build wasm_frontend --target web --release --no-typescript --out-dir ../static/pkg
34: 
35:       - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
36: 
37:       - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
38:         with:
39:           path: static
40: 
41:   deploy:
42:     needs: build
43:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
44:     environment:
45:       name: github-pages
46:       url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
47:     steps:
48:       - id: deployment
49:         uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
````

## File: examples/generate_samples.rs
````rust
 1: use std::fs;
 2: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 3: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 4: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 5: use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan;
 6: use vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::{
 7:     render_large_voxel_blueprint_svg, BlueprintSlice,
 8: };
 9: 
10: fn main() {
11:     let out_dir = "/home/dbslim/vackrooms/static/samples";
12:     fs::create_dir_all(out_dir).unwrap();
13: 
14:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
15:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
16:     let chunk_size = config.chunk_size;
17:     let size_world = 100.0;
18:     let steps = (size_world / chunk_size).round() as i32;
19: 
20:     let chunk_w = (chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
21:     let chunk_d = (chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
22:     let total_w = steps as usize * chunk_w;
23:     let total_d = steps as usize * chunk_d;
24: 
25:     println!("Generating 100 B&W/Red SVGs (seeds 1 to 100) inside static/samples...");
26: 
27:     for seed in 1..=100 {
28:         // Generate plan
29:         let _plan = generate_region_plan(
30:             seed,
31:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
32:             size_world,
33:             &config,
34:             &noise,
35:         );
36: 
37:         let generator = vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
38: 
39:         // Generate combined cells (1 for wall, 3 for light)
40:         let mut combined_cells = vec![0u8; total_w * total_d];
41: 
42:         for i in 0..steps {
43:             for j in 0..steps {
44:                 let chunk_pos = Position::new(i as f32 * chunk_size, j as f32 * chunk_size);
45:                 let grid = generator.execute(chunk_pos, seed, config.clone());
46: 
47:                 for cz in 0..chunk_d {
48:                     for cx in 0..chunk_w {
49:                         let vx = cx + 1;
50:                         let vz = cz + 1;
51: 
52:                         let mut has_wall = false;
53:                         let mut has_light = false;
54: 
55:                         for y in 0..grid.height() {
56:                             let v = grid.get(vx, y, vz);
57:                             if v == 1 || v == 5 || v == 8 {
58:                                 has_wall = true;
59:                             }
60:                             if v == 4 || v == 9 {
61:                                 has_light = true;
62:                             }
63:                         }
64: 
65:                         let target_x = i as usize * chunk_w + cx;
66:                         let target_z = j as usize * chunk_d + cz;
67:                         let idx = target_z * total_w + target_x;
68: 
69:                         if has_wall {
70:                             combined_cells[idx] = 1; // Wall
71:                         } else if has_light {
72:                             combined_cells[idx] = 3; // Light
73:                         }
74:                     }
75:                 }
76:             }
77:         }
78: 
79:         // Render composite view in B&W style (white bg, black walls, red lights)
80:         let svg = render_large_voxel_blueprint_svg(
81:             &combined_cells,
82:             total_w,
83:             total_d,
84:             0.0,
85:             0.0,
86:             config.voxel_scale,
87:             size_world,
88:             BlueprintSlice::Composite,
89:             None,
90:             true, // is_bw = true
91:         );
92: 
93:         // Write file
94:         fs::write(format!("{}/seed_{}.svg", out_dir, seed), &svg).unwrap();
95:     }
96: 
97:     println!("All 100 SVGs written successfully!");
98: }
````

## File: scripts/build-single-file.mjs
````javascript
  1: #!/usr/bin/env node
  2: 
  3: /**
  4:  * Pack the whole app into one self-contained HTML file.
  5:  *
  6:  * Input:  static/index.html            presentation shell
  7:  *         static/pkg/wasm_frontend.js  wasm-bindgen ES-module glue
  8:  *         static/pkg/wasm_frontend_bg.wasm
  9:  *         static/worker.js             chunk-generation worker
 10:  * Output: dist/vackrooms.html
 11:  *
 12:  * How the pieces are stitched together at runtime:
 13:  *   - The .wasm binary travels as base64 in an inert <script type="text/plain">
 14:  *     tag and is decoded into a blob: URL.
 15:  *   - The glue module is embedded as a string and imported through a blob:
 16:  *     URL, so both the page and the workers share one copy.
 17:  *   - worker.js is rewritten to import that glue blob and init from the wasm
 18:  *     blob; its own blob: URL is published as
 19:  *     `globalThis.__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__`, which the Rust worker spawner
 20:  *     (drivers/worker_source.rs) prefers over the sibling "worker.js" path.
 21:  *     Where blob workers are unavailable the engine's existing in-thread
 22:  *     generation fallback takes over.
 23:  *
 24:  * Run scripts/build-wasm.mjs first; this script only packages static/.
 25:  */
 26: 
 27: import { mkdir, readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
 28: import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
 29: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
 30: 
 31: const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
 32: const staticDir = join(root, 'static');
 33: const outFile = join(root, 'dist', 'vackrooms.html');
 34: 
 35: const [html, glue, worker, wasm] = await Promise.all([
 36:   readFile(join(staticDir, 'index.html'), 'utf8'),
 37:   readFile(join(staticDir, 'pkg', 'wasm_frontend.js'), 'utf8'),
 38:   readFile(join(staticDir, 'worker.js'), 'utf8'),
 39:   readFile(join(staticDir, 'pkg', 'wasm_frontend_bg.wasm')),
 40: ]);
 41: 
 42: /** Embed arbitrary source as a JS string literal that can never terminate
 43:  *  the surrounding <script> element (every `<` becomes <). */
 44: const jsString = (source) => JSON.stringify(source).replace(/</g, '\\u003c');
 45: 
 46: /** Replace exactly `count` occurrences, failing loudly when the source
 47:  *  drifts and a pattern no longer matches — a silently broken bundle is
 48:  *  worse than no bundle. */
 49: function mustReplace(source, pattern, replacement, count = 1) {
 50:   const matches = source.match(new RegExp(pattern.source, pattern.flags + 'g'));
 51:   if ((matches?.length ?? 0) !== count) {
 52:     throw new Error(
 53:       `expected exactly ${count} match(es) of ${pattern} (found ${matches?.length ?? 0})`,
 54:     );
 55:   }
 56:   return source.replace(pattern, replacement);
 57: }
 58: 
 59: // Worker: import the shared glue blob, init from the wasm blob. The
 60: // placeholders are substituted with live blob: URLs by the page bootstrap.
 61: let workerSrc = mustReplace(
 62:   worker,
 63:   /from "\.\/pkg\/wasm_frontend\.js"/,
 64:   'from "__GLUE_URL__"',
 65: );
 66: workerSrc = mustReplace(
 67:   workerSrc,
 68:   /wasmReady = init\(\)/,
 69:   'wasmReady = init({ module_or_path: "__WASM_URL__" })',
 70: );
 71: 
 72: const bootstrap = `
 73:         // ---- Single-file bootstrap (generated by build-single-file.mjs) ----
 74:         const __b64 = document.getElementById('vackrooms-wasm').textContent;
 75:         const __bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(__b64.replace(/\\s+/g, '')), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
 76:         const __blobUrl = (parts, type) => URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(parts, { type }));
 77:         const __wasmUrl = __blobUrl([__bytes], 'application/wasm');
 78:         const __glueUrl = __blobUrl([${jsString(glue)}], 'text/javascript');
 79:         globalThis.__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__ = __blobUrl([
 80:             ${jsString(workerSrc)}
 81:                 .replaceAll('__GLUE_URL__', __glueUrl)
 82:                 .replaceAll('__WASM_URL__', __wasmUrl),
 83:         ], 'text/javascript');
 84:         const { default: __wbgInit,`;
 85: 
 86: // Page: swap the static ESM import for the glue blob, and make the bare
 87: // `init()` call at the bottom of the shell resolve to the embedded binary
 88: // (argument-less init would try `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` against a
 89: // blob: base and throw).
 90: let page = mustReplace(
 91:   html,
 92:   /import init, \{/,
 93:   bootstrap.trimStart(),
 94: );
 95: page = mustReplace(
 96:   page,
 97:   /\} from '\.\/pkg\/wasm_frontend\.js';/,
 98:   "} = await import(__glueUrl);\n        const init = () => __wbgInit({ module_or_path: __wasmUrl });",
 99: );
100: 
101: // Base64 payload sits in an inert tag so the module script stays readable.
102: const wasmB64 = wasm.toString('base64');
103: page = mustReplace(
104:   page,
105:   /    <script type="module">/,
106:   `    <script type="text/plain" id="vackrooms-wasm">${wasmB64}</script>\n    <script type="module">`,
107: );
108: 
109: await mkdir(dirname(outFile), { recursive: true });
110: await writeFile(outFile, page);
111: console.log(
112:   `wrote ${outFile} (${(page.length / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2)} MiB, wasm ${(wasm.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KiB)`,
113: );
````

## File: scripts/build-wasm.mjs
````javascript
 1: #!/usr/bin/env node
 2: 
 3: /**
 4:  * Build the browser WebAssembly package without exposing a half-written
 5:  * `static/pkg` directory to the dev server.
 6:  *
 7:  * wasm-pack reads an existing output package before replacing it, and older
 8:  * wasm-pack releases cannot parse the newer `files: [...]` manifest they just
 9:  * generated. A fresh staging directory avoids that version-skew trap. Only a
10:  * successful build is copied over the live browser assets.
11:  */
12: 
13: import { cp, mkdir, mkdtemp, readdir, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
14: import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
15: import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
16: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
17: import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
18: 
19: const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
20: const output = join(root, 'static', 'pkg');
21: const staging = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'vackrooms-wasm-'));
22: 
23: function run(command, args) {
24:   return new Promise((resolveRun, rejectRun) => {
25:     const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' });
26:     child.once('error', rejectRun);
27:     child.once('exit', (code, signal) => {
28:       if (code === 0) resolveRun();
29:       else rejectRun(new Error(`${command} failed (${signal ?? `exit ${code}`})`));
30:     });
31:   });
32: }
33: 
34: try {
35:   await run('wasm-pack', [
36:     'build',
37:     'wasm_frontend',
38:     '--target',
39:     'web',
40:     '--release',
41:     '--out-dir',
42:     staging,
43:   ]);
44: 
45:   await mkdir(output, { recursive: true });
46:   for (const entry of await readdir(staging, { withFileTypes: true })) {
47:     await cp(join(staging, entry.name), join(output, entry.name), {
48:       force: true,
49:       recursive: entry.isDirectory(),
50:     });
51:   }
52: } finally {
53:   await rm(staging, { force: true, recursive: true });
54: }
````

````rust
 42:     .assembly-corrupt {{ fill: #a21caf; fill-opacity: 0.15; stroke: #d946ef; stroke-width: 1.0; }}
 43:     .assembly-label {{ fill: #94a3b8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 9px; font-weight: bold; }}

 46:     .entrance {{ stroke: #10b981; stroke-width: 2; stroke-linecap: square; }}
 47:     .entrance-node {{ fill: #10b981; }}

 49:     .fixture-unlit {{ fill: #475569; stroke: #334155; stroke-width: 0.5; }}

 56: "##,

283: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
284: pub enum BlueprintSlice {
285:     FloorPlan,       // y = 0: floor, walls projected upward

287:     CeilingPlan,     // ceiling and LIGHT voxels

291: pub fn render_voxel_chunk_svg(
292:     grid: &crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid,
293:     origin: crate::entities::models::Position,
294:     config: &crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig,
295:     slice: BlueprintSlice,
296:     semantics: Option<&RegionPlan>,
297: ) -> String {
298:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
299:         VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT,
300:         VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_WATER,
301:     };
302: 
303:     let w_voxels = grid.width().saturating_sub(2);
304:     let d_voxels = grid.depth().saturating_sub(2);
305: 
306:     let cell_size = 12.0;
307:     let width_px = w_voxels as f32 * cell_size;
308:     let height_px = d_voxels as f32 * cell_size;
309: 
310:     let mut svg = String::new();
311:     svg.push_str(&format!(
312:         r##"<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {} {}" width="{}" height="{}">
313:   <style>
314:     .bg {{ fill: #070a13; }}
315:     .cell-air {{ fill: #0b0f19; }}
316:     .cell-main-corridor {{ fill: #083344; fill-opacity: 0.8; }}
317:     .cell-secondary-corridor {{ fill: #1e1b4b; fill-opacity: 0.8; }}
318:     .cell-assembly {{ fill: #111827; fill-opacity: 0.8; }}
319:     
320:     .voxel-wall {{ fill: #1e293b; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
321:     .voxel-red-wall {{ fill: #7f1d1d; stroke: #b91c1c; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
322:     .voxel-floor {{ fill: #78350f; stroke: #92400e; stroke-dasharray: 1,1; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
323:     .voxel-grass {{ fill: #14532d; stroke: #166534; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
324:     .voxel-water {{ fill: #1e3a8a; stroke: #1d4ed8; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
325:     .voxel-tree {{ fill: #064e3b; stroke: #047857; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
326:     .voxel-ceiling {{ fill: #334155; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
327:     .voxel-light {{ fill: #fef08a; stroke: #ca8a04; stroke-width: 0.5; filter: drop-shadow(0px 0px 2px #fef08a); }}
328:     .voxel-red-light {{ fill: #fecaca; stroke: #dc2626; stroke-width: 0.5; filter: drop-shadow(0px 0px 2px #fecaca); }}
329: 
330:     .grid-line {{ stroke: #1e293b; stroke-width: 0.25; }}
331:     .label-text {{ fill: #94a3b8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 10px; }}
332:   </style>
333:   <rect class="bg" width="{}" height="{}" />
334: "##,
335:         width_px, height_px, width_px, height_px, width_px, height_px
336:     ));
337: 
338:     // Render cells
339:     for z in 0..d_voxels {
340:         for x in 0..w_voxels {
341:             // Voxel coordinates are 1-indexed due to padding
342:             let vx = x + 1;
343:             let vz = z + 1;
344: 
345:             // World coordinates
346:             let wx = origin.x + x as f32 * config.voxel_scale;
347:             let wz = origin.z + z as f32 * config.voxel_scale;
348: 
349:             // 1. Semantic background classification
350:             let mut semantic_class = "cell-air";
351:             if let Some(plan) = semantics {
352:                 let mut inside_main = false;
353:                 let mut inside_secondary = false;
354:                 for c in &plan.corridors {
355:                     if c.path.len() >= 2 {
356:                         let dist = point_to_polyline_distance(
357:                             wx + config.voxel_scale * 0.5,
358:                             wz + config.voxel_scale * 0.5,
359:                             &c.path,
360:                         );
361:                         if dist <= c.width * 0.5 {
362:                             if c.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor {
363:                                 inside_main = true;
364:                             } else {
365:                                 inside_secondary = true;
366:                             }
367:                         }
368:                     }
369:                 }
370:                 if inside_main {
371:                     semantic_class = "cell-main-corridor";
372:                 } else if inside_secondary {
373:                     semantic_class = "cell-secondary-corridor";
374:                 } else {
375:                     for a in &plan.assemblies {
376:                         if a.footprint.contains(
377:                             wx + config.voxel_scale * 0.5,
378:                             wz + config.voxel_scale * 0.5,
379:                         ) {
380:                             semantic_class = "cell-assembly";
381:                             break;
382:                         }
383:                     }
384:                 }
385:             }
386: 
387:             // 2. Voxel classification based on BlueprintSlice
388:             let mut has_wall = false;
389:             let mut has_red_wall = false;
390:             let mut has_light = false;
391:             let mut has_red_light = false;
392:             let mut has_floor = false;
393:             let mut has_ceiling = false;
394:             let mut has_tree = false;
395:             let mut has_grass = false;
396:             let mut has_water = false;
397: 
398:             for y in 0..grid.height() {
399:                 match grid.get(vx, y, vz) {
400:                     VOXEL_WALL => has_wall = true,
401:                     VOXEL_RED_WALL => has_red_wall = true,
402:                     VOXEL_LIGHT => has_light = true,
403:                     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => has_red_light = true,
404:                     VOXEL_FLOOR => has_floor = true,
405:                     VOXEL_CEILING => has_ceiling = true,
406:                     VOXEL_TREE => has_tree = true,
407:                     VOXEL_GRASS => has_grass = true,
408:                     VOXEL_WATER => has_water = true,
409:                     _ => {}
410:                 }
411:             }
412: 
413:             let voxel_class = match slice {
414:                 BlueprintSlice::FloorPlan => {
415:                     if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
416:                         Some(if has_red_wall { "voxel-red-wall" } else { "voxel-wall" })
417:                     } else if has_floor || has_grass || has_water {
418:                         Some(if has_water { "voxel-water" } else if has_grass { "voxel-grass" } else { "voxel-floor" })
419:                     } else {
420:                         None
421:                     }
422:                 }
423:                 BlueprintSlice::WallPlan => {
424:                     if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
425:                         Some(if has_red_wall { "voxel-red-wall" } else { "voxel-wall" })
426:                     } else {
427:                         None
428:                     }
429:                 }
430:                 BlueprintSlice::CeilingPlan => {
431:                     if has_light || has_red_light {
432:                         Some(if has_red_light { "voxel-red-light" } else { "voxel-light" })
433:                     } else if has_ceiling {
434:                         Some("voxel-ceiling")
435:                     } else {
436:                         None
437:                     }
438:                 }
439:                 BlueprintSlice::Composite => {
440:                     if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
441:                         Some(if has_red_wall { "voxel-red-wall" } else { "voxel-wall" })
442:                     } else if has_light || has_red_light {
443:                         Some(if has_red_light { "voxel-red-light" } else { "voxel-light" })
444:                     } else if has_floor || has_grass || has_water {
445:                         Some(if has_water { "voxel-water" } else if has_grass { "voxel-grass" } else { "voxel-floor" })
446:                     } else {
447:                         None
448:                     }
449:                 }
450:             };
451: 
452:             // Render rect in SVG coordinates (origin top-left)
453:             let svg_x = x as f32 * cell_size;
454:             let svg_y = (d_voxels - 1 - z) as f32 * cell_size;
455: 
456:             if let Some(vc) = voxel_class {
457:                 svg.push_str(&format!(
458:                     r##"  <rect class="{}" x="{}" y="{}" width="{}" height="{}" />
459: "##,
460:                     vc, svg_x, svg_y, cell_size, cell_size
461:                 ));
462:             } else {
463:                 svg.push_str(&format!(
464:                     r##"  <rect class="{}" x="{}" y="{}" width="{}" height="{}" />
465: "##,
466:                     semantic_class, svg_x, svg_y, cell_size, cell_size
467:                 ));
468:             }
469:         }
470:     }
471: 
472:     // Draw coordinate label on top
473:     svg.push_str(&format!(
474:         r##"  <text class="label-text" x="10" y="20">Chunk: ({:.1}, {:.1}) | Slice: {:?}</text>
475: "##,
476:         origin.x, origin.z, slice
477:     ));
478: 
479:     svg.push_str("</svg>\n");
480:     svg
481: }
482: 
483: fn point_to_polyline_distance(x: f32, z: f32, path: &[crate::entities::models::Position]) -> f32 {
484:     let mut min_dist = f32::MAX;
485:     for seg in path.windows(2) {
486:         let p1 = seg[0];
487:         let p2 = seg[1];
488:         let dist = point_to_segment_distance(x, z, p1.x, p1.z, p2.x, p2.z);
489:         if dist < min_dist {
490:             min_dist = dist;
491:         }
492:     }
493:     min_dist
494: }
495: 
496: fn point_to_segment_distance(x: f32, z: f32, x1: f32, z1: f32, x2: f32, z2: f32) -> f32 {
497:     let dx = x2 - x1;
498:     let dz = z2 - z1;
499:     let len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
500:     if len2 == 0.0 {
501:         let t_dx = x - x1;
502:         let t_dz = z - z1;
503:         return (t_dx * t_dx + t_dz * t_dz).sqrt();
504:     }
505:     let t = ((x - x1) * dx + (z - z1) * dz) / len2;
506:     let t_clamped = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
507:     let proj_x = x1 + t_clamped * dx;
508:     let proj_z = z1 + t_clamped * dz;
509:     let diff_x = x - proj_x;
510:     let diff_z = z - proj_z;
511:     (diff_x * diff_x + diff_z * diff_z).sqrt()
512: }

514: pub fn render_large_voxel_blueprint_svg(
515:     combined_cells: &[u8],
516:     total_w: usize,
517:     total_d: usize,
518:     rx_origin: f32,
519:     rz_origin: f32,
520:     voxel_scale: f32,
521:     size_world: f32,
522:     slice: BlueprintSlice,
523:     semantics: Option<&RegionPlan>,
524:     is_bw: bool,
525: ) -> String {
526:     let scale = 10.0; // 10 pixels per world unit
527:     let size_px = size_world * scale;
528: 
529:     let mut svg = String::new();
530:     if is_bw {
531:         svg.push_str(&format!(
532:             r##"<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {} {}" width="{}" height="{}">
533:   <style>
534:     .bg {{ fill: #ffffff; }}
535:     .voxel-wall {{ fill: #000000; }}
536:     .voxel-red-wall {{ fill: #000000; }}
537:     .voxel-light {{ fill: #ff0000; }}
538:     .voxel-red-light {{ fill: #ff0000; }}
539:   </style>
540:   <rect class="bg" width="{}" height="{}" />
541: "##,
542:             size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px
543:         ));
544:     } else {
545:         svg.push_str(&format!(
546:             r##"<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {} {}" width="{}" height="{}">
547:   <style>
548:     .bg {{ fill: #070a13; }}
549:     .grid {{ stroke: #1e293b; stroke-width: 0.5; }}
550:     .chunk-grid {{ stroke: #f43f5e; stroke-width: 1.0; stroke-dasharray: 4,4; fill: none; }}
551:     .chunk-label {{ fill: #f43f5e; font-family: monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: bold; }}
552:     
553:     .assembly {{ fill: #1e293b; fill-opacity: 0.25; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 1.0; }}
554:     .assembly-corrupt {{ fill: #a21caf; fill-opacity: 0.2; stroke: #d946ef; stroke-width: 1.0; }}
555:     .assembly-label {{ fill: #94a3b8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 9px; font-weight: bold; }}
556:     .corridor-main {{ stroke: #083344; stroke-width: 3.0; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; fill: none; }}
557:     .corridor-secondary {{ stroke: #1e1b4b; stroke-width: 2.0; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; fill: none; }}
558: 
559:     .voxel-wall {{ fill: #1e293b; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 0.25; }}
560:     .voxel-red-wall {{ fill: #7f1d1d; stroke: #b91c1c; stroke-width: 0.25; }}
561:     .voxel-floor {{ fill: #78350f; fill-opacity: 0.4; stroke: #92400e; stroke-width: 0.1; }}
562:     .voxel-grass {{ fill: #14532d; fill-opacity: 0.4; stroke: #166534; stroke-width: 0.1; }}
563:     .voxel-water {{ fill: #1e3a8a; fill-opacity: 0.4; stroke: #1d4ed8; stroke-width: 0.1; }}
564:     .voxel-ceiling {{ fill: #334155; fill-opacity: 0.4; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 0.1; }}
565:     .voxel-light {{ fill: #fef08a; stroke: #ca8a04; stroke-width: 0.25; }}
566:     .voxel-red-light {{ fill: #fecaca; stroke: #dc2626; stroke-width: 0.25; }}
567: 
568:     .title-bg {{ fill: #0f172a; fill-opacity: 0.95; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 1.5; }}
569:     .title-text {{ fill: #f8fafc; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: bold; }}
570:     .title-sub {{ fill: #94a3b8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 9px; }}
571:   </style>
572:   <rect class="bg" width="{}" height="{}" />
573: "##,
574:             size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px, size_px
575:         ));
576:     }
577: 
578:     // Helpers
579:     let to_svg_x = |wx: f32| -> f32 { (wx - rx_origin) * scale };
580:     let to_svg_y = |wz: f32| -> f32 { size_px - (wz - rz_origin) * scale };
581: 
582:     // 1. Draw semantics first (corridors and assemblies)
583:     if !is_bw {
584:         if let Some(plan) = semantics {
585:             // Assemblies
586:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
587:                 let mut points_str = String::new();
588:                 for &(vx, vz) in &a.footprint.vertices {
589:                     points_str.push_str(&format!("{},{} ", to_svg_x(vx), to_svg_y(vz)));
590:                 }
591:                 let class_name = if a.corruption.misalignment.0 != 0.0 || a.corruption.misalignment.1 != 0.0 || a.corruption.abandoned {
592:                     "assembly-corrupt"
593:                 } else {
594:                     "assembly"
595:                 };
596:                 svg.push_str(&format!(
597:                     r##"  <polygon class="{}" points="{}" />
598: "##,
599:                     class_name, points_str
600:                 ));
601:             }
602: 
603:             // Corridors
604:             for c in &plan.corridors {
605:                 if c.path.len() >= 2 {
606:                     let mut d_str = String::new();
607:                     for (idx, p) in c.path.iter().enumerate() {
608:                         let prefix = if idx == 0 { "M" } else { "L" };
609:                         d_str.push_str(&format!("{} {},{} ", prefix, to_svg_x(p.x), to_svg_y(p.z)));
610:                     }
611:                     let class_name = if c.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor {
612:                         "corridor-main"
613:                     } else {
614:                         "corridor-secondary"
615:                     };
616:                     svg.push_str(&format!(
617:                         r##"  <path class="{}" d="{}" stroke-width="{}" />
618: "##,
619:                         class_name, d_str, c.width * scale
620:                     ));
621:                 }
622:             }
623:         }
624:     }
625: 
626:     // 2. Draw 5-unit background grid lines
627:     if !is_bw {
628:         let grid_step = 5.0 * scale;
629:         let mut grid_val = 0.0;
630:         while grid_val < size_px {
631:             svg.push_str(&format!(
632:                 r##"  <line class="grid" x1="{}" y1="0" x2="{}" y2="{}" />
633:   <line class="grid" x1="0" y1="{}" x2="{}" y2="{}" />
634: "##,
635:                 grid_val, grid_val, size_px, grid_val, size_px, grid_val
636:             ));
637:             grid_val += grid_step;
638:         }
639:     }
640: 
641:     // 3. Draw voxels
642:     let voxel_px = voxel_scale * scale;
643:     for z in 0..total_d {
644:         for x in 0..total_w {
645:             let idx = z * total_w + x;
646:             let val = combined_cells[idx];
647:             if val == 0 {
648:                 continue; // Air is transparent to show background plan
649:             }
650: 
651:             let class_name = match val {
652:                 1 => "voxel-wall",
653:                 2 => "voxel-red-wall",
654:                 3 => "voxel-light",
655:                 4 => "voxel-red-light",
656:                 5 if !is_bw => "voxel-floor",
657:                 6 if !is_bw => "voxel-grass",
658:                 7 if !is_bw => "voxel-water",
659:                 9 if !is_bw => "voxel-ceiling",
660:                 _ => continue,
661:             };
662: 
663:             let svg_x = x as f32 * voxel_px;
664:             let svg_y = size_px - (z + 1) as f32 * voxel_px;
665: 
666:             // In BW mode, we don't want strokes on elements
667:             let stroke_attr = if is_bw { "" } else { "" };
668: 
669:             svg.push_str(&format!(
670:                 r##"  <rect class="{}" x="{}" y="{}" width="{}" height="{}"{} />
671: "##,
672:                 class_name, svg_x, svg_y, voxel_px, voxel_px, stroke_attr
673:             ));
674:         }
675:     }
676: 
677:     // 4. Draw chunk boundaries on top
678:     if !is_bw {
679:         let chunk_size = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 { 20.0 } else { 10.0 };
680:         let steps = (size_world / chunk_size).round() as i32;
681:         for i in 0..steps {
682:             for j in 0..steps {
683:                 let min_x = rx_origin + i as f32 * chunk_size;
684:                 let min_z = rz_origin + j as f32 * chunk_size;
685:                 let svg_min_x = to_svg_x(min_x);
686:                 let svg_max_x = to_svg_x(min_x + chunk_size);
687:                 let svg_min_y = to_svg_y(min_z + chunk_size);
688:                 let svg_max_y = to_svg_y(min_z);
689: 
690:                 let w_px = svg_max_x - svg_min_x;
691:                 let h_px = svg_max_y - svg_min_y;
692: 
693:                 let chunk_coord_x = (min_x / chunk_size).round() as i64;
694:                 let chunk_coord_z = (min_z / chunk_size).round() as i64;
695: 
696:                 svg.push_str(&format!(
697:                     r##"  <rect class="chunk-grid" x="{}" y="{}" width="{}" height="{}" />
698:   <text class="chunk-label" x="{}" y="{}" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="hanging">[{}, {}]</text>
699: "##,
700:                     svg_min_x, svg_min_y, w_px, h_px,
701:                     svg_min_x + 6.0, svg_min_y + 6.0, chunk_coord_x, chunk_coord_z
702:                 ));
703:             }
704:         }
705:     }
706: 
707:     // 5. Title Block
708:     if !is_bw {
709:         let title_x = size_px - 230.0;
710:         let title_y = size_px - 140.0;
711:         svg.push_str(&format!(
712:             r##"  <g transform="translate({}, {})">
713:     <rect class="title-bg" width="215" height="125" rx="6" />
714:     <text class="title-text" x="15" y="25">VOXEL MAP BLUEPRINT</text>
715:     <text class="title-sub" x="15" y="45">Slice Mode: {:?}</text>
716:     <text class="title-sub" x="15" y="60">Region: ({:.1}, {:.1})</text>
717:     <text class="title-sub" x="15" y="75">Region Size: {:.1}m x {:.1}m</text>
718:     <text class="title-sub" x="15" y="90">Voxel Scale: {}m</text>
719:     <text class="title-sub" x="15" y="105">Resolution: {}x{} cells</text>
720:   </g>
721: "##,
722:             title_x, title_y,
723:             slice,
724:             rx_origin, rz_origin,
725:             size_world, size_world,
726:             voxel_scale,
727:             total_w, total_d
728:         ));
729:     }
730: 
731:     svg.push_str("</svg>\n");
732:     svg
733: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Rectilinear world geometry shared by every anomaly family.
  2: //!
  3: //! Anomalies are authored on an orthogonal lattice. Keeping the transforms in
  4: //! one small module makes that invariant visible: planners choose a footprint,
  5: //! while samplers only translate between world and footprint-local space.
  6: 
  7: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  8: 
  9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
 10: #[repr(u8)]
 11: pub enum Axis2 {
 12:     X = 0,
 13:     Z = 1,
 14: }
 15: 
 16: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
 17: #[repr(u8)]
 18: pub enum AxisDirection {
 19:     Negative = 0,
 20:     Positive = 1,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: impl AxisDirection {
 24:     pub fn sign(self) -> f32 {
 25:         match self {
 26:             Self::Negative => -1.0,
 27:             Self::Positive => 1.0,
 28:         }
 29:     }
 30: }

 32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]

 34: pub enum QuarterTurn {
 35:     Zero = 0,
 36:     Clockwise = 1,
 37: }

 39: /// Axis-aligned bounds in world X/Z. All anomaly footprints are rectangles
 40: /// rotated in 90-degree increments so construction remains rectilinear.
 41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 42: pub struct WorldBounds {
 43:     pub min_x: f32,
 44:     pub min_z: f32,
 45:     pub max_x: f32,
 46:     pub max_z: f32,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: impl WorldBounds {
 50:     pub fn new(min_x: f32, min_z: f32, max_x: f32, max_z: f32) -> Self {
 51:         Self {
 52:             min_x: min_x.min(max_x),
 53:             min_z: min_z.min(max_z),
 54:             max_x: min_x.max(max_x),
 55:             max_z: min_z.max(max_z),
 56:         }
 57:     }
 58: 
 59:     pub fn contains(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> bool {
 60:         x >= self.min_x && x <= self.max_x && z >= self.min_z && z <= self.max_z
 61:     }
 62: 
 63:     pub fn intersects(&self, other: Self) -> bool {
 64:         self.min_x <= other.max_x
 65:             && self.max_x >= other.min_x
 66:             && self.min_z <= other.max_z
 67:             && self.max_z >= other.min_z
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     pub fn expanded(self, margin: f32) -> Self {
 71:         Self::new(
 72:             self.min_x - margin,
 73:             self.min_z - margin,
 74:             self.max_x + margin,
 75:             self.max_z + margin,
 76:         )
 77:     }
 78: }

 80: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 81: pub struct OrthoBasis {
 82:     pub turn: QuarterTurn,
 83: }
 84: 
 85: impl OrthoBasis {
 86:     pub fn to_local(self, dx: f32, dz: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
 87:         match self.turn {
 88:             QuarterTurn::Zero => (dx, dz),
 89:             QuarterTurn::Clockwise => (dz, -dx),
 90:         }
 91:     }
 92: 
 93:     pub fn to_world(self, lx: f32, lz: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
 94:         match self.turn {
 95:             QuarterTurn::Zero => (lx, lz),
 96:             QuarterTurn::Clockwise => (-lz, lx),
 97:         }
 98:     }
 99: 
100:     pub fn local_axis_in_world(self, axis: Axis2) -> Axis2 {
101:         match (self.turn, axis) {
102:             (QuarterTurn::Zero, a) => a,
103:             (QuarterTurn::Clockwise, Axis2::X) => Axis2::Z,
104:             (QuarterTurn::Clockwise, Axis2::Z) => Axis2::X,
105:         }
106:     }
107: }

109: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
110: pub struct OrientedFootprint {
111:     pub center: Position,
112:     /// Half extents in the instance's local coordinates.
113:     pub half_x: f32,
114:     pub half_z: f32,
115:     pub basis: OrthoBasis,
116: }
117: 
118: impl OrientedFootprint {
119:     pub fn local_coords(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> (f32, f32) {
120:         self.basis.to_local(wx - self.center.x, wz - self.center.z)
121:     }
122: 
123:     pub fn world_coords(&self, lx: f32, lz: f32) -> Position {
124:         let (dx, dz) = self.basis.to_world(lx, lz);
125:         Position::new(self.center.x + dx, self.center.z + dz)
126:     }
127: 
128:     pub fn contains(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> bool {
129:         let (x, z) = self.local_coords(wx, wz);
130:         x.abs() <= self.half_x && z.abs() <= self.half_z
131:     }
132: 
133:     pub fn boundary_distance(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
134:         let (x, z) = self.local_coords(wx, wz);
135:         (self.half_x - x.abs()).min(self.half_z - z.abs())
136:     }
137: 
138:     pub fn normalized_depth(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
139:         (self.boundary_distance(wx, wz) / self.half_x.min(self.half_z).max(0.001)).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
140:     }
141: 
142:     pub fn bounds(&self) -> WorldBounds {
143:         let (hx, hz) = match self.basis.turn {
144:             QuarterTurn::Zero => (self.half_x, self.half_z),
145:             QuarterTurn::Clockwise => (self.half_z, self.half_x),
146:         };
147:         WorldBounds::new(
148:             self.center.x - hx,
149:             self.center.z - hz,
150:             self.center.x + hx,
151:             self.center.z + hz,
152:         )
153:     }
154: }

156: pub(super) fn decode_axis(value: u32) -> Option<Axis2> {
157:     match value {
158:         0 => Some(Axis2::X),
159:         1 => Some(Axis2::Z),
160:         _ => None,
161:     }
162: }
163: 
164: pub(super) fn decode_direction(value: u32) -> Option<AxisDirection> {
165:     match value {
166:         0 => Some(AxisDirection::Negative),
167:         1 => Some(AxisDirection::Positive),
168:         _ => None,
169:     }
170: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Shared material/environment semantics for Level 0.
  2: //!
  3: //! Generation decides *meaning* here — wall treatment, carpet depth and
  4: //! condition, floor state, ceiling character, fixture policy, ambience, and
  5: //! stability class — and every consumer (voxelization, renderers via the
  6: //! material palette, engine audio hooks, debug tooling) derives from the same
  7: //! profile instead of re-inventing ad hoc zone checks.
  8: 
  9: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 10:     VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_FLUID,
 11:     VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_PALE_WALL, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL,
 12:     VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_WALL,
 13: };
 14: 
 15: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 16: pub enum WallTreatment {
 17:     /// Ordinary Level 0 yellow wallpaper.
 18:     YellowWallpaper,
 19:     /// Pale bone-tinted arch-room masonry.
 20:     PaleArch,
 21:     /// Rough, damaged blackout-expanse surface.
 22:     RoughBlackout,
 23:     /// Peeled wallpaper with crimson underneath (red-room contamination).
 24:     CrimsonPeeled,
 25: }

 27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 28: pub enum CarpetDepth {
 29:     Shallow,
 30:     Normal,
 31:     Deep,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 35: pub enum CarpetCondition {
 36:     Dry,
 37:     Damp,
 38:     /// Wet, sticky, coarse — the red-room approach and interior.
 39:     WetSticky,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 43: pub enum FloorState {
 44:     Level,
 45:     /// Recessed basin pooling dark ankle-deep fluid (visual-only; collision
 46:     /// stays flat so no random unavoidable deaths).
 47:     RecessedFluid,

 49:     Open,
 50: }
 51: 
 52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 53: pub enum CeilingCharacter {
 54:     Compressed,

 59: 
 60: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 61: pub enum FixturePolicy {
 62:     /// Dense office fluorescent grid.
 63:     OfficeGrid,
 64:     /// Wider, sparser rhythm (expanses).
 65:     SparseWide,
 66:     /// Only the cool recovery-skeleton glimmers.
 67:     GlimmerSkeleton,

 69:     RedPressure,

 71:     WarmPendant,

 88: 
 89: /// How a space participates in the spatial-reality contract.

 91: pub enum StabilityClass {

 96:     StaticSpace,

100:     /// Regenerates as a closed loop through explicit threshold events
101:     /// (red rooms).
102:     ThresholdLoop,

104: 
105: /// One compact semantic profile for a column/space of Level 0.
106: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
107: pub struct EnvironmentProfile {
108:     pub wall: WallTreatment,
109:     pub carpet_depth: CarpetDepth,
110:     pub carpet_condition: CarpetCondition,
111:     pub floor: FloorState,
112:     pub ceiling: CeilingCharacter,
113:     pub fixtures: FixturePolicy,
114:     pub audio: AudioAmbience,
115:     pub stability: StabilityClass,
116: }
117: 
118: impl EnvironmentProfile {
119:     pub const fn level0_fabric() -> Self {
120:         Self {
121:             wall: WallTreatment::YellowWallpaper,
122:             carpet_depth: CarpetDepth::Normal,
123:             carpet_condition: CarpetCondition::Damp,
124:             floor: FloorState::Level,
125:             ceiling: CeilingCharacter::Dropped,
126:             fixtures: FixturePolicy::OfficeGrid,
127:             audio: AudioAmbience::FluorescentBuzz,
128:             stability: StabilityClass::StaticSpace,
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Calmer, drier, paler than ordinary Level 0.
133:     pub const fn pillar_expanse() -> Self {
134:         Self {
135:             wall: WallTreatment::YellowWallpaper,
136:             carpet_depth: CarpetDepth::Shallow,
137:             carpet_condition: CarpetCondition::Dry,
138:             floor: FloorState::Level,
139:             ceiling: CeilingCharacter::Open,
140:             fixtures: FixturePolicy::SparseWide,
141:             audio: AudioAmbience::FluorescentBuzz,
142:             stability: StabilityClass::WakeRemappable,
143:         }
144:     }
145: 
146:     /// `depth` is the normalized distance into the footprint (0 boundary,
147:     /// 1 core): the approach earns its darkness gradually.
148:     pub fn blackout(depth: f32) -> Self {
149:         Self {
150:             wall: if depth > 0.15 {
151:                 WallTreatment::RoughBlackout
152:             } else {
153:                 WallTreatment::YellowWallpaper
154:             },
155:             carpet_depth: CarpetDepth::Normal,
156:             carpet_condition: CarpetCondition::Damp,
157:             floor: if depth > 0.35 {
158:                 FloorState::RecessedFluid
159:             } else {
160:                 FloorState::Level
161:             },
162:             ceiling: if depth > 0.68 {
163:                 CeilingCharacter::Compressed
164:             } else {
165:                 CeilingCharacter::Dropped
166:             },
167:             fixtures: if depth > 0.22 {
168:                 FixturePolicy::GlimmerSkeleton
169:             } else {
170:                 FixturePolicy::OfficeGrid
171:             },
172:             audio: if depth > 0.55 {
173:                 AudioAmbience::BlackoutSilence
174:             } else if depth > 0.22 {
175:                 AudioAmbience::GlimmerCue
176:             } else {
177:                 AudioAmbience::FadingBuzz
178:             },
179:             stability: StabilityClass::WakeRemappable,
180:         }
181:     }
182: 
183:     /// `contamination` is 0 outside the warning band, 1 at the threshold.
184:     pub fn red_room(contamination: f32) -> Self {
185:         Self {
186:             wall: if contamination > 0.33 {
187:                 WallTreatment::CrimsonPeeled
188:             } else {
189:                 WallTreatment::YellowWallpaper
190:             },
191:             carpet_depth: CarpetDepth::Deep,
192:             carpet_condition: CarpetCondition::WetSticky,
193:             floor: FloorState::Level,
194:             ceiling: CeilingCharacter::Compressed,
195:             fixtures: FixturePolicy::RedPressure,
196:             audio: AudioAmbience::RedPressure,
197:             stability: StabilityClass::ThresholdLoop,
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:     pub const fn archway_room() -> Self {
202:         Self {
203:             wall: WallTreatment::PaleArch,
204:             carpet_depth: CarpetDepth::Deep,
205:             carpet_condition: CarpetCondition::WetSticky,
206:             floor: FloorState::Level,
207:             ceiling: CeilingCharacter::Dropped,
208:             fixtures: FixturePolicy::WarmPendant,
209:             audio: AudioAmbience::FluorescentBuzz,
210:             stability: StabilityClass::ImmutableAnchor,
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:     /// The wall material this profile voxelizes as.
215:     pub fn wall_voxel(&self) -> u8 {
216:         match self.wall {
217:             WallTreatment::YellowWallpaper => VOXEL_WALL,
218:             WallTreatment::PaleArch => VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
219:             WallTreatment::RoughBlackout => VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
220:             WallTreatment::CrimsonPeeled => VOXEL_RED_WALL,
221:         }
222:     }
223: 
224:     /// The floor material this profile voxelizes as.
225:     pub fn floor_voxel(&self) -> u8 {
226:         if self.floor == FloorState::RecessedFluid {
227:             return VOXEL_FLUID;
228:         }
229:         match (self.carpet_depth, self.carpet_condition) {
230:             (CarpetDepth::Shallow, _) | (_, CarpetCondition::Dry) => VOXEL_DRY_CARPET,
231:             (CarpetDepth::Deep, CarpetCondition::WetSticky) => match self.wall {
232:                 WallTreatment::CrimsonPeeled => VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET,
233:                 _ => VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET,
234:             },
235:             (CarpetDepth::Deep, _) => VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET,
236:             _ => VOXEL_FLOOR,
237:         }
238:     }
239: 
240:     /// The fixture material this profile voxelizes as.
241:     pub fn light_voxel(&self) -> u8 {
242:         match self.fixtures {
243:             FixturePolicy::GlimmerSkeleton => VOXEL_GLIMMER,
244:             FixturePolicy::RedPressure => VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
245:             _ => VOXEL_LIGHT,
246:         }
247:     }
248: }
````

## File: src/domain/entities/player_vitals.rs
````rust
  1: //! Survival vitals: the wanderer's hydration, satiety, and condition.
  2: //!
  3: //! Pure domain math — no clocks, no frames, no renderer knowledge. The
  4: //! application advances a value copy once per simulation step with the
  5: //! ambient temperature it measured, and reads back plain numbers for the
  6: //! HUD. All quantities are normalized 0..=1 so presenters never re-scale.
  7: 
  8: /// Neutral indoor temperature, °C. Depletion multipliers are centered here.
  9: const COMFORT_TEMPERATURE_C: f32 = 21.0;
 10: 
 11: /// Seconds for full hydration to deplete at comfort temperature.
 12: const HYDRATION_SECONDS: f32 = 18.0 * 60.0;
 13: /// Seconds for full satiety to deplete (hunger is the slower pressure).
 14: const SATIETY_SECONDS: f32 = 40.0 * 60.0;
 15: /// Extra thirst per °C above comfort: at Level 0's ~33 °C the multiplier
 16: /// is 1 + 12 * 0.07 ≈ 1.8x, turning the mono-yellow heat into real urgency.
 17: const HEAT_THIRST_PER_DEGREE: f32 = 0.07;
 18: /// Seconds for full condition to collapse while a vital sits at zero.
 19: /// Both vitals empty drain twice as fast.
 20: const CONDITION_SECONDS: f32 = 90.0;
 21: /// Condition slowly mends while both vitals are comfortable (> 0.3).
 22: const CONDITION_RECOVERY_SECONDS: f32 = 120.0;
 23: 
 24: /// One almond water restores this much hydration (canon: the safest liquid
 25: /// in the Backrooms) and calms a fraction of lost condition. Public so the
 26: /// application can price the *waste* of drinking past a full reserve.
 27: pub const ALMOND_WATER_HYDRATION: f32 = 0.65;
 28: const ALMOND_WATER_CONDITION: f32 = 0.15;
 29: /// One ration restores this much satiety. Public for the same waste math.
 30: pub const RATION_SATIETY: f32 = 0.55;
 31: 
 32: /// Normalized survival state. `1.0` is fully provisioned; `0.0` is empty.
 33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 34: pub struct PlayerVitals {
 35:     /// Thirst reserve. Depletes constantly; ambient heat accelerates it.
 36:     pub hydration: f32,
 37:     /// Hunger reserve. Depletes constantly, slower than hydration.
 38:     pub satiety: f32,
 39:     /// Physical condition. Collapses only while a reserve is empty;
 40:     /// reaching zero is death (the application decides what death does).
 41:     pub condition: f32,
 42: }
 43: 
 44: impl Default for PlayerVitals {
 45:     fn default() -> Self {
 46:         Self {
 47:             hydration: 1.0,
 48:             satiety: 1.0,
 49:             condition: 1.0,
 50:         }
 51:     }
 52: }
 53: 
 54: impl PlayerVitals {
 55:     /// Advances the vitals by `dt_seconds` under `ambient_c` degrees Celsius.
 56:     /// Pure: same inputs, same outputs; the application owns the clock.
 57:     #[must_use]
 58:     pub fn advanced(mut self, dt_seconds: f32, ambient_c: f32) -> Self {
 59:         let dt = dt_seconds.max(0.0);
 60:         let heat = 1.0 + (ambient_c - COMFORT_TEMPERATURE_C).max(0.0) * HEAT_THIRST_PER_DEGREE;
 61:         self.hydration = (self.hydration - dt * heat / HYDRATION_SECONDS).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 62:         self.satiety = (self.satiety - dt / SATIETY_SECONDS).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 63: 
 64:         let starved = u32::from(self.hydration <= 0.0) + u32::from(self.satiety <= 0.0);
 65:         self.condition = if starved > 0 {
 66:             (self.condition - dt * starved as f32 / CONDITION_SECONDS).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 67:         } else if self.hydration > 0.3 && self.satiety > 0.3 {
 68:             (self.condition + dt / CONDITION_RECOVERY_SECONDS).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
 69:         } else {
 70:             self.condition
 71:         };
 72:         self
 73:     }
 74: 
 75:     /// Drinks one almond water bottle.
 76:     #[must_use]
 77:     pub fn drank_almond_water(mut self) -> Self {
 78:         self.hydration = (self.hydration + ALMOND_WATER_HYDRATION).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 79:         self.condition = (self.condition + ALMOND_WATER_CONDITION).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 80:         self
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     /// Eats one ration.
 84:     #[must_use]
 85:     pub fn ate_ration(mut self) -> Self {
 86:         self.satiety = (self.satiety + RATION_SATIETY).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 87:         self
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     /// True once condition has fully collapsed.
 91:     pub fn is_dead(&self) -> bool {
 92:         self.condition <= 0.0
 93:     }
 94: }
 95: 
 96: #[cfg(test)]
 97: mod tests {
 98:     use super::*;
 99: 
100:     #[test]
101:     fn heat_accelerates_thirst_but_not_hunger() {
102:         let cool = PlayerVitals::default().advanced(600.0, 21.0);
103:         let hot = PlayerVitals::default().advanced(600.0, 33.0);
104:         assert!(hot.hydration < cool.hydration, "heat must cost extra water");
105:         assert!((hot.satiety - cool.satiety).abs() < 1e-6);
106:     }
107: 
108:     #[test]
109:     fn empty_reserves_collapse_condition_and_zero_condition_is_death() {
110:         let mut vitals = PlayerVitals {
111:             hydration: 0.0,
112:             satiety: 0.0,
113:             condition: 1.0,
114:         };
115:         assert!(!vitals.is_dead());
116:         vitals = vitals.advanced(30.0, 21.0);
117:         assert!(vitals.condition < 0.4, "double starvation drains fast");
118:         vitals = vitals.advanced(60.0, 21.0);
119:         assert!(vitals.is_dead());
120:     }
121: 
122:     #[test]
123:     fn condition_recovers_only_while_provisioned() {
124:         let hurt = PlayerVitals {
125:             hydration: 0.8,
126:             satiety: 0.8,
127:             condition: 0.5,
128:         };
129:         assert!(hurt.advanced(60.0, 21.0).condition > 0.5);
130: 
131:         let parched = PlayerVitals {
132:             hydration: 0.1,
133:             satiety: 0.8,
134:             condition: 0.5,
135:         };
136:         assert!(parched.advanced(60.0, 21.0).condition <= 0.5);
137:     }
138: 
139:     #[test]
140:     fn supplies_restore_their_vital() {
141:         let weary = PlayerVitals {
142:             hydration: 0.2,
143:             satiety: 0.2,
144:             condition: 0.4,
145:         };
146:         let refreshed = weary.drank_almond_water();
147:         assert!((refreshed.hydration - 0.85).abs() < 1e-6);
148:         assert!(refreshed.condition > 0.4);
149:         let fed = weary.ate_ration();
150:         assert!((fed.satiety - 0.75).abs() < 1e-6);
151:     }
152: 
153:     #[test]
154:     fn vitals_never_leave_the_unit_interval() {
155:         let v = PlayerVitals::default()
156:             .drank_almond_water()
157:             .ate_ration()
158:             .advanced(1_000_000.0, 50.0);
159:         assert_eq!(v.hydration, 0.0);
160:         assert_eq!(v.satiety, 0.0);
161:         assert!(v.condition >= 0.0 && v.condition <= 1.0);
162:     }
163: }
````

## File: src/domain/entities/supplies.rs
````rust
 1: //! Consumable supply items exported beside generated voxel geometry.
 2: //!
 3: //! A supply item is a semantic pickup point: generation places it (and a
 4: //! small marker of matching voxels), the application detects proximity and
 5: //! consumes it. Whether an item still exists is *reality* state — consumed
 6: //! ids live in the `RealitySnapshot`, so a regenerated chunk deterministically
 7: //! omits what the wanderer already drank.
 8: 
 9: use crate::entities::models::Position;
10: 
11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
12: #[repr(u8)]
13: pub enum SupplyKind {
14:     /// Canon Backrooms hydration: the safest liquid on Level 0 and Level 1.
15:     AlmondWater = 0,
16:     /// Scavenged food (Level 1 supply crates, rare Level 0 finds).
17:     Ration = 1,
18: }
19: 
20: pub(crate) fn decode_supply_kind(value: u32) -> Option<SupplyKind> {
21:     match value {
22:         0 => Some(SupplyKind::AlmondWater),
23:         1 => Some(SupplyKind::Ration),
24:         _ => None,
25:     }
26: }
27: 
28: /// One placed consumable. `position` is the marker's floor point; `rest_y`
29: /// is the marker's base height in world units (bottles sit on crates too).
30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
31: pub struct SupplyItem {
32:     pub id: u64,
33:     pub kind: SupplyKind,
34:     pub position: Position,
35:     pub rest_y: f32,
36: }
37: 
38: impl SupplyItem {
39:     pub const WORDS: usize = 6;
40: 
41:     pub fn within_reach(&self, x: f32, z: f32, reach: f32) -> bool {
42:         let dx = x - self.position.x;
43:         let dz = z - self.position.z;
44:         dx * dx + dz * dz <= reach * reach
45:     }
46: 
47:     pub fn to_words(self) -> [u32; Self::WORDS] {
48:         [
49:             self.id as u32,
50:             (self.id >> 32) as u32,
51:             self.kind as u32,
52:             self.position.x.to_bits(),
53:             self.position.z.to_bits(),
54:             self.rest_y.to_bits(),
55:         ]
56:     }
57: 
58:     pub fn from_words(words: &[u32]) -> Option<Self> {
59:         if words.len() != Self::WORDS {
60:             return None;
61:         }
62:         Some(Self {
63:             id: words[0] as u64 | ((words[1] as u64) << 32),
64:             kind: decode_supply_kind(words[2])?,
65:             position: Position::new(f32::from_bits(words[3]), f32::from_bits(words[4])),
66:             rest_y: f32::from_bits(words[5]),
67:         })
68:     }
69: }
70: 
71: #[cfg(test)]
72: mod tests {
73:     use super::*;
74: 
75:     #[test]
76:     fn transport_words_round_trip() {
77:         let item = SupplyItem {
78:             id: 0xDEAD_BEEF_0042_1177,
79:             kind: SupplyKind::Ration,
80:             position: Position::new(-12.25, 830.5),
81:             rest_y: 0.8,
82:         };
83:         assert_eq!(SupplyItem::from_words(&item.to_words()), Some(item));
84:         assert_eq!(SupplyItem::from_words(&[0; 3]), None);
85:     }
86: 
87:     #[test]
88:     fn reach_is_a_horizontal_disc() {
89:         let item = SupplyItem {
90:             id: 1,
91:             kind: SupplyKind::AlmondWater,
92:             position: Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
93:             rest_y: 0.0,
94:         };
95:         assert!(item.within_reach(10.5, 10.0, 0.6));
96:         assert!(!item.within_reach(11.0, 11.0, 0.6));
97:     }
98: }
````

````rust
 1: /// Position represents a 2D coordinate in the continuous noise space.
 2: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 3: pub struct Position {
 4:     pub x: f32,
 5:     pub z: f32,
 6: }
 7: 
 8: impl Position {
 9:     pub fn new(x: f32, z: f32) -> Self {
10:         Self { x, z }
11:     }
12: 
13:     pub fn distance(&self, other: &Position) -> f32 {
14:         ((self.x - other.x).powi(2) + (self.z - other.z).powi(2)).sqrt()
15:     }
16: }
17:

24:         let p1 = Position::new(0.0, 0.0);
25:         let p2 = Position::new(3.0, 4.0);
26:         assert_eq!(p1.distance(&p2), 5.0);
27:     }
````

## File: src/use_cases/anomalies/determinism.rs
````rust
 1: //! Shared deterministic primitives for anomaly planners.
 2: //!
 3: //! These helpers are intentionally integer-first. A candidate's identity must
 4: //! depend on the world seed and its stable lattice anchor, never on which
 5: //! region or voxel chunk happened to request it.
 6: 
 7: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 8: 
 9: pub(crate) const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
10: 
11: pub(crate) fn snap(value: f32) -> f32 {
12:     (value / SNAP).round() * SNAP
13: }
14: 
15: pub(crate) fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
16:     value ^= value >> 30;
17:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
18:     value ^= value >> 27;
19:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
20:     value ^ (value >> 31)
21: }
22: 
23: pub(crate) fn hash(seed: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> u64 {
24:     mix64(
25:         seed as u64
26:             ^ salt
27:             ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
28:             ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(31),
29:     )
30: }
31: 
32: pub(crate) fn unit(hash: u64) -> f32 {
33:     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
34: }
35: 
36: pub(crate) fn stable_id(seed: u32, kind: AnomalyKind, anchor_x: i64, anchor_z: i64) -> u64 {
37:     hash(
38:         seed,
39:         0xA110_4A1E_0000_0000 | kind as u64,
40:         anchor_x,
41:         anchor_z,
42:     )
43: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/project_onto_solid_receivers.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
 2: 
 3: use super::exposed_emissive_faces::emission_rgb;
 4: use super::propagate_through_air::{AirPropagation, UNREACHABLE};
 5: use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
 6: use super::voxel_neighborhood::{for_each_face_neighbor, for_each_voxel};
 7: use super::world_space_attenuation::{accumulate_attenuated, pack_emission, pack_rgb};
 8: 
 9: /// Copies incident air irradiance onto the first occupied voxel at a surface.
10: /// Receivers are never fed back into propagation, which is the invariant that
11: /// prevents a lit wall from leaking energy into the room behind it.
12: pub(crate) fn project_onto_solid_receivers(
13:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
14:     propagated: &AirPropagation,
15:     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
16: ) {
17:     for_each_voxel(propagated.dimensions, |coord| {
18:         let voxel_type = grid.get(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z);
19:         if voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
20:             return;
21:         }
22: 
23:         if let Some(rgb) = emission_rgb(voxel_type) {
24:             grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_emission(rgb));
25:             return;
26:         }
27: 
28:         let mut irradiance = [0.0; 3];
29:         for emission in &propagated.emissions {
30:             let mut nearest_air_steps = UNREACHABLE;
31:             for_each_face_neighbor(coord, propagated.dimensions, |neighbor| {
32:                 if grid.get(neighbor.x, neighbor.y, neighbor.z) != VOXEL_AIR {
33:                     return;
34:                 }
35:                 nearest_air_steps = nearest_air_steps
36:                     .min(emission.distance_steps[propagated.dimensions.index(neighbor)]);
37:             });
38:             if nearest_air_steps != UNREACHABLE {
39:                 accumulate_attenuated(
40:                     &mut irradiance,
41:                     emission.profile,
42:                     nearest_air_steps,
43:                     1.0,
44:                     settings,
45:                 );
46:             }
47:         }
48:         grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_rgb(irradiance));
49:     });
50: }
````

````rust
 4: /// Default finite reach of baked fixture light, measured in world units.
 5: ///
 6: /// Six units keeps ordinary 3.2--5.4 unit rooms illuminated while still
 7: /// reaching zero before distant fixtures can flatten a whole streamed scene.
 8: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS: f32 = 6.0;
 9: 
10: /// Physical sampling settings for one voxel-light bake.
11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
12: pub struct VoxelLightingSettings {
13:     voxel_size_world_units: f32,
14:     max_range_world_units: f32,
15: }
16: 
17: impl VoxelLightingSettings {
18:     /// Creates validated settings. Both values are lengths in the same world
19:     /// coordinate system used by generated architecture and runtime lights.
20:     pub fn new(
21:         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
22:         max_range_world_units: f32,
23:     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
24:         if !voxel_size_world_units.is_finite() || voxel_size_world_units <= 0.0 {
25:             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::VoxelSize);
26:         }
27:         if !max_range_world_units.is_finite() || max_range_world_units <= 0.0 {
28:             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::MaxRange);
29:         }
30:         Ok(Self {
31:             voxel_size_world_units,
32:             max_range_world_units,
33:         })
34:     }
35: 
36:     /// Uses the engine's ordinary finite fixture range with an exact scene
37:     /// voxel size supplied by the generation configuration.
38:     pub fn with_default_range(
39:         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
40:     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
41:         Self::new(voxel_size_world_units, DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS)
42:     }
43: 
44:     pub fn voxel_size_world_units(self) -> f32 {
45:         self.voxel_size_world_units
46:     }
47: 
48:     pub fn max_range_world_units(self) -> f32 {
49:         self.max_range_world_units
50:     }
51: }
52: 
53: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
54: pub enum InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
55:     VoxelSize,
56:     MaxRange,
57: }
58: 
59: impl Display for InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
60:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
61:         match self {
62:             Self::VoxelSize => {
63:                 formatter.write_str("voxel size must be finite and greater than zero")
64:             }
65:             Self::MaxRange => {
66:                 formatter.write_str("maximum light range must be finite and greater than zero")
67:             }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/voxel_neighborhood.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
 2: 
 3: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 4: pub(crate) struct VoxelCoord {
 5:     pub(crate) x: usize,
 6:     pub(crate) y: usize,
 7:     pub(crate) z: usize,
 8: }
 9: 
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11: pub(crate) struct GridDimensions {
12:     pub(crate) width: usize,
13:     pub(crate) height: usize,
14:     pub(crate) depth: usize,
15: }
16: 
17: impl GridDimensions {
18:     pub(crate) fn of(grid: &VoxelGrid) -> Self {
19:         Self {
20:             width: grid.width(),
21:             height: grid.height(),
22:             depth: grid.depth(),
23:         }
24:     }
25: 
26:     pub(crate) fn volume(self) -> usize {
27:         self.width * self.height * self.depth
28:     }
29: 
30:     /// Matches `VoxelGrid`'s y-major, then z, then x storage order without
31:     /// exposing the entity's backing vectors to the use case.
32:     pub(crate) fn index(self, coord: VoxelCoord) -> usize {
33:         coord.y * (self.width * self.depth) + coord.z * self.width + coord.x
34:     }
35: }
36: 
37: pub(crate) fn for_each_voxel(dimensions: GridDimensions, mut visit: impl FnMut(VoxelCoord)) {
38:     for z in 0..dimensions.depth {
39:         for y in 0..dimensions.height {
40:             for x in 0..dimensions.width {
41:                 visit(VoxelCoord { x, y, z });
42:             }
43:         }
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// Visits the six face-sharing cells in a fixed order. The order makes the
48: /// implementation reproducible, while shortest integer distances make the
49: /// result independent of which equally short route was visited first.
50: pub(crate) fn for_each_face_neighbor(
51:     coord: VoxelCoord,
52:     dimensions: GridDimensions,
53:     mut visit: impl FnMut(VoxelCoord),
54: ) {
55:     if coord.x + 1 < dimensions.width {
56:         visit(VoxelCoord {
57:             x: coord.x + 1,
58:             ..coord
59:         });
60:     }
61:     if coord.x > 0 {
62:         visit(VoxelCoord {
63:             x: coord.x - 1,
64:             ..coord
65:         });
66:     }
67:     if coord.y + 1 < dimensions.height {
68:         visit(VoxelCoord {
69:             y: coord.y + 1,
70:             ..coord
71:         });
72:     }
73:     if coord.y > 0 {
74:         visit(VoxelCoord {
75:             y: coord.y - 1,
76:             ..coord
77:         });
78:     }
79:     if coord.z + 1 < dimensions.depth {
80:         visit(VoxelCoord {
81:             z: coord.z + 1,
82:             ..coord
83:         });
84:     }
85:     if coord.z > 0 {
86:         visit(VoxelCoord {
87:             z: coord.z - 1,
88:             ..coord
89:         });
90:     }
91: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/world_space_attenuation.rs
````rust
 1: use super::exposed_emissive_faces::EmissionProfile;
 2: use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
 3: 
 4: /// Adds one emission class after finite-range linear attenuation.
 5: ///
 6: /// `cell_offsets` accounts for the half-cell from an emitting face to its
 7: /// first air center. Air samples use 0.5. A solid receiver adds the second
 8: /// half-cell from its neighboring air center to the receiving face and uses
 9: /// 1.0. Those two halves make equal physical gaps agree at 0.1 and 0.2 unit
10: /// voxel sizes instead of differing by one resolution-dependent cell center.
11: pub(crate) fn accumulate_attenuated(
12:     accumulated: &mut [f32; 3],
13:     profile: EmissionProfile,
14:     distance_steps: u32,
15:     cell_offsets: f32,
16:     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
17: ) {
18:     let distance_world = (distance_steps as f32 + cell_offsets) * settings.voxel_size_world_units();
19:     let remaining = (1.0 - distance_world / settings.max_range_world_units()).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
20:     for channel in 0..3 {
21:         accumulated[channel] += profile.rgb[channel] * remaining;
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: pub(crate) fn pack_rgb(accumulated: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
26:     accumulated.map(|channel| channel.round().clamp(0.0, 15.0) as u8)
27: }
28: 
29: pub(crate) fn pack_emission(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
30:     pack_rgb(rgb)
31: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_one/mod.rs
````rust
 1: //! Level 1 — the Habitable Zone.
 2: //!
 3: //! A sprawling warehouse/parking structure honoring the Backrooms wiki canon:
 4: //! bare concrete walls and massive pillars, institutional tile floors,
 5: //! exposed ceiling pipes, low-hanging fog (the renderer's atmosphere, not
 6: //! voxels), and fluorescent fixtures dimmer and less reliable than Level 0's.
 7: //! No entities are generated at this stage.
 8: //!
 9: //! The level is carved into functional **sectors** on a fixed world lattice,
10: //! each with its own `StructuralSystem` flavor:
11: //!
12: //! * **Aquila** — bland parking-lot expanses: concrete slab, huge square
13: //!   pillars on a deep-span grid, sparse lighting.
14: //! * **Gild** — dense storage architecture: concrete room fabric packed with
15: //!   supply crates (almond water, food) behind doorway'd walls.
16: //! * **Gothic** — curved masonry: circular pillars joined by real arches
17: //!   under vaulted ceilings.
18: //! * **Construction** — perpetually unfinished: half-height walls, rebar
19: //!   clusters, dead ends, chaotic ceiling heights.
20: //!
21: //! Every column is a pure function of world-space coordinates and the seed,
22: //! so chunks tile seamlessly in any streaming order. Consumable supplies are
23: //! exported beside the geometry; whether one still exists is reality state
24: //! (`RealitySnapshot::supply_consumed`), never grid state.
25: 
26: pub(crate) mod generate;
27: #[cfg(test)]
28: mod tests;
29: 
30: /// Ceiling height budget shared with Level 0's grid allocation.
31: pub const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
32: 
33: /// Side of one sector cell, world units. Sector *type* changes per cell but
34: /// every structural lattice below is phased to world coordinates, so walls
35: /// and pillar grids run continuously across sector borders.
36: pub const SECTOR_CELL: f32 = 96.0;
37: 
38: /// Level 1 — one zero-sized generator, like its siblings.
39: pub struct HabitableLevel;
40: 
41: /// The functional sub-regions of Level 1.
42: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
43: pub enum Sector {
44:     Aquila,
45:     Gild,
46:     Gothic,
47:     Construction,
48: }
49: 
50: impl Sector {
51:     /// Deterministic sector of a world position (hash of its lattice cell).
52:     pub fn at(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> Self {
53:         let cx = (wx / SECTOR_CELL).floor() as i64;
54:         let cz = (wz / SECTOR_CELL).floor() as i64;
55:         let roll = crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::hash(
56:             seed,
57:             0x1EE1_5EC7_0A00_0001,
58:             cx,
59:             cz,
60:         ) % 100;
61:         // The arrival cell is always Aquila: the wanderer steps out of the
62:         // door into readable parking-lot openness, exactly the first-report
63:         // canon of Level 1.
64:         if cx == 0 && cz == 0 {
65:             return Self::Aquila;
66:         }
67:         match roll {
68:             0..=34 => Self::Aquila,
69:             35..=62 => Self::Gild,
70:             63..=81 => Self::Gothic,
71:             _ => Self::Construction,
72:         }
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// HUD name of this sector.
76:     pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
77:         match self {
78:             Self::Aquila => "AQUILA SECTOR",
79:             Self::Gild => "GILD SECTOR",
80:             Self::Gothic => "GOTHIC SECTOR",
81:             Self::Construction => "CONSTRUCTION SECTOR",
82:         }
83:     }
84: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/assembly_sampler.rs
````rust
  1: //! Sampling one planned assembly: perimeter walls pierced by entrances,
  2: //! sparse interior partitions, structural bays (plus a renovator's
  3: //! contradictory grid), and fixtures on the room's ceiling modules.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  6:     AssemblyInstance, CeilingLanguage, StructuralSystem, StructuralSystemInstance,
  7: };
  8: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::LevelTuning;
  9: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 10: 
 11: use super::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan, DOOR_HEIGHT};
 12: 
 13: impl BackroomsLevel {
 14:     /// Is (wx, wz) on a structural column of this system?
 15:     pub(super) fn on_column(st: &StructuralSystemInstance, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> bool {
 16:         if st.system == StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell {
 17:             // Core-and-shell designers hide columns in walls; none inside.
 18:             return false;
 19:         }
 20:         let mut mx = (wx - st.phase.0).rem_euclid(st.bay_x);
 21:         let mz = (wz - st.phase.1).rem_euclid(st.bay_z);
 22:         if st.system == StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid {
 23:             let row = ((wz - st.phase.1) / st.bay_z).floor() as i64;
 24:             if row.rem_euclid(2) == 1 {
 25:                 mx = (wx - st.phase.0 + st.bay_x * 0.5).rem_euclid(st.bay_x);
 26:             }
 27:         }
 28:         mx < st.column_side && mz < st.column_side
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     /// Column plan for a point inside an assembly footprint or its
 32:     /// surrounding wall band (`inside == false`).
 33:     pub(super) fn assembly_column(
 34:         a: &AssemblyInstance,
 35:         inside: bool,
 36:         renovator: Option<&StructuralSystemInstance>,
 37:         tuning: &LevelTuning,
 38:         wx: f32,
 39:         wz: f32,
 40:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 41:         let walls_on = tuning.walls > 0.0;
 42:         let zone = a.ceiling_zones.first();
 43:         let mut ceiling_units = zone.map_or(3.4, |c| c.height_units);
 44:         match zone.map(|c| c.language) {
 45:             // Coffered reads as a shading pattern now (see the splat
 46:             // shader), not stepped geometry.
 47:             Some(CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit) => ceiling_units -= 0.2,
 48:             _ => {}
 49:         }
 50:         let mut plan = ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units);
 51: 
 52:         // Entrances pierce the wall band (and win over everything solid).
 53:         for e in &a.entrances {
 54:             let (da, db) = if e.through_x_wall {
 55:                 ((wx - e.center.x).abs(), (wz - e.center.z).abs())
 56:             } else {
 57:                 ((wz - e.center.z).abs(), (wx - e.center.x).abs())
 58:             };
 59:             if da < e.width * 0.5 && db <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
 60:                 plan.lintel_from_units = walls_on
 61:                     .then_some(e.lintel_units.unwrap_or(0.0))
 62:                     .filter(|u| *u > 0.0);
 63:                 return plan;
 64:             }
 65:         }
 66: 
 67:         if !inside {
 68:             // Perimeter wall band.
 69:             plan.solid = walls_on;
 70:             return plan;
 71:         }
 72: 
 73:         // Interior partitions: walls on space boundaries that are not the
 74:         // footprint perimeter, each with a centered doorway.
 75:         let fb = a.footprint.bounds();
 76:         if walls_on {
 77:             for s in &a.spaces {
 78:                 let sb = s.footprint.bounds();
 79:                 if wz >= sb.1 && wz <= sb.3 {
 80:                     for plane in [sb.0, sb.2] {
 81:                         if (plane - fb.0).abs() > 0.1
 82:                             && (plane - fb.2).abs() > 0.1
 83:                             && (wx - plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 84:                         {
 85:                             let door_c = (sb.1 + sb.3) * 0.5;
 86:                             if (wz - door_c).abs() < 0.6 {
 87:                                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(DOOR_HEIGHT);
 88:                             } else {
 89:                                 plan.solid = true;
 90:                             }
 91:                         }
 92:                     }
 93:                 }
 94:                 if wx >= sb.0 && wx <= sb.2 {
 95:                     for plane in [sb.1, sb.3] {
 96:                         if (plane - fb.1).abs() > 0.1
 97:                             && (plane - fb.3).abs() > 0.1
 98:                             && (wz - plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 99:                         {
100:                             let door_c = (sb.0 + sb.2) * 0.5;
101:                             if (wx - door_c).abs() < 0.6 {
102:                                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(DOOR_HEIGHT);
103:                             } else {
104:                                 plan.solid = true;
105:                             }
106:                         }
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:             }
110:         }
111: 
112:         // Structure: the original grid, plus the renovator's contradictory
113:         // grid where a renovation overlays the assembly.
114:         if tuning.pillars > 0.0 && !plan.solid {
115:             if Self::on_column(&a.structure, wx, wz) {
116:                 plan.solid = true;
117:             }
118:             if let Some(r) = renovator {
119:                 if a.corruption.renovation_overlay && Self::on_column(r, wx, wz) {
120:                     // Renovation columns intrude on the original bay rhythm;
121:                     // the contradiction itself is the corruption. They stay
122:                     // ordinary wall material — Level 0 has no red masonry.
123:                     plan.solid = true;
124:                 }
125:             }
126:         }
127: 
128:         // Fixtures, tied to the assembly's ceiling modules. In a red room
129:         // every fixture burns red: the anomaly is the room's light, applied
130:         // after all geometry decisions and on the same fixture spacing.
131:         if !plan.solid && tuning.lights > 0.0 {
132:             for f in &a.fixtures {
133:                 if f.lit && (wx - f.at.x).abs() <= f.half_x && (wz - f.at.z).abs() <= f.half_z {
134:                     plan.light = true;
135:                     plan.red_light = a.corruption.red_room;
136:                     break;
137:                 }
138:             }
139:         }
140:         plan
141:     }
142: }
````

````rust
 1: //! The shared column vocabulary every Level 0 sampler speaks.

 6: /// What one (x, z) column of the level looks like.

23:     /// ever true inside an assembly whose whole room is the anomaly.

26:     /// lintels). The space below stays walkable.
````
