## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/planning.rs
````rust
  1: //! Assembly-derived Red Room encounter planning.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room is not a macro-lattice shape. It inherits a real assembly's
  4: //! footprint and entrance, then adds stable semantic crossing planes.
  5: 
  6: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  7:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, AxisDirection, OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, QuarterTurn,
  8:     TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
  9: };
 10: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::AssemblyInstance;
 11: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 12: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{SNAP, mix64, stable_id};
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: 
 15: const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
 16: const THRESHOLD_DEPTH: f32 = 2.8;
 17: const LOOP_GATE_DEPTH: f32 = 6.0;
 18: 
 19: fn clamp_inward(desired: f32, far_inner_plane: f32, direction: AxisDirection) -> f32 {
 20:     match direction {
 21:         AxisDirection::Positive => desired.min(far_inner_plane),
 22:         AxisDirection::Negative => desired.max(far_inner_plane),
 23:     }
 24: }
 25: 
 26: fn red_room_instance(
 27:     seed: u32,
 28:     region_origin: Position,
 29:     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
 30: ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
 31:     let entrance = *assembly.entrances.first()?;
 32:     let bounds = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 33:     let center = Position::new((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
 34:     let region_x = (region_origin.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 35:     let region_z = (region_origin.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 36:     let id = mix64(
 37:         stable_id(seed, AnomalyKind::RedRoom, region_x, region_z)
 38:             ^ (assembly.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
 39:     );
 40:     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
 41:         center,
 42:         half_x: (bounds.2 - bounds.0) * 0.5,
 43:         half_z: (bounds.3 - bounds.1) * 0.5,
 44:         basis: OrthoBasis {
 45:             turn: QuarterTurn::Zero,
 46:         },
 47:     };
 48:     let axis = if entrance.through_x_wall {
 49:         Axis2::Z
 50:     } else {
 51:         Axis2::X
 52:     };
 53:     let (edge_coordinate, center_coordinate, half_depth) = match axis {
 54:         Axis2::X => (entrance.center.x, center.x, footprint.half_x),
 55:         Axis2::Z => (entrance.center.z, center.z, footprint.half_z),
 56:     };
 57:     let forward = if center_coordinate >= edge_coordinate {
 58:         AxisDirection::Positive
 59:     } else {
 60:         AxisDirection::Negative
 61:     };
 62: 
 63:     // Commitment happens inside the room, beyond the externally readable
 64:     // doorway. Entrance placement guarantees enough depth for this vestibule.
 65:     let threshold_plane = edge_coordinate + forward.sign() * THRESHOLD_DEPTH;
 66:     let (span_min, span_max) = if axis == Axis2::Z {
 67:         (
 68:             entrance.center.x - entrance.width * 0.5,
 69:             entrance.center.x + entrance.width * 0.5,
 70:         )
 71:     } else {
 72:         (
 73:             entrance.center.z - entrance.width * 0.5,
 74:             entrance.center.z + entrance.width * 0.5,
 75:         )
 76:     };
 77:     let affected_bounds = footprint.bounds();
 78:     let threshold_gate = TraversalGate {
 79:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x6A7E_0ED0),
 80:         instance_id: id,
 81:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
 82:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
 83:         axis,
 84:         plane: threshold_plane,
 85:         span_min,
 86:         span_max,
 87:         forward,
 88:         affected_bounds,
 89:     };
 90: 
 91:     // The loop checkpoint is six units beyond commitment when the room has
 92:     // that depth. Shallow rooms clamp it one plan voxel inside the far wall,
 93:     // keeping the semantic crossing on geometry owned by this encounter.
 94:     let far_inner_plane = center_coordinate + forward.sign() * (half_depth - SNAP).max(0.0);
 95:     let loop_plane = clamp_inward(
 96:         threshold_plane + forward.sign() * LOOP_GATE_DEPTH,
 97:         far_inner_plane,
 98:         forward,
 99:     );
100:     let loop_gate = TraversalGate {
101:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x9B4C_1A2F),
102:         instance_id: id,
103:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
104:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
105:         axis,
106:         plane: loop_plane,
107:         span_min,
108:         span_max,
109:         // `forward` records the authored inward direction. Runtime state owns
110:         // the separate policy for which traversal directions advance a loop.
111:         forward,
112:         affected_bounds,
113:     };
114: 
115:     Some(AnomalyInstance {
116:         id,
117:         kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
118:         footprint,
119:         basis: footprint.basis,
120:         macro_anchor: (region_x, region_z),
121:         pillar_lattice: None,
122:         pit_lattice: None,
123:         arch: None,
124:         gates: vec![threshold_gate, loop_gate],
125:         skeleton_half_width: 1.0,
126:         entry_band: THRESHOLD_DEPTH,
127:     })
128: }
129: 
130: pub(crate) fn plan_red_rooms(
131:     seed: u32,
132:     region_origin: Position,
133:     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
134:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
135: ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
136:     let forced = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
137:     let organic_enabled = config.anomalies.frequency > 0.0 && config.anomalies.red_rooms > 0.0;
138:     if !forced && !organic_enabled {
139:         return Vec::new();
140:     }
141: 
142:     assemblies
143:         .iter()
144:         .filter(|assembly| assembly.corruption.red_room)
145:         .filter_map(|assembly| red_room_instance(seed, region_origin, assembly))
146:         .collect()
147: }
148: 
149: #[cfg(test)]
150: mod tests {
151:     use super::*;
152:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
153:         CorruptionProfile, Opening, Polygon2, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystem,
154:         StructuralSystemInstance,
155:     };
156: 
157:     fn red_assembly(entrance_z: f32) -> AssemblyInstance {
158:         AssemblyInstance {
159:             id: 7,
160:             program: SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
161:             footprint: Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 12.0, 8.0),
162:             entrances: vec![Opening {
163:                 center: Position::new(6.0, entrance_z),
164:                 width: 1.2,
165:                 through_x_wall: true,
166:                 lintel_units: Some(2.2),
167:             }],
168:             spaces: Vec::new(),
169:             structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
170:                 system: StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
171:                 bay_x: 4.0,
172:                 bay_z: 4.0,
173:                 phase: (0.0, 0.0),
174:                 column_side: 0.4,
175:             },
176:             ceiling_zones: Vec::new(),
177:             fixtures: Vec::new(),
178:             service_voids: Vec::new(),
179:             corruption: CorruptionProfile {
180:                 red_room: true,
181:                 ..CorruptionProfile::default()
182:             },
183:         }
184:     }
185: 
186:     #[test]
187:     fn forced_red_room_survives_zero_frequency_and_zero_family_weight() {
188:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
189:         config.anomalies.frequency = 0.0;
190:         config.anomalies.red_rooms = 0.0;
191:         config.anomalies.forced_kind = Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
192:         let rooms = plan_red_rooms(42, Position::new(0.0, 0.0), &[red_assembly(0.0)], &config);
193:         assert_eq!(rooms.len(), 1);
194:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].kind, AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
195:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].gates.len(), 2);
196:     }
197: 
198:     #[test]
199:     fn loop_gate_is_inside_both_entrance_orientations() {
200:         let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
201:         for entrance_z in [0.0, 8.0] {
202:             let room = plan_red_rooms(
203:                 42,
204:                 Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
205:                 &[red_assembly(entrance_z)],
206:                 &config,
207:             )
208:             .pop()
209:             .unwrap();
210:             let loop_gate = room
211:                 .gates
212:                 .iter()
213:                 .find(|gate| gate.kind == TraversalGateKind::RedLoop)
214:                 .unwrap();
215:             let bounds = room.footprint.bounds();
216:             assert!(loop_gate.plane >= bounds.min_z + SNAP - f32::EPSILON);
217:             assert!(loop_gate.plane <= bounds.max_z - SNAP + f32::EPSILON);
218:         }
219:     }
220: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/recursive_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Addressing for the Level 0 world reached through a committed Red Room.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room does not invent a second procedural grammar.  It addresses a
  4: //! distant, deterministic copy of Level 0 and changes its presentation.  The
  5: //! address must therefore be stable across chunk order and worker boundaries,
  6: //! while retaining all 64 bits of anomaly identity until hashing is complete.
  7: //! Converting an `AnomalyId` directly to `f32` loses most of those bits and can
  8: //! make distinct rooms share a world; this module derives integer region
  9: //! coordinates first and converts only the small final translation.
 10: 
 11: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
 12:     AnomalyId, AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, PitHazard, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase, TraversalGate,
 13:     WorldBounds,
 14: };
 15: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
 19: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
 20: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 21: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 22: 
 23: const ADDRESS_DOMAIN: u64 = 0x5245_4452_4F4F_4D00; // "REDROOM\0"
 24: // Keep translated coordinates near enough to the origin that f32 retains
 25: // sub-centimetre detail for future fine voxel requests. Branch uniqueness is
 26: // carried by the derived seed, so the translation itself need not be huge.
 27: const MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS: i64 = 64;
 28: const TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN: u64 = 192;
 29: 
 30: /// Stable procedural address of the recursive Level 0 associated with one
 31: /// Red Room instance.
 32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
 33: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelAddress {
 34:     instance_id: AnomalyId,
 35:     derived_seed: u32,
 36:     translation_regions: (i64, i64),
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// The finite planning window needed to render one request into a recursive
 40: /// Level 0 branch.  The branch remains infinite; this value is only its local
 41: /// query cache, just like an ordinary chunk's region window.
 42: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelWindow {
 43:     address: RecursiveLevelAddress,
 44:     seed: u32,
 45:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 46:     regions: InfiniteRegionWindow,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: impl RecursiveLevelWindow {
 50:     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 51:         source_origin: Position,
 52:         chunk_size: f32,
 53:         halo: f32,
 54:         world_seed: u32,
 55:         base_config: GeneratorConfig,
 56:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 57:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 58:     ) -> Option<Self> {
 59:         let (address, _) = RecursiveLevelAddress::from_reality(world_seed, reality)?;
 60:         let seed = address.derived_seed();
 61:         let config = address.recursive_config(base_config);
 62:         let recursive_origin = address.to_recursive_world(source_origin);
 63:         let regions = InfiniteRegionWindow::around_chunk(
 64:             recursive_origin,
 65:             chunk_size,
 66:             halo,
 67:             seed,
 68:             &config,
 69:             noise,
 70:         );
 71:         Some(Self {
 72:             address,
 73:             seed,
 74:             config,
 75:             regions,
 76:         })
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     pub(crate) fn seed(&self) -> u32 {
 80:         self.seed
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     pub(crate) fn instance_id(&self) -> AnomalyId {
 84:         self.address.instance_id
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     pub(crate) fn config(&self) -> &GeneratorConfig {
 88:         &self.config
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /// Returns both the recursive coordinate and the plan that owns it.
 92:     /// Keeping them paired prevents the old failure where a recursive plan
 93:     /// was sampled with the base world's seed and coordinates.
 94:     pub(crate) fn plan_at(&self, source: Position) -> Option<(Position, &RegionPlan)> {
 95:         let recursive = self.address.to_recursive_world(source);
 96:         self.regions
 97:             .plan_at(recursive)
 98:             .map(|plan| (recursive, plan))
 99:     }
100: 
101:     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
102:         self.regions.iter()
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// Project a semantic gate authored in the recursive branch back into
106:     /// the player's visible coordinate frame.
107:     pub(crate) fn project_gate(&self, mut gate: TraversalGate) -> TraversalGate {
108:         let offset = self.address.translation_world();
109:         match gate.axis {
110:             Axis2::X => {
111:                 gate.plane -= offset.x;
112:                 gate.span_min -= offset.z;
113:                 gate.span_max -= offset.z;
114:             }
115:             Axis2::Z => {
116:                 gate.plane -= offset.z;
117:                 gate.span_min -= offset.x;
118:                 gate.span_max -= offset.x;
119:             }
120:         }
121:         gate.affected_bounds = self.project_bounds(gate.affected_bounds);
122:         gate
123:     }
124: 
125:     pub(crate) fn project_hazard(&self, mut hazard: PitHazard) -> PitHazard {
126:         hazard.center = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.center);
127:         hazard.recovery = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.recovery);
128:         hazard
129:     }
130: 
131:     pub(crate) fn project_position(&self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
132:         self.address.to_source_world(recursive)
133:     }
134: 
135:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
136:         let min = self
137:             .address
138:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
139:         let max = self
140:             .address
141:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
142:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
143:     }
144: 
145:     fn project_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
146:         let min = self
147:             .address
148:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
149:         let max = self
150:             .address
151:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
152:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
153:     }
154: }
155: 
156: impl RecursiveLevelAddress {
157:     /// Derives an address using integer avalanche hashes only.  Both halves of
158:     /// the 64-bit instance id participate in the seed and in each axis.
159:     pub(crate) fn derive(world_seed: u32, instance_id: AnomalyId) -> Self {
160:         let root = mix64(
161:             ADDRESS_DOMAIN ^ instance_id ^ (world_seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15),
162:         );
163:         let seed_hash = mix64(root ^ 0x5EED_5EED_A11C_0DE5);
164:         let derived_seed = (seed_hash as u32) ^ ((seed_hash >> 32) as u32);
165:         let translation_regions = (
166:             translation_component(root, 0x5841_5849_5300_0001),
167:             translation_component(root, 0x5A41_5849_5300_0002),
168:         );
169: 
170:         Self {
171:             instance_id,
172:             derived_seed,
173:             translation_regions,
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// Selects the committed Red Room represented by a canonical reality
178:     /// snapshot, then derives its recursive address.
179:     pub(crate) fn from_reality(
180:         world_seed: u32,
181:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
182:     ) -> Option<(Self, &AnomalyStateStamp)> {
183:         let state = active_red_room(reality)?;
184:         Some((Self::derive(world_seed, state.instance_id), state))
185:     }
186: 
187:     pub(crate) fn derived_seed(self) -> u32 {
188:         self.derived_seed
189:     }
190: 
191:     pub(crate) fn translation_regions(self) -> (i64, i64) {
192:         self.translation_regions
193:     }
194: 
195:     /// Exact transform for region keys.  Planning should prefer this form so
196:     /// large-world floating-point precision never participates in identity.
197:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_region(self, source_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
198:         (
199:             source_region.0.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.0),
200:             source_region.1.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.1),
201:         )
202:     }
203: 
204:     pub(crate) fn to_source_region(self, recursive_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
205:         (
206:             recursive_region
207:                 .0
208:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.0),
209:             recursive_region
210:                 .1
211:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.1),
212:         )
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// World-space form used by column sampling.  The translation is an exact
216:     /// multiple of the 80u region lattice, preserving portals and 0.4u plan
217:     /// geometry across every chunk and LOD.
218:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_world(self, source: Position) -> Position {
219:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(source);
220:         let recursive = self.to_recursive_region(region);
221:         join_world_position(recursive, local)
222:     }
223: 
224:     pub(crate) fn to_source_world(self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
225:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(recursive);
226:         let source = self.to_source_region(region);
227:         join_world_position(source, local)
228:     }
229: 
230:     pub(crate) fn translation_world(self) -> Position {
231:         let translation = self.translation_regions();
232:         Position::new(
233:             translation.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
234:             translation.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
235:         )
236:     }
237: 
238:     /// Produces a Level 0 config for the addressed world.  Organic anomaly
239:     /// tuning is preserved, allowing recursive Level 0 to remain the complete
240:     /// generator; only the one-shot debug override is cleared so it cannot be
241:     /// cloned into every recursive address.
242:     pub(crate) fn recursive_config(self, mut base: GeneratorConfig) -> GeneratorConfig {
243:         base.level = LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
244:         base.anomalies.forced_kind = None;
245:         base
246:     }
247: }
248: 
249: /// Chooses one committed Red Room without depending on snapshot insertion
250: /// order.  Under the current state machine, only red thresholds can produce a
251: /// non-`Outside` phase.  Progress is compared explicitly because `epoch` is
252: /// the best available recency signal; stable identity is the final tie-break.
253: pub(crate) fn active_red_room(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Option<&AnomalyStateStamp> {
254:     reality
255:         .stamps()
256:         .iter()
257:         .filter(|state| state.phase != RedRoomPhase::Outside)
258:         .max_by_key(|state| {
259:             (
260:                 state.epoch,
261:                 state.phase,
262:                 state.loop_count,
263:                 state.last_gate_id,
264:                 state.instance_id,
265:             )
266:         })
267: }
268: 
269: fn translation_component(root: u64, axis_domain: u64) -> i64 {
270:     let hash = mix64(root ^ axis_domain);
271:     let magnitude = MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS + (hash % TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN) as i64;
272:     if hash & (1 << 63) == 0 {
273:         magnitude
274:     } else {
275:         -magnitude
276:     }
277: }
278: 
279: fn split_world_position(position: Position) -> ((i64, i64), (f32, f32)) {
280:     let region = (
281:         (position.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
282:         (position.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
283:     );
284:     let local = (
285:         position.x - region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
286:         position.z - region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
287:     );
288:     (region, local)
289: }
290: 
291: fn join_world_position(region: (i64, i64), local: (f32, f32)) -> Position {
292:     Position::new(
293:         region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.0,
294:         region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.1,
295:     )
296: }
297: 
298: fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
299:     value ^= value >> 30;
300:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
301:     value ^= value >> 27;
302:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
303:     value ^ (value >> 31)
304: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/circulation.rs
````rust
  1: //! Circulation routing: one dominant cross-region spine plus rare branches.
  2: //!
  3: //! The main spine always runs west portal -> east portal, so circulation
  4: //! chains across regions forever; branches are optional and never form a
  5: //! competing street grid.
  6: 
  7: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  8: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  9: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
 10: 
 11: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap, snap_width, v_edge_portal_z};
 12: 
 13: /// Z coordinate of the main spine where it passes world x (assumes the spine
 14: /// is a west-to-east Manhattan path).
 15: fn spine_z_at(path: &[Position], x: f32) -> f32 {
 16:     for seg in path.windows(2) {
 17:         let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 18:         if a.z == b.z && (x >= a.x.min(b.x)) && (x <= a.x.max(b.x)) {
 19:             return a.z;
 20:         }
 21:     }
 22:     path[0].z
 23: }
 24: 
 25: pub(super) fn build_corridors(
 26:     seed: u32,
 27:     rx: i64,
 28:     rz: i64,
 29:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 30:     origin: Position,
 31:     size: f32,
 32: ) -> Vec<CirculationSpine> {
 33:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0 + k, rx, rz]);
 34:     let (x0, x1) = (origin.x, origin.x + size);
 35:     let (z0, z1) = (origin.z, origin.z + size);
 36:     let west_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx, rz);
 37:     let east_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx + 1, rz);
 38:     // The primary route is deliberately too broad for an ordinary office
 39:     // corridor. It carries the infinite cross-region continuity; anything
 40:     // else is an optional branch, never a competing street grid.
 41:     let main_w = snap_width(4.8 + 2.4 * h(1));
 42:     let sec_w = snap_width(3.6 + 1.4 * hash01(seed, &[0xC1, rx, rz]));
 43: 
 44:     let mut spines = Vec::new();
 45:     let mut id = 0u32;
 46:     let mut push = |kind: SpaceProgram, path: Vec<Position>, width: f32, id: &mut u32| {
 47:         spines_push(&mut spines, kind, path, width, id);
 48:     };
 49: 
 50:     // Main spine: west portal -> east portal, always. Its Manhattan bend
 51:     // position is the designer's one free choice.
 52:     let bend_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.35 + 0.30 * h(2)));
 53:     let main_path: Vec<Position> = match genome.circulation {
 54:         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine => {
 55:             let mid_z = snap(z0 + size * (0.30 + 0.40 * h(3)));
 56:             let bend2_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.60 + 0.25 * h(4)));
 57:             vec![
 58:                 Position::new(x0, west_z),
 59:                 Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
 60:                 Position::new(bend_x, mid_z),
 61:                 Position::new(bend2_x, mid_z),
 62:                 Position::new(bend2_x, east_z),
 63:                 Position::new(x1, east_z),
 64:             ]
 65:         }
 66:         _ => vec![
 67:             Position::new(x0, west_z),
 68:             Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
 69:             Position::new(bend_x, east_z),
 70:             Position::new(x1, east_z),
 71:         ],
 72:     };
 73:     let main_z_at = main_path.clone();
 74:     push(SpaceProgram::MainCorridor, main_path, main_w, &mut id);
 75: 
 76:     // Secondary routes are branches, not a second regional grid: roughly a
 77:     // quarter of regions have none, most have one, and a few have two. The
 78:     // former ring and north/south through-route are intentionally absent.
 79:     let branch_count = match genome.circulation {
 80:         CirculationStyle::StraightSpine if h(11) < 0.45 => 0,
 81:         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine if h(11) < 0.20 => 0,
 82:         _ if h(11) < 0.28 => 0,
 83:         _ if h(11) < 0.82 => 1,
 84:         _ => 2,
 85:     };
 86:     for k in 0..branch_count {
 87:         let sx = snap(x0 + size * (0.18 + 0.64 * h(12 + k)));
 88:         let sz = spine_z_at(&main_z_at, sx);
 89:         let len = snap(12.0 + 14.0 * h(22 + k));
 90:         let dir = if h(32 + k) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
 91:         let end = (sz + dir * len).clamp(z0 + EDGE_MARGIN, z1 - EDGE_MARGIN);
 92:         if (end - sz).abs() >= 8.0 {
 93:             push(
 94:                 SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall,
 95:                 vec![Position::new(sx, sz), Position::new(sx, snap(end))],
 96:                 sec_w,
 97:                 &mut id,
 98:             );
 99:         }
100:     }
101:     spines
102: }
103: 
104: fn spines_push(
105:     spines: &mut Vec<CirculationSpine>,
106:     kind: SpaceProgram,
107:     path: Vec<Position>,
108:     width: f32,
109:     id: &mut u32,
110: ) {
111:     spines.push(CirculationSpine {
112:         id: *id,
113:         spine_kind: kind,
114:         path,
115:         width,
116:     });
117:     *id += 1;
118: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/corruption.rs
````rust
  1: //! The Backrooms corruption pass: the plan was sane; the building is not.
  2: //!
  3: //! Duplicated suites, abandoned expansions, renovation overlays, and the
  4: //! realization of macro-graph red-room events on eligible assemblies.
  5: 
  6: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
  7: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  8: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  9: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 10: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 11: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
 12: 
 13: use super::suites::{aabb_overlap, place_suite};
 14: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, PLAN_WALL_T, REGION_SIZE, pick_index, region_index, snap, spawn_point};
 15: 
 16: /// Backrooms corruption: the plan was sane; the building is not.
 17: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 18: pub(super) fn corrupt(
 19:     seed: u32,
 20:     rx: i64,
 21:     rz: i64,
 22:     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
 23:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 24:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 25:     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
 26:     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
 27:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 28: ) {
 29:     if assemblies.is_empty() {
 30:         return;
 31:     }
 32:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0DE + k, rx, rz]);
 33: 
 34:     // 1. A suite repeats itself further down the corridor, slightly wrong.
 35:     if h(1) < 0.6 {
 36:         let src = pick_index(h(2), assemblies.len());
 37:         let shift = snap(12.0 + 12.0 * h(3));
 38:         // Keep the copied threshold flush with its source corridor. The
 39:         // repetition is wrong in its longitudinal position, not sealed away
 40:         // behind an accidental strip of wall.
 41:         let skew = 0.0;
 42:         let mut dup = assemblies[src].clone();
 43:         let translate = |poly: &mut Polygon2| {
 44:             for v in &mut poly.vertices {
 45:                 v.0 += shift;
 46:                 v.1 += skew;
 47:             }
 48:         };
 49:         translate(&mut dup.footprint);
 50:         for s in &mut dup.spaces {
 51:             translate(&mut s.footprint);
 52:         }
 53:         for c in &mut dup.ceiling_zones {
 54:             translate(&mut c.area);
 55:         }
 56:         for f in &mut dup.fixtures {
 57:             f.at.x += shift;
 58:             f.at.z += skew;
 59:         }
 60:         for e in &mut dup.entrances {
 61:             e.center.x += shift;
 62:             e.center.z += skew;
 63:         }
 64:         dup.id = assemblies.len() as u32 + 1000;
 65:         dup.corruption.misalignment = (shift, skew);
 66:         let b = dup.footprint.bounds();
 67:         let inside = b.0 > rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
 68:             && b.2 < (rx + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN
 69:             && b.1 > rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
 70:             && b.3 < (rz + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN;
 71:         // The skewed entrance must still reach a corridor, or the copy would
 72:         // be a sealed pocket.
 73:         let reachable = dup.entrances.iter().any(|e| {
 74:             spines
 75:                 .iter()
 76:                 .any(|s| s.distance(e.center.x, e.center.z) <= s.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05)
 77:         });
 78:         if inside && reachable && !taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.4)) {
 79:             taken.push(b);
 80:             assemblies.push(dup);
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     // 2. One assembly was built and then never occupied.
 85:     if h(6) < 0.6 {
 86:         let k = pick_index(h(7), assemblies.len());
 87:         let a = &mut assemblies[k];
 88:         a.program = SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion;
 89:         a.corruption.abandoned = true;
 90:         a.spaces.clear(); // an empty shell
 91:         for f in &mut a.fixtures {
 92:             f.lit = false;
 93:         }
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     // 3. A renovation overlays the original structural grid.
 97:     if dominant.renovation_history != RenovationStyle::Untouched {
 98:         let k = pick_index(h(8), assemblies.len());
 99:         assemblies[k].corruption.renovation_overlay = true;
100:     }
101: 
102:     // 4. Rarely, one occupied room's fixtures all burn red. The lighting is
103:     // the anomaly, and it belongs to a whole architectural space — never a
104:     // lone fixture, never red masonry. Applied last so it respects whatever
105:     // the earlier corruption passes decided (an abandoned shell stays dark).
106:     //
107:     // Where a red room happens is a *graph event*, not a per-region coin
108:     // flip: the macro topology plans separated events on its lattice (see
109:     // `world_topology::red_room_event_for_region`), and this pass merely
110:     // realizes an event that targets this region on one eligible assembly.
111:     let red_room_scale = config.anomalies.frequency * config.anomalies.red_rooms;
112:     let mut red_room_forced = false;
113:     let sp = spawn_point(seed);
114:     if config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom)
115:         && rx == region_index(sp.x)
116:         && rz == region_index(sp.z)
117:     {
118:         if let Some(a) = assemblies
119:             .iter_mut()
120:             .find(|a| !a.entrances.is_empty() && !a.corruption.abandoned)
121:         {
122:             a.corruption.red_room = true;
123:             red_room_forced = true;
124:         } else if let Some(spine) = spines
125:             .iter()
126:             .find(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
127:         {
128:             if let Some(seg) = spine.path.windows(2).find(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z) {
129:                 let lx0 = seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x);
130:                 let lz = seg[0].z;
131:                 let origin = Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE);
132:                 if let Some(mut a) = place_suite(
133:                     9999,
134:                     SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
135:                     dominant,
136:                     0.5,
137:                     0.5,
138:                     lx0 + 12.0,
139:                     lz,
140:                     spine.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T,
141:                     1.0,
142:                     origin,
143:                     REGION_SIZE,
144:                     taken,
145:                     spines,
146:                 ) {
147:                     a.corruption.red_room = true;
148:                     taken.push(a.footprint.bounds());
149:                     assemblies.push(a);
150:                     red_room_forced = true;
151:                 }
152:             }
153:         }
154:     }
155: 
156:     if !red_room_forced
157:         && let Some(event) = crate::use_cases::world_topology::red_room_event_for_region(
158:             seed,
159:             noise,
160:             rx,
161:             rz,
162:             red_room_scale.clamp(0.0, 4.0),
163:         )
164:     {
165:         // Realize the event on one occupied, reachable assembly, rotating
166:         // from a stable start so the choice replays for every query of this
167:         // region. If no assembly qualifies the event stays unrealized — a
168:         // planned encounter never overwrites navigable circulation.
169:         let count = assemblies.len();
170:         let start = (event.id % count as u64) as usize;
171:         for offset in 0..count {
172:             let a = &mut assemblies[(start + offset) % count];
173:             if !a.corruption.abandoned && !a.entrances.is_empty() {
174:                 a.corruption.red_room = true;
175:                 break;
176:             }
177:         }
178:     }
179: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/debug.rs
````rust
 1: //! Debug hook: ASCII plan view of one region.
 2: 
 3: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 4: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 5: 
 6: /// ASCII plan view at `step` world units per character. Corridors `=`, macro
 7: /// anomalies `P/B/H` (pillar/blackout/pits), red loops `R`, assembly interiors
 8: /// by program initial, entrances `+`, empty fabric `.`.
 9: pub fn debug_region_ascii(plan: &RegionPlan, step: f32) -> String {
10:     let n = (plan.size_world / step) as usize;
11:     let mut out = String::with_capacity((n + 1) * n);
12:     for iz in 0..n {
13:         for ix in 0..n {
14:             let x = plan.origin_world.x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * step;
15:             let z = plan.origin_world.z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * step;
16:             let mut ch = '.';
17:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
18:                 if a.footprint.contains(x, z) {
19:                     ch = match a.program {
20:                         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 'o',
21:                         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 'p',
22:                         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 'c',
23:                         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 'b',
24:                         SpaceProgram::Storage => 's',
25:                         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 'v',
26:                         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 'w',
27:                         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => 'x',
28:                         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 'A',
29:                         SpaceProgram::Stair => 'S',
30:                         _ => 'r',
31:                     };
32:                 }
33:             }
34:             for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
35:                 if anomaly.contains(x, z) {
36:                     ch = match anomaly.kind {
37:                         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => 'P',
38:                         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => 'B',
39:                         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => 'H',
40:                         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => 'R',
41:                         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => 'M',
42:                     };
43:                 }
44:             }
45:             for s in &plan.corridors {
46:                 if s.distance(x, z) <= s.width * 0.5 {
47:                     ch = '=';
48:                 }
49:             }
50:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
51:                 for e in &a.entrances {
52:                     if (x - e.center.x).abs() < e.width * 0.5 && (z - e.center.z).abs() < step {
53:                         ch = '+';
54:                     }
55:                 }
56:             }
57:             out.push(ch);
58:         }
59:         out.push('\n');
60:     }
61:     out
62: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/genome.rs
````rust
 1: //! Architect genomes: the designers a region inherits.
 2: //!
 3: //! `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator, 2 = intruder. The circulation style
 4: //! comes from low-frequency noise so neighboring regions tend to share a
 5: //! culture; everything else hashes.
 6: 
 7: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 8: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 9: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
10: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
11: 
12: use super::{REGION_SIZE, pick_index};
13: 
14: /// Derive one designer for a region. `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator,
15: /// 2 = intruder. The circulation style comes from low-frequency noise so
16: /// neighboring regions tend to share a culture; everything else hashes.
17: pub fn derive_genome(
18:     seed: u32,
19:     rx: i64,
20:     rz: i64,
21:     salt: i64,
22:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
23: ) -> ArchitectGenome {
24:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0x6E0 + salt, rx, rz, k]);
25:     // ~130 u wavelength: cultures span a few regions.
26:     let culture = noise.evaluate_2d(
27:         seed ^ 0xA11C_0DE ^ (salt as u32),
28:         Position::new(
29:             (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
30:             (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
31:         ),
32:     );
33:     let circulation = match ((culture * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999) * 4.0) as u32 {
34:         0 => CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
35:         1 => CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine,
36:         2 => CirculationStyle::PairedBranches,
37:         _ => CirculationStyle::TreeWithCulDeSacs,
38:     };
39:     let structural_system = *[
40:         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
41:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams,
42:         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid,
43:         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
44:     ]
45:     .get(pick_index(h(1), 4))
46:     .unwrap();
47:     // A framed office door is now an anomaly. The chosen language is only a
48:     // bias; each assembly still picks its own threshold so a whole region
49:     // never turns into a row of identical openings.
50:     let threshold_language = match h(2) {
51:         v if v < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
52:         v if v < 0.55 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
53:         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
54:     };
55:     let ceiling_language = *[
56:         CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
57:         CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
58:         CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
59:     ]
60:     .get(pick_index(h(3), 3))
61:     .unwrap();
62:     let lighting_language = *[
63:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
64:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
65:         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation,
66:         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants,
67:     ]
68:     .get(pick_index(h(4), 4))
69:     .unwrap();
70:     let renovation_history = *[
71:         RenovationStyle::Untouched,
72:         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit,
73:         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits,
74:     ]
75:     .get(pick_index(h(5), 3))
76:     .unwrap();
77:     ArchitectGenome {
78:         circulation,
79:         structural_system,
80:         room_proportions: ProportionRules {
81:             // Level 0 reads as broken retail-backroom masses, not a cubicle
82:             // tiling. A suite frontage normally survives 12--24 u before a
83:             // meaningful interruption.
84:             min_side: 12.0 + 4.0 * h(6),
85:             max_side: 20.0 + 8.0 * h(7),
86:             elongation: h(8),
87:         },
88:         threshold_language,
89:         ceiling_language,
90:         lighting_language,
91:         furnishing_density: 0.3 + 0.7 * h(9),
92:         renovation_history,
93:         tolerance_for_symmetry: h(10),
94:     }
95: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/mod.rs
````rust
  1: //! Region-scale architectural planning for Backrooms Level 0.
  2: //!
  3: //! The world is tiled by fixed 80 u square regions on a world-space lattice.
  4: //! [`generate_region_plan`] is a *pure* function of `(seed, region)`: it
  5: //! derives the region's designers ([`ArchitectGenome`]), routes a dominant
  6: //! circulation spine first (between edge portals shared with the neighboring
  7: //! regions), attaches incomplete program masses ([`AssemblyInstance`]) beside
  8: //! that circulation,
  9: //! gives them structure / ceilings / fixtures, and finally applies a
 10: //! Backrooms corruption pass (duplicated suites, abandoned expansions,
 11: //! renovation overlays).
 12: //!
 13: //! Cross-region continuity: a corridor leaves a region only at a *portal* on
 14: //! a shared edge, and the portal position is derived from the *edge's*
 15: //! lattice coordinate — both neighbors compute the identical portal, so
 16: //! corridors chain across regions forever (a main corridor that never ends
 17: //! is the first and cheapest corruption).
 18: //!
 19: //! All coordinates are snapped to a 0.4 u lattice — the coarsest voxel size —
 20: //! so plan geometry lands identically at every LOD.
 21: 
 22: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 23: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 24: use crate::use_cases::anomaly_plan::plan_anomalies_for_region;
 25: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 26: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 27: 
 28: /// Side of a region, world units. A multiple of both chunk sizes (10/20).
 29: pub const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
 30: /// Plan wall thickness: one coarse voxel, so walls survive every LOD.
 31: pub const PLAN_WALL_T: f32 = 0.4;
 32: /// Snap lattice for all plan geometry (= coarsest voxel size).
 33: const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
 34: /// Keep-out margin from region edges for assembly footprints.
 35: const EDGE_MARGIN: f32 = 3.2;
 36: 
 37: /// Region lattice index of a world coordinate.
 38: pub fn region_index(w: f32) -> i64 {
 39:     (w / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64
 40: }
 41: 
 42: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 43:     (v / SNAP).round() * SNAP
 44: }
 45: 
 46: /// Corridor widths snap to 0.8 so *half*-widths stay on the 0.4 lattice and
 47: /// suite front walls land flush against corridor edges.
 48: fn snap_width(v: f32) -> f32 {
 49:     ((v / (2.0 * SNAP)).round() * 2.0 * SNAP).max(2.0 * SNAP)
 50: }
 51: 
 52: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 53: // Deterministic hashing and edge portals.
 54: //
 55: // All "randomness" flows through `world_topology::hash01`, and the portal a
 56: // corridor uses to cross a region border is the macro graph's portal — one
 57: // derivation shared by both neighbors of the edge and by the topology layer.
 58: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 59: 
 60: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::{hash01, primary_portal_z as v_edge_portal_z};
 61: 
 62: fn pick_index(h: f32, len: usize) -> usize {
 63:     ((h * len as f32) as usize).min(len - 1)
 64: }
 65: 
 66: /// World spawn: a point *on the main corridor centerline* of region (0, 0),
 67: /// a few units east of its west portal. The first thing the player sees is
 68: /// therefore the region's dominant circulation route — walls running away in
 69: /// both directions — rather than unplanned fabric. Both the generator core
 70: /// and the browser composition root derive spawn from this single function,
 71: /// so the player and the voxelizer can never disagree about where "here" is.
 72: pub fn spawn_point(seed: u32) -> Position {
 73:     // The main spine's west leg always runs from (0, west_z) to at least
 74:     // x = 0.35 * REGION_SIZE, so a few units in we are guaranteed to stand
 75:     // on a straight, readable stretch of corridor.
 76:     Position::new(6.0, v_edge_portal_z(seed, 0, 0))
 77: }
 78: 
 79: 
 80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 81: // The planning stages, one intent per module.
 82: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 83: 
 84: mod circulation;
 85: mod corruption;
 86: mod debug;
 87: mod genome;
 88: mod suites;
 89: #[cfg(test)]
 90: mod tests;
 91: 
 92: pub use debug::debug_region_ascii;
 93: pub use genome::derive_genome;
 94: 
 95: use circulation::build_corridors;
 96: use corruption::corrupt;
 97: use suites::{SUITE_PROGRAMS, place_suite};
 98: 
 99: /// Pure, deterministic plan for the region whose lower-left corner is
100: /// `region_origin` (must lie on the region lattice).
101: pub fn generate_region_plan(
102:     seed: u32,
103:     region_origin: Position,
104:     region_size: f32,
105:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
106:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
107: ) -> RegionPlan {
108:     let rx = region_index(region_origin.x + 0.1);
109:     let rz = region_index(region_origin.z + 0.1);
110:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xA0 + k, rx, rz]);
111: 
112:     let dominant = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 0, noise);
113:     let renovator = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 1, noise);
114:     let mut architects = vec![dominant.clone(), renovator];
115:     // A third designer intrudes where the style-blend field runs high: the
116:     // macro fields decide *where* cultures leak into each other; the hash
117:     // only decides whether this particular region exposes the seam.
118:     let fields = crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields(
119:         noise,
120:         seed,
121:         (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
122:         (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
123:     );
124:     if h(0) < 0.10 + 0.55 * fields.style_blend {
125:         architects.push(derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 2, noise));
126:     }
127: 
128:     let corridors = build_corridors(seed, rx, rz, &dominant, region_origin, region_size);
129: 
130:     // --- incomplete masses beside the dominant route -----------------------
131:     // Only the primary route receives masses. The secondary stubs remain
132:     // mostly exposed circulation, which prevents a region from resolving
133:     // into a tiled office floorplan.
134:     let mut assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
135:     let mut taken: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = Vec::new();
136:     let mut id = 0u32;
137:     let legs: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = corridors
138:         .iter()
139:         .filter(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
140:         .flat_map(|s| {
141:             let w = s.width;
142:             s.path
143:                 .windows(2)
144:                 .filter(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z)
145:                 .map(move |seg| (seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x), seg[0].x.max(seg[1].x), seg[0].z, w))
146:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
147:         })
148:         .filter(|(a, b, _, _)| b - a >= 14.0)
149:         .collect();
150: 
151:     for (li, &(lx0, lx1, lz, lw)) in legs.iter().enumerate() {
152:         let mut cursor = lx0 + 4.0;
153:         let mut side = if h(40 + li as i64) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
154:         while cursor < lx1 - 12.0 {
155:             let aseed = hash01(seed, &[0x5EA, rx, rz, id as i64]);
156:             let threshold_seed = hash01(seed, &[0x7A11, rx, rz, id as i64]);
157:             // Leave substantial pieces of the route exposed. When a mass is
158:             // placed, the next candidate begins 8--16 u beyond its end.
159:             if hash01(seed, &[0x5E8, rx, rz, id as i64]) < 0.62 {
160:                 let program = SUITE_PROGRAMS[pick_index(aseed, SUITE_PROGRAMS.len())];
161:                 if let Some(a) = place_suite(
162:                     id,
163:                     program,
164:                     &dominant,
165:                     aseed,
166:                     threshold_seed,
167:                     cursor,
168:                     lz,
169:                     lw * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T,
170:                     side,
171:                     region_origin,
172:                     region_size,
173:                     &taken,
174:                     &corridors,
175:                 ) {
176:                     let b = a.footprint.bounds();
177:                     cursor += (b.2 - b.0) + 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
178:                     taken.push(b);
179:                     assemblies.push(a);
180:                 } else {
181:                     cursor += 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
182:                 }
183:             } else {
184:                 cursor += 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
185:             }
186:             side = -side;
187:             id += 1;
188:         }
189:     }
190: 
191:     // --- corruption pass ----------------------------------------------------
192:     corrupt(
193:         seed,
194:         rx,
195:         rz,
196:         &dominant,
197:         config,
198:         noise,
199:         &mut assemblies,
200:         &mut taken,
201:         &corridors,
202:     );
203: 
204:     // --- vertical circulation ------------------------------------------------
205:     // The macro graph may have reserved a stairwell here. Upward links are
206:     // realized as a Stair assembly beside the main spine; downward links
207:     // stay graph reservations until the engine streams below elevation 0.
208:     // Placed after corruption so no pass can duplicate, abandon, or redden
209:     // a stair core.
210:     if let Some(link) =
211:         crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, rx, rz)
212:         && crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry(&link)
213:         && let Some(stair) = crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::place_stairwell(
214:             id + 2000,
215:             &link,
216:             &legs,
217:             region_origin,
218:             region_size,
219:             EDGE_MARGIN,
220:             PLAN_WALL_T,
221:             &taken,
222:             |cx, cz, clearance| {
223:                 corridors
224:                     .iter()
225:                     .all(|s| s.distance(cx, cz) >= s.width * 0.5 + clearance)
226:             },
227:         )
228:     {
229:         taken.push(stair.footprint.bounds());
230:         assemblies.push(stair);
231:     }
232: 
233:     // Macro anomalies are derived after ordinary architecture so compact red
234:     // rooms can promote a real assembly, while region-spanning families keep
235:     // stable world-lattice identities independent of this region query.
236:     let anomalies = plan_anomalies_for_region(
237:         seed,
238:         region_origin,
239:         region_size,
240:         &assemblies,
241:         spawn_point(seed),
242:         config,
243:         noise,
244:     );
245: 
246:     RegionPlan {
247:         origin_world: region_origin,
248:         size_world: region_size,
249:         architects,
250:         assemblies,
251:         corridors,
252:         anomalies,
253:     }
254: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/suites.rs
````rust
  1: //! Program masses beside the dominant route: suite placement, structure,
  2: //! ceilings, fixtures, and sparse interior partitioning.
  3: 
  4: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  5: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  6: 
  7: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap};
  8: 
  9: /// The suite program palette placed beside main corridors, roughly weighted.
 10: /// Large, unfinished open-office masses dominate. Small private rooms remain
 11: /// present only as occasional evidence that this once had an office program.
 12: pub(super) const SUITE_PROGRAMS: [SpaceProgram; 12] = [
 13:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 14:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 15:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 16:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 17:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 18:     SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom,
 19:     SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom,
 20:     SpaceProgram::BreakRoom,
 21:     SpaceProgram::Storage,
 22:     SpaceProgram::ServerRoom,
 23:     SpaceProgram::WaitingArea,
 24:     SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
 25: ];
 26: 
 27: fn ceiling_height_for(program: SpaceProgram, aseed: f32) -> f32 {
 28:     match program {
 29:         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 4.8 + 0.6 * aseed,
 30:         // Compression is a deliberate contrast, never the default ceiling.
 31:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom | SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 2.6 + 0.2 * aseed,
 32:         SpaceProgram::Storage | SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 3.0 + 0.3 * aseed,
 33:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 3.5 + 0.7 * aseed,
 34:         _ => 3.2 + 0.5 * aseed,
 35:     }
 36: }
 37: 
 38: fn structure_for(genome: &ArchitectGenome, aseed: f32) -> StructuralSystemInstance {
 39:     let bay = snap(4.4 + 1.6 * aseed);
 40:     let (bay_x, bay_z) = match genome.structural_system {
 41:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => (bay * 1.5, bay),
 42:         _ => (bay, bay),
 43:     };
 44:     StructuralSystemInstance {
 45:         system: genome.structural_system,
 46:         bay_x,
 47:         bay_z,
 48:         phase: (snap(aseed * 4.0), snap(aseed * 8.0 % 4.0)),
 49:         column_side: 0.4,
 50:     }
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Fixtures for a rectangular footprint in the genome's lighting language.
 54: fn fixtures_for(
 55:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 56:     footprint: &Polygon2,
 57:     lit: bool,
 58:     aseed: f32,
 59: ) -> Vec<Fixture> {
 60:     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
 61:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 62:     match genome.lighting_language {
 63:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels => {
 64:             let step = 2.4;
 65:             let mut z = z0 + 1.2;
 66:             while z < z1 - 0.8 {
 67:                 let mut x = x0 + 1.2;
 68:                 while x < x1 - 0.8 {
 69:                     out.push(Fixture {
 70:                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(z)),
 71:                         half_x: 0.4,
 72:                         half_z: 0.4,
 73:                         lit,
 74:                     });
 75:                     x += step;
 76:                 }
 77:                 z += step;
 78:             }
 79:         }
 80:         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation => {
 81:             // Strips run down the room's long axis.
 82:             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
 83:             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
 84:             let step = 3.2;
 85:             if long_x {
 86:                 let mut x = x0 + 1.6;
 87:                 while x < x1 - 1.2 {
 88:                     out.push(Fixture {
 89:                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(cz)),
 90:                         half_x: 1.0,
 91:                         half_z: 0.25,
 92:                         lit,
 93:                     });
 94:                     x += step;
 95:                 }
 96:             } else {
 97:                 let mut z = z0 + 1.6;
 98:                 while z < z1 - 1.2 {
 99:                     out.push(Fixture {
100:                         at: Position::new(snap(cx), snap(z)),
101:                         half_x: 0.25,
102:                         half_z: 1.0,
103:                         lit,
104:                     });
105:                     z += step;
106:                 }
107:             }
108:         }
109:         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants => {
110:             let n = 1 + (aseed * 2.0) as i32;
111:             for k in 0..n {
112:                 let fx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.618 + aseed) % 1.0));
113:                 let fz = z0 + (z1 - z0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.382 + aseed * 2.0) % 1.0));
114:                 out.push(Fixture {
115:                     at: Position::new(snap(fx), snap(fz)),
116:                     half_x: 0.3,
117:                     half_z: 0.3,
118:                     lit,
119:                 });
120:             }
121:         }
122:     }
123:     out
124: }
125: 
126: /// Interior partitioning is deliberately sparse. A private-office suite may
127: /// split once, producing one long interruption rather than a cell grid.
128: fn spaces_for(
129:     program: SpaceProgram,
130:     footprint: &Polygon2,
131:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
132:     aseed: f32,
133: ) -> Vec<Space> {
134:     if program != SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice {
135:         return Vec::new();
136:     }
137:     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
138:     let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
139:     let span = if long_x { x1 - x0 } else { z1 - z0 };
140:     let want = genome.room_proportions.min_side.max(12.0);
141:     let n = ((span / want) as usize).clamp(1, 2);
142:     let n = if aseed > 0.62 { n } else { 1 };
143:     if n <= 1 {
144:         return Vec::new();
145:     }
146:     let mut out = Vec::new();
147:     for k in 0..n {
148:         let (a, b) = (
149:             snap(k as f32 / n as f32 * span),
150:             snap((k + 1) as f32 / n as f32 * span),
151:         );
152:         let rect = if long_x {
153:             Polygon2::rect(x0 + a, z0, b - a, z1 - z0)
154:         } else {
155:             Polygon2::rect(x0, z0 + a, x1 - x0, b - a)
156:         };
157:         out.push(Space {
158:             program: SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
159:             footprint: rect,
160:         });
161:     }
162:     out
163: }
164: 
165: pub(super) fn aabb_overlap(a: (f32, f32, f32, f32), b: (f32, f32, f32, f32), gap: f32) -> bool {
166:     a.0 < b.2 + gap && b.0 < a.2 + gap && a.1 < b.3 + gap && b.1 < a.3 + gap
167: }
168: 
169: /// Places one suite beside a horizontal corridor segment. Returns `None` if
170: /// the footprint would leave the region, collide with a prior assembly, or
171: /// cross another corridor.
172: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
173: pub(super) fn place_suite(
174:     id: u32,
175:     program: SpaceProgram,
176:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
177:     aseed: f32,
178:     threshold_seed: f32,
179:     cursor_x: f32,
180:     corridor_z: f32,
181:     corridor_half: f32,
182:     side: f32, // +1 = suite on +Z side of corridor, -1 = -Z side
183:     origin: Position,
184:     size: f32,
185:     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
186:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
187: ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
188:     let p = &genome.room_proportions;
189:     let w = snap((p.min_side + (p.max_side - p.min_side) * aseed).clamp(12.0, 24.0));
190:     let d = snap((w * (0.72 - 0.28 * p.elongation)).clamp(8.0, 18.0));
191: 
192:     let x0 = snap(cursor_x);
193:     let z_front = snap(if side > 0.0 {
194:         corridor_z + corridor_half
195:     } else {
196:         corridor_z - corridor_half - d
197:     });
198:     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, w, d);
199:     let b = footprint.bounds();
200: 
201:     // Stay inside the region with margin.
202:     if b.0 < origin.x + EDGE_MARGIN
203:         || b.1 < origin.z + EDGE_MARGIN
204:         || b.2 > origin.x + size - EDGE_MARGIN
205:         || b.3 > origin.z + size - EDGE_MARGIN
206:     {
207:         return None;
208:     }
209:     if taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.8)) {
210:         return None;
211:     }
212:     // Don't let a suite swallow a *different* corridor (its front corridor
213:     // touching the footprint edge is fine and expected).
214:     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
215:     for s in spines {
216:         if s.distance(center.0, center.1) < s.width * 0.5 + d.min(w) * 0.25 {
217:             return None;
218:         }
219:     }
220: 
221:     // Entrance on the corridor-facing wall. The genome biases the language,
222:     // but a narrow framed door is only about 8--14% of thresholds globally.
223:     // Most fronts dissolve into a room through an unframed or broad portal.
224:     let threshold = match genome.threshold_language {
225:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.14 => {
226:             ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel
227:         }
228:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.08 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
229:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
230:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.62 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
231:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
232:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
233:         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
234:     };
235:     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
236:     let (width, lintel) = match threshold {
237:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel => (1.2, Some(2.2)),
238:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal => (4.8, None),
239:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal => (3.6, Some(3.0)),
240:     };
241:     let edge = width * 0.5 + 0.8;
242:     let door_x = snap((b.0 + w * (0.25 + 0.5 * threshold_seed)).clamp(b.0 + edge, b.2 - edge));
243:     let entrances = vec![Opening {
244:         center: Position::new(door_x, front_z),
245:         width,
246:         through_x_wall: true,
247:         lintel_units: lintel,
248:     }];
249: 
250:     let ceiling = CeilingZone {
251:         area: footprint.clone(),
252:         language: genome.ceiling_language,
253:         height_units: ceiling_height_for(program, aseed),
254:     };
255:     Some(AssemblyInstance {
256:         id,
257:         program,
258:         spaces: spaces_for(program, &footprint, genome, aseed),
259:         structure: structure_for(genome, aseed),
260:         ceiling_zones: vec![ceiling],
261:         fixtures: fixtures_for(genome, &footprint, true, aseed),
262:         service_voids: Vec::new(),
263:         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
264:         entrances,
265:         footprint,
266:     })
267: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Deterministic access to the finite window of an infinite planned level.
  2: //!
  3: //! Chunk generation is local, but Level 0 architecture is not: a chunk may
  4: //! sample corridors, assemblies, or anomaly footprints planned by any region
  5: //! that overlaps its voxel halo.  This module makes that query explicit.  The
  6: //! window owns a stable, row-major set of region plans and is otherwise just a
  7: //! world-point-to-plan lookup; callers do not need to reproduce region-range
  8: //! arithmetic or fall back to an unrelated plan when a lookup misses.
  9: 
 10: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
 11: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 12: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 15: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan, region_index};
 16: 
 17: /// The region plans needed to sample one bounded area of an infinite level.
 18: ///
 19: /// Plans are stored in `(z, x)` row-major order.  That order is deliberately
 20: /// independent of hash maps and request timing, so planning the same area is
 21: /// replayable on the main thread, in a worker, or during a test.
 22: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
 23: pub(crate) struct InfiniteRegionWindow {
 24:     min_region_x: i64,
 25:     min_region_z: i64,
 26:     max_region_x: i64,
 27:     max_region_z: i64,
 28:     plans: Vec<RegionPlan>,
 29: }
 30: 
 31: impl InfiniteRegionWindow {
 32:     /// Plans every region touched by `area` after expanding it by `halo` world
 33:     /// units.  Boundary-touching regions are included intentionally: a voxel
 34:     /// sampler may ask about the exact far edge while constructing skirts,
 35:     /// meshes, or collision data.
 36:     pub(crate) fn covering(
 37:         area: WorldBounds,
 38:         halo: f32,
 39:         seed: u32,
 40:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 41:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 42:     ) -> Self {
 43:         assert!(
 44:             halo.is_finite() && halo >= 0.0,
 45:             "region-window halo must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
 46:         );
 47:         let area = area.expanded(halo);
 48:         assert!(
 49:             [area.min_x, area.min_z, area.max_x, area.max_z]
 50:                 .into_iter()
 51:                 .all(f32::is_finite),
 52:             "an infinite-region window requires finite world bounds"
 53:         );
 54: 
 55:         let min_region_x = region_index(area.min_x);
 56:         let min_region_z = region_index(area.min_z);
 57:         let max_region_x = region_index(area.max_x);
 58:         let max_region_z = region_index(area.max_z);
 59:         let width = region_count(min_region_x, max_region_x);
 60:         let height = region_count(min_region_z, max_region_z);
 61:         let capacity = width
 62:             .checked_mul(height)
 63:             .expect("requested region window is too large to address");
 64:         let mut plans = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
 65: 
 66:         for region_z in min_region_z..=max_region_z {
 67:             for region_x in min_region_x..=max_region_x {
 68:                 plans.push(generate_region_plan(
 69:                     seed,
 70:                     region_origin(region_x, region_z),
 71:                     REGION_SIZE,
 72:                     config,
 73:                     noise,
 74:                 ));
 75:             }
 76:         }
 77: 
 78:         Self {
 79:             min_region_x,
 80:             min_region_z,
 81:             max_region_x,
 82:             max_region_z,
 83:             plans,
 84:         }
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     /// Convenience constructor for the common chunk-plus-voxel-halo query.
 88:     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 89:         chunk_origin: Position,
 90:         chunk_size: f32,
 91:         halo: f32,
 92:         seed: u32,
 93:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 94:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 95:     ) -> Self {
 96:         assert!(
 97:             chunk_size.is_finite() && chunk_size >= 0.0,
 98:             "chunk size must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
 99:         );
100:         Self::covering(
101:             WorldBounds::new(
102:                 chunk_origin.x,
103:                 chunk_origin.z,
104:                 chunk_origin.x + chunk_size,
105:                 chunk_origin.z + chunk_size,
106:             ),
107:             halo,
108:             seed,
109:             config,
110:             noise,
111:         )
112:     }
113: 
114:     /// Returns the authoritative plan for a world point, or `None` when the
115:     /// caller sampled beyond the area/halo declared at construction time.
116:     pub(crate) fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
117:         self.plan_for_region(region_index(world.x), region_index(world.z))
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub(crate) fn plan_for_region(&self, region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
121:         if region_x < self.min_region_x
122:             || region_x > self.max_region_x
123:             || region_z < self.min_region_z
124:             || region_z > self.max_region_z
125:         {
126:             return None;
127:         }
128: 
129:         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
130:         let local_x = usize::try_from(region_x - self.min_region_x).ok()?;
131:         let local_z = usize::try_from(region_z - self.min_region_z).ok()?;
132:         self.plans
133:             .get(local_z.saturating_mul(width).saturating_add(local_x))
134:     }
135: 
136:     #[cfg(test)]
137:     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
138:         self.plans.len()
139:     }
140: 
141:     #[cfg(test)]
142:     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
143:         self.plans.is_empty()
144:     }
145: 
146:     /// Stable row-major iteration for semantic export and deterministic tests.
147:     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
148:         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
149:         self.plans.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, plan)| {
150:             let local_z = index / width;
151:             let local_x = index % width;
152:             (
153:                 (
154:                     self.min_region_x + local_x as i64,
155:                     self.min_region_z + local_z as i64,
156:                 ),
157:                 plan,
158:             )
159:         })
160:     }
161: }
162: 
163: fn region_count(first: i64, last: i64) -> usize {
164:     let count = last
165:         .checked_sub(first)
166:         .and_then(|distance| distance.checked_add(1))
167:         .expect("requested region window exceeds integer address space");
168:     usize::try_from(count).expect("requested region window exceeds platform address space")
169: }
170: 
171: fn region_origin(region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Position {
172:     Position::new(region_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE, region_z as f32 * REGION_SIZE)
173: }
174:
````
