````rust
  1: //! Traverse the voxel scene and turn selected SVO nodes into shaded splats.
  2: //!
  3: //! `render_node` is deliberately a short dispatcher. Projection, atlas
  4: //! decoding, budget fallback, leaf handling, interior handling, MIP drawing,
  5: //! and child ordering each live in a small helper with an explicit data type.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightSource};
  8: 
  9: mod project_voxel_node;
 10: mod select_voxel_detail;
 11: mod visit_voxel_octants;
 12: 
 13: use super::super::atlas::{VOXEL_AIR, decode_node, emission_strength};
 14: use super::super::camera::Camera;
 15: use super::super::shading::{FrameLighting, HeroLightVisibility};
 16: use super::super::surface_geometry::{SurfaceExposure, project_surface_depth};
 17: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 18: use project_voxel_node::{ProjectedVoxelNode, node_is_in_flashlight_focus, project_voxel_node};
 19: use select_voxel_detail::{should_draw_mip_splat, should_subdivide_leaf};
 20: use visit_voxel_octants::{VoxelChildren, voxel_child_visits};
 21: 
 22: /// Attributes carried by a real atlas leaf or a virtually subdivided leaf.
 23: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 24: pub(super) struct LeafPayload {
 25:     voxel_type: u32,
 26:     linear_albedo: [f32; 3],
 27:     baked_rgb: [u8; 3],
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// Everything needed to visit one real or virtual node.
 31: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 32: pub(super) struct NodeVisit {
 33:     node_idx: usize,
 34:     min: [f32; 3],
 35:     size: f32,
 36:     crowded_siblings: u32,
 37:     virtual_leaf: Option<LeafPayload>,
 38:     virtual_depth: usize,
 39:     exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: impl NodeVisit {
 43:     fn root(chunk: &ChunkDraw) -> Self {
 44:         Self {
 45:             node_idx: chunk.root_index as usize,
 46:             min: chunk.origin,
 47:             size: chunk.world_size,
 48:             crowded_siblings: 1,
 49:             virtual_leaf: None,
 50:             virtual_depth: 0,
 51:             exposure: SurfaceExposure::ALL_FACES,
 52:         }
 53:     }
 54: }
 55: 
 56: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 57: enum NodeKind {
 58:     Leaf {
 59:         payload: LeafPayload,
 60:         exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 61:     },
 62:     Interior {
 63:         child_base: usize,
 64:         child_mask: u32,
 65:     },
 66: }
 67: 
 68: /// The exact finite-support cluster for one chunk plus the frame-global hero
 69: /// when (and only when) that same fixture belongs to the cluster.
 70: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 71: struct ChunkLighting<'a> {
 72:     fixtures: &'a [LightSource],
 73:     hero: Option<&'a LightSource>,
 74: }
 75: 
 76: impl<'a> ChunkLighting<'a> {
 77:     fn with_global_hero(fixtures: &'a [LightSource], global_hero_id: Option<u64>) -> Self {
 78:         let hero = global_hero_id.and_then(|id| fixtures.iter().find(|light| light.id == id));
 79:         Self { fixtures, hero }
 80:     }
 81: }
 82: 
 83: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 84:     /// Traversal entry point kept narrow for the frame orchestrator.
 85:     pub(super) fn traverse_voxel_chunk(
 86:         &mut self,
 87:         cam: &Camera,
 88:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 89:         chunk: &ChunkDraw,
 90:         scene_lights: &[LightSource],
 91:         global_hero_id: Option<u64>,
 92:     ) {
 93:         let lighting = ChunkLighting::with_global_hero(scene_lights, global_hero_id);
 94:         self.traverse_voxel_node(cam, chunks, lighting, NodeVisit::root(chunk));
 95:     }
 96: 
 97:     /// Projects, resolves, and dispatches one node. All branch-specific work
 98:     /// is delegated so the recursive control flow remains readable.
 99:     fn traverse_voxel_node(
100:         &mut self,
101:         cam: &Camera,
102:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
103:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
104:         visit: NodeVisit,
105:     ) {
106:         // These are absolute frame limits, checked before projection, atlas
107:         // decode, lighting, or a secondary visibility ray. In particular,
108:         // reaching the pixel-write cap must not leave an invisible tail of
109:         // expensive shading work in the recursion.
110:         if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes)
111:             || self.frame_work_budget.nodes_exhausted(self.visited_nodes)
112:         {
113:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
114:             return;
115:         }
116: 
117:         let Some(projected) = project_voxel_node(self, cam, visit) else {
118:             return;
119:         };
120: 
121:         // Preserve telemetry semantics: a projected malformed atlas node is
122:         // counted before its failed decode, just as the original traversal.
123:         self.visited_nodes += 1;
124:         let Some(kind) = self.resolve_node(visit) else {
125:             return;
126:         };
127: 
128:         let at_hard_cap = self.frame_work_budget.nodes_exhausted(self.visited_nodes);
129:         let outside_focus_reserve = self
130:             .frame_work_budget
131:             .outside_focus_reserve(self.visited_nodes)
132:             && !node_is_in_flashlight_focus(cam, &projected);
133:         if at_hard_cap || outside_focus_reserve {
134:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
135:             self.render_budget_fallback(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, &projected, kind);
136:             return;
137:         }
138: 
139:         match kind {
140:             NodeKind::Leaf { payload, exposure } => {
141:                 let visit = NodeVisit { exposure, ..visit };
142:                 self.render_leaf(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, &projected, payload)
143:             }
144:             NodeKind::Interior {
145:                 child_base,
146:                 child_mask,
147:             } => {
148:                 self.render_interior(
149:                     cam, chunks, lighting, visit, &projected, child_base, child_mask,
150:                 );
151:             }
152:         }
153:     }
154: 
155:     fn resolve_node(&self, visit: NodeVisit) -> Option<NodeKind> {
156:         if let Some(payload) = visit.virtual_leaf {
157:             return Some(NodeKind::Leaf {
158:                 payload,
159:                 exposure: visit.exposure,
160:             });
161:         }
162: 
163:         let node = decode_node(&self.atlas, visit.node_idx)?;
164:         if node.is_leaf {
165:             let linear_albedo = self
166:                 .mips
167:                 .get(visit.node_idx)
168:                 .map_or([0.0; 3], |mip| mip.linear_albedo);
169:             Some(NodeKind::Leaf {
170:                 payload: LeafPayload {
171:                     voxel_type: node.voxel_type,
172:                     linear_albedo,
173:                     baked_rgb: node.baked_rgb,
174:                 },
175:                 exposure: node.exposure,
176:             })
177:         } else {
178:             Some(NodeKind::Interior {
179:                 child_base: node.child_base,
180:                 child_mask: node.child_mask,
181:             })
182:         }
183:     }
184: 
185:     /// Safety-cap behavior: retain the current fidelity and stop descending.
186:     fn render_budget_fallback(
187:         &mut self,
188:         cam: &Camera,
189:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
190:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
191:         visit: NodeVisit,
192:         projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
193:         kind: NodeKind,
194:     ) {
195:         match kind {
196:             NodeKind::Leaf { payload, exposure } if payload.voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR => {
197:                 let visit = NodeVisit { exposure, ..visit };
198:                 self.draw_leaf_splat(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, projected, payload);
199:             }
200:             NodeKind::Leaf { .. } => {}
201:             NodeKind::Interior { .. } => {
202:                 self.draw_mip_splat(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, projected)
203:             }
204:         }
205:     }
206: 
207:     fn render_leaf(
208:         &mut self,
209:         cam: &Camera,
210:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
211:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
212:         visit: NodeVisit,
213:         projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
214:         payload: LeafPayload,
215:     ) {
216:         if payload.voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
217:             return;
218:         }
219:         self.max_virtual_depth_reached = self.max_virtual_depth_reached.max(visit.virtual_depth);
220: 
221:         let should_subdivide = should_subdivide_leaf(&self.settings, visit, projected);
222:         if should_subdivide {
223:             self.visit_children(
224:                 cam,
225:                 chunks,
226:                 lighting,
227:                 visit,
228:                 VoxelChildren::Virtual(payload),
229:                 visit.crowded_siblings,
230:             );
231:         } else {
232:             self.draw_leaf_splat(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, projected, payload);
233:         }
234:     }
235: 
236:     fn draw_leaf_splat(
237:         &mut self,
238:         cam: &Camera,
239:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
240:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
241:         visit: NodeVisit,
242:         projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
243:         payload: LeafPayload,
244:     ) {
245:         let half_px = projected.footprint.enclosing_radius().max(0.85);
246:         let emission_strength = emission_strength(payload.voxel_type);
247:         let emissive = emission_strength.is_some();
248:         let Some(surface_depth) = project_surface_depth(
249:             cam,
250:             projected.center,
251:             visit.size,
252:             payload.voxel_type,
253:             emissive,
254:             visit.exposure,
255:         ) else {
256:             return;
257:         };
258:         if self.settings.toggles.deferred_shading
259:             && !self.surface_splat_may_contribute(
260:                 projected.footprint.center[0],
261:                 projected.footprint.center[1],
262:                 half_px,
263:                 surface_depth,
264:                 emissive,
265:             )
266:         {
267:             return;
268:         }
269:         let hero_visibility = self.resolve_hero_light_visibility(
270:             chunks,
271:             projected.center,
272:             visit.size,
273:             emissive,
274:             surface_depth.representative_depth(),
275:             lighting.hero,
276:         );
277:         self.shade_predecoded_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
278:             cam,
279:             chunks,
280:             frame_lighting(lighting.fixtures, hero_visibility),
281:             projected.center,
282:             visit.size,
283:             projected.footprint.center[0],
284:             projected.footprint.center[1],
285:             half_px,
286:             surface_depth,
287:             payload.linear_albedo,
288:             payload.baked_rgb.map(f32::from),
289:             emission_strength,
290:             payload.voxel_type,
291:             visit.exposure,
292:             visit.crowded_siblings,
293:         );
294:     }
295: 
296:     fn render_interior(
297:         &mut self,
298:         cam: &Camera,
299:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
300:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
301:         visit: NodeVisit,
302:         projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
303:         child_base: usize,
304:         child_mask: u32,
305:     ) {
306:         // OPTIMIZATION (LOD): a subtree fitting in roughly a pixel becomes
307:         // one prefiltered MIP splat instead of a full descendant walk.
308:         let contains_emissive = self
309:             .mips
310:             .get(visit.node_idx)
311:             .is_some_and(|mip| mip.emissive_coverage > 0.0);
312:         if should_draw_mip_splat(&self.settings, projected) && !contains_emissive {
313:             self.draw_mip_splat(cam, chunks, lighting, visit, projected);
314:             return;
315:         }
316: 
317:         self.visit_children(
318:             cam,
319:             chunks,
320:             lighting,
321:             visit,
322:             VoxelChildren::Atlas {
323:                 base: child_base,
324:                 mask: child_mask,
325:             },
326:             child_mask.count_ones(),
327:         );
328:     }
329: 
330:     fn draw_mip_splat(
331:         &mut self,
332:         cam: &Camera,
333:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
334:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
335:         visit: NodeVisit,
336:         projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
337:     ) {
338:         let mip = self.mips.get(visit.node_idx).copied().unwrap_or_default();
339:         if mip.occupancy < self.settings.min_mip_occupancy {
340:             return;
341:         }
342:         let half_px = projected.footprint.enclosing_radius().max(0.85);
343:         let emissive = mip.emissive_coverage > 0.0;
344:         let mip_voxel_type = if emissive {
345:             vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_LIGHT as u32
346:         } else {
347:             mip.dominant_voxel_type
348:         };
349:         let Some(surface_depth) = project_surface_depth(
350:             cam,
351:             projected.center,
352:             visit.size,
353:             mip_voxel_type,
354:             emissive,
355:             mip.exposed_area,
356:         ) else {
357:             return;
358:         };
359:         if self.settings.toggles.deferred_shading
360:             && !self.surface_splat_may_contribute(
361:                 projected.footprint.center[0],
362:                 projected.footprint.center[1],
363:                 half_px,
364:                 surface_depth,
365:                 emissive,
366:             )
367:         {
368:             return;
369:         }
370:         let hero_visibility = self.resolve_hero_light_visibility(
371:             chunks,
372:             projected.center,
373:             visit.size,
374:             emissive,
375:             surface_depth.representative_depth(),
376:             lighting.hero,
377:         );
378:         self.shade_predecoded_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
379:             cam,
380:             chunks,
381:             frame_lighting(lighting.fixtures, hero_visibility),
382:             projected.center,
383:             visit.size,
384:             projected.footprint.center[0],
385:             projected.footprint.center[1],
386:             half_px,
387:             surface_depth,
388:             if emissive {
389:                 mip.emitted_radiance_density
390:             } else {
391:                 mip.linear_albedo
392:             },
393:             mip.baked_rgb,
394:             emissive.then_some(1.0),
395:             mip_voxel_type,
396:             mip.exposed_area,
397:             visit.crowded_siblings,
398:         );
399:     }
400: 
401:     /// Visits occupied octants either near-to-far or in reference index
402:     /// order. Virtual subdivision reuses one leaf payload at the next depth.
403:     fn visit_children(
404:         &mut self,
405:         cam: &Camera,
406:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
407:         lighting: ChunkLighting<'_>,
408:         parent: NodeVisit,
409:         children: VoxelChildren,
410:         crowding: u32,
411:     ) {
412:         for child in voxel_child_visits(
413:             parent,
414:             children,
415:             crowding,
416:             cam.pos,
417:             self.settings.toggles.front_to_back,
418:         )
419:         .into_iter()
420:         .flatten()
421:         {
422:             self.traverse_voxel_node(cam, chunks, lighting, child);
423:         }
424:     }
425: }
426: 
427: fn frame_lighting(
428:     scene_lights: &[LightSource],
429:     hero_visibility: Option<HeroLightVisibility>,
430: ) -> FrameLighting<'_> {
431:     match hero_visibility {
432:         Some(hero) => {
433:             FrameLighting::with_hero_visibility(scene_lights, hero.light_id, hero.visibility)
434:         }
435:         None => FrameLighting::unshadowed(scene_lights),
436:     }
437: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/traverse_voxel_scene/project_voxel_node.rs
````rust
 1: //! Project one voxel node and conservatively reject invisible bounds.
 2: 
 3: use super::super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 4: use super::super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 5: use super::super::project_aabb_footprint::{
 6:     NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH, ScreenFootprint, aabb_camera_depth_interval, project_screen_footprint,
 7: };
 8: use super::NodeVisit;
 9: 
10: /// Screen-space facts shared by traversal, LOD selection, and splat drawing.
11: pub(super) struct ProjectedVoxelNode {
12:     pub(super) center: [f32; 3],
13:     pub(super) relative_to_camera: [f32; 3],
14:     pub(super) camera_depth: f32,
15:     /// One eight-corner projection shared by culling, LOD, splitting, HZ,
16:     /// deferred-depth rejection, and the final splat write.
17:     pub(super) footprint: ScreenFootprint,
18: }
19: 
20: /// Returns `None` when the node cannot contribute a visible pixel.
21: pub(super) fn project_voxel_node(
22:     renderer: &SoftwareRasterizer,
23:     camera: &Camera,
24:     visit: NodeVisit,
25: ) -> Option<ProjectedVoxelNode> {
26:     let half_size = visit.size * 0.5;
27:     let center = [
28:         visit.min[0] + half_size,
29:         visit.min[1] + half_size,
30:         visit.min[2] + half_size,
31:     ];
32:     let relative_to_camera = [
33:         center[0] - camera.pos[0],
34:         center[1] - camera.pos[1],
35:         center[2] - camera.pos[2],
36:     ];
37:     let camera_depth = dot(relative_to_camera, camera.forward);
38:     let depth_interval = aabb_camera_depth_interval(camera, relative_to_camera, half_size);
39:     if depth_interval[1] <= NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH {
40:         return None;
41:     }
42: 
43:     let footprint = project_screen_footprint(camera, visit.min, visit.size, depth_interval[0])?;
44: 
45:     if footprint.outside_framebuffer(renderer.target.width(), renderer.target.height()) {
46:         return None;
47:     }
48: 
49:     // OPTIMIZATION (hierarchical z): every overlapping tile must be fully
50:     // covered and its farthest pixel nearer than the node's nearest bound.
51:     if renderer.settings.toggles.hierarchical_z
52:         && renderer.target.coarse_rect_occludes(
53:             footprint.center,
54:             footprint.half_extent,
55:             footprint.nearest_depth.max(0.0),
56:         )
57:     {
58:         return None;
59:     }
60: 
61:     Some(ProjectedVoxelNode {
62:         center,
63:         relative_to_camera,
64:         camera_depth,
65:         footprint,
66:     })
67: }
68: 
69: /// True when a projected node may use the bounded flashlight-focus reserve
70: /// between the soft degradation threshold and the absolute hard cap.
71: pub(super) fn node_is_in_flashlight_focus(camera: &Camera, projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode) -> bool {
72:     if !camera.flashlight {
73:         return false;
74:     }
75:     let distance = projected.camera_depth.max(0.001);
76:     if distance >= 15.0 {
77:         return false;
78:     }
79:     let direction = projected
80:         .relative_to_camera
81:         .map(|component| component / distance);
82:     dot(direction, camera.forward) > 0.88
83: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Select real-node MIP detail and virtual leaf subdivision.
 2: //!
 3: //! These predicates are the complete LOD policy. Traversal performs the
 4: //! chosen action but does not hide additional quality thresholds.
 5: 
 6: use super::super::super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 7: use super::NodeVisit;
 8: use super::project_voxel_node::ProjectedVoxelNode;

10: pub(super) fn should_subdivide_leaf(
11:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
12:     visit: NodeVisit,
13:     projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
14: ) -> bool {
15:     projected.footprint.enclosing_radius() > settings.max_splat_radius_px
16:         && visit.size > settings.min_split_size
17:         && visit.virtual_depth < settings.max_virtual_depth as usize
18: }
19: 
20: /// OPTIMIZATION (MIP LOD): a subtree fitting in roughly one pixel becomes
21: /// one prefiltered splat instead of a full descendant walk.
22: pub(super) fn should_draw_mip_splat(
23:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
24:     projected: &ProjectedVoxelNode,
25: ) -> bool {
26:     settings.toggles.mip_lod && projected.footprint.enclosing_radius() < settings.lod_cutoff_px
27: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/traverse_voxel_scene/visit_voxel_octants.rs
````rust
 1: //! Construct occupied child visits in the configured traversal order.
 2: 
 3: use super::super::super::surface_geometry::exposure_for_octant;
 4: use super::{LeafPayload, NodeVisit};
 5: 
 6: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 7: pub(super) enum VoxelChildren {
 8:     Atlas { base: usize, mask: u32 },
 9:     Virtual(LeafPayload),
10: }
11: 
12: impl VoxelChildren {
13:     fn occupied_mask(self) -> u32 {
14:         match self {
15:             Self::Atlas { mask, .. } => mask,
16:             Self::Virtual(_) => 0xFF,
17:         }
18:     }
19: 
20:     fn atlas_or_virtual_child(
21:         self,
22:         octant: u32,
23:         parent_virtual_depth: usize,
24:     ) -> (usize, Option<LeafPayload>, usize) {
25:         match self {
26:             Self::Atlas { base, .. } => (base + octant as usize, None, 0),
27:             Self::Virtual(payload) => (usize::MAX, Some(payload), parent_virtual_depth + 1),
28:         }
29:     }
30: }
31: 
32: /// Occupied child visits in near-to-far order, or plain atlas order when the
33: /// optimization is disabled. Empty slots let the caller use one stack-free,
34: /// fixed-size result without allocation.
35: pub(super) fn voxel_child_visits(
36:     parent: NodeVisit,
37:     children: VoxelChildren,
38:     crowded_siblings: u32,
39:     camera_position: [f32; 3],
40:     front_to_back: bool,
41: ) -> [Option<NodeVisit>; 8] {
42:     let half_size = parent.size * 0.5;
43:     let parent_center = [
44:         parent.min[0] + half_size,
45:         parent.min[1] + half_size,
46:         parent.min[2] + half_size,
47:     ];
48:     let camera_octant = (camera_position[0] >= parent_center[0]) as u32
49:         | (((camera_position[1] >= parent_center[1]) as u32) << 1)
50:         | (((camera_position[2] >= parent_center[2]) as u32) << 2);
51: 
52:     // XOR distances grouped by popcount: camera octant first, opposite last.
53:     const NEAR_TO_FAR_XOR: [u32; 8] = [0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7];
54:     let occupied_mask = children.occupied_mask();
55:     let mut visits = [None; 8];
56:     for (index, relative_octant) in NEAR_TO_FAR_XOR.into_iter().enumerate() {
57:         let octant = if front_to_back {
58:             camera_octant ^ relative_octant
59:         } else {
60:             index as u32
61:         };
62:         if occupied_mask & (1 << octant) == 0 {
63:             continue;
64:         }
65: 
66:         let min = [
67:             parent.min[0] + (octant & 1) as f32 * half_size,
68:             parent.min[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) as f32 * half_size,
69:             parent.min[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) as f32 * half_size,
70:         ];
71:         let (node_idx, virtual_leaf, virtual_depth) =
72:             children.atlas_or_virtual_child(octant, parent.virtual_depth);
73:         visits[index] = Some(NodeVisit {
74:             node_idx,
75:             min,
76:             size: half_size,
77:             crowded_siblings,
78:             virtual_leaf,
79:             virtual_depth,
80:             exposure: exposure_for_octant(parent.exposure, occupied_mask, octant),
81:         });
82:     }
83:     visits
84: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/draw_visible_flare_cores.rs
````rust
 1: //! Draw the visible cores of dynamic flare lights.
 2: //!
 3: //! A core is an ordinary depth-tested splat. Drawing it after scene geometry
 4: //! lets the fine depth buffer provide wall occlusion without another raycast.
 5: 
 6: use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
 7: 
 8: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 9: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
10: 
11: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
12:     pub(super) fn draw_visible_flare_cores(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, camera: &Camera) {
13:         for light in frame.active_dynamic_lights() {
14:             let Some(core) = project_flare_core(light.position, light.intensity, camera) else {
15:                 continue;
16:             };
17:             if core.depth > self.settings.max_draw_distance {
18:                 continue;
19:             }
20: 
21:             self.splat(
22:                 core.pixel[0],
23:                 core.pixel[1],
24:                 core.half_extent,
25:                 core.depth - 0.05,
26:                 core.color,
27:             );
28:         }
29:     }
30: }
31: 
32: struct ProjectedFlareCore {
33:     pixel: [f32; 2],
34:     half_extent: f32,
35:     depth: f32,
36:     color: [u8; 3],
37: }
38: 
39: fn project_flare_core(
40:     position: [f32; 3],
41:     intensity: f32,
42:     camera: &Camera,
43: ) -> Option<ProjectedFlareCore> {
44:     let relative = [
45:         position[0] - camera.pos[0],
46:         position[1] - camera.pos[1],
47:         position[2] - camera.pos[2],
48:     ];
49:     let depth = dot(relative, camera.forward);
50:     if depth <= 0.1 {
51:         return None;
52:     }
53: 
54:     let normalized_intensity = intensity.clamp(0.0, 1.6) / 1.6;
55:     Some(ProjectedFlareCore {
56:         pixel: [
57:             camera.half_w + dot(relative, camera.right) / depth * camera.focal_px,
58:             camera.half_h - dot(relative, camera.up) / depth * camera.focal_px,
59:         ],
60:         half_extent: (0.06 / depth * camera.focal_px).clamp(1.0, 6.0),
61:         depth,
62:         color: [
63:             (255.0 * normalized_intensity) as u8,
64:             (150.0 * normalized_intensity) as u8,
65:             (60.0 * normalized_intensity) as u8,
66:         ],
67:     })
68: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/frame_work_budget.rs
````rust
  1: //! Derive one bounded frame-work envelope from the actual render target.
  2: //!
  3: //! A fixed global cap makes a quality preset self-defeating: increasing the
  4: //! backing size or asking for smaller splats spends the same allowance over
  5: //! more pixels and can therefore reveal *less* of the scene.  This policy
  6: //! instead assigns work per target pixel, then raises that density as the
  7: //! validated geometry settings request more detail.
  8: //!
  9: //! The limits are safety valves, not quality targets.  Ordinary frames finish
 10: //! well below them.  Absolute ceilings remain so a corrupt target size or
 11: //! pathological atlas cannot monopolize the browser indefinitely.
 12: 
 13: use super::super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 14: 
 15: /// Hard stop for malformed/pathological traversal, independent of target
 16: /// dimensions.  The 1920x1080 Maximum regression remains below this ceiling.
 17: pub(super) const ABSOLUTE_NODE_VISIT_CEILING: usize = 8_000_000;
 18: /// Hard stop for fine-depth writes.  Large enough for several layers over a
 19: /// 1920x1080 Maximum target, but finite even if dimensions are corrupted.
 20: pub(super) const ABSOLUTE_PIXEL_WRITE_CEILING: usize = 16_000_000;
 21: 
 22: const MINIMUM_NODE_VISITS: usize = 16_384;
 23: const MINIMUM_PIXEL_WRITES: usize = 4_096;
 24: const FOCUS_RESERVE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.90;
 25: 
 26: /// Immutable work limits for one framebuffer/settings snapshot.
 27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 28: pub(super) struct FrameWorkBudget {
 29:     node_visit_limit: usize,
 30:     soft_node_visit_limit: usize,
 31:     pixel_write_limit: usize,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: impl FrameWorkBudget {
 35:     /// Builds a target-aware envelope from validated renderer settings.
 36:     ///
 37:     /// The density functions deliberately use only existing, user-visible
 38:     /// quality controls.  A custom profile therefore reproduces its budget
 39:     /// from its URL/settings values without another hidden preset identity.
 40:     pub(super) fn for_target(settings: &CpuRenderSettings, width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {
 41:         let settings = settings.validated();
 42:         let target_pixels = width.saturating_mul(height).max(1);
 43: 
 44:         let node_visit_limit = scaled_limit(
 45:             target_pixels,
 46:             node_visits_per_pixel(&settings),
 47:             MINIMUM_NODE_VISITS,
 48:             ABSOLUTE_NODE_VISIT_CEILING,
 49:         );
 50:         let soft_node_visit_limit = ((node_visit_limit as f64 * FOCUS_RESERVE_FRACTION).floor()
 51:             as usize)
 52:             .max(1)
 53:             .min(node_visit_limit);
 54: 
 55:         // At supported target sizes the fine-write allowance can always
 56:         // cover the framebuffer at least once.  Successful depth rewrites,
 57:         // rather than rejected fragments, consume the remaining allowance.
 58:         let one_full_coverage = target_pixels.min(ABSOLUTE_PIXEL_WRITE_CEILING);
 59:         let pixel_write_limit = scaled_limit(
 60:             target_pixels,
 61:             pixel_writes_per_pixel(&settings),
 62:             MINIMUM_PIXEL_WRITES.max(one_full_coverage),
 63:             ABSOLUTE_PIXEL_WRITE_CEILING,
 64:         );
 65: 
 66:         Self {
 67:             node_visit_limit,
 68:             soft_node_visit_limit,
 69:             pixel_write_limit,
 70:         }
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     pub(super) const fn node_visit_limit(self) -> usize {
 74:         self.node_visit_limit
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     pub(super) const fn soft_node_visit_limit(self) -> usize {
 78:         self.soft_node_visit_limit
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     pub(super) const fn pixel_write_limit(self) -> usize {
 82:         self.pixel_write_limit
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     pub(super) const fn nodes_exhausted(self, visited_nodes: usize) -> bool {
 86:         visited_nodes >= self.node_visit_limit
 87:     }
 88: 
 89:     pub(super) const fn outside_focus_reserve(self, visited_nodes: usize) -> bool {
 90:         visited_nodes >= self.soft_node_visit_limit
 91:     }
 92: 
 93:     pub(super) const fn writes_exhausted(self, pixel_writes: usize) -> bool {
 94:         pixel_writes >= self.pixel_write_limit
 95:     }
 96: 
 97:     pub(super) const fn remaining_pixel_writes(self, pixel_writes: usize) -> usize {
 98:         self.pixel_write_limit.saturating_sub(pixel_writes)
 99:     }
100: }
101: 
102: impl Default for FrameWorkBudget {
103:     fn default() -> Self {
104:         Self::for_target(&CpuRenderSettings::default(), 1, 1)
105:     }
106: }
107: 
108: fn scaled_limit(pixels: usize, density: f64, minimum: usize, ceiling: usize) -> usize {
109:     let requested = (pixels as f64 * density).ceil();
110:     if !requested.is_finite() || requested >= ceiling as f64 {
111:         return ceiling;
112:     }
113:     (requested as usize).max(minimum).min(ceiling)
114: }
115: 
116: /// Traversal density rises monotonically with virtual depth, smaller maximum
117: /// splats, and a smaller MIP cutoff.  Coefficients keep Balanced close to one
118: /// node allowance per target pixel while giving Maximum room for its much
119: /// finer geometry without restoring an effectively unbounded walk.
120: fn node_visits_per_pixel(settings: &CpuRenderSettings) -> f64 {
121:     0.35 + f64::from(settings.max_virtual_depth) * 0.08
122:         + 0.4 / f64::from(settings.max_splat_radius_px)
123:         + 0.15 / f64::from(settings.lod_cutoff_px)
124: }
125: 
126: /// Fine-write density is always greater than one complete coverage and rises
127: /// with detail.  This budget counts only successful depth writes; conservative
128: /// footprint scans and rejected pixels do not consume it.
129: fn pixel_writes_per_pixel(settings: &CpuRenderSettings) -> f64 {
130:     1.0 + f64::from(settings.max_virtual_depth) * 0.12
131:         + 1.0 / f64::from(settings.max_splat_radius_px).sqrt()
132:         + 0.2 / f64::from(settings.lod_cutoff_px)
133: }
134:

136: mod tests {

139: 
140:     #[test]
141:     fn preset_work_density_never_decreases() {
142:         let budgets = [

144:             CpuQualityPreset::Balanced,

147:         ]
148:         .map(|preset| FrameWorkBudget::for_target(&preset.settings(), 960, 540));
149: 
150:         for pair in budgets.windows(2) {

152:             assert!(pair[0].pixel_write_limit() <= pair[1].pixel_write_limit());

160: 
161:         assert!(budget.pixel_write_limit() >= pixels);
162:         assert!(budget.pixel_write_limit() < ABSOLUTE_PIXEL_WRITE_CEILING);
163:         assert!(budget.node_visit_limit() > 150_000);

173:         fine.max_virtual_depth = 8;
174:

176:         let fine = FrameWorkBudget::for_target(&fine, 640, 360);
177:         assert!(fine.node_visit_limit() > coarse.node_visit_limit());
178:         assert!(fine.pixel_write_limit() > coarse.pixel_write_limit());

186:             usize::MAX,
187:         );
188:

190:         assert_eq!(budget.pixel_write_limit(), ABSOLUTE_PIXEL_WRITE_CEILING);
191:         assert!(budget.soft_node_visit_limit() < budget.node_visit_limit());
192:     }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/project_aabb_footprint.rs
````rust
  1: //! Exact conservative screen bounds for one axis-aligned voxel box.
  2: //!
  3: //! Projecting only the box center and multiplying its world half-size by a
  4: //! fudge factor under-covers oblique boxes.  Perspective projection is a
  5: //! linear-fractional map, so each screen-coordinate extremum over the AABB
  6: //! clipped to the near half-space occurs at a clipped-polyhedron vertex.
  7: //! Those vertices are the original corners in front of the near plane plus
  8: //! intersections of the twelve box edges with that plane. Projecting this
  9: //! small fixed set gives the exact axis-aligned screen rectangle used by
 10: //! culling, LOD selection, splitting, and splat writing.
 11: 
 12: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 13: 
 14: pub(super) const NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH: f32 = 0.01;
 15: 
 16: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 17: pub(super) struct ScreenFootprint {
 18:     pub(super) center: [f32; 2],
 19:     pub(super) half_extent: [f32; 2],
 20:     /// Nearest camera-space depth of any AABB corner.
 21:     pub(super) nearest_depth: f32,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl ScreenFootprint {
 25:     /// Scalar radius used by the square-splat target and square HZ tiles.
 26:     /// It encloses the exact projected rectangle without an empirical pad.
 27:     pub(super) fn enclosing_radius(self) -> f32 {
 28:         self.half_extent[0].max(self.half_extent[1])
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     pub(super) fn outside_framebuffer(self, width: usize, height: usize) -> bool {
 32:         self.center[0] + self.half_extent[0] < 0.0
 33:             || self.center[0] - self.half_extent[0] >= width as f32
 34:             || self.center[1] + self.half_extent[1] < 0.0
 35:             || self.center[1] - self.half_extent[1] >= height as f32
 36:     }
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// Exact camera-depth interval of an AABB.  This support-function form is
 40: /// equivalent to testing all corners but avoids eight dot products for the
 41: /// behind/near-plane decision.
 42: pub(super) fn aabb_camera_depth_interval(
 43:     camera: &Camera,
 44:     center_relative_to_camera: [f32; 3],
 45:     half_size: f32,
 46: ) -> [f32; 2] {
 47:     let center_depth = dot(center_relative_to_camera, camera.forward);
 48:     let depth_radius =
 49:         half_size * (camera.forward[0].abs() + camera.forward[1].abs() + camera.forward[2].abs());
 50:     [center_depth - depth_radius, center_depth + depth_radius]
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Projects the exact vertices of an AABB clipped against the near plane.
 54: /// Returns `None` for non-finite/malformed or wholly-behind geometry.
 55: pub(super) fn project_screen_footprint(
 56:     camera: &Camera,
 57:     min: [f32; 3],
 58:     size: f32,
 59:     nearest_depth: f32,
 60: ) -> Option<ScreenFootprint> {
 61:     if !size.is_finite()
 62:         || size <= 0.0
 63:         || !nearest_depth.is_finite()
 64:         || min.into_iter().any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite())
 65:     {
 66:         return None;
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     let mut relative_corners = [[0.0; 3]; 8];
 70:     let mut depths = [0.0; 8];
 71:     for octant in 0..8usize {
 72:         let corner = [
 73:             min[0] + if octant & 1 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 74:             min[1] + if octant & 2 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 75:             min[2] + if octant & 4 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 76:         ];
 77:         let relative = [
 78:             corner[0] - camera.pos[0],
 79:             corner[1] - camera.pos[1],
 80:             corner[2] - camera.pos[2],
 81:         ];
 82:         let depth = dot(relative, camera.forward);
 83:         if !depth.is_finite() || relative.into_iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
 84:             return None;
 85:         }
 86:         relative_corners[octant] = relative;
 87:         depths[octant] = depth;
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     let mut screen_min = [f32::INFINITY; 2];
 91:     let mut screen_max = [f32::NEG_INFINITY; 2];
 92:     let mut include_projection = |relative: [f32; 3], depth: f32| -> Option<()> {
 93:         let inverse_depth = 1.0 / depth;
 94:         let screen = [
 95:             camera.half_w + dot(relative, camera.right) * inverse_depth * camera.focal_px,
 96:             camera.half_h - dot(relative, camera.up) * inverse_depth * camera.focal_px,
 97:         ];
 98:         if screen.into_iter().any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite()) {
 99:             return None;
100:         }
101:         for axis in 0..2 {
102:             screen_min[axis] = screen_min[axis].min(screen[axis]);
103:             screen_max[axis] = screen_max[axis].max(screen[axis]);
104:         }
105:         Some(())
106:     };
107: 
108:     for octant in 0..8usize {
109:         if depths[octant] >= NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH {
110:             include_projection(relative_corners[octant], depths[octant])?;
111:         }
112:     }
113: 
114:     // Each undirected AABB edge appears once: its low endpoint has the
115:     // corresponding axis bit clear. Crossing edges add the vertices created
116:     // by clipping the box against camera-space z = near.
117:     for axis_bit in [1usize, 2, 4] {
118:         for low in 0..8usize {
119:             if low & axis_bit != 0 {
120:                 continue;
121:             }
122:             let high = low | axis_bit;
123:             let low_depth = depths[low];
124:             let high_depth = depths[high];
125:             let crosses = (low_depth < NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH && high_depth > NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH)
126:                 || (high_depth < NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH && low_depth > NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH);
127:             if !crosses {
128:                 continue;
129:             }
130:             let t = (NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH - low_depth) / (high_depth - low_depth);
131:             let intersection = [
132:                 relative_corners[low][0]
133:                     + (relative_corners[high][0] - relative_corners[low][0]) * t,
134:                 relative_corners[low][1]
135:                     + (relative_corners[high][1] - relative_corners[low][1]) * t,
136:                 relative_corners[low][2]
137:                     + (relative_corners[high][2] - relative_corners[low][2]) * t,
138:             ];
139:             include_projection(intersection, NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH)?;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     if screen_min[0] == f32::INFINITY {
144:         return None;
145:     }
146: 
147:     let center = [
148:         (screen_min[0] + screen_max[0]) * 0.5,
149:         (screen_min[1] + screen_max[1]) * 0.5,
150:     ];
151:     let half_extent = [
152:         (screen_max[0] - screen_min[0]) * 0.5,
153:         (screen_max[1] - screen_min[1]) * 0.5,
154:     ];
155:     Some(ScreenFootprint {
156:         center,
157:         half_extent,
158:         nearest_depth: nearest_depth.max(NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH),
159:     })
160: }
161:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/render_cpu_frame.rs
````rust
  1: //! Orchestrate one complete CPU-splat frame.
  2: //!
  3: //! The sequence is intentionally visible in [`SoftwareRasterizer::render_cpu_frame`]:
  4: //! capture atmosphere, clear reusable buffers, build the camera, choose chunk
  5: //! order, reject non-contributing chunks, traverse, then draw flare cores.
  6: //! Individual rendering algorithms live behind those named operations.
  7: 
  8: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams};
  9: 
 10: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 11: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 12: use super::frame_work_budget::FrameWorkBudget;
 13: use super::project_aabb_footprint::{
 14:     NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH, aabb_camera_depth_interval, project_screen_footprint,
 15: };
 16: use super::select_lights_for_chunk::select_lights_for_chunk;
 17: 
 18: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 19:     pub(super) fn render_cpu_frame(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
 20:         self.environment = frame.environment;
 21:         self.frame_work_budget =
 22:             FrameWorkBudget::for_target(&self.settings, self.width(), self.height());
 23:         self.clear();
 24:         self.reset_frame_telemetry();
 25:         if self.atlas.is_empty() {
 26:             return;
 27:         }
 28: 
 29:         let camera = Camera::new(frame, self.width(), self.height(), &self.settings);
 30:         let ordered_chunks = chunks_in_draw_order(
 31:             chunks,
 32:             frame.camera_pos,
 33:             self.settings.toggles.front_to_back,
 34:         );
 35:         // Reused across chunks: one world-fixture scan per chunk, no
 36:         // per-splat allocation and no truncation of overlapping lights.
 37:         let mut chunk_scene_lights = std::mem::take(&mut self.chunk_light_scratch);
 38:         let global_hero_id = frame.active_scene_lights().first().map(|light| light.id);
 39: 
 40:         for chunk in ordered_chunks {
 41:             // Do not keep scanning fixtures/chunks after an absolute work
 42:             // budget has ended traversal for this frame.
 43:             if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes)
 44:                 || self.frame_work_budget.nodes_exhausted(self.visited_nodes)
 45:             {
 46:                 self.budget_exhausted = true;
 47:                 break;
 48:             }
 49:             if self.settings.toggles.distance_cull
 50:                 && !chunk_can_contribute(
 51:                     chunk,
 52:                     &camera,
 53:                     self.width(),
 54:                     self.height(),
 55:                     self.settings.max_draw_distance,
 56:                 )
 57:             {
 58:                 continue;
 59:             }
 60:             select_lights_for_chunk(frame.active_scene_lights(), chunk, &mut chunk_scene_lights);
 61:             self.traverse_voxel_chunk(&camera, chunks, chunk, &chunk_scene_lights, global_hero_id);
 62:         }
 63: 
 64:         self.chunk_light_scratch = chunk_scene_lights;
 65:         self.draw_visible_flare_cores(frame, &camera);
 66:         self.hero_light_visibility.advance_frame();
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     fn reset_frame_telemetry(&mut self) {
 70:         self.visited_nodes = 0;
 71:         self.budget_exhausted = false;
 72:         self.max_virtual_depth_reached = 0;
 73:         self.splat_count = 0;
 74:         self.pixel_writes = 0;
 75:     }
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Front-to-back ordering is an optional performance policy; fine depth
 79: /// testing makes the original chunk order the output-equivalent reference.
 80: fn chunks_in_draw_order(
 81:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 82:     camera_position: [f32; 3],
 83:     front_to_back: bool,
 84: ) -> Vec<&ChunkDraw> {
 85:     let mut ordered: Vec<_> = chunks.iter().collect();
 86:     if front_to_back {
 87:         ordered.sort_by(|a, b| {
 88:             chunk_distance_sq(a, camera_position).total_cmp(&chunk_distance_sq(b, camera_position))
 89:         });
 90:     }
 91:     ordered
 92: }
 93: 
 94: /// Conservative chunk-level distance and screen-bounds rejection.
 95: fn chunk_can_contribute(
 96:     chunk: &ChunkDraw,
 97:     camera: &Camera,
 98:     width: usize,
 99:     height: usize,
100:     max_draw_distance: f32,
101: ) -> bool {
102:     let half_size = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
103:     let center = [
104:         chunk.origin[0] + half_size,
105:         chunk.origin[1] + half_size,
106:         chunk.origin[2] + half_size,
107:     ];
108:     let radius = chunk.world_size * 0.5 * 3.0_f32.sqrt();
109:     let relative_to_camera = [
110:         center[0] - camera.pos[0],
111:         center[1] - camera.pos[1],
112:         center[2] - camera.pos[2],
113:     ];
114: 
115:     if dot(relative_to_camera, relative_to_camera).sqrt() - radius > max_draw_distance {
116:         return false;
117:     }
118:     let depth_interval = aabb_camera_depth_interval(camera, relative_to_camera, half_size);
119:     if depth_interval[1] <= NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH {
120:         return false;
121:     }
122: 
123:     project_screen_footprint(camera, chunk.origin, chunk.world_size, depth_interval[0])
124:         .is_some_and(|footprint| !footprint.outside_framebuffer(width, height))
125: }
126: 
127: fn chunk_distance_sq(chunk: &ChunkDraw, position: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
128:     let half = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
129:     let dx = chunk.origin[0] + half - position[0];
130:     let dz = chunk.origin[2] + half - position[2];
131:     dx * dx + dz * dz
132: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/resolve_hero_light_visibility.rs
````rust
  1: //! Resolve the CPU renderer's optional hero-light visibility term.
  2: //!
  3: //! Hero rays are intentionally a policy layer around the exact SVO raycast:
  4: //! they are limited to nearby, non-emissive receivers, stopped when the frame
  5: //! is already expensive, and amortized through a position-hashed cache. The
  6: //! traversal only asks for a visibility factor; it does not know how that
  7: //! factor is budgeted or cached.
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightSource};
 10: 
 11: use super::super::camera::dot;
 12: use super::super::raycast::{ray_box_interval, svo_segment_is_occluded};
 13: use super::super::settings::CpuShadowMode;
 14: use super::super::shading::HeroLightVisibility;
 15: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 16: 
 17: const CACHE_ENTRIES: usize = 65_536;
 18: const RETRACE_PERIOD_FRAMES: usize = 4;
 19: const MAX_RECEIVER_DISTANCE: f32 = 24.0;
 20: const RECEIVER_EXIT_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 21: const EMITTER_ENDPOINT_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 22: /// Above this write level, hero shadow rays are no longer affordable.
 23: const SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET: usize = 1_500_000;
 24: 
 25: /// Persistent visibility samples and the staggered refresh clock.
 26: pub(super) struct HeroLightVisibilityCache {
 27:     samples: Vec<CachedVisibility>,
 28:     frame_index: usize,
 29: }
 30: 
 31: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
 32: struct CachedVisibility {
 33:     query_key: u64,
 34:     visibility: f32,
 35:     valid: bool,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl HeroLightVisibilityCache {
 39:     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
 40:         Self {
 41:             samples: vec![CachedVisibility::default(); CACHE_ENTRIES],
 42:             frame_index: 0,
 43:         }
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     pub(super) fn advance_frame(&mut self) {
 47:         self.frame_index = self.frame_index.wrapping_add(1);
 48:     }
 49: }
 50: 
 51: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 52:     /// Returns no override for the reference/no-shadow path, otherwise an
 53:     /// id-matched binary SVO visibility sample for one real scene fixture.
 54:     pub(super) fn resolve_hero_light_visibility(
 55:         &mut self,
 56:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 57:         center: [f32; 3],
 58:         receiver_world_size: f32,
 59:         is_emissive: bool,
 60:         receiver_distance: f32,
 61:         hero: Option<&LightSource>,
 62:     ) -> Option<HeroLightVisibility> {
 63:         let hero = hero?;
 64:         let affordable =
 65:             receiver_distance <= MAX_RECEIVER_DISTANCE && self.pixel_writes < SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET;
 66:         if self.settings.shadows != CpuShadowMode::Hero || is_emissive || !affordable {
 67:             return None;
 68:         }
 69: 
 70:         let query_key = hash_receiver_and_light(center, receiver_world_size, hero.id);
 71:         let cache_index = query_key as usize % self.hero_light_visibility.samples.len();
 72:         let should_trace = (query_key as usize + self.hero_light_visibility.frame_index)
 73:             .is_multiple_of(RETRACE_PERIOD_FRAMES);
 74:         let cached = self.hero_light_visibility.samples[cache_index];
 75:         if !should_trace && cached.valid && cached.query_key == query_key {
 76:             return Some(HeroLightVisibility {
 77:                 light_id: hero.id,
 78:                 visibility: cached.visibility,
 79:             });
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         let visibility = trace_hero_fixture(
 83:             &self.atlas,
 84:             chunks,
 85:             center,
 86:             receiver_world_size,
 87:             hero.position,
 88:         );
 89:         self.hero_light_visibility.samples[cache_index] = CachedVisibility {
 90:             query_key,
 91:             visibility,
 92:             valid: true,
 93:         };
 94:         Some(HeroLightVisibility {
 95:             light_id: hero.id,
 96:             visibility,
 97:         })
 98:     }
 99: }
100: 
101: fn hash_receiver_and_light(center: [f32; 3], world_size: f32, light_id: u64) -> u64 {
102:     let mut key = light_id ^ 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
103:     for value in [center[0], center[1], center[2], world_size] {
104:         let bits = if value == 0.0 { 0 } else { value.to_bits() };
105:         key ^= u64::from(bits);
106:         key = key.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
107:     }
108:     key ^= key >> 33;
109:     key = key.wrapping_mul(0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd);
110:     key ^ (key >> 33)
111: }
112: 
113: fn trace_hero_fixture(
114:     atlas: &[u32],
115:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
116:     center: [f32; 3],
117:     receiver_world_size: f32,
118:     light_position: [f32; 3],
119: ) -> f32 {
120:     let to_light = [
121:         light_position[0] - center[0],
122:         light_position[1] - center[1],
123:         light_position[2] - center[2],
124:     ];
125:     let distance_to_light = dot(to_light, to_light).sqrt();
126:     if distance_to_light <= 0.001 {
127:         return 1.0;
128:     }
129: 
130:     let inverse_distance = 1.0 / distance_to_light;
131:     let direction = to_light.map(|component| component * inverse_distance);
132:     let receiver_half = receiver_world_size * 0.5;
133:     let receiver_min = center.map(|coordinate| coordinate - receiver_half);
134:     let receiver_max = center.map(|coordinate| coordinate + receiver_half);
135:     let Some(receiver_interval) = ray_box_interval(center, direction, receiver_min, receiver_max)
136:     else {
137:         return 1.0;
138:     };
139:     let origin_offset = receiver_interval.exit.max(0.0) + RECEIVER_EXIT_BIAS;
140:     let trace_length = distance_to_light - origin_offset - EMITTER_ENDPOINT_BIAS;
141:     if trace_length <= 0.0 {
142:         return 1.0;
143:     }
144:     let origin = [
145:         center[0] + direction[0] * origin_offset,
146:         center[1] + direction[1] * origin_offset,
147:         center[2] + direction[2] * origin_offset,
148:     ];
149:     if svo_segment_is_occluded(atlas, chunks, origin, direction, trace_length) {
150:         0.0
151:     } else {
152:         1.0
153:     }
154: }
155: 
156: #[cfg(test)]
157: mod tests {
158:     use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
159: 
160:     use super::trace_hero_fixture;
161: 
162:     #[test]
163:     fn coarse_receiver_does_not_occlude_its_own_hero_ray() {
164:         // One solid root leaf fills the whole 4u chunk. A center-biased ray
165:         // would immediately hit it; exiting the represented receiver first
166:         // leaves no geometry between its top face and the fixture.
167:         let atlas = [1, 1, 0xFF_FF_FF, 15];
168:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
169:             origin: [0.0; 3],
170:             root_index: 0,
171:             world_size: 4.0,
172:             voxel_size: 4.0,
173:             svo_depth: 0,
174:         }];
175: 
176:         let visibility = trace_hero_fixture(&atlas, &chunks, [2.0, 2.0, 2.0], 4.0, [2.0, 8.0, 2.0]);
177: 
178:         assert_eq!(visibility, 1.0);
179:     }
180: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/select_lights_for_chunk.rs
````rust
  1: //! Build an exact finite-support fixture cluster for one voxel chunk.
  2: //!
  3: //! Traversal shades many splats from the same chunk. Scanning every world
  4: //! fixture for every splat would dominate the CPU path, so the frame scans
  5: //! the fixture list once per chunk. A light is rejected only when the minimum
  6: //! distance between its emitter geometry and the chunk AABB exceeds its
  7: //! authored finite range; this changes no radiometric result.
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightKind, LightSource};
 10: 
 11: pub(super) fn select_lights_for_chunk(
 12:     scene_lights: &[LightSource],
 13:     chunk: &ChunkDraw,
 14:     selected: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
 15: ) {
 16:     selected.clear();
 17:     selected.extend(
 18:         scene_lights
 19:             .iter()
 20:             .copied()
 21:             .filter(|light| light_can_reach_chunk(light, chunk)),
 22:     );
 23: }
 24: 
 25: fn light_can_reach_chunk(light: &LightSource, chunk: &ChunkDraw) -> bool {
 26:     if !light.enabled
 27:         || !light.radius.is_finite()
 28:         || light.radius <= 0.0
 29:         || light
 30:             .position
 31:             .iter()
 32:             .any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite())
 33:     {
 34:         return false;
 35:     }
 36: 
 37:     let emitter_half_size = match light.kind {
 38:         LightKind::Point => [0.0, 0.0],
 39:         LightKind::CeilingPanel | LightKind::Strip | LightKind::Emergency => {
 40:             if light
 41:                 .half_size
 42:                 .iter()
 43:                 .any(|half| !half.is_finite() || *half <= 0.0)
 44:             {
 45:                 return false;
 46:             }
 47:             light.half_size
 48:         }
 49:     };
 50: 
 51:     let chunk_max = chunk.origin.map(|minimum| minimum + chunk.world_size);
 52:     let dx = interval_distance(
 53:         light.position[0] - emitter_half_size[0],
 54:         light.position[0] + emitter_half_size[0],
 55:         chunk.origin[0],
 56:         chunk_max[0],
 57:     );
 58:     let dy = point_interval_distance(light.position[1], chunk.origin[1], chunk_max[1]);
 59:     let dz = interval_distance(
 60:         light.position[2] - emitter_half_size[1],
 61:         light.position[2] + emitter_half_size[1],
 62:         chunk.origin[2],
 63:         chunk_max[2],
 64:     );
 65:     dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= light.radius * light.radius
 66: }
 67: 
 68: fn interval_distance(a_min: f32, a_max: f32, b_min: f32, b_max: f32) -> f32 {
 69:     if a_max < b_min {
 70:         b_min - a_max
 71:     } else if b_max < a_min {
 72:         a_min - b_max
 73:     } else {
 74:         0.0
 75:     }
 76: }
 77: 
 78: fn point_interval_distance(point: f32, minimum: f32, maximum: f32) -> f32 {
 79:     if point < minimum {
 80:         minimum - point
 81:     } else if point > maximum {
 82:         point - maximum
 83:     } else {
 84:         0.0
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: 
 88: #[cfg(test)]
 89: mod tests {
 90:     use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightKind, LightSource};
 91: 
 92:     use super::select_lights_for_chunk;
 93: 
 94:     fn chunk() -> ChunkDraw {
 95:         ChunkDraw {
 96:             origin: [0.0; 3],
 97:             root_index: 0,
 98:             world_size: 4.0,
 99:             voxel_size: 0.5,
100:             svo_depth: 3,
101:         }
102:     }
103: 
104:     fn light(position: [f32; 3], radius: f32) -> LightSource {
105:         LightSource {
106:             id: 7,
107:             position,
108:             radius,
109:             intensity: 1.0,
110:             color: [1.0; 3],
111:             enabled: true,
112:             ..LightSource::default()
113:         }
114:     }
115: 
116:     #[test]
117:     fn point_support_rejects_only_lights_outside_the_chunk_range() {
118:         let lights = [light([5.0, 2.0, 2.0], 1.0), light([5.1, 2.0, 2.0], 1.0)];
119:         let mut selected = Vec::new();
120: 
121:         select_lights_for_chunk(&lights, &chunk(), &mut selected);
122: 
123:         assert_eq!(selected.len(), 1);
124:         assert_eq!(selected[0].position, [5.0, 2.0, 2.0]);
125:     }
126: 
127:     #[test]
128:     fn rectangular_extent_is_part_of_the_conservative_intersection() {
129:         let panel = LightSource {
130:             kind: LightKind::CeilingPanel,
131:             half_size: [2.0, 0.5],
132:             ..light([6.5, 2.0, 2.0], 0.5)
133:         };
134:         let mut selected = Vec::new();
135: 
136:         select_lights_for_chunk(&[panel], &chunk(), &mut selected);
137: 
138:         assert_eq!(selected, vec![panel]);
139:     }
140: 
141:     #[test]
142:     fn disabled_lights_are_not_carried_into_splat_shading() {
143:         let disabled = LightSource {
144:             enabled: false,
145:             ..light([2.0; 3], 10.0)
146:         };
147:         let mut selected = Vec::new();
148: 
149:         select_lights_for_chunk(&[disabled], &chunk(), &mut selected);
150: 
151:         assert!(selected.is_empty());
152:     }
153: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Validated configuration for the CPU splatter.
  2: //!
  3: //! The browser owns *selection* (preset or custom controls), while the
  4: //! renderer receives one immutable [`CpuRenderSettings`] snapshot per frame.
  5: //! No traversal or shading function reads DOM state or atomics directly.
  6: //!
  7: //! The neighboring files make the two policies explicit:
  8: //!
  9: //! * [`quality_preset`] is the small, typed product model shown in Settings.
 10: //! * [`validation`] is the only place that accepts untrusted browser values.
 11: 
 12: mod quality_preset;
 13: mod validation;
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;
 16: 
 17: pub use quality_preset::CpuQualityPreset;
 18: pub use validation::CpuSettingsLimits;
 19: 
 20: /// Per-splat shadow tracing mode.
 21: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 22: pub enum CpuShadowMode {
 23:     /// No fixture shadow rays. Direct diffuse lighting still renders.
 24:     Off,
 25:     /// Trace the selected hero fixture for each affordable splat.
 26:     Hero,
 27:     /// Correctness reference: trace every contributing point-light endpoint
 28:     /// and every 2x2 rectangle quadrature endpoint through the SVO scene.
 29:     Full,
 30: }
 31: 
 32: /// Effective flashlight visibility policy. It is derived from the independent
 33: /// `rt_beam_occlusion` switch instead of being silently coupled to a preset.
 34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 35: pub enum CpuFlashlightVisibility {
 36:     /// Fast diagnostic path: the cone is evaluated without scene visibility.
 37:     Unoccluded,
 38:     /// Correctness path: trace the scene between the light and receiver.
 39:     TraceScene,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: impl CpuShadowMode {
 43:     /// Stable browser-facing representation.
 44:     pub const fn from_id(id: u32) -> Self {
 45:         match id {
 46:             1 => Self::Hero,
 47:             2 => Self::Full,
 48:             _ => Self::Off,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     pub const fn id(self) -> u32 {
 53:         match self {
 54:             Self::Off => 0,
 55:             Self::Hero => 1,
 56:             Self::Full => 2,
 57:         }
 58:     }
 59: }
 60: 
 61: /// Quality controls for the software rasterizer.
 62: ///
 63: /// Fields are public because native reference fixtures construct exact test
 64: /// configurations. Browser values must enter through [`Self::validated`].
 65: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 66: pub struct CpuRenderSettings {
 67:     /// Multiplier on the CPU renderer's quarter-viewport baseline.
 68:     /// `1.0` is 25% of the GPU backing dimensions; `2.0` is 50%.
 69:     pub internal_scale: f32,
 70:     /// Projected-radius threshold below which a subtree becomes one MIP
 71:     /// splat. Smaller values preserve finer distant geometry.
 72:     pub lod_cutoff_px: f32,
 73:     /// Largest allowed projected splat *radius*. Smaller values virtually
 74:     /// subdivide large leaves and reduce block artifacts.
 75:     pub max_splat_radius_px: f32,
 76:     /// Recursion cap for virtual subdivision of a solid leaf.
 77:     pub max_virtual_depth: u8,
 78:     /// World-space floor for virtual subdivision.
 79:     pub min_split_size: f32,
 80:     /// Chunk/node rejection distance in world units.
 81:     pub max_draw_distance: f32,
 82:     /// Minimum occupancy for one collapsed MIP splat.
 83:     pub min_mip_occupancy: f32,
 84:     /// Fixture-shadow quality. This is independent from flashlight
 85:     /// occlusion, which remains an individually diagnosable optimization.
 86:     pub shadows: CpuShadowMode,
 87:     /// `tan(vertical_fov / 2)`; supplied by the camera composition root.
 88:     pub fov_tan: f32,
 89:     /// Independent optimization switches shared with other renderers.
 90:     pub toggles: RenderToggles,
 91: }
 92: 
 93: impl Default for CpuRenderSettings {
 94:     fn default() -> Self {
 95:         CpuQualityPreset::Balanced.settings()
 96:     }
 97: }
 98: 
 99: impl CpuRenderSettings {
100:     pub fn flashlight_visibility(self) -> CpuFlashlightVisibility {
101:         if self.toggles.flashlight_occlusion {
102:             CpuFlashlightVisibility::TraceScene
103:         } else {
104:             CpuFlashlightVisibility::Unoccluded
105:         }
106:     }
107: }
108: 
109: #[cfg(test)]
110: mod tests {
111:     use super::*;
112: 
113:     #[test]
114:     fn presets_do_not_hide_the_flashlight_visibility_switch() {
115:         let mut settings = CpuQualityPreset::Maximum.settings();
116:         assert_eq!(
117:             settings.flashlight_visibility(),
118:             CpuFlashlightVisibility::TraceScene
119:         );
120:         settings.toggles.flashlight_occlusion = false;
121:         assert_eq!(
122:             settings.flashlight_visibility(),
123:             CpuFlashlightVisibility::Unoccluded
124:         );
125:     }
126: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Named CPU quality profiles.
  2: //!
  3: //! Presets only choose scalar quality and workload budgets. They never hide
  4: //! or mutate the renderer optimization switchboard, so an optimization can
  5: //! still be disabled independently while diagnosing an image.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;
  8: 
  9: use super::{CpuRenderSettings, CpuShadowMode};
 10: 
 11: /// Stable IDs cross the WASM boundary; names remain presentation concerns.
 12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 13: #[repr(u32)]
 14: pub enum CpuQualityPreset {
 15:     Performance = 0,
 16:     Balanced = 1,
 17:     Quality = 2,
 18:     Maximum = 3,
 19: }
 20: 
 21: impl CpuQualityPreset {
 22:     pub const fn from_id(id: u32) -> Self {
 23:         match id {
 24:             0 => Self::Performance,
 25:             2 => Self::Quality,
 26:             3 => Self::Maximum,
 27:             _ => Self::Balanced,
 28:         }
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     /// Complete renderer settings for this profile.
 32:     pub fn settings(self) -> CpuRenderSettings {
 33:         let (
 34:             internal_scale,
 35:             lod_cutoff_px,
 36:             max_splat_radius_px,
 37:             max_virtual_depth,
 38:             max_draw_distance,
 39:             min_mip_occupancy,
 40:             shadows,
 41:         ) = match self {
 42:             Self::Performance => (0.5, 1.5, 14.0, 4, 72.0, 0.35, CpuShadowMode::Off),
 43:             Self::Balanced => (1.0, 1.0, 8.0, 5, 96.0, 0.25, CpuShadowMode::Off),
 44:             Self::Quality => (1.5, 0.65, 4.0, 6, 128.0, 0.12, CpuShadowMode::Hero),
 45:             Self::Maximum => (2.0, 0.35, 2.0, 8, 160.0, 0.05, CpuShadowMode::Full),
 46:         };
 47: 
 48:         CpuRenderSettings {
 49:             internal_scale,
 50:             lod_cutoff_px,
 51:             max_splat_radius_px,
 52:             max_virtual_depth,
 53:             min_split_size: 0.005,
 54:             max_draw_distance,
 55:             min_mip_occupancy,
 56:             shadows,
 57:             fov_tan: 0.767,
 58:             toggles: RenderToggles::default(),
 59:         }
 60:     }
 61: }
 62:

 66:

 69:         let presets = [
 70:             CpuQualityPreset::Performance.settings(),
 71:             CpuQualityPreset::Balanced.settings(),
 72:             CpuQualityPreset::Quality.settings(),
 73:             CpuQualityPreset::Maximum.settings(),
 74:         ];
 75: 
 76:         for pair in presets.windows(2) {
 77:             assert!(pair[0].internal_scale < pair[1].internal_scale);
 78:             assert!(pair[0].lod_cutoff_px > pair[1].lod_cutoff_px);
 79:             assert!(pair[0].max_splat_radius_px > pair[1].max_splat_radius_px);
 80:             assert!(pair[0].max_virtual_depth < pair[1].max_virtual_depth);
````

````rust
  1: //! Boundary validation for CPU render settings.
  2: //!
  3: //! Sliders, saved JSON, and query strings are untrusted input. Keeping every
  4: //! numerical limit here prevents the UI, WASM exports, and renderer from
  5: //! developing slightly different interpretations of the same setting.
  6: 
  7: use super::CpuRenderSettings;
  8: 
  9: pub struct CpuSettingsLimits;
 10: 
 11: impl CpuSettingsLimits {
 12:     pub const INTERNAL_SCALE: (f32, f32) = (0.25, 2.0);
 13:     pub const LOD_CUTOFF_PX: (f32, f32) = (0.25, 2.0);
 14:     pub const MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_PX: (f32, f32) = (1.0, 16.0);
 15:     pub const MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH: (u8, u8) = (3, 8);
 16:     pub const MIN_SPLIT_SIZE: (f32, f32) = (0.005, 1.0);
 17:     pub const MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE: (f32, f32) = (16.0, 256.0);
 18:     pub const MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY: (f32, f32) = (0.0, 0.5);
 19:     pub const FOV_TAN: (f32, f32) = (0.1, 4.0);
 20: }
 21: 
 22: fn finite_clamp(value: f32, fallback: f32, limits: (f32, f32)) -> f32 {
 23:     if value.is_finite() {
 24:         value.clamp(limits.0, limits.1)
 25:     } else {
 26:         fallback
 27:     }
 28: }
 29: 
 30: impl CpuRenderSettings {
 31:     /// Returns a finite, bounded snapshot safe for traversal and allocation.
 32:     pub fn validated(mut self) -> Self {
 33:         let fallback = Self::default();
 34:         self.internal_scale = finite_clamp(
 35:             self.internal_scale,
 36:             fallback.internal_scale,
 37:             CpuSettingsLimits::INTERNAL_SCALE,
 38:         );
 39:         self.lod_cutoff_px = finite_clamp(
 40:             self.lod_cutoff_px,
 41:             fallback.lod_cutoff_px,
 42:             CpuSettingsLimits::LOD_CUTOFF_PX,
 43:         );
 44:         self.max_splat_radius_px = finite_clamp(
 45:             self.max_splat_radius_px,
 46:             fallback.max_splat_radius_px,
 47:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_PX,
 48:         );
 49:         self.max_virtual_depth = self.max_virtual_depth.clamp(
 50:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.0,
 51:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.1,
 52:         );
 53:         self.min_split_size = finite_clamp(
 54:             self.min_split_size,
 55:             fallback.min_split_size,
 56:             CpuSettingsLimits::MIN_SPLIT_SIZE,
 57:         );
 58:         self.max_draw_distance = finite_clamp(
 59:             self.max_draw_distance,
 60:             fallback.max_draw_distance,
 61:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE,
 62:         );
 63:         self.min_mip_occupancy = finite_clamp(
 64:             self.min_mip_occupancy,
 65:             fallback.min_mip_occupancy,
 66:             CpuSettingsLimits::MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY,
 67:         );
 68:         self.fov_tan = finite_clamp(self.fov_tan, fallback.fov_tan, CpuSettingsLimits::FOV_TAN);
 69:         self
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     /// CPU canvas size relative to the ordinary GPU canvas. The baseline is
 73:     /// deliberately one quarter per axis; presets scale from 12.5% to 50%.
 74:     pub fn canvas_resolution_factor(self) -> f64 {
 75:         (self.validated().internal_scale * 0.25) as f64
 76:     }
 77: }
 78: 
 79: #[cfg(test)]
 80: mod tests {
 81:     use super::*;
 82: 
 83:     #[test]
 84:     fn validation_clamps_every_untrusted_scalar() {
 85:         let settings = CpuRenderSettings {
 86:             internal_scale: f32::INFINITY,
 87:             lod_cutoff_px: -5.0,
 88:             max_splat_radius_px: 200.0,
 89:             max_virtual_depth: u8::MAX,
 90:             min_split_size: f32::NAN,
 91:             max_draw_distance: 10_000.0,
 92:             min_mip_occupancy: -2.0,

 95:         }
 96:         .validated();
 97: 
 98:         assert_eq!(settings.internal_scale, 1.0);
 99:         assert_eq!(settings.lod_cutoff_px, 0.25);
100:         assert_eq!(settings.max_splat_radius_px, 16.0);
101:         assert_eq!(settings.max_virtual_depth, 8);
102:         assert_eq!(settings.min_split_size, 0.005);
103:         assert_eq!(settings.max_draw_distance, 256.0);
104:         assert_eq!(settings.min_mip_occupancy, 0.0);
105:         assert_eq!(settings.fov_tan, 4.0);
106:     }
107: 
108:     #[test]

110:         let mut settings = CpuRenderSettings::default();
111:         settings.internal_scale = 0.25;
112:         assert_eq!(settings.canvas_resolution_factor(), 0.0625);
113:         settings.internal_scale = 1.0;
114:         assert_eq!(settings.canvas_resolution_factor(), 0.25);
115:         settings.internal_scale = 2.0;
116:         assert_eq!(settings.canvas_resolution_factor(), 0.5);
````

````rust
 1: //! Ambient visibility and the optional cached diffuse-fill contribution.
 2: //! Neither term owns direct-light, flashlight, emission, or atmosphere math.
 3: 
 4: use crate::application::ports::Environment;
 5: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 6: 
 7: use super::super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 8: use super::SplatSurface;
 9: 
10: const CACHED_FILL_GAIN: f32 = 0.12;
11: const INDOOR_AMBIENT: LinearRgb = [0.045, 0.040, 0.024];
12: const OUTDOOR_AMBIENT: LinearRgb = [0.32, 0.38, 0.48];
13: 
14: pub(super) fn ambient_irradiance(environment: &Environment) -> LinearRgb {
15:     let base = if environment.outdoor {
16:         OUTDOOR_AMBIENT
17:     } else {
18:         INDOOR_AMBIENT
19:     };
20:     base.map(|channel| channel * environment.ambient_scale.max(0.0))
21: }
22: 
23: /// Crowding is only an ambient-visibility approximation. Analytic lights,
24: /// flashlight visibility, and emission are never multiplied by it.
25: pub(super) fn ambient_visibility(crowded_siblings: u32) -> f32 {
26:     let neighbors = crowded_siblings.saturating_sub(1).min(7) as f32;
27:     (1.0 - 0.055 * neighbors).clamp(0.62, 1.0)
28: }
29: 
30: pub(super) fn cached_fill_irradiance(
31:     surface: &SplatSurface,
32:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
33: ) -> LinearRgb {
34:     if !settings.toggles.baked_lighting {
35:         return [0.0; 3];
36:     }
37:     surface
38:         .baked_irradiance
39:         .map(|channel| (channel / 15.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * CACHED_FILL_GAIN)
40: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/evaluate_dynamic_irradiance.rs

````rust
 1: //! Runtime point-light irradiance (currently dropped flares).
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 4: 
 5: use super::super::camera::Camera;
 6: use super::evaluate_fixture_irradiance::point_light_irradiance;
 7: 
 8: pub(super) fn dynamic_irradiance(
 9:     cam: &Camera,
10:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
11:     normal: [f32; 3],
12: ) -> LinearRgb {
13:     let mut sum = [0.0; 3];
14:     for light in &cam.dynamic_lights[..cam.dynamic_light_count] {
15:         let contribution = point_light_irradiance(
16:             surface_position,
17:             normal,
18:             light.position,
19:             light.color,
20:             light.radius,
21:             light.intensity,
22:         );
23:         for channel in 0..3 {
24:             sum[channel] += contribution[channel];
25:         }
26:     }
27:     sum
28: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Emitted radiance for exposed fixture undersides.
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 4: 
 5: use super::SplatSurface;
 6: 
 7: pub(crate) fn emission_strength(base_color: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
 8:     let near = |reference: [f32; 3]| {
 9:         base_color
10:             .into_iter()
11:             .zip(reference)
12:             .all(|(actual, expected)| (actual - expected).abs() <= 0.5)
13:     };
14:     if near([255.0, 248.0, 214.0]) {
15:         10.0
16:     } else if near([255.0, 68.0, 51.0]) {
17:         8.0
18:     } else if near([159.0, 196.0, 232.0]) {
19:         0.9
20:     } else {
21:         1.0
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: #[cfg(test)]
26: pub(super) fn emitted_radiance(
27:     surface: &SplatSurface,
28:     albedo: LinearRgb,
29:     normal: [f32; 3],
30: ) -> Option<LinearRgb> {
31:     emitted_radiance_with_strength(
32:         surface,
33:         albedo,
34:         normal,
35:         surface
36:             .is_emissive
37:             .then(|| emission_strength(surface.base_color)),
38:     )
39: }
40: 
41: /// Prepared-material variant used by production traversal. Its scalar comes
42: /// from the material id, so no encoded color has to travel through every
43: /// virtual-node visit merely to identify one of three fixture strengths.
44: pub(super) fn emitted_radiance_with_strength(
45:     surface: &SplatSurface,
46:     albedo: LinearRgb,
47:     normal: [f32; 3],
48:     strength: Option<f32>,
49: ) -> Option<LinearRgb> {
50:     if !surface.is_emissive || normal[1] >= -0.5 {
51:         return None;
52:     }
53:     Some(albedo.map(|channel| channel * strength.unwrap_or(1.0)))
54: }
````
