## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/evaluate_fixture_irradiance.rs
````rust
  1: //! Analytic static-fixture irradiance. Point emitters and finite rectangular
  2: //! ceiling emitters share one sanitized radiometric boundary.
  3: 
  4: use crate::application::ports::{LightKind, LightSource};
  5: use crate::application::rendering::{LinearRgb, finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation};
  6: 
  7: use super::super::camera::dot;
  8: use super::FrameLighting;
  9: use super::trace_direct_light_visibility::DirectLightVisibility;
 10: 
 11: const GAUSS_ABSCISSA: f32 = 0.577_350_26;
 12: const MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE: f32 = 0.2;
 13: 
 14: /// Exact zero test for the four quadrature samples. This is not a lighting
 15: /// approximation: it rejects work only when every sample is outside the
 16: /// finite support, behind the one-sided emitter, or behind the receiver.
 17: fn rectangle_can_contribute(
 18:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
 19:     normal: [f32; 3],
 20:     light: &LightSource,
 21: ) -> bool {
 22:     if !light.radius.is_finite() || light.radius <= 0.0 {
 23:         return false;
 24:     }
 25:     let center_delta = [
 26:         light.position[0] - surface_position[0],
 27:         light.position[1] - surface_position[1],
 28:         light.position[2] - surface_position[2],
 29:     ];
 30:     if center_delta
 31:         .into_iter()
 32:         .chain(normal)
 33:         .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
 34:     {
 35:         return false;
 36:     }
 37: 
 38:     // Every sample shares the emitter height. A horizontal panel emits only
 39:     // downward, so receivers level with or above it get exactly zero.
 40:     if center_delta[1] <= 0.0 {
 41:         return false;
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     let sample_extent_x = GAUSS_ABSCISSA * light.half_size[0];
 45:     let sample_extent_z = GAUSS_ABSCISSA * light.half_size[1];
 46:     let nearest_x = (center_delta[0].abs() - sample_extent_x).max(0.0);
 47:     let nearest_z = (center_delta[2].abs() - sample_extent_z).max(0.0);
 48:     let nearest_squared =
 49:         nearest_x * nearest_x + center_delta[1] * center_delta[1] + nearest_z * nearest_z;
 50:     if nearest_squared >= light.radius * light.radius {
 51:         return false;
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     // Dot products are affine over the sample rectangle, so this bound is
 55:     // the exact maximum receiver cosine numerator among its four corners.
 56:     let maximum_receiver_dot = dot(normal, center_delta)
 57:         + normal[0].abs() * sample_extent_x
 58:         + normal[2].abs() * sample_extent_z;
 59:     maximum_receiver_dot > 0.0
 60: }
 61: 
 62: fn sanitized_light_scale(color: LinearRgb, intensity: f32) -> LinearRgb {
 63:     if !intensity.is_finite() || intensity <= 0.0 {
 64:         return [0.0; 3];
 65:     }
 66:     color.map(|channel| {
 67:         if channel.is_finite() {
 68:             channel.max(0.0) * intensity
 69:         } else {
 70:             0.0
 71:         }
 72:     })
 73: }
 74: 
 75: fn normalized(vector: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
 76:     if vector.into_iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
 77:         return None;
 78:     }
 79:     let scale = vector
 80:         .into_iter()
 81:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
 82:     if scale == 0.0 {
 83:         return None;
 84:     }
 85:     let scaled = vector.map(|component| component / scale);
 86:     let length = dot(scaled, scaled).sqrt();
 87:     Some(scaled.map(|component| component / length))
 88: }
 89: 
 90: /// Reuses the one surface-to-light normalization for every geometric term.
 91: /// The generic rendering helpers normalize each argument independently;
 92: /// doing that twice per Gauss sample is mathematically redundant and was the
 93: /// dominant arithmetic cost in fixture-heavy CPU frames.
 94: pub(super) fn sample_geometry(
 95:     receiver_normal: [f32; 3],
 96:     surface_to_light: [f32; 3],
 97: ) -> Option<(f32, f32, f32)> {
 98:     let distance = dot(surface_to_light, surface_to_light).sqrt();
 99:     if !distance.is_finite() || distance <= 0.0 {
100:         return None;
101:     }
102:     let inverse_distance = 1.0 / distance;
103:     let direction = surface_to_light.map(|component| component * inverse_distance);
104:     let receiver_cosine = dot(receiver_normal, direction).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
105:     // Horizontal rectangular fixtures point down. For direction L from the
106:     // receiver to the light, dot(-Y, direction_light_to_receiver) == L.y.
107:     let downward_emitter_cosine = direction[1].clamp(0.0, 1.0);
108:     Some((distance, receiver_cosine, downward_emitter_cosine))
109: }
110: 
111: pub(super) fn point_light_irradiance(
112:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
113:     normal: [f32; 3],
114:     light_position: [f32; 3],
115:     color: LinearRgb,
116:     range: f32,
117:     intensity: f32,
118: ) -> LinearRgb {
119:     let delta = [
120:         light_position[0] - surface_position[0],
121:         light_position[1] - surface_position[1],
122:         light_position[2] - surface_position[2],
123:     ];
124:     let distance_squared = dot(delta, delta);
125:     if !range.is_finite()
126:         || range <= 0.0
127:         || !distance_squared.is_finite()
128:         || distance_squared >= range * range
129:     {
130:         return [0.0; 3];
131:     }
132:     let Some(normal) = normalized(normal) else {
133:         return [0.0; 3];
134:     };
135:     let Some((distance, geometry, _)) = sample_geometry(normal, delta) else {
136:         return [0.0; 3];
137:     };
138:     let attenuation =
139:         finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(distance, range, MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE);
140:     let scale = sanitized_light_scale(color, intensity);
141:     scale.map(|channel| channel * geometry * attenuation)
142: }
143: 
144: /// Deterministic 2x2 Gauss quadrature over a physical XZ rectangle.
145: #[cfg(test)]
146: pub(super) fn rectangle_light_irradiance(
147:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
148:     normal: [f32; 3],
149:     light: &LightSource,
150: ) -> LinearRgb {
151:     rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(
152:         surface_position,
153:         normal,
154:         light,
155:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded(),
156:     )
157: }
158: 
159: fn rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(
160:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
161:     normal: [f32; 3],
162:     light: &LightSource,
163:     visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
164: ) -> LinearRgb {
165:     let [half_x, half_z] = light.half_size;
166:     if !half_x.is_finite() || !half_z.is_finite() || half_x <= 0.0 || half_z <= 0.0 {
167:         return [0.0; 3];
168:     }
169:     if !rectangle_can_contribute(surface_position, normal, light) {
170:         return [0.0; 3];
171:     }
172:     let mut integral = 0.0;
173:     for x in [-GAUSS_ABSCISSA, GAUSS_ABSCISSA] {
174:         for z in [-GAUSS_ABSCISSA, GAUSS_ABSCISSA] {
175:             let sample = [
176:                 light.position[0] + x * half_x,
177:                 light.position[1],
178:                 light.position[2] + z * half_z,
179:             ];
180:             let surface_to_light = [
181:                 sample[0] - surface_position[0],
182:                 sample[1] - surface_position[1],
183:                 sample[2] - surface_position[2],
184:             ];
185:             let Some((distance, receiver_cosine, emitter_cosine)) =
186:                 sample_geometry(normal, surface_to_light)
187:             else {
188:                 continue;
189:             };
190:             if receiver_cosine <= 0.0
191:                 || emitter_cosine <= 0.0
192:                 || !visibility.sample_is_visible(surface_position, normal, sample)
193:             {
194:                 continue;
195:             }
196:             integral += receiver_cosine
197:                 * emitter_cosine
198:                 * finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(
199:                     distance,
200:                     light.radius,
201:                     MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE,
202:                 );
203:         }
204:     }
205:     let area = 4.0 * half_x * half_z;
206:     let scale = sanitized_light_scale(light.color, light.intensity);
207:     scale.map(|channel| channel * area * integral * 0.25)
208: }
209: 
210: fn scene_light_irradiance(
211:     light: &LightSource,
212:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
213:     normal: [f32; 3],
214:     visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
215: ) -> LinearRgb {
216:     if !light.enabled {
217:         return [0.0; 3];
218:     }
219:     match light.kind {
220:         LightKind::Point => {
221:             let contribution = point_light_irradiance(
222:                 surface_position,
223:                 normal,
224:                 light.position,
225:                 light.color,
226:                 light.radius,
227:                 light.intensity,
228:             );
229:             if contribution != [0.0; 3]
230:                 && !visibility.sample_is_visible(surface_position, normal, light.position)
231:             {
232:                 [0.0; 3]
233:             } else {
234:                 contribution
235:             }
236:         }
237:         LightKind::CeilingPanel | LightKind::Strip | LightKind::Emergency => {
238:             rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(surface_position, normal, light, visibility)
239:         }
240:     }
241: }
242: 
243: #[cfg(test)]
244: pub(super) fn fixture_irradiance(
245:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
246:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
247:     normal: [f32; 3],
248: ) -> LinearRgb {
249:     fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(
250:         lighting,
251:         surface_position,
252:         normal,
253:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded(),
254:     )
255: }
256: 
257: pub(super) fn fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(
258:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
259:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
260:     normal: [f32; 3],
261:     direct_visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
262: ) -> LinearRgb {
263:     let mut sum = [0.0; 3];
264:     for light in lighting.scene_lights {
265:         let visibility = lighting
266:             .hero_visibility
267:             .filter(|hero| hero.light_id == light.id)
268:             .map_or(1.0, |hero| hero.visibility.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
269:         let contribution =
270:             scene_light_irradiance(light, surface_position, normal, direct_visibility);
271:         for channel in 0..3 {
272:             sum[channel] += contribution[channel] * visibility;
273:         }
274:     }
275:     sum
276: }

362:         }];
363:         let partial = rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(
364:             receiver,
365:             normal,
366:             &light,
367:             DirectLightVisibility::trace_scene(&atlas, &chunks, 0.5),
368:         );
369: 
370:         assert!(partial[0] > 0.0);
371:         assert!(partial[0] < unoccluded[0]);
372:     }
373: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/mod.rs
````rust
 1: //! Linear-radiance shading for one CPU splat.
 2: //!
 3: //! The file tree is the rendering sentence:
 4: //!
 5: //! 1. [`surface_reconstruction`] selects one physical receiver sample;
 6: //! 2. [`compose_environment_irradiance`], [`evaluate_fixture_irradiance`],
 7: //!    and [`evaluate_dynamic_irradiance`] build independent light terms;
 8: //! 3. [`evaluate_emission`] handles exposed luminous panel undersides;
 9: //! 4. [`shade_visible_splat`] composes reflection and flashlight energy;
10: //! 5. [`present_radiance`] applies atmosphere and display encoding once.
11: //!
12: //! Static fixtures in [`FrameLighting`] are authoritative. The quantized SVO
13: //! light level is an optional, restrained fill and cannot replace them.
14: 
15: mod compose_environment_irradiance;
16: mod evaluate_dynamic_irradiance;
17: mod evaluate_emission;
18: mod evaluate_fixture_irradiance;
19: mod present_radiance;
20: mod shade_visible_splat;
21: mod surface_reconstruction;
22: mod trace_direct_light_visibility;
23: 
24: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
25: 
26: use super::surface_geometry::SurfaceExposure;
27: 
28: #[cfg(test)]
29: pub(crate) use evaluate_emission::emission_strength;
30: pub(crate) use shade_visible_splat::shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting;
31: pub use shade_visible_splat::shade_with_frame_lighting;
32: 
33: /// Everything the lighting model needs to know about one splat.
34: pub struct SplatSurface {
35:     /// World-space center of the shaded box.
36:     pub center: [f32; 3],
37:     /// World-space side length of the box.
38:     pub world_size: f32,
39:     /// Camera-space depth used by projection/depth testing. Fog recomputes
40:     /// the Euclidean path length from `center`; depth is not a path length.
41:     pub dist: f32,
42:     /// Authored sRGB albedo, 0..255 per channel.
43:     pub base_color: [f32; 3],
44:     /// Quantized colored cached diffuse-fill channels, 0..15. Analytic
45:     /// fixtures remain authoritative; this optional field is never promoted
46:     /// to direct light.
47:     pub baked_irradiance: [f32; 3],
48:     /// Authored voxel material. Thin architectural materials use this to
49:     /// preserve their physical orientation instead of behaving like cubes.
50:     pub voxel_type: u32,
51:     pub is_emissive: bool,
52:     /// Prepared physical surface area open to air. Shading may choose among
53:     /// these faces but must never invent a face outside this contract.
54:     pub exposure: SurfaceExposure,
55:     /// Number of occupied siblings in the parent octant (ambient AO proxy).
56:     pub crowded_siblings: u32,
57: }
58: 
59: /// Visibility of one specific analytic fixture at the current receiver.
60: /// Keeping the light id beside the factor prevents an assumed-grid shadow
61: /// from accidentally darkening ambient or a different fixture.
62: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
63: pub struct HeroLightVisibility {
64:     pub light_id: u64,
65:     pub visibility: f32,
66: }
67: 
68: /// Immutable per-frame fixture inputs plus the one per-receiver hero query.
69: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
70: pub struct FrameLighting<'a> {
71:     pub scene_lights: &'a [LightSource],
72:     pub hero_visibility: Option<HeroLightVisibility>,
73: }
74: 
75: impl<'a> FrameLighting<'a> {
76:     pub fn unshadowed(scene_lights: &'a [LightSource]) -> Self {
77:         Self {
78:             scene_lights,
79:             hero_visibility: None,
80:         }
81:     }
82: 
83:     pub fn with_hero_visibility(
84:         scene_lights: &'a [LightSource],
85:         light_id: u64,
86:         visibility: f32,
87:     ) -> Self {
88:         Self {
89:             scene_lights,
90:             hero_visibility: Some(HeroLightVisibility {
91:                 light_id,
92:                 visibility: visibility.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
93:             }),
94:         }
95:     }
96: }
97: 
98: #[cfg(test)]
99: mod tests;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/present_radiance.rs
````rust
 1: //! Compose the level atmosphere in linear RGB, tone-map, and encode once.
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::ports::Environment;
 4: use crate::application::rendering::{
 5:     LinearRgb, compose_fog, encode_display_color, fog_transmittance,
 6: };
 7: 
 8: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 9: use super::SplatSurface;
10: 
11: pub(super) fn view_distance(
12:     cam: &Camera,
13:     surface: &SplatSurface,
14:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
15: ) -> f32 {
16:     let delta = [
17:         surface_position[0] - cam.pos[0],
18:         surface_position[1] - cam.pos[1],
19:         surface_position[2] - cam.pos[2],
20:     ];
21:     let distance = dot(delta, delta).sqrt();
22:     if distance.is_finite() {
23:         distance
24:     } else {
25:         surface.dist.max(0.0)
26:     }
27: }
28: 
29: pub(super) fn present_radiance(
30:     radiance: LinearRgb,
31:     distance: f32,
32:     environment: &Environment,
33: ) -> [u8; 3] {
34:     let transmittance = fog_transmittance(distance, environment.fog_start, environment.fog_density);
35:     let through_fog = compose_fog(radiance, environment.fog_color, transmittance);
36:     encode_display_color(through_fog)
37:         .map(|channel| (channel * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8)
38: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/shade_visible_splat.rs
````rust
  1: //! Facade for one complete visible-splat shading evaluation.
  2: 
  3: use std::f32::consts::PI;
  4: 
  5: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, Environment};
  6: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
  7: 
  8: use super::super::camera::Camera;
  9: use super::super::flashlight;
 10: use super::super::settings::{CpuRenderSettings, CpuShadowMode};
 11: use super::compose_environment_irradiance::{
 12:     ambient_irradiance, ambient_visibility, cached_fill_irradiance,
 13: };
 14: use super::evaluate_dynamic_irradiance::dynamic_irradiance;
 15: use super::evaluate_emission::{emission_strength, emitted_radiance_with_strength};
 16: use super::evaluate_fixture_irradiance::fixture_irradiance_with_visibility;
 17: use super::present_radiance::{present_radiance, view_distance};
 18: use super::surface_reconstruction::{
 19:     decode_albedo, representative_normal, representative_surface_position,
 20: };
 21: use super::trace_direct_light_visibility::DirectLightVisibility;
 22: use super::{FrameLighting, SplatSurface};
 23: 
 24: /// Correctness path with the complete analytic fixture contract.
 25: pub fn shade_with_frame_lighting(
 26:     cam: &Camera,
 27:     environment: &Environment,
 28:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
 29:     atlas: &[u32],
 30:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 31:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
 32:     surface: &SplatSurface,
 33: ) -> [u8; 3] {
 34:     shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting(
 35:         cam,
 36:         environment,
 37:         settings,
 38:         atlas,
 39:         chunks,
 40:         lighting,
 41:         surface,
 42:         decode_albedo(surface.base_color),
 43:         surface
 44:             .is_emissive
 45:             .then(|| emission_strength(surface.base_color)),
 46:     )
 47: }
 48: 
 49: /// Hot production path. Atlas upload already decoded authored sRGB and MIP
 50: /// filtering already averaged in linear space, so shading consumes the
 51: /// prepared albedo without repeating transfer-function powers per splat.
 52: pub(crate) fn shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting(
 53:     cam: &Camera,
 54:     environment: &Environment,
 55:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
 56:     atlas: &[u32],
 57:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 58:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
 59:     surface: &SplatSurface,
 60:     albedo: LinearRgb,
 61:     emission_strength: Option<f32>,
 62: ) -> [u8; 3] {
 63:     let camera_to_surface = [
 64:         surface.center[0] - cam.pos[0],
 65:         surface.center[1] - cam.pos[1],
 66:         surface.center[2] - cam.pos[2],
 67:     ];
 68:     let reconstructed_normal = representative_normal(surface, camera_to_surface);
 69:     let normal = reconstructed_normal.unwrap_or([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]);
 70:     let surface_position =
 71:         representative_surface_position(surface.center, surface.world_size, normal);
 72:     let distance = view_distance(cam, surface, surface_position);
 73: 
 74:     if let Some(emission) =
 75:         emitted_radiance_with_strength(surface, albedo, normal, emission_strength)
 76:     {
 77:         return present_radiance(emission, distance, environment);
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     let ambient_visibility = if settings.toggles.ambient_occlusion {
 81:         ambient_visibility(surface.crowded_siblings)
 82:     } else {
 83:         1.0
 84:     };
 85:     let mut irradiance =
 86:         ambient_irradiance(environment).map(|channel| channel * ambient_visibility);
 87:     let cached =
 88:         cached_fill_irradiance(surface, settings).map(|channel| channel * ambient_visibility);
 89:     let direct_visibility = if settings.shadows == CpuShadowMode::Full {
 90:         DirectLightVisibility::trace_scene(atlas, chunks, surface.world_size)
 91:     } else {
 92:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded()
 93:     };
 94:     let fixtures =
 95:         fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(lighting, surface_position, normal, direct_visibility);
 96:     let dynamics = dynamic_irradiance(cam, surface_position, normal);
 97:     let flashlight = if cam.flashlight && reconstructed_normal.is_some() {
 98:         flashlight::beam_contribution(
 99:             cam,
100:             atlas,
101:             chunks,
102:             flashlight::BeamReceiver::surface_sample(
103:                 surface.center,
104:                 surface.world_size,
105:                 surface_position,
106:                 normal,
107:             ),
108:             settings.flashlight_visibility(),
109:         )
110:     } else {
111:         [0.0; 3]
112:     };
113: 
114:     for channel in 0..3 {
115:         irradiance[channel] +=
116:             cached[channel] + fixtures[channel] + dynamics[channel] + flashlight[channel];
117:     }
118:     let reflected = [
119:         albedo[0] * irradiance[0] / PI,
120:         albedo[1] * irradiance[1] / PI,
121:         albedo[2] * irradiance[2] / PI,
122:     ];
123:     present_radiance(reflected, distance, environment)
124: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/surface_reconstruction.rs
````rust
 1: //! Reconstruct one representative point and normal from an axis-aligned
 2: //! splat, then decode its authored albedo into linear RGB.
 3: 
 4: pub(super) use super::super::decode_srgb_albedo::decode_albedo;
 5: #[cfg(test)]
 6: pub(super) use super::super::decode_srgb_albedo::srgb_channel_to_linear;
 7: pub(super) use super::super::surface_geometry::representative_surface_position;
 8: use super::super::surface_geometry::select_surface_normal;
 9: use super::SplatSurface;
10: 
11: /// Exact normal of the AABB face entered by the center-directed camera ray.
12: /// For a centered cube this is the dominant ray axis. Ties use X, then Y,
13: /// then Z, making edge/corner views deterministic without inventing a
14: /// diagonal receiver cosine.
15: #[cfg(test)]
16: pub(super) fn camera_facing_aabb_normal(camera_to_surface: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
17:     if camera_to_surface
18:         .into_iter()
19:         .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
20:     {
21:         return None;
22:     }
23:     let absolute = camera_to_surface.map(f32::abs);
24:     let axis = if absolute[0] >= absolute[1] && absolute[0] >= absolute[2] {
25:         0
26:     } else if absolute[1] >= absolute[2] {
27:         1
28:     } else {
29:         2
30:     };
31:     if absolute[axis] <= 1.0e-6 {
32:         return None;
33:     }
34:     let mut normal = [0.0; 3];
35:     normal[axis] = if camera_to_surface[axis] > 0.0 {
36:         -1.0
37:     } else {
38:         1.0
39:     };
40:     Some(normal)
41: }
42: 
43: /// Selects one actual exposed face, with authored orientation for floor,
44: /// ceiling, and emissive panel materials. Camera dominance is used only for
45: /// cube-like materials and only among faces present in the geometry contract.
46: pub(super) fn representative_normal(
47:     surface: &SplatSurface,
48:     camera_to_surface: [f32; 3],
49: ) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
50:     select_surface_normal(
51:         surface.voxel_type,
52:         surface.is_emissive,
53:         surface.exposure,
54:         camera_to_surface,
55:     )
56: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/trace_direct_light_visibility.rs
````rust
 1: //! Exact finite SVO visibility segments for analytic fixture samples.
 2: //!
 3: //! The expensive CPU `Full` shadow policy calls this once for a point light
 4: //! and once for each of a rectangle's four Gauss samples. Receiver and
 5: //! emitter biases mirror the strict GPU raymarch reference so neither the
 6: //! receiver voxel nor the luminous endpoint shadows itself.
 7: 
 8: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 9: 
10: use super::super::camera::dot;
11: use super::super::raycast::svo_segment_is_occluded;
12: 
13: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
14: pub(super) struct DirectLightVisibility<'a> {
15:     atlas: &'a [u32],
16:     chunks: &'a [ChunkDraw],
17:     receiver_world_size: f32,
18:     trace_scene: bool,
19: }
20: 
21: impl<'a> DirectLightVisibility<'a> {
22:     pub(super) fn unoccluded() -> Self {
23:         Self {
24:             atlas: &[],
25:             chunks: &[],
26:             receiver_world_size: 0.0,
27:             trace_scene: false,
28:         }
29:     }
30: 
31:     pub(super) fn trace_scene(
32:         atlas: &'a [u32],
33:         chunks: &'a [ChunkDraw],
34:         receiver_world_size: f32,
35:     ) -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             atlas,
38:             chunks,
39:             receiver_world_size,
40:             trace_scene: true,
41:         }
42:     }
43: 
44:     pub(super) fn sample_is_visible(
45:         self,
46:         surface_position: [f32; 3],
47:         surface_normal: [f32; 3],
48:         sample_position: [f32; 3],
49:     ) -> bool {
50:         if !self.trace_scene {
51:             return true;
52:         }
53: 
54:         let bias = (self.receiver_world_size.abs() * 1.0e-3).max(1.0e-5);
55:         let origin = [
56:             surface_position[0] + surface_normal[0] * bias,
57:             surface_position[1] + surface_normal[1] * bias,
58:             surface_position[2] + surface_normal[2] * bias,
59:         ];
60:         let segment = [
61:             sample_position[0] - origin[0],
62:             sample_position[1] - origin[1],
63:             sample_position[2] - origin[2],
64:         ];
65:         let segment_length = dot(segment, segment).sqrt();
66:         if !segment_length.is_finite() || segment_length <= bias * 2.0 {
67:             return true;
68:         }
69:         let inverse_length = 1.0 / segment_length;
70:         let direction = segment.map(|component| component * inverse_length);
71:         let blocker_limit = segment_length - bias * 2.0;
72:         !svo_segment_is_occluded(self.atlas, self.chunks, origin, direction, blocker_limit)
73:     }
74: }
75:

80:

83:         let atlas = [1, 1, 0x00ff_ffff, 0];
84:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
85:             origin: [0.0; 3],
86:             root_index: 0,
87:             world_size: 1.0,
88:             voxel_size: 1.0,
89:             svo_depth: 0,
90:         }];
91:         let visibility = DirectLightVisibility::trace_scene(&atlas, &chunks, 0.5);
92: 
93:         assert!(!visibility.sample_is_visible([0.5, 0.5, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], [0.5, 0.5, 2.0],));
94:         assert!(
95:             visibility.sample_is_visible([0.5, 0.5, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], [0.5, 0.5, -0.25],)
96:         );
97:     }
98: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/project_surface_depth.rs
````rust
  1: //! Project one selected box face into an exact per-pixel depth plane.
  2: //!
  3: //! A square splat covers more screen pixels than the projected voxel face.
  4: //! Giving that whole square the voxel-center depth makes adjacent coplanar
  5: //! voxels disagree about the depth of the same physical plane.  The error is
  6: //! especially visible when a ceiling voxel overlaps a luminous panel.
  7: //!
  8: //! For a pinhole camera, reciprocal camera depth on a world-space plane is
  9: //! affine in screen coordinates.  The three coefficients below therefore
 10: //! recover the exact ray/plane intersection depth at every pixel without a
 11: //! per-pixel world-space ray construction.
 12: 
 13: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 14: use super::{SurfaceExposure, select_surface_normal};
 15: 
 16: /// Camera-depth information for one selected physical box face.
 17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 18: pub(crate) struct ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
 19:     representative_depth: f32,
 20:     /// `1 / depth = ax + by + c`, evaluated at pixel centers.
 21:     reciprocal_depth: [f32; 3],
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
 25:     /// Constant-depth constructor retained for non-surface flare splats and
 26:     /// narrow renderer tests. Production voxel surfaces use [`project_surface_depth`].
 27:     pub(crate) fn constant(depth: f32) -> Self {
 28:         Self {
 29:             representative_depth: depth,
 30:             reciprocal_depth: [0.0, 0.0, depth.recip()],
 31:         }
 32:     }
 33: 
 34:     pub(crate) fn representative_depth(self) -> f32 {
 35:         self.representative_depth
 36:     }
 37: 
 38:     /// Exact positive reciprocal camera depth at a target-space sample.
 39:     /// Fine depth comparison consumes this directly, avoiding a division for
 40:     /// every candidate pixel.
 41:     pub(crate) fn reciprocal_at_pixel(self, pixel: [f32; 2]) -> Option<f32> {
 42:         let inverse_depth = self.reciprocal_depth[0].mul_add(
 43:             pixel[0],
 44:             self.reciprocal_depth[1].mul_add(pixel[1], self.reciprocal_depth[2]),
 45:         );
 46:         if !inverse_depth.is_finite() || inverse_depth <= 0.0 {
 47:             return None;
 48:         }
 49:         Some(inverse_depth)
 50:     }
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Selects one exposed face and projects its plane into target space.
 54: pub(crate) fn project_surface_depth(
 55:     camera: &Camera,
 56:     center: [f32; 3],
 57:     world_size: f32,
 58:     voxel_type: u32,
 59:     is_emissive: bool,
 60:     exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 61: ) -> Option<ProjectedSurfaceDepth> {
 62:     let camera_to_surface = [
 63:         center[0] - camera.pos[0],
 64:         center[1] - camera.pos[1],
 65:         center[2] - camera.pos[2],
 66:     ];
 67:     let normal = select_surface_normal(voxel_type, is_emissive, exposure, camera_to_surface)?;
 68:     let position = representative_surface_position(center, world_size, normal);
 69:     let position_from_camera = [
 70:         position[0] - camera.pos[0],
 71:         position[1] - camera.pos[1],
 72:         position[2] - camera.pos[2],
 73:     ];
 74:     let representative_depth = dot(position_from_camera, camera.forward);
 75:     let plane_offset = dot(normal, position_from_camera);
 76:     if !representative_depth.is_finite()
 77:         || representative_depth <= 0.0
 78:         || !plane_offset.is_finite()
 79:         || plane_offset.abs() <= 1.0e-8
 80:         || !camera.focal_px.is_finite()
 81:         || camera.focal_px <= 0.0
 82:     {
 83:         return None;
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     let normal_right = dot(normal, camera.right);
 87:     let normal_up = dot(normal, camera.up);
 88:     let reciprocal_scale = (camera.focal_px * plane_offset).recip();
 89:     let reciprocal_depth = [
 90:         normal_right * reciprocal_scale,
 91:         -normal_up * reciprocal_scale,
 92:         dot(normal, camera.forward) / plane_offset
 93:             + (-normal_right * camera.half_w + normal_up * camera.half_h) * reciprocal_scale,
 94:     ];
 95:     if reciprocal_depth
 96:         .into_iter()
 97:         .any(|coefficient| !coefficient.is_finite())
 98:     {
 99:         return None;
100:     }
101: 
102:     Some(ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
103:         representative_depth,
104:         reciprocal_depth,
105:     })
106: }
107: 
108: /// Intersects the normal ray from the box center with the AABB boundary.
109: /// Lighting and fine depth both use this same physical surface sample.
110: pub(crate) fn representative_surface_position(
111:     center: [f32; 3],
112:     world_size: f32,
113:     normal: [f32; 3],
114: ) -> [f32; 3] {
115:     let dominant = normal
116:         .into_iter()
117:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
118:     if !world_size.is_finite() || world_size <= 0.0 || dominant <= 1.0e-6 {
119:         return center;
120:     }
121:     let distance_to_boundary = world_size * 0.5 / dominant;
122:     [
123:         center[0] + normal[0] * distance_to_boundary,
124:         center[1] + normal[1] * distance_to_boundary,
125:         center[2] + normal[2] * distance_to_boundary,
126:     ]
127: }
128:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/propagate_exposure_to_octant.rs
````rust
 1: //! Propagate exposed parent and sibling boundaries into one octant.
 2: 
 3: use super::{SurfaceExposure, SurfaceFace};
 4: 
 5: /// Surface area visible on one occupied child octant.
 6: ///
 7: /// A face on the parent's outside inherits that parent's prepared exposure.
 8: /// A face inside the parent is exposed only when the adjacent sibling is
 9: /// absent from the occupancy mask. Passing `0xff` for a virtually subdivided
10: /// solid leaf is important: artificial children then inherit the real box's
11: /// exterior, but their internal cut planes stay closed.
12: pub(crate) fn exposure_for_octant(
13:     parent: SurfaceExposure,
14:     occupied_siblings: u32,
15:     octant: u32,
16: ) -> SurfaceExposure {
17:     debug_assert!(octant < 8);
18:     let mut result = SurfaceExposure::NONE;
19: 
20:     for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
21:         let bit = face.axis_bit();
22:         let child_on_positive_side = octant & bit != 0;
23:         let child_on_parent_face = child_on_positive_side == face.is_positive();
24:         let area = if child_on_parent_face {
25:             parent.area(face)
26:         } else {
27:             let adjacent_octant = octant ^ bit;
28:             if occupied_siblings & (1 << adjacent_octant) == 0 {
29:                 255
30:             } else {
31:                 0
32:             }
33:         };
34:         result.set_area(face, area);
35:     }
36: 
37:     result
38: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/select_surface_normal.rs
````rust
 1: //! Choose a lighting normal from prepared surface geometry.
 2: 
 3: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 4:     VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GRASS,
 5:     VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_WATER,
 6: };
 7: 
 8: use super::{SurfaceExposure, SurfaceFace};
 9: 
10: /// Material semantics orient thin architectural layers.
11: ///
12: /// Floors and carpets are authored walking surfaces, while ceiling voxels
13: /// are authored undersides. Cube-like walls deliberately return no hint and
14: /// use the most camera-visible exposed face instead.
15: fn material_face(voxel_type: u32, is_emissive: bool) -> Option<SurfaceFace> {
16:     if is_emissive {
17:         return Some(SurfaceFace::NegativeY);
18:     }
19:     let voxel_type = u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok()?;
20:     match voxel_type {
21:         VOXEL_FLOOR | VOXEL_DRY_CARPET | VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET | VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET | VOXEL_GRASS
22:         | VOXEL_WATER | VOXEL_FLUID => Some(SurfaceFace::PositiveY),
23:         VOXEL_CEILING => Some(SurfaceFace::NegativeY),
24:         _ => None,
25:     }
26: }
27: 
28: /// Select one exact axis normal that belongs to an exposed physical face.
29: ///
30: /// Thin-layer material orientation wins when that authored face is exposed;
31: /// this is why a floor in front of a mostly-horizontal camera remains a floor
32: /// and receives overhead Lambertian light. Generic cube materials choose the
33: /// exposed face with the largest positive surface-to-camera cosine. Area is
34: /// the deterministic tie-breaker and improves coarse MIP choices.
35: pub(crate) fn select_surface_normal(
36:     voxel_type: u32,
37:     is_emissive: bool,
38:     exposure: SurfaceExposure,
39:     camera_to_surface: [f32; 3],
40: ) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
41:     if exposure.is_empty()
42:         || camera_to_surface
43:             .into_iter()
44:             .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
45:     {
46:         return None;
47:     }
48: 
49:     if let Some(face) = material_face(voxel_type, is_emissive) {
50:         let normal = face.normal();
51:         let facing = -(normal[0] * camera_to_surface[0]
52:             + normal[1] * camera_to_surface[1]
53:             + normal[2] * camera_to_surface[2]);
54:         if exposure.contains(face) && facing > 1.0e-6 {
55:             return Some(face.normal());
56:         }
57:     }
58: 
59:     let mut best: Option<(f32, u8, SurfaceFace)> = None;
60:     for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
61:         let area = exposure.area(face);
62:         if area == 0 {
63:             continue;
64:         }
65:         let normal = face.normal();
66:         let facing = -(normal[0] * camera_to_surface[0]
67:             + normal[1] * camera_to_surface[1]
68:             + normal[2] * camera_to_surface[2]);
69:         if facing <= 1.0e-6 {
70:             continue;
71:         }
72:         let candidate = (facing, area, face);
73:         let replace = best.is_none_or(|current| {
74:             candidate.0 > current.0 || (candidate.0 == current.0 && candidate.1 > current.1)
75:         });
76:         if replace {
77:             best = Some(candidate);
78:         }
79:     }
80:     best.map(|(_, _, face)| face.normal())
81: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/surface_exposure.rs
````rust
  1: //! Compact directional surface-area data.
  2: 
  3: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  4:     FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z,
  5:     FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z,
  6: };
  7: 
  8: /// Stable direction order shared by traversal and MIP preparation.
  9: ///
 10: /// The discriminants index [`SurfaceExposure`]'s six bytes. Keeping the
 11: /// normal here makes it impossible for propagation and shading to disagree
 12: /// about bit/axis conventions.
 13: #[repr(u8)]
 14: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 15: pub enum SurfaceFace {
 16:     NegativeX = 0,
 17:     PositiveX = 1,
 18:     NegativeY = 2,
 19:     PositiveY = 3,
 20:     NegativeZ = 4,
 21:     PositiveZ = 5,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl SurfaceFace {
 25:     pub const ALL: [Self; 6] = [
 26:         Self::NegativeX,
 27:         Self::PositiveX,
 28:         Self::NegativeY,
 29:         Self::PositiveY,
 30:         Self::NegativeZ,
 31:         Self::PositiveZ,
 32:     ];
 33: 
 34:     pub const fn normal(self) -> [f32; 3] {
 35:         match self {
 36:             Self::NegativeX => [-1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 37:             Self::PositiveX => [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 38:             Self::NegativeY => [0.0, -1.0, 0.0],
 39:             Self::PositiveY => [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],
 40:             Self::NegativeZ => [0.0, 0.0, -1.0],
 41:             Self::PositiveZ => [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
 42:         }
 43:     }
 44: 
 45:     pub const fn opposite(self) -> Self {
 46:         match self {
 47:             Self::NegativeX => Self::PositiveX,
 48:             Self::PositiveX => Self::NegativeX,
 49:             Self::NegativeY => Self::PositiveY,
 50:             Self::PositiveY => Self::NegativeY,
 51:             Self::NegativeZ => Self::PositiveZ,
 52:             Self::PositiveZ => Self::NegativeZ,
 53:         }
 54:     }
 55: 
 56:     pub(super) const fn axis_bit(self) -> u32 {
 57:         match self {
 58:             Self::NegativeX | Self::PositiveX => 1,
 59:             Self::NegativeY | Self::PositiveY => 2,
 60:             Self::NegativeZ | Self::PositiveZ => 4,
 61:         }
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     pub(super) const fn is_positive(self) -> bool {
 65:         matches!(self, Self::PositiveX | Self::PositiveY | Self::PositiveZ)
 66:     }
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Exposed area in each axis direction, normalized to one node face.
 70: ///
 71: /// `0` means no known surface in that direction and `255` means one complete
 72: /// node face. MIP preparation may use intermediate values or saturate above
 73: /// one node-face worth of internal surface. Six bytes per node are enough to
 74: /// preserve orientation without putting floats in the atlas-side cache.
 75: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 76: pub struct SurfaceExposure {
 77:     area: [u8; 6],
 78: }
 79: 
 80: impl SurfaceExposure {
 81:     pub const NONE: Self = Self { area: [0; 6] };
 82:     pub const ALL_FACES: Self = Self { area: [255; 6] };
 83: 
 84:     pub const fn from_area(area: [u8; 6]) -> Self {
 85:         Self { area }
 86:     }
 87: 
 88:     /// Decodes the authoritative six neighbor bits carried by a real atlas
 89:     /// leaf. Clear occupancy means air, hence a fully exposed face.
 90:     pub const fn from_neighbor_occlusion(mask: u8) -> Self {
 91:         Self::from_area([
 92:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X),
 93:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X),
 94:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y),
 95:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y),
 96:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z),
 97:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z),
 98:         ])
 99:     }
100: 
101:     pub fn area(self, face: SurfaceFace) -> u8 {
102:         self.area[face as usize]
103:     }
104: 
105:     pub fn contains(self, face: SurfaceFace) -> bool {
106:         self.area(face) != 0
107:     }
108: 
109:     pub(super) fn set_area(&mut self, face: SurfaceFace, area: u8) {
110:         self.area[face as usize] = area;
111:     }
112: 
113:     pub(crate) fn add_saturating(&mut self, other: Self) {
114:         for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
115:             let index = face as usize;
116:             self.area[index] = self.area[index].saturating_add(other.area[index]);
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub(super) fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
121:         self.area == [0; 6]
122:     }
123: 
124:     /// Directional area of a child subtree expressed in parent-face units.
125:     /// One octant face has one quarter of its parent's face area.
126:     pub(crate) fn scaled_to_parent(self) -> Self {
127:         Self::from_area(self.area.map(|area| ((u16::from(area) + 2) / 4) as u8))
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: const fn exposed_area(mask: u8, neighbor_bit: u8) -> u8 {
132:     if mask & neighbor_bit == 0 { 255 } else { 0 }
133: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/decode_srgb_albedo.rs
````rust
 1: //! Decode authored 8-bit sRGB albedo at data-preparation boundaries.
 2: //!
 3: //! Production splats carry this linear value from the per-upload atlas/MIP
 4: //! pass, so the hot shading loop never evaluates three transfer-function
 5: //! powers. Reference callers that begin with an encoded color use the same
 6: //! functions and therefore retain exactly the same radiometric contract.
 7: 
 8: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 9: 
10: pub(crate) fn srgb_channel_to_linear(byte: f32) -> f32 {
11:     let encoded = (byte / 255.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
12:     if encoded <= 0.040_45 {
13:         encoded / 12.92
14:     } else {
15:         ((encoded + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
16:     }
17: }
18: 
19: pub(crate) fn decode_albedo(bytes: [f32; 3]) -> LinearRgb {
20:     bytes.map(srgb_channel_to_linear)
21: }
22: 
23: pub(crate) fn decode_packed_albedo(packed: u32) -> LinearRgb {
24:     decode_albedo([
25:         ((packed >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
26:         ((packed >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
27:         (packed & 0xFF) as f32,
28:     ])
29: }
30: 
31: #[cfg(test)]
32: mod tests {
33:     use super::{decode_albedo, decode_packed_albedo, srgb_channel_to_linear};
34: 
35:     #[test]
36:     fn packed_and_unpacked_authored_colors_share_one_decode() {
37:         assert_eq!(
38:             decode_packed_albedo(0x80_FF_00),
39:             decode_albedo([128.0, 255.0, 0.0])
40:         );
41:         assert!((srgb_channel_to_linear(128.0) - 0.215_86).abs() < 1.0e-4);
42:     }
43: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Validate and apply one independent pooled-atlas row update.
  2: //!
  3: //! Streaming supplies a complete row-aligned chunk slot whose child pointers
  4: //! were already rebased by [`crate::application::atlas::AtlasPool`]. This
  5: //! boundary validates that independence before mutating persistent renderer
  6: //! state, then rebuilds only the corresponding prepared MIP slice.
  7: 
  8: use std::ops::Range;
  9: 
 10: use crate::application::atlas::ROW_TEXELS;
 11: 
 12: use super::atlas::{MipNode, rebuild_mips_in_node_range};
 13: 
 14: const WORDS_PER_NODE: usize = 4;
 15: const WORDS_PER_ROW: usize = ROW_TEXELS * WORDS_PER_NODE;
 16: 
 17: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 18: struct ValidatedRowUpdate {
 19:     word_range: Range<usize>,
 20:     node_range: Range<usize>,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: /// Applies a complete independent slot update without reallocating the atlas.
 24: pub(super) fn update_prepared_atlas_rows(
 25:     atlas: &mut [u32],
 26:     mips: &mut [MipNode],
 27:     mip_visit_scratch: &mut Vec<bool>,
 28:     first_row: u32,
 29:     texels: &[u32],
 30: ) -> bool {
 31:     let Some(update) = validate_row_update(atlas, mips, first_row, texels) else {
 32:         return false;
 33:     };
 34: 
 35:     atlas[update.word_range].copy_from_slice(texels);
 36:     let rebuilt = rebuild_mips_in_node_range(atlas, mips, update.node_range, mip_visit_scratch);
 37:     debug_assert!(rebuilt, "validated row range must always rebuild");
 38:     rebuilt
 39: }
 40: 
 41: /// Validation is deliberately complete before the first persistent write.
 42: fn validate_row_update(
 43:     atlas: &[u32],
 44:     mips: &[MipNode],
 45:     first_row: u32,
 46:     texels: &[u32],
 47: ) -> Option<ValidatedRowUpdate> {
 48:     if atlas.is_empty()
 49:         || texels.is_empty()
 50:         || atlas.len() % WORDS_PER_ROW != 0
 51:         || texels.len() % WORDS_PER_ROW != 0
 52:         || mips.len().checked_mul(WORDS_PER_NODE)? != atlas.len()
 53:     {
 54:         return None;
 55:     }
 56: 
 57:     let first_row = usize::try_from(first_row).ok()?;
 58:     let word_start = first_row.checked_mul(WORDS_PER_ROW)?;
 59:     let word_end = word_start.checked_add(texels.len())?;
 60:     if word_end > atlas.len() {
 61:         return None;
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     let node_range = word_start / WORDS_PER_NODE..word_end / WORDS_PER_NODE;
 65:     validate_independent_node_block(texels, node_range.clone())?;
 66:     Some(ValidatedRowUpdate {
 67:         word_range: word_start..word_end,
 68:         node_range,
 69:     })
 70: }
 71: 
 72: /// Every internal node in a streamed slot must keep all eight child slots
 73: /// inside that same update. This rejects partial-slot rows and corrupted or
 74: /// unrebased pointers before they can invalidate an unrelated slot's MIPs.
 75: fn validate_independent_node_block(texels: &[u32], global_nodes: Range<usize>) -> Option<()> {
 76:     for node in texels.chunks_exact(WORDS_PER_NODE) {
 77:         match node[0] {
 78:             1 => {}
 79:             0 => {
 80:                 if node[2] & !0xff != 0 {
 81:                     return None;
 82:                 }
 83:                 let child_base = usize::try_from(node[1]).ok()?;
 84:                 let child_end = child_base.checked_add(8)?;
 85:                 if child_base < global_nodes.start || child_end > global_nodes.end {
 86:                     return None;
 87:                 }
 88:             }
 89:             _ => return None,
 90:         }
 91:     }
 92:     Some(())
 93: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/generation_worker_policy.rs
````rust
  1: //! Select concurrency for the browser's chunk-generation worker pool.
  2: //!
  3: //! This policy configures world generation and streaming only. The software
  4: //! splat renderer remains on the browser's main thread. Keeping query parsing
  5: //! and hardware clamping here makes the contract natively testable and keeps
  6: //! browser APIs out of the application layer.
  7: 
  8: /// Hard ceiling for generation workers. More workers duplicate the WASM
  9: /// module and atlas-building scratch memory without improving frame latency.
 10: pub const MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS: u8 = 4;
 11: 
 12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 13: pub enum GenerationWorkerPreference {
 14:     /// Reserve one reported hardware thread for the browser/render loop.
 15:     Auto,
 16:     /// Generate synchronously through `LocalChunkSource` on the main thread.
 17:     Disabled,
 18:     /// Request an explicit number, still bounded by reported hardware.
 19:     Fixed(u8),
 20: }
 21: 
 22: impl Default for GenerationWorkerPreference {
 23:     fn default() -> Self {
 24:         Self::Auto
 25:     }
 26: }
 27: 
 28: impl GenerationWorkerPreference {
 29:     /// Resolve a safe pool size from `Navigator.hardwareConcurrency`.
 30:     /// Unknown/invalid reports use the conservative historical fallback of
 31:     /// two hardware threads; automatic selection therefore uses one worker.
 32:     pub fn resolve(self, hardware_concurrency: f64) -> usize {
 33:         if self == Self::Disabled {
 34:             return 0;
 35:         }
 36: 
 37:         let reported_threads = if hardware_concurrency.is_finite() && hardware_concurrency >= 1.0 {
 38:             hardware_concurrency.floor().min(u32::MAX as f64) as u32
 39:         } else {
 40:             2
 41:         };
 42:         let auto_workers = reported_threads
 43:             .saturating_sub(1)
 44:             .clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
 45:         let fixed_worker_ceiling =
 46:             reported_threads.clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
 47:         match self {
 48:             Self::Auto => auto_workers,
 49:             Self::Fixed(requested) => requested.clamp(1, fixed_worker_ceiling),
 50:             Self::Disabled => 0,
 51:         }
 52:         .into()
 53:     }
 54: }
 55: 
 56: /// Parses the last exact `workers` query pair. Canonical values are `auto`,
 57: /// `0`, and positive integers; oversized integers clamp to the product cap.
 58: /// Missing or malformed values safely restore automatic selection.
 59: pub fn parse_generation_worker_preference(query: &str) -> GenerationWorkerPreference {
 60:     let mut preference = GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto;
 61:     for (key, value) in query
 62:         .trim_start_matches('?')
 63:         .split('&')
 64:         .filter_map(|pair| pair.split_once('='))
 65:     {
 66:         if key != "workers" {
 67:             continue;
 68:         }
 69:         preference = match value {
 70:             "auto" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto,
 71:             "0" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled,
 72:             _ => value
 73:                 .parse::<u32>()
 74:                 .ok()
 75:                 .filter(|requested| *requested > 0)
 76:                 .map(|requested| {
 77:                     GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(
 78:                         requested.min(u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8,
 79:                     )
 80:                 })
 81:                 .unwrap_or(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto),
 82:         };
 83:     }
 84:     preference
 85: }
 86: 
 87: #[cfg(test)]
 88: mod tests {
 89:     use super::*;
 90: 
 91:     #[test]
 92:     fn missing_and_malformed_values_restore_auto() {
 93:         assert_eq!(
 94:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?seed=7"),
 95:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto
 96:         );
 97:         assert_eq!(
 98:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=banana"),
 99:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto
100:         );
101:         assert_eq!(
102:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?not_workers=0"),
103:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto
104:         );
105:     }
106: 
107:     #[test]
108:     fn parses_disabled_auto_and_bounded_fixed_counts() {
109:         assert_eq!(
110:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=0"),
111:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled
112:         );
113:         assert_eq!(
114:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=auto"),
115:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto
116:         );
117:         assert_eq!(
118:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=3"),
119:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(3)
120:         );
121:         assert_eq!(
122:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=999"),
123:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(4)
124:         );
125:     }
126: 
127:     #[test]
128:     fn last_duplicate_pair_wins_deterministically() {
129:         assert_eq!(
130:             parse_generation_worker_preference("?workers=4&workers=0"),
131:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled
132:         );
133:     }
134: 
135:     #[test]
136:     fn resolution_reserves_the_main_thread_and_clamps_to_hardware() {
137:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(8.0), 4);
138:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(4.0), 3);
139:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(2.0), 1);
140:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(1.0), 1);
141:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(4).resolve(2.0), 2);
142:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(2).resolve(8.0), 2);
143:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled.resolve(8.0), 0);
144:     }

146:     #[test]
147:     fn invalid_hardware_reports_use_a_conservative_fallback() {
148:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(f64::NAN), 1);
149:         assert_eq!(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto.resolve(0.0), 1);
150:         assert_eq!(
151:             GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(4).resolve(f64::INFINITY),
152:             2
153:         );
154:     }
````

````rust
  1: //! Ambient temperature felt by the player, derived from the lit scene.
  2: //!
  3: //! The Backrooms' heat *is* its lighting: fluorescent tubes bake the air,
  4: //! so standing under working fixtures warms the wanderer while darkness
  5: //! (blackouts, dead bays, Level 1's failing grid) lets the air fall back to
  6: //! the level's unlit baseline. Enclosure matters too — a lit closet cooks
  7: //! faster than a lit atrium — approximated here by how much collision mass
  8: //! crowds the player. Everything is pure math over the same deduplicated,
  9: //! flicker-scaled fixture list every renderer sees: a sputtering tube that
 10: //! is dark this instant radiates nothing this instant.
 11: 
 12: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 13: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
 14: 
 15: /// Unlit-air baseline per level, °C. Level 0's dark corners still hold the
 16: /// building's stale warmth; Level 1's raw concrete is genuinely cold.
 17: pub fn dark_baseline_c(level: u32) -> f32 {
 18:     match level {
 19:         0 => 24.0,
 20:         1 => 13.0,
 21:         _ => 21.0,
 22:     }
 23: }
 24: 
 25: /// Maximum heating the fixture field can add above the baseline, °C.
 26: const MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C: f32 = 13.0;
 27: /// Scales summed fixture irradiance into °C before the cap.
 28: const HEAT_PER_IRRADIANCE: f32 = 9.0;
 29: /// Enclosure raises effective heating by up to this factor.
 30: const ENCLOSURE_GAIN: f32 = 0.6;
 31: /// Radius probed for enclosing collision mass.
 32: const ENCLOSURE_RADIUS: f32 = 6.0;
 33: /// Collision-box count that reads as "fully enclosed".
 34: const ENCLOSURE_SATURATION: f32 = 36.0;
 35: 
 36: /// The instantaneous ambient temperature at the player position.
 37: ///
 38: /// `lights` must already carry this frame's flicker gain so failing tubes
 39: /// heat exactly as much as they shine. The result is *unsmoothed*; the
 40: /// engine applies thermal inertia so doorways don't flip the rate per frame.
 41: pub fn ambient_celsius(
 42:     level: u32,
 43:     player: [f32; 3],
 44:     lights: &[LightSource],
 45:     collision: &[Aabb],
 46: ) -> f32 {
 47:     let mut irradiance = 0.0f32;
 48:     for light in lights {
 49:         let dx = light.position[0] - player[0];
 50:         let dy = light.position[1] - player[1];
 51:         let dz = light.position[2] - player[2];
 52:         let distance = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
 53:         let range = light.radius.max(0.01);
 54:         let falloff = (1.0 - distance / range).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 55:         irradiance += light.intensity * falloff * falloff;
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     let mut enclosing = 0usize;
 59:     for aabb in collision {
 60:         let center = [
 61:             (aabb.min[0] + aabb.max[0]) * 0.5,
 62:             (aabb.min[2] + aabb.max[2]) * 0.5,
 63:         ];
 64:         let dx = center[0] - player[0];
 65:         let dz = center[1] - player[2];
 66:         if dx * dx + dz * dz <= ENCLOSURE_RADIUS * ENCLOSURE_RADIUS {
 67:             enclosing += 1;
 68:         }
 69:     }
 70:     let enclosure = (enclosing as f32 / ENCLOSURE_SATURATION).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 71: 
 72:     let heat = (irradiance * HEAT_PER_IRRADIANCE).min(MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C)
 73:         * (1.0 + ENCLOSURE_GAIN * enclosure);
 74:     dark_baseline_c(level) + heat.min(MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C * (1.0 + ENCLOSURE_GAIN))
 75: }
 76: 
 77: #[cfg(test)]
 78: mod tests {
 79:     use super::*;
 80:     use crate::application::ports::LightKind;
 81: 
 82:     fn fixture(position: [f32; 3], intensity: f32) -> LightSource {
 83:         LightSource {
 84:             id: 1,
 85:             position,
 86:             half_size: [0.5, 0.5],
 87:             color: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
 88:             radius: 16.0,
 89:             intensity,
 90:             kind: LightKind::CeilingPanel,
 91:             flicker_mode: 0,
 92:             enabled: true,
 93:         }
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     fn walls_around(count: usize) -> Vec<Aabb> {
 97:         (0..count)
 98:             .map(|i| {
 99:                 let angle = i as f32;
100:                 Aabb::new(
101:                     [angle.cos() * 2.0, 0.0, angle.sin() * 2.0],
102:                     [angle.cos() * 2.0 + 0.4, 3.0, angle.sin() * 2.0 + 0.4],
103:                 )
104:             })
105:             .collect()
106:     }
107: 
108:     #[test]
109:     fn darkness_rests_at_the_level_baseline() {
110:         let ambient = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[], &[]);
111:         assert_eq!(ambient, dark_baseline_c(0));
112:         assert!(dark_baseline_c(1) < dark_baseline_c(0), "Level 1 runs cold");
113:     }
114: 
115:     #[test]
116:     fn standing_under_a_fixture_heats_the_air() {
117:         let lit = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[fixture([0.0, 3.0, 0.0], 1.5)], &[]);
118:         let far = ambient_celsius(0, [14.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[fixture([0.0, 3.0, 0.0], 1.5)], &[]);
119:         assert!(lit > dark_baseline_c(0) + 2.0, "lit air must run hot: {lit}");
120:         assert!(far < lit, "heat falls off with distance");
121:     }
122: 
123:     #[test]
124:     fn enclosure_amplifies_lit_spaces_but_not_dark_ones() {
125:         let light = [fixture([0.0, 3.0, 0.0], 1.5)];
126:         let open = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &light, &[]);
127:         let tight = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &light, &walls_around(40));
128:         assert!(tight > open, "small lit rooms cook: {tight} vs {open}");
129: 
130:         let dark_open = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[], &[]);
131:         let dark_tight = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[], &walls_around(40));
132:         assert_eq!(dark_open, dark_tight, "enclosure without light is inert");
133:     }
134: 
135:     #[test]
136:     fn a_flickered_out_tube_radiates_nothing() {
137:         // The engine multiplies flicker gain into intensity before calling;
138:         // a dropout frame arrives here as near-zero intensity.
139:         let out = ambient_celsius(0, [0.0, 1.7, 0.0], &[fixture([0.0, 3.0, 0.0], 0.02)], &[]);
140:         assert!(out - dark_baseline_c(0) < 0.5);
141:     }
142: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Conservative finite-range fixture clustering for a world-space AABB.
  2: //!
  3: //! Both rewritten GPU paths use this exact predicate. It removes work, not
  4: //! light: a fixture is omitted only when no point on its rectangle can be
  5: //! within its compact-support range of any receiver in the bounds.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
  8: 
  9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 10: pub struct LightRange {
 11:     pub first: i32,
 12:     pub count: i32,
 13: }
 14: 
 15: pub fn append_lights_reaching_bounds(
 16:     lights: &[LightSource],
 17:     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
 18:     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
 19:     clustered: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
 20: ) -> LightRange {
 21:     let first = clustered.len();
 22:     clustered.extend(
 23:         lights
 24:             .iter()
 25:             .copied()
 26:             .filter(|light| reaches_bounds(light, bounds_min, bounds_max)),
 27:     );
 28:     LightRange {
 29:         first: first.min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
 30:         count: clustered.len().saturating_sub(first).min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
 31:     }
 32: }
 33: 
 34: fn reaches_bounds(light: &LightSource, bounds_min: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 35:     // Expanding X/Z by the emitter half-size converts rectangle-to-box
 36:     // distance into point-to-box distance (the Minkowski-sum construction).
 37:     let expanded_min = [
 38:         bounds_min[0] - light.half_size[0],
 39:         bounds_min[1],
 40:         bounds_min[2] - light.half_size[1],
 41:     ];
 42:     let expanded_max = [
 43:         bounds_max[0] + light.half_size[0],
 44:         bounds_max[1],
 45:         bounds_max[2] + light.half_size[1],
 46:     ];
 47:     let mut distance_squared = 0.0;
 48:     for axis in 0..3 {
 49:         let delta = if light.position[axis] < expanded_min[axis] {
 50:             expanded_min[axis] - light.position[axis]
 51:         } else if light.position[axis] > expanded_max[axis] {
 52:             light.position[axis] - expanded_max[axis]
 53:         } else {
 54:             0.0
 55:         };
 56:         distance_squared += delta * delta;
 57:     }
 58:     distance_squared <= light.radius * light.radius
 59: }
 60: 
 61: #[cfg(test)]
 62: mod tests {
 63:     use super::*;
 64:     use crate::application::ports::{LightKind, LightSource};
 65: 
 66:     fn light(id: u64, position: [f32; 3]) -> LightSource {
 67:         LightSource {
 68:             id,
 69:             position,
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/light_volume.rs
````rust
 1: //! Baked 3D light-volume upload, shared by the surface and splat drivers.
 2: 
 3: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 4: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
 5: 
 6: use crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload;
 7: 
 8: /// Uploads a chunk's baked RGB light volume as a linearly-filtered 3D
 9: /// texture (the fragment shaders sample it at world positions).
10: pub fn upload_light_volume(gl: &Gl, mesh: &SurfaceMeshPayload) -> Result<WebGlTexture, JsValue> {
11:     let texture = gl
12:         .create_texture()
13:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create light texture"))?;
14:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Some(&texture));
15:     // RGB rows are width*3 bytes — rarely 4-aligned, and the default
16:     // unpack alignment of 4 makes texImage3D reject the upload.
17:     gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1);
18:     gl.tex_image_3d_with_opt_u8_array(
19:         Gl::TEXTURE_3D,
20:         0,
21:         Gl::RGB8 as i32,
22:         mesh.light_volume_size[0] as i32,
23:         mesh.light_volume_size[1] as i32,
24:         mesh.light_volume_size[2] as i32,
25:         0,
26:         Gl::RGB,
27:         Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
28:         Some(&mesh.light_volume),
29:     )?;
30:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
31:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
32:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
33:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
34:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_R, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
35:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, None);
36:     Ok(texture)
37: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/shadow_target.rs
````rust
 1: //! Depth-only render target for the hero-light shadow map.
 2: 
 3: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 4: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlFramebuffer, WebGlTexture};
 5: 
 6: pub struct ShadowTarget {
 7:     pub fbo: WebGlFramebuffer,
 8:     pub texture: WebGlTexture,
 9:     pub size: i32,
10: }
11: 
12: /// Creates a `size`² DEPTH_COMPONENT16 texture bound to a framebuffer's
13: /// depth attachment. NEAREST filtering: the shaders do their own PCF.
14: pub fn create_shadow_target(gl: &Gl, size: i32) -> Result<ShadowTarget, JsValue> {
15:     let texture = gl
16:         .create_texture()
17:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow texture"))?;
18:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
19:     gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_u8_array(
20:         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
21:         0,
22:         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT16 as i32,
23:         size,
24:         size,
25:         0,
26:         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT,
27:         Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
28:         None,
29:     )?;
30:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
31:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
32:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
33:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
34: 
35:     let fbo = gl
36:         .create_framebuffer()
37:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow FBO"))?;
38:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, Some(&fbo));
39:     gl.framebuffer_texture_2d(
40:         Gl::FRAMEBUFFER,
41:         Gl::DEPTH_ATTACHMENT,
42:         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
43:         Some(&texture),
44:         0,
45:     );
46: 
47:     // A depth-only WebGL2 target has no color attachment. Explicitly route
48:     // both drawing and reading to NONE; leaving the defaults at
49:     // COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 makes strict mobile drivers report an incomplete
50:     // framebuffer and silently discard the shadow pass.
51:     let draw_buffers = js_sys::Array::new();
52:     draw_buffers.push(&wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_f64(Gl::NONE as f64));
53:     gl.draw_buffers(draw_buffers.as_ref());
54:     gl.read_buffer(Gl::NONE);
55: 
56:     let status = gl.check_framebuffer_status(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER);
57:     if status != Gl::FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE {
58:         gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
59:         gl.delete_framebuffer(Some(&fbo));
60:         gl.delete_texture(Some(&texture));
61:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!(
62:             "shadow framebuffer is incomplete (status 0x{status:04x})"
63:         )));
64:     }
65:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
66: 
67:     Ok(ShadowTarget { fbo, texture, size })
68: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/timer.rs
````rust
 1: //! Asynchronous GPU frame timing via `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`.
 2: //!
 3: //! One query is in flight at a time; results are polled (never blocked on)
 4: //! at the top of the next frames, so the HUD's GPU number lags a frame or
 5: //! two but the pipeline never stalls. Toggleable (`RenderToggles::gpu_timer`)
 6: //! because some drivers serialize on timer queries.
 7: 
 8: use js_sys::Object;
 9: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlQuery};
10: 
11: /// Extension constants absent from WebGL2 core.
12: const TIME_ELAPSED_EXT: u32 = 0x88BF;
13: const GPU_DISJOINT_EXT: u32 = 0x8FBB;
14: 
15: pub struct GpuFrameTimer {
16:     extension: Option<Object>,
17:     pending: Option<WebGlQuery>,
18:     last_ms: Option<f32>,
19: }
20: 
21: impl GpuFrameTimer {
22:     /// Probes for the extension; a `None` extension makes every method a
23:     /// no-op so callers never branch on support.
24:     pub fn new(gl: &Gl) -> Self {
25:         Self {
26:             extension: gl
27:                 .get_extension("EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2")
28:                 .ok()
29:                 .flatten(),
30:             pending: None,
31:             last_ms: None,
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     pub fn last_ms(&self) -> Option<f32> {
36:         self.last_ms
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// Collects a finished query, if any. Disjoint intervals (GPU clock
40:     /// disturbance) discard the sample.
41:     pub fn poll(&mut self, gl: &Gl) {
42:         let Some(query) = self.pending.as_ref() else {
43:             return;
44:         };
45:         let available = gl
46:             .get_query_parameter(query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE)
47:             .as_bool()
48:             .unwrap_or(false);
49:         let disjoint = self.extension.is_some()
50:             && gl
51:                 .get_parameter(GPU_DISJOINT_EXT)
52:                 .ok()
53:                 .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
54:                 .unwrap_or(false);
55:         if !available && !disjoint {
56:             return;
57:         }
58:         let query = self.pending.take().expect("pending timer exists");
59:         if available && !disjoint {
60:             self.last_ms = gl
61:                 .get_query_parameter(&query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT)
62:                 .as_f64()
63:                 .map(|nanos| (nanos as f32) * 1.0e-6);
64:         }
65:         gl.delete_query(Some(&query));
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// Starts timing this frame. Returns whether a query was issued (pass
69:     /// it to [`Self::end`]). `enabled` comes from the toggle switchboard.
70:     pub fn begin(&mut self, gl: &Gl, enabled: bool) -> bool {
71:         if !enabled {
72:             // The HUD must not present an old sample as current after timing
73:             // has been switched off. An in-flight query is still collected
74:             // by `poll` and then discarded from view on this frame.
75:             self.last_ms = None;
76:             return false;
77:         }
78:         if self.extension.is_none() || self.pending.is_some() {
79:             return false;
80:         }
81:         let Some(query) = gl.create_query() else {
82:             return false;
83:         };
84:         gl.begin_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT, &query);
85:         self.pending = Some(query);
86:         true
87:     }
88: 
89:     pub fn end(&self, gl: &Gl, started: bool) {
90:         if started {
91:             gl.end_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT);
92:         }
93:     }
94: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/upload_scene_lights.rs
````rust
  1: //! Complete analytic-fixture upload shared by the surface and raymarch paths.
  2: //!
  3: //! A texture is used instead of fragment-uniform arrays for two reasons: the
  4: //! physical scene is not silently truncated to a camera-ranked slot budget,
  5: //! and the large raymarch chunk table no longer competes with lights for the
  6: //! WebGL minimum uniform-vector allowance. Each light occupies three RGBA32F
  7: //! texels in the layout decoded by `shaders/sample_scene_lights.rs`.
  8: 
  9: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 10: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
 11: 
 12: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
 13: 
 14: const PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS: i32 = 1024;
 15: const TEXELS_PER_LIGHT: usize = 3;
 16: 
 17: pub struct SceneLightTexture {
 18:     texture: WebGlTexture,
 19:     width: i32,
 20:     maximum_size: i32,
 21:     staging: Vec<f32>,
 22:     last_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
 23:     uploaded: bool,
 24: }
 25: 
 26: impl SceneLightTexture {
 27:     pub fn create(gl: &Gl) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 28:         let texture = gl
 29:             .create_texture()
 30:             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create scene-light texture"))?;
 31:         let maximum_size = gl
 32:             .get_parameter(Gl::MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE)?
 33:             .as_f64()
 34:             .unwrap_or(0.0) as i32;
 35:         if maximum_size < 1 {
 36:             return Err(JsValue::from_str("WebGL reported no 2-D texture capacity"));
 37:         }
 38:         let width = PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS.min(maximum_size);
 39:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
 40:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 41:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 42:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 43:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 44:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 45:         Ok(Self {
 46:             texture,
 47:             width,
 48:             maximum_size,
 49:             staging: Vec::new(),
 50:             last_lights: Vec::new(),
 51:             uploaded: false,
 52:         })
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /// Replaces the immutable frame snapshot and returns its exact light count.
 56:     pub fn upload(&mut self, gl: &Gl, lights: &[LightSource]) -> Result<i32, JsValue> {
 57:         if self.uploaded && self.last_lights == lights {
 58:             return Ok(lights.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32);
 59:         }
 60:         let texel_count = lights.len().max(1) * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT;
 61:         let rows = (texel_count as i32 + self.width - 1) / self.width;
 62:         if rows > self.maximum_size || lights.len() > i32::MAX as usize {
 63:             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
 64:                 "resident fixture list exceeds the WebGL scene-light texture",
 65:             ));
 66:         }
 67: 
 68:         self.staging.clear();
 69:         self.staging
 70:             .resize(self.width as usize * rows as usize * 4, 0.0);
 71:         for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
 72:             let offset = index * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT * 4;
 73:             self.staging[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
 74:             self.staging[offset + 3] = light.kind as u8 as f32;
 75:             self.staging[offset + 4..offset + 7].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
 76:             self.staging[offset + 7] = light.intensity;
 77:             self.staging[offset + 8] = light.radius;
 78:             self.staging[offset + 9] = light.half_size[0];
 79:             self.staging[offset + 10] = light.half_size[1];
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
 83:         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
 84:         let view = js_sys::Float32Array::from(self.staging.as_slice());
 85:         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 86:             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 87:             0,
 88:             Gl::RGBA32F as i32,
 89:             self.width,
 90:             rows,
 91:             0,
 92:             Gl::RGBA,
 93:             Gl::FLOAT,
 94:             Some(&view),
 95:         )?;
 96:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 97:         self.last_lights.clear();
 98:         self.last_lights.extend_from_slice(lights);
 99:         self.uploaded = true;
100:         Ok(lights.len() as i32)
101:     }
102: 
103:     pub fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
104:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
105:     }
106: 
107:     pub fn width(&self) -> i32 {
108:         self.width
109:     }
110: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/compose_surface_lighting.rs
````rust
 1: //! Compose emission, ambient fill, cached fill, fixtures, and flashlight.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: vec3 ambientIrradiance() {
 5:     if (uOutdoor == 1) return vec3(0.32, 0.38, 0.48) * uAmbientScale;
 6:     return vec3(0.045, 0.040, 0.024) * uAmbientScale;
 7: }
 8: 
 9: vec3 composeSurfaceLighting(vec3 normal, vec3 albedo) {
10:     if (isEmissiveMaterial(vMaterial) && isDownwardEmittingFace(normal)) {
11:         return emittedRadiance(vMaterial, albedo, normal);
12:     }
13: 
14:     float ambientOcclusion = mix(1.0, 0.62, clamp(vAo, 0.0, 1.0));
15:     vec3 ambient = ambientIrradiance();
16:     // The voxel field is deliberately a restrained diffuse-fill term.
17:     // It never substitutes for the analytic fixtures below.
18:     vec3 cachedStatic = sampleStaticIrradiance(vWorldPosition, normal) * 0.12;
19:     vec3 analyticDirect = vec3(0.0);
20: 
21:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < uLightCount; ++lightIndex) {
22:         SceneLight light = readSceneLight(uLightFirst + lightIndex);
23:         vec3 delta = light.position - vWorldPosition;
24:         vec3 surfaceToLight = normalize(delta);
25:         float visibility = lightIndex == uShadowedLightIndex
26:             ? shadowVisibility(vWorldPosition, normal, surfaceToLight)
27:             : 1.0;
28:         analyticDirect += evaluateSceneLight(
29:             vWorldPosition,
30:             normal,
31:             light.position,
32:             light.halfSize,
33:             light.color,
34:             light.range,
35:             light.intensity,
36:             light.kind
37:         ) * visibility;
38:     }
39:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < 4; ++lightIndex) {
40:         if (lightIndex >= uDynamicLightCount) break;
41:         analyticDirect += evaluatePointLight(
42:             vWorldPosition,
43:             normal,
44:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].xyz,
45:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].rgb,
46:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].w,
47:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].a
48:         );
49:     }
50: 
51:     // Screen-space/voxel AO is only a model of indirect sky/room
52:     // visibility. Applying it to analytic or already-occluded cached
53:     // fixture light darkens corners twice and violates the light model.
54:     vec3 radiance = albedo * (
55:         ambient * ambientOcclusion + cachedStatic + analyticDirect
56:     ) * (1.0 / PI);
57:     if (uFlashlightEnabled == 1) {
58:         radiance += albedo * spotBeam(
59:             uCameraPosition, uCamForward, vWorldPosition, normal
60:         );
61:     }
62:     return radiance;
63: }
64: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/hero_shadow_visibility.rs
````rust
 1: //! Sample the optional hero-light shadow map for one visible surface point.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: float shadowVisibility(vec3 worldPosition, vec3 normal, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
 5:     vec4 clip = uLightViewProjection * vec4(worldPosition + normal * 0.02, 1.0);
 6:     vec3 projected = clip.xyz / max(abs(clip.w), 1e-8);
 7:     vec2 uv = projected.xy * 0.5 + 0.5;
 8:     float receiverDepth = projected.z * 0.5 + 0.5;
 9:     if (any(lessThan(uv, vec2(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(uv, vec2(1.0)))
10:         || receiverDepth <= 0.0 || receiverDepth >= 1.0) {
11:         return 1.0;
12:     }
13: 
14:     vec2 texel = 1.0 / vec2(textureSize(uShadowMap, 0));
15:     float bias = max(0.0015 * (1.0 - dot(normal, surfaceToLight)), 0.0005);
16:     float visible = 0.0;
17:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
18:         vec2(-0.5, -0.5), vec2(0.5, -0.5),
19:         vec2(-0.5, 0.5), vec2(0.5, 0.5)
20:     );
21:     for (int tap = 0; tap < 4; ++tap) {
22:         float storedDepth = texture(uShadowMap, uv + offsets[tap] * texel).r;
23:         visible += receiverDepth - bias <= storedDepth ? 1.0 : 0.0;
24:     }
25:     return visible * 0.25;
26: }
27: "#;
````
