 1: //! Define which visible material faces emit and their linear radiance.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: bool isEmissiveMaterial(float material) {
 5:     return abs(material - 4.0) < 0.1
 6:         || abs(material - 9.0) < 0.1

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/collect_ordered_chunk_intervals.rs
````rust
 1: //! Intersect the camera ray with resident chunks and optionally order entries.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: int collectOrderedChunkIntervals(
 5:     vec3 rayDirection,
 6:     out ChunkInterval intervals[25]
 7: ) {
 8:     int intervalCount = 0;
 9:     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
10:         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
11:         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
12:             localOrigin,
13:             rayDirection,
14:             vec3(0.0),
15:             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
16:         );
17:         if (!box.hit) continue;
18: 
19:         int insertion = intervalCount;
20:         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1) {
21:             while (insertion > 0 && intervals[insertion - 1].entry > box.entry) {
22:                 intervals[insertion] = intervals[insertion - 1];
23:                 insertion--;
24:             }
25:         }
26:         intervals[insertion] = ChunkInterval(
27:             chunkIndex, box.entry, box.exit, box.entryNormal
28:         );
29:         intervalCount++;
30:     }
31:     return intervalCount;
32: }
33: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/decode_voxel_atlas.rs
````rust
 1: //! Stateless point lookup in the packed SVO atlas.
 2: //!
 3: //! Restarting at the root for each step costs a few integer fetches but
 4: //! removes the fragile mutable stack/pop state that caused cracks and phantom
 5: //! boxes. A masked-out child returns its exact empty octant bounds without a
 6: //! texture fetch; the optimization can then jump over that whole region.
 7: 
 8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 9: struct AtlasNode {
10:     bool leaf;
11:     uint payload;
12:     uint colorOrMask;
13:     uint lightWord;
14: };
15: 
16: struct VoxelLeaf {
17:     uint material;
18:     uint color;
19:     uint lightWord;
20:     vec3 boundsMin;
21:     vec3 boundsMax;
22: };
23: 
24: AtlasNode readAtlasNode(int nodeIndex) {
25:     ivec2 texel = ivec2(nodeIndex % 1024, nodeIndex / 1024);
26:     uvec4 packed = texelFetch(uNodeTexture, texel, 0);
27:     return AtlasNode(packed.x == 1u, packed.y, packed.z, packed.w);
28: }
29: 
30: VoxelLeaf lookupVoxelLeaf(
31:     vec3 point,
32:     int rootIndex,
33:     float worldSize,
34:     int svoDepth
35: ) {
36:     int nodeIndex = rootIndex;
37:     vec3 boundsMin = vec3(0.0);
38:     vec3 boundsMax = vec3(worldSize);
39: 
40:     // Generator validation bounds depth; the runtime value only shortens
41:     // this statically bounded loop for ordinary 6/8-level chunks.
42:     for (int level = 0; level <= 10; ++level) {
43:         AtlasNode node = readAtlasNode(nodeIndex);
44:         if (node.leaf || level >= svoDepth) {
45:             return VoxelLeaf(node.payload, node.colorOrMask, node.lightWord, boundsMin, boundsMax);
46:         }
47: 
48:         vec3 center = (boundsMin + boundsMax) * 0.5;
49:         int childX = point.x >= center.x ? 1 : 0;
50:         int childY = point.y >= center.y ? 1 : 0;
51:         int childZ = point.z >= center.z ? 1 : 0;
52:         int child = (childZ << 2) | (childY << 1) | childX;
53: 
54:         vec3 childMin = vec3(
55:             childX == 1 ? center.x : boundsMin.x,
56:             childY == 1 ? center.y : boundsMin.y,
57:             childZ == 1 ? center.z : boundsMin.z
58:         );
59:         vec3 childMax = vec3(
60:             childX == 1 ? boundsMax.x : center.x,
61:             childY == 1 ? boundsMax.y : center.y,
62:             childZ == 1 ? boundsMax.z : center.z
63:         );
64: 
65:         if ((node.colorOrMask & (1u << uint(child))) == 0u) {
66:             return VoxelLeaf(0u, 0u, 0u, childMin, childMax);
67:         }
68:         nodeIndex = int(node.payload) + child;
69:         boundsMin = childMin;
70:         boundsMax = childMax;
71:     }
72:     return VoxelLeaf(0u, 0u, 0u, boundsMin, boundsMax);
73: }
74: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/select_nearest_voxel_hit.rs
````rust
 1: //! Trace every candidate chunk interval and retain the nearest solid voxel.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: VoxelHit selectNearestVoxelHit(
 5:     vec3 rayDirection,
 6:     ChunkInterval intervals[25],
 7:     int intervalCount,
 8:     out int closestChunkIndex
 9: ) {
10:     VoxelHit closest = VoxelHit(
11:         false, TRACE_INFINITY, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u
12:     );
13:     closestChunkIndex = -1;
14:     for (int intervalIndex = 0; intervalIndex < intervalCount; ++intervalIndex) {
15:         ChunkInterval interval = intervals[intervalIndex];
16:         // Sorted traversal may stop only after every remaining AABB begins
17:         // beyond the nearest solid hit. Breaking after the first hit is wrong
18:         // because power-of-two padded chunk boxes overlap.
19:         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1 && interval.entry >= closest.distance) break;
20: 
21:         int chunkIndex = interval.chunkIndex;
22:         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
23:         RayBoxHit box = RayBoxHit(
24:             true, interval.entry, interval.exit, interval.entryNormal
25:         );
26:         VoxelHit candidate = traceChunk(
27:             localOrigin,
28:             rayDirection,
29:             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
30:             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
31:             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
32:             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
33:             box
34:         );
35:         if (candidate.hit && candidate.distance < closest.distance) {
36:             closest = candidate;
37:             closestChunkIndex = chunkIndex;
38:         }
39:     }
40:     return closest;
41: }
42: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/trace_direct_light_visibility.rs
````rust
  1: //! Occlusion queries from a visible voxel face to analytic emitter samples.
  2: //!
  3: //! The primary-ray hit and every shadow segment use the same chunk slabs,
  4: //! stateless SVO lookup, and selected stepping policy. Rectangle visibility
  5: //! is evaluated at the same four Gauss samples as its irradiance integral;
  6: //! a center-only visibility term would leak around partial blockers.
  7: 
  8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
  9: bool directSampleIsVisible(
 10:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 11:     vec3 surfaceNormal,
 12:     vec3 samplePosition,
 13:     float receiverVoxelSize
 14: ) {
 15:     if (uDirectVisibilityEnabled == 0) return true;
 16: 
 17:     float bias = max(receiverVoxelSize * 1e-3, 1e-5);
 18:     vec3 segmentOrigin = surfacePosition + surfaceNormal * bias;
 19:     vec3 segment = samplePosition - segmentOrigin;
 20:     float segmentLength = length(segment);
 21:     if (!(segmentLength > bias * 2.0)) return true;
 22:     vec3 direction = segment / segmentLength;
 23:     float blockerLimit = segmentLength - bias * 2.0;
 24: 
 25:     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
 26:         vec3 localOrigin = segmentOrigin - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
 27:         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
 28:             localOrigin,
 29:             direction,
 30:             vec3(0.0),
 31:             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
 32:         );
 33:         if (!box.hit || box.entry >= blockerLimit) continue;
 34:         box.exit = min(box.exit, blockerLimit);
 35:         VoxelHit blocker = traceChunk(
 36:             localOrigin,
 37:             direction,
 38:             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
 39:             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
 40:             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
 41:             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
 42:             box
 43:         );
 44:         if (blocker.hit && blocker.distance < blockerLimit) return false;
 45:     }
 46:     return true;
 47: }
 48: 
 49: vec3 evaluateVisiblePointLight(
 50:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 51:     vec3 normal,
 52:     vec3 lightPosition,
 53:     vec3 lightColor,
 54:     float range,
 55:     float intensity,
 56:     float receiverVoxelSize
 57: ) {
 58:     vec3 delta = lightPosition - surfacePosition;
 59:     float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 60:     vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 61:     float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range)
 62:         * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight);
 63:     if (!(weight > 0.0)
 64:         || !directSampleIsVisible(
 65:             surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, receiverVoxelSize
 66:         )) {
 67:         return vec3(0.0);
 68:     }
 69:     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0) * weight;
 70: }
 71: 
 72: vec3 evaluateVisibleSceneLight(
 73:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 74:     vec3 normal,
 75:     SceneLight light,
 76:     float receiverVoxelSize
 77: ) {
 78:     if (light.kind == LIGHT_POINT) {
 79:         return evaluateVisiblePointLight(
 80:             surfacePosition, normal, light.position, light.color,
 81:             light.range, light.intensity, receiverVoxelSize
 82:         );
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     float area = 4.0 * max(light.halfSize.x, 0.0) * max(light.halfSize.y, 0.0);
 86:     if (!(area > 0.0)) return vec3(0.0);
 87:     const float GAUSS = 0.5773502691896258;
 88:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
 89:         vec2(-GAUSS, -GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS, -GAUSS),
 90:         vec2(-GAUSS,  GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS,  GAUSS)
 91:     );
 92:     float integral = 0.0;
 93:     for (int sampleIndex = 0; sampleIndex < 4; ++sampleIndex) {
 94:         vec2 offset = offsets[sampleIndex] * light.halfSize;
 95:         vec3 samplePosition = light.position + vec3(offset.x, 0.0, offset.y);
 96:         vec3 delta = samplePosition - surfacePosition;
 97:         float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 98:         vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 99:         float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, light.range)
100:             * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight)
101:             * emitterCosine(light.kind, surfaceToLight);
102:         if (weight > 0.0
103:             && directSampleIsVisible(
104:                 surfacePosition, normal, samplePosition, receiverVoxelSize
105:             )) {
106:             integral += weight;
107:         }
108:     }
109:     return max(light.color, vec3(0.0)) * max(light.intensity, 0.0)
110:         * area * (integral * 0.25);
111: }
112: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/apply_distance_fog.rs
````rust
 1: //! Homogeneous distance fog shared by every new GPU path.
 2: //!
 3: //! This is deliberately one equation, not an art-effect stack. For an
 4: //! extinction coefficient `sigma` and travelled distance `d`, Beer–Lambert
 5: //! transmittance is `T = exp(-sigma * d)`. Medium radiance fills exactly the
 6: //! energy removed from the surface term.
 7: 
 8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 9: float fogTransmittance(float distanceToCamera, float fogStart, float sigmaExtinction) {
10:     float distanceInMedium = max(distanceToCamera - max(fogStart, 0.0), 0.0);
11:     return exp(-max(sigmaExtinction, 0.0) * distanceInMedium);
12: }
13: 
14: vec3 applyDistanceFog(
15:     vec3 surfaceRadiance,
16:     vec3 mediumRadiance,
17:     float distanceToCamera,
18:     float fogStart,
19:     float sigmaExtinction
20: ) {
21:     float transmittance = fogTransmittance(distanceToCamera, fogStart, sigmaExtinction);
22:     return surfaceRadiance * transmittance + mediumRadiance * (1.0 - transmittance);
23: }
24: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/encode_display_color.rs
````rust
 1: //! One linear-HDR to canvas conversion for surfaces and raymarching.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: vec3 srgbToLinear(vec3 encoded) {
 5:     vec3 lowPart = encoded / 12.92;
 6:     vec3 highPart = pow((encoded + 0.055) / 1.055, vec3(2.4));
 7:     return mix(lowPart, highPart, step(vec3(0.04045), encoded));
 8: }
 9: 
10: vec3 linearToSrgb(vec3 linearColor) {
11:     linearColor = max(linearColor, vec3(0.0));
12:     vec3 lowPart = linearColor * 12.92;
13:     vec3 highPart = 1.055 * pow(linearColor, vec3(1.0 / 2.4)) - 0.055;
14:     return mix(lowPart, highPart, step(vec3(0.0031308), linearColor));
15: }
16: 
17: vec3 encodeDisplayColor(vec3 radiance) {
18:     // A monotone, channel-independent Reinhard curve. Lighting and fog are
19:     // composed before this point in linear space.
20:     vec3 mapped = max(radiance, vec3(0.0)) / (vec3(1.0) + max(radiance, vec3(0.0)));
21:     return linearToSrgb(mapped);
22: }
23: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/supply_labels.rs
````rust
 1: //! Billboard pass for supply-item product labels.
 2: //!
 3: //! Each sprite is one camera-facing (cylindrical: yaw only, world-up locked)
 4: //! textured quad expanded entirely in the vertex shader from `gl_VertexID`,
 5: //! so the pass needs no vertex buffers at all. The atlas stacks one product
 6: //! logo per row; alpha cutout keeps the pass depth-tested and order-free.
 7: 
 8: use super::chunks;
 9: 
10: /// Matches `application::ports::MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES`.
11: pub const MAX_SPRITES: usize = 16;
12: /// Label quad half-extents in world units (matches the 4:3 label art).
13: pub const HALF_WIDTH: f32 = 0.26;
14: pub const HALF_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.195;
15: /// Atlas rows available to `SupplySprite::atlas_row`.
16: pub const ATLAS_ROWS: f32 = 2.0;
17: 
18: pub const VERTEX_SHADER: &str = r#"#version 300 es
19: precision highp float;
20: 
21: uniform mat4 uProjection;
22: uniform mat4 uView;
23: // xyz = world center of the label, w = atlas row.
24: uniform vec4 uSprites[16];
25: // Ground-plane camera right: the quad turns with the player's yaw and
26: // never tilts, like a stand-up card.
27: uniform vec3 uCamRight;
28: uniform vec2 uHalfSize;
29: 
30: out vec2 vUv;
31: flat out float vRow;
32: out vec3 vWorld;
33: 
34: const vec2 CORNERS[6] = vec2[6](
35:     vec2(-1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, 1.0),
36:     vec2(-1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, 1.0), vec2(-1.0, 1.0)
37: );
38: 
39: void main() {
40:     int sprite = gl_VertexID / 6;
41:     vec2 corner = CORNERS[gl_VertexID % 6];
42:     vec4 s = uSprites[sprite];
43:     vec3 world = s.xyz
44:         + uCamRight * (corner.x * uHalfSize.x)
45:         + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) * (corner.y * uHalfSize.y);
46:     vUv = vec2(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5);
47:     vRow = s.w;
48:     vWorld = world;
49:     gl_Position = uProjection * uView * vec4(world, 1.0);
50: }
51: "#;
52: 
53: pub fn fragment_source() -> String {
54:     let mut source = String::from(
55:         r#"#version 300 es
56: precision highp float;
57: 
58: in vec2 vUv;
59: flat in float vRow;
60: in vec3 vWorld;
61: 
62: uniform sampler2D uAtlas;
63: uniform vec3 uCameraPosition;
64: uniform vec3 uFogColor;
65: uniform float uFogDensity;
66: uniform float uFogStart;
67: 
68: out vec4 outColor;
69: "#,
70:     );
71:     source.push_str(chunks::TONE_MAP_GLSL);
72:     source.push_str(
73:         r#"
74: void main() {
75:     vec2 uv = vec2(vUv.x, (vUv.y + vRow) / 2.0);
76:     vec4 label = texture(uAtlas, uv);
77:     if (label.a < 0.5) discard;
78: 
79:     // Printed matter under ambient interior light, then the shared fog.
80:     vec3 color = label.rgb * 0.92;
81:     float dist = length(vWorld - uCameraPosition);
82:     float fog = 1.0 - exp(-uFogDensity * max(dist - uFogStart, 0.0));
83:     color = mix(color, uFogColor, clamp(fog, 0.0, 1.0));
84:     outColor = vec4(toneMap(color), 1.0);
85: }
86: "#,
87:     );
88:     source
89: }
````

  1: //! Instanced face-splat renderer — the GPU microvoxel path.
  2: //!
  3: //! One instance is one error-selected, axis-aligned surface rectangle. The
  4: //! vertex shader reconstructs its quad and evaluates lighting once per face;
  5: //! the fragment shader is deliberately limited to fog, grain, and tone
  6: //! mapping. Chunk uploads are incremental, so steady-state frames only cull
  7: //! contiguous instance ranges and submit draws.
  8: //!
  9: //! The module is split by responsibility:
 10: //!
 11: //! * this file owns composition, profile settings, programs, and uniforms;
 12: //! * [`resources`] owns per-chunk GPU buffers and textures;
 13: //! * [`draw`] owns the frame pipeline and renderer-port implementation.
 14: //!
 15: //! Cross-renderer WebGL plumbing lives in [`crate::drivers::gl`], while GLSL
 16: //! source composition lives in [`crate::drivers::shaders::splat`].

 44:     pub shadow_taps: i32,

110: /// WebGL2 face-splat renderer with one immutable resource page per resident
111: /// chunk. Mutable per-frame state is limited to the asynchronous timer and
112: /// telemetry counters.
113: pub struct SplatRenderer {
114:     pub(crate) gl: Gl,
115:     pub(crate) program: WebGlProgram,
116:     pub(crate) uniforms: Uniforms,
117:     pub(crate) attribs: InstanceAttribs,
118:     pub(crate) shadow_program: WebGlProgram,
119:     pub(crate) shadow_uniforms: ShadowUniforms,
120:     pub(crate) shadow: ShadowTarget,
121:     pub(crate) profile: SplatProfile,
122:     pub(crate) chunks: HashMap<SurfaceChunkKey, SplatChunk>,
123:     pub(crate) width: i32,
124:     pub(crate) height: i32,
125:     pub(crate) timer: GpuFrameTimer,
126:     pub(crate) stats: FrameStats,
127: }
128: 
129: impl SplatRenderer {
130:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement, profile: SplatProfile) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
131:         let gl = create_context(canvas, ContextOptions { depth: true })?;
132: 
133:         let vertex_source = splat::vertex_source();
134:         let fragment_source = splat::fragment_source();
135:         let program = link_program(&gl, &vertex_source, &fragment_source)?;
136:         let uniforms = Uniforms {
137:             projection: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uProjection"),
138:             view: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uView"),
139:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uChunkOrigin"),
140:             chunk_size: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uChunkSize"),
141:             voxel_scale: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uVoxelScale"),
142:             camera_position: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCameraPosition"),
143:             cam_forward: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCamForward"),
144:             flashlight: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFlashlightEnabled"),
145:             dither: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDitherEnabled"),
146:             light_volume: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightVolume"),
147:             light_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightCount"),
148:             light_positions: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightPositions"),
149:             light_colors: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightColors"),
150:             light_params: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightParams"),
151:             core_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreCount"),
152:             cores: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCores"),
153:             core_colors: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreColors"),
154:             shadow_map: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowMap"),
155:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightViewProjection"),
156:             shadowed_light_index: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowedLightIndex"),
157:             shadow_taps: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowTaps"),
158:             outdoor: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uOutdoor"),
159:             fog_color: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFogColor"),
160:             ambient_scale: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uAmbientScale"),
161:         };
162:         let attribs = InstanceAttribs::resolve(&gl, &program)?;
163: 
164:         let shadow_program = link_program(&gl, shadow::VERTEX_SHADER, shadow::FRAGMENT_SHADER)?;
165:         let shadow_uniforms = ShadowUniforms {
166:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uLightViewProjection"),
167:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uChunkOrigin"),
168:         };
169:         let shadow = create_shadow_target(&gl, profile.shadow_map_size)?;
170:         let timer = GpuFrameTimer::new(&gl);
171: 
172:         Ok(Self {
173:             gl,
174:             program,
175:             uniforms,
176:             attribs,
177:             shadow_program,
178:             shadow_uniforms,
179:             shadow,
180:             profile,
181:             chunks: HashMap::new(),
182:             width: canvas.width() as i32,
183:             height: canvas.height() as i32,
184:             timer,
185:             stats: FrameStats::default(),
186:         })
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Updates the backing-store viewport dimensions after adaptive scaling
190:     /// or a browser resize. GPU resources are resolution-independent.
191:     pub fn resize(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
192:         self.width = width as i32;
193:         self.height = height as i32;
194:     }
195: }

  1: //! Per-chunk GPU resources for the face-splat renderer.
  2: //!
  3: //! A chunk owns two representations derived from the same surface payload:
  4: //!
  5: //! * one packed instance page for the visible splat pass;
  6: //! * one retained greedy mesh used only as the hero-light shadow caster.
  7: //!
  8: //! WebGL2 has no `baseInstance`, so a cell-range draw re-points the four
  9: //! instance attributes at that range's byte offset before submission.
 10: 
 11: use js_sys::{Uint8Array, Uint32Array};
 12: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 13: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlBuffer, WebGlProgram, WebGlVertexArrayObject};
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::ports::{FaceCellRange, LightSource, SurfaceChunk};
 16: use crate::drivers::gl::light_volume::upload_light_volume;
 17: 
 18: use super::SplatRenderer;
 19: 
 20: /// Bytes per packed face instance uploaded to WebGL.
 21: pub(crate) const INSTANCE_STRIDE: i32 = 16;
 22: const SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE: i32 = 10;
 23: 
 24: /// Attribute locations are resolved once because every chunk uses the same
 25: /// packed instance layout.
 26: pub(crate) struct InstanceAttribs {
 27:     pos: u32,
 28:     extents: u32,
 29:     meta: u32,
 30:     flags: u32,
 31: }
 32: 
 33: impl InstanceAttribs {
 34:     pub(crate) fn resolve(gl: &Gl, program: &WebGlProgram) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 35:         let lookup = |name: &str| -> Result<u32, JsValue> {
 36:             let location = gl.get_attrib_location(program, name);
 37:             if location < 0 {
 38:                 return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("splat shader lost {name}")));
 39:             }
 40:             Ok(location as u32)
 41:         };
 42: 
 43:         Ok(Self {
 44:             pos: lookup("aFacePos")?,
 45:             extents: lookup("aFaceExtents")?,
 46:             meta: lookup("aFaceMeta")?,
 47:             flags: lookup("aFaceFlags")?,
 48:         })
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     fn enable(&self, gl: &Gl) {
 52:         for location in [self.pos, self.extents, self.meta, self.flags] {
 53:             gl.enable_vertex_attrib_array(location);
 54:             gl.vertex_attrib_divisor(location, 1);
 55:         }
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     /// Records attribute pointers for a range beginning at `first_instance`.
 59:     /// The caller must have the chunk VAO and its instance buffer bound.
 60:     pub(crate) fn point_at(&self, gl: &Gl, first_instance: u32) {
 61:         let base = first_instance as i32 * INSTANCE_STRIDE;
 62:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 63:             self.pos,
 64:             3,
 65:             Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
 66:             false,
 67:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 68:             base,
 69:         );
 70:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 71:             self.extents,
 72:             2,
 73:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 74:             false,
 75:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 76:             base + 6,
 77:         );
 78:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 79:             self.meta,
 80:             4,
 81:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 82:             false,
 83:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 84:             base + 8,
 85:         );
 86:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 87:             self.flags,
 88:             1,
 89:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 90:             false,
 91:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 92:             base + 12,
 93:         );
 94:     }
 95: }

 97: /// All GPU and frame-selection data owned by one resident chunk.
 98: pub(crate) struct SplatChunk {
 99:     pub instance_vao: WebGlVertexArrayObject,
100:     pub instance_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
101:     pub instance_count: i32,
102:     pub cells: Vec<FaceCellRange>,
103:     pub cell_size: f32,
104:     pub voxel_scale: f32,
105:     pub shadow_vao: WebGlVertexArrayObject,
106:     pub shadow_vertex_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
107:     pub shadow_index_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
108:     pub shadow_index_count: i32,
109:     pub origin: [f32; 3],
110:     pub bounds_max: [f32; 3],
111:     pub light_texture: web_sys::WebGlTexture,
112:     pub lights: Vec<LightSource>,
113: }
114: 
115: impl SplatRenderer {
116:     pub(crate) fn destroy_chunk(&self, chunk: SplatChunk) {
117:         let gl = &self.gl;
118:         gl.delete_vertex_array(Some(&chunk.instance_vao));
119:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.instance_buffer));
120:         gl.delete_vertex_array(Some(&chunk.shadow_vao));
121:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.shadow_vertex_buffer));
122:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.shadow_index_buffer));
123:         gl.delete_texture(Some(&chunk.light_texture));
124:     }
125: 
126:     pub(crate) fn upload_surface(&mut self, chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) {
127:         if let Some(old) = self.chunks.remove(&chunk.key) {
128:             self.destroy_chunk(old);
129:         }
130:         if chunk.mesh.faces.instances.is_empty() {
131:             return;
132:         }
133: 
134:         let (instance_vao, instance_buffer) = self.upload_instance_page(chunk);
135:         let (shadow_vao, shadow_vertex_buffer, shadow_index_buffer) =
136:             self.upload_shadow_mesh(chunk);
137:         let light_texture =
138:             upload_light_volume(&self.gl, chunk.mesh).expect("upload splat light volume");
139: 
140:         self.chunks.insert(
141:             chunk.key,
142:             SplatChunk {
143:                 instance_vao,
144:                 instance_buffer,
145:                 instance_count: chunk.mesh.faces.instances.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
146:                 cells: chunk.mesh.faces.cells.clone(),
147:                 cell_size: chunk.mesh.faces.cell_size,
148:                 voxel_scale: chunk.mesh.voxel_scale,
149:                 shadow_vao,
150:                 shadow_vertex_buffer,
151:                 shadow_index_buffer,
152:                 shadow_index_count: chunk.mesh.indices.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
153:                 origin: chunk.origin,
154:                 bounds_max: chunk.mesh.bounds.max,
155:                 light_texture,
156:                 lights: chunk.mesh.lights.clone(),
157:             },
158:         );
159:     }
160: 
161:     fn upload_instance_page(
162:         &self,
163:         chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>,
164:     ) -> (WebGlVertexArrayObject, WebGlBuffer) {
165:         let gl = &self.gl;
166:         let vao = gl.create_vertex_array().expect("create splat VAO");
167:         let buffer = gl.create_buffer().expect("create splat instance buffer");
168:         let packed = pack_instances(chunk);
169: 
170:         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&vao));
171:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&buffer));
172:         let bytes = Uint8Array::from(packed.as_slice());
173:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, &bytes, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
174:         self.attribs.enable(gl);
175:         self.attribs.point_at(gl, 0);
176:         gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
177:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
178: 
179:         (vao, buffer)
180:     }
181: 
182:     fn upload_shadow_mesh(
183:         &self,
184:         chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>,
185:     ) -> (WebGlVertexArrayObject, WebGlBuffer, WebGlBuffer) {
186:         let gl = &self.gl;
187:         let vao = gl.create_vertex_array().expect("create splat shadow VAO");
188:         let vertex_buffer = gl
189:             .create_buffer()
190:             .expect("create splat shadow vertex buffer");
191:         let index_buffer = gl
192:             .create_buffer()
193:             .expect("create splat shadow index buffer");
194:         let packed_vertices = pack_shadow_vertices(chunk);
195: 
196:         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&vao));
197:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&vertex_buffer));
198:         let vertices = Uint8Array::from(packed_vertices.as_slice());
199:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, &vertices, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
200: 
201:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&index_buffer));
202:         let indices = Uint32Array::from(chunk.mesh.indices.as_slice());
203:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, &indices, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
204: 
205:         // The shared shadow shader declares `aPosition` at location zero.
206:         gl.enable_vertex_attrib_array(0);
207:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(0, 3, Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT, false, SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE, 0);
208:         gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
209:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
210:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
211: 
212:         (vao, vertex_buffer, index_buffer)
213:     }
214: }
215: 
216: /// Serializes `PackedFaceInstance` explicitly so the GPU layout is stable
217: /// across Rust compiler versions and host alignment rules.
218: fn pack_instances(chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
219:     let instances = &chunk.mesh.faces.instances;
220:     let mut packed = Vec::with_capacity(instances.len() * INSTANCE_STRIDE as usize);
221:     for instance in instances {
222:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[0].to_le_bytes());
223:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[1].to_le_bytes());
224:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[2].to_le_bytes());
225:         packed.push(instance.extent_u);
226:         packed.push(instance.extent_v);
227:         packed.push(instance.normal_axis);
228:         packed.push(instance.material);
229:         packed.push(instance.baked_light);
230:         packed.push(instance.ao);
231:         packed.push(instance.flags);
232:         packed.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0]);
233:     }
234:     packed
235: }
236: 
237: /// Serializes the retained 10-byte greedy-mesh vertices. Only position is
238: /// consumed in the shadow pass, but retaining the canonical stride keeps the
239: /// caster byte-for-byte aligned with the visible surface representation.
240: fn pack_shadow_vertices(chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
241:     let mut packed = Vec::with_capacity(chunk.mesh.vertices.len() * SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE as usize);
242:     for vertex in &chunk.mesh.vertices {
243:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[0].to_le_bytes());
244:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[1].to_le_bytes());
245:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[2].to_le_bytes());
246:         packed.extend_from_slice(&[
247:             vertex.normal_axis,
248:             vertex.material,
249:             vertex.static_indirect,
250:             vertex.ao,
251:         ]);
252:     }
253:     packed
254: }
````

  1: //! RGBA32UI SVO node-atlas lifecycle.
  2: //!
  3: //! The serializer pads every atlas row to [`ATLAS_WIDTH`], which makes both a
  4: //! full replacement and an incremental row overwrite exact typed-array copies.
  5: 
  6: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
  7: 
  8: /// Must match the raymarch shader's node-index decoder and the core
  9: /// `OctreeGpuSerializer` row padding.
 10: const ATLAS_WIDTH: i32 = 1024;
 11: 
 12: pub(super) struct AtlasTexture {
 13:     texture: Option<WebGlTexture>,
 14:     /// Allocated atlas height, used to reject out-of-bounds row patches.
 15:     rows: i32,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: impl AtlasTexture {
 19:     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
 20:         Self {
 21:             texture: None,
 22:             rows: 0,
 23:         }
 24:     }
 25: 
 26:     /// Replaces the whole atlas. An empty stream intentionally releases the
 27:     /// previous texture so level transitions cannot sample stale nodes.
 28:     pub(super) fn replace(&mut self, gl: &Gl, texels: &[u32]) {
 29:         if let Some(old) = self.texture.take() {
 30:             gl.delete_texture(Some(&old));
 31:         }
 32:         self.rows = 0;
 33:         if texels.is_empty() {
 34:             return;
 35:         }
 36: 
 37:         debug_assert_eq!(texels.len() % 4, 0, "atlas texels are RGBA u32 values");
 38:         let texel_count = (texels.len() / 4) as i32;
 39:         let rows = (texel_count + ATLAS_WIDTH - 1) / ATLAS_WIDTH;
 40:         let texture = gl.create_texture().expect("create SVO atlas texture");
 41: 
 42:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
 43:         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
 44:         let view = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(texels);
 45:         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 46:             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 47:             0,
 48:             Gl::RGBA32UI as i32,
 49:             ATLAS_WIDTH,
 50:             rows,
 51:             0,
 52:             Gl::RGBA_INTEGER,
 53:             Gl::UNSIGNED_INT,
 54:             Some(&view),
 55:         )
 56:         .expect("SVO atlas texture upload failed");
 57:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 58:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 59:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 60:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 61:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 62: 
 63:         self.texture = Some(texture);
 64:         self.rows = rows;
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     /// Patches complete atlas rows without reallocating the texture.
 68:     pub(super) fn update_rows(&mut self, gl: &Gl, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
 69:         let row_stride = 4 * ATLAS_WIDTH as usize;
 70:         let patch_rows = texels.len() / row_stride;
 71:         if self.texture.is_none()
 72:             || patch_rows == 0
 73:             || texels.len() % row_stride != 0
 74:             || first_row as i32 + patch_rows as i32 > self.rows
 75:         {
 76:             return false;
 77:         }
 78: 
 79:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, self.texture.as_ref());
 80:         let view = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(texels);
 81:         let uploaded = gl
 82:             .tex_sub_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_u32_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 83:                 Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 84:                 0,
 85:                 0,
 86:                 first_row as i32,
 87:                 ATLAS_WIDTH,
 88:                 patch_rows as i32,
 89:                 Gl::RGBA_INTEGER,
 90:                 Gl::UNSIGNED_INT,
 91:                 Some(&view),
 92:             )
 93:             .is_ok();
 94:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 95:         uploaded
 96:     }
 97: 
 98:     pub(super) fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
 99:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, self.texture.as_ref());
100:     }
101: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/generation_worker_requests.rs
````rust
  1: //! Exact in-flight request bookkeeping for the generation-worker pool.
  2: //!
  3: //! Browser callbacks can arrive after a worker has failed or after the engine
  4: //! has already retried a chunk. This small ledger gives every callback one
  5: //! deterministic operation: finish the exact request it echoes, fail the
  6: //! oldest request after a malformed reply, or drain a failed worker.
  7: 
  8: use std::collections::VecDeque;
  9: 
 10: use crate::application::ports::ChunkRequest;
 11: 
 12: #[derive(Debug)]
 13: struct WorkerRequests {
 14:     accepting_work: bool,
 15:     in_flight: VecDeque<ChunkRequest>,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: /// Per-worker request ownership. Request identity is always checked through
 19: /// [`ChunkRequest::is_same_request`], never by chunk coordinates alone.
 20: #[derive(Debug)]
 21: pub(crate) struct GenerationWorkerRequests {
 22:     workers: Vec<WorkerRequests>,
 23: }
 24: 
 25: impl GenerationWorkerRequests {
 26:     pub(crate) fn new(worker_count: usize) -> Self {
 27:         assert!(
 28:             worker_count > 0,
 29:             "a worker ledger needs at least one worker"
 30:         );
 31:         Self {
 32:             workers: (0..worker_count)
 33:                 .map(|_| WorkerRequests {
 34:                     accepting_work: true,
 35:                     in_flight: VecDeque::new(),
 36:                 })
 37:                 .collect(),
 38:         }
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     /// Finds the next healthy worker, wrapping once from `start`.
 42:     pub(crate) fn next_accepting(&self, start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
 43:         (0..self.workers.len())
 44:             .map(|offset| (start + offset) % self.workers.len())
 45:             .find(|&index| self.workers[index].accepting_work)
 46:     }
 47: 
 48:     pub(crate) fn assign(&mut self, worker_index: usize, request: ChunkRequest) {
 49:         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
 50:         debug_assert!(worker.accepting_work);
 51:         worker.in_flight.push_back(request);
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     /// Retires only the exact request echoed by a well-formed worker reply.
 55:     /// Unknown and stale replies leave all current work untouched.
 56:     pub(crate) fn finish_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> bool {
 57:         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed).is_some()
 58:     }
 59: 
 60:     /// Retires an exact request reported as failed by the worker protocol.
 61:     pub(crate) fn fail_exact(
 62:         &mut self,
 63:         worker_index: usize,
 64:         echoed: &ChunkRequest,
 65:     ) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 66:         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed)
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     /// A worker processes its queue serially, so a malformed response belongs
 70:     /// to its oldest outstanding request even when its envelope cannot be
 71:     /// decoded far enough to recover an id.
 72:     pub(crate) fn fail_oldest(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 73:         self.workers[worker_index].in_flight.pop_front()
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     /// Stops scheduling to a broken worker and returns all work the engine
 77:     /// must retry. Calling this more than once is harmless.
 78:     pub(crate) fn disable_and_drain(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
 79:         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
 80:         worker.accepting_work = false;
 81:         worker.in_flight.drain(..).collect()
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     fn take_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 85:         let queue = &mut self.workers[worker_index].in_flight;
 86:         let position = queue
 87:             .iter()
 88:             .position(|request| request.is_same_request(echoed))?;
 89:         queue.remove(position)
 90:     }
 91: }
 92: 
 93: #[cfg(test)]
 94: mod tests {
 95:     use super::*;
 96:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 97: 
 98:     fn request(id: u32, x: f32) -> ChunkRequest {
 99:         ChunkRequest {
100:             request_id: id,
101:             origin_x: x,
102:             origin_z: -4.0,
103:             level: 0,
104:             lod: 1,
105:             reality: RealitySnapshot::default(),
106:         }
107:     }
108: 
109:     #[test]
110:     fn scheduling_wraps_and_skips_disabled_workers() {
111:         let mut requests = GenerationWorkerRequests::new(3);
112:         assert_eq!(requests.next_accepting(2), Some(2));
113:         requests.disable_and_drain(2);
114:         assert_eq!(requests.next_accepting(2), Some(0));
115:         requests.disable_and_drain(0);
116:         requests.disable_and_drain(1);
117:         assert_eq!(requests.next_accepting(0), None);
118:     }
119: 
120:     #[test]
121:     fn stale_reply_cannot_retire_current_work() {
122:         let mut requests = GenerationWorkerRequests::new(1);
123:         let current = request(8, 12.0);
124:         requests.assign(0, current.clone());
125: 
126:         let mut stale = current.clone();
127:         stale.request_id = 7;
128:         assert!(!requests.finish_exact(0, &stale));
129:         assert!(requests.finish_exact(0, &current));
130:     }
131: 
132:     #[test]
133:     fn malformed_reply_fails_only_the_oldest_serial_request() {
134:         let mut requests = GenerationWorkerRequests::new(1);
135:         let first = request(1, 0.0);
136:         let second = request(2, 16.0);
137:         requests.assign(0, first.clone());
138:         requests.assign(0, second.clone());
139: 
140:         assert_eq!(requests.fail_oldest(0), Some(first));
141:         assert!(requests.finish_exact(0, &second));
142:     }
143: 
144:     #[test]
145:     fn worker_failure_drains_its_work_without_affecting_other_workers() {
146:         let mut requests = GenerationWorkerRequests::new(2);
147:         let first = request(1, 0.0);
148:         let second = request(2, 16.0);
149:         requests.assign(0, first.clone());
150:         requests.assign(1, second.clone());
151: 
152:         assert_eq!(requests.disable_and_drain(0), vec![first]);
153:         assert_eq!(requests.next_accepting(0), Some(1));
154:         assert!(requests.finish_exact(1, &second));
155:         assert!(requests.disable_and_drain(0).is_empty());
156:     }
157: 
158:     #[test]
159:     fn explicit_failure_requires_the_exact_request_identity() {
160:         let mut requests = GenerationWorkerRequests::new(1);
161:         let current = request(5, 0.0);
162:         requests.assign(0, current.clone());
163:         let mut wrong_identity = current.clone();
164:         wrong_identity.lod = 0;
165: 
166:         assert!(requests.fail_exact(0, &wrong_identity).is_none());
167:         assert_eq!(requests.fail_exact(0, &current), Some(current));
168:     }
169: }

 1: # Workspace root. Layout:
 2: #   .              -> `vackrooms` core: Entities + Use Cases + Interface Adapters,
 3: #                     plus the native dev server binary (Frameworks & Drivers).
 4: #                     The library is platform-agnostic and also compiles to wasm32.

11: name = "vackrooms"
12: version = "0.1.0"
13: edition = "2024"
14: 
15: [dependencies]
16: # default-features disabled so the `os_rng`/getrandom backend is never pulled in;
17: # every RNG in the engine is deterministically seeded (StdRng::seed_from_u64),
18: # which keeps the core buildable on wasm32-unknown-unknown.

  1: You did **well on the renderer architecture**: the new `SplatRenderer` is actually implemented as the intended GPU microvoxel-face path, with flat per-face lighting, compact 16-byte instances, hardware depth/culling, retained greedy shadow casting, and low/high Pi-oriented budgets. The remaining problems are concentrated in two places: **chunk work is still synchronous on the browser’s only WASM thread**, causing generation locks, and **the splat lighting path is not preserving the yellow wall albedo under flashlight/direct light**.   2: 
  3: ## What is complete
  4: 
  5: The face path is much better than the original “one raw face per voxel” direction: `faceinstances.rs` derives its instances from the same greedy `MergedQuad` source as the mesh shadow caster, caps large faces to 2.5 world units so flat lighting cannot smear across a huge wall, and buckets them into cells for range-level culling. That means visible geometry and shadow geometry share the same boundary instead of drifting apart.  11: ## Why it locks up
 12: 
 13: The lockup is **not primarily a GPU splat issue**. The game remains single-threaded WASM: when a new section is required, `LocalChunkSource::load()` synchronously performs the full pipeline—halo generation, crop, surface-mesh/face-instance extraction, SVO construction, GPU serialization, and collision-AABB extraction—before the browser can render the next frame.  14: 
 15: Your engine does limit the *number* of loads per tick, and it loads coarse chunks before later refinement, but each selected load is still an indivisible, blocking job. The codebase’s architecture notes explicitly identify that there is no background meshing thread in single-threaded WASM; the current answer is time slicing, while Web Worker/WASM-thread generation is listed as the future solution.  16: 
 17: The likely trigger when crossing into another chunk is therefore:
 18: 
 19: ```text
 20: Player crosses streaming boundary
 21: -> required resident set changes
 22: -> Engine calls synchronous ChunkSource::load()
 23: -> one whole chunk pipeline runs on the main WASM/UI thread
 24: -> rendering/input/event loop cannot run
 25: -> visible freeze
 26: ```
 27: 
 28: The initial load may feel acceptable because it happens behind the loading overlay. Later section generation happens while the player is moving, so the same cost becomes a lock-up.
 29: 
 30: ## Multithreading target
 31: 
 32: Move **only pure chunk construction** to workers first. Keep the game loop, WebGL, renderer resource ownership, player state, input, and chunk-store mutation on the main thread.
 33: 
 34: ```text
 35: Main thread
 36:   StreamingPolicy decides required chunk keys
 37:   -> enqueue (origin, LOD, seed, config, request generation)
 38:   -> continue rendering current resident set
 39:   <- receive completed ChunkPayload
 40:   -> validate request is still wanted
 41:   -> upload face/mesh/light GPU buffers
 42:   -> install collision + chunk payload
 43: 
 44: Worker pool
 45:   Generate architectural VoxelGrid with halo
 46:   -> BFS voxel lighting
 47:   -> build greedy surface mesh / face instances
 48:   -> build SVO + serialize atlas data
 49:   -> extract collision AABBs
 50:   -> post ChunkPayload back
 51: ```
 52: 
 53: This split is clean because `LocalChunkSource::load()` already encapsulates exactly those pure operations, and its output is a self-contained `ChunkPayload`.  54: 
 55: ## Do this before threads
 56: 
 57: Before adding workers, add per-stage timing around `load()` so you know what actually freezes:
 58: 
 59: - Region/architectural generation
 60: - BFS light propagation
 61: - Surface mesh + face-instance extraction
 62: - SVO build
 63: - GPU serialization
 64: - Collision extraction
 65: - Main-thread GPU buffer upload
 66: 
 67: Your telemetry already has a port architecture, and the renderer already exposes GPU timing and splat counts, so adding per-chunk CPU stage timings will identify whether the main offender is generation, mesh extraction, SVO recursion, or WebGL upload.  69: Also make the main thread reject stale work: if the player has moved away before a worker completes a chunk, discard its payload rather than uploading it. Worker results must be keyed by `(origin, lod, generation_epoch)` so an old fine result cannot overwrite a newer resident decision.
 70: 
 71: ## Worker constraints
 72: 
 73: WebAssembly threads with shared memory require cross-origin isolation in browsers, typically `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` plus `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. If you do not want to impose that immediately, use ordinary Web Workers with a second WASM instance and transfer completed typed-array payloads back; it will still remove the visible UI freeze, though payload transfer/allocation overhead must be measured.
 74: 
 75: Do **not** share a WebGL context with generation workers. WebGL buffer and texture creation should remain on the render thread; workers should output plain serialized chunk data.

 83: The most likely failure modes are:
 84: 
 85: 1. **Direct flashlight light is added as neutral grey after albedo is lost**, such as writing `vec3(lightAmount)` instead of multiplying yellow wall albedo by illumination.
 86: 2. **The flashlight bypasses or overwrites the material palette**, especially if the shader branches into a generic “lit surface” color.
 87: 3. **The 3D light volume is treated as grayscale intensity instead of RGB indirect light**, removing the warm/yellow information under direct illumination.
 88: 4. **The flat vertex-stage light output uses a white direct term but fails to preserve `materialColor`**, then fog simply mixes the already-grey result.
 89: 5. **The face material mapping differs from the greedy shader mapping**, so wall instances resolve to a default grey material rather than `VOXELWALL`.
 90: 
 91: The evidence points away from missing material data: `PackedFaceInstance` explicitly uploads `material`, and wall color is defined in the core SVO builder.  92: 
 93: ## Correct lighting rule
 94: 
 95: Every non-emissive surface should follow this rule:
 96: 
 97: \[
 98: \text{final surface color} =
 99: \text{wall albedo} \times
100: (\text{indirect light} + \text{direct flashlight/light contribution})
101: \]
102: 
103: Not this:
104: 
105: \[
106: \text{final surface color} =
107: \text{indirectly colored wall} + \text{white flashlight replacement}
108: \]
109: 
110: In shader terms, make the material color the immutable base:
111: 
112: ```glsl
113: vec3 albedo = materialColor(aFaceMeta.w); // wall -> vec3(0.867, 0.800, 0.400)
114: 
115: vec3 indirect = sampleLightVolume(faceCenter) * aoTerm;
116: vec3 direct = flashlightTerm + selectedFixtureTerms;
117: vec3 lighting = max(indirect, vec3(0.04)) + direct;
118: 
119: // Preserve material hue under all direct illumination.
120: vec3 lit = albedo * lighting;
121: 
122: // Only emissive fixtures bypass ordinary albedo lighting.
123: if (isEmissive) {
124:     lit = max(lit, emissiveFixtureColor);
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: The flashlight should make the walls become **brighter yellow**, perhaps slightly desaturated at extreme brightness after tone mapping, but never neutral grey.
129: 
130: ## Lighting restoration order
131: 
132: 1. Render `materialColor` only—no fog, lights, AO, or shadow—and verify walls are unmistakably `0xddcc66`.
133: 2. Add baked light-volume RGB multiplied by albedo; verify dark walls remain yellow-brown rather than grey.
134: 3. Add AO and face-direction bands.
135: 4. Add flashlight alone; verify it brightens yellow, not replaces it.
136: 5. Add fixture lights.
137: 6. Add hero shadow.
138: 7. Add fog last.
139: 
140: This isolates the exact pass that destroys the wall color instead of tuning all lighting at once.
141: 
142: ## Best next change
143: 
144: Do **not** begin with all the complexity of shared-memory WASM threads. First, profile and split `LocalChunkSource::load()` into measurable stages; then put that pure pipeline in a worker queue while the current renderer keeps drawing the previous resident set. In parallel, add the material-only shader debug mode and fix the flashlight equation before changing any more lighting aesthetics. [ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/6575456/ab41dcc8-f278-45ea-bf6f-5471d0de6e55/repomix-output.json?AWSAccessKeyId=ASIA2F3EMEYEUNKBDGCY&Signature=F%2FDYJSkuyq%2F7o9epLmsNDjRFXyQ%3D&x-amz-security-token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEPL%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJGMEQCIBLo83%2BRB7u8wThue5C96yz28Sm1LtoJD9cbXhhWUtThAiB7Yfj0JmF4YAPykj5galiYafeTL6BujDFOWTtD2sQmEir8BAi7%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F8BEAEaDDY5OTc1MzMwOTcwNSIMVbIUrxiHU%2FAKYJ87KtAEZcM0pjXLz2Mkg7pl18xV%2FSYpnjZ5NXbFXxF7X5YnbhlIZVljbiApa4J0XFqb3WVStFYHwUhqm76dFL%2Flkq47gQdRdM%2F%2B7oA5ZuxGOiZv6EbJTXr2HCnUbMUK4zA8BYKZiavzkpjIUDfM3hmxJHfBPEXoHIxKbyPVkPxEN6P9NA9WqsuQIFxJ4hCMuQHIpKqKm5MDki38U0G4OKlwjEEN2UGQSY4ZT2TWeV%2BN0Z%2FKyf2OZ87FwQKq%2FovUMVnZLweb9mhzeb7nTCNJgCDT3aGIE67RnOQAOuKFQ48L%2B%2FNcK%2BNtz%2Flm7%2BHXpONNlgK2%2F0ulovyLBa%2FGlRMBKwkUrPR38yjD9EdOfNzc31CpiCIaH6q4Mzlqnxfq6XBwPfdhkKI2OlxmaVx3CZ4ybTSBYln1uKZOsTwaQWaYIAyFy9G0NLOEb4q%2F3B%2FLvpfpQHWDG4KDUezz%2BKjIwitmArnFsCpLfxppZfRMmLPV%2BLvE%2BU%2Bk7BFyMXc%2FymY8CrcLyIIu208NHKYsR0%2F22nqqfmneV1RTYVng%2BIlUgdIkvMHhIMdZoy%2FPFjCnuMv3DYCatMnlLg93t%2B2fbOFExP%2Fo0dzDoC7cx3SxyBJ%2BMl0%2B0t45LjpGTwzIHChQKrbuSRtgPmMXs%2FgSuWe06SWIrT5UOdYlr%2B3q%2BE%2FzOYxxcd9tyWMLVOQE5YwnOrcl5TrnrLcPoAoj9L88UQwVXF3qWPSuZQtRLnFSZlKo0LT55j%2Fhr6lfrUyqpVFy9yseh4s2rIkxEuN2kYdTYJUik7u1j1ESyX%2FnJyCwpzCt3sTSBjqZAZvHbt1emQDF054tPL%2F6z%2B0gwNXwe%2BYK8YoT2BbL0J%2FznQgBxYy%2Bf%2F6AfY%2Bgql6QoxtiXr0pLcxg0oAOnPBMqtsKILP1HJiaMofgZb0ndEIbfYJacko5EeBwKmVgnOA3vEPZuBVt7EmuTmu4kVNnwR%2F8xxsfVP7DgGtlhBAZiqMVRaje%2Fkf2njBCdm5cJBKZEmpN9E3Xs4nMeg%3D%3D&Expires=1783708928)

 1: # hierarchical z-buffer logic prototype
 2: import math
 3: 
 4: class CoarseZBuffer:
 5:     def __init__(self, width, height, cell_size=16):
 6:         self.width = width
 7:         self.height = height
 8:         self.cell_size = cell_size
 9:         self.cols = (width + cell_size - 1) // cell_size
10:         self.rows = (height + cell_size - 1) // cell_size
11:         self.buffer = [float('inf')] * (self.cols * self.rows)
12:     
13:     def test(self, x0, y0, x1, y1, z_near):
14:         # returns True if node is visible
15:         c0 = max(0, int(x0) // self.cell_size)
16:         r0 = max(0, int(y0) // self.cell_size)
17:         c1 = min(self.cols - 1, int(x1) // self.cell_size)
18:         r1 = min(self.rows - 1, int(y1) // self.cell_size)
19:         
20:         for r in range(r0, r1 + 1):
21:             for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
22:                 if z_near <= self.buffer[r * self.cols + c]:
23:                     return True
24:         return False
25:         
26:     def update(self, x0, y0, x1, y1, z_far):
27:         # Update is tricky. If we just splat a small node, it doesn't cover the whole cell.
28:         # We can only update the cell's stored depth if the splat COVERs the entire cell?
29:         # No, a coarse z-buffer stores the FARTHEST depth of any pixel in the cell.
30:         # Actually, if we track the NEAREST depth written so far per cell...
31:         pass
