## File: src/adapters/ascii_renderer.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
 2: 
 3: /// Interface for rendering the grid.
 4: pub trait GridRenderer {
 5:     fn render(&self, grid: &Grid) -> String;
 6: }
 7: 
 8: /// A concrete adapter that renders the Grid as an ASCII string.
 9: /// This fulfills the Clean Architecture requirement of decoupling the domain logic
10: /// from the presentation layer.
11: pub struct AsciiRenderer;
12: 
13: impl GridRenderer for AsciiRenderer {
14:     fn render(&self, grid: &Grid) -> String {
15:         let mut output = String::new();
16: 
17:         for y in 0..grid.depth() {
18:             // Top walls for this row
19:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
20:                 let cell = grid.get(x, y).unwrap();
21:                 output.push('+');
22:                 if cell.walls[0] {
23:                     // North
24:                     output.push_str("---");
25:                 } else {
26:                     output.push_str("   ");
27:                 }
28:             }
29:             output.push_str("+\n");
30: 
31:             // Side walls for this row
32:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
33:                 let cell = grid.get(x, y).unwrap();
34:                 if cell.walls[3] {
35:                     // West
36:                     output.push('|');
37:                 } else {
38:                     output.push(' ');
39:                 }
40:                 output.push_str("   "); // Inside of the room
41:             }
42:             // East wall of the last cell in the row
43:             let last_cell = grid.get(grid.width() - 1, y).unwrap();
44:             if last_cell.walls[1] {
45:                 // East
46:                 output.push('|');
47:             } else {
48:                 output.push(' ');
49:             }
50:             output.push('\n');
51:         }
52: 
53:         // Bottom walls for the last row
54:         for x in 0..grid.width() {
55:             let cell = grid.get(x, grid.depth() - 1).unwrap();
56:             output.push('+');
57:             if cell.walls[2] {
58:                 // South
59:                 output.push_str("---");
60:             } else {
61:                 output.push_str("   ");
62:             }
63:         }
64:         output.push_str("+\n");
65: 
66:         output
67:     }
68: }
69: 
70: #[cfg(test)]
71: mod tests {
72:     use super::*;
73:     use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
74: 
75:     #[test]
76:     fn test_ascii_renderer() {
77:         let mut grid = Grid::new(2, 2);
78:         // Modify some walls to test rendering
79:         if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(0, 0) {
80:             cell.walls[1] = false; // Remove East wall of (0,0)
81:         }
82:         if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(1, 0) {
83:             cell.walls[3] = false; // Remove West wall of (1,0)
84:         }
85: 
86:         let renderer = AsciiRenderer;
87:         let output = renderer.render(&grid);
88: 
89:         // Very basic validation, actual visual check is better in integration tests
90:         assert!(output.contains("+---+---+"));
91:     }
92: }
````

## File: src/adapters/chunk_voxel_renderer.rs
````rust
  1: /// Per-chunk voxel blueprint renderer.
  2: ///
  3: /// # Why a separate module?
  4: ///
  5: /// The existing `render_large_voxel_blueprint_svg` stitches N×N chunks into
  6: /// one giant SVG and is designed for batch export.  This module renders a
  7: /// *single* chunk — typically a 50×50 voxel grid at default spec — so the
  8: /// WASM call completes in < 5 ms and the browser can display the result
  9: /// instantly without a reload delay.
 10: ///
 11: /// # Architecture (Clean Architecture – Interface Adapter layer)
 12: ///
 13: /// This module occupies the Interface Adapter layer: it takes domain entities
 14: /// (`VoxelGrid`, `RegionPlan`, `Position`) and converts them into a string
 15: /// artifact (SVG) for the browser presentation layer.  It contains no
 16: /// business logic; all meaning lives in the entities it receives.
 17: 
 18: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
 19:     RegionPlan, SpaceProgram,
 20: };
 21: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 22:     VoxelGrid,
 23:     VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_CEILING,
 24:     VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_WATER, VOXEL_TREE,
 25: };
 26: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 27: 
 28: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 29: // Public API types
 30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 31: 
 32: /// Display toggles for the chunk voxel blueprint.
 33: ///
 34: /// Every field is a plain boolean so the JavaScript caller can wire each to a
 35: /// checkbox.  The `pixels_per_voxel` float controls visual density.
 36: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 37: pub struct VoxelBlueprintOptions {
 38:     /// SVG pixels per voxel cell.  8–12 works well for a 50×50 grid.
 39:     pub pixels_per_voxel: f32,
 40:     /// Draw hairline grid lines between every voxel cell.
 41:     pub show_grid: bool,
 42:     /// Fill each voxel cell with its material colour.
 43:     pub show_voxels: bool,
 44:     /// Draw coloured semantic bounding boxes (corridors, assemblies, doors…).
 45:     pub show_semantics: bool,
 46:     /// Print text labels on each semantic box.
 47:     pub show_labels: bool,
 48:     /// Include ceiling / light voxels in the fill pass.
 49:     pub show_ceiling: bool,
 50: }
 51: 
 52: impl Default for VoxelBlueprintOptions {
 53:     fn default() -> Self {
 54:         Self {
 55:             pixels_per_voxel: 10.0,
 56:             show_grid: true,
 57:             show_voxels: true,
 58:             show_semantics: true,
 59:             show_labels: true,
 60:             show_ceiling: true,
 61:         }
 62:     }
 63: }
 64: 
 65: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 66: // Pure helper functions (all deterministic, no side-effects)
 67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 68: 
 69: /// Convert a single world-space axis value into the chunk-local voxel float
 70: /// coordinate.  The VoxelGrid interior starts at index 1 (there is a 1-cell
 71: /// padding border), so we add +1.0 to align semantic world objects with the
 72: /// rendered cells.
 73: #[inline]
 74: fn world_to_voxel(world: f32, chunk_origin: f32, voxel_scale: f32) -> f32 {
 75:     (world - chunk_origin) / voxel_scale + 1.0
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Clip an axis-aligned rectangle given in voxel coordinates to the grid's
 79: /// interior region [1, grid_dim-1].  Returns `None` if the result is empty.
 80: ///
 81: /// Why +1 / -1 bounds? The VoxelGrid has a 1-cell padding on every face; the
 82: /// "real" chunk interior occupies [1, width-1] × [1, depth-1].
 83: #[inline]
 84: fn clip_rect(
 85:     x0: f32, z0: f32, x1: f32, z1: f32,
 86:     grid_w: f32, grid_d: f32,
 87: ) -> Option<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 88:     let cx0 = x0.max(1.0);
 89:     let cz0 = z0.max(1.0);
 90:     let cx1 = x1.min(grid_w - 1.0);
 91:     let cz1 = z1.min(grid_d - 1.0);
 92:     if cx1 > cx0 && cz1 > cz0 { Some((cx0, cz0, cx1, cz1)) } else { None }
 93: }
 94: 
 95: /// Return the canonical debug label for a `SpaceProgram` variant.
 96: const fn program_label(p: SpaceProgram) -> &'static str {
 97:     match p {
 98:         SpaceProgram::Arrival            => "ARRIVAL",
 99:         SpaceProgram::Reception          => "RECEPTION",
100:         SpaceProgram::MainCorridor       => "MAIN CORRIDOR",
101:         SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall      => "SECONDARY HALL",
102:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice         => "OPEN OFFICE",
103:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice      => "PRIVATE OFFICE",
104:         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom     => "CONFERENCE RM",
105:         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea        => "WAITING AREA",
106:         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom          => "BREAK ROOM",
107:         SpaceProgram::Storage            => "STORAGE",
108:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom         => "SERVER ROOM",
109:         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore       => "RESTROOM",
110:         SpaceProgram::Stair              => "STAIR",
111:         SpaceProgram::Mechanical         => "MECHANICAL",
112:         SpaceProgram::Atrium             => "ATRIUM",
113:         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "ABANDONED",
114:     }
115: }
116: 
117: /// Priority value for material layering: higher priority wins when a voxel
118: /// column contains multiple material types.
119: #[inline]
120: const fn material_priority(voxel: u8) -> u8 {
121:     match voxel {
122:         VOXEL_WALL | VOXEL_RED_WALL | VOXEL_TREE => 4,
123:         VOXEL_LIGHT | VOXEL_RED_LIGHT             => 3,
124:         VOXEL_CEILING                             => 2,
125:         VOXEL_FLOOR | VOXEL_GRASS | VOXEL_WATER   => 1,
126:         _                                         => 0,
127:     }
128: }
129: 
130: /// Map a winning material byte to its CSS class name.
131: #[inline]
132: const fn material_class(voxel: u8) -> &'static str {
133:     match voxel {
134:         VOXEL_WALL      => "vw",
135:         VOXEL_RED_WALL  => "vrw",
136:         VOXEL_TREE      => "vwt",
137:         VOXEL_LIGHT     => "vli",
138:         VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => "vrli",
139:         VOXEL_CEILING   => "vce",
140:         VOXEL_FLOOR     => "vfl",
141:         VOXEL_GRASS     => "vgr",
142:         VOXEL_WATER     => "vwa",
143:         _               => "vair",
144:     }
145: }
146: 
147: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148: // Main public function
149: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
150: 
151: /// Render a single chunk as a voxel-level blueprint SVG.
152: ///
153: /// # Render order (matches the spec)
154: /// 1. Dark background (set on the `<svg>` element itself).
155: /// 2. Per-voxel cell fills (column-collapsed material colour).
156: /// 3. Hairline voxel grid lines.
157: /// 4. Semantic bounding-box fills at ~13% opacity.
158: /// 5. Semantic outlines with contrasting stroke colour.
159: /// 6. Door / portal markers (green boxes).
160: /// 7. Text labels on each semantic box.
161: /// 8. Header bar and legend.
162: ///
163: /// # Arguments
164: /// * `grid`         – The generated `VoxelGrid` for this chunk.
165: /// * `plan`         – The `RegionPlan` that covers this chunk's world region.
166: /// * `chunk_origin` – World-space (x, z) of the chunk's min corner.
167: /// * `voxel_scale`  – World units per voxel (0.2 for low-spec, 0.1 for high-spec).
168: /// * `options`      – Display toggles.
169: pub fn render_chunk_voxel_blueprint_svg(
170:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
171:     plan: &RegionPlan,
172:     chunk_origin: Position,
173:     voxel_scale: f32,
174:     options: VoxelBlueprintOptions,
175: ) -> String {
176:     let ppv = options.pixels_per_voxel;
177: 
178:     let gw = grid.width();   // includes 1-cell padding on each side
179:     let gd = grid.depth();
180:     let gh = grid.height();
181: 
182:     let canvas_w = gw as f32 * ppv;
183:     let canvas_h = gd as f32 * ppv;
184: 
185:     // Derive chunk grid coordinates for the header label.
186:     // Interior cell count = width - 2 (strip the padding border).
187:     let interior = (gw as i32 - 2).max(1) as f32;
188:     let chunk_size_world = interior * voxel_scale;
189:     let cx_idx = if chunk_size_world > 0.0 {
190:         (chunk_origin.x / chunk_size_world).floor() as i32
191:     } else { 0 };
192:     let cz_idx = if chunk_size_world > 0.0 {
193:         (chunk_origin.z / chunk_size_world).floor() as i32
194:     } else { 0 };
195: 
196:     // ── Coordinate transform closures ─────────────────────────────────
197:     //
198:     // SVG Y axis is flipped: Y=0 is the top of the canvas, Y=canvas_h is the
199:     // bottom.  We want world-Z increasing upward, so:
200:     //   svg_y  = canvas_h - (vz + 1) * ppv   for integer voxel index vz
201:     //   svg_y  = canvas_h - vz_float * ppv    for float voxel coordinate
202:     //
203:     // The +1 in the integer version accounts for the padding border offset
204:     // already baked into the float version via world_to_voxel().
205: 
206:     let vox_px_x = |vx: usize| -> f32 { vx as f32 * ppv };
207:     let vox_px_y = |vz: usize| -> f32 { canvas_h - (vz + 1) as f32 * ppv };
208: 
209:     // World coord → float voxel index (accounts for padding offset).
210:     let w2vx = |wx: f32| -> f32 { world_to_voxel(wx, chunk_origin.x, voxel_scale) };
211:     let w2vz = |wz: f32| -> f32 { world_to_voxel(wz, chunk_origin.z, voxel_scale) };
212: 
213:     // Float voxel → SVG pixel.
214:     let vpx = |vx_f: f32| -> f32 { vx_f * ppv };
215:     let vpy_top = |vz_f: f32| -> f32 { canvas_h - vz_f * ppv };   // top edge of a box whose Z min = vz_f
216: 
217:     let label_fs  = (ppv * 1.1).max(7.0_f32).min(13.0_f32);
218:     let label_sm  = (ppv * 0.85).max(5.5_f32).min(10.0_f32);
219: 
220:     // ── Build SVG string ───────────────────────────────────────────────
221:     let mut svg = String::with_capacity(256 * 1024);
222: 
223:     // Header.
224:     svg.push_str(&format!(
225:         r#"<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
226:   viewBox="0 0 {cw} {ch}" width="{cw}" height="{ch}"
227:   style="display:block;background:#0b0f19;font-family:monospace">
228: <defs>
229:   <style>
230:     .vw   {{ fill:#1c2333 }}
231:     .vrw  {{ fill:#3b0b0b }}
232:     .vwt  {{ fill:#251510 }}
233:     .vli  {{ fill:#ff2222 }}
234:     .vrli {{ fill:#ff6666 }}
235:     .vce  {{ fill:#1a1f2e }}
236:     .vfl  {{ fill:#1a120880 }}
237:     .vgr  {{ fill:#0d1f0d80 }}
238:     .vwa  {{ fill:#0a102080 }}
239:     .vair {{ fill:#0b1422 }}
240:     .vgrid{{ stroke:#1e2d40; stroke-width:0.4; fill:none }}
241:     .lbl  {{ font-size:{lfs}px; dominant-baseline:hanging; pointer-events:none }}
242:     .lsm  {{ font-size:{lsm}px; dominant-baseline:hanging; pointer-events:none }}
243:   </style>
244: </defs>
245: "#,
246:         cw = canvas_w, ch = canvas_h,
247:         lfs = label_fs, lsm = label_sm,
248:     ));
249: 
250:     // ── Pass 1: voxel fills ────────────────────────────────────────────
251:     if options.show_voxels {
252:         svg.push_str("<g id=\"voxels\">\n");
253:         for vz in 0..gd {
254:             for vx in 0..gw {
255:                 // Column collapse: scan all Y layers, keep highest-priority material.
256:                 let mut winning: u8 = 0;
257:                 let mut winning_pri: u8 = 0;
258:                 for vy in 0..gh {
259:                     let v = grid.get(vx, vy, vz);
260:                     // Skip ceiling/fixture voxels when show_ceiling is off.
261:                     // Glimmers are ceiling fixtures too: leaving them in made
262:                     // blackout debug captures look like floor-level lights.
263:                     if !options.show_ceiling
264:                         && (v == VOXEL_CEILING
265:                             || v == VOXEL_LIGHT
266:                             || v == VOXEL_RED_LIGHT
267:                             || v == crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_GLIMMER)
268:                     {
269:                         continue;
270:                     }
271:                     let pri = material_priority(v);
272:                     if pri > winning_pri {
273:                         winning_pri = pri;
274:                         winning = v;
275:                     }
276:                 }
277:                 let px = vox_px_x(vx);
278:                 let py = vox_px_y(vz);
279:                 let cls = material_class(winning);
280:                 svg.push_str(&format!(
281:                     "<rect class=\"{cls}\" x=\"{px}\" y=\"{py}\" width=\"{ppv}\" height=\"{ppv}\"/>\n"
282:                 ));
283:             }
284:         }
285:         svg.push_str("</g>\n");
286:     }
287: 
288:     // ── Pass 2: voxel grid lines ───────────────────────────────────────
289:     if options.show_grid {
290:         svg.push_str("<g id=\"grid\" class=\"vgrid\">\n");
291:         for vx in 0..=gw {
292:             let px = vx as f32 * ppv;
293:             svg.push_str(&format!(
294:                 "<line x1=\"{px}\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"{px}\" y2=\"{canvas_h}\"/>\n"
295:             ));
296:         }
297:         for vz in 0..=gd {
298:             let py = vz as f32 * ppv;
299:             svg.push_str(&format!(
300:                 "<line x1=\"0\" y1=\"{py}\" x2=\"{canvas_w}\" y2=\"{py}\"/>\n"
301:             ));
302:         }
303:         svg.push_str("</g>\n");
304:     }
305: 
306:     // ── Pass 3+4+5: semantic overlays ─────────────────────────────────
307:     if options.show_semantics {
308:         svg.push_str("<g id=\"semantics\" pointer-events=\"none\">\n");
309: 
310:         // Inner macro: emit one semantic bounding box clipped to the chunk.
311:         //
312:         // Why a macro? The borrow checker forbids closures that capture `svg`
313:         // mutably while also borrowing coordinate-transform closures.  A macro
314:         // expands inline and avoids the borrow conflict entirely.
315:         macro_rules! emit_box {
316:             ($wx0:expr, $wz0:expr, $wx1:expr, $wz1:expr,
317:              $fill:literal, $stroke:literal, $dash:expr, $label:expr) => {{
318:                 let vx0 = w2vx($wx0);
319:                 let vz0 = w2vz($wz0);
320:                 let vx1 = w2vx($wx1);
321:                 let vz1 = w2vz($wz1);
322:                 let (rx0, rz0, rx1, rz1) = (vx0.min(vx1), vz0.min(vz1),
323:                                              vx0.max(vx1), vz0.max(vz1));
324:                 if let Some((cx0, cz0, cx1, cz1)) =
325:                     clip_rect(rx0, rz0, rx1, rz1, gw as f32, gd as f32)
326:                 {
327:                     // SVG box: top-left corner is the largest Z (because Y is flipped).
328:                     let sx  = vpx(cx0);
329:                     let sy  = vpy_top(cz1);  // SVG top = world Z max
330:                     let bw  = vpx(cx1) - sx;
331:                     let bh  = vpy_top(cz0) - sy; // world Z min → SVG bottom
332:                     let da: &str = if $dash { "stroke-dasharray=\"5,3\"" } else { "" };
333:                     svg.push_str(&format!(
334:                         "<rect fill=\"{fill}\" fill-opacity=\"0.13\" stroke=\"{stroke}\" stroke-width=\"1.5\" {da} x=\"{sx}\" y=\"{sy}\" width=\"{bw}\" height=\"{bh}\"/>\n",
335:                         fill = $fill, stroke = $stroke, da = da,
336:                         sx = sx, sy = sy, bw = bw, bh = bh,
337:                     ));
338:                     if options.show_labels {
339:                         let label_str: &str = $label;
340:                         if !label_str.is_empty() {
341:                             svg.push_str(&format!(
342:                                 "<text class=\"lbl\" x=\"{tx}\" y=\"{ty}\" fill=\"{stroke}\">{label}</text>\n",
343:                                 tx = sx + 3.0, ty = sy + 3.0,
344:                                 stroke = $stroke, label = label_str,
345:                             ));
346:                         }
347:                     }
348:                 }
349:             }};
350:         }
351: 
352:         // Corridors — draw each path segment's bounding rect ± half-width.
353:         // We draw per-segment rather than the whole path AABB so that
354:         // L-shaped corridors clip correctly at the chunk boundary.
355:         for spine in &plan.corridors {
356:             if spine.path.len() < 2 { continue; }
357:             let hw = spine.width * 0.5;
358:             let (fill, stroke, label_text) = match spine.spine_kind {
359:                 SpaceProgram::MainCorridor =>
360:                     ("#00ffff", "#00e5ff",
361:                      format!("{} · {:.1}m", program_label(spine.spine_kind), spine.width)),
362:                 _ =>
363:                     ("#a855f7", "#c084fc",
364:                      format!("{} · {:.1}m", program_label(spine.spine_kind), spine.width)),
365:             };
366:             for seg in spine.path.windows(2) {
367:                 let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
368:                 let x0 = a.x.min(b.x) - hw;
369:                 let z0 = a.z.min(b.z) - hw;
370:                 let x1 = a.x.max(b.x) + hw;
371:                 let z1 = a.z.max(b.z) + hw;
372:                 if fill == "#00ffff" {
373:                     emit_box!(x0, z0, x1, z1, "#00ffff", "#00e5ff", false, label_text.as_str());
374:                 } else {
375:                     emit_box!(x0, z0, x1, z1, "#a855f7", "#c084fc", false, label_text.as_str());
376:                 }
377:             }
378:         }
379: 
380:         // Assemblies (rooms).
381:         for asm in &plan.assemblies {
382:             let (mx, mz, xx, xz) = asm.footprint.bounds();
383:             let label_text = format!("#{} {}", asm.id, program_label(asm.program));
384:             if asm.corruption.abandoned {
385:                 emit_box!(mx, mz, xx, xz, "#ff00ff", "#e879f9", false, label_text.as_str());
386:             } else {
387:                 emit_box!(mx, mz, xx, xz, "#ffffff", "#cbd5e1", false, label_text.as_str());
388:             }
389: 
390:             // Sub-spaces within the assembly.
391:             for space in &asm.spaces {
392:                 let (sx0, sz0, sx1, sz1) = space.footprint.bounds();
393:                 emit_box!(sx0, sz0, sx1, sz1, "#94a3b8", "#64748b", false,
394:                           program_label(space.program));
395:             }
396: 
397:             // Ceiling zones (dashed gold).
398:             for cz in &asm.ceiling_zones {
399:                 let (zx0, zz0, zx1, zz1) = cz.area.bounds();
400:                 let clabel = format!("VAULT · {:.1}m", cz.height_units);
401:                 emit_box!(zx0, zz0, zx1, zz1, "#ca8a04", "#fbbf24", true, clabel.as_str());
402:             }
403: 
404:             // Openings / portals (green).
405:             for opening in &asm.entrances {
406:                 let hw = opening.width * 0.5;
407:                 let (ox0, oz0, ox1, oz1) = if opening.through_x_wall {
408:                     (opening.center.x - hw, opening.center.z - voxel_scale,
409:                      opening.center.x + hw, opening.center.z + voxel_scale)
410:                 } else {
411:                     (opening.center.x - voxel_scale, opening.center.z - hw,
412:                      opening.center.x + voxel_scale, opening.center.z + hw)
413:                 };
414:                 let plabel = format!("PORTAL · {:.1}m", opening.width);
415:                 emit_box!(ox0, oz0, ox1, oz1, "#10b981", "#34d399", false, plabel.as_str());
416:             }
417:         }
418: 
419:         svg.push_str("</g>\n");
420:     }
421: 
422:     // ── Chunk boundary dashed border ──────────────────────────────────
423:     let bi = 0.5_f32;
424:     svg.push_str(&format!(
425:         "<rect id=\"chunk-border\" x=\"{bi}\" y=\"{bi}\" width=\"{bw}\" height=\"{bh}\" \
426:          fill=\"none\" stroke=\"#6b7280\" stroke-width=\"1.5\" stroke-dasharray=\"6,4\"/>\n",
427:         bi = bi,
428:         bw = canvas_w - bi * 2.0,
429:         bh = canvas_h - bi * 2.0,
430:     ));
431: 
432:     // ── Header strip ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
433:     let header = format!(
434:         "CHUNK ({cx}, {cz})  ·  {ic}×{ic} voxels  ·  {vs}m/voxel",
435:         cx = cx_idx, cz = cz_idx,
436:         ic = interior as usize, vs = voxel_scale,
437:     );
438:     let header_h = ppv * 1.8;
439:     svg.push_str(&format!(
440:         "<rect x=\"0\" y=\"0\" width=\"{cw}\" height=\"{hh}\" fill=\"#0f172a\" fill-opacity=\"0.9\"/>\n\
441:          <text class=\"lbl\" x=\"6\" y=\"5\" fill=\"#38bdf8\" font-weight=\"bold\">{header}</text>\n",
442:         cw = canvas_w, hh = header_h, header = header,
443:     ));
444: 
445:     // ── Legend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
446:     if options.show_labels {
447:         let legend_items: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
448:             ("vw",   "WALL"),
449:             ("vrw",  "RED WALL"),
450:             ("vli",  "LIGHT"),
451:             ("vrli", "RED LIGHT"),
452:             ("vfl",  "FLOOR"),
453:             ("vce",  "CEILING"),
454:         ];
455:         let legend_col_w = ppv * 8.5;
456:         let legend_row_h = ppv * 1.1;
457:         let legend_x = canvas_w - legend_col_w - 4.0;
458:         let legend_total_h = legend_row_h * (legend_items.len() as f32) + 6.0;
459:         let legend_y = canvas_h - legend_total_h - 4.0;
460:         svg.push_str(&format!(
461:             "<rect x=\"{lx}\" y=\"{ly}\" width=\"{lw}\" height=\"{lh}\" \
462:              fill=\"#0f172a\" fill-opacity=\"0.88\" rx=\"3\"/>\n",
463:             lx = legend_x, ly = legend_y,
464:             lw = legend_col_w, lh = legend_total_h,
465:         ));
466:         for (i, (cls, label)) in legend_items.iter().enumerate() {
467:             let ry = legend_y + 3.0 + i as f32 * legend_row_h;
468:             svg.push_str(&format!(
469:                 "<rect class=\"{cls}\" x=\"{sx}\" y=\"{ry}\" width=\"{ppv}\" height=\"{ppv}\"/>\n\
470:                  <text class=\"lsm\" x=\"{tx}\" y=\"{ry}\" fill=\"#94a3b8\">{label}</text>\n",
471:                 cls = cls,
472:                 sx = legend_x + 3.0,
473:                 ry = ry, ppv = ppv,
474:                 tx = legend_x + ppv + 6.0,
475:                 label = label,
476:             ));
477:         }
478:     }
479: 
480:     svg.push_str("</svg>\n");
481:     svg
482: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Semantic crossings and hazards exported beside generated voxel geometry.
  2: //!
  3: //! These records describe interaction surfaces; they do not decide how a
  4: //! reality changes. The application detects a crossing, then the reality
  5: //! reducer interprets it as a deterministic state transition.
  6: 
  7: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  8: 
  9: use super::geometry::{Axis2, AxisDirection, WorldBounds, decode_axis, decode_direction};
 10: use super::phenomena::{AnomalyId, AnomalyKind, decode_kind};
 11: 
 12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
 13: #[repr(u8)]
 14: pub enum TraversalGateKind {
 15:     Remap = 0,
 16:     RedThreshold = 1,
 17:     RedLoop = 2,
 18:     RedEscape = 3,
 19: }
 20: 
 21: /// A semantic plane crossing. `span_*` lies on the perpendicular world axis.
 22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 23: pub struct TraversalGate {
 24:     pub id: u64,
 25:     pub instance_id: AnomalyId,
 26:     pub anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind,
 27:     pub kind: TraversalGateKind,
 28:     pub axis: Axis2,
 29:     pub plane: f32,
 30:     pub span_min: f32,
 31:     pub span_max: f32,
 32:     /// For directional thresholds (red rooms), the authored inward direction.
 33:     pub forward: AxisDirection,
 34:     pub affected_bounds: WorldBounds,
 35: }
 36: 
 37: impl TraversalGate {
 38:     /// Returns traversal direction when a movement segment crosses the plane
 39:     /// inside its span. Merely touching or moving parallel does not fire.
 40:     pub fn crossing(&self, old: [f32; 2], new: [f32; 2]) -> Option<AxisDirection> {
 41:         let (a0, a1, b0, b1) = match self.axis {
 42:             Axis2::X => (old[0], new[0], old[1], new[1]),
 43:             Axis2::Z => (old[1], new[1], old[0], new[0]),
 44:         };
 45:         let delta = a1 - a0;
 46:         if delta.abs() < 1e-6 {
 47:             return None;
 48:         }
 49:         let t = (self.plane - a0) / delta;
 50:         if !(0.0 < t && t <= 1.0) {
 51:             return None;
 52:         }
 53:         let across = b0 + (b1 - b0) * t;
 54:         if across < self.span_min || across > self.span_max {
 55:             return None;
 56:         }
 57:         Some(if delta > 0.0 {
 58:             AxisDirection::Positive
 59:         } else {
 60:             AxisDirection::Negative
 61:         })
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     pub const WORDS: usize = 15;
 65: 
 66:     pub fn to_words(self) -> [u32; Self::WORDS] {
 67:         [
 68:             self.id as u32,
 69:             (self.id >> 32) as u32,
 70:             self.instance_id as u32,
 71:             (self.instance_id >> 32) as u32,
 72:             self.anomaly_kind as u32,
 73:             self.kind as u32,
 74:             self.axis as u32,
 75:             self.plane.to_bits(),
 76:             self.span_min.to_bits(),
 77:             self.span_max.to_bits(),
 78:             self.forward as u32,
 79:             self.affected_bounds.min_x.to_bits(),
 80:             self.affected_bounds.min_z.to_bits(),
 81:             self.affected_bounds.max_x.to_bits(),
 82:             self.affected_bounds.max_z.to_bits(),
 83:         ]
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     pub fn from_words(words: &[u32]) -> Option<Self> {
 87:         if words.len() != Self::WORDS {
 88:             return None;
 89:         }
 90:         Some(Self {
 91:             id: words[0] as u64 | ((words[1] as u64) << 32),
 92:             instance_id: words[2] as u64 | ((words[3] as u64) << 32),
 93:             anomaly_kind: decode_kind(words[4])?,
 94:             kind: match words[5] {
 95:                 0 => TraversalGateKind::Remap,
 96:                 1 => TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
 97:                 2 => TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
 98:                 3 => TraversalGateKind::RedEscape,
 99:                 _ => return None,
100:             },
101:             axis: decode_axis(words[6])?,
102:             plane: f32::from_bits(words[7]),
103:             span_min: f32::from_bits(words[8]),
104:             span_max: f32::from_bits(words[9]),
105:             forward: decode_direction(words[10])?,
106:             affected_bounds: WorldBounds::new(
107:                 f32::from_bits(words[11]),
108:                 f32::from_bits(words[12]),
109:                 f32::from_bits(words[13]),
110:                 f32::from_bits(words[14]),
111:             ),
112:         })
113:     }
114: }
115: 
116: /// A physical doorway between Backrooms levels. Unlike a [`TraversalGate`],
117: /// crossing one does not advance encounter state — it swaps which level
118: /// generator the application streams from, arriving at `arrival`.
119: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
120: pub struct LevelExit {
121:     pub id: u64,
122:     /// The `GeneratorConfig::level` id on the far side of the door.
123:     pub target_level: u32,
124:     /// Trigger-volume center on the walking plane.
125:     pub center: Position,
126:     /// Trigger half-extent (square) around `center`.
127:     pub half_extent: f32,
128:     /// Arrival point in the *target* level's coordinate space.
129:     pub arrival: Position,
130: }
131: 
132: impl LevelExit {
133:     pub const WORDS: usize = 9;
134: 
135:     pub fn contains(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> bool {
136:         (x - self.center.x).abs() <= self.half_extent
137:             && (z - self.center.z).abs() <= self.half_extent
138:     }
139: 
140:     pub fn to_words(self) -> [u32; Self::WORDS] {
141:         [
142:             self.id as u32,
143:             (self.id >> 32) as u32,
144:             self.target_level,
145:             self.center.x.to_bits(),
146:             self.center.z.to_bits(),
147:             self.half_extent.to_bits(),
148:             self.arrival.x.to_bits(),
149:             self.arrival.z.to_bits(),
150:             0, // reserved (orientation, future arrival yaw)
151:         ]
152:     }
153: 
154:     pub fn from_words(words: &[u32]) -> Option<Self> {
155:         if words.len() != Self::WORDS {
156:             return None;
157:         }
158:         Some(Self {
159:             id: words[0] as u64 | ((words[1] as u64) << 32),
160:             target_level: words[2],
161:             center: Position::new(f32::from_bits(words[3]), f32::from_bits(words[4])),
162:             half_extent: f32::from_bits(words[5]),
163:             arrival: Position::new(f32::from_bits(words[6]), f32::from_bits(words[7])),
164:         })
165:     }
166: }
167: 
168: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
169: pub struct PitHazard {
170:     pub id: u64,
171:     pub instance_id: AnomalyId,
172:     pub center: Position,
173:     pub half_side: f32,
174:     pub depth: f32,
175:     pub recovery: Position,
176: }
177: 
178: impl PitHazard {
179:     pub fn contains(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> bool {
180:         (x - self.center.x).abs() < self.half_side && (z - self.center.z).abs() < self.half_side
181:     }
182: 
183:     pub const TRANSPORT_WORDS: usize = 10;
184: 
185:     pub fn write_words(self, out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
186:         out.extend_from_slice(&[
187:             self.id as u32,
188:             (self.id >> 32) as u32,
189:             self.instance_id as u32,
190:             (self.instance_id >> 32) as u32,
191:             self.center.x.to_bits(),
192:             self.center.z.to_bits(),
193:             self.half_side.to_bits(),
194:             self.depth.to_bits(),
195:             self.recovery.x.to_bits(),
196:             self.recovery.z.to_bits(),
197:         ]);
198:     }
199: 
200:     pub fn from_transport_words(words: &[u32]) -> Option<Self> {
201:         if words.len() != Self::TRANSPORT_WORDS {
202:             return None;
203:         }
204:         Some(Self {
205:             id: words[0] as u64 | ((words[1] as u64) << 32),
206:             instance_id: words[2] as u64 | ((words[3] as u64) << 32),
207:             center: Position::new(f32::from_bits(words[4]), f32::from_bits(words[5])),
208:             half_side: f32::from_bits(words[6]),
209:             depth: f32::from_bits(words[7]),
210:             recovery: Position::new(f32::from_bits(words[8]), f32::from_bits(words[9])),
211:         })
212:     }
213: }
````

````rust
 2: pub enum MicrobiomeZone {

18: /// Represents a single room or cell in the Backrooms maze.

26:     pub is_corridor: bool, // Part 1: Hallways
27: }

29: impl Cell {
30:     /// Creates a new, unvisited cell with all walls intact and no anomalies.
31:     pub fn new() -> Self {
32:         Self {
33:             visited: false,

42: #[cfg(test)]
````

## File: src/domain/entities/world_topology.rs

  1: //! Pure domain language for the infinite macro-scale world graph.
  2: //!
  3: //! The world is not a heap of independent regions: it is an unbounded,
  4: //! lazily evaluated *graph* whose vertices are architectural places and whose
  5: //! edges are portals and vertical links. This module holds only that
  6: //! language — plain data with stable identities — so every layer above it
  7: //! (macro planner, region planner, voxelizer) can agree on what the world
  8: //! *is* without agreeing on how it is rendered.
  9: //!
 10: //! Scale hierarchy (each level constrains the one below it):
 11: //!
 12: //! ```text
 13: //! world seed
 14: //!   -> MacroFields        multi-octave parameter fields (this file: data)
 15: //!     -> MacroCell        160 u graph cell: nodes, portals, vertical links
 16: //!       -> RegionPlan     80 u architectural plan (entities::architecture)
 17: //!         -> ColumnPlan   one voxel column (use_cases::level_zero)
 18: //! ```
 19: //!
 20: //! Determinism contract: everything here is derived from
 21: //! `(seed, lattice coordinate)` by the planner in
 22: //! `use_cases::world_topology`; nothing stored in these types may depend on
 23: //! query order, chunk size, or LOD. Neighboring macro cells must compute
 24: //! *identical* shared portals from their own side of an edge.
 25: 
 26: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 27: 
 28: /// Side of one macro graph cell, world units. Exactly 2×2 regions and one
 29: /// anomaly macro-lattice cell, so all three lattices stay phase-aligned.
 30: pub const MACRO_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 160.0;
 31: 
 32: /// Regions per macro cell along each axis (`MACRO_CELL_SIZE / REGION_SIZE`).
 33: pub const REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL: i64 = 2;
 34: 
 35: /// Address of one macro cell on the infinite lattice.
 36: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
 37: pub struct MacroCellId {
 38:     pub x: i64,
 39:     pub z: i64,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: impl MacroCellId {
 43:     pub fn new(x: i64, z: i64) -> Self {
 44:         Self { x, z }
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     /// The macro cell containing a world point.
 48:     pub fn containing(world_x: f32, world_z: f32) -> Self {
 49:         Self {
 50:             x: (world_x / MACRO_CELL_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 51:             z: (world_z / MACRO_CELL_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 52:         }
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /// The macro cell containing a region lattice coordinate.
 56:     pub fn of_region(region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Self {
 57:         Self {
 58:             x: region_x.div_euclid(REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL),
 59:             z: region_z.div_euclid(REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL),
 60:         }
 61:     }
 62: 
 63:     /// Lower-left world corner.
 64:     pub fn origin(&self) -> Position {
 65:         Position::new(
 66:             self.x as f32 * MACRO_CELL_SIZE,
 67:             self.z as f32 * MACRO_CELL_SIZE,
 68:         )
 69:     }
 70: 
 71:     /// World-space center (where the cell samples its parameter fields).
 72:     pub fn center(&self) -> Position {
 73:         Position::new(
 74:             (self.x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL_SIZE,
 75:             (self.z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL_SIZE,
 76:         )
 77:     }
 78: }
 79: 
 80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 81: // Parameter fields: what the fractal math is actually *for*.
 82: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 83: 
 84: /// Multi-octave deterministic parameters sampled at a world point.
 85: ///
 86: /// Noise never places a wall. It selects *where the building's rules change*:
 87: /// each field below biases a probability or a style choice in a planner, and
 88: /// the planner still decides the actual corridors, rooms, stairs and
 89: /// thresholds. All values are in `[0, 1]`.
 90: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
 91: pub struct MacroFields {
 92:     /// 0 = dense office warren, 1 = large incomplete open floor plates.
 93:     pub openness: f32,
 94:     /// Probability weight for stairwells, shafts and multi-height volumes.
 95:     pub vertical_pressure: f32,
 96:     /// 0 = freshly fitted out, 1 = decayed: dead lights, remnants, refits.
 97:     pub institution_age: f32,
 98:     /// Chance multiplier for impossible-architecture macro anomalies.
 99:     pub anomaly_pressure: f32,
100:     /// Red-room event clustering weight — rare, clustered, never uniform.
101:     pub redroom_pressure: f32,
102:     /// How much a neighboring architect genome leaks into this area.
103:     pub style_blend: f32,
104: }
105: 
106: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
107: // Graph vertices.
108: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
109: 
110: /// What a graph node *is*, architecturally. Region planners translate the
111: /// kind into concrete circulation and assemblies; the kind never carries
112: /// geometry itself.
113: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
114: pub enum PlaceKind {
115:     /// The default endless office labyrinth fabric.
116:     Warren,
117:     /// A broad incomplete floor plate: sparse columns, long sight lines.
118:     OpenPlate,
119:     /// A multi-height volume with exposed structure.
120:     Atrium,
121:     /// A region that hosts a planned vertical link (stairs / shaft).
122:     Stairwell,
123:     /// A region reserved for a red-room encounter assembly.
124:     RedRoomEncounter,
125: }
126: 
127: /// One vertex of the world graph: a region-sized place with a stable
128: /// identity, a kind, and a macro elevation. `elevation` is an integer story
129: /// index in macro space — vertical links connect nodes whose elevations
130: /// differ, they never invent terrain-style fractional heights.
131: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
132: pub struct WorldNode {
133:     pub id: u64,
134:     /// Region lattice coordinate this node plans.
135:     pub region: (i64, i64),
136:     pub kind: PlaceKind,
137:     /// Story index. The streamed world currently voxelizes elevation 0;
138:     /// links to other elevations are contracts for the vertical roadmap.
139:     pub elevation: i32,
140: }
141: 
142: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143: // Graph edges.
144: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
145: 
146: /// A shared crossing point on a region edge. Both regions adjacent to the
147: /// edge derive the identical portal from the *edge's* lattice coordinate —
148: /// this is the contract that lets the primary circulation chain across
149: /// regions forever.
150: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
151: pub struct Portal {
152:     pub id: u64,
153:     /// Vertical edge lattice coordinate: the edge plane is
154:     /// `x = edge_x * REGION_SIZE`.
155:     pub edge_x: i64,
156:     /// Region row the portal belongs to.
157:     pub row_z: i64,
158:     /// World point where the primary route crosses the edge.
159:     pub at: Position,
160: }
161: 
162: /// How a vertical link behaves. Ordinary stairs are honest; the endless
163: /// variants are anomalies whose far ends re-address the world instead of
164: /// meshing a literal infinite staircase.
165: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
166: pub enum VerticalLinkKind {
167:     /// Connects `elevation n` to `n + 1` over a constrained footprint.
168:     OrdinaryStair,
169:     /// Rises into a higher ceiling regime that never resolves — the flight
170:     /// visually continues into a dark aperture.
171:     EndlessAscent,
172:     /// Descends past believable landings into a re-addressed reality.
173:     EndlessDescent,
174:     /// A rare utilitarian shortcut: ladders, platforms, mechanical rooms.
175:     ServiceShaft,
176: }
177: 
178: /// One planned vertical connection anchored inside a region. The anchor is a
179: /// *reservation*: the region planner must place the corresponding stair
180: /// assembly near it (or fail loudly), never silently relocate it into a
181: /// different region.
182: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
183: pub struct VerticalLink {
184:     pub id: u64,
185:     pub kind: VerticalLinkKind,
186:     /// Region lattice coordinate that owns the reservation.
187:     pub region: (i64, i64),
188:     /// World-space anchor the stair footprint should gravitate toward.
189:     pub anchor: Position,
190:     pub from_elevation: i32,
191:     pub to_elevation: i32,
192: }
193: 
194: /// A red-room encounter planned as a *graph event*, not a biome. Events are
195: /// separated by a minimum macro-cell radius (the cooldown), and each event
196: /// targets exactly one region, where the planner promotes one ordinary
197: /// assembly into the encounter.
198: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
199: pub struct RedRoomEvent {
200:     pub id: u64,
201:     /// The single region this event targets.
202:     pub region: (i64, i64),
203:     /// Tournament score in `[0, 1)` — lower wins. Kept for debugging and
204:     /// snapshot stability; consumers never branch on it.
205:     pub score: f32,
206: }
207: 
208: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
209: // The cell.
210: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
211: 
212: /// Everything the world graph knows about one 160 u macro cell. A pure
213: /// function of `(seed, cell id)` — see `use_cases::world_topology`.
214: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
215: pub struct MacroCell {
216:     pub id: MacroCellId,
217:     /// Parameter fields sampled at the cell center.
218:     pub fields: MacroFields,
219:     /// One node per region in the cell (row-major, 2×2).
220:     pub nodes: Vec<WorldNode>,
221:     /// Primary-route portals on the region edges this cell can see. Portals
222:     /// on shared edges are duplicated identically by both neighbors.
223:     pub portals: Vec<Portal>,
224:     /// Stair / shaft reservations inside this cell.
225:     pub vertical_links: Vec<VerticalLink>,
226:     /// The red-room event this cell won, if any.
227:     pub red_room_event: Option<RedRoomEvent>,
228: }

## File: src/domain/use_cases/level_builder.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
 2: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 3:     VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid,
 4: };
 5: 
 6: /// Strategy Pattern for generating dense VoxelGrids from abstract room Grids.
 7: /// This fulfills the "engine should be extensible for other backrooms levels" rule.
 8: pub trait LevelBuilder {
 9:     fn build_voxels(&self, grid: &Grid) -> VoxelGrid;
10: }
11: 
12: /// Concrete implementation for Backrooms Level 0.
13: /// Uses smaller voxels (e.g. 8x8x4 per room) to allow realistic light sources.
14: pub struct Level0Builder {
15:     pub room_size: usize,
16:     pub wall_height: usize,
17: }
18: 
19: impl LevelBuilder for Level0Builder {
20:     fn build_voxels(&self, grid: &Grid) -> VoxelGrid {
21:         let rs = self.room_size;
22:         let wh = self.wall_height;
23: 
24:         // Voxel grid dimensions
25:         let vw = grid.width() * rs;
26:         let vh = wh + 3; // Floor (1) + Walls (wh) + Ceiling (1) + Recessed Lights (1)
27:         let vd = grid.depth() * rs;
28: 
29:         let mut voxels = VoxelGrid::new(vw, vh, vd);
30: 
31:         for gy in 0..grid.depth() {
32:             for gx in 0..grid.width() {
33:                 let cell = grid.get(gx, gy).unwrap();
34:                 let base_x = gx * rs;
35:                 let base_z = gy * rs;
36: 
37:                 for lx in 0..rs {
38:                     for lz in 0..rs {
39:                         let vx = base_x + lx;
40:                         let vz = base_z + lz;
41: 
42:                         // Floor
43:                         voxels.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
44: 
45:                         // Walls
46:                         let is_north_wall = lz == 0 && cell.walls[0];
47:                         let is_east_wall = lx == rs - 1 && cell.walls[1];
48:                         let is_south_wall = lz == rs - 1 && cell.walls[2];
49:                         let is_west_wall = lx == 0 && cell.walls[3];
50: 
51:                         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
52:                         let wall_type = if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
53:                             VOXEL_RED_WALL
54:                         } else {
55:                             VOXEL_WALL
56:                         };
57: 
58:                         if is_north_wall || is_east_wall || is_south_wall || is_west_wall {
59:                             for h in 1..=wh {
60:                                 voxels.set(vx, h, vz, wall_type);
61:                             }
62:                         }
63: 
64:                         // Checkerboard fluorescent lights (Realistic light sources)
65:                         // With 16x16 rooms, we can model actual recessed 2x6 fluorescent fixtures.
66:                         let mut is_light = false;
67:                         if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Blackout {
68:                             // Two fixtures per room
69:                             let fixture1 = lx >= 4 && lx < 6 && lz >= 5 && lz < 11;
70:                             let fixture2 = lx >= 10 && lx < 12 && lz >= 5 && lz < 11;
71:                             if fixture1 || fixture2 {
72:                                 is_light = true;
73:                             }
74:                         }
75: 
76:                         if is_light {
77:                             // Recessed light: hole in the ceiling, light block above it
78:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 2, vz, VOXEL_AIR); // hole
79:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT); // light emitting block above
80:                         } else {
81:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 2, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
82:                         }
83:                     }
84:                 }
85:             }
86:         }
87: 
88:         voxels
89:     }
90: }
````

## File: src/frameworks_drivers/simple_noise.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 2: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 3: 
 4: /// SimpleNoiseProvider is a concrete implementation of the NoiseProvider port.
 5: /// It resides in the Frameworks/Drivers layer.
 6: /// In a production scenario, this might wrap `noise-rs` or SIMD-accelerated noise.
 7: /// For Dependency Minimalism, we implement a basic seeded value noise.
 8: pub struct SimpleNoiseProvider;
 9: 
10: impl SimpleNoiseProvider {
11:     pub fn new() -> Self {
12:         Self
13:     }
14: 
15:     /// A deterministic pseudo-random hash function for 2D integer coordinates.
16:     fn hash2d(seed: u32, x: i32, y: i32) -> f32 {
17:         // Simple hash mixing
18:         let mut h = seed
19:             .wrapping_add(x as u32 ^ 0x9E3779B9)
20:             .wrapping_add(y as u32 ^ 0x85EBCA6B);
21:         h ^= h >> 16;
22:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EBCA6B);
23:         h ^= h >> 13;
24:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2AE35);
25:         h ^= h >> 16;
26: 
27:         // Normalize to [-1.0, 1.0]
28:         ((h as f32) / (std::u32::MAX as f32)) * 2.0 - 1.0
29:     }
30: 
31:     /// Linear interpolation
32:     fn lerp(a: f32, b: f32, t: f32) -> f32 {
33:         a + t * (b - a)
34:     }
35: 
36:     /// Smoothstep for softer transitions
37:     fn smoothstep(t: f32) -> f32 {
38:         t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
39:     }
40: }
41: 
42: impl NoiseProvider for SimpleNoiseProvider {
43:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32 {
44:         // Scale frequency to make the fields low-frequency
45:         let freq = 0.05;
46:         let x = position.x * freq;
47:         let y = position.z * freq;
48: 
49:         let x0 = x.floor() as i32;
50:         let x1 = x0 + 1;
51:         let y0 = y.floor() as i32;
52:         let y1 = y0 + 1;
53: 
54:         let tx = x - (x0 as f32);
55:         let ty = y - (y0 as f32);
56: 
57:         let u = Self::smoothstep(tx);
58:         let v = Self::smoothstep(ty);
59: 
60:         let v00 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y0);
61:         let v10 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y0);
62:         let v01 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y1);
63:         let v11 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y1);
64: 
65:         let nx0 = Self::lerp(v00, v10, u);
66:         let nx1 = Self::lerp(v01, v11, u);
67: 
68:         Self::lerp(nx0, nx1, v)
69:     }
70: }
71: 
72: #[cfg(test)]
73: mod tests {
74:     use super::*;
75: 
76:     #[test]
77:     fn test_noise_determinism() {
78:         let provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
79:         let pos = Position::new(42.5, -17.2);
80: 
81:         let val1 = provider.evaluate_2d(123, pos);
82:         let val2 = provider.evaluate_2d(123, pos);
83:         let val3 = provider.evaluate_2d(999, pos);
84: 
85:         assert_eq!(val1, val2);
86:         assert_ne!(val1, val3);
87:     }
88: }
````

## File: src/interface_adapters/web_renderer.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::adapters::json_presenter::JsonPresenter;
  2: use crate::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
  3: use crate::adapters::voxel_mapper::VoxelMapper;
  4: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
  5: use crate::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
  6: 
  7: /// WebRendererAdapter acts as a Presenter in Clean Architecture.
  8: /// It translates the core domain object (VoxelGrid) into formats
  9: /// suitable for the Web Presentation layer.
 10: pub struct WebRendererAdapter;
 11: 
 12: impl WebRendererAdapter {
 13:     /// Translates VoxelGrid into a JSON string representing greedy-meshed quads.
 14:     pub fn to_json(grid: &VoxelGrid, _chunk_size: f32) -> String {
 15:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(0.1);
 16:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid(grid);
 17:         JsonPresenter::render_voxels(&quads)
 18:     }
 19: 
 20:     /// Converts VoxelGrid into a Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) and serializes
 21:     /// the flattened node texture buffer and structural metadata to JSON.
 22:     pub fn to_octree_json(grid: &VoxelGrid, depth: u32, world_size: f32) -> String {
 23:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
 24:         let svo = builder.execute(grid, depth, world_size);
 25:         let gpu_data = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 26: 
 27:         let mut json = String::with_capacity(gpu_data.texel_data.len() * 8 + 128);
 28:         json.push_str("{\"root\":");
 29:         json.push_str(&svo.root.to_string());
 30:         json.push_str(",\"depth\":");
 31:         json.push_str(&svo.depth.to_string());
 32:         json.push_str(",\"world_size\":");
 33:         json.push_str(&svo.world_size.to_string());
 34:         json.push_str(",\"nodes\":[");
 35: 
 36:         for (i, &val) in gpu_data.texel_data.iter().enumerate() {
 37:             json.push_str(&val.to_string());
 38:             if i < gpu_data.texel_data.len() - 1 {
 39:                 json.push(',');
 40:             }
 41:         }
 42:         json.push_str("]}");
 43:         json
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     /// High-performance Binary Serializer for SVO Raymarching:
 47:     /// Compiles SVO nodes directly to little-endian bytes to avoid JSON parsing cost.
 48:     ///
 49:     /// BINARY SCHEMATIC (Byte offset -> payload):
 50:     /// - `0..4`: `root` node index (u32, little-endian)
 51:     /// - `4..8`: `depth` of tree (u32, little-endian)
 52:     /// - `8..12`: `world_size` scale (f32, little-endian)
 53:     /// - `12..16`: `texture_width` (u32, little-endian)
 54:     /// - `16..20`: `texture_height` (u32, little-endian)
 55:     /// - `20..24`: `voxel_scale` (f32, little-endian)
 56:     /// - `24..28`: `chunk_size` (f32, little-endian)
 57:     /// - `28..`: flat `u32` texel array data (4 * width * height * 4 bytes)
 58:     pub fn to_octree_binary(
 59:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
 60:         depth: u32,
 61:         world_size: f32,
 62:         voxel_scale: f32,
 63:         chunk_size: f32,
 64:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
 65:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
 66:         let svo = builder.execute(grid, depth, world_size);
 67:         let gpu_data = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 68: 
 69:         let header_size = 28; // 7 values * 4 bytes
 70:         let mut binary = Vec::with_capacity(header_size + gpu_data.texel_data.len() * 4);
 71: 
 72:         binary.extend_from_slice(&(svo.root as u32).to_le_bytes());
 73:         binary.extend_from_slice(&depth.to_le_bytes());
 74:         binary.extend_from_slice(&world_size.to_le_bytes());
 75:         binary.extend_from_slice(&gpu_data.texture_width.to_le_bytes());
 76:         binary.extend_from_slice(&gpu_data.texture_height.to_le_bytes());
 77:         binary.extend_from_slice(&voxel_scale.to_le_bytes());
 78:         binary.extend_from_slice(&chunk_size.to_le_bytes());
 79: 
 80:         for &val in &gpu_data.texel_data {
 81:             binary.extend_from_slice(&val.to_le_bytes());
 82:         }
 83: 
 84:         binary
 85:     }
 86: }
 87:
````

````rust
  3: //! This module composes two independent sources of immutable plans:

 19: /// Returns every immutable anomaly instance whose footprint overlaps a region.
 20: ///
 21: /// Identity is independent of the query partition: callers may ask through
 22: /// adjacent regions or different voxel sizes and receive the same instance.
 23: /// The noise port feeds the macro `anomaly_pressure` field, which clusters
 24: /// candidates without ever placing one itself.
 25: pub fn plan_anomalies_for_region(
 26:     seed: u32,
 27:     region_origin: Position,
 28:     region_size: f32,
 29:     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
 30:     protected_point: Position,
 31:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 32:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 33: ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
 34:     let query = WorldBounds::new(
 35:         region_origin.x,
 36:         region_origin.z,
 37:         region_origin.x + region_size,
 38:         region_origin.z + region_size,
 39:     );
 40:     let mut instances =
 41:         macro_planner::plan_macro_anomalies(seed, query, protected_point, config, noise);
 42:     instances.extend(plan_red_rooms(seed, region_origin, assemblies, config));
 43:     instances.sort_by_key(|instance| instance.id);
 44:     instances.dedup_by_key(|instance| instance.id);
 45:     instances
 46: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/exposed_emissive_faces.rs

````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 2:     VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VoxelGrid,
 3: };
 4: 
 5: use super::voxel_neighborhood::{GridDimensions, VoxelCoord, for_each_voxel};
 6: 
 7: /// One spectral emission class in the compact 0--15 bake domain.
 8: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 9: pub(crate) struct EmissionProfile {
10:     pub(crate) voxel_type: u8,
11:     pub(crate) rgb: [f32; 3],
12: }
13: 
14: pub(crate) const EMISSION_PROFILES: [EmissionProfile; 3] = [
15:     EmissionProfile {
16:         voxel_type: VOXEL_LIGHT,
17:         rgb: [15.0, 14.0, 11.0],
18:     },
19:     EmissionProfile {
20:         voxel_type: VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
21:         rgb: [15.0, 3.0, 2.0],
22:     },
23:     EmissionProfile {
24:         voxel_type: VOXEL_GLIMMER,
25:         rgb: [3.0, 5.0, 7.0],
26:     },
27: ];
28: 
29: pub(crate) fn emission_rgb(voxel_type: u8) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
30:     EMISSION_PROFILES
31:         .iter()
32:         .find(|profile| profile.voxel_type == voxel_type)
33:         .map(|profile| profile.rgb)
34: }
35: 
36: /// Returns the air-cell centers immediately below exposed fixture undersides.
37: ///
38: /// The voxel materials in [`EMISSION_PROFILES`] describe ceiling-style
39: /// fixtures: ordinary fluorescent panels, red panels, and dim emergency
40: /// glimmers. They all emit through their downward face. A material placed on
41: /// the floor (`y == 0`), buried below a solid, or exposed only on a side is
42: /// still visible geometry, but it does not seed the diffuse-fill field. This
43: /// is the same one-sided source contract used by analytic scene lights.
44: pub(crate) fn exposed_downward_air_cells(
45:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
46:     dimensions: GridDimensions,
47:     profile: EmissionProfile,
48: ) -> Vec<VoxelCoord> {
49:     let mut exposed = Vec::new();
50:     for_each_voxel(dimensions, |coord| {
51:         if let Some(air_cell) = exposed_air_cell_below(grid, coord, profile.voxel_type) {
52:             exposed.push(air_cell);
53:         }
54:     });
55:     exposed
56: }
57: 
58: /// Identifies the single face through which a ceiling fixture may seed the
59: /// approximate diffuse-fill field. Keeping this predicate separate makes the
60: /// orientation and boundary behavior explicit and independently testable.
61: fn exposed_air_cell_below(
62:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
63:     emitter: VoxelCoord,
64:     expected_material: u8,
65: ) -> Option<VoxelCoord> {
66:     if emitter.y == 0 || grid.get(emitter.x, emitter.y, emitter.z) != expected_material {
67:         return None;
68:     }
69: 
70:     let air_cell = VoxelCoord {
71:         y: emitter.y - 1,
72:         ..emitter
73:     };
74:     (grid.get(air_cell.x, air_cell.y, air_cell.z) == VOXEL_AIR).then_some(air_cell)
75: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/mod.rs
````rust
 1: //! Bake finite-range voxel irradiance from the scene's emissive geometry.
 2: //!
 3: //! This use case deliberately separates four physically meaningful stages:
 4: //!
 5: //! 1. erase the previous bake;
 6: //! 2. inject emission through exposed downward faces of ceiling fixtures;
 7: //! 3. find shortest unobstructed paths through air in world-space units;
 8: //! 4. project that air irradiance onto the first solid surface it reaches.
 9: //!
10: //! Solids are receivers, never propagation nodes. A wall can therefore be lit
11: //! on its near side without becoming a light source for the room behind it.
12: //! The working calculation is floating point; quantization happens only when
13: //! the result is written back to the grid's established RGB 0--15 contract.
14: //! This field is deliberately an approximate, finite-range diffuse fill. The
15: //! renderer's analytic area lights remain authoritative for direct lighting;
16: //! this bake neither invents omnidirectional emitters nor requires unbounded
17: //! cross-chunk propagation halos.
18: 
19: mod clear_previous_bake;
20: mod exposed_emissive_faces;
21: mod project_onto_solid_receivers;
22: mod propagate_through_air;
23: mod settings;
24: mod voxel_neighborhood;
25: mod world_space_attenuation;
26: mod write_air_irradiance;
27: 
28: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
29: 
30: pub use settings::{
31:     DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings, VoxelLightingSettings,
32: };
33: 
34: /// Replaces every prior light sample in `grid` with a deterministic bake.
35: ///
36: /// Once light has entered the air below a fixture, approximate diffuse fill
37: /// attenuates symmetrically along face-connected paths. Its independent
38: /// variable is shortest unobstructed path length in world units, so changing
39: /// voxel resolution does not silently change a fixture's physical reach.
40: pub fn bake_voxel_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, settings: VoxelLightingSettings) {
41:     clear_previous_bake::clear_previous_bake(grid);
42: 
43:     let propagated = propagate_through_air::propagate_through_air(grid, settings);
44:     write_air_irradiance::write_air_irradiance(grid, &propagated, settings);
45:     project_onto_solid_receivers::project_onto_solid_receivers(grid, &propagated, settings);
46: }
47: 
48: #[cfg(test)]
49: mod tests;
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/propagate_through_air.rs
````rust
 1: use std::collections::VecDeque;
 2: 
 3: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
 4: 
 5: use super::exposed_emissive_faces::{
 6:     EMISSION_PROFILES, EmissionProfile, exposed_downward_air_cells,
 7: };
 8: use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
 9: use super::voxel_neighborhood::{GridDimensions, for_each_face_neighbor};
10: 
11: pub(crate) const UNREACHABLE: u32 = u32::MAX;
12: 
13: pub(crate) struct PropagatedEmission {
14:     pub(crate) profile: EmissionProfile,
15:     /// Shortest count of air-cell center transitions from an exposed seed.
16:     pub(crate) distance_steps: Vec<u32>,
17: }
18: 
19: pub(crate) struct AirPropagation {
20:     pub(crate) dimensions: GridDimensions,
21:     pub(crate) emissions: Vec<PropagatedEmission>,
22: }
23: 
24: /// Finds shortest face-connected paths through air for every emission class.
25: ///
26: /// A class uses one multi-source breadth-first search. This means equally
27: /// colored panels form a nearest-emitter envelope instead of multiplying
28: /// energy merely because a large panel occupies several source voxels.
29: pub(crate) fn propagate_through_air(
30:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
31:     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
32: ) -> AirPropagation {
33:     let dimensions = GridDimensions::of(grid);
34:     let mut emissions = Vec::with_capacity(EMISSION_PROFILES.len());
35: 
36:     for profile in EMISSION_PROFILES {
37:         let mut distance_steps = vec![UNREACHABLE; dimensions.volume()];
38:         let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
39: 
40:         // An exposed air center is half a voxel from the emitting face. Do
41:         // not inject a sample that is already beyond the requested range.
42:         if settings.voxel_size_world_units() * 0.5 < settings.max_range_world_units() {
43:             for seed in exposed_downward_air_cells(grid, dimensions, profile) {
44:                 let index = dimensions.index(seed);
45:                 if distance_steps[index] == UNREACHABLE {
46:                     distance_steps[index] = 0;
47:                     queue.push_back(seed);
48:                 }
49:             }
50:         }
51: 
52:         while let Some(coord) = queue.pop_front() {
53:             let current_steps = distance_steps[dimensions.index(coord)];
54:             let next_steps = current_steps + 1;
55:             let next_center_distance =
56:                 (next_steps as f32 + 0.5) * settings.voxel_size_world_units();
57:             if next_center_distance >= settings.max_range_world_units() {
58:                 continue;
59:             }
60: 
61:             for_each_face_neighbor(coord, dimensions, |neighbor| {
62:                 if grid.get(neighbor.x, neighbor.y, neighbor.z) != VOXEL_AIR {
63:                     return;
64:                 }
65:                 let neighbor_index = dimensions.index(neighbor);
66:                 if next_steps < distance_steps[neighbor_index] {
67:                     distance_steps[neighbor_index] = next_steps;
68:                     queue.push_back(neighbor);
69:                 }
70:             });
71:         }
72: 
73:         emissions.push(PropagatedEmission {
74:             profile,
75:             distance_steps,
76:         });
77:     }
78: 
79:     AirPropagation {
80:         dimensions,
81:         emissions,
82:     }
83: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/circulation_sampler.rs
````rust
  1: //! Sampling planned circulation: corridor ceilings drift slowly in long
  2: //! quantized runs, and corridor edge walls persist or dissolve into rooms
  3: //! and fabric on a rhythm that never reads as a doorway grid.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
  6: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{CirculationSpine, SpaceProgram};
  7: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  8: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point;
  9: 
 10: use super::BackroomsLevel;
 11: 
 12: /// Within this radius of the spawn point the main corridor keeps both of its
 13: /// edge walls fully intact: the first thing the player reads is an
 14: /// unambiguous walled corridor, not a dissolved edge into open fabric. The
 15: /// world only starts opening up once that grammar has been established.
 16: pub(super) const SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS: f32 = 26.0;
 17: 
 18: impl BackroomsLevel {
 19:     pub(super) fn corridor_ceiling(
 20:         spine: &CirculationSpine,
 21:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 22:         seed: u32,
 23:         wx: f32,
 24:         wz: f32,
 25:     ) -> f32 {
 26:         // Slow, quantized drift: one sample per 12 u corridor zone snapped
 27:         // to the voxel lattice, so long runs hold one height and then step
 28:         // once — instead of per-column ripple overhead.
 29:         const DRIFT_ZONE: f32 = 12.0;
 30:         let zone_x = (wx / DRIFT_ZONE).floor() * DRIFT_ZONE + DRIFT_ZONE * 0.5;
 31:         let zone_z = (wz / DRIFT_ZONE).floor() * DRIFT_ZONE + DRIFT_ZONE * 0.5;
 32:         let drift = Self::n(
 33:             noise,
 34:             seed,
 35:             0xCA00_u32.wrapping_add(spine.id),
 36:             zone_x,
 37:             zone_z,
 38:             0.35,
 39:         );
 40:         let (height, lo, hi) = match spine.spine_kind {
 41:             SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => (3.8 + 0.4 * drift, 3.4, 4.2),
 42:             SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall => (3.3 + 0.3 * drift, 3.0, 3.6),
 43:             _ => (3.4, 3.4, 3.4),
 44:         };
 45:         // Snap first, clamp last (f32 lattice snap can overshoot the band).
 46:         ((height / 0.2).round() * 0.2).clamp(lo, hi)
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     /// Whether a corridor-side wall dissolves into the adjacent room/fabric.
 50:     /// Main-route openings take 8--10 u from a 32 u macro span: around a
 51:     /// quarter to a third of an eligible edge is directly open, while the
 52:     /// remaining wall runs stay long enough to avoid a doorway cadence.
 53:     ///
 54:     /// The openings are the fabric's mouths onto circulation, so the
 55:     /// Peripheral Shift re-deals them: the drift epoch (read at the wall
 56:     /// column's own 40 u cell) re-salts each section's width and phase, and
 57:     /// the strain tier narrows them — at deep strain whole sections seal.
 58:     /// The corridor interior itself never closes: a shut mouth costs the
 59:     /// route you knew, never the spine.
 60:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 61:     pub(super) fn corridor_edge_opens(
 62:         spine: &CirculationSpine,
 63:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 64:         seed: u32,
 65:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 66:         along: f32,
 67:         is_horizontal: bool,
 68:         wx: f32,
 69:         wz: f32,
 70:     ) -> bool {
 71:         // The opening spine sequence is sacred: near spawn the corridor keeps
 72:         // both edge walls so the player's first minute reads as circulation
 73:         // through a building, before any dissolution into fabric.
 74:         let sp = spawn_point(seed);
 75:         let spawn_d2 = (wx - sp.x) * (wx - sp.x) + (wz - sp.z) * (wz - sp.z);
 76:         if spawn_d2 < SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS * SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS {
 77:             return false;
 78:         }
 79: 
 80:         if Self::in_expanse(noise, seed, wx, wz) {
 81:             return true;
 82:         }
 83: 
 84:         let span = 32.0;
 85:         let section = (along / span).floor() as i64;
 86:         let perpendicular = if is_horizontal { wz } else { wx };
 87:         let side = (perpendicular / spine.width.max(1.0)).floor() as i64;
 88:         let epoch = reality.fabric_drift_epoch(wx, wz);
 89:         let tier = reality.delirium() as u32;
 90:         let salt = (0xCB00_u32.wrapping_add(spine.id)) ^ epoch.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9);
 91:         // Deep strain seals whole sections: the opening the wanderer relied
 92:         // on is simply wall now. The threshold shrinks the same hash's
 93:         // acceptance, so rising tiers close mouths instead of moving them.
 94:         if tier >= 2
 95:             && Self::cell_hash(noise, seed, salt ^ 0x2B, section, side)
 96:                 < 0.22 * (tier - 1) as f32
 97:         {
 98:             return false;
 99:         }
100:         let width_hash = Self::cell_hash(noise, seed, salt, section, side);
101:         let phase_hash = Self::cell_hash(noise, seed, salt ^ 0x19, section, side);
102:         let (mut width, start) = match spine.spine_kind {
103:             SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => (8.0 + 2.0 * width_hash, 6.0 + 10.0 * phase_hash),
104:             _ => (4.0 + 1.6 * width_hash, 10.0 + 8.0 * phase_hash),
105:         };
106:         // Strain narrows every mouth that survives.
107:         width *= 1.0 - 0.15 * tier as f32;
108:         let offset = along.rem_euclid(span);
109:         offset >= start && offset < start + width
110:     }
111: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/column_field.rs
````rust
 1: //! A sampled Level 0 area plus the one-column halo needed for clean caps.
 2: 
 3: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 4: 
 5: /// Resolution-dependent samples of a resolution-independent world plan.
 6: ///
 7: /// The halo is part of this type's invariant.  Callers cannot accidentally
 8: /// voxelize a chunk without knowing its neighbours' ceiling heights, which is
 9: /// what keeps separately generated requests sealed at their shared edge.
10: pub(crate) struct ColumnField {
11:     width: usize,
12:     depth: usize,
13:     columns: Vec<ColumnPlan>,
14: }
15: 
16: impl ColumnField {
17:     pub(crate) fn sample(
18:         width: usize,
19:         depth: usize,
20:         mut plan_at: impl FnMut(i64, i64) -> ColumnPlan,
21:     ) -> Self {
22:         let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity((width + 2) * (depth + 2));
23:         for z in -1..=depth as i64 {
24:             for x in -1..=width as i64 {
25:                 columns.push(plan_at(x, z));
26:             }
27:         }
28:         Self {
29:             width,
30:             depth,
31:             columns,
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     pub(crate) fn width(&self) -> usize {
36:         self.width
37:     }
38: 
39:     pub(crate) fn depth(&self) -> usize {
40:         self.depth
41:     }
42: 
43:     /// Local coordinates include the halo, so `x` and `z` may be `-1` or
44:     /// exactly the corresponding output dimension.
45:     pub(crate) fn get(&self, x: i64, z: i64) -> &ColumnPlan {
46:         debug_assert!((-1..=self.width as i64).contains(&x));
47:         debug_assert!((-1..=self.depth as i64).contains(&z));
48:         &self.columns[((z + 1) as usize) * (self.width + 2) + (x + 1) as usize]
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: #[cfg(test)]
53: mod tests {
54:     use super::*;
55: 
56:     #[test]
57:     fn sampler_owns_a_one_column_halo() {
58:         let field = ColumnField::sample(2, 3, |x, z| ColumnPlan::open((x + z + 10) as f32));
59:         assert_eq!(field.get(-1, -1).ceiling_units, 8.0);
60:         assert_eq!(field.get(2, 3).ceiling_units, 15.0);
61:     }
62: }
````
