  1: //! Chunk generation: voxelize the planned world (plus recursive Red Room
  2: //! addresses) into one output grid, exporting traversal gates, pit hazards,
  3: //! and runtime lights from the same immutable plans as the geometry.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  6:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, RealitySnapshot, TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
  7:     WorldBounds,
  8: };
  9: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 10: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
 11: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 12: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 13: use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
 14: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
 15: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 16: use crate::use_cases::red_rooms::recursive_level::RecursiveLevelWindow;
 17: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::region_index;
 18: 
 19: use super::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnField, ColumnPlan, GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS, voxelize_columns};
 20: 
 21: /// Runtime direct lights sit below their visible ceiling panel. Tall atria
 22: /// need a longer pendant drop so the light reaches occupied space and casts
 23: /// useful column shadows instead of flattening against the vault.
 24: fn runtime_light_height(ceiling_units: f32, is_atrium: bool) -> f32 {
 25:     let pendant_drop = if is_atrium { 1.6 } else { 1.1 };
 26:     (ceiling_units - pendant_drop).max(2.4)
 27: }
 28: 
 29: fn gate_crosses_bounds(gate: &TraversalGate, bounds: WorldBounds) -> bool {
 30:     match gate.axis {
 31:         Axis2::X => {
 32:             gate.plane >= bounds.min_x - 0.01
 33:                 && gate.plane <= bounds.max_x + 0.01
 34:                 && gate.span_max >= bounds.min_z
 35:                 && gate.span_min <= bounds.max_z
 36:         }
 37:         Axis2::Z => {
 38:             gate.plane >= bounds.min_z - 0.01
 39:                 && gate.plane <= bounds.max_z + 0.01
 40:                 && gate.span_max >= bounds.min_x
 41:                 && gate.span_min <= bounds.max_x
 42:         }
 43:     }
 44: }
 45: 
 46: impl BackroomsLevel {
 47: 
 48:     /// Region plans for every region a chunk (plus a margin) overlaps.
 49:     pub(crate) fn region_plans_for(
 50:         chunk_pos: Position,
 51:         chunk_size: f32,
 52:         seed: u32,
 53:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 54:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 55:     ) -> Vec<((i64, i64), RegionPlan)> {
 56:         InfiniteRegionWindow::around_chunk(chunk_pos, chunk_size, 1.0, seed, config, noise)
 57:             .iter()
 58:             .map(|(key, plan)| (key, plan.clone()))
 59:             .collect()
 60:     }
 61: }
 62: 
 63: impl LevelGenerator for BackroomsLevel {
 64:     fn generate(
 65:         &self,
 66:         chunk_pos: Position,
 67:         seed: u32,
 68:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 69:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 70:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
 71:         self.generate_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, noise, &RealitySnapshot::empty())
 72:     }
 73: 
 74:     fn generate_with_reality(
 75:         &self,
 76:         chunk_pos: Position,
 77:         seed: u32,
 78:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 79:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 80:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 81:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
 82:         let s = config.voxel_scale;
 83:         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 84:         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 85:         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
 86:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
 87: 
 88:         // Base plans remain available for the authored threshold and for
 89:         // ordinary reality. A committed Red Room adds a second, explicitly
 90:         // addressed Level 0 window instead of smuggling offsets and seeds
 91:         // through the voxel loop.
 92:         let plans =
 93:             BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(chunk_pos, config.chunk_size, seed, &config, noise);
 94:         let recursive_level = RecursiveLevelWindow::around_chunk(
 95:             chunk_pos,
 96:             config.chunk_size,
 97:             1.0,
 98:             seed,
 99:             config,
100:             noise,
101:             reality,
102:         );
103: 
104:         // Architecture first: plan every region this chunk overlaps.
105:         let plan_of = |wx: f32, wz: f32| -> &RegionPlan {
106:             let key = (region_index(wx), region_index(wz));
107:             plans
108:                 .iter()
109:                 .find(|(k, _)| *k == key)
110:                 .map(|(_, p)| p)
111:                 .expect("region window covers the requested voxel halo")
112:         };
113: 
114:         // Export semantic crossings/hazards from the same immutable plans as
115:         // voxel geometry. Neighboring region plans repeat macro instances, so
116:         // deduplicate by stable IDs before the payload reaches the engine.
117:         let chunk_bounds = WorldBounds::new(
118:             chunk_pos.x,
119:             chunk_pos.z,
120:             chunk_pos.x + config.chunk_size,
121:             chunk_pos.z + config.chunk_size,
122:         );
123:         let mut seen_instances = std::collections::HashSet::new();
124:         let mut seen_gates = std::collections::HashSet::new();
125:         let mut seen_hazards = std::collections::HashSet::new();
126:         let authored_bounds = recursive_level.as_ref().map_or(chunk_bounds, |recursive| {
127:             recursive.to_recursive_bounds(chunk_bounds)
128:         });
129:         let mut export_interactions = |plan: &RegionPlan| {
130:             for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
131:                 if !seen_instances.insert(anomaly.id)
132:                     || !anomaly
133:                         .footprint
134:                         .bounds()
135:                         .intersects(authored_bounds.expanded(1.0))
136:                 {
137:                     continue;
138:                 }
139:                 for gate in anomaly.traversal_gates() {
140:                     if gate_crosses_bounds(gate, authored_bounds) && seen_gates.insert(gate.id) {
141:                         grid.traversal_gates.push(
142:                             recursive_level
143:                                 .as_ref()
144:                                 .map_or(*gate, |recursive| recursive.project_gate(*gate)),
145:                         );
146:                     }
147:                 }
148:                 for hazard in anomaly.pit_hazards_for_bounds(authored_bounds) {
149:                     if seen_hazards.insert(hazard.id) {
150:                         grid.pit_hazards.push(
151:                             recursive_level
152:                                 .as_ref()
153:                                 .map_or(hazard, |recursive| recursive.project_hazard(hazard)),
154:                         );
155:                     }
156:                 }
157:             }
158:         };
159:         if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
160:             for (_, plan) in recursive.iter() {
161:                 export_interactions(plan);
162:             }
163:         } else {
164:             for (_, plan) in &plans {
165:                 export_interactions(plan);
166:             }
167:         }
168:         drop(export_interactions);
169: 
170:         // The recursive branch supplies its own anomaly semantics, while the
171:         // encounter that opened it retains one checkpoint in visible space.
172:         // Alternating across that authored plane advances the closed loop.
173:         if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
174:             for gate in plans
175:                 .iter()
176:                 .flat_map(|(_, plan)| plan.anomalies.iter())
177:                 .filter(|anomaly| anomaly.id == recursive.instance_id())
178:                 .flat_map(AnomalyInstance::traversal_gates)
179:                 .filter(|gate| gate.kind == TraversalGateKind::RedLoop)
180:             {
181:                 if gate_crosses_bounds(gate, chunk_bounds) && seen_gates.insert(gate.id) {
182:                     grid.traversal_gates.push(*gate);
183:                 }
184:             }
185:         }
186: 
187:         use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{LightKind, RuntimeLight};
188:         let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
189:         let mut collect_runtime_lights = |plan: &RegionPlan| {
190:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
191:                 if a.corruption.abandoned {
192:                     continue;
193:                 }
194:                 for f in &a.fixtures {
195:                     if !f.lit {
196:                         continue;
197:                     }
198:                     let rendered_at = recursive_level
199:                         .as_ref()
200:                         .map_or(f.at, |recursive| recursive.project_position(f.at));
201:                     let key = (rendered_at.x.to_bits(), rendered_at.z.to_bits());
202:                     if !seen.insert(key) {
203:                         continue;
204:                     }
205: 
206:                     let (sample_at, fixture_plan) = if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
207:                         recursive
208:                             .plan_at(rendered_at)
209:                             .expect("recursive region window covers its projected fixtures")
210:                     } else {
211:                         (f.at, plan_of(f.at.x, f.at.z))
212:                     };
213: 
214:                     // Region-scale anomaly interiors own their fixture
215:                     // rhythm. Do not leak an overwritten assembly's runtime
216:                     // light into a blackout/pillar/pit payload.
217:                     if fixture_plan.anomalies.iter().any(|anomaly| {
218:                         anomaly.kind != AnomalyKind::RedRoom
219:                             && anomaly.contains(sample_at.x, sample_at.z)
220:                     }) {
221:                         continue;
222:                     }
223: 
224:                     let cx = rendered_at.x - chunk_pos.x;
225:                     let cz = rendered_at.z - chunk_pos.z;
226:                     if cx >= -15.0
227:                         && cx <= config.chunk_size + 15.0
228:                         && cz >= -15.0
229:                         && cz <= config.chunk_size + 15.0
230:                     {
231:                         let ceiling_units = a
232:                             .ceiling_zones
233:                             .iter()
234:                             .find(|z| z.area.contains(f.at.x, f.at.z))
235:                             .map(|z| z.height_units)
236:                             .unwrap_or(4.0);
237:                         let is_atrium = matches!(
238:                             a.program,
239:                             crate::domain::entities::architecture::SpaceProgram::Atrium
240:                         );
241:                         let y = runtime_light_height(ceiling_units, is_atrium);
242: 
243:                         let kind = if f.half_x > f.half_z * 2.0 || f.half_z > f.half_x * 2.0 {
244:                             LightKind::Strip
245:                         } else {
246:                             LightKind::CeilingPanel
247:                         };
248: 
249:                         // Runtime lights are collected before voxelization, so
250:                         // query the architectural column plan rather than the
251:                         // still-empty grid when rejecting pillar intersections.
252:                         let is_buried = if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
253:                             BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
254:                                 fixture_plan,
255:                                 noise,
256:                                 recursive.seed(),
257:                                 recursive.config(),
258:                                 reality,
259:                                 sample_at.x,
260:                                 sample_at.z,
261:                             )
262:                             .solid
263:                         } else {
264:                             BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
265:                                 fixture_plan,
266:                                 noise,
267:                                 seed,
268:                                 &config,
269:                                 reality,
270:                                 sample_at.x,
271:                                 sample_at.z,
272:                             )
273:                             .solid
274:                         };
275: 
276:                         if !is_buried {
277:                             // Red rooms are exposed purely by their light
278:                             // color; the fixtures keep the room's spacing.
279:                             let rgb = if recursive_level.is_some() || a.corruption.red_room {
280:                                 [1.0, 0.22, 0.16]
281:                             } else {
282:                                 [1.0, 0.95, 0.8]
283:                             };
284:                             grid.runtime_lights.push(RuntimeLight {
285:                                 world_pos: [rendered_at.x, y, rendered_at.z],
286:                                 half_size: [f.half_x, f.half_z],
287:                                 rgb,
288:                                 range: if is_atrium { 24.0 } else { 16.0 },
289:                                 intensity: if is_atrium { 4.0 } else { 1.0 },
290:                                 enabled: true,
291:                                 kind,
292:                             });
293:                         }
294:                     }
295:                 }
296:             }
297:         };
298:         if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
299:             for (_, plan) in recursive.iter() {
300:                 collect_runtime_lights(plan);
301:             }
302:         } else {
303:             for (_, plan) in &plans {
304:                 collect_runtime_lights(plan);
305:             }
306:         }
307: 
308:         // Plan every column plus a 1-voxel margin: ceiling skirts must seal
309:         // height steps across chunk borders too.
310:         let plan_at = |lx: i64, lz: i64| -> ColumnPlan {
311:             let wx = chunk_pos.x + (lx as f32 + 0.5) * s;
312:             let wz = chunk_pos.z + (lz as f32 + 0.5) * s;
313: 
314:             if let Some(recursive) = &recursive_level {
315:                 let (recursive_point, plan) = recursive
316:                     .plan_at(Position::new(wx, wz))
317:                     .expect("recursive region window covers the voxel halo");
318:                 let mut column = BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
319:                     plan,
320:                     noise,
321:                     recursive.seed(),
322:                     recursive.config(),
323:                     reality,
324:                     recursive_point.x,
325:                     recursive_point.z,
326:                 );
327:                 column.red_light = true;
328:                 column
329:             } else {
330:                 BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
331:                     plan_of(wx, wz),
332:                     noise,
333:                     seed,
334:                     &config,
335:                     reality,
336:                     wx,
337:                     wz,
338:                 )
339:             }
340:         };
341: 
342:         let columns = ColumnField::sample(width, depth, plan_at);
343:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &columns, s);
344: 
345:         // Provisions live only in ordinary Level 0 space: a committed Red
346:         // Room's recursive address stays barren by design.
347:         if recursive_level.is_none() {
348:             super::provisions::stamp_level_zero_provisions(
349:                 &mut grid,
350:                 chunk_pos,
351:                 &super::provisions::ProvisionContext {
352:                     seed,
353:                     config: &config,
354:                     reality,
355:                     noise,
356:                     plans: &plans,
357:                 },
358:             );
359:         }
360: 
361:         grid
362:     }
363: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/provisions.rs
````rust
  1: //! Level 0 provisions: scattered almond water and the rare physical door.
  2: //!
  3: //! Both are a deterministic post-pass over the already-voxelized chunk,
  4: //! derived purely from (seed, world lattice, reality). Supplies follow the
  5: //! 40u fabric-drift lattice; doors follow the 80u region lattice plus one
  6: //! authored door near spawn, so a fresh wanderer can always find Level 1.
  7: //! Red-room interiors and pit lattices never receive provisions: a sealed
  8: //! loop must stay barren, and nothing may hover over a pit.
  9: 
 10: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyKind, LevelExit, RealitySnapshot};
 11: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 12: use crate::domain::entities::supplies::{SupplyItem, SupplyKind};
 13: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid};
 14: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 15: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
 16: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 17: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_HABITABLE;
 18: use crate::use_cases::level_one::generate::{
 19:     ARRIVAL_POINT, DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF, stamp_level_door, stamp_supply_marker,
 20: };
 21: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 22: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, region_index};
 23: 
 24: use super::BackroomsLevel;
 25: 
 26: /// Supply lattice: one candidate per fabric-drift-sized cell.
 27: const SUPPLY_CELL: f32 = 40.0;
 28: /// Fraction of supply cells that roll a candidate spot. Each cell gets one
 29: /// deterministic spot (never a probe sequence, which would make placement
 30: /// depend on which chunk evaluates it); spots landing on solid columns are
 31: /// simply lost, so this is tuned above the desired field density.
 32: const ALMOND_CHANCE: f32 = 0.72;
 33: /// Of the successful cells, this fraction holds food instead of water.
 34: const RATION_SHARE: f32 = 0.25;
 35: 
 36: /// Fraction of 80u regions holding an organic door to Level 1 (at the
 37: /// default `level_doors` tuning of 1.0).
 38: const DOOR_CHANCE: f32 = 0.08;
 39: /// How far past its bounds a chunk stamps door geometry. Must stay within
 40: /// the region-plan window margin (1.0) and cover the frame plus clearing.
 41: const DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN: f32 = 1.0;
 42: /// The authored always-present door: guaranteed to exist, but a real hike
 43: /// from spawn — finding it should feel earned, not scripted. Debug runs
 44: /// raise `level_doors` (or walk straight here).
 45: const SPAWN_DOOR: (f32, f32) = (172.0, -116.0);
 46: 
 47: pub(crate) struct ProvisionContext<'a> {
 48:     pub seed: u32,
 49:     pub config: &'a GeneratorConfig,
 50:     pub reality: &'a RealitySnapshot,
 51:     pub noise: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 52:     pub plans: &'a [((i64, i64), RegionPlan)],
 53: }
 54: 
 55: impl ProvisionContext<'_> {
 56:     fn plan_of(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
 57:         let key = (region_index(wx), region_index(wz));
 58:         self.plans
 59:             .iter()
 60:             .find(|(k, _)| *k == key)
 61:             .map(|(_, plan)| plan)
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     /// True when the walking plane at a world point is ordinary open fabric:
 65:     /// not solid, not raised, and not inside a barren anomaly family.
 66:     fn is_open_floor(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> bool {
 67:         let Some(plan) = self.plan_of(wx, wz) else {
 68:             return false;
 69:         };
 70:         let forbidden = plan.anomalies.iter().any(|anomaly| {
 71:             matches!(anomaly.kind, AnomalyKind::RedRoom | AnomalyKind::PitLattice)
 72:                 && anomaly.contains(wx, wz)
 73:         });
 74:         if forbidden {
 75:             return false;
 76:         }
 77:         let column = BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
 78:             plan,
 79:             self.noise,
 80:             self.seed,
 81:             self.config,
 82:             self.reality,
 83:             wx,
 84:             wz,
 85:         );
 86:         column.floor && !column.solid && column.floor_units < 0.05
 87:     }
 88: }
 89: 
 90: /// Stamps supplies and doors into one Level 0 chunk and exports their
 91: /// semantic records. Never called for recursive (red-room-interior) chunks.
 92: pub(crate) fn stamp_level_zero_provisions(
 93:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
 94:     chunk_pos: Position,
 95:     ctx: &ProvisionContext<'_>,
 96: ) {
 97:     let water = ctx.config.tuning.almond_water.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
 98:     let food = ctx.config.tuning.rations.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
 99:     let doors = ctx.config.tuning.level_doors.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
100:     if water <= 0.0 && food <= 0.0 && doors <= 0.0 {
101:         return;
102:     }
103:     let s = ctx.config.voxel_scale;
104:     let max_x = chunk_pos.x + ctx.config.chunk_size;
105:     let max_z = chunk_pos.z + ctx.config.chunk_size;
106:     let in_chunk = |x: f32, z: f32| x >= chunk_pos.x && x < max_x && z >= chunk_pos.z && z < max_z;
107:     // Markers span a few voxels, so an item just outside this grid must
108:     // still stamp its overlapping voxels here or seams (and the halo crop)
109:     // would disagree with the neighbor that owns it. Stamping quantizes in
110:     // world space, making the overlap exact; the semantic export stays with
111:     // every grid whose bounds contain the item (halo overlaps are deduped by
112:     // id on the consuming side).
113:     let near_chunk = |x: f32, z: f32, m: f32| {
114:         x >= chunk_pos.x - m && x < max_x + m && z >= chunk_pos.z - m && z < max_z + m
115:     };
116: 
117:     // -- almond water on the 40u supply lattice ------------------------------
118:     let c0x = ((chunk_pos.x - 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
119:     let c1x = ((max_x + 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
120:     let c0z = ((chunk_pos.z - 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
121:     let c1z = ((max_z + 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
122:     for cz in c0z..=c1z {
123:         for cx in c0x..=c1x {
124:             let roll = hash(ctx.seed, 0x0A1A_09D0_57A7_0000, cx, cz);
125:             // Water and food frequencies scale their halves of the density
126:             // independently; the kind roll then splits proportionally, so
127:             // e.g. rations=0 yields a pure-water world at water's density.
128:             let water_weight = (1.0 - RATION_SHARE) * water;
129:             let food_weight = RATION_SHARE * food;
130:             // A mismanaged wanderer finds a stingier level: each strain tier
131:             // withholds a share of the supply cells (same hash, lower
132:             // threshold, so rising strain removes bottles rather than
133:             // shuffling them). Tier 0 is the unstrained field.
134:             let strain_keep = 1.0 - 0.15 * ctx.reality.delirium() as f32;
135:             let cell_chance = ALMOND_CHANCE * (water_weight + food_weight) * strain_keep;
136:             if unit(roll) > cell_chance {
137:                 continue;
138:             }
139:             let id = roll | 1;
140:             if ctx.reality.supply_consumed(id) {
141:                 continue;
142:             }
143:             // One deterministic spot per cell. Chunks that cannot even
144:             // stamp it (outside the 0.5u marker margin) skip without
145:             // evaluating, so no decision ever depends on the asking chunk.
146:             let probe = hash(ctx.seed, 0x0A1A_09D0_0000_0000, cx, cz);
147:             let px = (cx as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe)) * SUPPLY_CELL;
148:             let pz = (cz as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe.rotate_left(23))) * SUPPLY_CELL;
149:             if !near_chunk(px, pz, 0.5) || !ctx.is_open_floor(px, pz) {
150:                 continue;
151:             }
152:             let kind = if unit(roll.rotate_left(11)) * (water_weight + food_weight) < food_weight
153:             {
154:                 SupplyKind::Ration
155:             } else {
156:                 SupplyKind::AlmondWater
157:             };
158:             let item = SupplyItem {
159:                 id,
160:                 kind,
161:                 position: Position::new(px, pz),
162:                 rest_y: 0.0,
163:             };
164:             stamp_supply_marker(grid, chunk_pos, s, &item);
165:             if in_chunk(px, pz) {
166:                 grid.supply_items.push(item);
167:             }
168:         }
169:     }
170: 
171:     // -- doors to Level 1 on the 80u region lattice ---------------------------
172:     let r0x = (chunk_pos.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
173:     let r1x = ((max_x - 0.01) / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
174:     let r0z = (chunk_pos.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
175:     let r1z = ((max_z - 0.01) / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
176:     // The whole door footprint (frame + clearing) fits inside the region
177:     // plan window's 1.0u margin, so every chunk that must stamp part of a
178:     // door can also evaluate its acceptance identically.
179:     if doors <= 0.0 {
180:         return;
181:     }
182:     for rz in r0z..=r1z {
183:         for rx in r0x..=r1x {
184:             let spawn_door_region =
185:                 rx == region_index(SPAWN_DOOR.0) && rz == region_index(SPAWN_DOOR.1);
186:             let (dx, dz) = if spawn_door_region {
187:                 // The authored guaranteed door carves its own clearing; no
188:                 // floor check, so it exists in every reality.
189:                 SPAWN_DOOR
190:             } else {
191:                 let roll = hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_5EED_0000, rx, rz);
192:                 if unit(roll) > DOOR_CHANCE * doors {
193:                     continue;
194:                 }
195:                 // One deterministic spot per region; a spot on solid or
196:                 // anomalous ground simply means this region has no door.
197:                 let probe = hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_0000_0000, rx, rz);
198:                 let px = (rx as f32 + 0.15 + 0.7 * unit(probe)) * REGION_SIZE;
199:                 let pz = (rz as f32 + 0.15 + 0.7 * unit(probe.rotate_left(19))) * REGION_SIZE;
200:                 if !near_chunk(px, pz, DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN) || !ctx.is_open_floor(px, pz) {
201:                     continue;
202:                 }
203:                 (px, pz)
204:             };
205:             if !near_chunk(dx, dz, DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN) {
206:                 continue;
207:             }
208: 
209:             carve_door_clearing(grid, chunk_pos, s, dx, dz);
210:             stamp_level_door(grid, chunk_pos, s, dx, dz, VOXEL_WALL);
211:             if in_chunk(dx, dz) {
212:                 grid.level_exits.push(LevelExit {
213:                     id: hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_0000_1D00, rx, rz),
214:                     target_level: LEVEL_HABITABLE,
215:                     center: Position::new(dx, dz),
216:                     half_extent: DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF,
217:                     arrival: Position::new(ARRIVAL_POINT.0, ARRIVAL_POINT.1),
218:                 });
219:             }
220:         }
221:     }
222: }
223: 
224: /// Guarantees approach space on both sides of a door: air to 2.6u within a
225: /// small square, with the floor slab restored underneath. The radius stays
226: /// under `DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN` so the carve never outruns what neighboring
227: /// chunks can reproduce.
228: fn carve_door_clearing(
229:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
230:     chunk_pos: Position,
231:     voxel_size: f32,
232:     cx: f32,
233:     cz: f32,
234: ) {
235:     let radius = 0.95;
236:     let height_v = (2.6 / voxel_size).round() as i64;
237:     let x0 = ((cx - radius - chunk_pos.x) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
238:     let x1 = ((cx + radius - chunk_pos.x) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
239:     let z0 = ((cz - radius - chunk_pos.z) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
240:     let z1 = ((cz + radius - chunk_pos.z) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
241:     for z in z0.max(0)..=z1.max(-1) {
242:         for x in x0.max(0)..=x1.max(-1) {
243:             let (xu, zu) = (x as usize, z as usize);
244:             if xu >= grid.width() || zu >= grid.depth() {
245:                 continue;
246:             }
247:             for y in 1..=height_v {
248:                 grid.set(xu, y as usize, zu, VOXEL_AIR);
249:             }
250:             if grid.get(xu, 0, zu) == VOXEL_AIR {
251:                 grid.set(
252:                     xu,
253:                     0,
254:                     zu,
255:                     crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_FLOOR,
256:                 );
257:             }
258:         }
259:     }
260: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/geometry.rs
````rust
  1: //! Red Room presentation layered over an authored Level 0 assembly.
  2: //!
  3: //! This sampler knows nothing about chunks or voxel indices.  It receives one
  4: //! world column and returns one architectural decision, leaving recursive
  5: //! world addressing and voxelization to their own stages.
  6: 
  7: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyInstance, Axis2, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase};
  8: use crate::domain::entities::environment::EnvironmentProfile;
  9: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
 10: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 11: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 12: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 13: 
 14: /// Applies avoidable warning cues and the committed encounter topology.
 15: pub(crate) fn sample_red_room(
 16:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 17:     mut column: ColumnPlan,
 18:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 19:     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 20:     world_x: f32,
 21:     world_z: f32,
 22: ) -> ColumnPlan {
 23:     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
 24:     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
 25:     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
 26:     let loop_width = 2.0f32.min(half_x * 0.35).min(half_z * 0.35).max(1.2);
 27:     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
 28: 
 29:     // Warning cues intensify toward the shell but never replace masonry with
 30:     // a special red wall.  The anomaly is read through carpet, compression,
 31:     // and light; collision remains ordinary Level 0 architecture.
 32:     let contamination = (1.0 - boundary / (loop_width * 2.0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 33:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::red_room(contamination);
 34:     if boundary > PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
 35:         if contamination > 0.15 {
 36:             column.floor_material = profile.floor_voxel();
 37:         }
 38:         if contamination > 0.33 {
 39:             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.2).max(2.6);
 40:         }
 41:         if contamination > 0.66 {
 42:             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.4).max(2.4);
 43:         }
 44:     }
 45:     column.red_light = true;
 46: 
 47:     let Some(state) = instance.state(reality) else {
 48:         return column;
 49:     };
 50:     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::Outside {
 51:         return column;
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     // Commitment closes the remembered entrance and reduces the authored
 55:     // room to one walkable perimeter loop around an opaque core.
 56:     let in_core = local_x.abs() < half_x - loop_width && local_z.abs() < half_z - loop_width;
 57:     column.solid = boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T || in_core;
 58:     column.lintel_from_units = None;
 59:     column.floor_material = VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
 60:     column.ceiling_units = column.ceiling_units.min(2.8);
 61:     if column.solid {
 62:         column.light = false;
 63:     }
 64: 
 65:     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::EscapeOpen {
 66:         open_single_escape(
 67:             instance,
 68:             state.epoch,
 69:             config.anomalies.red_escape_bias,
 70:             local_x,
 71:             local_z,
 72:             &mut column,
 73:         );
 74:     }
 75:     column
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Opens one deterministic side of the loop.  The bias is an authored width
 79: /// control: zero keeps the encounter sealed; positive values widen a single
 80: /// breach without turning both symmetric walls into exits.
 81: fn open_single_escape(
 82:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 83:     epoch: u32,
 84:     bias: f32,
 85:     local_x: f32,
 86:     local_z: f32,
 87:     column: &mut ColumnPlan,
 88: ) {
 89:     let width = bias.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.4;
 90:     if width <= 0.0 {
 91:         return;
 92:     }
 93:     let Some(threshold) = instance.gates.first() else {
 94:         return;
 95:     };
 96:     let side_sign = if stable_bit(instance.id, epoch) {
 97:         1.0
 98:     } else {
 99:         -1.0
100:     };
101:     let (side_coordinate, side_extent, along) = match threshold.axis {
102:         Axis2::Z => (local_x, instance.footprint.half_x, local_z),
103:         Axis2::X => (local_z, instance.footprint.half_z, local_x),
104:     };
105:     let on_selected_wall = (side_coordinate - side_sign * side_extent).abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
106:     if on_selected_wall && along.abs() < width {
107:         column.solid = false;
108:     }
109: }
110: 
111: fn stable_bit(instance_id: u64, epoch: u32) -> bool {
112:     let mut value = instance_id ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(29) ^ 0xE5CA_9E5C_A9E5_CA9E;
113:     value ^= value >> 30;
114:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
115:     value ^= value >> 27;
116:     value & 1 == 1
117: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/ports.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 2: 
 3: /// The Ports layer implements the Dependency Inversion Principle (SOLID).
 4: /// Instead of the Use Cases depending on a concrete external noise library or framework,
 5: /// the Use Cases define the interface (Port) they need, and the external layers
 6: /// (Adapters/Drivers) must implement this interface.
 7: 
 8: /// NoiseProvider is a pure interface for extracting deterministic continuous noise.
 9: /// We use this to evaluate the Macro Field (Drift, Density, Motif Selection).
10: pub trait NoiseProvider {
11:     /// Returns a noise value, ideally in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
12:     /// The function must be deterministic given the same seed and position.
13:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32;
14: }
15: 
16: /// TelemetryPort abstracts wall-clock access and log emission so Use Cases
17: /// never touch `std::time` or stdout directly. Both are frameworks concerns,
18: /// and `SystemTime::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
19: pub trait TelemetryPort {
20:     /// Monotonic-ish timestamp in microseconds from an arbitrary epoch.
21:     /// Only ever used to compute durations, never absolute dates.
22:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64;
23:     /// Emits one log line to whatever sink the outer layer provides.
24:     fn log(&self, message: &str);
25: }
26: 
27: /// Silent TelemetryPort used by default and in tests.
28: pub struct NullTelemetry;
29: 
30: impl TelemetryPort for NullTelemetry {
31:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64 {
32:         0
33:     }
34:     fn log(&self, _message: &str) {}
35: }
36: 
37: /// Shared instance so constructors can hand out `&'static dyn TelemetryPort`
38: /// without forcing callers to own a telemetry object.
39: pub static NULL_TELEMETRY: NullTelemetry = NullTelemetry;
````

  6: /// WHY THESE TESTS EXIST:
  7: /// The player reported spawning inside a wall.  Before changing any logic
  8: /// we must prove (a) what coordinates the spawn point produces and (b) whether
  9: /// the floor voxel's collision box overlaps the player's AABB at spawn.
 10: ///
 11: /// Test-first order:
 12: ///   1. Prove the exact world-space coordinates the chunk generator places floor/wall
 13: ///      voxels at for the (0,0) hub chunk in low-spec mode.
 14: ///   2. Prove the spawn point (5.0, 1.7, 5.0) does NOT overlap any wall voxel.
 15: ///   3. Prove the floor voxel box does NOT block the player at spawn.
 16: ///   4. Prove terminal velocity is sane (<= 5 world-units/second).
 17: ///
 18: /// If test 2 or 3 fails, it proves the bug.  Then we add a fix and verify
 19: /// the test passes.
 20: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 21: 
 22: /// The JavaScript side extracts wall collision boxes from the SVO.
 23: /// This Rust analogue extracts the same information directly from the VoxelGrid
 24: /// so we can verify coordinates without the JS/SVO layer.
 25: fn grid_wall_boxes_at_spawn_x(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 26:     // Returns (minX, maxX, minY, maxY, minZ, maxZ) for every solid wall voxel
 27:     // at approximately x=5 world-units inside the chunk.
 28:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 29:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 30:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 31:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 32: 
 33:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 34:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 35: 
 36:     for y in 0..grid.height() {
 37:         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 38:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
 39:                 let vt = grid.get(x, y, z);
 40:                 if vt == VOXEL_WALL {
 41:                     let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 42:                     let wy = y as f32 * scale;
 43:                     let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 44:                     // The JS collision system gives walls a 1-voxel-size box
 45:                     boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, wy, wy + scale, wz, wz + scale));
 46:                 }
 47:             }
 48:         }
 49:     }
 50:     boxes
 51: }
 52: 
 53: fn floor_boxes(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 54:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 55:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 56:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 57:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 58: 
 59:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 60:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 61: 
 62:     for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 63:         for x in 0..grid.width() {
 64:             let vt = grid.get(x, 0, z);
 65:             if vt == VOXEL_FLOOR {
 66:                 let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 67:                 let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 68:                 // Floor voxel: y=0 to y=scale
 69:                 boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, 0.0_f32, scale, wz, wz + scale));
 70:             }
 71:         }
 72:     }
 73:     boxes
 74: }
 75: 
 76: /// Player AABB: eye-level at pos.y, feet at pos.y - 1.65, head at pos.y + 0.1
 77: fn player_overlaps(
 78:     pos: (f32, f32, f32),
 79:     radius: f32,
 80:     vbox: (f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32),
 81: ) -> bool {
 82:     let (px, py, pz) = pos;
 83:     let p_min_x = px - radius;
 84:     let p_max_x = px + radius;
 85:     let p_min_y = py - 1.65;
 86:     let p_max_y = py + 0.1;
 87:     let p_min_z = pz - radius;
 88:     let p_max_z = pz + radius;
 89:     let (v_min_x, v_max_x, v_min_y, v_max_y, v_min_z, v_max_z) = vbox;
 90: 
 91:     p_max_x > v_min_x
 92:         && p_min_x < v_max_x
 93:         && p_max_y > v_min_y
 94:         && p_min_y < v_max_y
 95:         && p_max_z > v_min_z
 96:         && p_min_z < v_max_z
 97: }

172:     let friction: f32 = 10.0; // damping coefficient
173:     let terminal = speed / friction;
174: 
175:     // The old code used speed=15.0 → terminal = 1.5 units/frame @60fps = 90 u/s

179:          This causes the 'too fast' movement bug.\n\

 1: //! Pinhole camera for the splatter, matching the GPU shaders' yaw/pitch
 2: //! basis exactly (same formulas as `drivers::webgl`'s per-frame uniforms),
 3: //! so switching renderers never changes the framing.
 4: 
 5: use crate::application::ports::{DynamicLight, FrameParams, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 6: 
 7: use super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 8: 
 9: pub fn dot(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
10:     a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
11: }
12: 
13: /// Camera basis + per-frame light state, derived once per frame.
14: pub struct Camera {
15:     pub pos: [f32; 3],
16:     pub right: [f32; 3],
17:     pub up: [f32; 3],
18:     pub forward: [f32; 3],
19:     /// Focal length in pixels: h / (2 * tan(fov/2)).
20:     pub focal_px: f32,
21:     pub half_w: f32,
22:     pub half_h: f32,
23:     pub flashlight: bool,
24:     /// Per-frame dynamic lights (flares), pre-flickered by the engine.
25:     pub dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
26:     pub dynamic_light_count: usize,
27: }
28: 
29: impl Camera {
30:     pub fn new(
31:         frame: &FrameParams,
32:         width: usize,
33:         height: usize,
34:         settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
35:     ) -> Self {
36:         let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
37:         let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
38:         Self {
39:             pos: frame.camera_pos,
40:             right: [cy, 0.0, -sy],
41:             up: [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy],
42:             forward: [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy],
43:             focal_px: height as f32 / (2.0 * settings.fov_tan),
44:             half_w: width as f32 / 2.0,
45:             half_h: height as f32 / 2.0,
46:             flashlight: frame.flashlight,
47:             dynamic_lights: frame.dynamic_lights,
48:             dynamic_light_count: (frame.dynamic_light_count as usize).min(MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS),
49:         }
50:     }
51: }
52: 
53: #[cfg(test)]
54: mod tests {

56: 
57:     #[test]
58:     fn malformed_dynamic_light_count_is_clamped_to_storage() {
59:         let frame = FrameParams {
60:             dynamic_light_count: u8::MAX,
61:             ..FrameParams::default()
62:         };
63:         let camera = Camera::new(&frame, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
64: 
65:         assert_eq!(frame.active_dynamic_lights().len(), MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS);
66:         assert_eq!(camera.dynamic_light_count, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS);

126:         let pixel_budget_limited =
127:             self.budget_exhausted && self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes);
128:         SoftwareRasterizerTelemetry {
129:             visited_nodes: self.visited_nodes,
130:             node_soft_limit: self.frame_work_budget.soft_node_visit_limit(),
131:             node_visit_limit: self.frame_work_budget.node_visit_limit(),
132:             node_budget_limited,
133:             budget_exhausted: self.budget_exhausted,
134:             max_virtual_depth: self.max_virtual_depth_reached,
135:             splat_count: self.splat_count,
136:             pixel_writes: self.pixel_writes,
137:             pixel_write_limit: self.frame_work_budget.pixel_write_limit(),
138:             pixel_budget_limited,
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Test seam and frame clear: atmosphere chooses the background; target
143:     /// storage owns color/depth/HZ reset mechanics.
144:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
145:         let background_radiance = if self.environment.outdoor {
146:             self.environment.sky_color
147:         } else {
148:             self.environment.fog_color
149:         };
150:         let background = encode_display_color(background_radiance)
151:             .map(|channel| (channel * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8);
152:         self.target.clear(background);
153:     }
154: 
155:     /// Frame-policy wrapper around the pixel-only target operation. It keeps
156:     /// the exact in-loop write cap and renderer telemetry out of `target`.
157:     fn splat(&mut self, cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, z: f32, rgb: [u8; 3]) {
158:         self.write_splat_request(SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, z, rgb));
159:     }
160: 
161:     /// Writes a shaded voxel surface using its exact ray/plane depth. The
162:     /// emissive flag affects only exact coplanar reconstruction ties.
163:     fn surface_splat(
164:         &mut self,
165:         cx: f32,
166:         cy: f32,
167:         half: f32,
168:         depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
169:         rgb: [u8; 3],
170:         emissive: bool,
171:     ) {
172:         let mut splat = SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, depth.representative_depth(), rgb)
173:             .with_surface_depth(depth);
174:         if emissive {
175:             splat = splat.with_equal_depth_priority();
176:         }
177:         self.write_splat_request(splat);
178:     }
179: 
180:     fn write_splat_request(&mut self, splat: SquareSplat) {
181:         if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes) {
182:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
183:             return;
184:         }
185:         self.splat_count += 1;
186: 
187:         let result = self.target.write_splat(
188:             splat,
189:             self.frame_work_budget
190:                 .remaining_pixel_writes(self.pixel_writes),
191:             self.settings.toggles.hierarchical_z,
192:         );
193:         self.pixel_writes += result.pixel_writes;
194:         self.budget_exhausted |= result.budget_exhausted;
195:     }
196: 
197:     /// Exact pre-shading fine-depth rejection. This deliberately lives at the
198:     /// renderer boundary: traversal can avoid radiance and visibility work,
199:     /// while the pixel target remains the single owner of clipping/depth math.
200:     fn surface_splat_may_contribute(
201:         &self,
202:         cx: f32,
203:         cy: f32,
204:         half: f32,
205:         depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
206:         emissive: bool,
207:     ) -> bool {
208:         if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes) {
209:             return false;
210:         }
211:         let mut splat = SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, depth.representative_depth(), [0; 3])
212:             .with_surface_depth(depth);
213:         if emissive {
214:             splat = splat.with_equal_depth_priority();
215:         }
216:         self.target.surface_splat_may_contribute(&splat)
217:     }
218:

220:     /// test seam; lighting itself remains in `shading`.

362:     }

365:         self.render_cpu_frame(frame, chunks);

369: #[cfg(test)]
370: mod atlas_row_upload_tests {
371:     use crate::application::atlas::ROW_TEXELS;
372:     use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
373: 
374:     use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
375: 
376:     const WORDS_PER_NODE: usize = 4;
377:     const AIR: [u32; WORDS_PER_NODE] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
378: 
379:     fn air_rows(rows: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
380:         AIR.repeat(ROW_TEXELS * rows)
381:     }
382: 
383:     #[test]
384:     fn renderer_port_row_upload_matches_a_full_reference_upload() {
385:         let initial = air_rows(2);
386:         let mut changed_row = air_rows(1);
387:         changed_row[1] = 1;
388:         changed_row[2] = 0x66aa44;
389:         changed_row[3] = 9 | (9 << 16) | (7 << 20) | (5 << 24);
390: 
391:         let mut incremental = SoftwareRasterizer::new(8, 8);
392:         incremental.upload_atlas(&initial);
393:         assert!(incremental.upload_atlas_rows(1, &changed_row));
394: 
395:         let mut expected_atlas = initial;
396:         let second_row_start = ROW_TEXELS * WORDS_PER_NODE;
397:         expected_atlas[second_row_start..].copy_from_slice(&changed_row);
398:         let mut reference = SoftwareRasterizer::new(8, 8);
399:         reference.upload_atlas(&expected_atlas);
400: 
401:         assert_eq!(incremental.atlas, reference.atlas);
402:         assert_eq!(incremental.mips, reference.mips);
403:         assert_eq!(incremental.mip_update_scratch.len(), ROW_TEXELS);
404: 
405:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
406:             origin: [0.0; 3],
407:             root_index: ROW_TEXELS as i32,
408:             world_size: 1.0,
409:             voxel_size: 1.0,
410:             svo_depth: 0,
411:         }];
412:         let frame = FrameParams {
413:             camera_pos: [0.5, 0.5, -2.0],
414:             yaw: std::f32::consts::PI,
415:             ..FrameParams::default()
416:         };
417:         incremental.draw(&frame, &chunks);
418:         reference.draw(&frame, &chunks);
419:         assert_eq!(incremental.framebuffer(), reference.framebuffer());
420:     }
421: }

  1: //! Names the section of the world the player is standing in, for the HUD.
  2: //!
  3: //! The locator re-derives the deterministic region plan for the player's
  4: //! current region (cached per region key, so the plan is recomputed only on
  5: //! a region crossing) and classifies the position against, in priority
  6: //! order: anomaly footprints, assembly footprints, and circulation spines.
  7: //! Platform-agnostic — no browser types — so the classification is natively
  8: //! unit-testable.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 11: use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::{RegionPlan, SpaceProgram};
 12: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 13: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 14: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 15: use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan};
 16: 
 17: /// Backrooms level ids, mirroring the engine's.
 18: const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
 19: const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
 20: 
 21: pub struct SectionLocator {
 22:     seed: u32,
 23:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 24:     noise: SimpleNoiseProvider,
 25:     cached_region: Option<(i64, i64)>,
 26:     plan: Option<RegionPlan>,
 27: }
 28: 
 29: impl SectionLocator {
 30:     pub fn new(seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> Self {
 31:         Self {
 32:             seed,
 33:             config,
 34:             noise: SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
 35:             cached_region: None,
 36:             plan: None,
 37:         }
 38:     }
 39: 
 40:     /// Human-readable "where am I" line for the HUD, e.g.
 41:     /// `LEVEL 0 · PILLAR EXPANSE · REGION (2, -1)`.
 42:     pub fn describe(&mut self, level: u32, x: f32, z: f32) -> String {
 43:         if level == LEVEL_GRASSLAND {
 44:             return "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND".to_string();
 45:         }
 46:         if level == LEVEL_HABITABLE {
 47:             // Level 1's sectors are a pure world-lattice function; no
 48:             // region plan exists (or is needed) on the Habitable Zone.
 49:             let sector =
 50:                 vackrooms::use_cases::level_one::Sector::at(self.seed, x, z).name();
 51:             return format!("LEVEL 1 · HABITABLE ZONE · {sector}");
 52:         }
 53:         let rx = (x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 54:         let rz = (z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 55:         let zone = self.zone_name(rx, rz, x, z);
 56:         format!("LEVEL {level} · {zone} · REGION ({rx}, {rz})")
 57:     }
 58: 
 59:     fn zone_name(&mut self, rx: i64, rz: i64, x: f32, z: f32) -> &'static str {
 60:         if self.cached_region != Some((rx, rz)) {
 61:             self.plan = Some(generate_region_plan(
 62:                 self.seed,
 63:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 64:                 REGION_SIZE,
 65:                 &self.config,
 66:                 &self.noise,
 67:             ));
 68:             self.cached_region = Some((rx, rz));
 69:         }
 70:         let plan = self.plan.as_ref().expect("plan cached above");
 71: 
 72:         // Anomalies dominate: standing inside one matters more than which
 73:         // office footprint it swallowed.
 74:         for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 75:             if anomaly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 76:                 return match anomaly.kind {
 77:                     AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => "PILLAR EXPANSE",
 78:                     AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => "BLACKOUT EXPANSE",
 79:                     AnomalyKind::PitLattice => "PIT LATTICE",
 80:                     AnomalyKind::RedRoom => "RED LOOP",
 81:                     AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => "ARCHWAY ANCHOR",
 82:                 };
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85:         for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 86:             if assembly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 87:                 return program_name(assembly.program);
 88:             }
 89:         }
 90:         for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 91:             if corridor.distance(x, z) <= corridor.width * 0.5 {
 92:                 return program_name(corridor.spine_kind);
 93:             }
 94:         }
 95:         "OPEN FABRIC"
 96:     }
 97: }
 98: 
 99: fn program_name(program: SpaceProgram) -> &'static str {
100:     match program {
101:         SpaceProgram::Arrival => "ARRIVAL",
102:         SpaceProgram::Reception => "RECEPTION",
103:         SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => "MAIN CORRIDOR",
104:         SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall => "SECONDARY HALL",
105:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => "OPEN OFFICE",
106:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => "PRIVATE OFFICE",
107:         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => "CONFERENCE ROOM",
108:         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => "WAITING AREA",
109:         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => "BREAK ROOM",
110:         SpaceProgram::Storage => "STORAGE",
111:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => "SERVER ROOM",
112:         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => "RESTROOM CORE",
113:         SpaceProgram::Stair => "STAIRWELL",
114:         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => "MECHANICAL",
115:         SpaceProgram::Atrium => "ATRIUM",
116:         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "ABANDONED EXPANSION",
117:     }
118: }
119: 
120: #[cfg(test)]
121: mod tests {
122:     use super::*;
123:     use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point;
124: 
125:     #[test]
126:     fn grassland_never_computes_a_plan() {
127:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
128:         assert_eq!(
129:             locator.describe(34, 12345.0, -9876.0),
130:             "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND"
131:         );
132:         assert!(locator.plan.is_none(), "no region plan needed outdoors");
133:     }
134: 
135:     #[test]
136:     fn spawn_is_on_the_main_corridor() {
137:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
138:         let at = spawn_point(42);
139:         let text = locator.describe(0, at.x, at.z);
140:         assert!(
141:             text.contains("MAIN CORRIDOR") || text.contains("ARRIVAL"),
142:             "spawn should sit on readable circulation, got: {text}"
143:         );
144:         assert!(text.starts_with("LEVEL 0 · "), "{text}");
145:         assert!(text.contains("REGION (0, 0)"), "{text}");
146:     }
147: 
148:     #[test]
149:     fn region_plan_is_cached_until_a_region_crossing() {
150:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
151:         locator.describe(0, 5.0, 5.0);
152:         let first = locator.cached_region;
153:         locator.describe(0, 6.0, 6.0);
154:         assert_eq!(locator.cached_region, first, "same region: no recompute");
155:         locator.describe(0, 5.0 + REGION_SIZE, 5.0);
156:         assert_ne!(locator.cached_region, first, "crossing must recompute");
157:     }
158: 
159:     #[test]
160:     fn forced_anomaly_is_reported_at_its_own_center() {
161:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
162:         config.anomalies.forced_kind =
163:             Some(vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
164:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, config);
165:         // Find the forced instance's center via the same plan the locator
166:         // uses; standing on its center must classify as the anomaly.
167:         let plan = generate_region_plan(
168:             42,
169:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
170:             REGION_SIZE,
171:             &config,
172:             &SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
173:         );
174:         let forced = plan
175:             .anomalies
176:             .iter()
177:             .find(|a| a.kind == vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
178:         if let Some(instance) = forced {
179:             let c = instance.footprint.center;
180:             let text = locator.describe(0, c.x, c.z);
181:             assert!(text.contains("PILLAR EXPANSE"), "{text}");
182:         }
183:     }
184: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/rendering/mod.rs
````rust
  1: //! Renderer-independent reference equations.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module defines the small, platform-free mathematical contract that
  4: //! presentation drivers can implement. Values are linear (never gamma
  5: //! encoded), distances are in world units, and all cosine terms are
  6: //! dimensionless.
  7: 
  8: /// Linear RGB radiance or radiance-like intensity.
  9: pub type LinearRgb = [f32; 3];
 10: 
 11: /// Converts linear HDR radiance to the canvas' ordinary sRGB encoding.
 12: ///
 13: /// The same monotone Reinhard curve and IEC sRGB transfer function are used
 14: /// by both new GPU shaders. Keeping a CPU form here prevents clear colors and
 15: /// test probes from accidentally treating linear atmosphere values as display
 16: /// values (which made unloaded outdoor space much too dark).
 17: pub fn encode_display_color(radiance: LinearRgb) -> LinearRgb {
 18:     radiance.map(|channel| {
 19:         let linear = nonnegative_radiance(channel);
 20:         let mapped = if linear == f32::INFINITY {
 21:             1.0
 22:         } else {
 23:             linear / (1.0 + linear)
 24:         };
 25:         if mapped <= 0.003_130_8 {
 26:             mapped * 12.92
 27:         } else {
 28:             1.055 * mapped.powf(1.0 / 2.4) - 0.055
 29:         }
 30:     })
 31: }
 32: 
 33: /// Beer-Lambert transmittance through a homogeneous medium.
 34: ///
 35: /// ```text
 36: /// T(d) = exp(-sigma_t * d)
 37: /// ```
 38: ///
 39: /// `distance` is a path length in world units and `extinction` is the total
 40: /// extinction coefficient `sigma_t` in inverse world units. Negative lengths
 41: /// and coefficients are treated as zero. A `NaN` input produces full
 42: /// transmittance rather than contaminating the frame with `NaN` values.
 43: pub fn beer_lambert_transmittance(distance: f32, extinction: f32) -> f32 {
 44:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
 45:         return 1.0;
 46:     };
 47:     let Some(extinction) = nonnegative(extinction) else {
 48:         return 1.0;
 49:     };
 50: 
 51:     if distance == 0.0 || extinction == 0.0 {
 52:         return 1.0;
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     (-extinction * distance).exp()
 56: }
 57: 
 58: /// Beer-Lambert transmittance with a clear near field.
 59: ///
 60: /// Fog occupies only the portion of the view ray beyond `fog_start`:
 61: ///
 62: /// ```text
 63: /// d_fog = max(view_distance - fog_start, 0)
 64: /// T     = exp(-sigma_t * d_fog)
 65: /// ```
 66: ///
 67: /// All distances use world units. Negative distances and starts are clamped
 68: /// to zero. Invalid (`NaN`) values fail open with full transmittance.
 69: pub fn fog_transmittance(view_distance: f32, fog_start: f32, extinction: f32) -> f32 {
 70:     let (Some(view_distance), Some(fog_start)) =
 71:         (nonnegative(view_distance), nonnegative(fog_start))
 72:     else {
 73:         return 1.0;
 74:     };
 75: 
 76:     let fog_distance = if view_distance <= fog_start {
 77:         0.0
 78:     } else {
 79:         view_distance - fog_start
 80:     };
 81:     beer_lambert_transmittance(fog_distance, extinction)
 82: }
 83: 
 84: /// Composes surface radiance with homogeneous fog in linear RGB.
 85: ///
 86: /// ```text
 87: /// L = T * L_surface + (1 - T) * L_fog
 88: /// ```
 89: ///
 90: /// Both RGB inputs must use the same linear radiometric units. Negative and
 91: /// `NaN` channels are treated as zero. `transmittance` is clamped to `[0, 1]`;
 92: /// `NaN` fails open (`T = 1`). Endpoint branches avoid `0 * infinity`.
 93: pub fn compose_fog(
 94:     surface_radiance: LinearRgb,
 95:     fog_radiance: LinearRgb,
 96:     transmittance: f32,
 97: ) -> LinearRgb {
 98:     let surface = surface_radiance.map(nonnegative_radiance);
 99:     let fog = fog_radiance.map(nonnegative_radiance);
100:     let transmittance = unit_interval_or_one(transmittance);
101: 
102:     if transmittance == 1.0 {
103:         return surface;
104:     }
105:     if transmittance == 0.0 {
106:         return fog;
107:     }
108: 
109:     let scattered = 1.0 - transmittance;
110:     [
111:         surface[0] * transmittance + fog[0] * scattered,
112:         surface[1] * transmittance + fog[1] * scattered,
113:         surface[2] * transmittance + fog[2] * scattered,
114:     ]
115: }
116: 
117: /// Smooth compact-support window for a finite-range light.
118: ///
119: /// For distance `d` and range `R` (both world lengths), the window is
120: ///
121: /// ```text
122: /// w(d, R) = (1 - (d / R)^4)^2,  0 <= d < R
123: ///           0,                    d >= R
124: /// ```
125: ///
126: /// The value and first derivative are zero at `R`, avoiding a hard lighting
127: /// seam. A non-positive, `NaN`, or otherwise invalid range disables the light.
128: pub fn compact_support_window(distance: f32, range: f32) -> f32 {
129:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
130:         return 0.0;
131:     };
132:     let Some(range) = positive(range) else {
133:         return 0.0;
134:     };
135: 
136:     if distance >= range || distance == f32::INFINITY {
137:         return 0.0;
138:     }
139:     if range == f32::INFINITY {
140:         return 1.0;
141:     }
142: 
143:     let ratio_squared = (distance / range).powi(2);
144:     let one_minus_fourth = 1.0 - ratio_squared * ratio_squared;
145:     one_minus_fourth * one_minus_fourth
146: }
147: 
148: /// Finite-range inverse-square attenuation.
149: ///
150: /// ```text
151: /// A(d) = w(d, R) / max(d, d_min)^2
152: /// ```
153: ///
154: /// `distance`, `range`, and `minimum_distance` are world lengths, so the
155: /// result has units of inverse world-units squared. `minimum_distance` is the
156: /// finite emitter-size clamp that removes the point-light singularity. A
157: /// non-positive or `NaN` range/clamp disables the term; `NaN` distance also
158: /// returns zero.
159: pub fn finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(
160:     distance: f32,
161:     range: f32,
162:     minimum_distance: f32,
163: ) -> f32 {
164:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
165:         return 0.0;
166:     };
167:     let Some(minimum_distance) = positive(minimum_distance) else {
168:         return 0.0;
169:     };
170: 
171:     let window = compact_support_window(distance, range);
172:     if window == 0.0 {
173:         return 0.0;
174:     }
175: 
176:     let denominator = distance.max(minimum_distance).powi(2);
177:     if denominator == f32::INFINITY {
178:         0.0
179:     } else {
180:         window / denominator
181:     }
182: }
183: 
184: /// Lambertian receiver cosine.
185: ///
186: /// ```text
187: /// cos_receiver = max(dot(n_receiver, omega_to_light), 0)
188: /// ```
189: ///
190: /// Vectors are normalized internally, so callers may use any finite non-zero
191: /// magnitude. Zero-length or non-finite vectors return zero.
192: pub fn lambertian_receiver_cosine(receiver_normal: [f32; 3], direction_to_light: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
193:     positive_cosine(receiver_normal, direction_to_light)
194: }
195: 
196: /// One-sided emission cosine for a horizontal rectangular ceiling panel.
197: ///
198: /// The panel's emitting normal is `(0, -1, 0)`. For a direction from a point
199: /// on the emitter toward the receiver,
200: ///
201: /// ```text
202: /// cos_emitter = max(dot((0, -1, 0), omega_to_receiver), 0)
203: /// ```
204: ///
205: /// Rectangle area belongs to the later irradiance integral; this function is
206: /// only its dimensionless directional factor. Zero-length or non-finite
207: /// directions return zero.
208: pub fn downward_rectangular_emitter_cosine(direction_to_receiver: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
209:     positive_cosine([0.0, -1.0, 0.0], direction_to_receiver)
210: }
211: 
212: fn positive_cosine(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
213:     let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (normalize(a), normalize(b)) else {
214:         return 0.0;
215:     };
216:     (a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
217: }
218: 
219: /// Normalizes without overflowing when a finite component is near `f32::MAX`.
220: fn normalize(vector: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
221:     if vector.iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
222:         return None;
223:     }
224: 
225:     let scale = vector
226:         .iter()
227:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
228:     if scale == 0.0 {
229:         return None;
230:     }
231: 
232:     let scaled = vector.map(|component| component / scale);
233:     let length = (scaled[0] * scaled[0] + scaled[1] * scaled[1] + scaled[2] * scaled[2]).sqrt();
234:     Some(scaled.map(|component| component / length))
235: }
236: 
237: fn nonnegative(value: f32) -> Option<f32> {
238:     if value.is_nan() {
239:         None
240:     } else {
241:         Some(value.max(0.0))
242:     }
243: }
244: 
245: fn positive(value: f32) -> Option<f32> {
246:     if value.is_nan() || value <= 0.0 {
247:         None
248:     } else {
249:         Some(value)
250:     }
251: }
252: 
253: fn nonnegative_radiance(value: f32) -> f32 {
254:     if value.is_nan() || value < 0.0 {
255:         0.0
256:     } else {
257:         value
258:     }
259: }
260: 
261: fn unit_interval_or_one(value: f32) -> f32 {
262:     if value.is_nan() {
263:         1.0
264:     } else {
265:         value.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
266:     }
267: }

  1: //! Axis-aligned collision primitives and the sliding-collision world.
  2: //!
  3: //! Collision geometry is *derived from the SVO itself* (solid leaf nodes of
  4: //! type WALL / RED_WALL become world-space boxes), so the physical world and
  5: //! the rendered world can never drift apart.
  6: 
  7: /// Axis-aligned bounding box in world space.
  8: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  9: pub struct Aabb {
 10:     pub min: [f32; 3],
 11:     pub max: [f32; 3],
 12: }
 13: 
 14: impl Aabb {
 15:     pub fn new(min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 16:         Self { min, max }
 17:     }
 18: 
 19:     pub fn intersects(&self, other: &Aabb) -> bool {
 20:         self.max[0] > other.min[0]
 21:             && self.min[0] < other.max[0]
 22:             && self.max[1] > other.min[1]
 23:             && self.min[1] < other.max[1]
 24:             && self.max[2] > other.min[2]
 25:             && self.min[2] < other.max[2]
 26:     }
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Player capsule approximated as an AABB, matching the original client:
 30: /// radius 0.35 around the eye, extending 1.65 below and 0.1 above eye level.
 31: pub const PLAYER_RADIUS: f32 = 0.35;
 32: pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET: f32 = 1.65;
 33: pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD: f32 = 0.1;
 34: 
 35: /// Builds the player's AABB from an eye-level position.
 36: pub fn player_aabb(eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> Aabb {
 37:     Aabb::new(
 38:         [
 39:             eye_pos[0] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
 40:             eye_pos[1] - PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET,
 41:             eye_pos[2] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
 42:         ],
 43:         [
 44:             eye_pos[0] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
 45:             eye_pos[1] + PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD,
 46:             eye_pos[2] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
 47:         ],
 48:     )
 49: }
 50: 
 51: /// The set of solid boxes the player can collide with.
 52: /// Rebuilt whenever the chunk set changes.
 53: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 54: pub struct CollisionWorld {
 55:     boxes: Vec<Aabb>,
 56: }
 57: 
 58: impl CollisionWorld {
 59:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 60:         Self { boxes: Vec::new() }
 61:     }
 62: 
 63:     pub fn rebuild<'a, I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Aabb>>(&mut self, boxes: I) {
 64:         self.boxes.clear();
 65:         self.boxes.extend(boxes.into_iter().copied());
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 69:         self.boxes.len()
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 73:         self.boxes.is_empty()
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     pub fn boxes(&self) -> &[Aabb] {
 77:         &self.boxes
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     /// True if a player standing at `eye_pos` overlaps any solid box.
 81:     pub fn collides(&self, eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 82:         let p = player_aabb(eye_pos);
 83:         self.boxes.iter().any(|b| p.intersects(b))
 84:     }
 85: }
 86:

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/prepare_frame_lighting.rs
````rust
  1: //! Prepare the immutable fixture list consumed by a render frame.
  2: //!
  3: //! Chunk payloads overlap on purpose, so the same ceiling panel can arrive
  4: //! from several neighboring halos. Selection belongs here, before any GPU
  5: //! driver: all renderers must see the same deduplicated physical scene.
  6: 
  7: use std::collections::HashMap;
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
 10: 
 11: /// Collects every finite, enabled fixture and orders it by conservative
 12: /// contribution at `camera_position`.
 13: ///
 14: /// The ordering is not a budget: no fixture is discarded. It keeps the hero
 15: /// shadow choice stable and makes output independent of hash-map/chunk arrival
 16: /// order. Projected emitter area and authored intensity raise importance while
 17: /// squared distance lowers it.
 18: pub fn select_scene_lights<'a>(
 19:     lights: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
 20:     camera_position: [f32; 3],
 21: ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 22:     let mut unique = HashMap::<u64, LightSource>::new();
 23:     for light in lights.copied() {
 24:         if light.enabled && valid(&light) {
 25:             unique.entry(light.id).or_insert(light);
 26:         }
 27:     }
 28: 
 29:     let mut ranked: Vec<(LightSource, f32)> = unique
 30:         .into_values()
 31:         .map(|light| {
 32:             let delta = [
 33:                 light.position[0] - camera_position[0],
 34:                 light.position[1] - camera_position[1],
 35:                 light.position[2] - camera_position[2],
 36:             ];
 37:             let distance_squared = delta.into_iter().map(|v| v * v).sum::<f32>();
 38:             let area = (4.0 * light.half_size[0] * light.half_size[1]).max(0.01);
 39:             let importance = light.intensity * area / (distance_squared + area);
 40:             (light, importance)
 41:         })
 42:         .collect();
 43:     ranked.sort_by(|(a, a_score), (b, b_score)| {
 44:         b_score.total_cmp(a_score).then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
 45:     });
 46: 
 47:     ranked.into_iter().map(|(light, _)| light).collect()
 48: }
 49: 
 50: fn valid(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
 51:     light.position.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
 52:         && light.color.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
 53:         && light
 54:             .half_size
 55:             .into_iter()

 8: const ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS: usize = 8;

32: impl RoomScene {
33:     /// One closed 4x4x4-world-unit room with a single 0.5-unit fluorescent
34:     /// ceiling panel. The panel replaces one ceiling voxel and its underside
35:     /// borders air; the entire floor remains ordinary non-emissive carpet.
36:     pub fn single_ceiling_fixture() -> Self {
37:         let mut voxels = VoxelGrid::new(ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS, ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS, ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS);
38:         fill_floor(&mut voxels);
39:         fill_boundary_walls(&mut voxels);
40:         fill_ceiling(&mut voxels);
41:         voxels.set(PANEL_X, ROOM_CEILING_Y, PANEL_Z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
42: 
43:         Self {
44:             voxels,
45:             voxel_size: REFERENCE_VOXEL_SIZE,
46:             origin: [0.0; 3],
47:         }
48:     }

51:         &self.voxels

56:     }
57: 
58:     pub fn origin(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
59:         self.origin
60:     }
61: 
62:     pub(crate) fn into_parts(self) -> (VoxelGrid, f32, [f32; 3]) {
63:         (self.voxels, self.voxel_size, self.origin)
64:     }

67: fn fill_floor(voxels: &mut VoxelGrid) {
68:     for z in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
69:         for x in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
70:             voxels.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_FLOOR);
71:         }
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: fn fill_boundary_walls(voxels: &mut VoxelGrid) {
76:     for y in 1..=ROOM_CEILING_Y {
77:         for edge in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
78:             voxels.set(0, y, edge, VOXEL_WALL);
79:             voxels.set(ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS - 1, y, edge, VOXEL_WALL);
80:             voxels.set(edge, y, 0, VOXEL_WALL);

89:             voxels.set(x, ROOM_CEILING_Y, z, VOXEL_CEILING);
