## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/program.rs
````rust
 1: //! WebGL2 context creation and shader program linking — the one copy of
 2: //! this plumbing for all drivers.
 3: 
 4: use js_sys::Reflect;
 5: use wasm_bindgen::{JsCast, JsValue};
 6: use web_sys::{HtmlCanvasElement, WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlProgram, WebGlShader};
 7: 
 8: /// Options for [`create_context`]. Raster paths want a depth buffer; the
 9: /// fullscreen raymarcher resolves visibility itself, so depth and MSAA
10: /// would be wasted bandwidth on low-spec GPUs.
11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
12: pub struct ContextOptions {
13:     pub depth: bool,
14: }
15: 
16: /// Creates a WebGL2 context with the engine's standard attributes
17: /// (no antialiasing, opaque, high-performance GPU preference).
18: pub fn create_context(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement, options: ContextOptions) -> Result<Gl, JsValue> {
19:     let attrs = js_sys::Object::new();
20:     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"antialias".into(), &false.into())?;
21:     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"depth".into(), &options.depth.into())?;
22:     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"stencil".into(), &false.into())?;
23:     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"alpha".into(), &false.into())?;
24:     Reflect::set(
25:         &attrs,
26:         &"powerPreference".into(),
27:         &"high-performance".into(),
28:     )?;
29:     canvas
30:         .get_context_with_context_options("webgl2", &attrs)?
31:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("WebGL2 is not supported on this browser"))?
32:         .dyn_into::<Gl>()
33:         .map_err(|_| JsValue::from_str("webgl2 context has an unexpected type"))
34: }
35: 
36: pub fn compile_shader(gl: &Gl, kind: u32, source: &str) -> Result<WebGlShader, JsValue> {
37:     let shader = gl
38:         .create_shader(kind)
39:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create shader object"))?;
40:     gl.shader_source(&shader, source);
41:     gl.compile_shader(&shader);
42:     if gl
43:         .get_shader_parameter(&shader, Gl::COMPILE_STATUS)
44:         .as_bool()
45:         .unwrap_or(false)
46:     {
47:         Ok(shader)
48:     } else {
49:         let log = gl.get_shader_info_log(&shader).unwrap_or_default();
50:         gl.delete_shader(Some(&shader));
51:         Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("shader compile error: {log}")))
52:     }
53: }
54: 
55: pub fn link_program(gl: &Gl, vertex: &str, fragment: &str) -> Result<WebGlProgram, JsValue> {
56:     let vs = compile_shader(gl, Gl::VERTEX_SHADER, vertex)?;
57:     let fs = compile_shader(gl, Gl::FRAGMENT_SHADER, fragment)?;
58:     let program = gl
59:         .create_program()
60:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create shader program"))?;
61:     gl.attach_shader(&program, &vs);
62:     gl.attach_shader(&program, &fs);
63:     gl.link_program(&program);
64:     if gl
65:         .get_program_parameter(&program, Gl::LINK_STATUS)
66:         .as_bool()
67:         .unwrap_or(false)
68:     {
69:         Ok(program)
70:     } else {
71:         let log = gl.get_program_info_log(&program).unwrap_or_default();
72:         gl.delete_program(Some(&program));
73:         Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("shader link error: {log}")))
74:     }
75: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/sample_static_irradiance.rs
````rust
 1: //! Sample the baked field in the air cell adjacent to a visible face.
 2: //!
 3: //! Texture texels represent voxel centers. Sampling on the geometric face
 4: //! plane blends the solid receiver with air and was the source of false
 5: //! floor patches. A half-voxel normal offset lands exactly at the adjacent
 6: //! air-cell center for every axis-aligned face.
 7: 
 8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 9: vec3 sampleStaticIrradiance(vec3 worldPosition, vec3 normal) {
10:     if (uBakedLightingEnabled == 0) return vec3(0.0);
11: 
12:     ivec3 dimensions = textureSize(uLightVolume, 0);
13:     if (any(lessThanEqual(dimensions, ivec3(0)))) {
14:         float scalarFallback = clamp(vStaticIndirect * (1.0 / 15.0), 0.0, 1.0);
15:         return vec3(scalarFallback);
16:     }
17: 
18:     vec3 worldExtent = vec3(dimensions) * uVoxelSize;
19:     vec3 adjacentAirCenter = worldPosition + normal * (0.5 * uVoxelSize);
20:     vec3 uvw = (adjacentAirCenter - uLightVolumeOrigin) / worldExtent;
21:     if (any(lessThan(uvw, vec3(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(uvw, vec3(1.0)))) {
22:         return vec3(0.0);
23:     }
24:     return texture(uLightVolume, uvw).rgb;
25: }
26: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/evaluate_scene_lighting.rs
````rust
  1: //! Direct-light equations shared by the surface and voxel-hit shaders.
  2: //!
  3: //! Rectangular emitters use deterministic 2×2 Gauss quadrature over their
  4: //! physical area. Point lights use the same finite-range inverse-square law
  5: //! without the area integral. This is intentionally compact and diagnosable;
  6: //! shadow visibility is an explicit input owned by the caller.
  7: 
  8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
  9: const float PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
 10: const int LIGHT_POINT = 0;
 11: const int LIGHT_CEILING_PANEL = 1;
 12: const int LIGHT_STRIP = 2;
 13: const int LIGHT_EMERGENCY = 3;
 14: 
 15: float finiteRangeInverseSquare(float distanceSquared, float range) {
 16:     if (!(range > 0.0) || !(distanceSquared >= 0.0)) return 0.0;
 17:     float rangeSquared = range * range;
 18:     float normalizedSquared = distanceSquared / rangeSquared;
 19:     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
 20:     return (window * window) / max(distanceSquared, 0.04);
 21: }
 22: 
 23: float receiverCosine(vec3 normal, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
 24:     return max(dot(normal, surfaceToLight), 0.0);
 25: }
 26: 
 27: float emitterCosine(int kind, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
 28:     if (kind == LIGHT_POINT) return 1.0;
 29:     // Rectangular fixtures lie in XZ and point down. `surfaceToLight.y` is
 30:     // positive exactly when the receiver is in their emitting hemisphere.
 31:     return max(surfaceToLight.y, 0.0);
 32: }
 33: 
 34: vec3 evaluatePointLight(
 35:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 36:     vec3 normal,
 37:     vec3 lightPosition,
 38:     vec3 lightColor,
 39:     float range,
 40:     float intensity
 41: ) {
 42:     vec3 delta = lightPosition - surfacePosition;
 43:     float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 44:     vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 45:     float geometry = receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight);
 46:     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0)
 47:         * finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range) * geometry;
 48: }
 49: 
 50: vec3 evaluateRectangleLight(
 51:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 52:     vec3 normal,
 53:     vec3 lightPosition,
 54:     vec2 halfSize,
 55:     vec3 lightColor,
 56:     float range,
 57:     float intensity,
 58:     int kind
 59: ) {
 60:     const float GAUSS = 0.5773502691896258;
 61:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
 62:         vec2(-GAUSS, -GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS, -GAUSS),
 63:         vec2(-GAUSS,  GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS,  GAUSS)
 64:     );
 65:     vec3 integral = vec3(0.0);
 66:     for (int sampleIndex = 0; sampleIndex < 4; ++sampleIndex) {
 67:         vec2 offset = offsets[sampleIndex] * halfSize;
 68:         vec3 samplePosition = lightPosition + vec3(offset.x, 0.0, offset.y);
 69:         vec3 delta = samplePosition - surfacePosition;
 70:         float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 71:         vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 72:         float geometry = receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight)
 73:             * emitterCosine(kind, surfaceToLight);
 74:         integral += finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range) * geometry;
 75:     }
 76:     float area = 4.0 * max(halfSize.x, 0.0) * max(halfSize.y, 0.0);
 77:     if (!(area > 0.0)) return vec3(0.0);
 78:     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0)
 79:         * area * (integral * 0.25);
 80: }
 81: 
 82: vec3 evaluateSceneLight(
 83:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 84:     vec3 normal,
 85:     vec3 lightPosition,
 86:     vec2 halfSize,
 87:     vec3 lightColor,
 88:     float range,
 89:     float intensity,
 90:     int kind
 91: ) {
 92:     if (kind == LIGHT_POINT) {
 93:         return evaluatePointLight(
 94:             surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, lightColor, range, intensity
 95:         );
 96:     }
 97:     return evaluateRectangleLight(
 98:         surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, halfSize,
 99:         lightColor, range, intensity, kind
100:     );
101: }
102: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/fs_artifact_sink.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::application::ports::{POSITION_FIXED_SCALE, SurfaceChunk};
 2: use crate::core::ports::artifact_sink::ArtifactSinkPort;
 3: use crate::core::ports::reference_renderer::RenderedImage;
 4: use std::fs;
 5: use std::io::Write;
 6: use std::path::Path;
 7: 
 8: pub struct FsArtifactSink;
 9: 
10: impl ArtifactSinkPort for FsArtifactSink {
11:     fn write_png(&self, path: &Path, image: &RenderedImage) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
12:         // Encode raw RGBA bytes into a PNG file.
13:         image::save_buffer(
14:             path,
15:             &image.rgba,
16:             image.width,
17:             image.height,
18:             image::ExtendedColorType::Rgba8,
19:         )
20:         .map_err(|error| std::io::Error::other(error.to_string()))
21:     }
22: 
23:     fn write_obj(&self, path: &Path, chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
24:         let mut file = fs::File::create(path)?;
25: 
26:         writeln!(file, "o backrooms_scene")?;
27: 
28:         let mut vertex_offset = 1; // OBJ indices are 1-based
29: 
30:         for chunk in chunks {
31:             writeln!(file, "g chunk_{}_{}", chunk.key.0, chunk.key.1)?;
32: 
33:             for v in &chunk.mesh.vertices {
34:                 let px = (v.position[0] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[0];
35:                 let py = (v.position[1] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[1];
36:                 let pz = (v.position[2] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[2];
37:                 writeln!(file, "v {:.6} {:.6} {:.6}", px, py, pz)?;
38:             }
39: 
40:             let mut i = 0;
41:             while i + 2 < chunk.mesh.indices.len() {
42:                 let i1 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i] as usize) + vertex_offset;
43:                 let i2 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 1] as usize) + vertex_offset;
44:                 let i3 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 2] as usize) + vertex_offset;
45:                 writeln!(file, "f {} {} {}", i1, i2, i3)?;
46:                 i += 3;
47:             }
48: 
49:             vertex_offset += chunk.mesh.vertices.len();
50:         }
51: 
52:         Ok(())
53:     }
54: }
````

````rust
 21:     pub fn new(screen_width: usize, screen_height: usize) -> Self {
 22:         Self {
 23:             grid_data: Vec::new(),

 29:             screen_width,

 34:     pub fn set_grid(
 35:         &mut self,
 36:         width: usize,
 37:         height: usize,
 38:         depth: usize,
 39:         data: &[u8],
 40:         light: &[u8],
 41:     ) {
 42:         self.width = width;
 43:         self.height = height;
 44:         self.depth = depth;
 45:         self.grid_data = data.to_vec();
 46:         self.light_data = light.to_vec();
 47:     }

 49:     pub fn get_frame_buffer(&self) -> *const u8 {
 50:         self.frame_buffer.as_ptr()
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     fn get_voxel(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 54:         if x < 0
 55:             || y < 0
 56:             || z < 0
 57:             || x >= self.width as isize
 58:             || y >= self.height as isize
 59:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 60:         {
 61:             return VOXEL_AIR;
 62:         }
 63:         self.grid_data
 64:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     fn get_light(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 68:         if x < 0
 69:             || y < 0
 70:             || z < 0
 71:             || x >= self.width as isize
 72:             || y >= self.height as isize
 73:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 74:         {
 75:             return 0;
 76:         }
 77:         self.light_data
 78:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 79:     }

 81:     pub fn render(&mut self, px: f32, py: f32, pz: f32, yaw: f32, pitch: f32, fov_deg: f32) {
 82:         // Clear background to dark fog
 83:         for i in (0..self.frame_buffer.len()).step_by(4) {
 84:             self.frame_buffer[i] = 10; // R
 85:             self.frame_buffer[i + 1] = 10; // G
 86:             self.frame_buffer[i + 2] = 10; // B
 87:             self.frame_buffer[i + 3] = 255; // A
 88:         }
 89: 
 90:         if self.width == 0 {
 91:             return;
 92:         }
 93: 
 94:         let fov_rad = fov_deg * std::f32::consts::PI / 180.0;
 95:         let half_fov = fov_rad / 2.0;
 96: 
 97:         let dir_x = -yaw.sin();
 98:         let dir_z = -yaw.cos();
 99:         let plane_x = yaw.cos() * half_fov.tan();
100:         let plane_z = -yaw.sin() * half_fov.tan();
101: 
102:         for x in 0..self.screen_width {
103:             let camera_x = 2.0 * (x as f32) / (self.screen_width as f32) - 1.0;
104:             let ray_dir_x = dir_x + plane_x * camera_x;
105:             let ray_dir_z = dir_z + plane_z * camera_x;
106: 
107:             let mut map_x = px.floor() as isize;
108:             let mut map_z = pz.floor() as isize;
109: 
110:             let delta_dist_x = if ray_dir_x == 0.0 {
111:                 f32::INFINITY
112:             } else {
113:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_x).abs()
114:             };
115:             let delta_dist_z = if ray_dir_z == 0.0 {
116:                 f32::INFINITY
117:             } else {
118:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_z).abs()
119:             };
120: 
121:             let mut side_dist_x;
122:             let mut side_dist_z;
123:             let step_x: isize;
124:             let step_z: isize;
125: 
126:             if ray_dir_x < 0.0 {
127:                 step_x = -1;
128:                 side_dist_x = (px - map_x as f32) * delta_dist_x;
129:             } else {
130:                 step_x = 1;
131:                 side_dist_x = (map_x as f32 + 1.0 - px) * delta_dist_x;
132:             }
133: 
134:             if ray_dir_z < 0.0 {
135:                 step_z = -1;
136:                 side_dist_z = (pz - map_z as f32) * delta_dist_z;
137:             } else {
138:                 step_z = 1;
139:                 side_dist_z = (map_z as f32 + 1.0 - pz) * delta_dist_z;
140:             }
141: 
142:             let mut hit = 0;
143:             let mut side = 0;
144:             let mut perp_wall_dist = 0.0;
145:             let mut hit_y = 0;
146: 
147:             let map_y = py.floor() as isize;
148:             let max_steps = 200;
149:             let mut steps = 0;
150: 
151:             while hit == 0 && steps < max_steps {
152:                 if side_dist_x < side_dist_z {
153:                     side_dist_x += delta_dist_x;
154:                     map_x += step_x;
155:                     side = 0;
156:                 } else {
157:                     side_dist_z += delta_dist_z;
158:                     map_z += step_z;
159:                     side = 1;
160:                 }
161: 
162:                 let v = self.get_voxel(map_x, map_y, map_z);
163:                 if v != VOXEL_AIR {
164:                     hit = v;
165:                     hit_y = map_y;
166:                 }
167:                 steps += 1;
168:             }
169: 
170:             if hit > 0 {
171:                 if side == 0 {
172:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_x - delta_dist_x;
173:                 } else {
174:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_z - delta_dist_z;
175:                 }
176: 
177:                 let line_height = (self.screen_height as f32 / perp_wall_dist).abs() as isize;
178:                 let pitch_offset = (pitch * self.screen_height as f32) as isize;
179: 
180:                 let mut draw_start =
181:                     -line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
182:                 let draw_start_clamped = if draw_start < 0 {
183:                     0
184:                 } else {
185:                     draw_start as usize
186:                 };
187:                 let mut draw_end = line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
188:                 if draw_end >= self.screen_height as isize {
189:                     draw_end = self.screen_height as isize - 1;
190:                 }
191:                 let draw_end_clamped = draw_end as usize;
192: 
193:                 let mut r = 200;
194:                 let mut g = 200;
195:                 let mut b = 200;
196: 
197:                 if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
198:                     r = 255;
199:                     g = 255;
200:                     b = 200;
201:                 } else if hit == 5 {
202:                     r = 150;
203:                     g = 30;
204:                     b = 30;
205:                 } else if hit == 1 {
206:                     r = 180;
207:                     g = 160;
208:                     b = 100;
209:                 }
210: 
211:                 let light = self.get_light(map_x, hit_y, map_z);
212:                 let light_factor = if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
213:                     1.0
214:                 } else {
215:                     light as f32 / 15.0
216:                 };
217:                 let fog_factor = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.05).exp();
218: 
219:                 r = (r as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
220:                 g = (g as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
221:                 b = (b as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
222: 
223:                 if side == 1 && hit != VOXEL_LIGHT {
224:                     r = (r as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
225:                     g = (g as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
226:                     b = (b as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
227:                 }
228: 
229:                 for y in draw_start_clamped..=draw_end_clamped {
230:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
231:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = r;
232:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = g;
233:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = b;
234:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
235:                 }
236: 
237:                 let floor_fog = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.01).exp(); // less fog on floor to see shape
238:                 for y in (draw_end_clamped + 1)..self.screen_height {
239:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
240:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
241:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
242:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
243:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
244:                 }
245: 
246:                 for y in 0..draw_start_clamped {
247:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
248:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (60.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
249:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (55.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
250:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (50.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
251:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
252:                 }
253:             }
254:         }
255:     }
256: }
````

````rust
 49: impl PillarLattice {
 50:     /// Variable wallpapered piers, always snapped to the shared 0.4u plan
 51:     /// lattice. Entry regularity comes from placement, not a fixed size.
 52:     pub fn pillar_size(&self, cell_x: i64, cell_z: i64) -> f32 {
 53:         let hash = mix64(
 54:             self.variation_seed
 55:                 ^ (cell_x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
 56:                 ^ (cell_z as u64).rotate_left(29),
 57:         );
 58:         let steps = (((self.max_side - self.min_side) / 0.4).round() as u64).max(1);
 59:         let step = (hash % (steps + 1)) as f32;
 60:         (self.min_side + 0.4 * step).clamp(self.min_side, self.max_side)
 61:     }
 62: }

168:     }

173:     }
174: 
175:     pub fn pit_hazards_for_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> Vec<PitHazard> {
176:         let Some(lattice) = self.pit_lattice else {
177:             return Vec::new();
178:         };
179:         let corners = [
180:             self.local_coords(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z),
181:             self.local_coords(bounds.min_x, bounds.max_z),
182:             self.local_coords(bounds.max_x, bounds.min_z),
183:             self.local_coords(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z),
184:         ];
185:         let min_lx = corners
186:             .iter()
187:             .map(|point| point.0)
188:             .fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
189:         let max_lx = corners
190:             .iter()
191:             .map(|point| point.0)
192:             .fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
193:         let min_lz = corners
194:             .iter()
195:             .map(|point| point.1)
196:             .fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
197:         let max_lz = corners
198:             .iter()
199:             .map(|point| point.1)
200:             .fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
201:         let ix0 = ((min_lx - lattice.phase_x) / lattice.spacing_x).floor() as i64 - 1;
202:         let ix1 = ((max_lx - lattice.phase_x) / lattice.spacing_x).ceil() as i64 + 1;
203:         let iz0 = ((min_lz - lattice.phase_z) / lattice.spacing_z).floor() as i64 - 1;
204:         let iz1 = ((max_lz - lattice.phase_z) / lattice.spacing_z).ceil() as i64 + 1;
205: 
206:         let mut hazards = Vec::new();
207:         for iz in iz0..=iz1 {
208:             for ix in ix0..=ix1 {
209:                 let lx = lattice.phase_x + ix as f32 * lattice.spacing_x;
210:                 let lz = lattice.phase_z + iz as f32 * lattice.spacing_z;
211:                 let center = self.world_coords(lx, lz);
212:                 if !self.contains(center.x, center.z)
213:                     || self.boundary_distance(center.x, center.z) < lattice.side
214:                     || !bounds.expanded(lattice.side).contains(center.x, center.z)
215:                 {
216:                     continue;
217:                 }
218:                 // The immutable center lane remains solid and navigable.
219:                 if lz.abs() < self.skeleton_half_width + lattice.side {
220:                     continue;
221:                 }
222:                 // The center between four pits is deterministically clear even
223:                 // when pit side and spacing vary between instances.
224:                 let recovery =
225:                     self.world_coords(lx + lattice.spacing_x * 0.5, lz + lattice.spacing_z * 0.5);
226:                 let id = mix64(self.id ^ (ix as u64).rotate_left(17) ^ (iz as u64).rotate_left(43));
227:                 hazards.push(PitHazard {
228:                     id,
229:                     instance_id: self.id,
230:                     center,
231:                     half_side: lattice.side * 0.5,
232:                     depth: lattice.depth,
233:                     recovery,
234:                 });
235:             }
236:         }
237:         hazards.sort_by_key(|hazard| hazard.id);
238:         hazards.dedup_by_key(|hazard| hazard.id);
239:         hazards
240:     }
241: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Immutable anomaly plans and deterministic encounter-state snapshots.
 2: //!
 3: //! The public surface remains a single `anomaly` namespace for callers, while
 4: //! its internals follow the domain's actual vocabulary:
 5: //!
 6: //! - [`geometry`] owns rectilinear bounds and coordinate transforms;
 7: //! - [`phenomena`] owns immutable anomaly instances and family parameters;
 8: //! - [`traversal`] owns semantic gates and hazards;
 9: //! - [`reality`] owns snapshots, transitions, and RTY v2 transport.
10: //!
11: //! The planner owns instance placement. Stateful geometry remains pure: a
12: //! chunk is sampled from an [`AnomalyInstance`] plus the matching stamp in a
13: //! [`RealitySnapshot`].
14: 
15: mod geometry;
16: mod phenomena;
17: mod reality;
18: mod traversal;
19: 
20: pub use geometry::*;
21: pub use phenomena::*;
22: pub use reality::*;
23: pub use traversal::*;
24: 
25: /// SplitMix64 finalizer shared by stable anomaly identities and fingerprints.
26: /// It stays private to the anomaly aggregate; callers consume only the stable
27: /// domain values produced from it.
28: fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
29:     value ^= value >> 30;
30:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
31:     value ^= value >> 27;
32:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
33:     value ^ (value >> 31)
34: }
35: 
36: #[cfg(test)]
37: mod tests {
38:     use super::*;
39: 
40:     #[test]
41:     fn pillar_sizes_vary_but_stay_snapped() {
42:         let lattice = PillarLattice {
43:             bay_x: 4.4,
44:             bay_z: 4.0,
45:             phase_x: 0.0,
46:             phase_z: 0.0,
47:             min_side: 1.2,
48:             max_side: 1.6,
49:             variation_seed: 42,
50:         };
51:         let mut seen = Vec::new();
52:         for z in 0..12 {
53:             for x in 0..12 {
54:                 let side = lattice.pillar_size(x, z);
55:                 assert!((1.2..=1.6).contains(&side));
56:                 assert!(((side / 0.4).round() - side / 0.4).abs() < 1e-4);
57:                 if !seen.contains(&side.to_bits()) {
58:                     seen.push(side.to_bits());
59:                 }
60:             }
61:         }
62:         assert!(seen.len() >= 2);
63:     }
````

## File: src/domain/use_cases/generate_maze.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
  2: use rand::Rng;
  3: #[allow(unused_imports)]
  4: use rand::RngExt;
  5: 
  6: /// Design Pattern: Strategy
  7: /// We use the Strategy pattern here to encapsulate the maze generation algorithm.
  8: /// This is the superior choice because different Backrooms levels (or even different regions of Level 0)
  9: /// might require different procedural generation rules. By decoupling the generation logic from the Grid entity,
 10: /// we ensure the Open/Closed Principle (workable iʃɛ́) — we can add new generators without modifying the Grid.
 11: pub trait MazeGenerator {
 12:     /// Generates the maze on the provided grid using the given random number generator.
 13:     fn generate<R: Rng + ?Sized>(&self, grid: &mut Grid, rng: &mut R);
 14: }
 15: 
 16: /// A concrete strategy for generating a maze using the Growing Tree algorithm.
 17: /// This algorithm produces non-linear, organic layouts suitable for the Backrooms,
 18: /// unlike standard depth-first search which produces long winding paths.
 19: pub struct GrowingTreeGenerator {
 20:     pub junction_density: f32,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: impl MazeGenerator for GrowingTreeGenerator {
 24:     fn generate<R: Rng + ?Sized>(&self, grid: &mut Grid, rng: &mut R) {
 25:         let width = grid.width();
 26:         let depth = grid.depth();
 27:         if width == 0 || depth == 0 {
 28:             return;
 29:         }
 30: 
 31:         // Starting point
 32:         let start_x = rng.random_range(0..width);
 33:         let start_y = rng.random_range(0..depth);
 34: 
 35:         if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(start_x, start_y) {
 36:             cell.visited = true;
 37:         }
 38: 
 39:         let mut frontier = vec![(start_x, start_y)];
 40: 
 41:         while !frontier.is_empty() {
 42:             // Pick a random cell from the frontier (this randomness defines the Growing Tree behavior)
 43:             let idx = rng.random_range(0..frontier.len());
 44:             let (cx, cy) = frontier[idx];
 45: 
 46:             // Define neighbors: (x, y, wall_here_idx, wall_there_idx)
 47:             // 0: North, 1: East, 2: South, 3: West
 48:             let neighbors: [(isize, isize, usize, usize); 4] = [
 49:                 (cx as isize, (cy as isize) - 1, 0, 2), // North
 50:                 ((cx as isize) + 1, cy as isize, 1, 3), // East
 51:                 (cx as isize, (cy as isize) + 1, 2, 0), // South
 52:                 ((cx as isize) - 1, cy as isize, 3, 1), // West
 53:             ];
 54: 
 55:             let mut unvisited = Vec::new();
 56:             for &(nx, ny, wall_here, wall_there) in &neighbors {
 57:                 if nx >= 0 && nx < width as isize && ny >= 0 && ny < depth as isize {
 58:                     let (nx_u, ny_u) = (nx as usize, ny as usize);
 59:                     if let Some(cell) = grid.get(nx_u, ny_u) {
 60:                         if !cell.visited {
 61:                             unvisited.push((nx_u, ny_u, wall_here, wall_there));
 62:                         }
 63:                     }
 64:                 }
 65:             }
 66: 
 67:             if unvisited.is_empty() {
 68:                 frontier.swap_remove(idx);
 69:             } else {
 70:                 let unvisited_idx = rng.random_range(0..unvisited.len());
 71:                 let (nx, ny, wall_here, wall_there) = unvisited[unvisited_idx];
 72: 
 73:                 // Knock down walls
 74:                 if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(cx, cy) {
 75:                     cell.walls[wall_here] = false;
 76:                 }
 77:                 if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(nx, ny) {
 78:                     cell.walls[wall_there] = false;
 79:                     cell.visited = true;
 80:                 }
 81: 
 82:                 frontier.push((nx, ny));
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85: 
 86:         // Add loops to break the "perfect maze" property and make it feel like the Backrooms
 87:         let base_openings = (width * depth) as f32 / 4.0;
 88:         let extra_openings = (base_openings * self.junction_density) as usize;
 89:         let mut actual_openings = 0;
 90:         let mut attempts = 0;
 91: 
 92:         while actual_openings < extra_openings && attempts < extra_openings * 3 {
 93:             attempts += 1;
 94:             let x = rng.random_range(0..width);
 95:             let y = rng.random_range(0..depth);
 96: 
 97:             // Blackout zones are knot-like dead-ends; suppress extra loops in them
 98:             if let Some(cell) = grid.get(x, y) {
 99:                 if cell.zone == crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone::Blackout {
100:                     continue;
101:                 }
102:             }
103: 
104:             let dir = rng.random_range(0..4);
105: 
106:             if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(x, y) {
107:                 cell.walls[dir] = false;
108:             }
109: 
110:             let (nx, ny) = match dir {
111:                 0 => (x as isize, y as isize - 1),
112:                 1 => (x as isize + 1, y as isize),
113:                 2 => (x as isize, y as isize + 1),
114:                 3 => (x as isize - 1, y as isize),
115:                 _ => unreachable!(),
116:             };
117: 
118:             if nx >= 0 && nx < width as isize && ny >= 0 && ny < depth as isize {
119:                 let (nx, ny) = (nx as usize, ny as usize);
120:                 let opposite_dir = (dir + 2) % 4;
121:                 if let Some(n_cell) = grid.get_mut(nx, ny) {
122:                     n_cell.walls[opposite_dir] = false;
123:                 }
124:             }
125: 
126:             actual_openings += 1;
127:         }
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: #[cfg(test)]
132: mod tests {
133:     use super::*;
134:     use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
135:     use rand::SeedableRng;
````

````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_LIGHT, VoxelGrid};
  2: use rand::RngExt;
  3: use rand::SeedableRng;
  4: use rand::rngs::StdRng;
  5: 
  6: /// A simple 3D DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) Raycaster
  7: fn cast_ray(
  8:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
  9:     x: f32,
 10:     y: f32,
 11:     z: f32,
 12:     dx: f32,
 13:     dy: f32,
 14:     dz: f32,
 15:     max_steps: usize,
 16: ) -> Option<(usize, usize, usize, u8)> {
 17:     let step_x = if dx > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 18:     let step_y = if dy > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 19:     let step_z = if dz > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 20: 
 21:     let mut t_max_x = if dx != 0.0 {
 22:         (x.floor() + if dx > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - x) / dx
 23:     } else {
 24:         f32::INFINITY
 25:     };
 26:     let mut t_max_y = if dy != 0.0 {
 27:         (y.floor() + if dy > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - y) / dy
 28:     } else {
 29:         f32::INFINITY
 30:     };
 31:     let mut t_max_z = if dz != 0.0 {
 32:         (z.floor() + if dz > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - z) / dz
 33:     } else {
 34:         f32::INFINITY
 35:     };
 36: 
 37:     let t_delta_x = if dx != 0.0 {
 38:         (1.0 / dx).abs()
 39:     } else {
 40:         f32::INFINITY
 41:     };
 42:     let t_delta_y = if dy != 0.0 {
 43:         (1.0 / dy).abs()
 44:     } else {
 45:         f32::INFINITY
 46:     };
 47:     let t_delta_z = if dz != 0.0 {
 48:         (1.0 / dz).abs()
 49:     } else {
 50:         f32::INFINITY
 51:     };
 52: 
 53:     let mut ix = x as isize;
 54:     let mut iy = y as isize;
 55:     let mut iz = z as isize;
 56: 
 57:     for _ in 0..max_steps {
 58:         if t_max_x < t_max_y {
 59:             if t_max_x < t_max_z {
 60:                 ix += step_x;
 61:                 t_max_x += t_delta_x;
 62:             } else {
 63:                 iz += step_z;
 64:                 t_max_z += t_delta_z;
 65:             }
 66:         } else {
 67:             if t_max_y < t_max_z {
 68:                 iy += step_y;
 69:                 t_max_y += t_delta_y;
 70:             } else {
 71:                 iz += step_z;
 72:                 t_max_z += t_delta_z;
 73:             }
 74:         }
 75: 
 76:         if ix < 0
 77:             || iy < 0
 78:             || iz < 0
 79:             || ix >= grid.width() as isize
 80:             || iy >= grid.height() as isize
 81:             || iz >= grid.depth() as isize
 82:         {
 83:             break;
 84:         }
 85: 
 86:         let vx = ix as usize;
 87:         let vy = iy as usize;
 88:         let vz = iz as usize;
 89: 
 90:         let v = grid.get(vx, vy, vz);
 91:         if v != VOXEL_AIR {
 92:             return Some((vx, vy, vz, v));
 93:         }
 94:     }
 95:     None
 96: }
 97: 
 98: /// Bakes lighting into the VoxelGrid using Monte Carlo Path Tracing
 99: pub fn bake_path_traced_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid) {
100:     let w = grid.width();
101:     let h = grid.height();
102:     let d = grid.depth();
103: 
104:     let rays_per_voxel = 64;
105:     let max_bounces = 1; // 0 for direct only, 1 for one bounce
106:     let max_steps = 30; // Max ray distance
107: 
108:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(42);
109: 
110:     // We only need to bake lighting into AIR blocks that are adjacent to solid blocks,
111:     // but for simplicity we can bake all AIR blocks, or directly bake solid blocks.
112:     // Actually, baking solid blocks is better. We evaluate light slightly outside the solid block face.
113:     // Since our map_voxel_grid just uses `grid.get_light(x, y, z)` for the solid block itself,
114:     // we can just store the light level in the solid block!
115: 
116:     for z in 0..d {
117:         for y in 0..h {
118:             for x in 0..w {
119:                 let v = grid.get(x, y, z);
120:                 if v == VOXEL_AIR || v == VOXEL_LIGHT {
121:                     continue;
122:                 }
123: 
124:                 // It's a solid block. Let's do path tracing from its center slightly offset by normals.
125:                 // To keep it simple, we shoot rays from the center of the block. If it immediately hits itself,
126:                 // we ignore it. Actually, start rays from the adjacent AIR voxels.
127: 
128:                 let mut total_light = 0.0;
129: 
130:                 // Find an adjacent air voxel to act as the emission point
131:                 let mut px = x as f32 + 0.5;
132:                 let mut py = y as f32 + 0.5;
133:                 let mut pz = z as f32 + 0.5;
134: 
135:                 // Shift point slightly towards the air
136:                 if x > 0 && grid.get(x - 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
137:                     px -= 0.55;
138:                 } else if x < w - 1 && grid.get(x + 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
139:                     px += 0.55;
140:                 } else if y > 0 && grid.get(x, y - 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
141:                     py -= 0.55;
142:                 } else if y < h - 1 && grid.get(x, y + 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
143:                     py += 0.55;
144:                 } else if z > 0 && grid.get(x, y, z - 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
145:                     pz -= 0.55;
146:                 } else if z < d - 1 && grid.get(x, y, z + 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
147:                     pz += 0.55;
148:                 } else {
149:                     continue; // Completely surrounded by solids, no light needed
150:                 }
151: 
152:                 for _ in 0..rays_per_voxel {
153:                     // Random spherical direction
154:                     let theta = rng.random::<f32>() * 2.0 * std::f32::consts::PI;
155:                     let phi = (rng.random::<f32>() * 2.0 - 1.0).acos();
156:                     let dx = phi.sin() * theta.cos();
157:                     let dy = phi.cos();
158:                     let dz = phi.sin() * theta.sin();
159: 
160:                     if let Some((_hx, _hy, _hz, hit_type)) =
161:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py, pz, dx, dy, dz, max_steps)
162:                     {
163:                         if hit_type == VOXEL_LIGHT {
164:                             total_light += 1.0;
165:                         } else if max_bounces > 0 {
166:                             // Secondary bounce (simplified)
167:                             // We don't do a full recursive call to avoid stack/performance issues,
168:                             // just a small probability addition to simulate ambient bounce.
169:                             // If we hit a wall, it bounces a bit of light.
170:                             total_light += 0.05;
171:                         }
172:                     }
173:                 }
174: 
175:                 // Normalize and map to 0-15 scale for compatibility with voxel_mapper
176:                 let mut light_level = ((total_light / rays_per_voxel as f32) * 15.0 * 2.0) as u8;
177:                 if light_level > 15 {
178:                     light_level = 15;
179:                 }
180: 
181:                 grid.set_light(x, y, z, light_level);
182:             }
183:         }
184:     }
185: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/anomalies/macro_planner.rs
````rust
  1: //! World-lattice planner for region-spanning Level 0 anomalies.
  2: //!
  3: //! Macro candidates live on a 160-unit lattice. Regions merely query that
  4: //! lattice, so overlapping region and chunk requests recover identical
  5: //! instance IDs, footprints, internal phases, and traversal gates.
  6: 
  7: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  8:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, ArchBehavior, ArchLayout, ArchProfile, Axis2, AxisDirection,
  9:     OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, PillarLattice, PitLattice, QuarterTurn, TraversalGate,
 10:     TraversalGateKind, WorldBounds,
 11: };
 12: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 15: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields;
 16: 
 17: use super::determinism::{hash, mix64, snap, stable_id, unit};
 18: 
 19: /// The anomaly lattice *is* the world-graph lattice, so anomaly anchors and
 20: /// macro-cell fields stay phase-aligned by construction.
 21: const MACRO_CELL: f32 = crate::domain::entities::world_topology::MACRO_CELL_SIZE;
 22: const MAX_QUERY_MARGIN: f32 = 400.0;
 23: 
 24: fn weighted_family(config: &GeneratorConfig, sample: f32) -> Option<AnomalyKind> {
 25:     let tuning = config.anomalies;
 26:     let weights = [
 27:         (AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse, tuning.pillar_expanses.max(0.0)),
 28:         (AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse, tuning.blackouts.max(0.0)),
 29:         (AnomalyKind::PitLattice, tuning.pit_lattices.max(0.0)),
 30:         (AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom, tuning.archways.max(0.0)),
 31:     ];
 32:     let total: f32 = weights.iter().map(|(_, weight)| weight).sum();
 33:     if total <= 0.0 {
 34:         return None;
 35:     }
 36: 
 37:     let mut cursor = sample * total;
 38:     for (kind, weight) in weights {
 39:         if cursor < weight {
 40:             return Some(kind);
 41:         }
 42:         cursor -= weight;
 43:     }
 44:     Some(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse)
 45: }
 46: 
 47: fn remap_gates(instance: &AnomalyInstance) -> Vec<TraversalGate> {
 48:     let (step, first, last) = match instance.kind {
 49:         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => {
 50:             let bay = instance.pillar_lattice.map_or(4.0, |lattice| lattice.bay_x);
 51:             (
 52:                 bay * 4.0,
 53:                 -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
 54:                 instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
 55:             )
 56:         }
 57:         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
 58:             22.0,
 59:             -instance.footprint.half_x + instance.entry_band,
 60:             instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band,
 61:         ),
 62:         _ => return Vec::new(),
 63:     };
 64: 
 65:     let mut gates = Vec::new();
 66:     let mut local_x = snap((first / step).ceil() * step);
 67:     let world_bounds = instance.footprint.bounds();
 68:     let axis = instance.basis.local_axis_in_world(Axis2::X);
 69:     while local_x <= last {
 70:         let at = instance.world_coords(local_x, 0.0);
 71:         let (plane, span_min, span_max) = match axis {
 72:             Axis2::X => (at.x, world_bounds.min_z, world_bounds.max_z),
 73:             Axis2::Z => (at.z, world_bounds.min_x, world_bounds.max_x),
 74:         };
 75:         let gate_index = (local_x / step).round() as i64;
 76:         gates.push(TraversalGate {
 77:             id: mix64(instance.id ^ (gate_index as u64).rotate_left(23) ^ 0x6A7E),
 78:             instance_id: instance.id,
 79:             anomaly_kind: instance.kind,
 80:             kind: TraversalGateKind::Remap,
 81:             axis,
 82:             plane,
 83:             span_min,
 84:             span_max,
 85:             forward: AxisDirection::Positive,
 86:             affected_bounds: world_bounds,
 87:         });
 88:         local_x += step;
 89:     }
 90:     gates
 91: }
 92: 
 93: fn macro_instance(
 94:     seed: u32,
 95:     anchor_x: i64,
 96:     anchor_z: i64,
 97:     kind: AnomalyKind,
 98:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 99: ) -> AnomalyInstance {
100:     let id = stable_id(seed, kind, anchor_x, anchor_z);
101:     let h = |salt| hash(seed, salt, anchor_x, anchor_z);
102:     let size_scale = config.anomalies.size.clamp(0.5, 2.0);
103:     let center_x = snap((anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC1)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
104:     let center_z = snap((anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL + (unit(h(0xC2)) - 0.5) * 48.0);
105:     let basis = OrthoBasis {
106:         turn: if h(0xC3) & 1 == 0 {
107:             QuarterTurn::Zero
108:         } else {
109:             QuarterTurn::Clockwise
110:         },
111:     };
112:     let (half_x, half_z, entry_band, skeleton_half_width) = match kind {
113:         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => (
114:             snap((75.0 + 85.0 * unit(h(0xD1))) * size_scale),
115:             snap((55.0 + 65.0 * unit(h(0xD2))) * size_scale),
116:             16.0,
117:             2.0,
118:         ),
119:         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => (
120:             snap((65.0 + 70.0 * unit(h(0xD3))) * size_scale),
121:             snap((50.0 + 55.0 * unit(h(0xD4))) * size_scale),
122:             12.0,
123:             2.0,
124:         ),
125:         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => (
126:             snap((32.0 + 30.0 * unit(h(0xD5))) * size_scale),
127:             snap((28.0 + 25.0 * unit(h(0xD6))) * size_scale),
128:             6.0,
129:             1.8,
130:         ),
131:         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => (
132:             snap(4.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD7))),
133:             snap(5.0 + 3.0 * unit(h(0xD8))),
134:             0.0,
135:             0.0,
136:         ),
137:         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms are planned from assemblies"),
138:     };
139:     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
140:         center: Position::new(center_x, center_z),
141:         half_x,
142:         half_z,
143:         basis,
144:     };
145:     let pillar_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse).then(|| PillarLattice {
146:         bay_x: snap(3.6 + 1.2 * unit(h(0xE1))),
147:         bay_z: snap(3.6 + 1.2 * unit(h(0xE2))),
148:         phase_x: snap((unit(h(0xE3)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
149:         phase_z: snap((unit(h(0xE4)) - 0.5) * 3.2),
150:         min_side: 1.2,
151:         max_side: 1.6,
152:         variation_seed: id ^ 0xA111_AA55_u64,
153:     });
154:     let pit_lattice = (kind == AnomalyKind::PitLattice).then(|| PitLattice {
155:         spacing_x: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF1))),
156:         spacing_z: snap(2.0 + 0.4 * unit(h(0xF2))),
157:         phase_x: snap(unit(h(0xF3)) * 1.2),
158:         phase_z: snap(unit(h(0xF4)) * 1.2),
159:         side: snap(0.8 + 0.2 * unit(h(0xF5))),
160:         depth: 2.4,
161:     });
162:     let arch = (kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom).then(|| {
163:         // Most arch rooms are walk-through connectors; the sheltered dead
164:         // end is the rarer find. Both stay immutable anchors.
165:         let layout = if unit(h(0xA0)) < 0.7 {
166:             ArchLayout::Transition
167:         } else {
168:             ArchLayout::DeadEnd
169:         };
170:         // Transition rooms are graph connectors: most stay plain anchors,
171:         // but some are seams into another culture or scale. A dead end
172:         // connects nothing, so it never claims a seam behavior.
173:         let behavior = if layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
174:             ArchBehavior::Anchor
175:         } else {
176:             match unit(h(0xA4)) {
177:                 v if v < 0.40 => ArchBehavior::Anchor,
178:                 v if v < 0.75 => ArchBehavior::CultureSeam,
179:                 _ => ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach,
180:             }
181:         };
182:         // Every instance is its own arcade: rhythm, clear width, springing
183:         // height, and blind cadence all vary, so no two arch rooms present
184:         // the same silhouette — yet every non-blind opening stays walkable
185:         // (the opening is capped so piers survive, and the head springs at
186:         // standing height before rising toward the center).
187:         let bay = snap(2.4 + 2.0 * unit(h(0xA1)));
188:         ArchProfile {
189:             layout,
190:             behavior,
191:             bay,
192:             opening: snap((1.4 + 1.4 * unit(h(0xA2))).min(bay - 0.8)),
193:             blind_every: 3 + (h(0xA3) % 4) as u8,
194:             spring_units: ((2.0 + 0.8 * unit(h(0xA5))) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
195:         }
196:     });
197:     let mut instance = AnomalyInstance {
198:         id,
199:         kind,
200:         footprint,
201:         basis,
202:         macro_anchor: (anchor_x, anchor_z),
203:         pillar_lattice,
204:         pit_lattice,
205:         arch,
206:         gates: Vec::new(),
207:         skeleton_half_width,
208:         entry_band,
209:     };
210:     instance.gates = remap_gates(&instance);
211:     instance
212: }
213: 
214: fn forced_instance(
215:     seed: u32,
216:     query: WorldBounds,
217:     protected_point: Position,
218:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
219: ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
220:     let kind = config.anomalies.forced_kind?;
221:     if kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom {
222:         return None;
223:     }
224: 
225:     if kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom {
226:         // A forced anchor is moved next to the protected point so it is both
227:         // resident and visible; organic anchors keep their macro-cell center.
228:         let center = Position::new(snap(protected_point.x + 10.0), snap(protected_point.z));
229:         let anchor_x = (center.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
230:         let anchor_z = (center.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
231:         let mut instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
232:         instance.footprint.center = center;
233:         return instance
234:             .footprint
235:             .bounds()
236:             .intersects(query)
237:             .then_some(instance);
238:     }
239: 
240:     let anchor_x = (protected_point.x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
241:     let anchor_z = (protected_point.z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
242:     let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
243:     instance
244:         .footprint
245:         .bounds()
246:         .intersects(query)
247:         .then_some(instance)
248: }
249: 
250: pub(crate) fn plan_macro_anomalies(
251:     seed: u32,
252:     query: WorldBounds,
253:     protected_point: Position,
254:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
255:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
256: ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
257:     let mut instances: Vec<_> = forced_instance(seed, query, protected_point, config)
258:         .into_iter()
259:         .collect();
260:     if config.anomalies.frequency <= 0.0 {
261:         return instances;
262:     }
263: 
264:     let expanded = query.expanded(MAX_QUERY_MARGIN);
265:     let anchor_x_min = (expanded.min_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
266:     let anchor_x_max = (expanded.max_x / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
267:     let anchor_z_min = (expanded.min_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
268:     let anchor_z_max = (expanded.max_z / MACRO_CELL).floor() as i64;
269:     let base_chance = (0.20 * config.anomalies.frequency.clamp(0.0, 4.0)).min(0.75);
270: 
271:     for anchor_z in anchor_z_min..=anchor_z_max {
272:         for anchor_x in anchor_x_min..=anchor_x_max {
273:             // The macro anomaly-pressure field clusters candidates: quiet
274:             // territory thins toward 0.4× the base chance and pressured
275:             // territory rises toward 1.6×, so anomalies arrive in loose
276:             // constellations instead of a uniform sprinkle. The field is a
277:             // pure world function, so every query that can see this anchor
278:             // computes the identical decision.
279:             let pressure = sample_fields(
280:                 noise,
281:                 seed,
282:                 (anchor_x as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
283:                 (anchor_z as f32 + 0.5) * MACRO_CELL,
284:             )
285:             .anomaly_pressure;
286:             let chance = base_chance * (0.40 + 1.20 * pressure);
287:             let candidate = hash(seed, 0xCAAD_1DA7, anchor_x, anchor_z);
288:             if unit(candidate) >= chance {
289:                 continue;
290:             }
291:             let Some(kind) = weighted_family(config, unit(candidate.rotate_left(21))) else {
292:                 continue;
293:             };
294:             let instance = macro_instance(seed, anchor_x, anchor_z, kind, config);
295:             if !instance.footprint.bounds().intersects(query) {
296:                 continue;
297:             }
298:             // Organic candidates honor the opening-region keep-out. Forced
299:             // candidates intentionally bypass it for developer inspection.
300:             if instance
301:                 .footprint
302:                 .bounds()
303:                 .expanded(48.0)
304:                 .contains(protected_point.x, protected_point.z)
305:             {
306:                 continue;
307:             }
308:             instances.push(instance);
309:         }
310:     }
311:     instances
312: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Level 1 chunk generation: sector-driven columns, supply exports, and the
  2: //! arrival plaza with its door back to Level 0.
  3: 
  4: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{LevelExit, RealitySnapshot};

  8:     VOXEL_PIPE, VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR, VoxelGrid,
  9: };
 10: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 11: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
 12: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 13: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::{LEVEL_BACKROOMS, LevelGenerator};

 17: use super::{GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS, HabitableLevel, Sector};
 18: 
 19: // -- structural lattices (world-phased so they cross sector borders) --------
 20: 
 21: /// Aquila / lighting bay: the deep-span parking grid.
 22: const BAY: f32 = 9.6;
 23: /// Massive square parking pillar side.
 24: const PILLAR_SIDE: f32 = 1.6;
 25: /// Gild / Gothic room lattice.
 26: const ROOM: f32 = 7.2;
 27: /// Structural wall thickness.
 28: const WALL_T: f32 = 0.25;
 29: /// Gild doorway width.
 30: const DOOR_W: f32 = 1.4;
 31: /// Gild doorway lintel height.
 32: const DOOR_H: f32 = 2.2;
 33: /// Doorway centers keep this margin from each wall end. The nearest gap
 34: /// edge (margin - DOOR_W/2 = 1.9) must clear the deepest corner-crate
 35: /// reach (1.1 inset + 0.75 max extent = 1.85).
 36: const GAP_BAND_MARGIN: f32 = 2.6;
 37: /// Construction obstacle lattice.
 38: const SCAFFOLD: f32 = 4.8;
 39: /// Gothic circular pillar radius.
 40: const GOTHIC_R: f32 = 0.75;
 41: 
 42: /// Ceiling pipe runs appear on this lattice of world lines.
 43: const PIPE_SPACING: f32 = 14.4;
 44: const PIPE_HALF_W: f32 = 0.18;
 45: const PIPE_DROP: f32 = 0.3;
 46: 
 47: // -- the arrival plaza -------------------------------------------------------
 48: 
 49: /// Radius kept clear around the world origin, where the Level 0 door lands.
 50: const PLAZA_R: f32 = 5.6;
 51: /// The door back to Level 0 stands just off the plaza center, placed to sit
 52: /// wholly inside one chunk at every supported chunk size.
 53: const RETURN_DOOR: (f32, f32) = (2.0, -2.0);
 54: /// Where a wanderer stepping through the Level 0 door arrives (outside the
 55: /// return door's own trigger, facing open floor).
 56: pub(crate) const ARRIVAL_POINT: (f32, f32) = (3.0, 3.0);
 57: /// Where the return door drops the wanderer in Level 0 (the spawn hub).
 58: const LEVEL0_ARRIVAL: (f32, f32) = (5.0, 5.0);
 59: /// Trigger half-extent of a level door.
 60: pub(crate) const DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF: f32 = 0.7;
 61: 
 62: // -- supplies ----------------------------------------------------------------
 63: 
 64: /// Supply placement cell (independent of sector cells so caches don't align).
 65: const SUPPLY_CELL: f32 = 24.0;
 66: 
 67: fn pillar_axis_dist(w: f32, spacing: f32) -> f32 {
 68:     let t = w - (w / spacing).floor() * spacing;
 69:     t.min(spacing - t)
 70: }
 71: 
 72: /// Distance from a world point to the nearest lattice *node* of `spacing`.
 73: fn node_dist(wx: f32, wz: f32, spacing: f32) -> f32 {
 74:     let dx = pillar_axis_dist(wx, spacing);
 75:     let dz = pillar_axis_dist(wz, spacing);
 76:     (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt()
 77: }
 78: 
 79: /// Stable id for a supply item at a lattice anchor.
 80: fn supply_id(seed: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64, salt: u64) -> u64 {
 81:     hash(seed, 0x5A17_AB1E_0000_0000 ^ salt, cx, cz) | 1
 82: }
 83: 
 84: impl HabitableLevel {
 85:     /// The architectural plan of one world column. Pure in (seed, position).
 86:     pub(crate) fn plan_column(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> ColumnPlan {
 87:         let sector = Sector::at(seed, wx, wz);
 88:         let mut column = ColumnPlan::open(3.6);
 89:         column.wall_material = VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL;
 90:         column.floor_material = VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR;
 91: 
 92:         match sector {
 93:             Sector::Aquila => Self::plan_aquila(seed, wx, wz, &mut column),
 94:             Sector::Gild => Self::plan_gild(seed, wx, wz, &mut column),
 95:             Sector::Gothic => Self::plan_gothic(seed, wx, wz, &mut column),
 96:             Sector::Construction => Self::plan_construction(seed, wx, wz, &mut column),
 97:         }
 98: 
 99:         Self::apply_pipes(seed, wx, wz, &mut column);
100:         Self::apply_plaza(wx, wz, &mut column);
101:         column
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// Bland parking lot: concrete slab, huge pillars, long sight lines.
105:     fn plan_aquila(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
106:         column.ceiling_units = 3.4;
107:         column.floor_material = VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR;
108:         let half = PILLAR_SIDE * 0.5;
109:         if pillar_axis_dist(wx, BAY) < half && pillar_axis_dist(wz, BAY) < half {
110:             column.solid = true;
111:         }
112:         // Sparse fixtures at bay centers; roughly one in three bays is dark.
113:         let bx = ((wx - BAY * 0.5) / BAY).round() as i64;
114:         let bz = ((wz - BAY * 0.5) / BAY).round() as i64;
115:         let lit = unit(hash(seed, 0xA10A_11A5_0000_0002, bx, bz)) > 0.34;
116:         let lx = pillar_axis_dist(wx - BAY * 0.5, BAY);
117:         let lz = pillar_axis_dist(wz - BAY * 0.5, BAY);
118:         if lit && lx < 0.65 && lz < 0.65 {
119:             column.light = true;
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// Dense storage fabric: doorway'd concrete rooms and crate stacks.
124:     fn plan_gild(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
125:         column.ceiling_units = 3.2;
126: 
127:         let cell_x = (wx / ROOM).floor() as i64;
128:         let cell_z = (wz / ROOM).floor() as i64;
129:         let in_x_wall = pillar_axis_dist(wx, ROOM) < WALL_T;
130:         let in_z_wall = pillar_axis_dist(wz, ROOM) < WALL_T;
131: 
132:         if in_x_wall || in_z_wall {
133:             // A doorway pierces every shared wall segment, so the storage
134:             // maze is dense but never sealed. The gap position is hashed per
135:             // wall edge; both cells sharing the edge derive the same gap.
136:             // Gap centers stay in the wall's central band so a doorway (and
137:             // the walk lane through it) can never reach a corner crate zone.
138:             let (edge_x, edge_z, along, salt) = if in_x_wall {
139:                 ((wx / ROOM).round() as i64, cell_z, wz, 0x11)
140:             } else {
141:                 (cell_x, (wz / ROOM).round() as i64, wx, 0x22)
142:             };
143:             let t = unit(hash(seed, 0x91D0_D008_0000_0000 | salt, edge_x, edge_z));
144:             let gap_center =
145:                 (along / ROOM).floor() * ROOM + GAP_BAND_MARGIN + t * (ROOM - 2.0 * GAP_BAND_MARGIN);
146:             let in_gap = (along - gap_center).abs() < DOOR_W * 0.5;
147:             if in_gap {
148:                 column.lintel_from_units = Some(DOOR_H);
149:             } else {
150:                 column.solid = true;
151:             }
152:         } else {
153:             // Crate stacks hug the room corners. Their maximum reach along
154:             // either wall (corner inset + extent) stays short of the nearest
155:             // possible doorway edge (GAP_BAND_MARGIN - DOOR_W/2), so a stack
156:             // can never stand in a doorway or its walk lane.
157:             let fx = wx - cell_x as f32 * ROOM;
158:             let fz = wz - cell_z as f32 * ROOM;
159:             let corner_x = if fx < ROOM * 0.5 { 1.1 } else { ROOM - 1.1 };
160:             let corner_z = if fz < ROOM * 0.5 { 1.1 } else { ROOM - 1.1 };
161:             let quadrant = (u64::from(fx >= ROOM * 0.5) << 1) | u64::from(fz >= ROOM * 0.5);
162:             let stack = hash(seed, 0xC0A7_E500_0000_0000 | quadrant, cell_x, cell_z);
163:             // ~55% of room corners hold crates: 1x1 to 1.5x1.5 world units.
164:             if unit(stack) < 0.55 {
165:                 let extent = 0.5 + unit(stack.rotate_left(17)) * 0.25;
166:                 if (fx - corner_x).abs() < extent && (fz - corner_z).abs() < extent {
167:                     column.floor_units = if unit(stack.rotate_left(33)) < 0.3 {
168:                         1.6
169:                     } else {
170:                         0.8
171:                     };
172:                     column.wall_material = VOXEL_CRATE;
173:                 }
174:             }
175:         }
176: 
177:         // Room-center fixtures, dimmer rhythm than Level 0 offices.
178:         let lx = pillar_axis_dist(wx - ROOM * 0.5, ROOM);
179:         let lz = pillar_axis_dist(wz - ROOM * 0.5, ROOM);
180:         if lx < 0.55 && lz < 0.55 && unit(hash(seed, 0x91D0_11A5, cell_x, cell_z)) > 0.42 {
181:             column.light = true;
182:         }
183:     }
184: 
185:     /// Curved masonry: circular pillars joined by parabolic arches under a
186:     /// vaulted ceiling.
187:     fn plan_gothic(_seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
188:         column.ceiling_units = 4.8;
189: 
190:         if node_dist(wx, wz, ROOM) < GOTHIC_R {
191:             column.solid = true;
192:             return;
193:         }
194: 
195:         // Arches span every lattice line between adjacent pillars: the
196:         // soffit rises from the pillar capitals (2.2u) to 3.6u at midspan.
197:         let arch = |perp: f32, along: f32| -> Option<f32> {
198:             if perp >= WALL_T + 0.1 {
199:                 return None;
200:             }
201:             let t = {
202:                 let s = along - (along / ROOM).floor() * ROOM;
203:                 (s / ROOM).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
204:             };
205:             let rise = (std::f32::consts::PI * t).sin();
206:             Some(2.2 + 1.4 * rise)
207:         };
208:         let x_line = pillar_axis_dist(wx, ROOM);
209:         let z_line = pillar_axis_dist(wz, ROOM);
210:         let soffit = match (arch(x_line, wz), arch(z_line, wx)) {
211:             (Some(a), Some(b)) => Some(a.min(b)),
212:             (a, b) => a.or(b),
213:         };
214:         if let Some(h) = soffit {
215:             column.lintel_from_units = Some(h);
216:         }
217: 
218:         // Sparse warm pools of light at alternating lattice centers.
219:         let cx = (wx / ROOM).floor() as i64;
220:         let cz = (wz / ROOM).floor() as i64;
221:         let lx = pillar_axis_dist(wx - ROOM * 0.5, ROOM);
222:         let lz = pillar_axis_dist(wz - ROOM * 0.5, ROOM);
223:         if lx < 0.5 && lz < 0.5 && (cx + cz).rem_euclid(2) == 0 {
224:             column.light = true;
225:         }
226:     }
227: 
228:     /// Perpetually unfinished: half walls, rebar clusters, dead ends.
229:     fn plan_construction(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
230:         let cell_x = (wx / SCAFFOLD).floor() as i64;
231:         let cell_z = (wz / SCAFFOLD).floor() as i64;
232:         let cell = hash(seed, 0xC095_7A0C_7100_0000, cell_x, cell_z);
233:         column.ceiling_units = 3.2 + unit(cell) * 1.4;
234:         column.floor_material = VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR;
235: 
236:         // Every third lattice lane each way stays clear, so the chaos can
237:         // never seal the walkable plane.
238:         let clear_lane = cell_x.rem_euclid(3) == 0 || cell_z.rem_euclid(3) == 0;
239:         if clear_lane {
240:             return;
241:         }
242: 
243:         let in_x_wall = pillar_axis_dist(wx, SCAFFOLD) < WALL_T;
244:         let in_z_wall = pillar_axis_dist(wz, SCAFFOLD) < WALL_T;
245:         if in_x_wall || in_z_wall {
246:             let salt = if in_x_wall { 0x31 } else { 0x32 };
247:             let roll = unit(hash(seed, 0xBAD5_CAFF_0000_0000 | salt, cell_x, cell_z));
248:             if roll < 0.35 {
249:                 column.solid = true; // a finished wall run (dead ends)
250:             } else if roll < 0.65 {
251:                 column.floor_units = 1.1; // an unfinished half wall
252:             }
253:         } else {
254:             // Rebar clusters: thin full-height pipe bundles.
255:             let sub_x = (wx / 1.2).floor() as i64;
256:             let sub_z = (wz / 1.2).floor() as i64;
257:             if unit(hash(seed, 0x4EBA_4000_0000_0000, sub_x, sub_z)) < 0.045
258:                 && pillar_axis_dist(wx, 1.2) < 0.12
259:                 && pillar_axis_dist(wz, 1.2) < 0.12
260:             {
261:                 column.solid = true;
262:                 column.wall_material = VOXEL_PIPE;
263:             }
264:         }
265: 
266:         // Work lights are rare and mostly failing; long dark stretches are
267:         // the sector's character.
268:         let lx = pillar_axis_dist(wx - SCAFFOLD, SCAFFOLD * 2.0);
269:         let lz = pillar_axis_dist(wz - SCAFFOLD, SCAFFOLD * 2.0);
270:         if lx < 0.5 && lz < 0.5 && unit(cell.rotate_left(11)) < 0.4 {
271:             column.light = true;
272:         }
273:     }
274: 
275:     /// Exposed service pipes traverse every sector just below the ceiling.
276:     fn apply_pipes(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
277:         if column.solid {
278:             return;
279:         }
280:         let run_z = (wz / PIPE_SPACING).round() as i64;
281:         let on_x_run = (wz - run_z as f32 * PIPE_SPACING).abs() < PIPE_HALF_W
282:             && unit(hash(seed, 0x9199_E000_0000_0001, run_z, 0)) < 0.7;
283:         let run_x = (wx / PIPE_SPACING).round() as i64;
284:         let on_z_run = (wx - run_x as f32 * PIPE_SPACING).abs() < PIPE_HALF_W
285:             && unit(hash(seed, 0x9199_E000_0000_0002, run_x, 1)) < 0.7;
286:         if on_x_run || on_z_run {
287:             let soffit = column.ceiling_units - PIPE_DROP;
288:             column.lintel_from_units = Some(
289:                 column
290:                     .lintel_from_units
291:                     .map_or(soffit, |existing| existing.min(soffit)),
292:             );
293:             column.wall_material = VOXEL_PIPE;
294:         }
295:     }
296: 
297:     /// The arrival plaza: an always-open, always-lit clearing at the origin
298:     /// holding the door back to Level 0.
299:     fn apply_plaza(wx: f32, wz: f32, column: &mut ColumnPlan) {
300:         let d2 = wx * wx + wz * wz;
301:         if d2 > PLAZA_R * PLAZA_R {
302:             return;
303:         }
304:         column.solid = false;
305:         column.floor_units = 0.0;
306:         column.lintel_from_units = None;
307:         column.ceiling_units = column.ceiling_units.max(3.4);
308:         column.floor_material = VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR;
309:         column.wall_material = VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL;
310:         // One dependable fixture above the arrival point.
311:         if (wx - ARRIVAL_POINT.0).abs() < 0.6 && (wz - ARRIVAL_POINT.1).abs() < 0.6 {
312:             column.light = true;
313:         }
314:     }
315: 
316:     /// Deterministic supply spot for one supply cell, or None. Supplies are
317:     /// canon-dense in Gild (crates), present in Aquila, rare elsewhere; the
318:     /// world tuning scales drink and food frequency independently.
319:     fn supply_for_cell(
320:         seed: u32,
321:         cx: i64,
322:         cz: i64,
323:         water: f32,
324:         food: f32,
325:     ) -> Option<SupplyItem> {
326:         let water_weight = 0.72 * water.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
327:         let food_weight = 0.28 * food.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
328:         if water_weight + food_weight <= 0.0 {
329:             return None;
330:         }
331:         let roll = hash(seed, 0x5A17_AB1E_00BB_0000, cx, cz);
332:         let origin_x = cx as f32 * SUPPLY_CELL;
333:         let origin_z = cz as f32 * SUPPLY_CELL;
334:         // Probe a few hashed candidate spots; accept the first that lands in
335:         // open, walkable floor (crate tops count — bottles sit on crates).
336:         for attempt in 0..6u64 {
337:             let probe = hash(seed, 0x5A17_AB1E_0000_0100 | attempt, cx, cz);
338:             let px = origin_x + 1.0 + unit(probe) * (SUPPLY_CELL - 2.0);
339:             let pz = origin_z + 1.0 + unit(probe.rotate_left(21)) * (SUPPLY_CELL - 2.0);
340:             let sector = Sector::at(seed, px, pz);
341:             let chance = match sector {
342:                 Sector::Gild => 0.85,
343:                 Sector::Aquila => 0.35,
344:                 Sector::Gothic => 0.2,
345:                 Sector::Construction => 0.15,
346:             } * (water_weight + food_weight);
347:             if unit(roll) > chance {
348:                 return None;
349:             }
350:             let column = Self::plan_column(seed, px, pz);
351:             if column.solid || !column.floor {
352:                 continue;
353:             }
354:             let kind = if unit(roll.rotate_left(9)) * (water_weight + food_weight) < water_weight
355:             {
356:                 SupplyKind::AlmondWater
357:             } else {
358:                 SupplyKind::Ration
359:             };
360:             return Some(SupplyItem {
361:                 id: supply_id(seed, cx, cz, attempt),
362:                 kind,
363:                 position: Position::new(px, pz),
364:                 rest_y: column.floor_units,
365:             });
366:         }
367:         None
368:     }
369: 
370:     /// All supply items overlapping a chunk, minus what reality consumed.
371:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
372:     fn supplies_in_bounds(
373:         seed: u32,
374:         min_x: f32,
375:         min_z: f32,
376:         max_x: f32,
377:         max_z: f32,
378:         water: f32,
379:         food: f32,
380:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
381:     ) -> Vec<SupplyItem> {
382:         let mut items = Vec::new();
383:         let c0x = (min_x / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
384:         let c1x = (max_x / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
385:         let c0z = (min_z / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
386:         let c1z = (max_z / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
387:         for cz in c0z..=c1z {
388:             for cx in c0x..=c1x {
389:                 let Some(item) = Self::supply_for_cell(seed, cx, cz, water, food) else {
390:                     continue;
391:                 };
392:                 if reality.supply_consumed(item.id) {
393:                     continue;
394:                 }
395:                 if item.position.x >= min_x
396:                     && item.position.x < max_x
397:                     && item.position.z >= min_z
398:                     && item.position.z < max_z
399:                 {
400:                     items.push(item);
401:                 }
402:             }
403:         }
404:         items
405:     }
406: }
407: 
408: /// Stamps a supply marker into the grid at a supply position. Shapes are
409: /// authored in world space so every voxel resolution and every overlapping
410: /// chunk quantizes them identically:
411: ///
412: /// * almond water — a milky bottle (~0.16u wide, ~0.3u tall) with a dark
413: ///   screw cap; the body is the faintly emissive bottle material, so it
414: ///   glints in dim fabric.
415: /// * ration — a squat blue-grey tin (~0.24u wide, ~0.16u tall).
416: pub(crate) fn stamp_supply_marker(
417:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
418:     chunk_pos: Position,
419:     voxel_size: f32,
420:     item: &SupplyItem,
421: ) {
422:     let base_y = (item.rest_y / voxel_size).round() as i64 + 1;
423:     // Fill the voxel columns covering a world-space square around the item
424:     // center, `rows` layers tall starting at `row`.
425:     let mut stamp_box = |half_w: f32, row: i64, rows: i64, material: u8| {
426:         let lo = |c: f32, origin: f32| ((c - half_w - origin) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
427:         let hi = |c: f32, origin: f32| ((c + half_w - origin) / voxel_size).ceil() as i64 - 1;
428:         for z in lo(item.position.z, chunk_pos.z)..=hi(item.position.z, chunk_pos.z) {
429:             for x in lo(item.position.x, chunk_pos.x)..=hi(item.position.x, chunk_pos.x) {
430:                 for y in row..row + rows {
431:                     if x >= 0 && y >= 1 && z >= 0 {
432:                         grid.set(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize, material);
433:                     }
434:                 }
435:             }
436:         }
437:     };
438:     match item.kind {
439:         SupplyKind::AlmondWater => {
440:             let body_rows = ((0.22 / voxel_size).round() as i64).max(1);
441:             stamp_box(0.08, base_y, body_rows, VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER);
442:             stamp_box(0.04, base_y + body_rows, 1, VOXEL_PIPE);
443:         }
444:         SupplyKind::Ration => {
445:             let rows = ((0.16 / voxel_size).round() as i64).max(1);
446:             stamp_box(0.12, base_y, rows, VOXEL_METAL_DOOR);
447:         }
448:     }
449: }
450: 
451: /// Stamps a free-standing metal door: jambs, lintel, and a walk-through
452: /// panel. The frame runs along the X axis (panel plane faces Z). The whole
453: /// footprint stays inside a 1.0u halo of its center so Level 0's region
454: /// window can always reproduce it across chunk seams.
455: pub(crate) fn stamp_level_door(
456:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
457:     chunk_pos: Position,
458:     voxel_size: f32,
459:     center_x: f32,
460:     center_z: f32,
461:     wall_material: u8,
462: ) {
463:     let to_local = |w: f32, origin: f32| ((w - origin) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
464:     let door_half = 0.6;
465:     let jamb_half = 0.15;
466:     let height_v = (2.4 / voxel_size).round() as i64;
467:     let lintel_v = (2.2 / voxel_size).round() as i64;
468:     let panel_t = ((0.12 / voxel_size).round() as i64).max(1);
469: 
470:     let x0 = to_local(center_x - door_half - jamb_half * 2.0, chunk_pos.x);
471:     let x1 = to_local(center_x + door_half + jamb_half * 2.0, chunk_pos.x);
472:     let z0 = to_local(center_z - panel_t as f32 * voxel_size * 0.5, chunk_pos.z);
473:     let jamb_from = to_local(center_x - door_half, chunk_pos.x);
474:     let jamb_to = to_local(center_x + door_half, chunk_pos.x);
475: 
476:     for x in x0..=x1 {
477:         for dz in 0..panel_t {
478:             let z = z0 + dz;
479:             if x < 0 || z < 0 {
480:                 continue;
481:             }
482:             for y in 1..=height_v {
483:                 let material = if x < jamb_from || x > jamb_to || y >= lintel_v {
484:                     wall_material
485:                 } else {
486:                     VOXEL_METAL_DOOR
487:                 };
488:                 grid.set(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize, material);
489:             }
490:         }
491:     }
492: }
493: 
494: impl LevelGenerator for HabitableLevel {
495:     fn generate(
496:         &self,
497:         chunk_pos: Position,
498:         seed: u32,
499:         config: GeneratorConfig,
500:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
501:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
502:         self.generate_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, noise, &RealitySnapshot::empty())
503:     }
504: 
505:     fn generate_with_reality(
506:         &self,
507:         chunk_pos: Position,
508:         seed: u32,
509:         config: GeneratorConfig,
510:         _noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
511:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
512:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
513:         let s = config.voxel_scale;
514:         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
515:         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
516:         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
517:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
518: 
519:         let plan_at = |lx: i64, lz: i64| -> ColumnPlan {
520:             let wx = chunk_pos.x + (lx as f32 + 0.5) * s;
521:             let wz = chunk_pos.z + (lz as f32 + 0.5) * s;
522:             HabitableLevel::plan_column(seed, wx, wz)
523:         };
524:         let columns = ColumnField::sample(width, depth, plan_at);
525:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &columns, s);
526: 
527:         // Supplies: exported beside the geometry, markers stamped after
528:         // voxelization so a crate top can hold a bottle. Enumeration runs
529:         // half a unit past the bounds so a boundary marker stamps its
530:         // spilled voxels into this grid too; the semantic export stays with
531:         // the grid whose bounds contain the item.
532:         let max_x = chunk_pos.x + config.chunk_size;
533:         let max_z = chunk_pos.z + config.chunk_size;
534:         for item in HabitableLevel::supplies_in_bounds(
535:             seed,
536:             chunk_pos.x - 0.5,
537:             chunk_pos.z - 0.5,
538:             max_x + 0.5,
539:             max_z + 0.5,
540:             config.tuning.almond_water,
541:             config.tuning.rations,
542:             reality,
543:         ) {
544:             stamp_supply_marker(&mut grid, chunk_pos, s, &item);
545:             if item.position.x >= chunk_pos.x
546:                 && item.position.x < max_x
547:                 && item.position.z >= chunk_pos.z
548:                 && item.position.z < max_z
549:             {
550:                 grid.supply_items.push(item);
551:             }
552:         }
553: 
554:         // The return door to Level 0 stands in the arrival plaza.
555:         let door_bounds_this_chunk = RETURN_DOOR.0 >= chunk_pos.x - 2.0
556:             && RETURN_DOOR.0 < max_x + 2.0
557:             && RETURN_DOOR.1 >= chunk_pos.z - 2.0
558:             && RETURN_DOOR.1 < max_z + 2.0;
559:         if door_bounds_this_chunk {
560:             stamp_level_door(
561:                 &mut grid,
562:                 chunk_pos,
563:                 s,
564:                 RETURN_DOOR.0,
565:                 RETURN_DOOR.1,
566:                 VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL,
567:             );
568:         }
569:         if RETURN_DOOR.0 >= chunk_pos.x
570:             && RETURN_DOOR.0 < max_x
571:             && RETURN_DOOR.1 >= chunk_pos.z
572:             && RETURN_DOOR.1 < max_z
573:         {
574:             grid.level_exits.push(LevelExit {
575:                 id: hash(seed, 0xD00E_0000_0000_0001, 1, 0),
576:                 target_level: LEVEL_BACKROOMS,
577:                 center: Position::new(RETURN_DOOR.0, RETURN_DOOR.1),
578:                 half_extent: DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF,
579:                 arrival: Position::new(LEVEL0_ARRIVAL.0, LEVEL0_ARRIVAL.1),
580:             });
581:         }
582: 
583:         grid
584:     }
585: }
````

````rust
 33: /// Column stride used by walkability scans. Coarser than the 0.4u plan

 37: #[test]

 39:     let a = generate(96.0, -64.0);
 40:     let b = generate(96.0, -64.0);
````
