````rust
 51: #[test]
 52: fn every_sector_keeps_the_ground_plane_walkable() {
 53:     // Flood-fill reachability over a 96u sector-sized window: from the
 54:     // arrival plaza, most open floor must be mutually reachable. Openings
 55:     // are >= 1 unit by construction (doorways 1.4u, lanes, bays).
 56:     let seed = 42;
 57:     let window = 96.0f32;
 58:     let cells = (window / SCAN_STEP) as usize;
 59:     let open = |ix: usize, iz: usize| -> bool {
 60:         let wx = ix as f32 * SCAN_STEP - window * 0.5;
 61:         let wz = iz as f32 * SCAN_STEP - window * 0.5;
 62:         let c = HabitableLevel::plan_column(seed, wx, wz);
 63:         !c.solid && c.floor_units < 0.5
 64:     };
 65:     let mut visited = vec![false; cells * cells];
 66:     let start = (cells / 2, cells / 2);
 67:     assert!(open(start.0, start.1), "arrival plaza must be open");
 68:     let mut stack = vec![start];
 69:     visited[start.1 * cells + start.0] = true;
 70:     let mut reached = 0usize;
 71:     while let Some((x, z)) = stack.pop() {
 72:         reached += 1;
 73:         let neighbors = [
 74:             (x.wrapping_sub(1), z),
 75:             (x + 1, z),
 76:             (x, z.wrapping_sub(1)),
 77:             (x, z + 1),
 78:         ];
 79:         for (nx, nz) in neighbors {
 80:             if nx < cells && nz < cells && !visited[nz * cells + nx] && open(nx, nz) {
 81:                 visited[nz * cells + nx] = true;
 82:                 stack.push((nx, nz));
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85:     }
 86:     let total_open = (0..cells * cells)
 87:         .filter(|i| open(i % cells, i / cells))
 88:         .count();
 89:     assert!(
 90:         reached * 100 >= total_open * 85,
 91:         "{reached} of {total_open} open columns reachable from the plaza"
 92:     );
 93: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Column composition: the one priority order in which Level 0's systems
  2: //! claim a world column. Circulation beats anomalies beats assemblies beats
  3: //! fabric — and archway anchors freeze every mutable family around them.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyKind, RealitySnapshot};
  6: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  7:     CirculationSpine, RegionPlan, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystemInstance,
  8: };

 12: use crate::use_cases::red_rooms::geometry::sample_red_room;
 13: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{PLAN_WALL_T, region_index, spawn_point};
 14: 
 15: use super::circulation_sampler::SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS;
 16: use super::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan};
 17: 
 18: #[cfg(test)]
 19: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::LevelTuning;
 20: 
 21: impl BackroomsLevel {
 22: 
 23:     /// The architectural column plan: corridor beats assembly beats fabric.
 24:     #[cfg(test)]
 25:     pub(crate) fn plan_column(
 26:         plan: &RegionPlan,
 27:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 28:         seed: u32,
 29:         tuning: &LevelTuning,
 30:         wx: f32,
 31:         wz: f32,
 32:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 33:         Self::plan_column_in_reality(
 34:             plan,
 35:             noise,
 36:             seed,
 37:             &GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_tuning(*tuning),
 38:             &RealitySnapshot::empty(),
 39:             wx,
 40:             wz,
 41:         )
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     pub(crate) fn plan_column_in_reality(
 45:         plan: &RegionPlan,
 46:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 47:         seed: u32,
 48:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 49:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 50:         wx: f32,
 51:         wz: f32,
 52:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 53:         let tuning = &config.tuning;
 54:         // -- circulation ----------------------------------------------------
 55:         let mut in_corridor = false;
 56:         let mut corridor_ceiling = 0.0f32;
 57:         let mut corridor_light = false;
 58:         let mut corridor_wall = false;
 59:         // Edge-gap decisions are deferred: they read the Peripheral Shift,
 60:         // and whether this column's fabric is frozen (spawn radius, arch
 61:         // anchors) is only known further down.
 62:         let mut gap_probes: Vec<(&CirculationSpine, f32, bool)> = Vec::new();
 63:         for s in &plan.corridors {
 64:             let (d, along, is_horizontal) = s.nearest(wx, wz);
 65:             let half = s.width * 0.5;
 66:             if d <= half {
 67:                 in_corridor = true;
 68:                 corridor_ceiling =
 69:                     corridor_ceiling.max(Self::corridor_ceiling(s, noise, seed, wx, wz));
 70:                 // Light strip modules follow the corridor in world space.
 71:                 if d < 0.45 && along.rem_euclid(4.0) < 1.0 {
 72:                     corridor_light = true;
 73:                 }
 74:             } else if d <= half + PLAN_WALL_T {
 75:                 corridor_wall = true;
 76:                 corridor_ceiling =
 77:                     corridor_ceiling.max(Self::corridor_ceiling(s, noise, seed, wx, wz));
 78:                 gap_probes.push((s, along, is_horizontal));
 79:             }
 80:         }
 81:         if in_corridor {
 82:             let mut column = ColumnPlan {
 83:                 light: corridor_light && tuning.lights > 0.0,
 84:                 ..ColumnPlan::open(corridor_ceiling)
 85:             };
 86:             // Geometry priority and presentation priority are different
 87:             // things: the corridor owns passability — its route through a
 88:             // blackout stays carved open — but a blackout owns the *dark*.
 89:             // Past the approach band the corridor's light strips die like
 90:             // every other fixture, thinning through the same gradient, so
 91:             // circulation never reads as a lit tunnel through the anomaly.
 92:             if let Some(blackout) = plan
 93:                 .anomalies
 94:                 .iter()
 95:                 .find(|a| a.kind == AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse && a.contains(wx, wz))
 96:             {
 97:                 let depth = blackout.normalized_depth(wx, wz);
 98:                 if depth > 0.22 {
 99:                     column.light = false;
100:                 } else if depth > 0.0 && column.light {
101:                     let module = (wx.floor() as i64) ^ ((wz.floor() as i64) << 17);
102:                     let hash = {
103:                         let mut h = (blackout.id ^ module as u64)
104:                             .wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
105:                         h ^= h >> 33;
106:                         (h >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
107:                     };
108:                     column.light = hash < 1.0 - depth / 0.22;
109:                 }
110:             }
111:             return column;
112:         }
113: 
114:         // Archway anchors take precedence over every hostile family, and any
115:         // hostile column within an anchor's margin generates as if no epoch
116:         // had ever advanced: arch rooms and their surroundings are immune to
117:         // non-Euclidean transformation by construction, not by policy.
118:         if let Some(anchor) = plan
119:             .anomalies
120:             .iter()
121:             .find(|a| a.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom && a.contains(wx, wz))
122:         {
123:             return sample_anomaly(anchor, noise, seed, config, reality, wx, wz);
124:         }
125:         let near_anchor = plan.anomalies.iter().any(|a| {
126:             a.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
127:                 && a.footprint.bounds().expanded(3.2).contains(wx, wz)
128:         });
129: 
130:         if let Some(instance) = plan
131:             .anomalies
132:             .iter()
133:             .filter(|a| {
134:                 a.kind != AnomalyKind::RedRoom
135:                     && a.kind != AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
136:                     && a.contains(wx, wz)
137:             })
138:             .max_by(|a, b| {
139:                 a.normalized_depth(wx, wz)
140:                     .total_cmp(&b.normalized_depth(wx, wz))
141:             })
142:         {
143:             let frozen = RealitySnapshot::empty();
144:             let effective_reality = if near_anchor { &frozen } else { reality };
145:             return sample_anomaly(instance, noise, seed, config, effective_reality, wx, wz);
146:         }
147: 
148:         // -- assemblies -------------------------------------------------------
149:         {
150:             let renovator_structure = plan.architects.get(1).map(|g| StructuralSystemInstance {
151:                 system: g.structural_system,
152:                 bay_x: 3.6,
153:                 bay_z: 4.4,
154:                 phase: (1.6, 2.4),
155:                 column_side: 0.4,
156:             });
157:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
158:                 let b = a.footprint.bounds();
159:                 let t = PLAN_WALL_T;
160:                 if wx < b.0 - t || wx > b.2 + t || wz < b.1 - t || wz > b.3 + t {
161:                     continue;
162:                 }
163:                 let inside = a.footprint.contains(wx, wz);
164:                 let mut base =
165:                     Self::assembly_column(a, inside, renovator_structure.as_ref(), tuning, wx, wz);
166:                 // A stair assembly shapes its interior as a flight: the
167:                 // vertical link that reserved it decides whether the flight
168:                 // lands or climbs endlessly. Stairs are architecture, so a
169:                 // walls=0 debug world flattens them along with everything.
170:                 if a.program == SpaceProgram::Stair && inside && !base.solid && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
171:                     let rx = region_index(plan.origin_world.x + 0.1);
172:                     let rz = region_index(plan.origin_world.z + 0.1);
173:                     let kind = crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(
174:                         seed, noise, rx, rz,
175:                     )
176:                     .map(|link| link.kind)
177:                     .unwrap_or(
178:                         crate::domain::entities::world_topology::VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair,
179:                     );
180:                     crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::apply_stair_profile(
181:                         a, kind, &mut base, wx, wz,
182:                     );
183:                 }
184:                 if a.corruption.red_room
185:                     && let Some(red) = plan.anomalies.iter().find(|r| {
186:                         r.kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom
187:                             && r.footprint
188:                                 .bounds()
189:                                 .expanded(PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05)
190:                                 .contains(wx, wz)
191:                     })
192:                 {
193:                     return sample_red_room(red, base, config, reality, wx, wz);
194:                 }
195:                 return base;
196:             }
197:         }
198: 
199:         // -- the endless unplanned office fabric -------------------------------
200:         // Ordinary fabric is the Peripheral Shift's territory — with two
201:         // sanctuaries. Arch-anchor surroundings are immune by construction
202:         // (the same guarantee their hostile-family freeze gives above), and
203:         // the spawn opening sequence never rearranges: the first hallways a
204:         // wanderer learns are the last ones the level may take away.
205:         let sp = spawn_point(seed);
206:         let near_spawn = (wx - sp.x) * (wx - sp.x) + (wz - sp.z) * (wz - sp.z)
207:             < SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS * SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS;
208:         let still_fabric = RealitySnapshot::empty();
209:         let fabric_reality = if near_anchor || near_spawn {
210:             &still_fabric
211:         } else {
212:             reality
213:         };
214: 
215:         // -- corridor edge walls through fabric -------------------------------
216:         // The mouths onto circulation drift and seal with the same reality
217:         // as the fabric they open into (frozen in the sanctuaries above).
218:         if corridor_wall && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
219:             let corridor_gap = gap_probes.iter().any(|&(s, along, is_horizontal)| {
220:                 Self::corridor_edge_opens(
221:                     s,
222:                     noise,
223:                     seed,
224:                     fabric_reality,
225:                     along,
226:                     is_horizontal,
227:                     wx,
228:                     wz,
229:                 )
230:             });
231:             if !corridor_gap {
232:                 return ColumnPlan {
233:                     solid: true,
234:                     ..ColumnPlan::open(corridor_ceiling.max(3.2))
235:                 };
236:             }
237:         }
238:         Self::column_plan_in_reality(noise, seed, tuning, fabric_reality, wx, wz)
239:     }
240: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Level 0 — the Backrooms proper.
 2: //!
 3: //! Everything is a pure function of *world-space* coordinates, so chunks tile
 4: //! seamlessly no matter which order they stream in. The goal is *believable
 5: //! building architecture* with depth — not flat mazes:
 6: //!
 7: //! * **Ceiling regions** use broad smooth fields instead of a low default
 8: //!   slab: regular dropped ceilings are 3.2--3.6 u, open expanses 3.8--4.4 u,
 9: //!   vaults 4.5--5.4 u, and compression zones are rare deliberate contrast.
10: //! * **Halls**: one dominant cross-region route is wide enough to read as
11: //!   circulation through a vast building, with at most two interior branches.
12: //!   Its edge walls persist in long runs and open into large rooms or fabric,
13: //!   not a repeated doorway grid.
14: //! * **Fabric**: the default fill *is* the labyrinth — an irregular warren
15: //!   of rooms on a hidden 7.2 u lattice, chained through hashed doorways
16: //!   (binary-tree rule guarantees global connectivity chunk-locally) and
17: //!   merged by porosity-driven wall dropout so no grid is ever readable.
18: //!   Open expanses are the exception that punctuates it, never the default.
19: //!
20: //! The stages scream their intent, one module each:
21: //!
22: //! * [`fabric`] — the endless unplanned warren between planned systems.
23: //! * [`circulation_sampler`] — corridor ceilings and dissolving edge walls.
24: //! * [`assembly_sampler`] — planned program masses and their fixtures.
25: //! * [`compose_column`] — the one priority order that arbitrates a column.
26: //! * [`generate`] — voxelization, semantic exports, and runtime lights.
27: 
28: mod assembly_sampler;
29: mod circulation_sampler;
30: mod column_field;
31: mod column_plan;
32: mod compose_column;
33: mod fabric;
34: mod generate;
35: mod provisions;
36: #[cfg(test)]
37: mod tests;
38: mod voxelize;
39: 
40: pub(crate) use column_field::ColumnField;
41: pub(crate) use column_plan::ColumnPlan;

44: /// Ceiling height of the tallest (atrium) vaults, world units.
````

````rust
  1: //! Materialize sampled Level 0 columns at the requested voxel size.
  2: 
  3: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VoxelGrid};
  4: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnField;
  5: 
  6: /// Writes geometry and fixture voxels without knowing seeds, regions,
  7: /// anomalies, chunks, or recursive branches.  Those are planning concerns;
  8: /// this stage only quantizes an already sampled physical area.
  9: pub(crate) fn voxelize_columns(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, field: &ColumnField, voxel_size: f32) {
 10:     let max_y = grid.height().saturating_sub(1);
 11:     let to_voxel = |units: f32| ((units / voxel_size) as usize).clamp(2, max_y);
 12: 
 13:     for z in 0..field.depth() {
 14:         for x in 0..field.width() {
 15:             let plan = *field.get(x as i64, z as i64);
 16:             let ceiling_y = to_voxel(plan.ceiling_units);
 17: 
 18:             if plan.floor {
 19:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, plan.floor_material);
 20:                 // Raised floor (stair treads, landings) is solid mass in
 21:                 // wall material: collision derives from solid voxels, so a
 22:                 // tread must block like architecture, not paint like carpet.
 23:                 let raised = (plan.floor_units / voxel_size).round() as usize;
 24:                 for y in 1..=raised.min(max_y) {
 25:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 26:                 }
 27:             }
 28: 
 29:             if plan.solid {
 30:                 for y in 1..ceiling_y {
 31:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 32:                 }
 33:             } else if let Some(lintel_height) = plan.lintel_from_units {
 34:                 for y in to_voxel(lintel_height)..ceiling_y {
 35:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 36:                 }
 37:             }
 38: 
 39:             // A lower ceiling grows a skirt up to its tallest neighbour.  A
 40:             // request therefore cannot see through a height step that lives
 41:             // just across its output boundary.
 42:             let neighbour_ceiling = [
 43:                 field.get(x as i64 - 1, z as i64),
 44:                 field.get(x as i64 + 1, z as i64),
 45:                 field.get(x as i64, z as i64 - 1),
 46:                 field.get(x as i64, z as i64 + 1),
 47:             ]
 48:             .iter()
 49:             .map(|neighbour| to_voxel(neighbour.ceiling_units))
 50:             .max()
 51:             .unwrap_or(ceiling_y);
 52: 
 53:             let cap_material = if plan.solid {
 54:                 plan.wall_material
 55:             } else {
 56:                 VOXEL_CEILING
 57:             };
 58:             for y in ceiling_y..=neighbour_ceiling.max(ceiling_y) {
 59:                 grid.set(x, y, z, cap_material);
 60:             }
 61: 
 62:             if plan.light && !plan.solid {
 63:                 let material = if plan.red_light {
 64:                     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT
 65:                 } else {
 66:                     plan.light_material
 67:                 };
 68:                 grid.set(x, ceiling_y, z, material);
 69:             }
 70:         }
 71:     }
 72: }
 73: 
 74: #[cfg(test)]
 75: mod tests {
 76:     use super::*;
 77:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{EMISSIVE_MATERIALS, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_WALL};
 78:     use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 79: 
 80:     /// Level 0 currently has one authored emitter contract: fixtures are
 81:     /// exposed panels in open ceiling columns. A fixture request on a solid
 82:     /// column must therefore remain ordinary architecture, never a buried
 83:     /// emissive voxel or a second light on the floor.
 84:     #[test]
 85:     fn solid_columns_cannot_voxelize_fake_emitters() {
 86:         let mut column = ColumnPlan::open(4.0);
 87:         column.solid = true;
 88:         column.light = true;
 89:         column.red_light = true;
 90:         column.light_material = VOXEL_RED_LIGHT;
 91: 
 92:         let field = ColumnField::sample(1, 1, |_, _| column);
 93:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(1, 6, 1);
 94:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &field, 1.0);
 95: 
 96:         assert_eq!(grid.get(0, 0, 0), VOXEL_FLOOR);
 97:         for y in 0..grid.height() {
 98:             let material = grid.get(0, y, 0);
 99:             assert!(
100:                 !EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material),
101:                 "solid column contains buried emitter {material} at y={y}"
102:             );
103:         }
104:         for y in 1..=4 {
105:             let material = grid.get(0, y, 0);
106:             assert_eq!(material, VOXEL_WALL);
107:         }
108:     }
109: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/grassland_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Level 34-B — "The Grassland".
  2: //!
  3: //! A safe, flat, endless grass plane you can noclip into from Level 0:
  4: //! * grass ground everywhere, with smooth-noise **lakes** of shallow water,
  5: //! * scattered **trees** (solid trunk, leaf canopy) on a hashed world grid,
  6: //! * a glowing **sky layer** at the top of the grid plus dim ground glow
  7: //!   sources hidden inside the turf, so the plane reads as daylight even
  8: //!   though lighting is the same BFS flood used indoors.
  9: //!
 10: //! Like every [`LevelGenerator`], all placement is a pure function of
 11: //! world-space coordinates so chunks tile seamlessly.
 12: 
 13: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 14:     VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
 15: };
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
 19: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 20: 
 21: /// Grid height in world units; the sky glow layer sits at the top.
 22: const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
 23: /// Trees sit on a world grid of this period (units); most cells are empty.
 24: const TREE_PERIOD: f32 = 9.0;
 25: /// Ground glow sources ("sun-lit turf") every N units.
 26: const GLOW_PERIOD: f32 = 3.2;
 27: 
 28: pub struct GrasslandLevel;
 29: 
 30: impl GrasslandLevel {
 31:     /// Uniform per-cell hash in [0, 1): samples the value noise exactly on
 32:     /// its lattice (provider frequency 0.05 → inputs that are multiples of
 33:     /// 20 hit lattice points, where the noise is a raw uniform hash).
 34:     fn hash(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, salt: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64) -> f32 {
 35:         let v = noise.evaluate_2d(
 36:             seed ^ salt,
 37:             Position::new(cx as f32 * 20.0, cz as f32 * 20.0),
 38:         );
 39:         (v * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999)
 40:     }
 41: }
 42: 
 43: impl LevelGenerator for GrasslandLevel {
 44:     fn generate(
 45:         &self,
 46:         chunk_pos: Position,
 47:         seed: u32,
 48:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 49:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 50:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
 51:         let s = config.voxel_scale;
 52:         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 53:         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 54:         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
 55:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
 56:         let sky_y = height - 1;
 57: 
 58:         for z in 0..depth {
 59:             for x in 0..width {
 60:                 let wx = chunk_pos.x + (x as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 61:                 let wz = chunk_pos.z + (z as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 62: 
 63:                 // Lakes: smooth blobs of the world-space noise field.
 64:                 let lake = noise.evaluate_2d(seed ^ 0x1A5E, Position::new(wx * 0.7, wz * 0.7));
 65:                 let ground = if lake > 0.62 {
 66:                     VOXEL_WATER
 67:                 } else {
 68:                     VOXEL_GRASS
 69:                 };
 70:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, ground);
 71: 
 72:                 // Sky glow: an unbroken luminous layer overhead.
 73:                 grid.set(x, sky_y, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 74: 
 75:                 // Ground glow grid keeps the turf bright at eye level (the
 76:                 // BFS light from the sky layer alone fades before the floor).
 77:                 let gx = wx.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 78:                 let gz = wz.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 79:                 if ground == VOXEL_GRASS && gx < s && gz < s {
 80:                     grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 81:                 }
 82: 
 83:                 // Trees: hashed world cells, never in water.
 84:                 let cell_x = (wx / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 85:                 let cell_z = (wz / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 86:                 if Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE5, cell_x, cell_z) > 0.6 && ground == VOXEL_GRASS {
 87:                     // Trunk position jittered inside the cell.
 88:                     let jx =
 89:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE6, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 90:                     let jz =
 91:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE7, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 92:                     let tx = cell_x as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jx;
 93:                     let tz = cell_z as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jz;
 94:                     let dx = wx - tx;
 95:                     let dz = wz - tz;
 96:                     let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 97: 
 98:                     let trunk_top = (2.2 / s) as usize;
 99:                     let canopy_top = (3.6 / s) as usize;
100:                     if d2 < (0.25f32).powi(2) {
101:                         for y in 1..trunk_top.min(height - 2) {
102:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_TREE);
103:                         }
104:                     }
105:                     if d2 < (1.6f32).powi(2) {
106:                         for y in trunk_top..canopy_top.min(height - 2) {
107:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_GRASS);
108:                         }
109:                     }
110:                 }
111:             }
112:         }
113: 
114:         grid
115:     }
116: }
117: 
118: #[cfg(test)]
119: mod tests {
120:     use super::*;
121:     use crate::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
122: 
123:     fn generate(ox: f32, oz: f32) -> VoxelGrid {
124:         GrasslandLevel.generate(
125:             Position::new(ox, oz),
126:             42,
127:             GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
128:             &SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
129:         )
130:     }
131: 
132:     #[test]
133:     fn grassland_has_grass_sky_and_open_walkway() {
134:         let grid = generate(0.0, 0.0);
135:         let sky_y = grid.height() - 1;
136:         let mut grass = 0;
137:         let mut open_at_eye = 0;
138:         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
139:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
140:                 assert_eq!(grid.get(x, sky_y, z), VOXEL_LIGHT, "sky layer must glow");
141:                 let g = grid.get(x, 0, z);
142:                 if g == VOXEL_GRASS || g == VOXEL_LIGHT {

144:                 }

151:         assert!(grass > total / 2, "mostly grass, got {grass}/{total}");

158:     #[test]
159:     fn grassland_scatters_trees_deterministically() {
160:         let a = generate(0.0, 0.0);
161:         let b = generate(0.0, 0.0);
162:         let mut trees = 0;
163:         for z in 0..a.depth() {
164:             for x in 0..a.width() {
165:                 assert_eq!(a.get(x, 3, z), b.get(x, 3, z), "must be deterministic");
166:                 if a.get(x, 3, z) == VOXEL_TREE {
167:                     trees += 1;
168:                 }
169:             }
170:         }
171:         // Trees are sparse but should exist across a few chunks.

173:         for (ox, oz) in [

175:             (0.0, 10.0),
176:             (10.0, 10.0),
177:             (-10.0, 0.0),
178:             (0.0, -10.0),
179:             (-10.0, -10.0),
180:             (20.0, 0.0),
181:             (0.0, 20.0),
182:         ] {
183:             let g = generate(ox, oz);
184:             for z in 0..g.depth() {
185:                 for x in 0..g.width() {
186:                     if g.get(x, 3, z) == VOXEL_TREE {
187:                         total_trees += 1;
188:                     }
189:                 }
190:             }
````

## File: src/use_cases/vertical_circulation.rs
````rust
  1: //! Stairwells: the first physical layer of the vertical world graph.
  2: //!
  3: //! The macro topology ([`crate::use_cases::world_topology`]) reserves
  4: //! [`VerticalLink`]s — stair and shaft obligations anchored inside regions.
  5: //! This module realizes the *upward* links as concrete architecture:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`place_stairwell`] gives the region planner a `SpaceProgram::Stair`
  8: //!   assembly beside its primary corridor, near the link's anchor.
  9: //! * [`apply_stair_profile`] shapes the interior per voxel column: a flat
 10: //!   vestibule, a flight of 0.2 u treads, and a landing. An
 11: //!   [`VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent`] flight never lands — it keeps
 12: //!   rising under a raised, unlit shaft ceiling until the far wall
 13: //!   swallows it in the dark.
 14: //!
 15: //! What this deliberately does **not** do yet: move the player between
 16: //! elevations. The engine's collision world is a fixed-eye-height slider,
 17: //! so a stair is currently a readable, colliding landmark and a topology
 18: //! contract. Downward links (`EndlessDescent`, `ServiceShaft`) stay
 19: //! reservation-only until chunks can stream below elevation 0; realizing
 20: //! them as fake geometry would spend the mystery without paying it off.
 21: //!
 22: //! Geometry invariants (tested in `region_plan` / here):
 23: //! * treads rise monotonically from the entrance, 0.2 u per 0.4 u of run;
 24: //! * headroom above every tread stays >= 2.2 u;
 25: //! * the entrance column itself is always flat and walkable;
 26: //! * the profile is a pure function of world position and the assembly.
 27: 
 28: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
 29:     AssemblyInstance, CeilingZone, CorruptionProfile, Fixture, Opening, Polygon2, SpaceProgram,
 30:     StructuralSystem, StructuralSystemInstance,
 31: };
 32: use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind};
 33: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 34: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 35: 
 36: /// Stairwell frontage along its corridor, world units.
 37: const STAIR_WIDTH: f32 = 4.8;
 38: /// Stairwell depth away from the corridor.
 39: const STAIR_DEPTH: f32 = 8.8;
 40: /// Flat entry vestibule before the first riser.
 41: const VESTIBULE_DEPTH: f32 = 2.0;
 42: /// One tread: rise per run, both on the 0.4/0.2 plan lattices.
 43: const TREAD_RUN: f32 = 0.4;
 44: const TREAD_RISE: f32 = 0.2;
 45: /// An ordinary flight lands here (half a story on the macro lattice).
 46: const LANDING_UNITS: f32 = 1.6;
 47: /// An endless ascent keeps climbing to this height before the dark takes it.
 48: const ASCENT_MAX_UNITS: f32 = 3.2;
 49: /// Clear space kept above every tread.
 50: const MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS: f32 = 2.2;
 51: /// Stairwell ceiling: high enough that the top of an endless flight still
 52: /// has headroom, low enough to fit the level's 5.8 u grid.
 53: const STAIR_CEILING_UNITS: f32 = 5.4;
 54: 
 55: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 56:     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
 57: }
 58: 
 59: /// Should this link become a stair assembly this iteration? Upward links
 60: /// voxelize; downward links remain graph reservations (see module docs).
 61: pub(crate) fn link_wants_geometry(link: &VerticalLink) -> bool {
 62:     matches!(
 63:         link.kind,
 64:         VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair | VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent
 65:     )
 66: }
 67: 
 68: /// Builds the stairwell assembly for one vertical link, beside a horizontal
 69: /// main-corridor leg. Mirrors the suite-placement contract: returns `None`
 70: /// if the footprint would escape the region, collide with a prior assembly,
 71: /// or swallow another corridor — the reservation then stays unrealized
 72: /// rather than corrupting the plan.
 73: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 74: pub(crate) fn place_stairwell(
 75:     id: u32,
 76:     link: &VerticalLink,
 77:     legs: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 78:     origin: Position,
 79:     size: f32,
 80:     edge_margin: f32,
 81:     wall_t: f32,
 82:     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 83:     corridor_clearance: impl Fn(f32, f32, f32) -> bool,
 84: ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
 85:     // The leg whose axis passes closest to the anchor hosts the stair.
 86:     let (lx0, lx1, lz, lw) = legs.iter().copied().min_by(|a, b| {
 87:         let da = (link.anchor.z - a.2).abs();
 88:         let db = (link.anchor.z - b.2).abs();
 89:         da.total_cmp(&db)
 90:     })?;
 91:     if lx1 - lx0 < STAIR_WIDTH + 8.0 {
 92:         return None;
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     let side = if link.anchor.z >= lz { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
 96:     let corridor_half = lw * 0.5 + wall_t;
 97:     let x0 = snap((link.anchor.x - STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5).clamp(lx0 + 4.0, lx1 - STAIR_WIDTH - 4.0));
 98:     let z_front = snap(if side > 0.0 {
 99:         lz + corridor_half
100:     } else {
101:         lz - corridor_half - STAIR_DEPTH
102:     });
103:     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, STAIR_WIDTH, STAIR_DEPTH);
104:     let b = footprint.bounds();
105: 
106:     if b.0 < origin.x + edge_margin
107:         || b.1 < origin.z + edge_margin
108:         || b.2 > origin.x + size - edge_margin
109:         || b.3 > origin.z + size - edge_margin
110:     {
111:         return None;
112:     }
113:     if taken
114:         .iter()
115:         .any(|t| t.0 < b.2 + 0.8 && b.0 < t.2 + 0.8 && t.1 < b.3 + 0.8 && b.1 < t.3 + 0.8)
116:     {
117:         return None;
118:     }
119:     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
120:     if !corridor_clearance(center.0, center.1, STAIR_DEPTH.min(STAIR_WIDTH) * 0.25) {
121:         return None;
122:     }
123: 
124:     // A broad, framed threshold: the stair announces itself as circulation.
125:     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
126:     let entrances = vec![Opening {
127:         center: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), front_z),
128:         width: 2.4,
129:         through_x_wall: true,
130:         lintel_units: Some(2.6),
131:     }];
132: 
133:     // One warm fixture over the vestibule; the flight above stays unlit so
134:     // the climb visibly leaves the light.
135:     let vestibule_z = if side > 0.0 {
136:         b.1 + VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
137:     } else {
138:         b.3 - VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
139:     };
140:     let fixtures = vec![Fixture {
141:         at: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), snap(vestibule_z)),
142:         half_x: 0.4,
143:         half_z: 0.4,
144:         lit: true,
145:     }];
146: 
147:     Some(AssemblyInstance {
148:         id,
149:         program: SpaceProgram::Stair,
150:         spaces: Vec::new(),
151:         // Core-and-shell: the stair core carries itself; no interior columns
152:         // may interrupt a flight.
153:         structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
154:             system: StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
155:             bay_x: 4.8,
156:             bay_z: 4.8,
157:             phase: (0.0, 0.0),
158:             column_side: 0.4,
159:         },
160:         ceiling_zones: vec![CeilingZone {
161:             area: footprint.clone(),
162:             language: crate::domain::entities::architecture::CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
163:             height_units: STAIR_CEILING_UNITS,
164:         }],
165:         fixtures,
166:         service_voids: Vec::new(),
167:         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
168:         entrances,
169:         footprint,
170:     })
171: }
172: 
173: /// Shapes one interior column of a stair assembly: vestibule, flight,
174: /// landing (or an endless climb). Pure in `(assembly, kind, wx, wz)`.
175: pub(crate) fn apply_stair_profile(
176:     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
177:     kind: VerticalLinkKind,
178:     plan: &mut ColumnPlan,
179:     _wx: f32,
180:     wz: f32,
181: ) {
182:     let Some(entrance) = assembly.entrances.first() else {
183:         return;
184:     };
185:     let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
186:     // Walk axis runs perpendicular to the entrance wall; depth is measured
187:     // from the entrance side inward.
188:     let depth_in = if entrance.through_x_wall {
189:         if (entrance.center.z - b.1).abs() < (entrance.center.z - b.3).abs() {
190:             wz - b.1
191:         } else {
192:             b.3 - wz
193:         }
194:     } else {
195:         // Stairwells are placed with X-wall entrances today; a Z-wall stair
196:         // would measure along X the same way.
197:         return;
198:     };
199: 
200:     let target = match kind {
201:         VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent => ASCENT_MAX_UNITS,
202:         _ => LANDING_UNITS,
203:     };
204:     let treads = ((depth_in - VESTIBULE_DEPTH) / TREAD_RUN).floor().max(0.0);
205:     let raw = treads * TREAD_RISE;
206:     plan.floor_units = raw.min(target);
207:     // Headroom is a hard invariant: the ceiling zone is planned high enough,
208:     // but clamp anyway so no future ceiling tweak can pinch a flight.
209:     plan.floor_units = plan
210:         .floor_units
211:         .min(plan.ceiling_units - MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS)
212:         .max(0.0);
213: 
214:     // The climb leaves the light: no fixture survives above the first riser,
215:     // and an endless flight rises into an unlit shaft.
216:     if plan.floor_units > 0.0 {
217:         plan.light = false;
218:     }
219: }
220: 
221: #[cfg(test)]
222: mod tests {
223:     use super::*;
224: 
225:     fn stair_assembly() -> AssemblyInstance {
226:         AssemblyInstance {
227:             id: 1,
228:             program: SpaceProgram::Stair,
229:             footprint: Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, STAIR_WIDTH, STAIR_DEPTH),
230:             entrances: vec![Opening {
231:                 center: Position::new(STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5, 0.0),
232:                 width: 2.4,
233:                 through_x_wall: true,
234:                 lintel_units: Some(2.6),
235:             }],
236:             spaces: Vec::new(),
237:             structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
238:                 system: StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
239:                 bay_x: 4.8,
240:                 bay_z: 4.8,
241:                 phase: (0.0, 0.0),
242:                 column_side: 0.4,
243:             },
244:             ceiling_zones: Vec::new(),
245:             fixtures: Vec::new(),
246:             service_voids: Vec::new(),
247:             corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
248:         }
249:     }
250: 
251:     fn profile_at(kind: VerticalLinkKind, wz: f32) -> ColumnPlan {
252:         let assembly = stair_assembly();
253:         let mut plan = ColumnPlan::open(STAIR_CEILING_UNITS);
254:         apply_stair_profile(&assembly, kind, &mut plan, 2.4, wz);
255:         plan
256:     }
257: 
258:     #[test]
259:     fn flight_rises_monotonically_and_lands() {
260:         let mut previous = -1.0f32;
261:         let mut landing_seen = false;
262:         let mut wz = 0.1;
263:         while wz < STAIR_DEPTH {
264:             let plan = profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, wz);
265:             assert!(
266:                 plan.floor_units >= previous - 1e-6,
267:                 "flight descends at depth {wz}"
268:             );
269:             assert!(
270:                 plan.ceiling_units - plan.floor_units >= MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS - 1e-6,
271:                 "headroom pinched at depth {wz}"
272:             );
273:             landing_seen |= (plan.floor_units - LANDING_UNITS).abs() < 1e-6;
274:             previous = plan.floor_units;
275:             wz += 0.1;
276:         }
277:         assert!(landing_seen, "ordinary flight never reaches its landing");
278:     }
279: 
280:     #[test]
281:     fn vestibule_is_flat_and_endless_ascent_outclimbs_the_landing() {
282:         assert_eq!(
283:             profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5).floor_units,
284:             0.0,
285:             "vestibule must stay walkable from the corridor"
286:         );
287:         let deep = profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, STAIR_DEPTH - 0.2);
288:         assert!(
289:             deep.floor_units > LANDING_UNITS,
290:             "endless ascent stops at an ordinary landing"
291:         );
292:         assert!(!deep.light, "the top of an endless flight must be unlit");
293:     }
294: }
````

````rust
  1: //! The pure macro-scale world planner: an infinite graph, one cell at a time.
  2: //!
  3: //! [`plan_macro_cell`] is a pure function of `(seed, cell id, red-room
  4: //! scale)` — the top of the planning hierarchy documented in
  5: //! [`crate::domain::entities::world_topology`]. It owns three jobs:
  6: //!
  7: //! 1. **Parameter fields.** [`sample_fields`] turns the noise port into
  8: //!    multi-octave `[0, 1]` fields (openness, vertical pressure, anomaly
  9: //!    pressure, ...). This is the *only* legitimate role of fractal math in
 10: //!    the world: it chooses where the building's rules change; it never
 11: //!    substitutes for an architectural decision.
 12: //! 2. **Graph events.** Red rooms are planned here as separated events on
 13: //!    the macro lattice (a deterministic tournament gives every event a
 14: //!    cooldown radius), and vertical links reserve stairwell footprints
 15: //!    where vertical pressure is high.
 16: //! 3. **Continuity contracts.** Primary-route portals are derived from the
 17: //!    *edge's* lattice coordinate, so both neighbors of an edge compute the
 18: //!    identical crossing — the invariant that lets circulation chain across
 19: //!    regions forever.
 20: //!
 21: //! Everything downstream (region planner, anomaly planner, voxelizer)
 22: //! consumes these obligations; nothing here writes a voxel or knows a chunk
 23: //! size. Determinism is testable: see the 5×5 snapshot test at the bottom.
 24: 
 25: use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{
 26:     MACRO_CELL_SIZE, MacroCell, MacroCellId, MacroFields, PlaceKind, Portal,
 27:     REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL, RedRoomEvent, VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind, WorldNode,
 28: };
 29: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 30: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
 31: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 32: 
 33: /// Side of a region, world units. Kept in lockstep with
 34: /// `region_plan::REGION_SIZE` by a compile-time-adjacent test below.
 35: const REGION_SIZE: f32 = MACRO_CELL_SIZE / REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL as f32;
 36: 
 37: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38: // Shared 32-bit deterministic hashing.
 39: //
 40: // All architectural "randomness" in region planning flows through these two
 41: // functions. They live here — at the top of the planning hierarchy — and
 42: // `region_plan` imports them, so the macro graph and the regional plans can
 43: // never disagree about a shared derivation (portals, most importantly).
 44: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45: 
 46: pub(crate) fn mix(mut h: u32) -> u32 {
 47:     h ^= h >> 16;
 48:     h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
 49:     h ^= h >> 13;
 50:     h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2_AE35);
 51:     h ^= h >> 16;
 52:     h
 53: }
 54: 
 55: /// Hash of a seed plus any number of integer keys, uniform in [0, 1).
 56: pub(crate) fn hash01(seed: u32, keys: &[i64]) -> f32 {
 57:     let mut h = mix(seed ^ 0x9E37_79B9);
 58:     for &k in keys {
 59:         h = mix(h ^ (k as u32)).wrapping_add(mix((k >> 32) as u32));
 60:     }
 61:     (mix(h) >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
 62: }
 63: 
 64: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 65: // Portals: the cross-region continuity contract.
 66: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 67: 
 68: /// World Z of the primary-route portal on the vertical edge
 69: /// `x = edge_x * REGION_SIZE` of region row `row_z`. Both regions sharing the
 70: /// edge derive the same value — this function is the single source of truth
 71: /// (the region planner routes its main spine between two of these).
 72: pub fn primary_portal_z(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> f32 {
 73:     let f = 0.30 + 0.40 * hash01(seed, &[0x0E1, edge_x, row_z]);
 74:     snap((row_z as f32 + f) * REGION_SIZE)
 75: }
 76: 
 77: /// Snap to the 0.4 u plan lattice (one coarse voxel).
 78: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 79:     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
 80: }
 81: 
 82: fn portal(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> Portal {
 83:     Portal {
 84:         id: hash(seed, 0x7047_A100, edge_x, row_z),
 85:         edge_x,
 86:         row_z,
 87:         at: Position::new(
 88:             edge_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 89:             primary_portal_z(seed, edge_x, row_z),
 90:         ),
 91:     }
 92: }
 93: 
 94: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 95: // Parameter fields.
 96: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 97: 
 98: /// One multi-octave field in [0, 1]:
 99: /// `F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ · N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`, rescaled and clamped. The provider's
100: /// base wavelength is ~20 u, so `20 / wavelength` stretches each octave.
101: fn field(
102:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
103:     seed: u32,
104:     salt: u32,
105:     wx: f32,
106:     wz: f32,
107:     wavelengths: [f32; 3],
108:     weights: [f32; 3],
109: ) -> f32 {
110:     let mut sum = 0.0;
111:     let mut norm = 0.0;
112:     for (octave, (&wavelength, &weight)) in wavelengths.iter().zip(weights.iter()).enumerate() {
113:         let s = 20.0 / wavelength;
114:         sum += weight
115:             * noise.evaluate_2d(
116:                 seed ^ salt.wrapping_add((octave as u32).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9)),
117:                 Position::new(wx * s, wz * s),
118:             );
119:         norm += weight;
120:     }
121:     // Octave sums cluster toward zero; stretch before biasing to [0, 1] so
122:     // thresholds see a usable spread instead of everything at 0.5.
123:     ((sum / norm) * 0.8 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
124: }
125: 
126: /// The institution-age field alone — how long this stretch of the building
127: /// has been rotting. Split out of [`sample_fields`] (and used by it, so the
128: /// two can never disagree) because per-column callers need one field, not
129: /// six: old territory keeps fewer of its fluorescents alive.
130: pub fn institution_age_at(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
131:     field(
132:         noise,
133:         seed,
134:         0xF1E1_0003,
135:         wx,
136:         wz,
137:         [260.0, 90.0, 30.0],
138:         [1.0, 0.5, 0.25],
139:     )
140: }
141: 
142: /// Sample every macro parameter field at one world point. Pure and
143: /// world-space: two callers asking about the same point always agree,
144: /// regardless of which cell, region, or chunk asked.
145: pub fn sample_fields(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> MacroFields {
146:     MacroFields {
147:         openness: field(
148:             noise,
149:             seed,
150:             0xF1E1_0001,
151:             wx,
152:             wz,
153:             [350.0, 130.0, 45.0],
154:             [1.0, 0.5, 0.2],
155:         ),
156:         vertical_pressure: field(
157:             noise,
158:             seed,
159:             0xF1E1_0002,
160:             wx,
161:             wz,
162:             [520.0, 170.0, 60.0],
163:             [1.0, 0.4, 0.15],
164:         ),
165:         institution_age: institution_age_at(noise, seed, wx, wz),
166:         anomaly_pressure: field(
167:             noise,
168:             seed,
169:             0xF1E1_0004,
170:             wx,
171:             wz,
172:             [620.0, 210.0, 70.0],
173:             [1.0, 0.35, 0.1],
174:         ),
175:         redroom_pressure: field(
176:             noise,
177:             seed,
178:             0xF1E1_0005,
179:             wx,
180:             wz,
181:             [700.0, 230.0, 80.0],
182:             [1.0, 0.3, 0.1],
183:         ),
184:         style_blend: field(
185:             noise,
186:             seed,
187:             0xF1E1_0006,
188:             wx,
189:             wz,
190:             [420.0, 140.0, 50.0],
191:             [1.0, 0.45, 0.2],
192:         ),
193:     }
194: }
195: 
196: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
197: // Red rooms as separated graph events.
198: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
199: 
200: /// Cooldown radius in macro cells (Chebyshev). Two committed events are
201: /// always at least one full macro cell (160 u) apart, so red rooms read as
202: /// rare landmarks instead of a recurring biome.
203: const RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS: i64 = 1;
204: 
205: /// Base per-cell candidate chance at `red_room_scale == 1.0`.
206: const RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE: f32 = 0.32;
207: 
208: /// The candidate score of one macro cell: `Some(score)` if the cell wants a
209: /// red room this epoch, lower score = higher priority in the tournament.
210: fn red_room_candidate(
211:     seed: u32,
212:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
213:     cell: MacroCellId,
214:     red_room_scale: f32,
215: ) -> Option<f32> {
216:     if red_room_scale <= 0.0 {
217:         return None;
218:     }
219:     let center = cell.center();
220:     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z).redroom_pressure;
221:     let score = unit(hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0011, cell.x, cell.z));
222:     // Pressure clusters events without ever making them uniform or certain.
223:     let chance = (RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE * red_room_scale).min(0.85) * (0.35 + 0.65 * pressure);
224:     (score < chance).then_some(score)
225: }
226: 
227: /// The red-room event a macro cell *wins*, if any. A candidate cell fires
228: /// only when no candidate within the separation radius beats its score
229: /// (ties broken by lattice coordinate), so any two firing cells are more
230: /// than the separation radius apart — a deterministic Matérn-style
231: /// exclusion, computed locally without global state.
232: pub fn red_room_event_for_cell(
233:     seed: u32,
234:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
235:     cell: MacroCellId,
236:     red_room_scale: f32,
237: ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
238:     let mine = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale)?;
239:     for dz in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
240:         for dx in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
241:             if dx == 0 && dz == 0 {
242:                 continue;
243:             }
244:             let rival_cell = MacroCellId::new(cell.x + dx, cell.z + dz);
245:             if let Some(rival) = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, rival_cell, red_room_scale) {
246:                 let rival_wins = (rival, rival_cell.x, rival_cell.z) < (mine, cell.x, cell.z);
247:                 if rival_wins {
248:                     return None;
249:                 }
250:             }
251:         }
252:     }
253:     // The event targets exactly one of the cell's 2×2 regions.
254:     let pick = hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0022, cell.x, cell.z);
255:     let region = (
256:         cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + (pick & 1) as i64,
257:         cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + ((pick >> 1) & 1) as i64,
258:     );
259:     Some(RedRoomEvent {
260:         id: hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0033, cell.x, cell.z),
261:         region,
262:         score: mine,
263:     })
264: }
265: 
266: /// Does a red-room event target this specific region? This is the query the
267: /// region planner asks; the answer is independent of which chunk, region, or
268: /// LOD triggered the plan.
269: pub fn red_room_event_for_region(
270:     seed: u32,
271:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
272:     region_x: i64,
273:     region_z: i64,
274:     red_room_scale: f32,
275: ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
276:     red_room_event_for_cell(
277:         seed,
278:         noise,
279:         MacroCellId::of_region(region_x, region_z),
280:         red_room_scale,
281:     )
282:     .filter(|event| event.region == (region_x, region_z))
283: }
284: 
285: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
286: // Vertical links.
287: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
288: 
289: /// The vertical link reserved inside one region, if any. Stairwells are
290: /// planned per region so the region planner can honor the reservation while
291: /// laying out its assemblies; the *kind* mix leans ordinary, with the
292: /// endless variants appearing only under high vertical pressure.
293: pub fn vertical_link_for_region(
294:     seed: u32,
295:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
296:     region_x: i64,
297:     region_z: i64,
298: ) -> Option<VerticalLink> {
299:     let center_x = (region_x as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
300:     let center_z = (region_z as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
301:     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z).vertical_pressure;
302:     let gate = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0001, region_x, region_z));
303:     if gate >= 0.06 + 0.30 * pressure * pressure {
304:         return None;
305:     }
306: 
307:     let kind_roll = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0002, region_x, region_z));
308:     let (kind, to_elevation) = if kind_roll < 0.55 {
309:         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
310:     } else if kind_roll < 0.75 && pressure > 0.55 {
311:         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, 1)
312:     } else if kind_roll < 0.90 && pressure > 0.55 {
313:         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessDescent, -1)
314:     } else if kind_roll < 0.97 {
315:         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
316:     } else {
317:         (VerticalLinkKind::ServiceShaft, -1)
318:     };
319: 
320:     // Anchor well inside the region so the stair mass never has to fight the
321:     // edge margin. The region planner snaps the actual footprint to its
322:     // corridor network; the anchor only says "near here".
323:     let ax = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0003, region_x, region_z));
324:     let az = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0004, region_x, region_z));
325:     Some(VerticalLink {
326:         id: hash(seed, 0x57A1_0005, region_x, region_z),
327:         kind,
328:         region: (region_x, region_z),
329:         anchor: Position::new(
330:             snap((region_x as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * ax) * REGION_SIZE),
331:             snap((region_z as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * az) * REGION_SIZE),
332:         ),
333:         from_elevation: 0,
334:         to_elevation,
335:     })
336: }
337: 
338: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
339: // The cell planner.
340: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
341: 
342: fn classify_region(
343:     seed: u32,
344:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
345:     region: (i64, i64),
346:     red_room_event: Option<&RedRoomEvent>,
347:     vertical: Option<&VerticalLink>,
348: ) -> PlaceKind {
349:     if red_room_event.is_some_and(|event| event.region == region) {
350:         return PlaceKind::RedRoomEncounter;
351:     }
352:     if vertical.is_some() {
353:         return PlaceKind::Stairwell;
354:     }
355:     let center_x = (region.0 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
356:     let center_z = (region.1 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
357:     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z);
358:     if fields.openness > 0.66 {
359:         if fields.vertical_pressure > 0.60 {
360:             PlaceKind::Atrium
361:         } else {
362:             PlaceKind::OpenPlate
363:         }
364:     } else {
365:         PlaceKind::Warren
366:     }
367: }
368: 
369: /// Plan one macro cell of the infinite world graph.
370: ///
371: /// Pure: the same `(seed, cell, red_room_scale)` always yields the same
372: /// graph, and shared contracts (portals, red-room tournaments) agree with
373: /// every neighboring cell's own computation. `red_room_scale` is the
374: /// world-wide `anomalies.frequency * anomalies.red_rooms` product; passing
375: /// different scales for different cells of one world is a caller bug.
376: pub fn plan_macro_cell(
377:     seed: u32,
378:     cell: MacroCellId,
379:     red_room_scale: f32,
380:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
381: ) -> MacroCell {
382:     let center = cell.center();
383:     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z);
384:     let red_room_event = red_room_event_for_cell(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale);
385: 
386:     let region_x0 = cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
387:     let region_z0 = cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
388: 
389:     let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity((REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL) as usize);
390:     let mut vertical_links = Vec::new();
391:     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
392:         for dx in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
393:             let region = (region_x0 + dx, region_z0 + dz);
394:             let vertical = vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, region.0, region.1);
395:             nodes.push(WorldNode {
396:                 id: hash(seed, 0x40DE_0001, region.0, region.1),
397:                 region,
398:                 kind: classify_region(
399:                     seed,
400:                     noise,
401:                     region,
402:                     red_room_event.as_ref(),
403:                     vertical.as_ref(),
404:                 ),
405:                 elevation: 0,
406:             });
407:             vertical_links.extend(vertical);
408:         }
409:     }
410: 
411:     // Every vertical edge the cell's regions touch: interior, west boundary,
412:     // and east boundary. Boundary portals are recomputed identically by the
413:     // neighboring cell (asserted by test below).
414:     let mut portals = Vec::new();
415:     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
416:         for edge in 0..=REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
417:             portals.push(portal(seed, region_x0 + edge, region_z0 + dz));
418:         }
419:     }
420: 
421:     MacroCell {
422:         id: cell,
423:         fields,
424:         nodes,
425:         portals,
426:         vertical_links,
427:         red_room_event,
428:     }
429: }

518:     fn digest(text: &str) -> u64 {
519:         let mut h = 0xCBF2_9CE4_8422_2325u64;
520:         for byte in text.bytes() {
521:             h = mix64(h ^ byte as u64);
522:         }
523:         h
524:     }
525: 
526:     /// The same seed, coordinates and scale must always produce the same
527:     /// graph — byte for byte. If this digest changes, the world changed for
528:     /// every player: update the constant only for an *intentional*
529:     /// generation change, and say so in the commit message.
530:     #[test]
531:     fn five_by_five_topology_snapshot_is_stable() {
532:         let text = snapshot_5x5();

535:             digest(&text),
536:             SNAPSHOT_DIGEST,
537:             "macro topology for seed {SEED} changed; snapshot follows:\n{text}"
538:         );
539:     }
````

````rust
 36: fn handle_client(mut stream: TcpStream) {

 39:         if bytes_read == 0 {

 48:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
 49:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/maze");
 50: 
 51:             let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
 52:             let mut chunk_z = 0.0;

 56:                 let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
 57:                 for param in query.split('&') {
 58:                     let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
 59:                     if key_val.len() == 2 {
 60:                         match key_val[0] {
 61:                             "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 62:                             "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 63:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
 64:                             _ => {}
 65:                         }
 66:                     }
 67:                 }
 68:             }
 69: 
 70:             let config = if spec == "low" {

 72:             } else {
 73:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()

 76:             let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();

 83:             // Adapt to Web Format (greedy meshed faces)

 87:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n{}",
 88:                 json.len(),

109:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],

111:                         }

113:                 }

126: 
127:             // Generate chunk at position with GeneratorConfig
128:             let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
129: 
130:             // Adapt to Web Format using SVO representation
131:             let depth = config.svo_depth();
132:             let world_size = config.svo_world_size();
133:             let binary = WebRendererAdapter::to_octree_binary(
134:                 &chunk,
135:                 depth,
136:                 world_size,
137:                 config.voxel_scale,
138:                 config.chunk_size,
139:             );
140: 
141:             let header = format!(
142:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
143:                 binary.len()
144:             );
145:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + binary.len());
146:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
147:             response.extend_from_slice(&binary);
148:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
149:         } else if request_line.starts_with("GET ") {
150:             // Static file service for the wasm front end (and the legacy page).
151:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
152:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/");
153:             let path = url.split('?').next().unwrap_or("/");
154:             serve_static(&mut stream, path);
155:         } else {

157:             let _ = stream.write_all(error.as_bytes());
158:         }
159:     }

162: /// Maps a URL path to a file under `static/` and serves it with the correct
163: /// MIME type. `application/wasm` matters: browsers refuse to instantiate
164: /// wasm streams served under the wrong content type.
165: fn serve_static(stream: &mut TcpStream, url_path: &str) {
166:     let relative = match url_path {
167:         "/" | "/index.html" => "index.html",
168:         "/legacy" => "legacy_threejs.html",
169:         other => other.trim_start_matches('/'),
170:     };
171: 
172:     // Path traversal guard: reject anything trying to escape `static/`.
173:     if relative.split('/').any(|seg| seg == "..") || relative.contains('\\') {
174:         let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n\r\n");
175:         return;
176:     }
177: 
178:     let file_path = format!("static/{}", relative);
179:     match fs::read(&file_path) {
180:         Ok(body) => {
181:             let mime = match file_path.rsplit('.').next() {
182:                 Some("html") => "text/html; charset=utf-8",
183:                 Some("js") | Some("mjs") => "text/javascript",
184:                 Some("wasm") => "application/wasm",
185:                 Some("css") => "text/css",
186:                 Some("json") => "application/json",
187:                 Some("png") => "image/png",
188:                 _ => "application/octet-stream",
189:             };
190:             let header = format!(
191:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
192:                 mime,
193:                 body.len()
194:             );
195:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + body.len());
196:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
197:             response.extend_from_slice(&body);
198:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
199:         }
200:         Err(_) => {
201:             let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\nFile not found.");
202:         }
203:     }
204: }
````

````javascript
  1: // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, running the
  2: // full chunk pipeline off the main thread. The onmessage handler is
  3: // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
  4: // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
  5: // promise chain.
  6: //
  7: // Protocol (main -> worker):
  8: //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
  9: //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality } one chunk order;
 10: //                                                        reality is Uint32Array
 11: // (worker -> main):
 12: //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality, ms, buf }
 13: //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
 14: //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality, message }
 15: //                                   one request failed and may be retried
 16: //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
 17: import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";

 19: let wasmReady = null;
 20: function ensureWasm() {
 21:   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
 22:   return wasmReady;
 23: }
 24: 
 25: let queue = Promise.resolve();
 26: 
 27: function errorMessage(error) {
 28:   if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
 29:   return String(error);
 30: }
 31: 
 32: function reportFailure(message, error) {
 33:   const description = errorMessage(error);
 34:   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
 35:   try {
 36:     if (message?.type === "gen") {
 37:       postMessage({
 38:         type: "failed",
 39:         requestId: message.requestId,
 40:         ox: message.ox,
 41:         oz: message.oz,
 42:         level: message.level,
 43:         lod: message.lod,
 44:         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
 45:         message: description,
 46:       });
 47:     } else {
 48:       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
 49:     }
 50:   } catch (reportError) {
 51:     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
 52:     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
 53:     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
 54:   }
 55: }
 56: 
 57: async function processMessage(message) {
 58:   await ensureWasm();
 59:   if (message.type === "init") {
 60:     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
 61:     return;
 62:   }
 63:   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
 64: 
 65:   const t0 = performance.now();
 66:   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
 67:   const bytes = worker_generate(
 68:     message.requestId >>> 0,
 69:     message.ox,
 70:     message.oz,
 71:     message.level,
 72:     message.lod,
 73:     reality
 74:   );
 75:   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
 76:   console.debug(
 77:     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
 78:   );
 79:   postMessage(
 80:     {
 81:       type: "done",
 82:       requestId: message.requestId,
 83:       ox: message.ox,
 84:       oz: message.oz,
 85:       level: message.level,
 86:       lod: message.lod,
 87:       reality,
 88:       ms,
 89:       buf: bytes.buffer,
 90:     },
 91:     [bytes.buffer]
 92:   );
 93: }
 94: 
 95: onmessage = (event) => {
 96:   const message = event.data;
 97:   // Catch each queue item independently. A failed request must not leave the
 98:   // promise chain rejected, which would silently skip every later request.
 99:   queue = queue
100:     .then(() => processMessage(message))
101:     .catch((error) => reportFailure(message, error));
102: };
````

````rust
  1: //! Write square splats into a reusable, depth-tested CPU framebuffer.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module knows only pixels. Traversal decides *what* to draw and owns
  4: //! frame policy; the target clips a square splat, performs fine depth tests,
  5: //! enforces the caller's remaining write budget exactly, and maintains the
  6: //! coarse occlusion summary when requested.

 17:     depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
 18:     color: [u8; 3],
 19:     /// Overlapping square reconstruction kernels can cover the same physical
 20:     /// coplanar face. An emitter owns that exact material tie, regardless of
 21:     /// traversal order; ordinary and genuinely farther samples never do.

 23: }
 24:

 26:     pub(super) fn new(cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, depth: f32, color: [u8; 3]) -> Self {
 27:         Self {
 28:             center: [cx, cy],
 29:             half,
 30:             depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth::constant(depth),
 31:             color,
 32:             equal_depth_wins: false,
 33:         }
 34:     }
 35: 
 36:     pub(super) fn with_surface_depth(mut self, depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth) -> Self {
 37:         self.depth = depth;
 38:         self
 39:     }

 42:         self.equal_depth_wins = true;
 43:         self
 44:     }
 45: }
 46: 
 47: /// Result of one square-splat write.
 48: pub(super) struct SplatWrite {
 49:     /// Fine-depth-tested pixels whose color and depth changed.
 50:     pub(super) pixel_writes: usize,
 51:     /// A further depth-passing pixel existed after the write budget ran out.
 52:     pub(super) budget_exhausted: bool,
 53: }
 54: 
 55: /// Reusable CPU render target. Reciprocal depth is affine under perspective,
 56: /// so zero means uncovered and larger finite values are nearer. A zero coarse
 57: /// value likewise means that the tile is not yet fully covered.
 58: pub(super) struct DepthTestedSplatTarget {
 59:     width: usize,
 60:     height: usize,
 61:     rgba: Vec<u8>,
 62:     reciprocal_depth: Vec<f32>,
 63:     /// Smallest (farthest) reciprocal fine depth in each fully covered tile.
 64:     coarse_reciprocal_depth: Vec<f32>,
 65:     /// Number of pixels that have transitioned from uncovered to covered.
 66:     coarse_filled: Vec<usize>,
 67:     coarse_width: usize,
 68:     coarse_height: usize,
 69: }
 70: 
 71: impl DepthTestedSplatTarget {
 72:     pub(super) fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {
 73:         let mut target = Self {
 74:             width: 0,
 75:             height: 0,
 76:             rgba: Vec::new(),
 77:             reciprocal_depth: Vec::new(),
 78:             coarse_reciprocal_depth: Vec::new(),
 79:             coarse_filled: Vec::new(),

 84:         target

 87:     pub(super) fn resize(&mut self, width: usize, height: usize) {
 88:         self.width = width.max(1);
 89:         self.height = height.max(1);

 91:         self.reciprocal_depth = vec![0.0; self.width * self.height];
 92:         self.coarse_width = self.width.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);
 93:         self.coarse_height = self.height.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);

108:     }

110:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self, background: [u8; 3]) {
111:         for pixel in self.rgba.chunks_exact_mut(4) {
112:             pixel[0] = background[0];
113:             pixel[1] = background[1];
114:             pixel[2] = background[2];

122:     /// Exact fine-depth query for an unshaded square splat.

124:     /// Traversal uses this immediately before fixture, hero, and flashlight

126:     /// every pixel, so skipping those radiance calculations cannot change the

128:     #[cfg(test)]
129:     pub(super) fn splat_may_contribute(&self, center: [f32; 2], half: f32, depth: f32) -> bool {
130:         self.request_may_contribute(&SquareSplat::new(center[0], center[1], half, depth, [0; 3]))

133:     /// Fine-depth query for a projected physical surface. The exact same

135:     pub(super) fn surface_splat_may_contribute(&self, splat: &SquareSplat) -> bool {

137:     }
````
