````rust
139:     fn request_may_contribute(&self, splat: &SquareSplat) -> bool {
140:         let [x0, x1, y0, y1] = self.clipped_square_bounds(splat.center, splat.half);
141:         for y in y0..y1 {
142:             let row = y * self.width;
143:             for x in x0..x1 {
144:                 let Some(reciprocal_depth) = splat
145:                     .depth
146:                     .reciprocal_at_pixel([x as f32 + 0.5, y as f32 + 0.5])
147:                 else {
148:                     continue;
149:                 };
150:                 let stored = self.reciprocal_depth[row + x];
151:                 if reciprocal_depth > stored
152:                     || (splat.equal_depth_wins && reciprocal_depth == stored)
153:                 {
154:                     return true;
155:                 }
156:             }
157:         }
158:         false
159:     }
160: 
161:     /// Fills a depth-tested square. `half` is its half-extent in pixels.
162:     ///
163:     /// The budget check lives inside the depth-passing branch: rejected
164:     /// pixels cost no writes, while the first additional visible pixel after
165:     /// the budget is exhausted stops the splat and reports exhaustion.
166:     pub(super) fn write_splat(
167:         &mut self,
168:         splat: SquareSplat,
169:         write_budget: usize,
170:         maintain_coarse: bool,
171:     ) -> SplatWrite {
172:         // Traversal normally subdivides large footprints. Camera-plane and
173:         // budget fallbacks remain legal here; clipping plus `write_budget`
174:         // bounds their work without changing their requested coverage.
175:         let [x0, x1, y0, y1] = self.clipped_square_bounds(splat.center, splat.half);
176: 
177:         let mut pixel_writes = 0;
178:         let mut budget_exhausted = false;
179:         'pixels: for y in y0..y1 {
180:             let row = y * self.width;
181:             for x in x0..x1 {
182:                 let idx = row + x;
183:                 let Some(reciprocal_depth) = splat
184:                     .depth
185:                     .reciprocal_at_pixel([x as f32 + 0.5, y as f32 + 0.5])
186:                 else {
187:                     continue;
188:                 };
189:                 let stored = self.reciprocal_depth[idx];
190:                 if reciprocal_depth > stored
191:                     || (splat.equal_depth_wins && reciprocal_depth == stored)
192:                 {
193:                     if pixel_writes >= write_budget {
194:                         budget_exhausted = true;
195:                         break 'pixels;
196:                     }
197:                     let was_uncovered = stored == 0.0;
198:                     self.reciprocal_depth[idx] = reciprocal_depth;
199:                     let rgba_index = idx * 4;
200:                     self.rgba[rgba_index] = splat.color[0];
201:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 1] = splat.color[1];
202:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 2] = splat.color[2];
203:                     pixel_writes += 1;
204:                     if maintain_coarse && was_uncovered {
205:                         self.record_first_coverage(x, y);
206:                     }
207:                 }
208:             }
209:         }
210: 
211:         SplatWrite {
212:             pixel_writes,
213:             budget_exhausted,
214:         }
215:     }
216: 
217:     fn clipped_square_bounds(&self, center: [f32; 2], half: f32) -> [usize; 4] {
218:         // Traversal normally subdivides to the configured maximum radius,
219:         // but camera-plane intersections and explicit budget fallbacks can
220:         // legitimately cover more than 32 pixels.  The framebuffer is
221:         // already a finite clip bound and the caller supplies an exact write
222:         // budget, so silently shrinking the requested footprint would only
223:         // create holes.  A malformed infinity conservatively covers the
224:         // finite target instead of entering float-to-integer edge cases.
225:         let half = if half.is_finite() {
226:             half.max(0.0)
227:         } else {
228:             self.width.max(self.height) as f32
229:         };
230:         [
231:             (center[0] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize,
232:             ((center[0] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.width),
233:             (center[1] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize,
234:             ((center[1] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.height),
235:         ]
236:     }
237: 
238:     /// True only when every coarse tile under the screen rect is fully
239:     /// covered and its farthest stored pixel is nearer than `z_near`.
240:     #[cfg(test)]
241:     pub(super) fn coarse_occludes(&self, px: f32, py: f32, proj_radius: f32, z_near: f32) -> bool {
242:         self.coarse_rect_occludes([px, py], [proj_radius, proj_radius], z_near)
243:     }
244: 
245:     /// Rectangular form used by the exact projected AABB footprint. Keeping
246:     /// X/Y extents separate avoids turning a wide wall or shallow floor into
247:     /// an unnecessarily large square HZ query.
248:     pub(super) fn coarse_rect_occludes(
249:         &self,
250:         center: [f32; 2],
251:         half_extent: [f32; 2],
252:         z_near: f32,
253:     ) -> bool {
254:         let lower_tile = |value: f32, tiles: usize| {
255:             ((value.max(0.0) as usize) / COARSE_TILE).min(tiles.saturating_sub(1))
256:         };
257:         // Upper bounds are exclusive after `ceil`, matching the fine
258:         // `x0..x1`/`y0..y1` loops. Dividing that exclusive coordinate
259:         // directly includes the next tile at every exact 8-pixel boundary.
260:         let upper_tile = |value: f32, tiles: usize| {
261:             ((value.ceil().max(0.0) as usize).saturating_sub(1) / COARSE_TILE)
262:                 .min(tiles.saturating_sub(1))
263:         };
264:         let x0 = lower_tile((center[0] - half_extent[0]).floor(), self.coarse_width);
265:         let x1 = upper_tile(center[0] + half_extent[0], self.coarse_width);
266:         let y0 = lower_tile((center[1] - half_extent[1]).floor(), self.coarse_height);
267:         let y1 = upper_tile(center[1] + half_extent[1], self.coarse_height);
268:         if !z_near.is_finite() || z_near <= 0.0 {
269:             return false;
270:         }
271:         let reciprocal_near = z_near.recip();
272: 
273:         for tile_y in y0..=y1 {
274:             for tile_x in x0..=x1 {
275:                 if reciprocal_near
276:                     >= self.coarse_reciprocal_depth[tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x]
277:                 {
278:                     return false;
279:                 }
280:             }
281:         }
282:         true
283:     }
284: 
285:     /// Records an infinity-to-finite transition. A tile is scanned exactly
286:     /// once, when its final uncovered pixel becomes covered. Later depth
287:     /// writes only decrease values, so the stored maximum becomes a stale
288:     /// upper bound: conservative for rejection and free to maintain.
289:     fn record_first_coverage(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize) {
290:         let tile_x = x / COARSE_TILE;
291:         let tile_y = y / COARSE_TILE;
292:         let tile_index = tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x;
293:         self.coarse_filled[tile_index] += 1;
294:         if self.coarse_filled[tile_index] == self.tile_pixel_count(tile_x, tile_y) {
295:             self.coarse_reciprocal_depth[tile_index] =
296:                 self.scan_tile_farthest_reciprocal_depth(tile_x, tile_y);
297:         }
298:     }
299: 
300:     fn tile_pixel_count(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> usize {
301:         let width = ((tile_x + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.width) - tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
302:         let height = ((tile_y + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.height) - tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
303:         width * height
304:     }
305: 
306:     fn scan_tile_farthest_reciprocal_depth(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> f32 {
307:         let x0 = tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
308:         let x1 = (x0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.width);
309:         let y0 = tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
310:         let y1 = (y0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.height);
311:         let mut farthest = f32::INFINITY;
312:         for y in y0..y1 {
313:             for x in x0..x1 {
314:                 farthest = farthest.min(self.reciprocal_depth[y * self.width + x]);
315:             }
316:         }
317:         farthest
318:     }
319: }
````

````rust
  1: //! SVO atlas decoding and MIP filtering.
  2: //!
  3: //! The atlas is the GPU-serialized octree shared with every other renderer:
  4: //! 4 `u32` per node (see the core's `OctreeGpuSerializer`). This module owns
  5: //! the two pieces of *data preparation* the splatter needs:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`decode_node`] — one node's texels → leaf payload or child pointer.
  8: //! * [`build_mips`] — a per-node pyramid of filtered attributes (average
  9: //!   linear albedo, max light, occupancy), computed once per atlas upload so the
 10: //!   LOD path can draw a whole subtree as a single splat.
 11: 
 12: use std::ops::Range;
 13: 
 14: use super::decode_srgb_albedo::decode_packed_albedo;
 15: use super::surface_geometry::SurfaceExposure;
 16: 
 17: /// Voxel type constants shared with the core serializer.
 18: pub const VOXEL_AIR: u32 = 0;
 19: 
 20: /// Single CPU-renderer predicate mirroring the domain's emissive palette.
 21: /// Keeping this beside atlas decoding prevents traversal and shading from
 22: /// growing renderer-specific material lists.
 23: pub fn is_emissive(voxel_type: u32) -> bool {
 24:     u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok().is_some_and(|material| {
 25:         vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material)
 26:     })
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Authored emitted-radiance scale for one emissive material.
 30: ///
 31: /// This is material data, not a color heuristic. Keeping it next to the
 32: /// palette predicate lets traversal carry only the compact material id while
 33: /// the shading boundary receives the exact scalar used by fixture extraction.
 34: pub fn emission_strength(voxel_type: u32) -> Option<f32> {
 35:     vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::material_emission_strength(
 36:         u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok()?,
 37:     )
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /// A decoded atlas node. Exactly one of the two shapes is meaningful:
 41: /// leaves carry material/color/light, while interiors carry
 42: /// `child_base`/`child_mask`.
 43: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 44: pub struct DecodedNode {
 45:     pub is_leaf: bool,
 46:     pub child_base: usize,
 47:     pub child_mask: u32,
 48:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 49:     /// Leaf albedo in the renderer's 0..255 reference range. Production CPU
 50:     /// traversal uses the upload-prepared linear value instead; the encoded
 51:     /// form remains part of the shared decoder for diagnostic renderers.
 52:     pub color: [f32; 3],
 53:     /// Leaf scalar diffuse-fill level, 0..15.
 54:     pub light: f32,
 55:     /// Quantized colored diffuse-fill channels, 0..15.
 56:     pub baked_rgb: [u8; 3],
 57:     /// Exact authored faces open to air, decoded from the serialized neighbor
 58:     /// occlusion mask.
 59:     pub exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 60: }
 61: 
 62: /// Reads node `node_idx` out of the texel stream. Returns `None` when the
 63: /// index runs past the atlas (defensive: a truncated upload must degrade to
 64: /// missing geometry, not out-of-bounds panics).
 65: pub fn decode_node(atlas: &[u32], node_idx: usize) -> Option<DecodedNode> {
 66:     let t = node_idx * 4;
 67:     if t + 3 >= atlas.len() {
 68:         return None;
 69:     }
 70:     let is_leaf = atlas[t] == 1;
 71:     if is_leaf {
 72:         let packed_color = atlas[t + 2];
 73:         let packed_lighting = atlas[t + 3];
 74:         Some(DecodedNode {
 75:             is_leaf: true,
 76:             child_base: 0,
 77:             child_mask: 0,
 78:             voxel_type: atlas[t + 1],
 79:             color: [
 80:                 ((packed_color >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
 81:                 ((packed_color >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
 82:                 (packed_color & 0xFF) as f32,
 83:             ],
 84:             light: (packed_lighting & 0xFF) as f32,
 85:             baked_rgb: decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting),
 86:             exposure: decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting),
 87:         })
 88:     } else {
 89:         Some(DecodedNode {
 90:             is_leaf: false,
 91:             child_base: atlas[t + 1] as usize,
 92:             child_mask: atlas[t + 2],
 93:             voxel_type: 0,
 94:             color: [0.0; 3],
 95:             light: 0.0,
 96:             baked_rgb: [0; 3],
 97:             exposure: SurfaceExposure::NONE,
 98:         })
 99:     }
100: }
101: 
102: /// Per-node MIP-filtered attributes, rebuilt on every atlas upload.
103: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq)]
104: pub struct MipNode {
105:     /// Occupancy-weighted linear albedo of the subtree. Decoding before the
106:     /// average is both physically correct and removes sRGB powers per splat.
107:     pub linear_albedo: [f32; 3],
108:     /// Occupancy-weighted colored diffuse fill (0..15). A maximum would smear
109:     /// one bright receiver across the entire collapsed subtree.
110:     pub baked_rgb: [f32; 3],
111:     /// Fraction of the subtree volume that is solid, 0..1.
112:     pub occupancy: f32,
113:     /// Material owning the largest occupied fraction of this subtree.
114:     pub dominant_voxel_type: u32,
115:     /// Occupied fraction represented by `dominant_voxel_type`.
116:     dominant_coverage: f32,
117:     /// Fraction of the subtree occupied by emissive material.
118:     pub emissive_coverage: f32,
119:     /// Emitted radiance averaged over the whole subtree volume. Ordinary LOD
120:     /// refuses to collapse emissive subtrees; this keeps a bounded hard-cap
121:     /// fallback visible instead of silently deleting a panel.
122:     pub emitted_radiance_density: [f32; 3],
123:     /// Directional exposed surface area prepared from exact leaf masks.
124:     pub exposed_area: SurfaceExposure,
125: }
126: 
127: fn decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting: u32) -> [u8; 3] {
128:     [
129:         ((packed_lighting >> 16) & 0xF) as u8,
130:         ((packed_lighting >> 20) & 0xF) as u8,
131:         ((packed_lighting >> 24) & 0xF) as u8,
132:     ]
133: }
134: 
135: fn decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting: u32) -> SurfaceExposure {
136:     SurfaceExposure::from_neighbor_occlusion(((packed_lighting >> 8) & 0x3F) as u8)
137: }
138: 
139: /// Bottom-up MIP filtering over the whole atlas. Node order in the arena is
140: /// not guaranteed (`SparseVoxelOctree::set` appends children after parents,
141: /// `BuildOctreeUseCase` pushes the root last), so each subtree is resolved by
142: /// memoized recursion instead of a single directional sweep. Still O(n): every
143: /// node is computed exactly once.
144: pub fn build_mips(atlas: &[u32]) -> Vec<MipNode> {
145:     let node_count = atlas.len() / 4;
146:     let mut mips = vec![MipNode::default(); node_count];
147:     let mut done = vec![false; node_count];
148:     for i in 0..node_count {
149:         compute_mip(atlas, i, &mut mips, &mut done, 0);
150:     }
151:     mips
152: }
153: 
154: /// Rebuilds one independent pooled-slot range without touching other MIPs.
155: ///
156: /// `done_scratch` is owned by the renderer and reused between stream updates;
157: /// its size is proportional to the changed slot, never the complete atlas.
158: pub(crate) fn rebuild_mips_in_node_range(
159:     atlas: &[u32],
160:     mips: &mut [MipNode],
161:     node_range: Range<usize>,
162:     done_scratch: &mut Vec<bool>,
163: ) -> bool {
164:     let node_count = atlas.len() / 4;
165:     if atlas.len() % 4 != 0
166:         || mips.len() != node_count
167:         || node_range.is_empty()
168:         || node_range.end > node_count
169:     {
170:         return false;
171:     }
172: 
173:     mips[node_range.clone()].fill(MipNode::default());
174:     done_scratch.clear();
175:     done_scratch.resize(node_range.len(), false);
176:     for node_index in node_range.clone() {
177:         compute_mip(atlas, node_index, mips, done_scratch, node_range.start);
178:     }
179:     true
180: }
181: 
182: fn compute_mip(atlas: &[u32], i: usize, mips: &mut [MipNode], done: &mut [bool], done_base: usize) {
183:     let Some(done_index) = i.checked_sub(done_base).filter(|&index| index < done.len()) else {
184:         return;
185:     };
186:     if done[done_index] {
187:         return;
188:     }
189:     // Marked before descending: a malformed cycle degrades to a zero mip
190:     // instead of infinite recursion.
191:     done[done_index] = true;
192: 
193:     let t = i * 4;
194:     if atlas[t] == 1 {
195:         // Leaf.
196:         let voxel_type = atlas[t + 1];
197:         if voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR {
198:             let c = atlas[t + 2];
199:             let packed_lighting = atlas[t + 3];
200:             let linear_albedo = decode_packed_albedo(c);
201:             let strength = emission_strength(voxel_type);
202:             mips[i] = MipNode {
203:                 linear_albedo,
204:                 baked_rgb: decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting).map(f32::from),
205:                 occupancy: 1.0,
206:                 dominant_voxel_type: voxel_type,
207:                 dominant_coverage: 1.0,
208:                 emissive_coverage: if strength.is_some() { 1.0 } else { 0.0 },
209:                 emitted_radiance_density: strength.map_or([0.0; 3], |scale| {
210:                     linear_albedo.map(|channel| channel * scale)
211:                 }),
212:                 exposed_area: decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting),
213:             };
214:         }
215:     } else {
216:         let child_base = atlas[t + 1] as usize;
217:         let child_mask = atlas[t + 2];
218:         let mut acc = MipNode::default();
219:         for child in 0..8usize {
220:             if child_mask & (1 << child) == 0 {
221:                 continue;
222:             }
223:             let idx = child_base + child;
224:             if idx >= mips.len() {
225:                 continue;
226:             }
227:             compute_mip(atlas, idx, mips, done, done_base);
228:             let m = mips[idx];
229:             let w = m.occupancy / 8.0;
230:             acc.linear_albedo[0] += m.linear_albedo[0] * w;
231:             acc.linear_albedo[1] += m.linear_albedo[1] * w;
232:             acc.linear_albedo[2] += m.linear_albedo[2] * w;
233:             acc.baked_rgb[0] += m.baked_rgb[0] * w;
234:             acc.baked_rgb[1] += m.baked_rgb[1] * w;
235:             acc.baked_rgb[2] += m.baked_rgb[2] * w;
236:             acc.emissive_coverage += m.emissive_coverage / 8.0;
237:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[0] += m.emitted_radiance_density[0] / 8.0;
238:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[1] += m.emitted_radiance_density[1] / 8.0;
239:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[2] += m.emitted_radiance_density[2] / 8.0;
240:             acc.exposed_area
241:                 .add_saturating(m.exposed_area.scaled_to_parent());
242:             let dominant_coverage = m.dominant_coverage / 8.0;
243:             if dominant_coverage > acc.dominant_coverage {
244:                 acc.dominant_coverage = dominant_coverage;
245:                 acc.dominant_voxel_type = m.dominant_voxel_type;
246:             }
247:             acc.occupancy += w;
248:         }
249:         if acc.occupancy > 0.0 {
250:             let inv = 1.0 / acc.occupancy;
251:             acc.linear_albedo[0] *= inv;
252:             acc.linear_albedo[1] *= inv;
253:             acc.linear_albedo[2] *= inv;
254:             acc.baked_rgb[0] *= inv;
255:             acc.baked_rgb[1] *= inv;
256:             acc.baked_rgb[2] *= inv;
257:         }
258:         mips[i] = acc;
259:     }
260: }
261:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/mod.rs
````rust
 1: //! CPU microvoxel splatting renderer — a software implementation of
 2: //! [`crate::application::ports::RendererPort`] for machines with no usable
 3: //! GPU (or `?renderer=cpu`).
 4: //!
 5: //! Instead of marching a ray per pixel, the CPU path inverts the loop: it
 6: //! walks the SVO front-to-back and *splats* nodes onto a z-buffered
 7: //! framebuffer, sized by their projected footprint. The module is split by
 8: //! responsibility — each file owns exactly one concern:
 9: //!
10: //! | module         | concern                                              |
11: //! |----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
12: //! | [`settings`]   | tuning knobs + the shared optimization switchboard   |
13: //! | [`atlas`]      | SVO texel decoding and per-upload MIP filtering      |
14: //! | decode_srgb_albedo | authored color -> linear albedo at upload       |
15: //! | [`raycast`]    | secondary rays (flashlight occlusion, shadow rays)   |
16: //! | [`camera`]     | yaw/pitch basis identical to the GPU shaders         |
17: //! | [`flashlight`] | the spotlight cone — the single spec of its shape    |
18: //! | surface_geometry | exposed faces and material-oriented normals       |
````

````rust
  1: //! Stack-based SVO ray traversal — the CPU twin of the GLSL `raymarchSVO`.
  2: //!
  3: //! Primary visibility comes from splatting, not marching. This module offers
  4: //! two explicit query contracts: [`trace_svo`] returns the nearest hit for
  5: //! reference/debug callers, while [`svo_segment_is_occluded`] is the
  6: //! allocation-free early-out used by flashlight and hero visibility.
  7: //! Both share the same bounded single-chunk marcher. Its work budget is
  8: //! derived from the chunk's real voxel resolution, so selecting 0.05-unit
  9: //! voxels cannot silently inherit the old 160-step coarse-scene limit:
 10: //!
 11: //! 1. Slab-test every chunk AABB and optionally sort hits near-to-far
 12: //!    ([`trace_svo`], controlled by `rt_f2b`).
 13: //! 2. Inside a chunk, descend toward the octant containing the current
 14: //!    point; **empty-space skip** jumps a whole empty leaf/octant in one
 15: //!    step via its AABB exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel DDA.
 16: //! 3. After a skip, pop every ancestor the point exited (a skip through a
 17: //!    shared plane can leave several boxes at once).
 18: 
 19: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 20: 
 21: use super::atlas::decode_node;
 22: 
 23: /// A solid-leaf intersection: ray parameter and the voxel's material type.
 24: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 25: pub struct RayHit {
 26:     pub t: f32,
 27:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// The parameter interval over which a ray lies inside an axis-aligned box.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 32: pub(super) struct RayInterval {
 33:     pub entry: f32,
 34:     pub exit: f32,
 35: }
 36: 
 37: /// Exact ray/AABB slab intersection shared by chunk traversal and flashlight
 38: /// receiver geometry.
 39: ///
 40: /// A zero direction component means that axis is parallel: the ray either
 41: /// remains inside that slab forever or can never enter it. Tiny *non-zero*
 42: /// components remain untouched. Replacing them with an epsilon changes the
 43: /// ray itself and made CPU flashlight shadows jump when yaw or pitch crossed
 44: /// a cardinal direction.
 45: pub(super) fn ray_box_interval(
 46:     origin: [f32; 3],
 47:     direction: [f32; 3],
 48:     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
 49:     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
 50: ) -> Option<RayInterval> {
 51:     let mut entry = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
 52:     let mut exit = f32::INFINITY;
 53:     let mut has_direction = false;
 54: 
 55:     for axis in 0..3 {
 56:         let origin_axis = origin[axis];
 57:         let direction_axis = direction[axis];
 58:         if !origin_axis.is_finite()
 59:             || !direction_axis.is_finite()
 60:             || !bounds_min[axis].is_finite()
 61:             || !bounds_max[axis].is_finite()
 62:         {
 63:             return None;
 64:         }
 65: 
 66:         if direction_axis == 0.0 {
 67:             if origin_axis < bounds_min[axis] || origin_axis > bounds_max[axis] {
 68:                 return None;
 69:             }
 70:             continue;
 71:         }
 72: 
 73:         has_direction = true;
 74:         let first = (bounds_min[axis] - origin_axis) / direction_axis;
 75:         let second = (bounds_max[axis] - origin_axis) / direction_axis;
 76:         entry = entry.max(first.min(second));
 77:         exit = exit.min(first.max(second));
 78: 
 79:         if entry > exit {
 80:             return None;
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     has_direction.then_some(RayInterval { entry, exit })
 85: }
 86: 
 87: /// One saved traversal level: the parent node and its bounds.
 88: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 89: struct TraversalFrame {
 90:     node_idx: usize,
 91:     b_min: [f32; 3],
 92:     b_max: [f32; 3],
 93: }
 94: 
 95: /// The mutable cursor of one chunk march: current node, its bounds, and the
 96: /// ancestor stack (an SVO chunk is at most 8 levels deep, +1 slack).
 97: struct TraversalCursor {
 98:     stack: [TraversalFrame; 9],
 99:     stack_ptr: usize,
100:     node: usize,
101:     b_min: [f32; 3],
102:     b_max: [f32; 3],
103: }
104: 
105: /// Result of marching one intersected chunk.
106: ///
107: /// `Indeterminate` is deliberately distinct from a clear segment. A corrupt
108: /// atlas or exhausted safety budget must not become a light leak: visibility
109: /// queries treat it as blocked, while the nearest-hit diagnostic API (which
110: /// cannot represent an unknown material) simply continues to another chunk.
111: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
112: enum ChunkMarch {
113:     Hit(RayHit),
114:     Clear,
115:     Indeterminate,
116: }
117: 
118: const MIN_TRAVERSAL_STEPS: usize = 160;
119: const MAX_TRAVERSAL_STEPS: usize = 32_768;
120: 
121: /// Conservative upper work bound for a valid octree traversal.
122: ///
123: /// A line crosses at most roughly three times the leaf count of a cubic grid.
124: /// In the pessimistic sparse-tree case each crossing can descend every SVO
125: /// level again. The absolute ceiling still protects a frame from malformed or
126: /// hostile metadata; reaching it produces [`ChunkMarch::Indeterminate`].
127: fn traversal_step_budget(world_size: f32, voxel_size: f32, svo_depth: u8) -> usize {
128:     let geometry_cells =
129:         if world_size.is_finite() && voxel_size.is_finite() && world_size > 0.0 && voxel_size > 0.0
130:         {
131:             (world_size / voxel_size).ceil().clamp(1.0, 1_048_576.0) as u64
132:         } else {
133:             1
134:         };
135:     let depth_cells = 1_u64
136:         .checked_shl(u32::from(svo_depth.min(20)))
137:         .unwrap_or(1_048_576);
138:     let cells_per_axis = geometry_cells.max(depth_cells);
139:     let levels = u64::from(svo_depth).saturating_add(1);
140:     let estimated = cells_per_axis
141:         .saturating_mul(3)
142:         .saturating_add(1)
143:         .saturating_mul(levels)
144:         .saturating_add(16);
145:     estimated.clamp(MIN_TRAVERSAL_STEPS as u64, MAX_TRAVERSAL_STEPS as u64) as usize
146: }
147: 
148: impl TraversalCursor {
149:     fn at_root(root: usize, world_size: f32) -> Self {
150:         Self {
151:             stack: [TraversalFrame {
152:                 node_idx: 0,
153:                 b_min: [0.0; 3],
154:                 b_max: [0.0; 3],
155:             }; 9],
156:             stack_ptr: 0,
157:             node: root,
158:             b_min: [0.0; 3],
159:             b_max: [world_size; 3],
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn push(&mut self) {
164:         if self.stack_ptr < 8 {
165:             self.stack[self.stack_ptr] = TraversalFrame {
166:                 node_idx: self.node,
167:                 b_min: self.b_min,
168:                 b_max: self.b_max,
169:             };
170:             self.stack_ptr += 1;
171:         }
172:     }
173: 
174:     /// Pops EVERY level `p` exited: a skip through a plane shared by several
175:     /// ancestor boxes leaves `p` outside more than one of them, and
176:     /// descending from a box that no longer contains `p` corrupts the
177:     /// traversal (wall cracks). Returns `false` when `p` left the chunk.
178:     fn pop_exited(&mut self, p: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
179:         while p[0] < self.b_min[0]
180:             || p[0] > self.b_max[0]
181:             || p[1] < self.b_min[1]
182:             || p[1] > self.b_max[1]
183:             || p[2] < self.b_min[2]
184:             || p[2] > self.b_max[2]
185:         {
186:             if self.stack_ptr == 0 {
187:                 return false;
188:             }
189:             self.stack_ptr -= 1;
190:             let frame = self.stack[self.stack_ptr];
191:             self.node = frame.node_idx;
192:             self.b_min = frame.b_min;
193:             self.b_max = frame.b_max;
194:         }
195:         true
196:     }
197: }
198: 
199: /// Advances the ray to `bounds`' exit and nudges every tied axis by one
200: /// representable float just past its plane.
201: ///
202: /// This is scale independent. The old fixed `0.001` world-unit push could
203: /// jump over geometry when the user selected 0.05-unit voxels, while its
204: /// fixed tie epsilon merged unrelated planes on long rays.
205: fn skip_to_exit(
206:     ro: [f32; 3],
207:     rd: [f32; 3],
208:     b_min: [f32; 3],
209:     b_max: [f32; 3],
210: ) -> Option<(f32, [f32; 3])> {
211:     let exit_plane = |axis: usize| match rd[axis].total_cmp(&0.0) {
212:         std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => b_max[axis],
213:         std::cmp::Ordering::Less => b_min[axis],
214:         std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => ro[axis],
215:     };
216:     let axis_exit = |axis: usize| {
217:         if rd[axis] == 0.0 {
218:             f32::INFINITY
219:         } else {
220:             (exit_plane(axis) - ro[axis]) / rd[axis]
221:         }
222:     };
223:     let t_max_planes = [axis_exit(0), axis_exit(1), axis_exit(2)];
224:     let t_exit = t_max_planes[0].min(t_max_planes[1]).min(t_max_planes[2]);
225:     if !t_exit.is_finite() {
226:         return None;
227:     }
228:     let mut p = [
229:         ro[0] + t_exit * rd[0],
230:         ro[1] + t_exit * rd[1],
231:         ro[2] + t_exit * rd[2],
232:     ];
233:     for axis in 0..3 {
234:         let axis_t = t_max_planes[axis];
235:         if !axis_t.is_finite() {
236:             continue;
237:         }
238:         let tie_tolerance = f32::EPSILON * 4.0 * t_exit.abs().max(axis_t.abs()).max(1.0);
239:         if (t_exit - axis_t).abs() <= tie_tolerance {
240:             let plane = exit_plane(axis);
241:             p[axis] = if rd[axis] > 0.0 {
242:                 plane.next_up()
243:             } else {
244:                 plane.next_down()
245:             };
246:         }
247:     }
248:     Some((t_exit, p))
249: }
250: 
251: /// Marches one chunk's SVO from `t_entry`. `ro`/`rd` are chunk-local.
252: /// Distinguishes a proven-clear segment from an invalid or exhausted march.
253: fn raymarch_svo_single(
254:     atlas: &[u32],
255:     ro: [f32; 3],
256:     rd: [f32; 3],
257:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
258:     t_entry: f32,
259:     max_t: f32,
260:     world_size: f32,
261:     voxel_size: f32,
262:     svo_depth: u8,
263: ) -> ChunkMarch {
264:     let mut t = t_entry;
265:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
266:     let mut cursor = TraversalCursor::at_root(chunk_root_idx, world_size);
267: 
268:     let max_steps = traversal_step_budget(world_size, voxel_size, svo_depth);
269:     for _ in 0..max_steps {
270:         // A finite visibility segment must not spend the rest of its step
271:         // budget walking geometry beyond the receiver. Equality remains a
272:         // valid endpoint hit, matching `trace_svo`'s public contract.
273:         if t > max_t {
274:             return ChunkMarch::Clear;
275:         }
276:         let Some(node) = decode_node(atlas, cursor.node) else {
277:             return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
278:         };
279: 
280:         if node.is_leaf {
281:             if node.voxel_type != 0 {
282:                 return ChunkMarch::Hit(RayHit {
283:                     t,
284:                     voxel_type: node.voxel_type,
285:                 });
286:             }
287:             // TRAVERSAL: empty-space skip — one step to this empty
288:             // leaf's exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel stepping.
289:             let Some(next) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, cursor.b_min, cursor.b_max) else {
290:                 return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
291:             };
292:             (t, p) = next;
293:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
294:                 return ChunkMarch::Clear;
295:             }
296:             continue;
297:         }
298: 
299:         let center = [
300:             (cursor.b_min[0] + cursor.b_max[0]) * 0.5,
301:             (cursor.b_min[1] + cursor.b_max[1]) * 0.5,
302:             (cursor.b_min[2] + cursor.b_max[2]) * 0.5,
303:         ];
304:         let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
305:         let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
306:         let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
307:         let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
308: 
309:         // The octant's own bounds, picked axis-by-axis from the parent box
310:         // and its center plane.
311:         //
312:         // BUG FIX (cone light): `oct_min[1]` used to read `center[1]` in
313:         // both branches. Every secondary ray crossing an empty lower-Y
314:         // octant computed a too-near exit plane, stalled until the step
315:         // budget ran out, and reported "no hit" — so the flashlight beam
316:         // shone through floors and hero-shadow rays never found occluders.
317:         let oct_min = [
318:             if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cursor.b_min[0] },
319:             if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cursor.b_min[1] },
320:             if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cursor.b_min[2] },
321:         ];
322:         let oct_max = [
323:             if ox == 1 { cursor.b_max[0] } else { center[0] },
324:             if oy == 1 { cursor.b_max[1] } else { center[1] },
325:             if oz == 1 { cursor.b_max[2] } else { center[2] },
326:         ];
327: 
328:         if (node.child_mask & (1 << child_idx)) != 0 {
329:             // Descend into the occupied octant.
330:             cursor.push();
331:             cursor.b_min = oct_min;
332:             cursor.b_max = oct_max;
333:             cursor.node = node.child_base + child_idx;
334:         } else {
335:             // TRAVERSAL: masked-out (air) octant skipped in one step.
336:             let Some(next) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, oct_min, oct_max) else {
337:                 return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
338:             };
339:             (t, p) = next;
340:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
341:                 return ChunkMarch::Clear;
342:             }
343:         }
344:     }
345:     ChunkMarch::Indeterminate
346: }
347: 
348: /// Traces a world-space ray through every resident chunk. Returns the first
349: /// solid hit within `max_t`.
350: pub fn trace_svo(
351:     atlas: &[u32],
352:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
353:     origin: [f32; 3],
354:     direction: [f32; 3],
355:     max_t: f32,
356:     front_to_back: bool,
357: ) -> Option<RayHit> {
358:     struct ChunkHit {
359:         idx: usize,
360:         t_min: f32,
361:     }
362: 
363:     let mut hits = Vec::with_capacity(chunks.len());
364: 
365:     for (i, chunk) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
366:         let local_ro = [
367:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
368:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
369:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
370:         ];
371: 
372:         let Some(interval) = ray_box_interval(local_ro, direction, [0.0; 3], [chunk.world_size; 3])
373:         else {
374:             continue;
375:         };
376: 
377:         if interval.entry < interval.exit && interval.exit > 0.0 && interval.entry < max_t {
378:             hits.push(ChunkHit {
379:                 idx: i,
380:                 t_min: interval.entry.max(0.0),
381:             });
382:         }
383:     }
384: 
385:     // OPTIMIZATION (rt_f2b): nearest chunk first permits the first valid hit
386:     // to return immediately. The disabled reference path visits input order
387:     // and explicitly retains the nearest hit, producing the same answer.
388:     if front_to_back {
389:         hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.t_min.total_cmp(&b.t_min));
390:     }
391: 
392:     let mut closest = None;
393:     for hit in hits {
394:         // OPTIMIZATION (rt_f2b): sorting permits a safe early exit once the
395:         // next chunk does not begin before the closest solid already found.
396:         // Returning after the first intersected chunk is not equivalent:
397:         // padded chunk AABBs overlap, so a nearer box entry can contain a
398:         // farther solid than the following box.
399:         if front_to_back && closest.is_some_and(|current: RayHit| current.t <= hit.t_min) {
400:             break;
401:         }
402: 
403:         let chunk = &chunks[hit.idx];
404:         let local_ro = [
405:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
406:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
407:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
408:         ];
409: 
410:         if let ChunkMarch::Hit(ray_hit) = raymarch_svo_single(
411:             atlas,
412:             local_ro,
413:             direction,
414:             chunk.root_index as usize,
415:             hit.t_min,
416:             max_t,
417:             chunk.world_size,
418:             chunk.voxel_size,
419:             chunk.svo_depth,
420:         ) {
421:             // BUG FIX (cone light): the old code ignored `max_t` once inside
422:             // a chunk, so a wall *behind* the lit surface could "occlude"
423:             // the flashlight ray and randomly black out beam splats.
424:             if ray_hit.t <= max_t {
425:                 if closest.is_none_or(|current: RayHit| ray_hit.t < current.t) {
426:                     closest = Some(ray_hit);
427:                 }
428:             }
429:         }
430:     }
431: 
432:     closest
433: }
434: 
435: /// Returns `true` as soon as any solid voxel intersects the finite ray
436: /// segment `[origin, origin + direction * max_t]`.
437: ///
438: /// Visibility queries do not need the nearest material hit. Keeping that
439: /// contract separate from [`trace_svo`] avoids its per-query chunk-hit
440: /// allocation and sort: each resident chunk is slab-tested in place and the
441: /// first solid hit inside the segment terminates the scan. The SVO march is
442: /// still resolution-bounded and absolutely capped, so malformed atlas data
443: /// cannot hang a flashlight or fixture-shadow query.
444: pub fn svo_segment_is_occluded(
445:     atlas: &[u32],
446:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
447:     origin: [f32; 3],
448:     direction: [f32; 3],
449:     max_t: f32,
450: ) -> bool {
451:     if !max_t.is_finite() || max_t <= 0.0 {
452:         return false;
453:     }
454: 
455:     for chunk in chunks {
456:         let local_origin = [
457:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
458:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
459:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
460:         ];
461:         let Some(interval) =
462:             ray_box_interval(local_origin, direction, [0.0; 3], [chunk.world_size; 3])
463:         else {
464:             continue;
465:         };
466:         if interval.entry >= interval.exit || interval.exit <= 0.0 || interval.entry >= max_t {
467:             continue;
468:         }
469: 
470:         let entry = interval.entry.max(0.0);
471:         match raymarch_svo_single(
472:             atlas,
473:             local_origin,
474:             direction,
475:             chunk.root_index as usize,
476:             entry,
477:             max_t,
478:             chunk.world_size,
479:             chunk.voxel_size,
480:             chunk.svo_depth,
481:         ) {
482:             ChunkMarch::Hit(hit) if hit.t <= max_t => return true,
483:             // Unknown traversal is conservatively shadowed. Treating it as
484:             // clear created bright leaks exactly where fine-voxel scenes
485:             // exceeded the former fixed step budget.
486:             ChunkMarch::Indeterminate => return true,
487:             ChunkMarch::Hit(_) | ChunkMarch::Clear => {}
488:         }
489:     }
490: 
491:     false
492: }

495: mod tests {

501:     #[test]

506:         let exact = ray_box_interval([1.0, 1.0, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], bounds_min, bounds_max)
507:             .expect("axis-aligned ray crosses the box");
508:         assert_eq!(exact.entry, 1.0);
509:         assert_eq!(exact.exit, 3.0);
510: 
511:         let tiny = ray_box_interval(
512:             [1.0, 1.0, -1.0],

514:             bounds_min,
515:             bounds_max,
516:         )
517:         .expect("tiny real components still cross the box");
518:         assert_eq!(tiny.entry, 1.0);
519:         assert_eq!(tiny.exit, 3.0);

530:             .expect("the moving z axis has an exit");

541:         assert!(fine > 6_000, "fine budget was only {fine} steps");
542:         assert!(fine > coarse);

545:     #[test]
546:     fn front_to_back_is_exact_for_overlapping_chunk_bounds() {
547:         // Root A starts first but contains its solid only in the far-z
548:         // octant. Root B starts later and is solid immediately. This is the
549:         // padded/overlapping-chunk case where returning the first chunk hit
550:         // reports t=3 instead of the true nearest t=2.
551:         let mut atlas = Vec::new();
552:         atlas.extend([0, 1, 1 << 4, 0]); // root A, child 4 occupied
553:         for child in 0..8 {
554:             let material = if child == 4 { 1 } else { 0 };
555:             atlas.extend([1, material, 0x00FF_FFFF, 0]);
556:         }
557:         let root_b = atlas.len() / 4;
558:         atlas.extend([1, 1, 0x00FF_FFFF, 0]);
559: 
560:         let chunks = [
561:             ChunkDraw {
562:                 origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
563:                 root_index: 0,
564:                 world_size: 4.0,
565:                 voxel_size: 2.0,
566:                 svo_depth: 1,
567:             },
568:             ChunkDraw {
569:                 origin: [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
570:                 root_index: root_b as i32,
571:                 world_size: 1.0,
572:                 voxel_size: 1.0,
573:                 svo_depth: 0,
574:             },
575:         ];
576:         let origin = [0.5, 0.5, -1.0];
577:         let direction = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0];
578:         let reference = trace_svo(&atlas, &chunks, origin, direction, 10.0, false)
579:             .expect("reference must hit root B");
580:         let optimized = trace_svo(&atlas, &chunks, origin, direction, 10.0, true)
581:             .expect("optimized path must hit root B");
582:         assert_eq!(reference, optimized);
583:         assert!((optimized.t - 2.0).abs() < 1.0e-6, "hit={optimized:?}");
584:     }
585: 
586:     #[test]
587:     fn allocation_free_segment_query_matches_nearest_hit_visibility() {
588:         let mut atlas = Vec::new();
589:         atlas.extend([1, 1, 0x00FF_FFFF, 0]);
590:         let chunks = [
591:             ChunkDraw {
592:                 origin: [0.0, 0.0, 8.0],
593:                 root_index: 0,
594:                 world_size: 2.0,
595:                 voxel_size: 2.0,
596:                 svo_depth: 0,
597:             },
598:             ChunkDraw {
599:                 origin: [0.0, 0.0, 2.0],
600:                 root_index: 0,
601:                 world_size: 2.0,
602:                 voxel_size: 2.0,
603:                 svo_depth: 0,
604:             },
605:         ];
606:         let origin = [1.0, 1.0, 0.0];
607:         let direction = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0];
608: 
609:         for max_t in [1.0, 2.0, 2.5, 20.0] {
610:             let reference = trace_svo(&atlas, &chunks, origin, direction, max_t, true).is_some();
611:             assert_eq!(
612:                 svo_segment_is_occluded(&atlas, &chunks, origin, direction, max_t),
613:                 reference,
614:                 "visibility differs at max_t={max_t}"
615:             );
616:         }
617:     }

619:     #[test]

622:             origin: [0.0; 3],
623:             root_index: 99,
624:             world_size: 4.0,
625:             voxel_size: 1.0,
````

````rust
 1: //! Compile a dense reference-room description into the same serialized SVO
 2: //! contract consumed by production renderers.
 3: 
 4: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 5: use crate::adapters::collect_emissive_lights::collect_emissive_lights;
 6: use crate::core::domain::room::RoomScene;
 7: use crate::core::ports::reference_renderer::RenderSceneSnapshot;
 8: use vackrooms::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
 9: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
10: use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
11: use vackrooms::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::{VoxelLightingSettings, bake_voxel_lighting};
12: 
13: pub fn build_render_scene(scene: RoomScene) -> RenderSceneSnapshot {
14:     let (mut voxels, voxel_size, origin) = scene.into_parts();
15:     let svo_depth = cube_depth(&voxels);
16:     let world_size = voxels.width() as f32 * voxel_size;
17:     let scene_lights = collect_emissive_lights(&voxels, voxel_size, origin, 0);
18: 
19:     let lighting = VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(voxel_size)
20:         .expect("RoomScene guarantees a positive finite voxel size");
21:     bake_voxel_lighting(&mut voxels, lighting);
22: 
23:     let svo = BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&voxels, svo_depth, world_size);
24:     let serialized = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
25:     RenderSceneSnapshot {
26:         atlas: serialized.texel_data,
27:         chunks: vec![ChunkDraw {
28:             origin,
29:             root_index: svo.root as i32,
30:             world_size,
31:             voxel_size,
32:             svo_depth: svo_depth as u8,
33:         }],
34:         scene_lights,
35:     }
36: }
37: 
38: fn cube_depth(voxels: &VoxelGrid) -> u32 {
39:     let edge = voxels.width();
40:     assert!(
41:         edge.is_power_of_two(),
42:         "reference room edge must be a power of two"
43:     );
44:     assert_eq!(voxels.height(), edge, "reference room must be cubic");
45:     assert_eq!(voxels.depth(), edge, "reference room must be cubic");
46:     edge.ilog2()
47: }
48: 
49: #[cfg(test)]
50: mod tests {
51:     use super::*;
52:     use crate::application::ports::LightKind;
53:

56:         let snapshot = build_render_scene(RoomScene::single_ceiling_fixture());
57: 
58:         assert_eq!(snapshot.scene_lights.len(), 1);
59:         let fixture = snapshot.scene_lights[0];
60:         assert!(fixture.enabled);
61:         assert_eq!(fixture.kind, LightKind::CeilingPanel);
62:         assert!(fixture.intensity > 0.0);
63:         assert!(fixture.radius > 0.0);
64:     }
65: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/lights.rs
````rust
  1: //! Per-frame light selection — one implementation for the surface and
  2: //! splat renderers, which previously carried diverging copies.
  3: //!
  4: //! Inputs: fixture lights from every visible chunk (deduplicated by id —
  5: //! a fixture near a chunk border is listed by several chunks) plus the
  6: //! frame's dynamic lights (dropped flares). The most important lights fill
  7: //! the bounded shader slots; the most important *fixture* light also
  8: //! wins the hero shadow map (a flare at ankle height would collapse the
  9: //! top-down shadow frustum, so dynamic lights never own it).
 10: //!
 11: //! Importance = radius * sqrt(intensity) / (distance² + 0.1): bigger and
 12: //! brighter lights reach farther, nearby lights dominate.
 13: 
 14: use crate::application::ports::{FrameParams, LightSource, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 15: 
 16: /// Maximum shader light slots (matches the GLSL uniform arrays).
 17: pub const MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS: usize = crate::application::ports::MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS;
 18: 
 19: /// The frame's selected lights, packed for `uniform[1i|3fv|4fv]` upload.
 20: pub struct SelectedLights {
 21:     pub count: usize,
 22:     pub positions: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 23:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 24:     /// Per light: radius, intensity, half_size.x, half_size.y.
 25:     pub params: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 26:     pub kinds: [i32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
 27:     /// Slot index of the shadow-casting hero light, or -1.
 28:     pub hero_slot: i32,
 29:     /// Hero light's position/radius (meaningful when `hero_slot >= 0`).
 30:     pub hero_position: [f32; 3],
 31:     pub hero_radius: f32,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// Wraps the frame's dynamic lights as fixture-shaped sources with sentinel
 35: /// ids in the top range, so one selection pass handles both kinds.
 36: pub fn dynamic_light_sources(frame: &FrameParams) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 37:     frame
 38:         .active_dynamic_lights()
 39:         .iter()
 40:         .enumerate()
 41:         .map(|(i, d)| LightSource {
 42:             id: u64::MAX - i as u64,
 43:             position: d.position,
 44:             half_size: [0.25, 0.25],
 45:             color: d.color,
 46:             radius: d.radius,
 47:             intensity: d.intensity,
 48:             kind: crate::application::ports::LightKind::Point,
 49:             flicker_mode: 0,
 50:             enabled: true,
 51:         })
 52:         .collect()
 53: }
 54: 
 55: fn is_dynamic(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
 56:     light.id > u64::MAX - 16
 57: }
 58: 
 59: /// Selects and packs the frame's lights. `fixtures` should already be
 60: /// deduplicated by id (pass a `HashMap`'s values); `dynamic` comes from
 61: /// [`dynamic_light_sources`].
 62: pub fn select_lights<'a>(
 63:     fixtures: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
 64:     dynamic: &'a [LightSource],
 65:     frame: &FrameParams,
 66: ) -> SelectedLights {
 67:     let mut ranked: Vec<(&LightSource, f32)> = fixtures
 68:         .chain(dynamic.iter())
 69:         .map(|light| {
 70:             let dx = light.position[0] - frame.camera_pos[0];
 71:             let dy = light.position[1] - frame.camera_pos[1];
 72:             let dz = light.position[2] - frame.camera_pos[2];
 73:             let dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
 74:             (light, light.radius * light.intensity.sqrt() / (dist2 + 0.1))
 75:         })
 76:         .collect();
 77:     ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 78: 
 79:     let count = ranked.len().min(MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS);
 80:     let mut selected = SelectedLights {
 81:         count,
 82:         positions: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 83:         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 84:         params: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 85:         kinds: [0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
 86:         hero_slot: -1,
 87:         hero_position: [0.0; 3],
 88:         hero_radius: 0.0,
 89:     };
 90:     for (i, (light, _)) in ranked[..count].iter().enumerate() {
 91:         selected.positions[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
 92:         selected.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
 93:         selected.params[i * 4] = light.radius;
 94:         selected.params[i * 4 + 1] = light.intensity;
 95:         selected.params[i * 4 + 2] = light.half_size[0];
 96:         selected.params[i * 4 + 3] = light.half_size[1];
 97:         selected.kinds[i] = light.kind as i32;
 98:     }
 99: 
100:     // Hero shadow: the strongest *fixture* light in the selected slots.
101:     if let Some(slot) = ranked[..count].iter().position(|(l, _)| !is_dynamic(l)) {
102:         selected.hero_slot = slot as i32;
103:         selected.hero_position = ranked[slot].0.position;
104:         selected.hero_radius = ranked[slot].0.radius;
105:     }
106:     selected
107: }
108: 
109: /// Flare-core uniforms (`uCoreCount`/`uCores`/`uCoreColors`), independent of
110: /// the merged light slots so a flare culled from the four shading lights
111: /// still shows its ember.
112: pub struct FlareCores {
113:     pub count: i32,
114:     /// xyz = position, w = pre-flickered intensity.
115:     pub pos_intensity: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
116:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
117: }
118: 
119: pub fn flare_cores(frame: &FrameParams) -> FlareCores {
120:     let cores = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
121:     let mut packed = FlareCores {
122:         count: cores.len() as i32,
123:         pos_intensity: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
124:         colors: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
125:     };
126:     for (i, c) in cores.iter().enumerate() {
127:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4..i * 4 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.position);
128:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4 + 3] = c.intensity;
129:         packed.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.color);
130:     }
131:     packed
132: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/math.rs
````rust
  1: //! Camera and light matrices — column-major, ready for `uniformMatrix4fv`.
  2: 
  3: use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
  4: 
  5: /// View + projection for the raster paths, from the same yaw/pitch basis
  6: /// the raymarcher and the CPU splatter use, so every renderer frames the
  7: /// world identically.
  8: pub fn camera_matrices(
  9:     frame: &FrameParams,
 10:     width: i32,
 11:     height: i32,
 12:     max_draw_distance: f32,
 13: ) -> ([f32; 16], [f32; 16]) {
 14:     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
 15:     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
 16:     let right = [cy, 0.0, -sy];
 17:     let up = [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy];
 18:     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
 19:     let p = frame.camera_pos;
 20:     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
 21:     let view = [
 22:         right[0],
 23:         up[0],
 24:         -forward[0],
 25:         0.0,
 26:         right[1],
 27:         up[1],
 28:         -forward[1],
 29:         0.0,
 30:         right[2],
 31:         up[2],
 32:         -forward[2],
 33:         0.0,
 34:         -dot(right, p),
 35:         -dot(up, p),
 36:         dot(forward, p),
 37:         1.0,
 38:     ];
 39:     let near = 0.03;
 40:     let far = max_draw_distance;
 41:     let f = 1.0 / crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
 42:     let aspect = width as f32 / height.max(1) as f32;
 43:     let projection = [
 44:         f / aspect,
 45:         0.0,
 46:         0.0,
 47:         0.0,
 48:         0.0,
 49:         f,
 50:         0.0,
 51:         0.0,
 52:         0.0,
 53:         0.0,
 54:         (far + near) / (near - far),
 55:         -1.0,
 56:         0.0,
 57:         0.0,
 58:         (2.0 * far * near) / (near - far),
 59:         0.0,
 60:     ];
 61:     (projection, view)
 62: }
 63: 
 64: pub fn ortho_matrix(
 65:     left: f32,
 66:     right: f32,
 67:     bottom: f32,
 68:     top: f32,
 69:     near: f32,
 70:     far: f32,
 71: ) -> [f32; 16] {
 72:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
 73:     m[0] = 2.0 / (right - left);
 74:     m[5] = 2.0 / (top - bottom);
 75:     m[10] = -2.0 / (far - near);
 76:     m[12] = -(right + left) / (right - left);
 77:     m[13] = -(top + bottom) / (top - bottom);
 78:     m[14] = -(far + near) / (far - near);
 79:     m[15] = 1.0;
 80:     m
 81: }
 82: 
 83: /// View matrix for a light looking straight down (-Y), up = -Z. Used by
 84: /// the hero-light shadow pass (ceiling fixtures shine downward).
 85: pub fn look_at_matrix_down(eye: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 16] {
 86:     let forward = [0.0, -1.0, 0.0];
 87:     let up = [0.0, 0.0, -1.0f32];
 88:     let right = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0f32];
 89: 
 90:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
 91:     m[0] = right[0];
 92:     m[1] = up[0];
 93:     m[2] = -forward[0];
 94: 
 95:     m[4] = right[1];
 96:     m[5] = up[1];
 97:     m[6] = -forward[1];
 98: 
 99:     m[8] = right[2];
100:     m[9] = up[2];
101:     m[10] = -forward[2];
102: 
103:     m[12] = -(right[0] * eye[0] + right[1] * eye[1] + right[2] * eye[2]);
104:     m[13] = -(up[0] * eye[0] + up[1] * eye[1] + up[2] * eye[2]);
105:     m[14] = -(-forward[0] * eye[0] + -forward[1] * eye[1] + -forward[2] * eye[2]);
106:     m[15] = 1.0;
107:     m
108: }
109: 
110: pub fn multiply_matrices(a: &[f32; 16], b: &[f32; 16]) -> [f32; 16] {
111:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
112:     for col in 0..4 {
113:         for row in 0..4 {
114:             m[col * 4 + row] = a[row] * b[col * 4]
115:                 + a[4 + row] * b[col * 4 + 1]
116:                 + a[8 + row] * b[col * 4 + 2]
117:                 + a[12 + row] * b[col * 4 + 3];
118:         }
119:     }
120:     m
121: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/visibility.rs
````rust
 1: //! Conservative visibility tests shared by the raster drivers.
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
 4: 
 5: /// Shared raster far plane and conservative culling boundary (world units).
 6: /// Beer--Lambert fog never becomes exactly opaque, so projection and culling
 7: /// must use the identical distance rather than hiding a ten-unit mismatch.
 8: pub const MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE: f32 = 110.0;
 9: 
10: /// Sphere visibility: inside the draw distance and not entirely behind the
11: /// camera plane. Returns the squared distance for near-to-far sorting, or
12: /// `None` when culled. Deliberately conservative (no side-plane frustum
13: /// test): a false "visible" costs a few draws, a false cull costs a hole
14: /// in the world.
15: pub fn sphere_visible(
16:     center: [f32; 3],
17:     radius: f32,
18:     frame: &FrameParams,
19:     max_draw_distance: f32,
20: ) -> Option<f32> {
21:     let to = [
22:         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
23:         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
24:         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
25:     ];
26:     let distance2 = to[0] * to[0] + to[1] * to[1] + to[2] * to[2];
27:     // Cull only when the *whole sphere* lies beyond the distance boundary.
28:     // Testing the center against `max_draw_distance` cuts chunks/cells that
29:     // still intersect the visible volume and creates a hard pop at the fog
30:     // edge.
31:     let farthest_visible_center = max_draw_distance + radius;
32:     if distance2 > farthest_visible_center * farthest_visible_center {
33:         return None;
34:     }
35:     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
36:     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
37:     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
38:     let dot = to[0] * forward[0] + to[1] * forward[1] + to[2] * forward[2];
39:     if dot >= -radius {
40:         Some(distance2)
41:     } else {
42:         None
43:     }
44: }
45: 
46: /// Center + bounding-sphere radius of a chunk from its origin and local
47: /// bounds-max — the shape both mesh and splat chunk records share.
48: pub fn chunk_bounding_sphere(origin: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> ([f32; 3], f32) {
49:     let center = [
50:         origin[0] + bounds_max[0] * 0.5,
51:         origin[1] + bounds_max[1] * 0.5,
52:         origin[2] + bounds_max[2] * 0.5,
53:     ];
54:     let radius = (bounds_max[0] * bounds_max[0]
55:         + bounds_max[1] * bounds_max[1]
56:         + bounds_max[2] * bounds_max[2])
57:         .sqrt()
58:         * 0.5;
59:     (center, radius)
60: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Indexed world-surface program.
  2: //!
  3: //! The module name states the use case; the files below state the successive
  4: //! mathematical responsibilities. Shader assembly is the only string work

 20: const FRAGMENT_INTERFACE: &str = r#"#version 300 es
 21: precision highp float;
 22: precision highp sampler3D;
 23: 
 24: in vec3 vWorldPosition;
 25: in vec3 vNormal;
 26: flat in float vMaterial;
 27: flat in float vStaticIndirect;
 28: flat in float vAo;

 67: /// Builds one readable GLSL translation unit from purpose-sized sections.

121:             assert!(
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/shade_voxel_hit.rs
````rust
 1: //! Turn one selected voxel hit into linear scene radiance.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: bool isEmissiveVoxel(uint material) {
 5:     return material == 4u || material == 9u || material == 16u;
 6: }
 7: 
 8: vec3 decodePackedColor(uint packed) {
 9:     return vec3(
10:         float((packed >> 16u) & 0xffu),
11:         float((packed >> 8u) & 0xffu),
12:         float(packed & 0xffu)
13:     ) * (1.0 / 255.0);
14: }
15: 
16: bool isDownwardEmittingFace(vec3 normal) {
17:     return normal.y < -0.5;
18: }
19: 
20: vec3 emittedVoxelRadiance(uint material, vec3 albedo, vec3 normal) {
21:     if (!isDownwardEmittingFace(normal)) return vec3(0.0);
22:     if (material == 4u) return albedo * 10.0;
23:     if (material == 9u) return albedo * 8.0;
24:     if (material == 16u) return albedo * 0.9;
25:     return vec3(0.0);
26: }
27: 
28: vec3 shadeVoxel(
29:     VoxelHit hit,
30:     vec3 worldPosition,
31:     float receiverVoxelSize,
32:     int receiverChunkIndex
33: ) {
34:     vec3 albedo = srgbToLinear(decodePackedColor(hit.color));
35:     if (isEmissiveVoxel(hit.material) && isDownwardEmittingFace(hit.normal)) {
36:         return emittedVoxelRadiance(hit.material, albedo, hit.normal);
37:     }
38: 
39:     vec3 ambient = (uOutdoor == 1
40:         ? vec3(0.32, 0.38, 0.48)
41:         : vec3(0.045, 0.040, 0.024)) * uAmbientScale;
42:     vec3 analyticDirect = vec3(0.0);
43: 
44:     // Analytic fixtures are the sole static-light authority. A single packed
45:     // RGB value cannot describe the six incident face directions, so this
46:     // correctness path deliberately does not consume the optional surface
47:     // diffuse field.
48:     int lightFirst = uChunkLightFirst[receiverChunkIndex];
49:     int lightCount = uChunkLightCounts[receiverChunkIndex];
50:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < lightCount; ++lightIndex) {
51:         SceneLight light = readSceneLight(lightFirst + lightIndex);
52:         analyticDirect += evaluateVisibleSceneLight(
53:             worldPosition, hit.normal, light, receiverVoxelSize
54:         );
55:     }
56:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < 4; ++lightIndex) {
57:         if (lightIndex >= uDynamicLightCount) break;
58:         analyticDirect += evaluateVisiblePointLight(
59:             worldPosition,
60:             hit.normal,
61:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].xyz,
62:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].rgb,
63:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].w,
64:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].a,
65:             receiverVoxelSize
66:         );
67:     }
68: 
69:     vec3 radiance = albedo * (
70:         ambient + analyticDirect
71:     ) * (1.0 / PI);
72:     if (uFlashlightEnabled == 1) {
73:         radiance += albedo * spotBeam(
74:             uCameraPosition, uCamForward, worldPosition, hit.normal
75:         );
76:     }
77:     return radiance;
78: }
79: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/splat.rs
````rust
  1: //! Instanced face-splat program — the GPU microvoxel path.
  2: //!
  3: //! One instance is one axis-aligned surface rectangle (`PackedFaceInstance`);
  4: //! the vertex shader rebuilds the quad from center + extents + axis via
  5: //! `gl_VertexID` (4-vertex TRIANGLE_STRIP) and evaluates ALL lighting once
  6: //! per face, flat — the voxel look, and the reason the fragment shader
  7: //! shrinks to fog + grain + dither (the Pi win).
  8: 
  9: use super::chunks;
 10: 
 11: /// Preamble: version, attributes, uniforms, varyings.
 12: const VERTEX_HEADER: &str = r#"#version 300 es
 13: precision highp float;
 14: precision highp sampler3D;
 15: 
 16: in vec3 aFacePos;      // face center, chunk-local fixed point (1/1024 u)
 17: in vec2 aFaceExtents;  // cells along the face's U/V axes
 18: in vec4 aFaceMeta;     // normal_axis, material, baked_light (0-15), ao
 19: in float aFaceFlags;   // bit 0: emissive
 20: 
 21: uniform mat4 uProjection;
 22: uniform mat4 uView;
 23: uniform vec3 uChunkOrigin;
 24: uniform vec3 uChunkSize;
 25: uniform float uVoxelScale;
 26: uniform vec3 uCameraPosition;
 27: // Camera forward axis for the flashlight cone.
 28: uniform vec3 uCamForward;
 29: uniform int uFlashlightEnabled;
 30: uniform sampler3D uLightVolume;
 31: 
 32: uniform int uLightCount;
 33: uniform vec3 uLightPositions[16];
 34: uniform vec3 uLightColors[16];
 35: uniform vec4 uLightParams[16];
 36: 
 37: uniform sampler2D uShadowMap;
 38: uniform mat4 uLightViewProjection;
 39: uniform int uShadowedLightIndex;
 40: uniform int uShadowTaps;
 41: 
 42: // Level atmosphere (see the surface shader).
 43: uniform int uOutdoor;
 44: uniform float uAmbientScale;
 45: 
 46: out vec3 vWorldPos;
 47: flat out vec3 vColor;
 48: flat out vec3 vNormal;
 49: flat out float vEmissive;
 50: flat out float vGrainAmp;
 51: flat out float vBeamPattern;
 52: "#;
 53: 
 54: /// Quad reconstruction + per-face lighting body.
 55: const VERTEX_BODY: &str = r#"
 56: vec3 normalForAxis(float axis) {
 57:     if (axis < 0.5) return vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);
 58:     if (axis < 1.5) return vec3(0.0, -1.0, 0.0);
 59:     if (axis < 2.5) return vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0);
 60:     if (axis < 3.5) return vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
 61:     if (axis < 4.5) return vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
 62:     return vec3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
 63: }
 64: 
 65: // In-plane basis with U x V = outward normal, so the TRIANGLE_STRIP corner
 66: // order (-1,-1)(1,-1)(-1,1)(1,1) is counter-clockwise from the front.
 67: void faceBasis(float axis, out vec3 u, out vec3 v) {
 68:     if (axis < 0.5)      { u = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0); }
 69:     else if (axis < 1.5) { u = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0); }
 70:     else if (axis < 2.5) { u = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, -1.0, 0.0); }
 71:     else if (axis < 3.5) { u = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); }
 72:     else if (axis < 4.5) { u = vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0); }
 73:     else                 { u = vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); v = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0); }
 74: }
 75: 
 76: // Face-center shadow visibility. Vertex shaders have no derivatives or
 77: // gl_FragCoord, so this uses a fixed symmetric tap pattern; tap count is a
 78: // spec-profile knob (1 on Pi-class, 4 on high).
 79: float shadowVisibility(vec3 worldPos, vec3 normal, vec3 lightDir) {
 80:     vec4 lightClip = uLightViewProjection * vec4(worldPos + normal * 0.025, 1.0);
 81:     vec3 p = lightClip.xyz / lightClip.w;
 82:     vec2 uv = p.xy * 0.5 + 0.5;
 83:     float receiverDepth = p.z * 0.5 + 0.5;
 84:     if (any(lessThan(uv, vec2(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(uv, vec2(1.0))) || receiverDepth >= 1.0) {
 85:         return 1.0;
 86:     }
 87:     float bias = max(0.003 * (1.0 - dot(normal, lightDir)), 0.0008);
 88:     float compare = receiverDepth - bias;
 89:     if (uShadowTaps <= 1) {
 90:         float d = textureLod(uShadowMap, uv, 0.0).r;
 91:         return (compare > d) ? 0.0 : 1.0;
 92:     }
 93:     vec2 texelSize = 1.0 / vec2(textureSize(uShadowMap, 0));
 94:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
 95:         vec2(-0.5, -0.5), vec2(0.5, -0.5),
 96:         vec2(-0.5,  0.5), vec2(0.5,  0.5)
 97:     );
 98:     float shadow = 0.0;
 99:     for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
100:         float d = textureLod(uShadowMap, uv + offsets[i] * texelSize, 0.0).r;
101:         shadow += (compare > d) ? 0.0 : 1.0;
102:     }
103:     return shadow * 0.25;
104: }
105: 
106: // Quantize the light magnitude while preserving its RGB ratio. Quantizing
107: // channels independently makes warm yellow light jump toward neutral grey.
108: vec3 quantizeLighting(vec3 lightColor) {
109:     float peak = max(max(lightColor.r, lightColor.g), lightColor.b);
110:     if (peak < 0.0001) {
111:         return vec3(0.08, 0.07, 0.035);
112:     }
113:     float band = max(floor(peak * 6.0 + 0.5) / 6.0, 0.08);
114:     return lightColor * (band / peak);
115: }
116: 
117: void main() {
118:     vec2 corner = vec2(
119:         (gl_VertexID == 1 || gl_VertexID == 3) ? 1.0 : -1.0,
120:         (gl_VertexID >= 2) ? 1.0 : -1.0
121:     );
122:     vec3 N = normalForAxis(aFaceMeta.x);
123:     vec3 U, V;
124:     faceBasis(aFaceMeta.x, U, V);
125: 
126:     vec3 center = uChunkOrigin + aFacePos * (1.0 / 1024.0);
127:     float halfU = aFaceExtents.x * uVoxelScale * 0.5;
128:     float halfV = aFaceExtents.y * uVoxelScale * 0.5;
129:     vec3 world = center + corner.x * halfU * U + corner.y * halfV * V;
130:     vWorldPos = world;
131:     vNormal = N;
132:     gl_Position = uProjection * uView * vec4(world, 1.0);
133: 
134:     vec3 albedo = materialColor(aFaceMeta.y);
135:     bool emissive = aFaceFlags > 0.5;
136:     vEmissive = emissive ? 1.0 : 0.0;
137:     // Per-voxel grain amplitude: subtle on walls/floors, none on ceilings
138:     // (a bright ceiling plane turns grain into salt-and-pepper noise) or
139:     // emissive fixtures.
140:     bool isCeiling = aFaceMeta.y > 2.5 && aFaceMeta.y < 3.5;
141:     vGrainAmp = (emissive || isCeiling) ? 0.0 : 0.02;
142:     // Coffer beams live in shading, not geometry: downward ceiling faces
143:     // get a world-locked beam-grid darkening in the fragment shader.
144:     vBeamPattern = (isCeiling && aFaceMeta.x > 0.5 && aFaceMeta.x < 1.5) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
145:     if (emissive) {
146:         vColor = albedo * 1.5;
147:         return;
148:     }
149: 
150:     vec3 toCamera = uCameraPosition - center;
151:     float distanceToCamera = length(toCamera);
152: 
153:     // Sample the baked light volume half a voxel into the air so a face
154:     // never reads the dark interior of its own wall.
155:     vec3 samplePos = center + N * (0.5 * uVoxelScale);
156:     vec3 uvw = (samplePos - uChunkOrigin) / uChunkSize;
157:     vec3 irradiance = textureLod(uLightVolume, clamp(uvw, 0.0, 1.0), 0.0).rgb;
158:     // The compact face record carries the scalar bake too. It is a robust
159:     // floor at chunk borders and preserves the CPU splatter's light bands,
160:     // while the 3D volume supplies the actual warm/red chroma.
161:     float baked = aFaceMeta.z * (1.0 / 15.0);
162:     vec3 bakedWarm = vec3(baked, baked * 0.94, baked * 0.72);
163:     vec3 roomAmbient = vec3(0.16, 0.145, 0.075);
164:     vec3 bouncedLight = irradiance * 0.75;
165:     irradiance = max(roomAmbient, bouncedLight);
166:     if (uOutdoor == 1) {
167:         irradiance = max(irradiance, vec3(0.30, 0.32, 0.36));
168:     }
169: 
170:     float faceResponse = 0.8;
171:     if (N.y > 0.5) {
172:         faceResponse = 1.0;
173:     } else if (N.y < -0.5) {
174:         faceResponse = 0.35;
175:     } else {
176:         faceResponse = 0.65 + 0.1 * N.x + 0.05 * N.z;
177:     }
178: 
179:     float ao = mix(1.0, 0.22, clamp(aFaceMeta.w * 1.3, 0.0, 1.0));
180: 
181:     vec3 ambientUp = vec3(1.05, 1.0, 0.72) * irradiance;
182:     vec3 ambientDown = vec3(0.58, 0.52, 0.30) * irradiance;
183:     if (uOutdoor == 1) {
184:         ambientUp = vec3(0.98, 1.02, 1.08) * irradiance;
185:         ambientDown = vec3(0.56, 0.58, 0.55) * irradiance;
186:     }
187:     vec3 ambient = mix(ambientDown, ambientUp, N.y * 0.5 + 0.5) * ao * faceResponse * uAmbientScale;
188: 
189:     vec3 directDiffuse = vec3(0.0);
190:     for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
191:         if (i >= uLightCount) break;
192:         vec3 toLight = uLightPositions[i] - center;
193:         float d2 = dot(toLight, toLight);
194:         float range = uLightParams[i].x;
195:         float range2 = range * range;
196:         if (d2 >= range2) continue;
197: 
198:         float d = sqrt(d2);
199:         vec3 L = toLight / max(d, 0.001);
200:         float ndotl = max(dot(N, L), 0.0);
201:         float x = clamp(d2 / range2, 0.0, 1.0);
202:         float falloff = (1.0 - x) * (1.0 - x);
203: 
204:         float visible = 1.0;
205:         if (i == uShadowedLightIndex) {
206:             visible = shadowVisibility(center, N, L);
207:         }
208: 
209:         float lightHash = hash3D(uLightPositions[i] * 10.0);
210:         float directMod = 1.0 + 0.05 * (lightHash - 0.5);
211:         vec3 lightColor = mix(uLightColors[i], vec3(1.0, 0.96, 0.85), 0.3);
212:         directDiffuse += lightColor * uLightParams[i].y * falloff * visible * ndotl * directMod;
213:     }
214: 
215:     // Flashlight: the shared spotlight cone (spec in the CPU splatter),
216:     // evaluated once per face at its center — flat like all splat lighting.
217:     // Kept INSIDE the light sum: the material color is the immutable base
218:     // and every light multiplies it, so the flashlight brightens yellow
219:     // walls toward brighter yellow, never neutral grey.
220:     vec3 flashlight = vec3(0.0);
221:     if (uFlashlightEnabled == 1) {
222:         flashlight = spotBeam(uCameraPosition, uCamForward, center, N);
223:     }
224: 
225:     vec3 lighting = quantizeLighting(ambient + directDiffuse + flashlight);
226:     vColor = albedo * lighting;
227: }
228: "#;
229: 
230: /// Fragment preamble.
231: const FRAGMENT_HEADER: &str = r#"#version 300 es
232: precision highp float;
233: // Fragment ints default to mediump; the vertex stage declares uOutdoor at
234: // its (highp) default, and linking demands the precisions match.
235: precision highp int;
236: 
237: in vec3 vWorldPos;
238: flat in vec3 vColor;
239: flat in vec3 vNormal;
240: flat in float vEmissive;
241: flat in float vGrainAmp;
242: flat in float vBeamPattern;
243: 
244: uniform vec3 uCameraPosition;
245: uniform float uVoxelScale;
246: // Optimization/effect toggle: grain + banding dither (RenderToggles).
247: uniform int uDitherEnabled;
248: 
249: // Dropped-flare cores: xyz = world position, w = intensity (pre-flickered).
250: uniform int uCoreCount;
251: uniform vec4 uCores[4];
252: uniform vec3 uCoreColors[4];
253: 
254: // Level atmosphere: outdoors the fog fades to a bright sky haze instead of
255: // black (the framebuffer is cleared to the matching sky color).
256: uniform int uOutdoor;
257: uniform vec3 uFogColor;
258: 
259: out vec4 fragColor;
260: "#;
261: 
262: /// The splat fragment body is deliberately tiny (the Pi win): fog,
263: /// voxel-lattice albedo grain, ordered dither, tone map. All lighting
264: /// arrived flat from the vertex shader.
265: const FRAGMENT_BODY: &str = r#"
266: void main() {
267:     vec3 color = vColor;
268:     float distanceToCamera = length(uCameraPosition - vWorldPos);
269: 
270:     if (vEmissive < 0.5) {
271:         // World-locked per-voxel albedo grain: sample half a voxel inside
272:         // the surface so faces lying exactly on lattice planes hash stably.
273:         // Amplitude is per-face (zero on ceilings) so large bright planes
274:         // read as solid construction, not noise.
275:         vec3 lattice = floor((vWorldPos - vNormal * (0.5 * uVoxelScale)) / uVoxelScale);
276:         float grain = 1.0 + (hash3D(lattice) - 0.5) * 2.0 * vGrainAmp * float(uDitherEnabled);
277:         color *= grain;
278: 
279:         // Coffer beam grid on ceilings (matches the generator's
280:         // COFFER_PERIOD): intentional construction lines, zero geometry.
281:         if (vBeamPattern > 0.5) {
282:             bool onBeam = mod(vWorldPos.x, 2.8) < 0.22 || mod(vWorldPos.z, 2.8) < 0.22;
283:             if (onBeam) {
284:                 color *= 0.86;
285:             }
286:         }
287: 
288:     }
289: 
290:     // Warm haze nearby, fading all the way to black before the draw limit.
291:     // The framebuffer is cleared to the same black, so a not-yet-generated
292:     // chunk reads as void instead of a brown rectangle.
293:     float fogOnset = 14.0;
294:     float fogDist = max(0.0, distanceToCamera - fogOnset);
295:     float fogDensity = 0.032;
296:     float heightFactor = 1.0 + 0.35 * smoothstep(0.0, 3.4, vWorldPos.y);
297:     float fogAmount = 1.0 - exp(-fogDist * fogDensity * heightFactor);
298:     fogAmount = max(fogAmount, smoothstep(34.0, 48.0, distanceToCamera));
299: 
300:     float hNorm = clamp(vWorldPos.y / 5.0, 0.0, 1.0);
301:     vec3 heightFogColor = mix(
302:         vec3(0.055, 0.040, 0.014),
303:         vec3(0.055, 0.060, 0.020),
304:         hNorm
305:     );
306:     float farFade = smoothstep(28.0, 48.0, distanceToCamera);
307:     vec3 currentFogColor = mix(heightFogColor, vec3(0.0), farFade);
308:     if (uOutdoor == 1) {
309:         currentFogColor = uFogColor;
310:     }
311:     color = mix(color, currentFogColor, clamp(fogAmount, 0.0, 1.0));
312: 
313:     // Flare cores (shared chunk; occluded by nearer surfaces).
314:     color += flareCores(vWorldPos, uCameraPosition);
315: 
316:     color = toneMap(color);
317:     color += (ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5) * (1.0 / 128.0) * (1.0 - fogAmount) * float(uDitherEnabled);
318: 
319:     fragColor = vec4(color, 1.0);
320: }
321: "#;
322: 
323: /// Assembles the vertex shader (quad rebuild + all lighting, flat).
324: pub fn vertex_source() -> String {
325:     let mut source = String::with_capacity(
326:         VERTEX_HEADER.len()
327:             + chunks::MATERIAL_COLOR_GLSL.len()
328:             + chunks::NOISE_GLSL.len()
329:             + chunks::SPOT_CONE_GLSL.len()
330:             + VERTEX_BODY.len(),
331:     );
332:     source.push_str(VERTEX_HEADER);
333:     source.push_str(chunks::MATERIAL_COLOR_GLSL);
334:     source.push_str(chunks::NOISE_GLSL);
335:     source.push_str(chunks::SPOT_CONE_GLSL);
336:     source.push_str(VERTEX_BODY);
337:     source
338: }
339: 
340: /// Assembles the (deliberately tiny) fragment shader.
341: pub fn fragment_source() -> String {
342:     let mut source = String::with_capacity(
343:         FRAGMENT_HEADER.len()
344:             + chunks::NOISE_GLSL.len()
345:             + chunks::TONE_MAP_GLSL.len()
346:             + chunks::FLARE_CORES_GLSL.len()
347:             + FRAGMENT_BODY.len(),
348:     );
349:     source.push_str(FRAGMENT_HEADER);
350:     source.push_str(chunks::NOISE_GLSL);
351:     source.push_str(chunks::TONE_MAP_GLSL);
352:     source.push_str(chunks::FLARE_CORES_GLSL);
353:     source.push_str(FRAGMENT_BODY);
354:     source
355: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Per-frame face-splat pipeline.
  2: //!
  3: //! The sequence is intentionally explicit and made of small stages:
  4: //!
  5: //! 1. clear and establish fixed-function state;
  6: //! 2. select visible chunks near-to-far;
  7: //! 3. select the bounded set of most important lights;
  8: //! 4. optionally render the hero-light shadow map;
  9: //! 5. bind frame uniforms once;
 10: //! 6. draw whole instance pages or coalesced visible cell ranges.
 11: //!
 12: //! Every optional shortcut is labeled at its branch and controlled by the
 13: //! shared `RenderToggles` switchboard.
````
