 1: //! The pluggable level-generator port: each Backrooms "level" (Level 0
 2: //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
 3: //!
 4: //! Contract for implementors:
 5: //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
 6: //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
 7: //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
 8: //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
 9: //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
10: //!   ~1 world unit wide.
11: //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
12: //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
13: //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the
14: //!   orchestrating use case runs the exposed-face lighting bake afterwards.
15: 
16: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
17: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
18: use crate::entities::models::Position;
19: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
20: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
21: 
22: /// Well-known level ids (the `GeneratorConfig::level` / noclip targets).
23: pub const LEVEL_BACKROOMS: u32 = 0;
24: /// Level 1, the Habitable Zone: concrete warehouse/parking structure.
25: pub const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
26: pub const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
27: /// The pre-canon office blueprint, kept reachable for tests and archaeology.
28: /// It vacated id 1 when the canonical Level 1 landed.
29: pub const LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES: u32 = 90;
30: 
31: pub trait LevelGenerator {
32:     /// Fills one chunk. `chunk_pos` is the chunk origin in world units.
33:     fn generate(
34:         &self,
35:         chunk_pos: Position,
36:         seed: u32,
37:         config: GeneratorConfig,
38:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
39:     ) -> VoxelGrid;
40: 
41:     /// Fills one chunk under a deterministic encounter-state snapshot.
42:     ///
43:     /// Most levels are entirely immutable and inherit this implementation.
44:     /// Level 0 overrides it so anomaly infill/topology can be a pure function
45:     /// of the same snapshot that keyed the chunk request. Keeping the legacy
46:     /// `generate` entry point makes stateless tools and tests explicit users
47:     /// of epoch zero.
48:     fn generate_with_reality(
49:         &self,
50:         chunk_pos: Position,
51:         seed: u32,
52:         config: GeneratorConfig,
53:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
54:         _reality: &RealitySnapshot,
55:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
56:         self.generate(chunk_pos, seed, config, noise)
57:     }
58: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs
````rust
  1: //! A finite, one-sided spotlight used by the CPU splatter.
  2: //!
  3: //! The module keeps the four independent responsibilities visible:
  4: //!
  5: //! 1. [`cone_falloff`] describes the lamp's angular intensity profile;
  6: //! 2. inverse-square attenuation describes transport through distance;
  7: //! 3. a Lambert cosine describes how the receiver faces the lamp;
  8: //! 4. [`segment_is_occluded`] optionally tests geometric visibility.
  9: //!
 10: //! Occlusion is deliberately not folded into the light equation. Disabling
 11: //! `rt_beam_occlusion` removes only the visibility query; it cannot change
 12: //! the cone, range, color, or receiver response.
 13: 
 14: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 15: #[cfg(test)]
 16: use crate::application::rendering::compact_support_window;
 17: use crate::application::rendering::{
 18:     finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation, lambertian_receiver_cosine,
 19: };
 20: 
 21: use super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 22: use super::raycast::{ray_box_interval, svo_segment_is_occluded};
 23: use super::settings::CpuFlashlightVisibility;
 24: 
 25: /// Full-strength core and soft outer edge of the angular profile.
 26: pub const INNER_DEG: f32 = 11.0;
 27: pub const OUTER_DEG: f32 = 24.0;
 28: /// Finite support of the lamp in world units.
 29: pub const RANGE_END: f32 = 14.0;
 30: /// Radiometric scale before inverse-square transport. It is intentionally a
 31: /// named calibration constant rather than a hidden post-lighting boost.
 32: pub const INTENSITY: f32 = 32.0;
 33: /// Finite source-radius clamp, preventing a singularity against the lamp.
 34: pub const MINIMUM_DISTANCE: f32 = 0.25;
 35: /// Lamp offset from the eye: a small hand-held parallax, not an eye glow.
 36: pub const LAMP_FORWARD: f32 = 0.18;
 37: pub const LAMP_DOWN: f32 = 0.10;
 38: /// Warm-white spectral tint in linear RGB.
 39: pub const TINT: [f32; 3] = [1.0, 0.91, 0.72];
 40: 
 41: /// Fixed world-space endpoint tolerances for the visibility segment.
 42: const OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 43: const OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 44: 
 45: fn smoothstep01(t: f32) -> f32 {
 46:     let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 47:     t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
 48: }
 49: 
 50: /// Angular intensity: one in the core, zero outside the outer cone, and a
 51: /// smooth transition between them. `alignment` is `cos(theta)`.
 52: pub fn cone_falloff(alignment: f32) -> f32 {
 53:     let inner_cos = INNER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 54:     let outer_cos = OUTER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 55:     if !alignment.is_finite() || alignment <= outer_cos {
 56:         return 0.0;
 57:     }
 58:     smoothstep01((alignment - outer_cos) / (inner_cos - outer_cos))
 59: }
 60: 
 61: /// Compact-support window used by the inverse-square term. Exposing it
 62: /// separately makes range behavior easy to inspect in diagnostics/tests.
 63: #[cfg(test)]
 64: pub fn range_falloff(distance: f32) -> f32 {
 65:     compact_support_window(distance, RANGE_END)
 66: }
 67: 
 68: fn lamp_position(cam: &Camera) -> [f32; 3] {
 69:     [
 70:         cam.pos[0] + cam.forward[0] * LAMP_FORWARD,
 71:         cam.pos[1] + cam.forward[1] * LAMP_FORWARD - LAMP_DOWN,
 72:         cam.pos[2] + cam.forward[2] * LAMP_FORWARD,
 73:     ]
 74: }
 75: 
 76: fn normalized_direction(from: [f32; 3], to: [f32; 3]) -> Option<([f32; 3], f32)> {
 77:     let delta = [to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1], to[2] - from[2]];
 78:     let distance = dot(delta, delta).sqrt();
 79:     if !distance.is_finite() || distance <= 1.0e-4 {
 80:         return None;
 81:     }
 82:     Some((delta.map(|component| component / distance), distance))
 83: }
 84: 
 85: /// The splatter shades an axis-aligned cube at one representative surface
 86: /// point and normal. Full bounds stop the visibility ray at the physical
 87: /// near face; transport is evaluated at `sample_position`.
 88: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 89: pub struct BeamReceiver {
 90:     center: [f32; 3],
 91:     sample_position: [f32; 3],
 92:     half_extent: f32,
 93:     normal: [f32; 3],
 94: }
 95: 
 96: impl BeamReceiver {
 97:     #[cfg(test)]
 98:     pub fn cube(center: [f32; 3], world_size: f32, normal: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 99:         Self {
100:             center,
101:             sample_position: center,
102:             half_extent: (world_size * 0.5).max(0.0),
103:             normal,
104:         }
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Uses an explicit representative point on the cube's visible surface
108:     /// while retaining the full bounds for the occlusion endpoint.
109:     pub fn surface_sample(
110:         center: [f32; 3],
111:         world_size: f32,
112:         sample_position: [f32; 3],
113:         normal: [f32; 3],
114:     ) -> Self {
115:         Self {
116:             center,
117:             sample_position,
118:             half_extent: (world_size * 0.5).max(0.0),
119:             normal,
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     fn bounds(self) -> ([f32; 3], [f32; 3]) {
124:         (
125:             self.center.map(|value| value - self.half_extent),
126:             self.center.map(|value| value + self.half_extent),
127:         )
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: /// Pure unoccluded spotlight irradiance at one representative receiver.
132: ///
133: /// ```text
134: /// E = tint * I * cone(theta) * window(d, R) / max(d, d_min)^2
135: ///          * max(dot(n, omega_to_lamp), 0)
136: /// ```
137: pub fn unoccluded_irradiance(cam: &Camera, receiver: BeamReceiver) -> [f32; 3] {
138:     let lamp = lamp_position(cam);
139:     let Some((lamp_to_receiver, distance)) = normalized_direction(lamp, receiver.sample_position)
140:     else {
141:         return [0.0; 3];
142:     };
143: 
144:     let cone = cone_falloff(dot(lamp_to_receiver, cam.forward));
145:     let facing = lambertian_receiver_cosine(receiver.normal, lamp_to_receiver.map(|v| -v));
146:     let attenuation =
147:         finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(distance, RANGE_END, MINIMUM_DISTANCE);
148:     let scalar = INTENSITY * cone * facing * attenuation;
149:     TINT.map(|channel| channel * scalar)
150: }
151: 
152: fn occlusion_trace_length(lamp_to_receiver_face: f32) -> Option<f32> {
153:     let length = lamp_to_receiver_face - OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS - OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS;
154:     (length > 0.0).then_some(length)
155: }
156: 
157: /// Tests only visibility of the finite lamp-to-receiver segment.
158: fn segment_is_occluded(
159:     cam: &Camera,
160:     atlas: &[u32],
161:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
162:     receiver: BeamReceiver,
163: ) -> bool {
164:     let lamp = lamp_position(cam);
165:     let Some((direction, _)) = normalized_direction(lamp, receiver.sample_position) else {
166:         return false;
167:     };
168:     let (bounds_min, bounds_max) = receiver.bounds();
169:     let Some(interval) = ray_box_interval(lamp, direction, bounds_min, bounds_max) else {
170:         return false;
171:     };
172:     let receiver_face = interval.entry.max(0.0);
173:     let Some(max_trace) = occlusion_trace_length(receiver_face) else {
174:         return false;
175:     };
176:     let origin = [
177:         lamp[0] + direction[0] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
178:         lamp[1] + direction[1] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
179:         lamp[2] + direction[2] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
180:     ];
181:     svo_segment_is_occluded(atlas, chunks, origin, direction, max_trace)
182: }
183: 
184: /// Spotlight irradiance with optional SVO visibility. The toggle is an
185: /// independent cost/quality switch: off is exactly the pure unoccluded term.
186: pub fn beam_contribution(
187:     cam: &Camera,
188:     atlas: &[u32],
189:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
190:     receiver: BeamReceiver,
191:     visibility: CpuFlashlightVisibility,
192: ) -> [f32; 3] {
193:     let irradiance = unoccluded_irradiance(cam, receiver);
194:     if irradiance == [0.0; 3] {
195:         return irradiance;
196:     }
197:     if visibility == CpuFlashlightVisibility::TraceScene
198:         && segment_is_occluded(cam, atlas, chunks, receiver)
199:     {
200:         [0.0; 3]
201:     } else {
202:         irradiance
203:     }
204: }
205:

  1: //! Derive static direct lights from the emissive surfaces that are actually
  2: //! present in a generated voxel grid.
  3: //!
  4: //! Architectural fixture metadata is useful while planning a scene, but it
  5: //! is not authoritative after voxelization: anomalies, walls, and LOD
  6: //! quantization can remove or reshape a fixture. This adapter therefore reads
  7: //! the same halo grid that is meshed. A direct light exists exactly when a
  8: //! downward-facing emissive surface exists.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 11:     VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VoxelGrid,
 12:     material_color_f32, material_emission_strength,
 13: };
 14: use vackrooms::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS;
 15: 
 16: use crate::application::ports::{LightKind, LightSource, POSITION_FIXED_SCALE};
 17: 
 18: /// The direct-light spectrum comes from the authoritative visible-material
 19: /// palette, decoded to linear RGB. The low-precision voxel bake has its own
 20: /// deliberately coarser 0--15 spectrum and must not leak into this contract.
 21: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 22: struct EmissionProfile {
 23:     linear_rgb: [f32; 3],
 24:     /// Linear emitted-radiance scale used by the analytic area-light model.
 25:     /// This deliberately matches `emittedRadiance`/`emittedVoxelRadiance`:
 26:     /// normalizing a 0--15 bake sample to intensity 1 made a physical area
 27:     /// integral roughly an order of magnitude too dark.
 28:     radiance: f32,
 29:     kind: LightKind,
 30: }
 31: 
 32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
 33: struct ComponentKey {
 34:     material: u8,
 35:     min_world_fixed: [i64; 3],
 36:     max_world_fixed: [i64; 3],
 37: }
 38: 
 39: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
 40: struct ComponentBounds {
 41:     material: u8,
 42:     y: usize,
 43:     min_x: usize,
 44:     max_x_exclusive: usize,
 45:     min_z: usize,
 46:     max_z_exclusive: usize,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: /// Collects non-overlapping world-space rectangles that exactly cover every
 50: /// exposed emissive underside owned by the logical chunk interior.
 51: ///
 52: /// Halo cells are deliberately excluded from ownership. Neighboring chunks
 53: /// may both *inspect* those cells for meshing, but only the chunk containing a
 54: /// cell emits its light rectangle. This prevents a boundary panel from being
 55: /// counted twice. A deterministic greedy rectangle cover preserves L-shaped
 56: /// or damaged fixtures without inventing emission over their empty holes.
 57: pub fn collect_emissive_lights(
 58:     halo_grid: &VoxelGrid,
 59:     voxel_size: f32,
 60:     halo_world_origin: [f32; 3],
 61:     lateral_padding: usize,
 62: ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 63:     if !valid_transform(voxel_size, halo_world_origin)
 64:         || halo_grid.width() <= lateral_padding * 2
 65:         || halo_grid.depth() <= lateral_padding * 2
 66:     {
 67:         return Vec::new();
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     let mut visited = vec![false; halo_grid.width() * halo_grid.height() * halo_grid.depth()];
 71:     let mut keyed_lights = Vec::new();
 72: 
 73:     // Explicit loop order plus a fixed neighbour order keeps component
 74:     // discovery deterministic without depending on a hash collection.
 75:     for y in 1..halo_grid.height() {
 76:         for z in lateral_padding..halo_grid.depth() - lateral_padding {
 77:             for x in lateral_padding..halo_grid.width() - lateral_padding {
 78:                 let index = grid_index(halo_grid, x, y, z);
 79:                 if visited[index] || !is_exposed_underside(halo_grid, x, y, z) {
 80:                     continue;
 81:                 }
 82: 
 83:                 let component =
 84:                     collect_owned_rectangle(halo_grid, x, y, z, lateral_padding, &mut visited);
 85:                 let key = component_key(component, voxel_size, halo_world_origin);
 86:                 keyed_lights.push((
 87:                     key,
 88:                     light_from_component(component, key, voxel_size, halo_world_origin),
 89:                 ));
 90:             }
 91:         }
 92:     }
 93: 
 94:     keyed_lights.sort_unstable_by_key(|(key, _)| *key);
 95:     keyed_lights.dedup_by(|(left, _), (right, _)| left == right);
 96:     keyed_lights.into_iter().map(|(_, light)| light).collect()
 97: }
 98: 
 99: fn valid_transform(voxel_size: f32, origin: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
100:     voxel_size.is_finite() && voxel_size > 0.0 && origin.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
101: }
102: 
103: fn is_exposed_underside(grid: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> bool {
104:     emission_profile(grid.get(x, y, z)).is_some() && grid.get(x, y - 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR
105: }
106: 
107: /// Finds the widest first row, then extends only while every cell in that row
108: /// remains the same exposed material. Marking exactly that rectangle makes
109: /// subsequent passes cover any remainder without overlaps or phantom area.
110: fn collect_owned_rectangle(
111:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
112:     start_x: usize,
113:     y: usize,
114:     start_z: usize,
115:     lateral_padding: usize,
116:     visited: &mut [bool],
117: ) -> ComponentBounds {
118:     let material = grid.get(start_x, y, start_z);
119:     let owned_x_end = grid.width() - lateral_padding;
120:     let owned_z_end = grid.depth() - lateral_padding;
121: 
122:     let mut max_x_exclusive = start_x;
123:     while max_x_exclusive < owned_x_end
124:         && rectangle_cell_matches(grid, max_x_exclusive, y, start_z, material, visited)
125:     {
126:         max_x_exclusive += 1;
127:     }
128: 
129:     let mut max_z_exclusive = start_z + 1;
130:     while max_z_exclusive < owned_z_end
131:         && (start_x..max_x_exclusive)
132:             .all(|x| rectangle_cell_matches(grid, x, y, max_z_exclusive, material, visited))
133:     {
134:         max_z_exclusive += 1;
135:     }
136: 
137:     for z in start_z..max_z_exclusive {
138:         for x in start_x..max_x_exclusive {
139:             visited[grid_index(grid, x, y, z)] = true;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     ComponentBounds {
144:         material,
145:         y,
146:         min_x: start_x,
147:         max_x_exclusive,
148:         min_z: start_z,
149:         max_z_exclusive,
150:     }
151: }
152: 
153: fn rectangle_cell_matches(
154:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
155:     x: usize,
156:     y: usize,
157:     z: usize,
158:     material: u8,
159:     visited: &[bool],
160: ) -> bool {
161:     !visited[grid_index(grid, x, y, z)]
162:         && grid.get(x, y, z) == material
163:         && is_exposed_underside(grid, x, y, z)
164: }
165: 
166: fn grid_index(grid: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> usize {
167:     y * grid.width() * grid.depth() + z * grid.width() + x
168: }
169: 
170: fn component_key(component: ComponentBounds, voxel_size: f32, origin: [f32; 3]) -> ComponentKey {
171:     let min_world = [
172:         origin[0] + component.min_x as f32 * voxel_size,
173:         origin[1] + component.y as f32 * voxel_size,
174:         origin[2] + component.min_z as f32 * voxel_size,
175:     ];
176:     let max_world = [
177:         origin[0] + component.max_x_exclusive as f32 * voxel_size,
178:         min_world[1],
179:         origin[2] + component.max_z_exclusive as f32 * voxel_size,
180:     ];
181:     ComponentKey {
182:         material: component.material,
183:         min_world_fixed: min_world.map(world_to_fixed),
184:         max_world_fixed: max_world.map(world_to_fixed),
185:     }
186: }
187: 
188: fn world_to_fixed(value: f32) -> i64 {
189:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE).round() as i64
190: }
191: 
192: fn light_from_component(
193:     component: ComponentBounds,
194:     key: ComponentKey,
195:     voxel_size: f32,
196:     origin: [f32; 3],
197: ) -> LightSource {
198:     let width = (component.max_x_exclusive - component.min_x) as f32 * voxel_size;
199:     let depth = (component.max_z_exclusive - component.min_z) as f32 * voxel_size;
200:     let profile = emission_profile(component.material)
201:         .expect("components are seeded only from emissive materials");
202:     let kind = if profile.kind == LightKind::Emergency {
203:         LightKind::Emergency
204:     } else if width > depth * 2.0 || depth > width * 2.0 {
205:         LightKind::Strip
206:     } else {
207:         LightKind::CeilingPanel
208:     };
209: 
210:     let id = stable_id(key);
211:     LightSource {
212:         id,
213:         position: [
214:             origin[0] + (component.min_x + component.max_x_exclusive) as f32 * voxel_size * 0.5,
215:             origin[1] + component.y as f32 * voxel_size,
216:             origin[2] + (component.min_z + component.max_z_exclusive) as f32 * voxel_size * 0.5,
217:         ],
218:         half_size: [width * 0.5, depth * 0.5],
219:         color: profile.linear_rgb,
220:         radius: DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS,
221:         intensity: profile.radiance,
222:         kind,
223:         flicker_mode: flicker_mode_for(component.material, id),
224:         enabled: true,
225:     }
226: }
227: 
228: /// "The lights buzz and fluctuate severely and randomly at a constant rate."
229: /// A deterministic share of the warm office panels carry a flicker mode the
230: /// application animates CPU-side each frame: most hum steadily, some shimmer
231: /// on a tired ballast, and a few are actively dying. Red pressure fixtures
232: /// and cold glimmers hold perfectly steady — their wrongness is composure.
233: fn flicker_mode_for(material: u8, id: u64) -> u8 {
234:     if material != VOXEL_LIGHT {
235:         return 0;
236:     }
237:     // The id is already an FNV hash of world-space identity; fold it once
238:     // more so the low bits used here are decorrelated from dedup ordering.
239:     let mut h = id ^ (id >> 33);
240:     h = h.wrapping_mul(0xFF51_AFD7_ED55_8CCD);
241:     match (h >> 40) % 100 {
242:         0..=11 => 1, // tired ballast shimmer
243:         12..=15 => 2, // dying tube: hard dropouts
244:         _ => 0,
245:     }
246: }
247: 
248: fn emission_profile(material: u8) -> Option<EmissionProfile> {
249:     let kind = match material {
250:         VOXEL_LIGHT | VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => LightKind::CeilingPanel,
251:         VOXEL_GLIMMER => LightKind::Emergency,
252:         _ => return None,
253:     };
254:     Some(EmissionProfile {
255:         linear_rgb: material_color_f32(material).map(srgb_channel_to_linear),
256:         radiance: material_emission_strength(material)?,
257:         kind,
258:     })
259: }
260: 
261: fn srgb_channel_to_linear(channel: f32) -> f32 {
262:     if channel <= 0.04045 {
263:         channel / 12.92
264:     } else {
265:         ((channel + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
266:     }
267: }
268: 
269: /// FNV-1a over the full fixed-point world-space identity. Hash collisions are
270: /// not used for local deduplication (the complete key is), while the compact
271: /// `u64` remains convenient for scene-wide halo deduplication.
272: fn stable_id(key: ComponentKey) -> u64 {
273:     const FNV_OFFSET: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
274:     const FNV_PRIME: u64 = 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3;
275: 
276:     let mut hash = FNV_OFFSET;
277:     for byte in std::iter::once(key.material).chain(
278:         key.min_world_fixed
279:             .into_iter()
280:             .chain(key.max_world_fixed)
281:             .flat_map(i64::to_le_bytes),
282:     ) {
283:         hash ^= u64::from(byte);
284:         hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
285:     }
286:     hash
287: }
288: 
289: #[cfg(test)]

````rust
  1: //! Converts greedy-merged quads into the splat renderer's compact face
  2: //! instances: one error-selected, axis-aligned surface rectangle each.
  3: //!
  4: //! The instances derive from the *same* [`MergedQuad`] list as the indexed
  5: //! mesh, so the splat renderer's visible boundary and the mesh-based shadow
  6: //! caster can never disagree. Two transformations happen on the way:
  7: //!
  8: //! * **Extent capping** — a merged quad longer than [`MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS`]
  9: //!   on either axis is split into pieces, because the splat path lights each
 10: //!   face with one flat sample; one sample across a 10 u wall would smear.
 11: //! * **Cell bucketing** — instances are sorted by [`FACE_CELL_UNITS`] cell so
 12: //!   the driver can draw or cull contiguous ranges with zero per-frame
 13: //!   rebuild work.
 14: //!
 15: //! Like the rest of the adapters layer this is platform-free and natively
 16: //! unit-tested.
 17: 
 18: use vackrooms::adapters::voxel_mapper::{FaceDirection, MergedQuad};
 19: 
 20: use crate::adapters::surface_mesh::material_id;
 21: use crate::application::ports::{
 22:     FACE_INSTANCE_FLAG_EMISSIVE, FaceCellRange, FaceInstanceSet, POSITION_FIXED_SCALE,
 23:     PackedFaceInstance,
 24: };
 25: 
 26: /// Longest face edge in world units before a quad is split. Keeps one flat
 27: /// per-face light/shadow sample honest on large merged planes.
 28: pub const MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS: f32 = 2.5;
 29: /// World size of one culling cell (matches the extent cap so a face never
 30: /// spans more than ~two cells).
 31: pub const FACE_CELL_UNITS: f32 = 2.5;
 32: 
 33: /// Builds the face-instance page for one chunk from its greedy quads.
 34: /// `voxel_scale` is the world size of one voxel cell at this LOD; quad
 35: /// geometry is exact multiples of it.
 36: pub fn build_face_instances(quads: &[MergedQuad], voxel_scale: f32) -> FaceInstanceSet {
 37:     let max_cells = ((MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS / voxel_scale).floor() as u32).max(1);
 38:     let mut instances = Vec::with_capacity(quads.len());
 39:     for quad in quads {
 40:         emit_capped(quad, voxel_scale, max_cells, &mut instances);
 41:     }
 42: 
 43:     // Sort by culling cell so each cell's instances form one contiguous run.
 44:     let cell_of = |inst: &PackedFaceInstance| -> [u8; 3] {
 45:         let mut cell = [0u8; 3];
 46:         for axis in 0..3 {
 47:             let world = inst.position[axis] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE;
 48:             cell[axis] = (world / FACE_CELL_UNITS).floor().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8;
 49:         }
 50:         cell
 51:     };
 52:     instances.sort_by_key(|inst| {
 53:         let c = cell_of(inst);
 54:         (c[0], c[1], c[2])
 55:     });
 56: 
 57:     let mut cells: Vec<FaceCellRange> = Vec::new();
 58:     for (index, inst) in instances.iter().enumerate() {
 59:         let cell = cell_of(inst);
 60:         match cells.last_mut() {
 61:             Some(range) if range.cell == cell => range.count += 1,
 62:             _ => cells.push(FaceCellRange {
 63:                 cell,
 64:                 offset: index as u32,
 65:                 count: 1,
 66:             }),
 67:         }
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     FaceInstanceSet {
 71:         instances,
 72:         cells,
 73:         cell_size: FACE_CELL_UNITS,
 74:     }
 75: }
 76: 
 77: /// Face frame of one quad: the fixed plane coordinate plus the two in-plane
 78: /// axes. U/V axis assignment matches the splat vertex shader (U = X for
 79: /// Y/Z-normal faces, Y for X-normal faces; V = the remaining axis).
 80: struct FaceFrame {
 81:     /// World axis index the face is perpendicular to.
 82:     plane_axis: usize,
 83:     /// Face plane coordinate along `plane_axis`.
 84:     plane: f32,
 85:     u_axis: usize,
 86:     v_axis: usize,
 87:     min_u: f32,
 88:     min_v: f32,
 89:     cells_u: u32,
 90:     cells_v: u32,
 91: }
 92: 
 93: fn face_frame(quad: &MergedQuad, s: f32) -> FaceFrame {
 94:     let cells = |len: f32| ((len / s).round() as u32).max(1);
 95:     match quad.dir {
 96:         // Horizontal faces: `w` spans X, `h` spans Z (see surface_mesh).
 97:         FaceDirection::Up | FaceDirection::Down => FaceFrame {
 98:             plane_axis: 1,
 99:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::Up {
100:                 quad.y + s
101:             } else {
102:                 quad.y
103:             },
104:             u_axis: 0,
105:             v_axis: 2,
106:             min_u: quad.x,
107:             min_v: quad.z,
108:             cells_u: cells(quad.w),
109:             cells_v: cells(quad.h),
110:         },
111:         // Z-normal faces: `w` spans X, `h` spans Y.
112:         FaceDirection::North | FaceDirection::South => FaceFrame {
113:             plane_axis: 2,
114:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::South {
115:                 quad.z + s
116:             } else {
117:                 quad.z
118:             },
119:             u_axis: 0,
120:             v_axis: 1,
121:             min_u: quad.x,
122:             min_v: quad.y,
123:             cells_u: cells(quad.w),
124:             cells_v: cells(quad.h),
125:         },
126:         // X-normal faces: `h` spans Y, `w` spans Z.
127:         FaceDirection::East | FaceDirection::West => FaceFrame {
128:             plane_axis: 0,
129:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::East {
130:                 quad.x + s
131:             } else {
132:                 quad.x
133:             },
134:             u_axis: 1,
135:             v_axis: 2,
136:             min_u: quad.y,
137:             min_v: quad.z,
138:             cells_u: cells(quad.h),
139:             cells_v: cells(quad.w),
140:         },
141:     }
142: }
143: 
144: fn emit_capped(quad: &MergedQuad, s: f32, max_cells: u32, out: &mut Vec<PackedFaceInstance>) {
145:     let frame = face_frame(quad, s);
146:     let material = material_id(quad.v_type);
147:     let flags = if vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material) {
148:         FACE_INSTANCE_FLAG_EMISSIVE
149:     } else {
150:         0
151:     };
152:     let normal_axis = normal_axis(quad.dir);
153: 
154:     let mut u_off = 0;
155:     while u_off < frame.cells_u {
156:         let piece_u = max_cells.min(frame.cells_u - u_off);
157:         let mut v_off = 0;
158:         while v_off < frame.cells_v {
159:             let piece_v = max_cells.min(frame.cells_v - v_off);
160:             let center_u = frame.min_u + (u_off as f32 + piece_u as f32 * 0.5) * s;
161:             let center_v = frame.min_v + (v_off as f32 + piece_v as f32 * 0.5) * s;
162:             let mut position = [0.0f32; 3];
163:             position[frame.plane_axis] = frame.plane;
164:             position[frame.u_axis] = center_u;
165:             position[frame.v_axis] = center_v;
166:             out.push(PackedFaceInstance {
167:                 position: position.map(pack_position),
168:                 extent_u: piece_u.min(u8::MAX as u32) as u8,
169:                 extent_v: piece_v.min(u8::MAX as u32) as u8,
170:                 normal_axis,
171:                 material,
172:                 baked_light: quad.light,
173:                 ao: quad.ao,
174:                 flags,
175:                 reserved: [0; 3],
176:             });
177:             v_off += piece_v;
178:         }
179:         u_off += piece_u;
180:     }
181: }
182: 
183: fn pack_position(value: f32) -> u16 {
184:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE)
185:         .round()
186:         .clamp(0.0, u16::MAX as f32) as u16
187: }
188: 
189: /// Same encoding as `surface_mesh::normal_axis` / the shaders' `normalForAxis`.
190: fn normal_axis(dir: FaceDirection) -> u8 {
191:     match dir {
192:         FaceDirection::Up => 0,
193:         FaceDirection::Down => 1,
194:         FaceDirection::North => 2,
195:         FaceDirection::South => 3,
196:         FaceDirection::East => 4,
197:         FaceDirection::West => 5,
198:     }
199: }
200:

206: 
207:     fn world(pos: u16) -> f32 {

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/player.rs
````rust
  1: //! First-person player controller: mouse look, WASD movement with friction,
  2: //! and axis-separated sliding collision against the [`CollisionWorld`].
  3: //!
  4: //! The tuning constants are carried over 1:1 from the original JS client so
  5: //! the wasm port feels identical.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::collision::CollisionWorld;
  8: 
  9: /// Acceleration applied while a movement key is held (units/s^2 toward the
 10: /// wish direction). Terminal speed = ACCELERATION / FRICTION = 2.5 u/s (increased from 0.5 u/s).
 11: const ACCELERATION: f32 = 20.0;
 12: /// Exponential velocity damping factor (1/s).
 13: const FRICTION: f32 = 8.0;
 14: /// Radians of yaw/pitch per pixel of mouse movement.
 15: const MOUSE_SENSITIVITY: f32 = 0.002;
 16: /// Pitch is clamped just short of straight up/down to avoid gimbal flip.
 17: const PITCH_LIMIT: f32 = std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2 - 0.05;
 18: 
 19: /// Which movement keys are currently held.
 20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
 21: pub struct MoveIntent {
 22:     pub forward: bool,
 23:     pub backward: bool,
 24:     pub left: bool,
 25:     pub right: bool,
 26:     pub turn_left: bool,
 27:     pub turn_right: bool,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// Player state. Position is the *eye* position in world space.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 32: pub struct Player {
 33:     pub position: [f32; 3],
 34:     pub yaw: f32,
 35:     pub pitch: f32,
 36:     /// Velocity in camera-local space: x = strafe, z = forward.
 37:     vel_strafe: f32,
 38:     vel_forward: f32,
 39: }
 40: 
 41: impl Player {
 42:     pub fn new(position: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 43:         Self {
 44:             position,
 45:             yaw: 0.0,
 46:             pitch: 0.0,
 47:             vel_strafe: 0.0,
 48:             vel_forward: 0.0,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     /// Moves the player to an authored recovery point and clears momentum.
 53:     /// Pit relocation uses this instead of assigning `position` directly so
 54:     /// the velocity that carried the player over the edge cannot immediately
 55:     /// push them back into the same hazard.
 56:     pub fn relocate(&mut self, position: [f32; 3]) {
 57:         self.position = position;
 58:         self.vel_strafe = 0.0;
 59:         self.vel_forward = 0.0;
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     /// Applies a mouse movement delta (in pixels) to yaw/pitch.
 63:     pub fn apply_look(&mut self, dx: f32, dy: f32) {
 64:         self.yaw -= dx * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY;
 65:         self.pitch = (self.pitch - dy * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY).clamp(-PITCH_LIMIT, PITCH_LIMIT);
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     /// World-space unit forward vector projected on the ground plane.
 69:     pub fn forward(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 70:         [-self.yaw.sin(), 0.0, -self.yaw.cos()]
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     /// World-space unit right vector on the ground plane.
 74:     pub fn right(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 75:         [self.yaw.cos(), 0.0, -self.yaw.sin()]
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     /// Integrates one physics step and resolves collision by sliding:
 79:     /// the X and Z axes are moved and tested independently, so hitting a
 80:     /// wall diagonally slides the player along it instead of stopping dead.
 81:     pub fn step(&mut self, dt: f32, intent: &MoveIntent, world: &CollisionWorld) {
 82:         // Friction: exponential-style decay, matching `v -= v * 8 * dt`.
 83:         self.vel_strafe -= self.vel_strafe * FRICTION * dt;
 84:         self.vel_forward -= self.vel_forward * FRICTION * dt;
 85: 
 86:         // Turn via keyboard (Doom controls)
 87:         let turn_speed = 3.0; // radians per second
 88:         if intent.turn_left {
 89:             self.yaw += turn_speed * dt;
 90:         }
 91:         if intent.turn_right {
 92:             self.yaw -= turn_speed * dt;
 93:         }
 94: 
 95:         let mut wish_forward = (intent.forward as i32 - intent.backward as i32) as f32;
 96:         let mut wish_strafe = (intent.right as i32 - intent.left as i32) as f32;
 97:         let len = (wish_forward * wish_forward + wish_strafe * wish_strafe).sqrt();
 98:         if len > 0.0 {
 99:             wish_forward /= len;
100:             wish_strafe /= len;
101:         }
102: 
103:         self.vel_forward += wish_forward * ACCELERATION * dt;
104:         self.vel_strafe += wish_strafe * ACCELERATION * dt;
105: 
106:         let fwd = self.forward();
107:         let rgt = self.right();
108:         let step_x = (fwd[0] * self.vel_forward + rgt[0] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
109:         let step_z = (fwd[2] * self.vel_forward + rgt[2] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
110: 
111:         let old = self.position;
112: 
113:         self.position[0] = old[0] + step_x;
114:         if world.collides(self.position) {
115:             self.position[0] = old[0];
116:         }
117: 
118:         self.position[2] = old[2] + step_z;
119:         if world.collides(self.position) {
120:             self.position[2] = old[2];
121:         }
122:     }
123: }
124:

  1: //! Renderer optimization toggles — one switch per labeled optimization.
  2: //!
  3: //! Every renderer in the engine (GPU surfaces, GPU face splats, the SVO
  4: //! raymarcher, and the CPU splatter) is written as a *correct, simple
  5: //! reference path* plus a set of clearly labeled optimizations layered on
  6: //! top. Each optimization can be disabled at runtime, which serves three
  7: //! purposes:
  8: //!
  9: //! 1. **Debugging** — when a frame looks wrong, binary-search the toggles to
 10: //!    find which optimization broke it.
 11: //! 2. **Benchmarking** — measure exactly what each optimization buys on a
 12: //!    given machine (the HUD shows frame times).
 13: //! 3. **Documentation** — the toggle list *is* the catalog of every shortcut
 14: //!    the pipeline takes.
 15: //!
 16: //! The struct is plain data with no browser dependencies, so it is natively
 17: //! unit-tested. It crosses the wasm boundary as a bitfield (one `AtomicU32`
 18: //! in `lib.rs`). Each browser driver snapshots it once at the frame boundary;
 19: //! platform-free render code receives the snapshot by value.
 20: //!
 21: //! URL controls: `?rt_hiz=0&rt_shadows=0` … (`rt_<name>=0|1`). The settings
 22: //! menu calls the `set_render_toggle(name, enabled)` wasm export with the
 23: //! same names.
 24: 
 25: /// One on/off switch per optimization, across all render paths.
 26: ///
 27: /// Correctness-preserving switches default on. The approximate diffuse-fill
 28: /// bake defaults off: first boot uses the strict analytic-light image, while
 29: /// `rt_bake=1` opts into the quantized field explicitly.
 30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 31: pub struct RenderToggles {
 32:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 33:     // CPU splatter (SoftwareRasterizer)
 34:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 35:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): 8x8-tile coarse hierarchical z-buffer. Rejects a
 36:     /// whole octree subtree with a handful of tile reads when something
 37:     /// nearer already covers its screen bounds. Off = every node is tested
 38:     /// per-pixel by the fine z-buffer only.
 39:     pub hierarchical_z: bool,
 40:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + raymarch): near-to-far traversal (chunks sorted
 41:     /// by distance, octants visited nearest-first). Maximizes early exits
 42:     /// and z-rejection. Off = input order plus explicit nearest-hit
 43:     /// comparison; identical image, more traversal/overdraw.
 44:     pub front_to_back: bool,
 45:     /// OPTIMIZATION (raymarch): jump across the complete empty SVO leaf
 46:     /// containing the current sample. Off = diagnostic finest-voxel DDA;
 47:     /// both paths use the same exact point lookup and must report the same
 48:     /// nearest hit/material/normal.
 49:     pub empty_space_skip: bool,
 50:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): coarse-to-fine LOD — a subtree whose projection
 51:     /// fits in ~a pixel is drawn as one MIP-filtered splat instead of being
 52:     /// descended. Off = full descent to leaves regardless of distance, except
 53:     /// for the renderer's non-optional malformed/workload safety cap.
 54:     pub mip_lod: bool,
 55:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): the flashlight's occlusion ray (one SVO trace per
 56:     /// shaded splat while the flashlight is on). This is a *quality*
 57:     /// optimization: off means the beam shines through walls but shading
 58:     /// gets cheaper.
 59:     pub flashlight_occlusion: bool,
 60:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): query the fine depth buffer before evaluating
 61:     /// fixture, hero, and flashlight radiance. Off = shade every projected
 62:     /// splat and let the ordinary write-time depth test reject it. The image
 63:     /// is identical; only hidden-splat shading work changes.
 64:     pub deferred_shading: bool,
 65:     /// APPROXIMATION (CPU): sibling-count ambient occlusion. Off is the
 66:     /// material/lighting reference with unit ambient visibility.
 67:     pub ambient_occlusion: bool,
 68:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 69:     // GPU paths (surface / splat / raymarch)
 70:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 71:     /// Direct-light visibility. The raymarcher casts exact SVO segments to
 72:     /// every emitter quadrature sample; raster paths use their shadow-map
 73:     /// approximation. Off is a faster explicitly unoccluded diagnostic.
 74:     pub shadow_pass: bool,
 75:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): per-cell instance-range culling. Face instances
 76:     /// are grouped into spatial cells; invisible cells are skipped and
 77:     /// visible neighbors coalesce into one instanced draw. Off = every
 78:     /// resident face is drawn every frame.
 79:     pub cell_culling: bool,
 80:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): stop submitting whole far chunks after the
 81:     /// profile's face budget is exhausted. Off = draw every visible face;
 82:     /// useful as the correctness/reference path when diagnosing pop-out.
 83:     pub face_budget: bool,
 84:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + raster GPU): chunk-level visibility culling
 85:     /// (distance + behind-camera tests). Off = every resident chunk is
 86:     /// submitted.
 87:     pub distance_cull: bool,
 88:     /// Dither/grain/banding-noise post effects (GPU). A visual feature more
 89:     /// than a speedup; toggle to isolate its contribution to the image.
 90:     pub dither: bool,
 91:     /// Optional quantized diffuse-fill field for the surface renderer.
 92:     /// Analytic fixtures remain authoritative because the path-distance bake
 93:     /// is not mathematically equivalent to an area-light integral. The
 94:     /// raymarcher deliberately rejects the field's face-independent SVO
 95:     /// encoding and stays on the strict analytic-light image.
 96:     pub baked_lighting: bool,
 97:     /// `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2` GPU frame timing for the HUD. Off =
 98:     /// no queries issued (some drivers stall on them).
 99:     pub gpu_timer: bool,
100: }
101: 
102: impl Default for RenderToggles {
103:     fn default() -> Self {
104:         Self {
105:             hierarchical_z: true,
106:             front_to_back: true,
107:             empty_space_skip: true,
108:             mip_lod: true,
109:             flashlight_occlusion: true,
110:             deferred_shading: true,
111:             ambient_occlusion: true,
112:             shadow_pass: true,
113:             cell_culling: true,
114:             face_budget: true,
115:             distance_cull: true,
116:             dither: true,
117:             baked_lighting: false,
118:             gpu_timer: true,
119:         }
120:     }
121: }
122: 
123: /// Canonical query-name/bit ordering used by parsing and bitfield round trips.
124: const TOGGLE_BITS: [(&str, u32); 14] = [
125:     ("hiz", 1 << 0),
126:     ("f2b", 1 << 1),
127:     ("mips", 1 << 2),
128:     ("beam_occlusion", 1 << 3),
129:     ("shadows", 1 << 4),
130:     ("cells", 1 << 5),
131:     ("budget", 1 << 6),
132:     ("cull", 1 << 7),
133:     ("dither", 1 << 8),
134:     ("timer", 1 << 9),
135:     ("skip", 1 << 10),
136:     ("bake", 1 << 11),
137:     ("deferred", 1 << 12),
138:     ("ao", 1 << 13),
139: ];
140: 
141: impl RenderToggles {
142:     fn field_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut bool> {
143:         Some(match name {
144:             "hiz" => &mut self.hierarchical_z,
145:             "f2b" => &mut self.front_to_back,
146:             "skip" => &mut self.empty_space_skip,
147:             "mips" => &mut self.mip_lod,
148:             "beam_occlusion" => &mut self.flashlight_occlusion,
149:             "deferred" => &mut self.deferred_shading,
150:             "ao" => &mut self.ambient_occlusion,
151:             "shadows" => &mut self.shadow_pass,
152:             "cells" => &mut self.cell_culling,
153:             "budget" => &mut self.face_budget,
154:             "cull" => &mut self.distance_cull,
155:             "dither" => &mut self.dither,
156:             "bake" => &mut self.baked_lighting,
157:             "timer" => &mut self.gpu_timer,
158:             _ => return None,
159:         })
160:     }
161: 
162:     fn field(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
163:         let mut copy = *self;
164:         copy.field_mut(name).map(|b| *b)
165:     }
166: 
167:     /// Sets one toggle by its short name. Unknown names are ignored (the
168:     /// settings menu and old URLs must never crash the engine).
169:     pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, enabled: bool) {
170:         if let Some(field) = self.field_mut(name) {
171:             *field = enabled;
172:         }
173:     }
174: 
175:     /// Reads one toggle by its short name. Returning `None` for unknown
176:     /// names keeps diagnostics and browser tests on the same catalog as the
177:     /// parser and setter.
178:     pub fn enabled(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
179:         self.field(name)
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Packs the toggles into a bitfield for the atomic global in `lib.rs`.
183:     pub fn to_bits(self) -> u32 {
184:         let mut bits = 0;
185:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
186:             if self.field(name).expect("table names match fields") {
187:                 bits |= bit;
188:             }
189:         }
190:         bits
191:     }
192: 
193:     /// Inverse of [`Self::to_bits`].
194:     pub fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Self {
195:         let mut toggles = Self::default();
196:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
197:             toggles.set(name, bits & bit != 0);
198:         }
199:         toggles
200:     }
201: }
202: 
203: /// Applies `rt_<name>=0|1` pairs from a URL query (with or without the
204: /// leading `?`) on top of the defaults. Unknown keys and malformed values
205: /// are ignored, matching the generation-knob parser's tolerance.
206: pub fn parse_render_toggles(query: &str) -> RenderToggles {
207:     let mut toggles = RenderToggles::default();
208:     for pair in query.trim_start_matches('?').split('&') {
209:         let Some((key, value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
210:             continue;
211:         };
212:         let Some(name) = key.strip_prefix("rt_") else {
213:             continue;
214:         };
215:         match value {
216:             "0" | "false" | "off" => toggles.set(name, false),
217:             "1" | "true" | "on" => toggles.set(name, true),
218:             _ => {}
219:         }
220:     }
221:     toggles
222: }
223:

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/mod.rs

 1: //! GLSL ES 3.00 programs for every GPU render path, one module per program:
 2: //!
 3: //! | module      | program                                                |
 4: //! |-------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
 5: //! | [`raymarch`]| fullscreen SVO raymarcher (`?renderer=raymarch`)       |
 6: //! | [`surface`] | indexed greedy meshes (default renderer)               |
 7: //! | [`splat`]   | instanced face splats (`?renderer=splat`)              |
 8: //! | [`shadow`]  | depth-only hero-light shadow pass (surface + splat)    |
 9: //! | [`chunks`]  | shared GLSL snippets spliced into the programs above   |
10: //!
11: //! Cross-cutting effects (the flashlight cone, the material palette, noise
12: //! helpers, tone mapping, flare cores) exist exactly once, in [`chunks`],
13: //! and are concatenated into each program's source at link time. The
14: //! flashlight cone's constants are the GLSL mirror of the CPU spec in
15: //! `adapters::cpu_splatter::flashlight` — change both together.
16: //!
17: //! The SVO node atlas texel encoding is documented in the core's
18: //! `OctreeGpuSerializer`; the compact vertex/instance formats in
19: //! `application::ports`.
20: 
21: pub mod apply_distance_fog;
22: pub mod chunks;

  1: //! Per-frame indexed-surface pipeline.

  3: //! The submission order is deliberately visible in [`render_frame`]:

102:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
103:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
104:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);

150: /// Camera-facing product labels over nearby supply pickups. A cutout pass:
151: /// depth-tested and depth-writing, so it needs no ordering against the
152: /// opaque world and never x-rays through walls.
153: fn draw_supply_labels(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams) {
154:     use crate::drivers::shaders::supply_labels;
155: 
156:     let Some(atlas) = renderer.label_atlas.as_ref() else {
157:         return;
158:     };
159:     if frame.supply_sprites.is_empty() {
160:         return;
161:     }
162:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
163:     let uniforms = &renderer.label_uniforms;
164:     gl.use_program(Some(&renderer.label_program));
165: 
166:     let (projection, view) =
167:         camera_matrices(frame, renderer.width, renderer.height, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE);
168:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.projection.as_ref(), false, &projection);
169:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.view.as_ref(), false, &view);
170: 
171:     let count = frame
172:         .supply_sprites
173:         .len()
174:         .min(supply_labels::MAX_SPRITES);
175:     let mut sprites = [0.0f32; supply_labels::MAX_SPRITES * 4];
176:     for (i, sprite) in frame.supply_sprites.iter().take(count).enumerate() {
177:         sprites[i * 4] = sprite.position[0];
178:         sprites[i * 4 + 1] = sprite.position[1];
179:         sprites[i * 4 + 2] = sprite.position[2];
180:         sprites[i * 4 + 3] = sprite.atlas_row as f32;
181:     }
182:     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.sprites.as_ref(), &sprites);
183:     // Cylindrical billboard: turn with the player's yaw, stay upright.
184:     let right = [frame.yaw.cos(), 0.0, -frame.yaw.sin()];
185:     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_right.as_ref(), &right);
186:     gl.uniform2f(
187:         uniforms.half_size.as_ref(),
188:         supply_labels::HALF_WIDTH,
189:         supply_labels::HALF_HEIGHT,
190:     );
191:     gl.uniform3f(
192:         uniforms.camera_position.as_ref(),
193:         frame.camera_pos[0],
194:         frame.camera_pos[1],
195:         frame.camera_pos[2],
196:     );
197:     let environment = frame.environment;
198:     gl.uniform3f(
199:         uniforms.fog_color.as_ref(),
200:         environment.fog_color[0],
201:         environment.fog_color[1],
202:         environment.fog_color[2],
203:     );
204:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_density.as_ref(), environment.fog_density);
205:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_start.as_ref(), environment.fog_start);
206: 
207:     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE7);
208:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(atlas));
209:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.atlas.as_ref(), 7);
210: 
211:     // Both label faces read; the quad expands entirely from gl_VertexID.
212:     gl.disable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
213:     gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
214:     gl.draw_arrays(Gl::TRIANGLES, 0, (count * 6) as i32);
215:     gl.enable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
216: }

218: /// Establishes every fixed-function state relied on by either raster pass.
219: fn begin_main_frame(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams) {
220:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
221:     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.width, renderer.height);
222: 
223:     // Match unloaded space to the level atmosphere so generated chunk edges
224:     // disappear into fog rather than exposing the canvas clear color.
225:     let environment = frame.environment;
226:     let atmosphere = if environment.outdoor {
227:         environment.sky_color
228:     } else {
229:         environment.fog_color
230:     };
231:     let clear = encode_display_color(atmosphere);
232:     gl.clear_color(clear[0], clear[1], clear[2], 1.0);
233:     gl.clear_depth(1.0);
234:     gl.clear(Gl::COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | Gl::DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
235:     gl.enable(Gl::DEPTH_TEST);
236:     gl.depth_func(Gl::LEQUAL);
237:     gl.depth_mask(true);
238:     gl.enable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
239:     gl.cull_face(Gl::BACK);
240: }

242: /// OPTIMIZATION (rt_cull): conservative distance and behind-camera sphere
243: /// rejection. The disabled reference path submits every resident mesh.
244: fn prepare_visible_draws(
245:     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
246:     frame: &FrameParams,
247:     culling_enabled: bool,
248: ) -> (
249:     Vec<VisibleDraw>,
250:     Vec<crate::application::ports::LightSource>,
251: ) {
252:     let mut draws = Vec::new();
253:     let mut clustered = Vec::new();
254:     let hero_id = frame.active_scene_lights().first().map(|light| light.id);
255:     for (&key, mesh) in &renderer.meshes {
256:         let visible = {
257:             if !culling_enabled {
258:                 true
259:             } else {
260:                 let (center, radius) = chunk_bounding_sphere(mesh.origin, mesh.bounds_max);
261:                 sphere_visible(center, radius, frame, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE).is_some()
262:             }
263:         };
264:         if !visible {
265:             continue;
266:         }
267:         let bounds_max = [
268:             mesh.origin[0] + mesh.bounds_max[0],
269:             mesh.origin[1] + mesh.bounds_max[1],
270:             mesh.origin[2] + mesh.bounds_max[2],
271:         ];
272:         let lights = append_lights_reaching_bounds(
273:             frame.active_scene_lights(),
274:             mesh.origin,
275:             bounds_max,
276:             &mut clustered,
277:         );
278:         let hero_local_index =
279:             if lights.count > 0 && hero_id == Some(clustered[lights.first as usize].id) {
280:                 0
281:             } else {
282:                 -1
283:             };
284:         draws.push(VisibleDraw {
285:             key,
286:             lights,
287:             hero_local_index,
288:         });
289:     }
290:     (draws, clustered)
291: }
292: 
293: /// FEATURE (rt_shadows): renders every resident greedy mesh into the selected
294: /// fixture's top-down depth map. Camera culling must not remove an off-screen
295: /// caster whose shadow lands on a visible receiver. With the feature
296: /// disabled, the returned state makes the main shader skip shadow sampling.
297: fn render_shadow_pass(
298:     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
299:     frame: &FrameParams,
300:     enabled: bool,
301: ) -> ShadowState {
302:     let Some(hero) = frame.active_scene_lights().first() else {
303:         return ShadowState::default();
304:     };
305:     if !enabled {
306:         return ShadowState::default();
307:     }
308: 
309:     let range = hero.radius;
310:     let emitter_half_diagonal =
311:         (hero.half_size[0] * hero.half_size[0] + hero.half_size[1] * hero.half_size[1]).sqrt();
312:     let ortho_half = range + emitter_half_diagonal;
313:     let projection = ortho_matrix(
314:         -ortho_half,
315:         ortho_half,
316:         -ortho_half,
317:         ortho_half,
318:         0.1,
319:         range + emitter_half_diagonal,
320:     );
321:     let view = look_at_matrix_down(hero.position);
322:     let light_view_projection = multiply_matrices(&projection, &view);
323: 
324:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
325:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, Some(&renderer.shadow.fbo));
326:     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.shadow.size, renderer.shadow.size);
327:     gl.color_mask(false, false, false, false);
328:     gl.clear_depth(1.0);
329:     gl.clear(Gl::DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
330:     gl.use_program(Some(&renderer.shadow_program));
331:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(
332:         renderer.shadow_uniforms.light_view_proj.as_ref(),
333:         false,
334:         &light_view_projection,
335:     );
336: 
337:     for mesh in renderer.meshes.values() {
338:         gl.uniform3f(
339:             renderer.shadow_uniforms.chunk_origin.as_ref(),
340:             mesh.origin[0],
341:             mesh.origin[1],
342:             mesh.origin[2],
343:         );
344:         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&mesh.vao));
345:         gl.draw_elements_with_i32(Gl::TRIANGLES, mesh.index_count, Gl::UNSIGNED_INT, 0);
346:     }
347: 
348:     // Restore the default target state required by the already-cleared main
349:     // pass. Depth/cull state is shared and remains intentionally unchanged.
350:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
351:     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.width, renderer.height);
352:     gl.color_mask(true, true, true, true);
353: 
354:     ShadowState {
355:         light_index: 0,
356:         light_view_projection,
357:     }
358: }
359: 
360: /// Binds state shared by every visible mesh exactly once per frame.
361: fn bind_frame_uniforms(
362:     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
363:     frame: &FrameParams,
364:     shadow: &ShadowState,
365:     dither_enabled: bool,
366:     baked_lighting_enabled: bool,
367: ) {
368:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
369:     let uniforms = &renderer.uniforms;
370:     gl.use_program(Some(&renderer.program));
371: 
372:     let (projection, view) =
373:         camera_matrices(frame, renderer.width, renderer.height, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE);
374:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.projection.as_ref(), false, &projection);
375:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.view.as_ref(), false, &view);
376:     gl.uniform3f(
377:         uniforms.camera_position.as_ref(),
378:         frame.camera_pos[0],
379:         frame.camera_pos[1],
380:         frame.camera_pos[2],
381:     );
382: 
383:     let forward = camera_forward(frame);
384:     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_forward.as_ref(), &forward);
385:     gl.uniform1i(
386:         uniforms.flashlight.as_ref(),
387:         if frame.flashlight { 1 } else { 0 },
388:     );
389:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.dither.as_ref(), if dither_enabled { 1 } else { 0 });
390:     gl.uniform1i(
391:         uniforms.baked_lighting.as_ref(),
392:         if baked_lighting_enabled { 1 } else { 0 },
393:     );
394: 
395:     let environment = frame.environment;
396:     gl.uniform1i(
397:         uniforms.outdoor.as_ref(),
398:         if environment.outdoor { 1 } else { 0 },
399:     );
400:     gl.uniform3f(
401:         uniforms.fog_color.as_ref(),
402:         environment.fog_color[0],
403:         environment.fog_color[1],
404:         environment.fog_color[2],
405:     );
406:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.ambient_scale.as_ref(), environment.ambient_scale);
407:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_density.as_ref(), environment.fog_density);
408:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_start.as_ref(), environment.fog_start);
409: 
410:     bind_light_uniforms(renderer, frame, shadow);
411:     bind_dynamic_light_uniforms(renderer, frame);
412: }
413: 
414: fn bind_dynamic_light_uniforms(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams) {
415:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
416:     let lights = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
417:     let mut position_radius = [0.0f32; 16];
418:     let mut color_intensity = [0.0f32; 16];
419:     for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
420:         let offset = index * 4;
421:         position_radius[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
422:         position_radius[offset + 3] = light.radius;
423:         color_intensity[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
424:         color_intensity[offset + 3] = light.intensity;
425:     }
426:     gl.uniform1i(
427:         renderer.uniforms.dynamic_light_count.as_ref(),
428:         lights.len() as i32,
429:     );
430:     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(
431:         renderer.uniforms.dynamic_pos_radius.as_ref(),
432:         &position_radius,
433:     );
434:     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(
435:         renderer.uniforms.dynamic_color_intensity.as_ref(),
436:         &color_intensity,
437:     );
438: }
439: 
440: fn camera_forward(frame: &FrameParams) -> [f32; 3] {
441:     let (sin_pitch, cos_pitch) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
442:     let (sin_yaw, cos_yaw) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
443:     [-cos_pitch * sin_yaw, sin_pitch, -cos_pitch * cos_yaw]
444: }
445: 
446: fn bind_light_uniforms(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams, shadow: &ShadowState) {
447:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
448:     let uniforms = &renderer.uniforms;
449:     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE2);
450:     renderer.scene_lights.bind(gl);
451:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.scene_light_texture.as_ref(), 2);
452:     gl.uniform1i(
453:         uniforms.scene_light_texture_width.as_ref(),
454:         renderer.scene_lights.width(),
455:     );
456: 
457:     // Flare cores are independent from the selected shading-light slots, so
458:     // an unselected flare still renders its small emissive ember.
459:     let cores = flare_cores(frame);
460:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.core_count.as_ref(), cores.count);
461:     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cores.as_ref(), &cores.pos_intensity);
462:     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.core_colors.as_ref(), &cores.colors);
463: 
464:     // sampler3D and sampler2D may never alias, even when no hero is active:
465:     // WebGL rejects the draw if both default to texture unit zero.
466:     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE1);
467:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&renderer.shadow.texture));
468:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.shadow_map.as_ref(), 1);
469:     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(
470:         uniforms.light_view_proj.as_ref(),
471:         false,
472:         &shadow.light_view_projection,
473:     );
474: }
475: 
476: fn draw_visible_meshes(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, visible: &[VisibleDraw], shadow: &ShadowState) {
477:     for draw in visible {
478:         let Some(mesh) = renderer.meshes.get(&draw.key) else {
479:             continue;
480:         };
481:         draw_mesh(renderer, mesh, draw, shadow);
482:     }
483:     renderer.gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
484: }
485: 
486: /// Binds the only per-mesh state: local transform bounds, baked light volume,
487: /// and indexed geometry.
488: fn draw_mesh(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, mesh: &GpuMesh, draw: &VisibleDraw, shadow: &ShadowState) {
489:     let gl = &renderer.gl;
490:     let uniforms = &renderer.uniforms;
491:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.light_first.as_ref(), draw.lights.first);
492:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.light_count.as_ref(), draw.lights.count);
493:     gl.uniform1i(
494:         uniforms.shadowed_light_index.as_ref(),
495:         if shadow.light_index >= 0 {
496:             draw.hero_local_index
497:         } else {
498:             -1
499:         },
500:     );
501:     gl.uniform3f(
502:         uniforms.chunk_origin.as_ref(),
503:         mesh.origin[0],
504:         mesh.origin[1],
505:         mesh.origin[2],
506:     );
507:     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.voxel_size.as_ref(), mesh.voxel_size);
508:     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(
509:         uniforms.light_volume_origin.as_ref(),
510:         &mesh.light_volume_origin,
511:     );
512:     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE0);
513:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Some(&mesh.light_texture));
514:     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.light_volume.as_ref(), 0);
515: 
516:     gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&mesh.vao));
517:     gl.draw_elements_with_i32(Gl::TRIANGLES, mesh.index_count, Gl::UNSIGNED_INT, 0);
518: }

  2: //! visibility. The SVO remains in the chunk payload for collision and debug

  8: //!   light volume), incremental upload/removal;

108: impl SurfaceRenderer {
109:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
110:         let gl = create_context(canvas, ContextOptions { depth: true })?;
111: 
112:         let program = link_program(&gl, surface::VERTEX_SHADER, &surface::fragment_source())?;
113:         let uniforms = Uniforms {
114:             projection: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uProjection"),
115:             view: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uView"),
116:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uChunkOrigin"),
117:             camera_position: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCameraPosition"),
118:             cam_forward: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCamForward"),
119:             flashlight: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFlashlightEnabled"),
120:             dither: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDitherEnabled"),
121:             baked_lighting: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uBakedLightingEnabled"),
122:             light_volume: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightVolume"),
123:             light_volume_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightVolumeOrigin"),
124:             voxel_size: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uVoxelSize"),
125:             light_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightCount"),
126:             light_first: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightFirst"),
127:             scene_light_texture: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uSceneLightTexture"),
128:             scene_light_texture_width: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uSceneLightTextureWidth"),
129:             dynamic_light_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDynamicLightCount"),
130:             dynamic_pos_radius: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDynamicPosRadius"),
131:             dynamic_color_intensity: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDynamicColorIntensity"),
132:             core_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreCount"),
133:             cores: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCores"),
134:             core_colors: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreColors"),
135:             shadow_map: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowMap"),
136:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightViewProjection"),
137:             shadowed_light_index: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowedLightIndex"),
138:             outdoor: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uOutdoor"),
139:             fog_color: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFogColor"),
140:             ambient_scale: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uAmbientScale"),
141:             fog_density: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFogDensity"),
142:             fog_start: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFogStart"),
143:         };
144:         let timer = GpuFrameTimer::new(&gl);
145:         let scene_lights = SceneLightTexture::create(&gl)?;
146: 
147:         let shadow_program = link_program(&gl, shadow::VERTEX_SHADER, shadow::FRAGMENT_SHADER)?;
148:         let shadow_uniforms = ShadowUniforms {
149:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uLightViewProjection"),
150:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uChunkOrigin"),
151:         };
152:         let shadow = create_shadow_target(&gl, 128)?;
153: 
154:         let label_program = link_program(
155:             &gl,
156:             supply_labels::VERTEX_SHADER,
157:             &supply_labels::fragment_source(),
158:         )?;
159:         let label_uniforms = LabelUniforms {
160:             projection: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uProjection"),
161:             view: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uView"),
162:             sprites: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uSprites"),
163:             cam_right: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uCamRight"),
164:             half_size: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uHalfSize"),
165:             atlas: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uAtlas"),
166:             camera_position: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uCameraPosition"),
167:             fog_color: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uFogColor"),
168:             fog_density: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uFogDensity"),
169:             fog_start: gl.get_uniform_location(&label_program, "uFogStart"),
170:         };
171: 
172:         Ok(Self {
173:             gl,
174:             program,
175:             uniforms,
176:             meshes: HashMap::new(),
177:             width: canvas.width() as i32,
178:             height: canvas.height() as i32,

193:         self.width = width as i32;

 1: use crate::adapters::voxel_mapper::{FaceDirection, MergedQuad, VoxelType};
 2: 
 3: /// Interface Adapter to convert MergedQuads to JSON format for the web presentation layer.
 4: pub struct JsonPresenter;
 5: 
 6: impl JsonPresenter {
 7:     pub fn render_voxels(quads: &[MergedQuad]) -> String {
 8:         let mut json = String::with_capacity(quads.len() * 100);
 9:         json.push('[');
10: 
11:         for (i, quad) in quads.iter().enumerate() {
12:             let dir_str = match quad.dir {
13:                 FaceDirection::Up => "\"up\"",
14:                 FaceDirection::Down => "\"down\"",
15:                 FaceDirection::North => "\"north\"",
16:                 FaceDirection::South => "\"south\"",
17:                 FaceDirection::East => "\"east\"",
18:                 FaceDirection::West => "\"west\"",
19:             };
20: 
21:             let type_str = match quad.v_type {
22:                 VoxelType::Wall => "\"wall\"",
23:                 VoxelType::Floor => "\"floor\"",
24:                 VoxelType::Ceiling => "\"ceiling\"",
25:                 VoxelType::Light => "\"light\"",
26:                 VoxelType::RedWall => "\"redwall\"",
27:                 VoxelType::Grass => "\"grass\"",
28:                 VoxelType::Water => "\"water\"",
29:                 VoxelType::Tree => "\"tree\"",
30:                 VoxelType::RedLight => "\"redlight\"",
31:                 VoxelType::PaleWall => "\"palewall\"",
32:                 VoxelType::DamagedWall => "\"damagedwall\"",
33:                 VoxelType::DryCarpet => "\"drycarpet\"",
34:                 VoxelType::DeepCarpet => "\"deepcarpet\"",
35:                 VoxelType::StickyCarpet => "\"stickycarpet\"",
36:                 VoxelType::Fluid => "\"fluid\"",
37:                 VoxelType::Glimmer => "\"glimmer\"",
38:                 VoxelType::ConcreteWall => "\"concretewall\"",
39:                 VoxelType::TileFloor => "\"tilefloor\"",
40:                 VoxelType::ConcreteFloor => "\"concretefloor\"",
41:                 VoxelType::Crate => "\"crate\"",
42:                 VoxelType::Pipe => "\"pipe\"",
43:                 VoxelType::MetalDoor => "\"metaldoor\"",
44:                 VoxelType::AlmondWater => "\"almondwater\"",
45:             };
46: 
47:             let obj = format!(
48:                 "{{\"x\":{},\"y\":{},\"z\":{},\"w\":{},\"h\":{},\"dir\":{},\"type\":{},\"color\":{}}}",
49:                 quad.x, quad.y, quad.z, quad.w, quad.h, dir_str, type_str, quad.color
50:             );
51: 
52:             json.push_str(&obj);
53:             if i < quads.len() - 1 {
54:                 json.push(',');
55:             }
56:         }
57: 
58:         json.push(']');
59:         json
60:     }
61: }
62: 
63: #[cfg(test)]
64: mod tests {
65:     use super::*;
66: 
67:     #[test]
68:     fn test_json_rendering() {
69:         let quads = vec![MergedQuad {
70:             x: 0.0,
71:             y: 1.0,
72:             z: 2.0,
73:             w: 4.0,
74:             h: 1.0,
75:             dir: FaceDirection::Up,
76:             v_type: VoxelType::Wall,
77:             color: 1441813,
78:             light: 0,
79:             ao: 0,
80:         }];
81: 
82:         let json = JsonPresenter::render_voxels(&quads);
83:         assert_eq!(
84:             json,
85:             r#"[{"x":0,"y":1,"z":2,"w":4,"h":1,"dir":"up","type":"wall","color":1441813}]"#
86:         );
87:     }
88: }

  1: //! Pure architectural domain types for procedurally *planned* levels.
  2: //!
  3: //! These describe a region-scale building plan — who designed it
  4: //! ([`ArchitectGenome`]), what each space is for ([`SpaceProgram`]), how
  5: //! circulation feeds spaces ([`CirculationSpine`]), and how spaces are
  6: //! assembled ([`AssemblyInstance`]) — before anything is voxelized. The
  7: //! planner (`use_cases::region_plan`) fills these in; the level generator
  8: //! samples them per voxel column. Nothing here knows about voxels, chunks,
  9: //! rendering, or WASM.
 10: //!
 11: //! All types are small, plain data. Determinism comes from how they are
 12: //! *derived* (seed + region coordinate), not from anything stored here.
 13: 
 14: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyInstance;
 15: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 16: 
 17: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 18: // Architect genomes: a "design culture" as a seed-derived parameter set.
 19: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 20: 
 21: /// How a designer routes people through a region.
 22: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 23: pub enum CirculationStyle {
 24:     /// One straight main corridor wall-to-wall.
 25:     StraightSpine,
 26:     /// A main corridor that bends at interior waypoints.
 27:     MeanderingSpine,
 28:     /// A primary spine with two short, disconnected-looking branches.
 29:     PairedBranches,
 30:     /// A spine plus stub branches that dead-end (unease by design).
 31:     TreeWithCulDeSacs,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// How a designer holds the ceiling up.
 35: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 36: pub enum StructuralSystem {
 37:     /// Columns on a square grid.
 38:     RegularGrid,
 39:     /// Wider bays in one axis, expressed as ceiling beams.
 40:     DeepSpansWithBeams,
 41:     /// Alternate column rows shifted half a bay.
 42:     OffsetGrid,
 43:     /// Columns only around cores and the perimeter.
 44:     CoreAndShell,
 45: }
 46: 
 47: /// Preferred room shapes.
 48: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
 49: pub struct ProportionRules {
 50:     /// Smallest room side a designer will draw, world units.
 51:     pub min_side: f32,
 52:     /// Largest room side, world units.
 53:     pub max_side: f32,
 54:     /// 0 = square rooms, 1 = strongly elongated rooms.
 55:     pub elongation: f32,
 56: }
 57: 
 58: /// How rooms open onto circulation.
 59: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 60: pub enum ThresholdLanguage {
 61:     /// Standard door-width opening under a solid lintel.
 62:     DoorWithLintel,
 63:     /// Full-height opening, no lintel.
 64:     OpenPortal,
 65:     /// Double-width opening under a lintel (suites, conference).
 66:     WidePortal,
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Ceiling articulation.
 70: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 71: pub enum CeilingLanguage {
 72:     /// Flat acoustic tile everywhere.
 73:     FlatTiles,
 74:     /// Beam grid with recessed panels.
 75:     Coffered,
 76:     /// Lowered continuous soffit (mechanical-heavy designers).
 77:     ExposedSoffit,
 78: }
 79: 
 80: /// Where the lights go.
 81: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 82: pub enum LightingLanguage {
 83:     /// Fluorescent modules on the ceiling grid.
 84:     GridPanels,
 85:     /// Continuous strips that follow circulation.
 86:     StripsAlongCirculation,
 87:     /// Sparse single fixtures (renovated or neglected areas).
 88:     SparsePendants,
 89: }
 90: 
 91: /// What later occupants did to the original plan.
 92: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 93: pub enum RenovationStyle {
 94:     /// Plan left as designed.
 95:     Untouched,
 96:     /// One assembly re-partitioned in a second designer's language.
 97:     PartialRefit,
 98:     /// Renovation structure overlaid on the original (contradictory columns).
 99:     LayeredRefits,
100: }
101: 
102: /// A design culture: every plan decision in a region is parameterized by one
103: /// of these. Derived deterministically from `(seed, region coordinate)`.
104: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
105: pub struct ArchitectGenome {
106:     pub circulation: CirculationStyle,
107:     pub structural_system: StructuralSystem,
108:     pub room_proportions: ProportionRules,
109:     pub threshold_language: ThresholdLanguage,
110:     pub ceiling_language: CeilingLanguage,
111:     pub lighting_language: LightingLanguage,
112:     /// 0 = bare shells, 1 = densely partitioned interiors.
113:     pub furnishing_density: f32,
114:     pub renovation_history: RenovationStyle,
115:     /// 0 = happily asymmetric, 1 = mirrors and centers everything.
116:     pub tolerance_for_symmetry: f32,
117: }
118: 
119: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
120: // Program: what a space is *for*.
121: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
122: 
123: /// First-class space semantics (the old room stamps, promoted to meaning).
124: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
125: pub enum SpaceProgram {
126:     Arrival,
127:     Reception,
128:     MainCorridor,
129:     SecondaryHall,
130:     OpenOffice,
131:     PrivateOffice,
132:     ConferenceRoom,
133:     WaitingArea,
134:     BreakRoom,
135:     Storage,
136:     ServerRoom,
137:     RestroomCore,
138:     Stair,
139:     Mechanical,
140:     Atrium,
141:     /// Planned, built, never occupied: lit shell or unlit void.
142:     AbandonedExpansion,
143: }
144: 
145: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146: // Geometry helpers (deliberately minimal — rectilinear plans only).
147: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148: 
149: /// A simple closed 2D polygon in world space. The planner only emits convex
150: /// rectilinear footprints, so containment is tested with the even-odd rule
151: /// and no general polygon library is needed.
152: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
153: pub struct Polygon2 {
154:     /// (x, z) vertices in world space, wound consistently.
155:     pub vertices: Vec<(f32, f32)>,
156: }
157: 
158: impl Polygon2 {
159:     /// Axis-aligned rectangle from min corner and size.
160:     pub fn rect(x: f32, z: f32, w: f32, d: f32) -> Self {
161:         Self {
162:             vertices: vec![(x, z), (x + w, z), (x + w, z + d), (x, z + d)],
163:         }
164:     }
165: 
166:     /// Even-odd containment test.
167:     pub fn contains(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> bool {
168:         let v = &self.vertices;
169:         let mut inside = false;
170:         let mut j = v.len() - 1;
171:         for i in 0..v.len() {
172:             let (xi, zi) = v[i];
173:             let (xj, zj) = v[j];
174:             if ((zi > z) != (zj > z)) && (x < (xj - xi) * (z - zi) / (zj - zi) + xi) {
175:                 inside = !inside;
176:             }
177:             j = i;
178:         }
179:         inside
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Axis-aligned bounds: (min_x, min_z, max_x, max_z).
183:     pub fn bounds(&self) -> (f32, f32, f32, f32) {
184:         let mut b = (f32::MAX, f32::MAX, f32::MIN, f32::MIN);
185:         for &(x, z) in &self.vertices {
186:             b.0 = b.0.min(x);
187:             b.1 = b.1.min(z);
188:             b.2 = b.2.max(x);
189:             b.3 = b.3.max(z);
190:         }
191:         b
192:     }
193: }
194: 
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: // Assemblies: planned spaces with structure, ceilings and fixtures.
197: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
198: 
199: /// A doorway/portal on an assembly boundary, opening onto circulation.

201: pub struct Opening {

210:     pub lintel_units: Option<f32>,
211: }
212: 
213: /// A named subspace inside an assembly (a private office in a suite, a stall
