````rust
322: impl CirculationSpine {
323:     /// Distance from (x, z) to the spine centerline (axis-aligned segments).
324:     pub fn distance(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> f32 {
325:         self.nearest(x, z).0
326:     }
327: 
328:     /// Nearest point on the centerline: `(distance, along, is_horizontal)`.
329:     /// `along` is the world coordinate *along* the nearest segment's axis, so
330:     /// modules (light strips, wall gaps) repeat in world space and stay
331:     /// continuous across chunk and region borders.
332:     pub fn nearest(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> (f32, f32, bool) {
333:         let mut best = (f32::MAX, 0.0, true);
334:         for seg in self.path.windows(2) {
335:             let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
336:             let (dx, dz) = (b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z);
337:             let len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
338:             let t = if len2 > 0.0 {
339:                 (((x - a.x) * dx + (z - a.z) * dz) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
340:             } else {
341:                 0.0
342:             };
343:             let (px, pz) = (a.x + t * dx, a.z + t * dz);
344:             let d2 = (x - px) * (x - px) + (z - pz) * (z - pz);
345:             if d2 < best.0 {
346:                 let horizontal = dx.abs() >= dz.abs();
347:                 best = (d2, if horizontal { px } else { pz }, horizontal);
348:             }
349:         }
350:         (best.0.sqrt(), best.1, best.2)
351:     }
352: }
353: 
354: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
355: // The region plan.
356: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
357: 
358: /// Everything planned for one square region of the world. Regions tile a
359: /// fixed world-space lattice; a chunk generator asks for the plan of every
360: /// region its chunk overlaps and samples them per column.
361: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
362: pub struct RegionPlan {
363:     /// Lower-left corner in world space.
364:     pub origin_world: Position,
365:     /// Side length, world units.
366:     pub size_world: f32,
367:     /// Dominant designer first, then renovator, then optional intruder.
368:     pub architects: Vec<ArchitectGenome>,
369:     pub assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
370:     pub corridors: Vec<CirculationSpine>,
371:     /// Region-overlapping anomaly instances. Macro instances deliberately
372:     /// repeat in every intersected region with the same stable identity;
373:     /// consumers deduplicate them by [`AnomalyInstance::id`].
374:     pub anomalies: Vec<AnomalyInstance>,
375: }
376:
````

````typescript
 35: async function renderedImageStats(
 36:   renderPage: import('@playwright/test').Page,
 37:   probePage: import('@playwright/test').Page,
 38: ) {
 39:   const png = await renderPage.locator('#view').screenshot();
 40:   const dataUrl = `data:image/png;base64,${png.toString('base64')}`;
 41: 
 42:   return probePage.evaluate(async encodedImage => {
 43:     const response = await fetch(encodedImage);
 44:     const bitmap = await createImageBitmap(await response.blob());
 45:     const sample = document.createElement('canvas');
 46:     sample.width = 64;
 47:     sample.height = 48;
 48:     const context = sample.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true });
 49:     if (!context) throw new Error('2D screenshot probe is unavailable');
 50:     context.drawImage(bitmap, 0, 0, sample.width, sample.height);
 51: 
 52:     const pixels = context.getImageData(0, 0, sample.width, sample.height).data;
 53:     const colors = new Set<number>();
 54:     let darkest = 255;
 55:     let brightest = 0;
 56:     for (let i = 0; i < pixels.length; i += 4) {
 57:       const red = pixels[i];
 58:       const green = pixels[i + 1];
 59:       const blue = pixels[i + 2];
 60:       const luminance = Math.round(red * 0.2126 + green * 0.7152 + blue * 0.0722);
 61:       darkest = Math.min(darkest, luminance);
 62:       brightest = Math.max(brightest, luminance);
 63:       colors.add(((red >> 4) << 8) | ((green >> 4) << 4) | (blue >> 4));
 64:     }
 65:     bitmap.close();
 66:     return { colorBuckets: colors.size, luminanceRange: brightest - darkest };
 67:   }, dataUrl);
 68: }

 96:         return (window as typeof window & { __sceneReady?: boolean }).__sceneReady === true;
 97:       },

100:     );
101: 
102:     await expect(page.locator('#hud-renderer')).toHaveText(backend.label);
103:     await expect(page.locator('#status-msg')).not.toContainText('Failed to start engine');
104: 
105:     const effectiveToggles = await page.evaluate(async names => {
106:       const moduleUrl = new URL('./pkg/wasm_frontend.js', window.location.href).href;
107:       const wasm = (await import(moduleUrl)) as {
108:         render_toggle_enabled(name: string): boolean | undefined;
109:       };
110:       return names.map(name => wasm.render_toggle_enabled(name));
111:     }, backend.disabled);

113:

115:     // compositor screenshot must contain real scene variation rather than a
116:     // uniform clear/error canvas.
````

````rust
 14: /// depth-2 SVO (4^3) with one solid voxel, serialized like production.
 15: fn one_voxel_atlas(color: u32, light: u8) -> (Vec<u32>, u32) {
 16:     let mut svo = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
 17:     svo.set(1, 1, 1, 1, color, [light; 3], 0);
 18:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 19:     (gpu.texel_data, svo.root as u32)
 20: }

 22: fn frame_at(pos: [f32; 3], yaw: f32) -> FrameParams {
 23:     FrameParams {
 24:         camera_pos: pos,
 25:         yaw,
 26:         pitch: 0.0,
 27:         flashlight: false,
 28:         ..FrameParams::default()
 29:     }
 30: }
 31: 
 32: fn center_pixel(r: &SoftwareRasterizer) -> [u8; 4] {
 33:     let idx = (r.height() / 2 * r.width() + r.width() / 2) * 4;
 34:     let fb = r.framebuffer();
 35:     [fb[idx], fb[idx + 1], fb[idx + 2], fb[idx + 3]]
 36: }

 42:     r.upload_atlas(&atlas);
 43: 
 44:     // Voxel spans (1..2)^3; look at its center from -z (yaw = PI faces +z).
 45:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {

 56:     assert!(px[0] > px[2], "red voxel must stay reddish, got {:?}", px);

395: #[test]
396: fn exact_entry_face_changes_the_lambert_response_at_an_axis_boundary() {
397:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(16, 16);
398:     let center = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
399: 
400:     // Case A: Camera Y is 1.01 (above the center, Y-dominant)
401:     let frame_a = FrameParams {
402:         camera_pos: [-1.0, 1.01, -0.1],
403:         yaw: 0.0,
404:         pitch: 0.0,
405:         flashlight: false,
406:         ..FrameParams::default()
407:     };
408:     let cam_a = Camera::new(&frame_a, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
409: 
410:     // Case B: Camera Y is 0.99 (below Case A, X-dominant)
411:     let frame_b = FrameParams {
412:         camera_pos: [-1.0, 0.99, -0.1],
413:         yaw: 0.0,
414:         pitch: 0.0,
415:         flashlight: false,
416:         ..FrameParams::default()
417:     };
418:     let cam_b = Camera::new(&frame_b, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
419: 
420:     r.clear();
421:     let fixture = [LightSource {
422:         id: 1,
423:         position: [0.0, 5.0, 0.0],
424:         half_size: [2.0, 2.0],
425:         color: [1.0, 0.9, 0.7],
426:         radius: 20.0,
427:         intensity: 10.0,
428:         kind: LightKind::CeilingPanel,
429:         flicker_mode: 0,
430:         enabled: true,
431:     }];
432: 
433:     r.shade_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
434:         &cam_a,
435:         &[],
436:         FrameLighting::unshadowed(&fixture),
437:         center,
438:         8.0,                   // world_size
439:         8.0,                   // px — the center pixel both cases read
440:         8.0,                   // py
441:         1.0,                   // half_px
442:         1.0,                   // dist
443:         [100.0, 100.0, 100.0], // base color
444:         15.0,                  // light level
445:         false,                 // is_emissive
446:         1,                     // crowded siblings
447:     );
448:     let color_a = center_pixel(&r);
449: 
450:     r.clear();
451:     r.shade_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
452:         &cam_b,
453:         &[],
454:         FrameLighting::unshadowed(&fixture),
455:         center,
456:         8.0,
457:         8.0,
458:         8.0,
459:         1.0,
460:         1.0,
461:         [100.0, 100.0, 100.0],
462:         15.0,
463:         false,
464:         1,
465:     );
466:     let color_b = center_pixel(&r);
467: 
468:     // The Y entry face sees the overhead panel. The neighboring X entry face
469:     // does not: this discontinuity is the exact AABB/Lambert result, not a
470:     // soft diagonal normal invented to hide a face boundary.
471:     assert!(
472:         color_a[0] > color_b[0] + 10,
473:         "expected exact face response: y-face={color_a:?}, x-face={color_b:?}"
474:     );
475: }

530: #[test]
531: fn test_splat_flat_shading_limitation() {
532:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(16, 16);
533:     let frame = FrameParams {
534:         camera_pos: [1.0, 5.0, 1.0],
535:         yaw: 0.0,
536:         pitch: 0.0,
537:         flashlight: false,
538:         ..FrameParams::default()
539:     };
540:     let cam = Camera::new(&frame, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
541: 
542:     // Draw a single large splat (half_px = 4.0) centered at [8.0, 8.0]
543:     r.clear();
544:     r.shade_and_splat(
545:         &cam,
546:         &[],
547:         [0.5, 0.0, 0.5],
548:         8.0,
549:         8.0,
550:         8.0,
551:         4.0, // half_px
552:         5.0,

559:     let idx_left = (8 * r.width() + 5) * 4;
560:     let idx_right = (8 * r.width() + 10) * 4;
561:     let fb = r.framebuffer();
562:     let color_left = [fb[idx_left], fb[idx_left + 1], fb[idx_left + 2]];

572: #[test]
573: fn camera_inside_large_solid_leaf_terminates_under_budget() {
574:     const VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP: u8 = 3;
575: 
576:     let mut atlas = vec![0u32; 4];
577:     atlas[0] = 1; // Leaf
578:     atlas[1] = 1; // Solid voxel type
579:     atlas[2] = 0xFFFFFF; // White color
580:     atlas[3] = 15; // quantized diffuse fill
581: 
582:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(64, 64);
583:     // A camera-plane box must subdivide for exact clipped coverage. Use the
584:     // minimum supported cap so even a completely visible eight-way walk has
585:     // a small, deterministic upper bound independent of culling details.
586:     r.settings.max_virtual_depth = VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP;
587:     r.upload_atlas(&atlas);
588: 
589:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
590:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
591:         root_index: 0,
592:         world_size: 16.0, // Very large leaf
593:         voxel_size: 16.0,
594:         svo_depth: 0,
595:     }];
596: 
597:     // Camera inside the bounding sphere of the root chunk.
598:     r.draw(&frame_at([8.0, 8.0, 8.0], 0.0), &chunks);
599: 
600:     let stats = r.telemetry();
601:     let complete_tree_visit_bound = (8usize.pow(u32::from(VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP) + 1) - 1) / (8 - 1);
602: 
603:     assert_eq!(
604:         stats.max_virtual_depth,
605:         usize::from(VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP),
606:         "camera-plane coverage should refine to the explicit virtual-depth cap"
607:     );
608:     assert!(
609:         complete_tree_visit_bound < stats.node_soft_limit,
610:         "test fixture's complete tree must fit below the soft work budget"
611:     );
612:     assert!(
613:         stats.visited_nodes <= complete_tree_visit_bound,
614:         "visited {} nodes, exceeding the depth-{VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP} complete-tree bound of {complete_tree_visit_bound}",
615:         stats.visited_nodes,
616:     );
617:     assert!(!stats.budget_exhausted);
618: }

667: /// REGRESSION (cone-light angles): a truly cardinal shadow ray must remain
668: /// cardinal. The old slab workaround changed every tiny/zero component to
669: /// +/-1e-4; by the time this +Z ray reached the voxel it had drifted across
670: /// x=2, selected the neighboring octant, and made the flashlight flicker off
671: /// as yaw crossed the axis.
672: #[test]
673: fn cardinal_secondary_ray_does_not_drift_across_an_octant_boundary() {
674:     let (atlas, root) = one_voxel_atlas(0xFFFFFF, 15);
675:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
676:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
677:         root_index: root as i32,
678:         world_size: 4.0,
679:         voxel_size: 1.0,
680:         svo_depth: 2,
681:     }];
682: 
683:     for x_direction in [-5.0e-7, -0.0, 0.0, 5.0e-7] {
684:         for front_to_back in [false, true] {
685:             let hit = trace_svo(
686:                 &atlas,
687:                 &chunks,
688:                 [2.0 - 5.0e-5, 1.5, -1.0],
689:                 [x_direction, 0.0, 1.0],
690:                 10.0,
691:                 front_to_back,
692:             )
693:             .expect("a near-cardinal +Z ray must stay inside the voxel's x slab");
694: 
695:             assert_eq!(hit.voxel_type, 1);
696:             assert!((hit.t - 2.0).abs() < 1.0e-4);
697:         }
698:     }
699: }

701: /// REGRESSION (cone light): a ray crossing an empty *lower-Y* masked-out
702: /// octant used to compute its exit plane from `center[1]` instead of the
703: /// octant floor, stall until the step budget, and report "no hit". The
704: /// flashlight then read as unoccluded through floors, and downward beam
705: /// rays randomly blacked out.
706: #[test]
707: fn trace_through_empty_lower_octant_still_finds_the_wall() {
708:     let mut svo = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
709:     svo.set(1, 0, 1, 1, 0xFFFFFF, [15; 3], 0); // solid at cell (1,0,1)
710:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
711:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
712:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
713:         root_index: svo.root as i32,
714:         world_size: 4.0,
715:         voxel_size: 1.0,
716:         svo_depth: 2,
717:     }];
718: 
719:     // Start in the empty lower-half cell (0,0,1) and head +x with a
720:     // downward slope: the march must cross the empty octant and hit the
721:     // solid voxel spanning (1..2, 0..1, 1..2).
722:     let dir_len = (1.0f32 + 0.3 * 0.3).sqrt();
723:     let dir = [1.0 / dir_len, -0.3 / dir_len, 0.0];
724:     let hit = trace_svo(&gpu.texel_data, &chunks, [0.5, 0.9, 1.5], dir, 10.0, true);
725:     assert!(
726:         hit.is_some(),
727:         "downward ray must cross the empty octant and hit the voxel"
728:     );
729:     assert_eq!(hit.unwrap().voxel_type, 1);
730: }

847: /// The beam must NOT reach a surface behind a wall (needs the fixed
848: /// occlusion trace to pass together with `test_flashlight_illuminates_voxel`).
849: #[test]
850: fn flashlight_is_blocked_by_a_wall() {
851:     // Two-voxel column along z: near wall at cell z=1, far wall at z=2,
852:     // camera looking down the column. The near wall face is lit; if we
853:     // remove it the far wall would be lit — here we just assert the lit
854:     // face is the near one by depth.
855:     let mut svo = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
856:     svo.set(1, 1, 1, 1, 0xFFFFFF, [0; 3], 0);
857:     svo.set(1, 1, 2, 1, 0xFFFFFF, [0; 3], 0);
858:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
859:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
860:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
861:         root_index: svo.root as i32,
862:         world_size: 4.0,
863:         voxel_size: 1.0,
864:         svo_depth: 2,
865:     }];
866: 
867:     // The beam from the camera toward the far voxel's center is blocked by
868:     // the near voxel: an occlusion trace stopping short of the far surface
869:     // must report the near wall.
870:     let hit = trace_svo(
871:         &gpu.texel_data,
872:         &chunks,
873:         [1.5, 1.5, -0.5],
874:         [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
875:         2.9,
876:         true,
877:     );
878:     assert!(hit.is_some(), "near wall must occlude");
879:     assert!(hit.unwrap().t < 2.0, "the NEAR wall is the occluder");
880: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Binary transport format for [`ChunkPayload`] between the generation
  2: //! workers and the main thread. One chunk becomes one contiguous byte
  3: //! buffer, so the browser can move it with a zero-copy `postMessage`
  4: //! transfer instead of structured-cloning a deep object graph.
  5: //!
  6: //! The format is little-endian, length-prefixed, and versioned by a magic
  7: //! header. Decode is defensive: any truncated or mismatched buffer yields
  8: //! `None` and the driver simply drops that chunk (the streamer re-requests).
  9: //! Platform-free and natively round-trip tested.
 10: 
 11: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 12: use crate::application::ports::{
 13:     ChunkPayload, FaceCellRange, FaceInstanceSet, LightKind, LightSource, PackedFaceInstance,
 14:     PackedVertex, SurfaceMeshPayload,
 15: };
 16: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{LevelExit, PitHazard, TraversalGate};
 17: use vackrooms::domain::entities::supplies::SupplyItem;
 18: 
 19: /// "VKC" + version 6. Version 6 adds supply items and level exits.
 20: const MAGIC: u32 = 0x564B_4306;
 21: 
 22: pub fn encode_chunk_payload(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u8> {
 23:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
 24:         64 + payload.nodes.len() * 4
 25:             + payload.surface.vertices.len() * 10
 26:             + payload.surface.indices.len() * 4
 27:             + payload.surface.light_volume.len()
 28:             + payload.surface.faces.instances.len() * 16
 29:             + payload.collision.len() * 24
 30:             + payload.traversal_gates.len() * TraversalGate::WORDS * 4
 31:             + payload.pit_hazards.len() * PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS * 4,
 32:     );
 33:     put_u32(&mut out, MAGIC);
 34:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.root);
 35:     put_f32(&mut out, payload.world_size);
 36:     put_f32(&mut out, payload.voxel_size);
 37:     out.push(payload.svo_depth);
 38: 
 39:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.nodes.len() as u32);
 40:     for &n in &payload.nodes {
 41:         put_u32(&mut out, n);
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     let s = &payload.surface;
 45:     put_u32(&mut out, s.vertices.len() as u32);
 46:     for v in &s.vertices {
 47:         for c in v.position {
 48:             put_u16(&mut out, c);
 49:         }
 50:         out.extend_from_slice(&[v.normal_axis, v.material, v.static_indirect, v.ao]);
 51:     }
 52:     put_u32(&mut out, s.indices.len() as u32);
 53:     for &i in &s.indices {
 54:         put_u32(&mut out, i);
 55:     }
 56:     put_aabb(&mut out, &s.bounds);
 57:     out.push(s.lod);
 58:     put_f32(&mut out, s.voxel_scale);
 59:     for d in s.light_volume_size {
 60:         put_u32(&mut out, d);
 61:     }
 62:     out.push(s.light_volume_padding);
 63:     put_u32(&mut out, s.light_volume.len() as u32);
 64:     out.extend_from_slice(&s.light_volume);
 65: 
 66:     put_u32(&mut out, s.lights.len() as u32);
 67:     for l in &s.lights {
 68:         out.extend_from_slice(&l.id.to_le_bytes());
 69:         for c in l.position {
 70:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 71:         }
 72:         for c in l.half_size {
 73:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 74:         }
 75:         for c in l.color {
 76:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 77:         }
 78:         put_f32(&mut out, l.radius);
 79:         put_f32(&mut out, l.intensity);
 80:         out.push(l.kind as u8);
 81:         out.push(l.flicker_mode);
 82:         out.push(u8::from(l.enabled));
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     put_u32(&mut out, s.faces.instances.len() as u32);
 86:     for inst in &s.faces.instances {
 87:         for c in inst.position {
 88:             put_u16(&mut out, c);
 89:         }
 90:         out.extend_from_slice(&[
 91:             inst.extent_u,
 92:             inst.extent_v,
 93:             inst.normal_axis,
 94:             inst.material,
 95:             inst.baked_light,
 96:             inst.ao,
 97:             inst.flags,
 98:         ]);
 99:     }
100:     put_u32(&mut out, s.faces.cells.len() as u32);
101:     for cell in &s.faces.cells {
102:         out.extend_from_slice(&cell.cell);
103:         put_u32(&mut out, cell.offset);
104:         put_u32(&mut out, cell.count);
105:     }
106:     put_f32(&mut out, s.faces.cell_size);
107: 
108:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.collision.len() as u32);
109:     for aabb in &payload.collision {
110:         put_aabb(&mut out, aabb);
111:     }
112: 
113:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.traversal_gates.len() as u32);
114:     for gate in &payload.traversal_gates {
115:         for word in gate.to_words() {
116:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
117:         }
118:     }
119:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.pit_hazards.len() as u32);
120:     for hazard in &payload.pit_hazards {
121:         let mut words = Vec::with_capacity(PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS);
122:         hazard.write_words(&mut words);
123:         for word in words {
124:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
125:         }
126:     }
127:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.supply_items.len() as u32);
128:     for item in &payload.supply_items {
129:         for word in item.to_words() {
130:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
131:         }
132:     }
133:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.level_exits.len() as u32);
134:     for exit in &payload.level_exits {
135:         for word in exit.to_words() {
136:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
137:         }
138:     }
139:     out
140: }

142: pub fn decode_chunk_payload(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
143:     let mut r = Reader { bytes, pos: 0 };
144:     if r.u32()? != MAGIC {
145:         return None;
146:     }
147:     let root = r.u32()?;
148:     let world_size = r.f32()?;
149:     let voxel_size = r.f32()?;
150:     let svo_depth = r.u8()?;
151: 
152:     let node_count = r.len(4)?;
153:     let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(node_count);
154:     for _ in 0..node_count {
155:         nodes.push(r.u32()?);
156:     }
157: 
158:     let vertex_count = r.len(10)?;
159:     let mut vertices = Vec::with_capacity(vertex_count);
160:     for _ in 0..vertex_count {
161:         vertices.push(PackedVertex {
162:             position: [r.u16()?, r.u16()?, r.u16()?],
163:             normal_axis: r.u8()?,
164:             material: r.u8()?,
165:             static_indirect: r.u8()?,
166:             ao: r.u8()?,
167:         });
168:     }
169:     let index_count = r.len(4)?;
170:     let mut indices = Vec::with_capacity(index_count);
171:     for _ in 0..index_count {
172:         indices.push(r.u32()?);
173:     }
174:     let bounds = r.aabb()?;
175:     let lod = r.u8()?;
176:     let voxel_scale = r.f32()?;
177:     let light_volume_size = [r.u32()?, r.u32()?, r.u32()?];
178:     let light_volume_padding = r.u8()?;
179:     let volume_len = r.len(1)?;
180:     let light_volume = r.slice(volume_len)?.to_vec();
181: 
182:     let light_count = r.len(51)?;
183:     let mut lights = Vec::with_capacity(light_count);
184:     for _ in 0..light_count {
185:         lights.push(LightSource {
186:             id: r.u64()?,
187:             position: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
188:             half_size: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
189:             color: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
190:             radius: r.f32()?,
191:             intensity: r.f32()?,
192:             kind: LightKind::from_u8(r.u8()?)?,
193:             flicker_mode: r.u8()?,
194:             enabled: r.u8()? != 0,
195:         });
196:     }
197: 
198:     let instance_count = r.len(13)?;
199:     let mut instances = Vec::with_capacity(instance_count);
200:     for _ in 0..instance_count {
201:         instances.push(PackedFaceInstance {
202:             position: [r.u16()?, r.u16()?, r.u16()?],
203:             extent_u: r.u8()?,
204:             extent_v: r.u8()?,
205:             normal_axis: r.u8()?,
206:             material: r.u8()?,
207:             baked_light: r.u8()?,
208:             ao: r.u8()?,
209:             flags: r.u8()?,
210:             reserved: [0; 3],
211:         });
212:     }
213:     let cell_count = r.len(11)?;
214:     let mut cells = Vec::with_capacity(cell_count);
215:     for _ in 0..cell_count {
216:         cells.push(FaceCellRange {
217:             cell: [r.u8()?, r.u8()?, r.u8()?],
218:             offset: r.u32()?,
219:             count: r.u32()?,
220:         });
221:     }
222:     let cell_size = r.f32()?;
223: 
224:     let collision_count = r.len(24)?;
225:     let mut collision = Vec::with_capacity(collision_count);
226:     for _ in 0..collision_count {
227:         collision.push(r.aabb()?);
228:     }
229: 
230:     let gate_count = r.len(TraversalGate::WORDS * 4)?;
231:     let mut traversal_gates = Vec::with_capacity(gate_count);
232:     for _ in 0..gate_count {
233:         let mut words = [0u32; TraversalGate::WORDS];
234:         for word in &mut words {
235:             *word = r.u32()?;
236:         }
237:         traversal_gates.push(TraversalGate::from_words(&words)?);
238:     }
239:     let hazard_count = r.len(PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS * 4)?;
240:     let mut pit_hazards = Vec::with_capacity(hazard_count);
241:     for _ in 0..hazard_count {
242:         let mut words = [0u32; PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS];
243:         for word in &mut words {
244:             *word = r.u32()?;
245:         }
246:         pit_hazards.push(PitHazard::from_transport_words(&words)?);
247:     }
248:     let supply_count = r.len(SupplyItem::WORDS * 4)?;
249:     let mut supply_items = Vec::with_capacity(supply_count);
250:     for _ in 0..supply_count {
251:         let mut words = [0u32; SupplyItem::WORDS];
252:         for word in &mut words {
253:             *word = r.u32()?;
254:         }
255:         supply_items.push(SupplyItem::from_words(&words)?);
256:     }
257:     let exit_count = r.len(LevelExit::WORDS * 4)?;
258:     let mut level_exits = Vec::with_capacity(exit_count);
259:     for _ in 0..exit_count {
260:         let mut words = [0u32; LevelExit::WORDS];
261:         for word in &mut words {
262:             *word = r.u32()?;
263:         }
264:         level_exits.push(LevelExit::from_words(&words)?);
265:     }
266: 
267:     Some(ChunkPayload {
268:         root,
269:         nodes,
270:         world_size,
271:         voxel_size,
272:         svo_depth,
273:         surface: SurfaceMeshPayload {
274:             vertices,
275:             indices,
276:             bounds,
277:             lod,
278:             light_volume,
279:             light_volume_size,
280:             light_volume_padding,
281:             lights,
282:             faces: FaceInstanceSet {
283:                 instances,
284:                 cells,
285:                 cell_size,
286:             },
287:             voxel_scale,
288:         },
289:         collision,
290:         traversal_gates,
291:         pit_hazards,
292:         supply_items,
293:         level_exits,
294:     })
295: }

297: fn put_u16(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u16) {
298:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
299: }
300: fn put_u32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {
301:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
302: }
303: fn put_f32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: f32) {
304:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
305: }
306: fn put_aabb(out: &mut Vec<u8>, aabb: &Aabb) {
307:     for c in aabb.min {
308:         put_f32(out, c);
309:     }
310:     for c in aabb.max {
311:         put_f32(out, c);
312:     }
313: }
314: 
315: struct Reader<'a> {
316:     bytes: &'a [u8],
317:     pos: usize,
318: }
319: 
320: impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
321:     fn slice(&mut self, n: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
322:         let end = self.pos.checked_add(n)?;
323:         let s = self.bytes.get(self.pos..end)?;
324:         self.pos = end;
325:         Some(s)
326:     }
327:     fn u8(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
328:         Some(self.slice(1)?[0])
329:     }
330:     fn u16(&mut self) -> Option<u16> {
331:         Some(u16::from_le_bytes(self.slice(2)?.try_into().ok()?))
332:     }
333:     fn u32(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
334:         Some(u32::from_le_bytes(self.slice(4)?.try_into().ok()?))
335:     }
336:     fn u64(&mut self) -> Option<u64> {
337:         Some(u64::from_le_bytes(self.slice(8)?.try_into().ok()?))
338:     }
339:     fn f32(&mut self) -> Option<f32> {
340:         Some(f32::from_le_bytes(self.slice(4)?.try_into().ok()?))
341:     }
342:     fn aabb(&mut self) -> Option<Aabb> {
343:         Some(Aabb::new(
344:             [self.f32()?, self.f32()?, self.f32()?],
345:             [self.f32()?, self.f32()?, self.f32()?],
346:         ))
347:     }
348:     /// Reads a length prefix and sanity-bounds it: each element occupies at
349:     /// least `min_element_bytes`, so a corrupt length cannot force a huge
350:     /// allocation before the reads start failing.
351:     fn len(&mut self, min_element_bytes: usize) -> Option<usize> {
352:         let n = self.u32()? as usize;
353:         let remaining = self.bytes.len().saturating_sub(self.pos);
354:         if n.saturating_mul(min_element_bytes.max(1)) > remaining {
355:             return None;
356:         }
357:         Some(n)
358:     }
359: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/input.rs
````rust
  1: //! Input adapter: accumulates raw browser events (key codes, mouse deltas,
  2: //! pointer-lock state) and translates them into one [`InputFrame`] per tick.
  3: //!
  4: //! The driver layer feeds this from DOM event listeners; the frame loop
  5: //! drains it with [`InputCollector::take_frame`]. Keeping the mapping here —
  6: //! not in the driver — means "which key means forward" is a testable rule,
  7: //! not something buried in an event closure.
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::engine::InputFrame;
 10: use crate::application::player::MoveIntent;
 11: 
 12: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 13: pub struct InputCollector {
 14:     intent: MoveIntent,
 15:     pending_dx: f32,
 16:     pending_dy: f32,
 17:     locked: bool,
 18:     flashlight: bool,
 19:     /// One queued flare drop, consumed by the next frame. Edge-triggered:
 20:     /// holding G never queues a second drop until the key is released.
 21:     flare_queued: bool,
 22:     flare_key_held: bool,
 23: }
 24: 
 25: impl InputCollector {
 26:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 27:         Self::default()
 28:     }
 29: 
 30:     /// Handles a keydown/keyup pair by `KeyboardEvent.code` value.
 31:     /// Unknown codes are ignored. Both WASD and arrow keys are mapped.
 32:     pub fn key_event(&mut self, code: &str, pressed: bool) {
 33:         #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 34:         let doom = crate::DOOM_CONTROLS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
 35: 
 36:         #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
 37:         let doom = false;
 38: 
 39:         if pressed && code == "KeyF" {
 40:             self.flashlight = !self.flashlight;
 41:         }
 42: 
 43:         // Flare drop: fires once per press, only while playing (the engine
 44:         // additionally ignores drops when the session is not locked, so a
 45:         // G typed into the settings menu can never reach gameplay).
 46:         if code == "KeyG" {
 47:             if pressed && !self.flare_key_held && self.locked {
 48:                 self.flare_queued = true;
 49:             }
 50:             self.flare_key_held = pressed;
 51:         }
 52: 
 53:         if doom {
 54:             match code {
 55:                 "KeyW" | "ArrowUp" => self.intent.forward = pressed,
 56:                 "KeyS" | "ArrowDown" => self.intent.backward = pressed,
 57:                 "KeyQ" => self.intent.left = pressed,
 58:                 "KeyE" => self.intent.right = pressed,
 59:                 "KeyA" | "ArrowLeft" => self.intent.turn_left = pressed,
 60:                 "KeyD" | "ArrowRight" => self.intent.turn_right = pressed,
 61:                 _ => {}
 62:             }
 63:         } else {
 64:             match code {
 65:                 "KeyW" | "ArrowUp" => self.intent.forward = pressed,
 66:                 "KeyS" | "ArrowDown" => self.intent.backward = pressed,
 67:                 "KeyA" | "ArrowLeft" => self.intent.left = pressed,
 68:                 "KeyD" | "ArrowRight" => self.intent.right = pressed,
 69:                 "KeyQ" => self.intent.turn_left = pressed,
 70:                 "KeyE" => self.intent.turn_right = pressed,
 71:                 _ => {}
 72:             }
 73:         }
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     /// Accumulates a mouse movement (only meaningful while pointer-locked).
 77:     pub fn mouse_delta(&mut self, dx: f32, dy: f32) {
 78:         if self.locked {
 79:             #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 80:             let (sens, invert) = {
 81:                 use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
 82:                 (
 83:                     f32::from_bits(crate::MOUSE_SENSITIVITY_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
 84:                     crate::INVERT_Y.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
 85:                 )
 86:             };
 87:             #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
 88:             let (sens, invert) = (1.0f32, false);
 89: 
 90:             self.pending_dx += dx * sens;
 91:             self.pending_dy += dy * sens * if invert { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
 92:         }
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     /// Sets movement intent from an analog source (the touch joystick).
 96:     /// `x` is strafe (-1..1, right positive), `y` is walk (-1..1, forward
 97:     /// positive). Values inside the dead zone clear the intent, so lifting
 98:     /// the thumb stops the player.
 99:     pub fn set_move_axes(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32) {
100:         const DEAD_ZONE: f32 = 0.25;
101:         self.intent.forward = y > DEAD_ZONE;
102:         self.intent.backward = y < -DEAD_ZONE;
103:         self.intent.right = x > DEAD_ZONE;
104:         self.intent.left = x < -DEAD_ZONE;
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Toggles the flashlight (touch button; keyboard uses KeyF).
108:     pub fn toggle_flashlight(&mut self) {
109:         self.flashlight = !self.flashlight;
110:     }
111: 
112:     /// Queues one flare drop (touch button; keyboard uses KeyG). One queued
113:     /// drop per frame regardless of how many events bubble in.
114:     pub fn queue_flare(&mut self) {
115:         if self.locked {
116:             self.flare_queued = true;
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     /// Pointer lock engaged/released. Releasing clears held keys so the
121:     /// player doesn't keep walking while the overlay is up.
122:     pub fn set_locked(&mut self, locked: bool) {
123:         self.locked = locked;
124:         if !locked {
125:             self.intent = MoveIntent::default();
126:             self.pending_dx = 0.0;
127:             self.pending_dy = 0.0;
128:             self.flare_queued = false;
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     pub fn is_locked(&self) -> bool {
133:         self.locked
134:     }
135: 
136:     /// Drains accumulated input into a frame snapshot. Mouse deltas reset;
137:     /// key intent persists until the matching keyup.
138:     pub fn take_frame(&mut self) -> InputFrame {
139:         let frame = InputFrame {
140:             intent: self.intent,
141:             look_dx: self.pending_dx,
142:             look_dy: self.pending_dy,
143:             locked: self.locked,
144:             flashlight: self.flashlight,
145:             drop_flare: self.flare_queued,
146:         };
147:         self.pending_dx = 0.0;
148:         self.pending_dy = 0.0;
149:         self.flare_queued = false;
150:         frame
151:     }
152: }
153: 
154: #[cfg(test)]
155: mod tests {
156:     use super::*;
157: 
158:     #[test]
159:     fn wasd_maps_to_intent_and_persists_across_frames() {
160:         let mut input = InputCollector::new();
161:         input.set_locked(true);
162:         input.key_event("KeyW", true);
163:         input.key_event("KeyD", true);
164:         let f1 = input.take_frame();
165:         assert!(f1.intent.forward && f1.intent.right);
166:         let f2 = input.take_frame();
167:         assert!(f2.intent.forward, "held keys persist");
168:         input.key_event("KeyW", false);
169:         assert!(!input.take_frame().intent.forward);
170:     }
171: 
172:     #[test]
173:     fn mouse_deltas_accumulate_then_drain() {
174:         let mut input = InputCollector::new();
175:         input.set_locked(true);
176:         input.mouse_delta(3.0, -1.0);
177:         input.mouse_delta(2.0, 1.0);
178:         let f = input.take_frame();
179:         assert_eq!((f.look_dx, f.look_dy), (5.0, 0.0));
180:         let f2 = input.take_frame();
181:         assert_eq!((f2.look_dx, f2.look_dy), (0.0, 0.0));
182:     }
183: 
184:     #[test]
185:     fn unlock_clears_held_keys_and_ignores_mouse() {
186:         let mut input = InputCollector::new();
187:         input.set_locked(true);
188:         input.key_event("KeyW", true);
189:         input.set_locked(false);
190:         input.mouse_delta(10.0, 10.0);
191:         let f = input.take_frame();
192:         assert!(!f.intent.forward);
193:         assert_eq!(f.look_dx, 0.0);
194:         assert!(!f.locked);
195:     }
196: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Shared GLSL chunks — snippets spliced into more than one shader so the
  2: //! engine has exactly one definition of each cross-cutting effect.
  3: //!
  4: //! Shader sources are assembled at startup by `format!` concatenation (a
  5: //! few string copies once per program link — nothing per frame). Each chunk
  6: //! is a self-contained set of GLSL functions/consts with no `uniform`
  7: //! declarations, so any stage can include it.
  8: 
  9: /// The flashlight spotlight cone — **GLSL mirror of the single spec in
 10: /// `adapters::cpu_splatter::flashlight`** (inner/outer angle, finite-range
 11: /// inverse-square transport, lamp offset, and tint). A tuning change there
 12: /// must be mirrored here.
 13: ///
 14: /// Shape: smoothstep between an inner cone (full strength, 11°) and an
 15: /// outer cone (zero, 24°) around the camera forward axis. Transport uses a
 16: /// compact-support inverse-square law and a strict Lambert receiver cosine.
 17: pub const SPOT_CONE_GLSL: &str = r#"
 18: // --- flashlight cone (spec: adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs) ---
 19: const float SPOT_INNER_COS = 0.9816272; // cos(11 deg)
 20: const float SPOT_OUTER_COS = 0.9135455; // cos(24 deg)
 21: const float SPOT_RANGE_END = 14.0;
 22: const float SPOT_INTENSITY = 32.0;
 23: const float SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE = 0.25;
 24: const float SPOT_INV_PI = 0.3183098861837907;
 25: const vec3  SPOT_TINT = vec3(1.0, 0.91, 0.72);
 26: 
 27: // The hand-held lamp sits slightly forward of and below the eye.
 28: vec3 spotLampPos(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward) {
 29:     return camPos + camForward * 0.18 - vec3(0.0, 0.10, 0.0);
 30: }
 31: 
 32: // Angular falloff: 1 inside the inner cone, 0 outside the outer.
 33: float spotCone(vec3 beam, vec3 camForward) {
 34:     return smoothstep(SPOT_OUTER_COS, SPOT_INNER_COS, dot(beam, camForward));
 35: }
 36: 
 37: // Finite-range inverse-square transport. The compact window and its first
 38: // derivative both reach zero at RANGE_END, so the beam has no hard rim.
 39: float spotAttenuation(float dist) {
 40:     if (!(dist >= 0.0) || dist >= SPOT_RANGE_END) return 0.0;
 41:     float normalizedSquared = (dist * dist) / (SPOT_RANGE_END * SPOT_RANGE_END);
 42:     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
 43:     float minimumSquared = SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE * SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE;
 44:     return (window * window) / max(dist * dist, minimumSquared);
 45: }
 46: 
 47: // Lambertian reflected-radiance factor at a surface point with normal N.
 48: // The CPU contract evaluates irradiance first and multiplies albedo / PI;
 49: // folding 1/PI here preserves that exact composition at GPU call sites.
 50: vec3 spotBeam(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward, vec3 surfacePos, vec3 N) {
 51:     vec3 lamp = spotLampPos(camPos, camForward);
 52:     vec3 toSurf = surfacePos - lamp;
 53:     float dist = length(toSurf);
 54:     vec3 beam = toSurf / max(dist, 1e-4);
 55:     float cone = spotCone(beam, camForward);
 56:     float attenuation = spotAttenuation(dist);
 57:     float facing = max(-dot(beam, N), 0.0);
 58:     return SPOT_TINT * (SPOT_INTENSITY * SPOT_INV_PI * cone * attenuation * facing);
 59: }
 60: "#;
 61: 
 62: /// Material palette lookup, shared by the surface and splat paths so both
 63: /// rasterizers color a wall identically.
 64: pub const MATERIAL_COLOR_GLSL: &str = r#"
 65: vec3 materialColor(float material) {
 66:     // Exact bytes from domain::voxel_grid::MATERIAL_COLORS. Keeping the
 67:     // integer numerators visible makes palette drift reviewable.
 68:     if (material < 1.5) return vec3(221.0, 204.0, 102.0) / 255.0;
 69:     if (material < 2.5) return vec3(153.0, 136.0,  17.0) / 255.0;
 70:     if (material < 3.5) return vec3(204.0, 204.0, 204.0) / 255.0;
 71:     if (material < 4.5) return vec3(255.0, 248.0, 214.0) / 255.0;
 72:     if (material < 5.5) return vec3(136.0,   0.0,   0.0) / 255.0;

 74:     if (material < 7.5) return vec3( 58.0, 111.0, 184.0) / 255.0;
 75:     if (material < 8.5) return vec3(107.0,  74.0,  47.0) / 255.0;
 76:     if (material < 9.5) return vec3(255.0,  68.0,  51.0) / 255.0;
 77:     if (material < 10.5) return vec3(216.0, 210.0, 192.0) / 255.0;
 78:     if (material < 11.5) return vec3(138.0, 127.0,  92.0) / 255.0;
 79:     if (material < 12.5) return vec3(194.0, 183.0, 107.0) / 255.0;
 80:     if (material < 13.5) return vec3(107.0,  94.0,  34.0) / 255.0;
 81:     if (material < 14.5) return vec3(122.0,  74.0,  38.0) / 255.0;
 82:     if (material < 15.5) return vec3( 46.0,  42.0,  34.0) / 255.0;
 83:     if (material < 16.5) return vec3(159.0, 196.0, 232.0) / 255.0;
 84:     if (material < 17.5) return vec3(143.0, 141.0, 136.0) / 255.0;
 85:     if (material < 18.5) return vec3(189.0, 187.0, 176.0) / 255.0;
 86:     if (material < 19.5) return vec3(110.0, 108.0, 102.0) / 255.0;
 87:     if (material < 20.5) return vec3(156.0, 123.0,  74.0) / 255.0;
 88:     if (material < 21.5) return vec3( 62.0,  67.0,  72.0) / 255.0;
 89:     if (material < 22.5) return vec3( 74.0,  90.0, 106.0) / 255.0;
 90:     return vec3(237.0, 230.0, 208.0) / 255.0;
 91: }
 92: "#;
 93: 
 94: /// World-hash and interleaved-gradient-noise helpers.
 95: ///
 96: /// OPTIMIZATION: IGN is two `fract`s and a `dot` — far cheaper than a
 97: /// sin-hash — and is used to break up 8-bit banding in fog gradients,
 98: /// which is especially visible at reduced internal resolutions.
 99: pub const NOISE_GLSL: &str = r#"
100: float hash3D(vec3 p) {
101:     return fract(sin(dot(p, vec3(12.9898, 78.233, 45.164))) * 43758.5453);
102: }
103: 
104: float ign(vec2 p) {
105:     vec3 magic = vec3(0.06711056, 0.00583715, 52.9829189);
106:     return fract(magic.z * fract(dot(p, magic.xy)));
107: }
108: "#;
109: 
110: /// Reinhard tone map + gamma, shared by the surface and splat fragments.
111: pub const TONE_MAP_GLSL: &str = r#"
112: vec3 toneMap(vec3 color) {
113:     color = color / (color + vec3(1.0));
114:     return pow(color, vec3(1.0 / 2.2));
115: }
116: "#;
117: 
118: /// Flare-core glow sprites: additive embers occluded by any surface nearer
119: /// than the flare along the fragment's view ray — no x-ray dots. Shared by
120: /// the surface and splat fragments; requires the `uCoreCount` / `uCores` /
121: /// `uCoreColors` uniforms to be declared before this chunk is spliced in
122: /// (both programs declare them identically).
123: pub const FLARE_CORES_GLSL: &str = r#"
124: vec3 flareCoresThroughMedium(
125:     vec3 worldPos,
126:     vec3 camPos,
127:     float fogStart,
128:     float sigmaExtinction
129: ) {
130:     vec3 toFrag = worldPos - camPos;
131:     float fragDist = length(toFrag);
132:     vec3 rd = toFrag / max(fragDist, 1e-4);
133:     vec3 sum = vec3(0.0);
134:     for (int i = 0; i < uCoreCount; i++) {
135:         vec3 toLight = uCores[i].xyz - camPos;
136:         float along = dot(toLight, rd);
137:         if (along <= 0.05 || along >= fragDist) continue;
138:         float perp = length(toLight - rd * along);
139:         float coreSize = 0.06 + along * 0.004;
140:         float core = 1.0 - smoothstep(coreSize * 0.4, coreSize, perp);
141:         float mediumDistance = max(along - max(fogStart, 0.0), 0.0);
142:         float transmittance = exp(-max(sigmaExtinction, 0.0) * mediumDistance);
143:         sum += uCoreColors[i] * uCores[i].w * core * 1.4 * transmittance;
144:     }
145:     return sum;
146: }
147: 
148: vec3 flareCores(vec3 worldPos, vec3 camPos) {
149:     return flareCoresThroughMedium(worldPos, camPos, 0.0, 0.0);
150: }
151: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/worker_source.rs
````rust
  1: //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
  2: //!
  3: //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
  4: //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
  5: //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality}` messages round-robin; workers run the full
  6: //! chunk pipeline (generation, voxel diffuse bake, greedy mesh + face instances,
  7: //! SVO build/serialize, collision) and transfer one encoded byte buffer
  8: //! back (`adapters::chunk_codec`). No WebGL object ever leaves the main
  9: //! thread. Healthy pools keep generation off the frame loop; if every worker
 10: //! fatally fails, the driver uses its same-thread source as a correctness
 11: //! fallback instead of leaving the world permanently pending.
 12: //!
 13: //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
 14: //! by the echoed request. This driver owns transport failure detection and
 15: //! reports exact failed requests through the same application port.
 16: 
 17: use std::cell::RefCell;
 18: use std::rc::Rc;
 19: 
 20: use js_sys::{ArrayBuffer, Reflect, Uint8Array};
 21: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
 22: use web_sys::{MessageEvent, Worker, WorkerOptions, WorkerType};
 23: 
 24: use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::decode_chunk_payload;
 25: use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
 26: use crate::application::generation_worker_policy::MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS;
 27: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkPayload, ChunkRequest, ChunkSourcePort, CompletedChunk};
 28: use crate::drivers::generation_worker_requests::GenerationWorkerRequests;
 29: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 30: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 31: 
 32: pub struct WorkerChunkSource {
 33:     workers: Vec<Worker>,
 34:     next_worker: usize,
 35:     completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>>,
 36:     failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>>,
 37:     requests: Rc<RefCell<GenerationWorkerRequests>>,
 38:     /// Keeps browser callbacks alive for the workers' lifetime.
 39:     _message_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>>,
 40:     _error_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>>,
 41:     /// Same-thread source for the synchronous [`ChunkSourcePort::load`]
 42:     /// contract and as a last-resort recovery if every worker has failed.
 43:     fallback: LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>,
 44:     reported_emergency_fallback: bool,
 45: }
 46: 
 47: impl WorkerChunkSource {
 48:     /// Spawns the pool and hands every worker the URL query, so main thread
 49:     /// and workers derive the identical generator configuration.
 50:     pub fn new(query: &str, default_seed: u32, pool_size: usize) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 51:         if !(1..=usize::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)).contains(&pool_size) {
 52:             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
 53:                 "generation worker pool size must be 1..=4",
 54:             ));
 55:         }
 56: 
 57:         let completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
 58:         let failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
 59:         let requests = Rc::new(RefCell::new(GenerationWorkerRequests::new(pool_size)));
 60:         // The single-file bundle (scripts/build-single-file.mjs) has no
 61:         // sibling worker.js on disk; it publishes a blob: URL for the inlined
 62:         // worker script on the global scope instead.
 63:         let script_url = Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__".into())
 64:             .ok()
 65:             .and_then(|value| value.as_string())
 66:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "worker.js".to_string());
 67:         let mut workers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 68:         let mut message_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 69:         let mut error_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 70:         for worker_index in 0..pool_size {
 71:             let options = WorkerOptions::new();
 72:             options.set_type(WorkerType::Module);
 73:             // Relative (not `/worker.js`): resolved against the document's
 74:             // URL, so this still finds the sibling file when the site is
 75:             // served from a subpath (e.g. a GitHub Pages project page at
 76:             // `<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) instead of the domain root.
 77:             let worker = Worker::new_with_options(&script_url, &options)?;
 78: 
 79:             let completed_sink = completed.clone();
 80:             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
 81:             let message_requests = requests.clone();
 82:             let worker_for_fatal_reply = worker.clone();
 83:             let handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>::new(move |event: MessageEvent| {
 84:                 match parse_worker_reply(&event) {
 85:                     WorkerReply::Completed(done) => {
 86:                         if message_requests
 87:                             .borrow_mut()
 88:                             .finish_exact(worker_index, &done.request)
 89:                         {
 90:                             completed_sink.borrow_mut().push(done);
 91:                         }
 92:                     }
 93:                     WorkerReply::Failed(echoed) => {
 94:                         if let Some(failed_request) = message_requests
 95:                             .borrow_mut()
 96:                             .fail_exact(worker_index, &echoed)
 97:                         {
 98:                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
 99:                         }
100:                     }
101:                     WorkerReply::Fatal => {
102:                         let abandoned = message_requests
103:                             .borrow_mut()
104:                             .disable_and_drain(worker_index);
105:                         failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
106:                         worker_for_fatal_reply.terminate();
107:                     }
108:                     WorkerReply::Malformed => {
109:                         if let Some(failed_request) =
110:                             message_requests.borrow_mut().fail_oldest(worker_index)
111:                         {
112:                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
113:                         }
114:                     }
115:                 }
116:             });
117:             worker.set_onmessage(Some(handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
118: 
119:             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
120:             let error_requests = requests.clone();
121:             let worker_for_error = worker.clone();
122:             let error_handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |_event| {
123:                 let abandoned = error_requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
124:                 failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
125:                 worker_for_error.terminate();
126:             });
127:             worker.set_onerror(Some(error_handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
128: 
129:             let init = js_sys::Object::new();
130:             Reflect::set(&init, &"type".into(), &"init".into())?;
131:             Reflect::set(&init, &"query".into(), &query.into())?;
132:             Reflect::set(&init, &"seed".into(), &(default_seed as f64).into())?;
133:             worker.post_message(&init)?;
134: 
135:             workers.push(worker);
136:             message_handlers.push(handler);
137:             error_handlers.push(error_handler);
138:         }
139: 
140:         let (seed, config) =
141:             crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
142:         Ok(Self {
143:             workers,
144:             next_worker: 0,
145:             completed,
146:             failed,
147:             requests,
148:             _message_handlers: message_handlers,
149:             _error_handlers: error_handlers,
150:             fallback: LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config),
151:             reported_emergency_fallback: false,
152:         })
153:     }
154: 
155:     pub fn pool_size(&self) -> usize {
156:         self.workers.len()
157:     }
158: }
159: 
160: impl ChunkSourcePort for WorkerChunkSource {
161:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
162:         self.fallback.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
163:     }
164: 
165:     fn load_with_reality(
166:         &self,
167:         origin_x: f32,
168:         origin_z: f32,
169:         level: u32,
170:         lod: u8,
171:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
172:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
173:         self.fallback
174:             .load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
175:     }
176: 
177:     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
178:         true
179:     }
180: 
181:     fn request(&mut self, request: ChunkRequest) {
182:         let worker_index = self.requests.borrow().next_accepting(self.next_worker);
183:         let Some(worker_index) = worker_index else {
184:             // Fatal worker startup/runtime failures must not strand streaming.
185:             // This path is deliberately exceptional: the healthy path always
186:             // generates off-thread, while an exhausted pool favors a complete
187:             // world over a permanently pending chunk.
188:             if !self.reported_emergency_fallback {
189:                 web_sys::console::warn_1(
190:                     &"generation worker pool failed; using same-thread recovery".into(),
191:                 );
192:                 self.reported_emergency_fallback = true;
193:             }
194:             let payload = self.fallback.load_with_reality(
195:                 request.origin_x,
196:                 request.origin_z,
197:                 request.level,
198:                 request.lod,
199:                 &request.reality,
200:             );
201:             self.completed
202:                 .borrow_mut()
203:                 .push(CompletedChunk { request, payload });
204:             return;
205:         };
206: 
207:         let message = js_sys::Object::new();
208:         let set = |k: &str, v: JsValue| {
209:             let _ = Reflect::set(&message, &k.into(), &v);
210:         };
211:         set("type", "gen".into());
212:         set("requestId", (request.request_id as f64).into());
213:         set("ox", (request.origin_x as f64).into());
214:         set("oz", (request.origin_z as f64).into());
215:         set("level", (request.level as f64).into());
216:         set("lod", (request.lod as f64).into());
217:         let reality_words = request.reality.to_words();
218:         let reality = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(reality_words.as_slice());
219:         set("reality", reality.into());
220:         let worker = &self.workers[worker_index];
221:         self.next_worker = (worker_index + 1) % self.workers.len();
222:         self.requests
223:             .borrow_mut()
224:             .assign(worker_index, request.clone());
225:         if let Err(error) = worker.post_message(&message) {
226:             // A synchronous send failure means this worker can no longer be
227:             // trusted with its already queued requests. Retire all of them;
228:             // the engine will validate their ids and retry on healthy slots.
229:             let abandoned = self.requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
230:             self.failed.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
231:             worker.terminate();
232:             web_sys::console::warn_2(
233:                 &"generation worker postMessage failed; disabling worker:".into(),
234:                 &error,
235:             );
236:         }
237:     }
238: 
239:     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
240:         std::mem::take(&mut *self.completed.borrow_mut())
241:     }
242: 
243:     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
244:         std::mem::take(&mut *self.failed.borrow_mut())
245:     }
246: }
247: 
248: enum WorkerReply {
249:     Completed(CompletedChunk),
250:     Failed(ChunkRequest),
251:     Fatal,
252:     Malformed,
253: }
254: 
255: /// Decodes the deliberately small worker protocol. Malformed replies are a
256: /// first-class outcome: the worker queue is serial, so the caller can fail its
257: /// oldest assigned request instead of leaving that chunk pending forever.
258: fn parse_worker_reply(event: &MessageEvent) -> WorkerReply {
259:     let data = event.data();
260:     let message_type = Reflect::get(&data, &"type".into())
261:         .ok()
262:         .and_then(|value| value.as_string());
263:     match message_type.as_deref() {
264:         Some("done") => parse_request(&data)
265:             .and_then(|request| {
266:                 parse_payload(&data).map(|payload| CompletedChunk { request, payload })
267:             })
268:             .map(WorkerReply::Completed)
269:             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
270:         Some("failed") => parse_request(&data)
271:             .map(WorkerReply::Failed)
272:             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
273:         Some("fatal") => WorkerReply::Fatal,
274:         _ => WorkerReply::Malformed,
275:     }
276: }
277: 
278: fn parse_request(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
279:     let field = |name: &str| Reflect::get(data, &name.into()).ok();
280:     Some(ChunkRequest {
281:         request_id: exact_u32(field("requestId")?)?,
282:         origin_x: finite_f32(field("ox")?)?,
283:         origin_z: finite_f32(field("oz")?)?,
284:         level: exact_u32(field("level")?)?,
285:         lod: u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("lod")?)?).ok()?,
286:         reality: {
287:             let encoded = field("reality")?;
288:             let words = encoded.dyn_into::<js_sys::Uint32Array>().ok()?.to_vec();
289:             RealitySnapshot::from_words(&words).ok()?
290:         },
291:     })
292: }
293: 
294: fn parse_payload(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
295:     let buffer: ArrayBuffer = Reflect::get(data, &"buf".into()).ok()?.dyn_into().ok()?;
296:     let bytes = Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec();
297:     decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
298: }
299: 
300: fn exact_u32(value: JsValue) -> Option<u32> {
301:     let number = value.as_f64()?;
302:     (number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..=f64::from(u32::MAX)).contains(&number))
303:         .then_some(number as u32)
304: }
305: 
306: fn finite_f32(value: JsValue) -> Option<f32> {
307:     let number = value.as_f64()?;
308:     let narrowed = number as f32;
309:     (number.is_finite() && narrowed.is_finite()).then_some(narrowed)
310: }
````

````rust
 79: /// Occupancy lookup used by the surface extractor. Coordinates are relative
 80: /// to the meshed chunk; implementations may resolve a one-voxel halo from
 81: /// adjacent chunks or a deterministically generated border. Missing lateral
 82: /// neighbors must be conservative (solid), never treated as air.
 83: pub trait VoxelNeighborhood {
 84:     fn voxel(&self, x: i32, y: i32, z: i32) -> u8;
 85: }
 86: 
 87: struct GridNeighborhood<'a> {
 88:     grid: &'a VoxelGrid,
 89:     origin: [usize; 3],
 90:     conservative_lateral_border: bool,
 91: }
 92: 
 93: impl VoxelNeighborhood for GridNeighborhood<'_> {
 94:     fn voxel(&self, x: i32, y: i32, z: i32) -> u8 {
 95:         let gx = self.origin[0] as i32 + x;
 96:         let gy = self.origin[1] as i32 + y;
 97:         let gz = self.origin[2] as i32 + z;
 98:         if gy < 0 || gy >= self.grid.height() as i32 {
 99:             return VOXEL_AIR;
100:         }
101:         if gx < 0 || gx >= self.grid.width() as i32 || gz < 0 || gz >= self.grid.depth() as i32 {
102:             return if self.conservative_lateral_border {
103:                 VOXEL_WALL
104:             } else {
105:                 VOXEL_AIR
106:             };
107:         }
108:         self.grid.get(gx as usize, gy as usize, gz as usize)
109:     }
110: }
111: 
112: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
113: struct FaceKey {
114:     v_type: VoxelType,
115:     color: u32,
116:     light: u8,
117:     ao: u8,
118: }

120: pub struct VoxelMapper {

124: impl VoxelMapper {
125:     pub fn new(voxel_scale: f32) -> Self {
126:         Self { voxel_scale }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Maps the entire grid into merged exposed quads. This compatibility
130:     /// helper treats out-of-grid X/Z as air; streamed rendering should use
131:     /// [`Self::map_voxel_grid_with_padding`] instead.
132:     pub fn map_voxel_grid(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
133:         let neighborhood = GridNeighborhood {
134:             grid,
135:             origin: [0, 0, 0],
136:             conservative_lateral_border: false,
137:         };
138:         self.map_voxel_region(
139:             grid,
140:             [0, 0, 0],
141:             [grid.width(), grid.height(), grid.depth()],
142:             &neighborhood,
143:         )
144:     }
145: 
146:     /// Greedily meshes the interior of a grid carrying a one-voxel X/Z halo.
147:     /// Faces across a chunk edge are emitted only when the halo says the
148:     /// adjacent voxel is air, eliminating duplicate boundary faces and the
149:     /// pop that comes from assuming an unavailable neighbor is air.
150:     pub fn map_voxel_grid_with_padding(
151:         &self,
152:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
153:         lateral_padding: usize,
154:     ) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
155:         assert!(lateral_padding > 0, "surface meshing requires a voxel halo");
156:         assert!(grid.width() > lateral_padding * 2 && grid.depth() > lateral_padding * 2);
157:         let neighborhood = GridNeighborhood {
158:             grid,
159:             origin: [lateral_padding, 0, lateral_padding],
160:             conservative_lateral_border: true,
161:         };
162:         self.map_voxel_region(
163:             grid,
164:             [lateral_padding, 0, lateral_padding],
165:             [
166:                 grid.width() - lateral_padding * 2,
167:                 grid.height(),
168:                 grid.depth() - lateral_padding * 2,
169:             ],
170:             &neighborhood,
171:         )
172:     }
173: 
174:     /// Surface extraction against a supplied occupancy neighborhood. The
175:     /// dense `grid` supplies material/light/AO attributes for the interior;
176:     /// `neighborhood` decides whether each candidate face is exposed.
177:     pub fn map_voxel_region(
178:         &self,
179:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
180:         interior_origin: [usize; 3],
181:         dimensions: [usize; 3],
182:         neighborhood: &dyn VoxelNeighborhood,
183:     ) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
184:         let mut quads = Vec::new();
185:         let scale = self.voxel_scale;
186:         let [w_dim, h_dim, d_dim] = dimensions;
187: 
188:         let attrs = |x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, v: u8, dir: FaceDirection| {
189:             self.face_key(
190:                 grid,
191:                 interior_origin[0] + x,
192:                 interior_origin[1] + y,
193:                 interior_origin[2] + z,
194:                 v,
195:                 dir,
196:             )
197:         };
198:         let mut append = |x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, w: f32, h: f32, dir, key: FaceKey| {
199:             quads.push(MergedQuad {
200:                 x,
201:                 y,
202:                 z,
203:                 w,
204:                 h,
205:                 dir,
206:                 v_type: key.v_type,
207:                 color: key.color,
208:                 light: key.light,
209:                 ao: key.ao,
210:             });
211:         };
212: 
213:         // +Y / -Y faces: 2D slices in X/Z.
214:         for y in 0..h_dim {
215:             for (dir, dy) in [(FaceDirection::Up, 1), (FaceDirection::Down, -1)] {
216:                 let get_face = |x: usize, z: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
217:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
218:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
219:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32 + dy, z as i32) == VOXEL_AIR)
220:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
221:                 };
222:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(w_dim, d_dim, &get_face) {
223:                     append(
224:                         u as f32 * scale,
225:                         y as f32 * scale,
226:                         v as f32 * scale,
227:                         qw as f32 * scale,
228:                         qh as f32 * scale,
229:                         dir,
230:                         key,
231:                     );
232:                 }
233:             }
234:         }
235: 
236:         // -Z / +Z faces: 2D slices in X/Y.
237:         for z in 0..d_dim {
238:             for (dir, dz) in [(FaceDirection::North, -1), (FaceDirection::South, 1)] {
239:                 let get_face = |x: usize, y: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
240:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
241:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
242:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32 + dz) == VOXEL_AIR)
243:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
244:                 };
245:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(w_dim, h_dim, &get_face) {
246:                     append(
247:                         u as f32 * scale,
248:                         v as f32 * scale,
249:                         z as f32 * scale,
250:                         qw as f32 * scale,
251:                         qh as f32 * scale,
252:                         dir,
253:                         key,
254:                     );
255:                 }
256:             }
257:         }
258: 
259:         // +X / -X faces: 2D slices in Z/Y.
260:         for x in 0..w_dim {
261:             for (dir, dx) in [(FaceDirection::East, 1), (FaceDirection::West, -1)] {
262:                 let get_face = |z: usize, y: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
263:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
264:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
265:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32 + dx, y as i32, z as i32) == VOXEL_AIR)
266:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
267:                 };
268:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(d_dim, h_dim, &get_face) {
269:                     append(
270:                         x as f32 * scale,
271:                         v as f32 * scale,
272:                         u as f32 * scale,
273:                         qw as f32 * scale,
274:                         qh as f32 * scale,
275:                         dir,
276:                         key,
277:                     );
278:                 }
279:             }
280:         }
281: 
282:         quads
283:     }
284: 
285:     fn face_key(
286:         &self,
287:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
288:         x: usize,
289:         y: usize,
290:         z: usize,
291:         voxel: u8,
292:         dir: FaceDirection,
293:     ) -> FaceKey {
294:         let ao = u8::from(grid.get_face_occlusion(x, y, z) & dir.occlusion_bit() != 0);
295:         FaceKey {
296:             v_type: Self::voxel_type(voxel),
297:             color: Self::material_color(voxel),
298:             light: grid.get_light(x, y, z),
299:             ao,
300:         }
301:     }

303:     fn voxel_type(voxel: u8) -> VoxelType {

305:             VOXEL_WALL => VoxelType::Wall,
306:             VOXEL_FLOOR => VoxelType::Floor,
307:             VOXEL_CEILING => VoxelType::Ceiling,
308:             VOXEL_LIGHT => VoxelType::Light,
309:             VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => VoxelType::RedLight,
310:             VOXEL_RED_WALL => VoxelType::RedWall,
311:             VOXEL_GRASS => VoxelType::Grass,
312:             VOXEL_WATER => VoxelType::Water,
313:             VOXEL_TREE => VoxelType::Tree,
314:             VOXEL_PALE_WALL => VoxelType::PaleWall,
315:             VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL => VoxelType::DamagedWall,
316:             VOXEL_DRY_CARPET => VoxelType::DryCarpet,
317:             VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET => VoxelType::DeepCarpet,
318:             VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET => VoxelType::StickyCarpet,
319:             VOXEL_FLUID => VoxelType::Fluid,
320:             VOXEL_GLIMMER => VoxelType::Glimmer,
321:             VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL => VoxelType::ConcreteWall,
322:             VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR => VoxelType::TileFloor,
323:             VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR => VoxelType::ConcreteFloor,
324:             VOXEL_CRATE => VoxelType::Crate,
325:             VOXEL_PIPE => VoxelType::Pipe,
326:             VOXEL_METAL_DOOR => VoxelType::MetalDoor,
327:             VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER => VoxelType::AlmondWater,
328:             _ => VoxelType::Wall,
329:         }
330:     }
331: 
332:     fn material_color(voxel: u8) -> u32 {
333:         // Single authority: the palette table beside the material ids.
334:         MATERIAL_COLORS
335:             .get(voxel as usize)
336:             .copied()
337:             .unwrap_or(0x000000)
338:     }
339: 
340:     /// Helper that performs 2D greedy meshing on a slice.
341:     fn greedy_mesh_2d(
342:         &self,
343:         w_slice: usize,
344:         h_slice: usize,
345:         get_face: &dyn Fn(usize, usize) -> Option<FaceKey>,
346:     ) -> Vec<(usize, usize, usize, usize, FaceKey)> {
347:         let mut visited = vec![vec![false; h_slice]; w_slice];
348:         let mut quads = Vec::new();
349: 
350:         for v in 0..h_slice {
351:             for u in 0..w_slice {
352:                 if visited[u][v] {
353:                     continue;
354:                 }
355: 
356:                 if let Some(key) = get_face(u, v) {
357:                     // Find max width along u
358:                     let mut quad_w = 1;
359:                     while u + quad_w < w_slice {
360:                         if visited[u + quad_w][v] {
361:                             break;
362:                         }
363:                         if let Some(next) = get_face(u + quad_w, v) {
364:                             if next == key {
365:                                 quad_w += 1;
366:                                 continue;
367:                             }
368:                         }
369:                         break;
370:                     }
371: 
372:                     // Find max height along v
373:                     let mut quad_h = 1;
374:                     'expand_h: while v + quad_h < h_slice {
375:                         for du in 0..quad_w {
376:                             if visited[u + du][v + quad_h] {
377:                                 break 'expand_h;
378:                             }
379:                             if let Some(next) = get_face(u + du, v + quad_h) {
380:                                 if next != key {
381:                                     break 'expand_h;
382:                                 }
383:                             } else {
384:                                 break 'expand_h;
385:                             }
386:                         }
387:                         quad_h += 1;
388:                     }
389: 
390:                     // Mark matched area as visited
391:                     for dv in 0..quad_h {
392:                         for du in 0..quad_w {
393:                             visited[u + du][v + dv] = true;
394:                         }
395:                     }
396: 
397:                     quads.push((u, v, quad_w, quad_h, key));
398:                 }
399:             }
400:         }
401:         quads
402:     }
403: }

417:         // Single isolated wall block should have 6 faces merged as 6 quads of size 1x1
418:         assert_eq!(quads.len(), 6);

450:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 1, 3);

454:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(1.0);
455:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid_with_padding(&grid, 1);
456:         assert!(
457:             !quads.iter().any(|q| q.dir == FaceDirection::East),
````
