 12:     /// Converts a dense VoxelGrid into an SVO of the specified depth.
 13:     pub fn execute(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, depth: u32, world_size: f32) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
 14:         let mut nodes = Vec::new();
 15:         let size = 1 << depth;
 16: 
 17:         // Recursive build from root
 18:         let root_node = self.build_recursive(grid, &mut nodes, 0, 0, 0, size, depth);
 19: 
 20:         // Push the root node to the end of the nodes array
 21:         let root_idx = nodes.len();
 22:         nodes.push(root_node);
 23: 
 24:         SparseVoxelOctree {
 25:             root: root_idx,
 26:             nodes,
 27:             depth,
 28:             world_size,
 29:         }
 30:     }
 31: 
 32:     fn build_recursive(
 33:         &self,
 34:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
 35:         nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
 36:         x: u32,
 37:         y: u32,
 38:         z: u32,
 39:         size: u32,
 40:         depth: u32,
 41:     ) -> SvoNode {
 42:         if depth == 0 {
 43:             let (v_type, color, ll, fo) = self.get_voxel_attrs(grid, x, y, z);
 44:             return SvoNode::Leaf {
 45:                 voxel_type: v_type,
 46:                 color,
 47:                 light_rgb: ll,
 48:                 face_occlusion: fo,
 49:             };
 50:         }
 51: 
 52:         let child_size = size / 2;
 53:         let mut children = [SvoNode::Leaf {
 54:             voxel_type: 0,
 55:             color: 0,
 56:             light_rgb: [0; 3],
 57:             face_occlusion: 0,
 58:         }; 8];
 59: 
 60:         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
 61:             let dx = (octant_idx & 1) * child_size;
 62:             let dy = ((octant_idx >> 1) & 1) * child_size;
 63:             let dz = ((octant_idx >> 2) & 1) * child_size;
 64: 
 65:             children[octant_idx as usize] =
 66:                 self.build_recursive(grid, nodes, x + dx, y + dy, z + dz, child_size, depth - 1);
 67:         }
 68: 
 69:         // Check if all 8 children are uniform leaves
 70:         let mut uniform = true;
 71:         let mut first_val = None;
 72:         for child in &children {
 73:             match child {
 74:                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
 75:                     uniform = false;
 76:                     break;
 77:                 }
 78:                 SvoNode::Leaf {
 79:                     voxel_type,
 80:                     color,
 81:                     light_rgb,
 82:                     face_occlusion,
 83:                 } => {
 84:                     if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
 85:                         if vt != *voxel_type
 86:                             || col != *color
 87:                             || ll != *light_rgb
 88:                             || fo != *face_occlusion
 89:                         {
 90:                             uniform = false;
 91:                             break;
 92:                         }
 93:                     } else {
 94:                         first_val = Some((*voxel_type, *color, *light_rgb, *face_occlusion));
 95:                     }
 96:                 }
 97:             }
 98:         }
 99: 
100:         if uniform {
101:             if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
102:                 return SvoNode::Leaf {
103:                     voxel_type: vt,
104:                     color: col,
105:                     light_rgb: ll,
106:                     face_occlusion: fo,
107:                 };
108:             }
109:         }
110: 
111:         // Push 8 children contiguously to arena
112:         let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
113:         let mut child_mask = 0;
114: 
115:         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
116:             let child = children[octant_idx as usize];
117:             match child {
118:                 SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
119:                     if voxel_type != 0 {
120:                         child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
121:                     }
122:                 }
123:                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
124:                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
125:                 }
126:             }
127:             nodes.push(child);
128:         }
129: 
130:         SvoNode::Internal {
131:             child_base_index,
132:             child_mask,
133:         }
134:     }
135: 
136:     fn get_voxel_attrs(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
137:         if x >= grid.width() as u32 || y >= grid.height() as u32 || z >= grid.depth() as u32 {
138:             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0); // Out of bounds is air
139:         }
140: 
141:         let v_id = grid.get(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
142:         if v_id == VOXEL_AIR {
143:             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
144:         }
145: 
146:         let ll = grid.get_light_rgb(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
147:         let fo = grid.get_face_occlusion(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
148:         let base_color = MATERIAL_COLORS
149:             .get(v_id as usize)
150:             .copied()
151:             .unwrap_or(0x000000);
152: 
153:         (v_id, base_color, ll, fo)
154:     }
155: }
156: 
157: #[cfg(test)]
158: mod tests {
159:     use super::*;
160:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
161: 
162:     #[test]
163:     fn test_empty_grid_collapses_to_single_root_leaf() {
164:         let grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
165:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
166:         let svo = builder.execute(&grid, 2, 4.0);
167: 
168:         // An entirely empty grid should collapse into a single root node (Leaf containing air)
169:         assert_eq!(svo.nodes.len(), 1);
170:         match svo.nodes[svo.root] {
171:             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => assert_eq!(voxel_type, 0),
172:             _ => panic!("Expected root to be a collapsed leaf node"),
173:         }
174:     }
175: 
176:     #[test]
177:     fn test_single_voxel_splits_octree() {
178:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
179:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL); // Set wall at origin
180: 
181:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
182:         let svo = builder.execute(&grid, 2, 4.0); // depth 2
183: 
184:         // Since there is a single wall voxel, the tree must split and cannot be collapsed completely
185:         assert!(svo.nodes.len() > 1);
186: 
187:         // The root should be an internal node
188:         match svo.nodes[svo.root] {
189:             SvoNode::Internal { child_mask, .. } => {
190:                 assert!(child_mask > 0);
191:             }
192:             _ => panic!("Expected root to be an internal parent node"),
193:         }
194: 
195:         // Let's verify we can query the wall voxel at (0,0,0)
196:         let val = svo.get(0, 0, 0);
197:         assert!(val.is_some());
198:         let (v_type, color, _, _) = val.unwrap();
199:         assert_eq!(v_type, VOXEL_WALL);
200:         assert_eq!(color, 0xddcc66);
201:     }
202: }

  1: //! Exact ray/box math, diagnostic DDA, and optional empty-leaf stepping.
  2: 
  3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
  4: const float TRACE_INFINITY = 1e30;
  5: const float TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON = 1e-7;
  6: 
  7: struct RayBoxHit {
  8:     bool hit;
  9:     float entry;
 10:     float exit;
 11:     vec3 entryNormal;
 12: };
 13: 
 14: struct ChunkInterval {
 15:     int chunkIndex;
 16:     float entry;
 17:     float exit;
 18:     vec3 entryNormal;
 19: };
 20: 
 21: struct VoxelHit {
 22:     bool hit;
 23:     float distance;
 24:     vec3 normal;
 25:     uint material;
 26:     uint color;
 27:     uint lightWord;
 28: };
 29: 
 30: float inverseDirection(float direction) {
 31:     if (abs(direction) < 1e-20) {
 32:         return direction < 0.0 ? -TRACE_INFINITY : TRACE_INFINITY;
 33:     }
 34:     return 1.0 / direction;
 35: }
 36: 
 37: float distanceTieTolerance(float distance) {
 38:     return max(abs(distance) * 1e-6, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
 39: }
 40: 
 41: float traversalSampleBias(float voxelSize) {
 42:     // This moves classification points off an exactly shared plane; it must
 43:     // remain smaller than nearby, genuinely distinct boundary crossings.
 44:     // At the 0.2 m reference grid, 1e-4 skipped a 13 micrometre
 45:     // interval between a wall and ceiling and changed the reported face.
 46:     return max(voxelSize * 1e-5, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
 47: }
 48: 
 49: RayBoxHit intersectBox(vec3 rayOrigin, vec3 rayDirection, vec3 boundsMin, vec3 boundsMax) {
 50:     // Parallel axes are handled explicitly so a boundary value never forms
 51:     // the undefined product 0 * infinity.
 52:     if ((abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.x < boundsMin.x || rayOrigin.x > boundsMax.x))
 53:         || (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.y < boundsMin.y || rayOrigin.y > boundsMax.y))
 54:         || (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.z < boundsMin.z || rayOrigin.z > boundsMax.z))) {
 55:         return RayBoxHit(false, 0.0, 0.0, vec3(0.0));
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     vec3 inverseRay = vec3(
 59:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.x),
 60:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.y),
 61:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.z)
 62:     );
 63:     vec3 first = (boundsMin - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
 64:     vec3 second = (boundsMax - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
 65:     vec3 nearTimes = min(first, second);
 66:     vec3 farTimes = max(first, second);
 67:     if (abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.x = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.x = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 68:     if (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.y = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.y = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 69:     if (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.z = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.z = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 70: 
 71:     float entry = max(nearTimes.x, max(nearTimes.y, nearTimes.z));
 72:     float exit = min(farTimes.x, min(farTimes.y, farTimes.z));
 73:     if (entry > exit || exit < 0.0) {
 74:         return RayBoxHit(false, entry, exit, vec3(0.0));
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     vec3 normal;
 78:     if (entry <= 0.0) {
 79:         vec3 absoluteRay = abs(rayDirection);
 80:         if (absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.y && absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(-sign(rayDirection.x), 0.0, 0.0);
 81:         else if (absoluteRay.y >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(0.0, -sign(rayDirection.y), 0.0);
 82:         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -sign(rayDirection.z));
 83:     } else if (nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.y && nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.z) {
 84:         normal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
 85:     } else if (nearTimes.y >= nearTimes.z) {
 86:         normal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
 87:     } else {
 88:         normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
 89:     }
 90:     return RayBoxHit(true, max(entry, 0.0), exit, normal);
 91: }
 92: 
 93: float exitDistanceFromBox(
 94:     vec3 rayOrigin,
 95:     vec3 rayDirection,
 96:     vec3 boundsMin,
 97:     vec3 boundsMax,
 98:     out vec3 nextNormal
 99: ) {
100:     vec3 exitTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
101:     if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.x = ((rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? boundsMax.x : boundsMin.x) - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
102:     if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.y = ((rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? boundsMax.y : boundsMin.y) - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
103:     if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.z = ((rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? boundsMax.z : boundsMin.z) - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
104: 
105:     float nearest = min(exitTimes.x, min(exitTimes.y, exitTimes.z));
106:     // Traversal bias and tie tolerance solve different problems. The former
107:     // moves a sample into the next cell; using that comparatively large value
108:     // here incorrectly merges distinct, very close wall/ceiling crossings.
109:     float tolerance = distanceTieTolerance(nearest);
110:     // Use the same tolerant X/Y/Z precedence as finest-cell DDA. Without
111:     // this, a mathematically tied edge ray can acquire a different face
112:     // normal solely because one path jumped across a larger empty leaf.
113:     if (abs(exitTimes.x - nearest) <= tolerance) {
114:         nextNormal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
115:         return nearest;
116:     }
117:     if (abs(exitTimes.y - nearest) <= tolerance) {
118:         nextNormal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
119:         return nearest;
120:     }
121:     nextNormal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
122:     return nearest;
123: }
124: 
125: VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
126:     vec3 rayOrigin,
127:     vec3 rayDirection,
128:     int rootIndex,
129:     float worldSize,
130:     float voxelSize,
131:     int svoDepth,
132:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
133: );
134: 
135: VoxelHit traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
136:     vec3 rayOrigin,
137:     vec3 rayDirection,
138:     int rootIndex,
139:     float worldSize,
140:     float voxelSize,
141:     int svoDepth,
142:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
143: ) {
144:     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
145:     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
146:     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
147:     float refinementEntry = chunkBox.entry;
148:     vec3 refinementEntryNormal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
149: 
150:     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
151:         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
152:         vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
153:         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
154:         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
155:             // The coarse walk proves emptiness only. Resolve the final
156:             // voxel-scale crossing with the diagnostic algorithm so both
157:             // policies produce one canonical distance, material, and normal.
158:             RayBoxHit refinementBox = RayBoxHit(
159:                 true, refinementEntry, chunkBox.exit, refinementEntryNormal
160:             );
161:             return traceChunkDda(
162:                 rayOrigin,
163:                 rayDirection,
164:                 rootIndex,
165:                 worldSize,
166:                 voxelSize,
167:                 svoDepth,
168:                 refinementBox
169:             );
170:         }
171: 
172:         vec3 crossedNormal;
173:         float nextDistance = exitDistanceFromBox(
174:             rayOrigin, rayDirection, leaf.boundsMin, leaf.boundsMax, crossedNormal
175:         );
176:         if (nextDistance <= distance + sampleBias * 0.25) {
177:             nextDistance = distance + sampleBias;
178:         }
179:         // A normalized ray moves at most one voxel per axis over this short
180:         // interval. Retaining it lets the exact resolver reconstruct every
181:         // potentially competing face without replaying the skipped octant.
182:         refinementEntry = max(distance, nextDistance - voxelSize);
183:         refinementEntryNormal = normal;
184:         distance = nextDistance;
185:         normal = crossedNormal;
186:     }
187:     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
188: }
189: 
190: VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
191:     vec3 rayOrigin,
192:     vec3 rayDirection,
193:     int rootIndex,
194:     float worldSize,
195:     float voxelSize,
196:     int svoDepth,
197:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
198: ) {
199:     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
200:     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
201:     vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
202:     vec3 cell = floor(samplePoint / voxelSize);
203:     vec3 directionStep = sign(rayDirection);
204:     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
205: 
206:     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
207:         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
208:         samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
209:         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
210:         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
211:             return VoxelHit(true, distance, normal, leaf.material, leaf.color, leaf.lightWord);
212:         }
213: 
214:         // Recompute boundary times from the canonical integer cell each step.
215:         // Repeated `nextTime += deltaTime` accumulates enough rounding error
216:         // to reverse two distinct wall/ceiling crossings near a long ray.
217:         vec3 nextBoundary = (cell + max(directionStep, vec3(0.0))) * voxelSize;
218:         vec3 nextTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
219:         if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.x = (nextBoundary.x - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
220:         if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.y = (nextBoundary.y - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
221:         if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.z = (nextBoundary.z - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
222: 
223:         float nextDistance = min(nextTimes.x, min(nextTimes.y, nextTimes.z));
224:         if (nextDistance > chunkBox.exit) break;
225:         // Step every tied axis so a ray through an edge/corner cannot stall.
226:         // This is a floating-point equality tolerance, not the sampling bias.
227:         // Keeping them separate preserves the mathematically nearer face when
228:         // two boundaries are close but not actually coincident.
229:         float tieEpsilon = distanceTieTolerance(nextDistance);
230:         bool crossX = abs(nextTimes.x - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
231:         bool crossY = abs(nextTimes.y - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
232:         bool crossZ = abs(nextTimes.z - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
233:         if (crossX) cell.x += directionStep.x;
234:         if (crossY) cell.y += directionStep.y;
235:         if (crossZ) cell.z += directionStep.z;
236:         if (crossX) normal = vec3(-directionStep.x, 0.0, 0.0);
237:         else if (crossY) normal = vec3(0.0, -directionStep.y, 0.0);
238:         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -directionStep.z);
239:         distance = nextDistance;
240:     }
241:     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
242: }
243: 
244: VoxelHit traceChunk(
245:     vec3 rayOrigin,
246:     vec3 rayDirection,
247:     int rootIndex,
248:     float worldSize,
249:     float voxelSize,
250:     int svoDepth,
251:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
252: ) {
253:     if (uEmptySpaceSkipEnabled == 1) {
254:         return traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
255:             rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
256:         );
257:     }
258:     return traceChunkDda(
259:         rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
260:     );
261: }

  1: //! Canvas-2D blit driver for the CPU splatting renderer.
  2: //!
  3: //! All rendering logic lives in the platform-free
  4: //! `adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer`; this wrapper's only job is
  5: //! to copy the finished RGBA framebuffer into the canvas via `ImageData` —
  6: //! no WebGL context is created at all.
  7: 
  8: use wasm_bindgen::{Clamped, JsCast, JsValue};
  9: use web_sys::{CanvasRenderingContext2d, HtmlCanvasElement, ImageData};
 10: 
 11: use crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer;
 12: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
 13: 
 14: pub struct CpuCanvasRenderer {
 15:     rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer,
 16:     ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2d,
 17:     settings: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings,
 18:     /// Most recent synchronous CPU stages, measured independently so the
 19:     /// HUD can distinguish renderer cost from Canvas-2D presentation cost.
 20:     rasterizer_ms: f64,
 21:     blit_ms: f64,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl CpuCanvasRenderer {
 25:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 26:         let ctx = canvas
 27:             .get_context("2d")?
 28:             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no 2d context available"))?
 29:             .dyn_into::<CanvasRenderingContext2d>()?;
 30:         let settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
 31:         Ok(Self {
 32:             rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer::new(canvas.width() as usize, canvas.height() as usize),
 33:             ctx,
 34:             settings,
 35:             rasterizer_ms: 0.0,
 36:             blit_ms: 0.0,
 37:         })
 38:     }
 39: 
 40:     pub fn resize(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
 41:         // The browser composition root already applies the validated CPU
 42:         // resolution factor to the canvas. Matching it exactly is essential:
 43:         // `put_image_data` does not scale a smaller image and would otherwise
 44:         // leave most of the canvas stale or black.
 45:         self.rasterizer
 46:             .resize(width.max(1) as usize, height.max(1) as usize);
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     pub fn telemetry_string(&self) -> String {
 50:         let stats = self.rasterizer.telemetry();
 51:         format!(
 52:             "CPU:{:.1}+{:.1}ms V:{}/{}{} (D:{})/S:{}/P:{}K/{}K{}{}",
 53:             self.rasterizer_ms,
 54:             self.blit_ms,
 55:             stats.visited_nodes,
 56:             stats.node_visit_limit,
 57:             if stats.node_budget_limited { "N!" } else { "" },
 58:             stats.max_virtual_depth,
 59:             stats.splat_count,
 60:             stats.pixel_writes / 1000,
 61:             stats.pixel_write_limit / 1000,
 62:             if stats.pixel_budget_limited { "P!" } else { "" },
 63:             if stats.budget_exhausted { "!" } else { "" }
 64:         )
 65:     }
 66: }
 67: 
 68: impl RendererPort for CpuCanvasRenderer {
 69:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
 70:         self.rasterizer.upload_atlas(texels);
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
 74:         self.rasterizer.upload_atlas_rows(first_row, texels)
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
 78:         Some(self.telemetry_string())
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
 82:         self.settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
 83:         self.settings.fov_tan = crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
 84:         // The optimization switchboard is sampled once per frame here; the
 85:         // platform-free rasterizer itself never reads globals.
 86:         self.settings.toggles = crate::get_render_toggles();
 87:         self.rasterizer.settings = self.settings;
 88: 
 89:         let render_start = browser_now_ms();
 90:         self.rasterizer.draw(frame, chunks);
 91:         let render_end = browser_now_ms();
 92:         let width = self.rasterizer.width() as u32;
 93:         let height = self.rasterizer.height() as u32;
 94:         let fb = self.rasterizer.framebuffer();
 95: 
 96:         if let Ok(image) = ImageData::new_with_u8_clamped_array_and_sh(Clamped(fb), width, height) {
 97:             let _ = self.ctx.put_image_data(&image, 0.0, 0.0);
 98:         }
 99:         let blit_end = browser_now_ms();
100:         self.rasterizer_ms = render_end - render_start;
101:         self.blit_ms = blit_end - render_end;
102:     }
103: }
104: 
105: fn browser_now_ms() -> f64 {
106:     web_sys::window()
107:         .and_then(|window| window.performance())
108:         .map_or(0.0, |performance| performance.now())
109: }

  16: 
  17: fn generate(ox: f32, oz: f32) -> VoxelGrid {
  18:     BackroomsLevel.generate(
  19:         Position::new(ox, oz),
  20:         42,
  21:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
  22:         &SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
  23:     )

  25: 
  26: fn is_open(grid: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, z: usize) -> bool {
  27:     grid.get(x, 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR
  28: }
  29: 
  30: /// Walkable-plane connectivity: nearly all open floor must be mutually
  31: /// reachable (walls always leave doorways, pillars never seal a region).
  32: /// We exclude a 2-voxel border to avoid edge-of-chunk artifacts where
  33: /// walls at boundaries form isolated strips that would be connected by
  34: /// the adjacent chunk at runtime.
  35: #[test]
  36: fn walkable_plane_is_connected() {
  37:     let grid = generate(0.0, 0.0);
  38:     let (w, d) = (grid.width(), grid.depth());
  39:     let margin = 2usize; // exclude edge voxels
  40: 
  41:     let open: Vec<(usize, usize)> = (margin..w - margin)
  42:         .flat_map(|x| (margin..d - margin).map(move |z| (x, z)))
  43:         .filter(|&(x, z)| is_open(&grid, x, z))
  44:         .collect();
  45:     assert!(
  46:         open.len() > (w - 2 * margin) * (d - 2 * margin) / 2,
  47:         "backrooms must be mostly open space"
  48:     );
  49: 
  50:     // BFS from the first open interior voxel.
  51:     let &(sx, sz) = open.first().expect("some open floor exists");
  52:     let mut visited = vec![false; w * d];
  53:     let mut queue = std::collections::VecDeque::from([(sx, sz)]);
  54:     visited[sx * d + sz] = true;
  55:     let mut reached = 0usize;
  56:     while let Some((x, z)) = queue.pop_front() {
  57:         reached += 1;
  58:         for (dx, dz) in [(1i64, 0i64), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)] {
  59:             let (nx, nz) = (x as i64 + dx, z as i64 + dz);
  60:             if nx < margin as i64
  61:                 || nz < margin as i64
  62:                 || nx >= (w - margin) as i64
  63:                 || nz >= (d - margin) as i64
  64:             {
  65:                 continue;
  66:             }
  67:             let (nx, nz) = (nx as usize, nz as usize);
  68:             if !visited[nx * d + nz] && is_open(&grid, nx, nz) {
  69:                 visited[nx * d + nz] = true;
  70:                 queue.push_back((nx, nz));
  71:             }
  72:         }
  73:     }
  74:     let ratio = reached as f32 / open.len() as f32;
  75:     assert!(
  76:         ratio > 0.95,
  77:         "only {:.0}% of open floor is reachable from spawn",
  78:         ratio * 100.0
  79:     );
  80: }

  95:     for z in 0..a.depth() {
  96:         for (grid, lx, gx) in [(&a, w - 1, w - 1), (&b, 0usize, w)] {
  97:             let wx = (gx as f32 + 0.5) * config.voxel_scale;
  98:             let wz = (z as f32 + 0.5) * config.voxel_scale;
  99:             let key = (
 100:                 crate::use_cases::region_plan::region_index(wx),

 110:             let got_solid = grid.get(lx, 1, z) == VOXEL_WALL;

 112:             // the walkable layer, so it counts as expected solid here.

 115:             assert_eq!(
 116:                 got_solid, expect_solid,
 117:                 "column mismatch at world x={gx} z={z}"
 118:             );
 119:         }

 124: fn recursive_level_zero_is_independent_of_output_partition() {

 133:         0xDEAD_BEEF_1234_5678,
 134:         1,

 136:         Axis2::X,

 144:     let mut large_config = small_config;

 146: 
 147:     let large = BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 148:         Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
 149:         42,
 150:         large_config,
 151:         &noise,
 152:         &reality,

 154:     let chunks = [
 155:         BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 156:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),

 160:             &reality,

 163:             Position::new(10.0, 0.0),

 165:             small_config,

 185:     let tile = chunks[0].width();
 186:     assert_eq!(large.width(), tile * 2);
 187:     assert_eq!(large.depth(), tile * 2);
 188:     for z in 0..large.depth() {
 189:         for x in 0..large.width() {
 190:             let tile_index = usize::from(x >= tile) + 2 * usize::from(z >= tile);
 191:             let local_x = x % tile;
 192:             let local_z = z % tile;
 193:             for y in 0..large.height() {

 195:                     large.get(x, y, z),

 198:                 );

 204: /// The plan is authoritative: corridor centerlines must be carved open
 205: /// in the voxelized chunks they cross.
 206: #[test]
 207: fn corridors_from_the_plan_are_carved_open() {
 208:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 209:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 210:     let plans =
 211:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 212:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 213:     let spine = &plan.corridors[0];
 214: 
 215:     let mut checked = 0;
 216:     for seg in spine.path.windows(2) {
 217:         let (p0, p1) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 218:         let steps = 8;
 219:         for k in 1..steps {
 220:             let t = k as f32 / steps as f32;
 221:             let (wx, wz) = (p0.x + (p1.x - p0.x) * t, p0.z + (p1.z - p0.z) * t);
 222:             // Stay inside region (0,0) and off chunk edges.
 223:             if !(1.0..79.0).contains(&wx) || !(1.0..79.0).contains(&wz) {
 224:                 continue;
 225:             }
 226:             let (cx, cz) = ((wx / 10.0).floor() * 10.0, (wz / 10.0).floor() * 10.0);
 227:             let grid = generate(cx, cz);
 228:             let (lx, lz) = (
 229:                 ((wx - cx) / config.voxel_scale) as usize,
 230:                 ((wz - cz) / config.voxel_scale) as usize,
 231:             );
 232:             assert!(
 233:                 is_open(&grid, lx.min(grid.width() - 1), lz.min(grid.depth() - 1)),
 234:                 "main corridor blocked at world ({wx:.1}, {wz:.1})"
 235:             );
 236:             checked += 1;
 237:         }
 238:     }
 239:     assert!(checked > 5, "spine barely sampled ({checked} points)");
 240: }

 291: /// Assemblies voxelize as walled rooms whose planned entrance is open
 292: /// (with a lintel when the designer's threshold language wants one).
 293: #[test]
 294: fn assemblies_have_walls_and_open_entrances() {
 295:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 296:     let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 297:     config.anomalies.frequency = 0.0;
 298:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 299:     let plans =
 300:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 301:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 302:     assert!(!plan.assemblies.is_empty());
 303: 
 304:     for a in &plan.assemblies {
 305:         let e = &a.entrances[0];
 306:         // The entrance column itself: open (possibly under a lintel).
 307:         let door =
 308:             BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, e.center.x, e.center.z);
 309:         assert!(!door.solid, "assembly {} door is walled shut", a.id);
 310:         // Somewhere along the same front wall, clear of the door span,
 311:         // there must be solid wall. Probe the middle of the wall band
 312:         // (the entrance center sits exactly on the footprint boundary,
 313:         // where containment is ambiguous).
 314:         let b = a.footprint.bounds();
 315:         let band = |c: f32, lo: f32, hi: f32| {
 316:             if (c - lo).abs() < (c - hi).abs() {
 317:                 lo - PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 318:             } else {
 319:                 hi + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 320:             }
 321:         };
 322:         let (lo, hi, door_along) = if e.through_x_wall {
 323:             (b.0, b.2, e.center.x)
 324:         } else {
 325:             (b.1, b.3, e.center.z)
 326:         };
 327:         let mut solid_found = false;
 328:         let mut along = lo + 0.3;
 329:         while along < hi - 0.2 {
 330:             if (along - door_along).abs() > e.width * 0.5 + 0.4 {
 331:                 let (wx, wz) = if e.through_x_wall {
 332:                     (along, band(e.center.z, b.1, b.3))
 333:                 } else {
 334:                     (band(e.center.x, b.0, b.2), along)
 335:                 };
 336:                 if BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz).solid {
 337:                     solid_found = true;
 338:                     break;
 339:                 }
 340:             }
 341:             along += 0.2;
 342:         }
 343:         assert!(
 344:             solid_found,
 345:             "assembly {} has no solid front wall anywhere",
 346:             a.id
 347:         );
 348:     }
 349: }

 351: /// An abandoned expansion is a dark shell: it keeps its walls but none of
 352: /// its fixtures are lit.
 353: #[test]
 354: fn abandoned_expansions_are_unlit() {
 355:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 356:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 357:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 358:     let mut found = false;
 359:     for rx in -3i64..3 {
 360:         for rz in -3i64..3 {
 361:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 362:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * 80.0, rz as f32 * 80.0),
 363:                 1.0,
 364:                 42,
 365:                 &config,
 366:                 &noise,
 367:             );
 368:             let plan = &plans[0].1;
 369:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
 370:                 if !a.corruption.abandoned {
 371:                     continue;
 372:                 }
 373:                 found = true;
 374:                 let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = a.footprint.bounds();
 375:                 // No interior column may carry a lit fixture.
 376:                 let mut probe_z = z0 + 0.6;
 377:                 while probe_z < z1 - 0.4 {
 378:                     let mut probe_x = x0 + 0.6;
 379:                     while probe_x < x1 - 0.4 {
 380:                         // A corridor clipping the footprint may still run
 381:                         // its own lit strip through the shell — that is
 382:                         // canon ("unreachable but still lit"). Only the
 383:                         // room's fixtures must be dark.
 384:                         let in_corridor = plan
 385:                             .corridors
 386:                             .iter()
 387:                             .any(|s| s.distance(probe_x, probe_z) <= s.width * 0.5);
 388:                         if !in_corridor {
 389:                             let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(
 390:                                 plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, probe_x, probe_z,
 391:                             );
 392:                             assert!(!c.light, "abandoned assembly {} is lit", a.id);
 393:                         }
 394:                         probe_x += 0.8;
 395:                     }
 396:                     probe_z += 0.8;
 397:                 }
 398:             }
 399:         }
 400:     }
 401:     assert!(found, "no abandoned expansion within 36 regions");
 402: }

 404: /// A planned stairwell samples through the full column pipeline as a
 405: /// walkable flight: flat at the door, rising monotonically along the
 406: /// walk axis, reaching its landing with headroom intact.
 407: #[test]
 408: fn stairwells_sample_as_rising_flights() {
 409:     use crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry;
 410:     use crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region;
 411:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 412:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 413:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 414: 
 415:     let mut checked = 0usize;
 416:     for rz in -8i64..=8 {
 417:         for rx in -8i64..=8 {
 418:             let Some(link) = vertical_link_for_region(42, &noise, rx, rz) else {
 419:                 continue;
 420:             };
 421:             if !link_wants_geometry(&link) {
 422:                 continue;
 423:             }
 424:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 425:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 426:                 1.0,
 427:                 42,
 428:                 &config,
 429:                 &noise,
 430:             );
 431:             let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (rx, rz)).unwrap().1;
 432:             let Some(stair) = plan
 433:                 .assemblies
 434:                 .iter()
 435:                 .find(|a| a.program == SpaceProgram::Stair)
 436:             else {
 437:                 continue;
 438:             };
 439:             let door = stair.entrances[0].center;
 440:             let b = stair.footprint.bounds();
 441:             let inward = if (door.z - b.1).abs() < (door.z - b.3).abs() {
 442:                 1.0
 443:             } else {
 444:                 -1.0
 445:             };
 446: 
 447:             let at_door =
 448:                 BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, door.x, door.z);
 449:             assert!(!at_door.solid, "stair door is walled shut");
 450:             assert_eq!(at_door.floor_units, 0.0, "stair door is not flat");
 451: 
 452:             let mut previous = 0.0f32;
 453:             let mut peak = 0.0f32;
 454:             let mut depth = 0.7;
 455:             while depth < (b.3 - b.1) - 0.6 {
 456:                 let wz = door.z + inward * depth;
 457:                 let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, door.x, wz);
 458:                 if !c.solid {
 459:                     assert!(
 460:                         c.floor_units >= previous - 1e-6,
 461:                         "flight descends inside stair at region ({rx},{rz})"
 462:                     );
 463:                     assert!(
 464:                         c.ceiling_units - c.floor_units >= 2.2 - 1e-6,
 465:                         "flight headroom pinched at region ({rx},{rz})"
 466:                     );
 467:                     previous = c.floor_units;
 468:                     peak = peak.max(c.floor_units);
 469:                 }
 470:                 depth += 0.2;
 471:             }
 472:             assert!(
 473:                 peak >= 1.6 - 1e-6,
 474:                 "flight in ({rx},{rz}) peaked at {peak} u"
 475:             );
 476:             checked += 1;
 477:         }
 478:     }
 479:     assert!(checked >= 3, "only {checked} stairwells sampled");
 480: }

 482: /// The baseline is broad regular dropped ceiling, with enough expansive
 483: /// and vaulted territory to prevent Level 0 from reading as a low maze.
 484: #[test]
 485: fn ceilings_are_vast_and_varied() {
 486:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 487:     let mut counts = [0usize; 4];
 488:     let mut lowest = f32::MAX;
 489:     let mut tallest = 0.0f32;
 490:     for z in (-600..=600).step_by(8) {
 491:         for x in (-600..=600).step_by(8) {
 492:             let (wx, wz) = (x as f32 + 0.5, z as f32 + 0.5);
 493:             let band = BackroomsLevel::fabric_ceiling_band(&noise, 42, wx, wz);
 494:             let ceiling = BackroomsLevel::fabric_ceiling_height(&noise, 42, wx, wz, band);
 495:             let index = match band {
 496:                 FabricCeilingBand::Compression => 0,
 497:                 FabricCeilingBand::Regular => 1,
 498:                 FabricCeilingBand::Expanse => 2,
 499:                 FabricCeilingBand::Vault => 3,
 500:             };
 501:             counts[index] += 1;
 502:             lowest = lowest.min(ceiling);
 503:             tallest = tallest.max(ceiling);
 504:         }
 505:     }
 506:     let total = counts.iter().sum::<usize>() as f32;
 507:     let ratio = |index| counts[index] as f32 / total;
 508:     // The labyrinth fabric is the default; open volumes punctuate it.
 509:     assert!(
 510:         (0.60..=0.85).contains(&ratio(1)),
 511:         "ceiling territories: compression {:.1}%, regular {:.1}%, expanse {:.1}%, vault {:.1}%",
 512:         ratio(0) * 100.0,
 513:         ratio(1) * 100.0,
 514:         ratio(2) * 100.0,
 515:         ratio(3) * 100.0
 516:     );
 517:     assert!(
 518:         (0.10..=0.28).contains(&ratio(2)),
 519:         "open expanse territory was {:.1}%",
 520:         ratio(2) * 100.0
 521:     );
 522:     assert!(
 523:         (0.03..=0.15).contains(&ratio(3)),
 524:         "vault territory was {:.1}%",
 525:         ratio(3) * 100.0
 526:     );
 527:     assert!(
 528:         (0.01..=0.10).contains(&ratio(0)),
 529:         "compression territory was {:.1}%",
 530:         ratio(0) * 100.0
 531:     );
 532:     assert!(
 533:         lowest <= 2.8 && tallest >= 4.5,
 534:         "ceiling range was only {lowest:.1}--{tallest:.1} u"
 535:     );
 536: }

 577: /// The generation knobs actually steer the output: zeroing pillars and
 578: /// walls empties the world of solids; cranking them fills it back up.
 579: #[test]
 580: fn tuning_knobs_control_density() {
 581:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 582:     // Aggregate over chunks in different fabric regimes (walled rooms
 583:     // and open expanses) so both knobs have something to steer.
 584:     let count_solids = |tuning: LevelTuning| -> usize {
 585:         let mut n = 0;
 586:         for (ox, oz) in [(10.0, 10.0), (30.0, 10.0), (50.0, 30.0), (10.0, 50.0)] {
 587:             let grid = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 588:                 Position::new(ox, oz),
 589:                 42,
 590:                 GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_tuning(tuning),
 591:                 &noise,
 592:             );
 593:             for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 594:                 for x in 0..grid.width() {
 595:                     if grid.get(x, 1, z) != VOXEL_AIR {
 596:                         n += 1;
 597:                     }
 598:                 }
 599:             }
 600:         }
 601:         n
 602:     };
 603: 
 604:     // Provisions (bottles, doors) are content, not architecture: zero them
 605:     // so the knob comparison sees only pillar/wall mass.
 606:     let no_provisions = LevelTuning {
 607:         almond_water: 0.0,
 608:         rations: 0.0,
 609:         level_doors: 0.0,
 610:         ..Default::default()
 611:     };
 612:     let none = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 613:         pillars: 0.0,
 614:         walls: 0.0,
 615:         ..no_provisions
 616:     });
 617:     let sparse = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 618:         pillars: 0.3,
 619:         walls: 0.3,
 620:         ..no_provisions
 621:     });
 622:     let default = count_solids(no_provisions);
 623:     let dense = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 624:         pillars: 2.0,
 625:         walls: 2.0,
 626:         ..no_provisions
 627:     });
 628: 
 629:     assert_eq!(none, 0, "pillars=0 walls=0 must produce an empty plane");
 630:     assert!(
 631:         sparse < default,
 632:         "sparse ({sparse}) must be < default ({default})"
 633:     );
 634:     assert!(
 635:         default < dense,
 636:         "default ({default}) must be < dense ({dense})"
 637:     );
 638: }

 667: /// Every LOD of a chunk must voxelize the same plan: coarse walls stay
 668: /// within one fine voxel of fine walls (the streaming engine swaps LODs
 669: /// of a chunk in place, so they must be faithful proxies).
 670: #[test]
 671: fn lods_of_the_same_chunk_correspond() {
 672:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 673:     let fine = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 674:         Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 675:         42,
 676:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
 677:         &noise,
 678:     );
 679:     let coarse = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 680:         Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 681:         42,
 682:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec().at_lod(1),
 683:         &noise,
 684:     );
 685:     let solid = |g: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, z: usize| g.get(x, 1, z) == VOXEL_WALL;
 686:     let (mut matches, mut total) = (0usize, 0usize);
 687:     for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
 688:         for x in 0..coarse.width() {
 689:             if !solid(&coarse, x, z) {
 690:                 continue;
 691:             }
 692:             total += 1;
 693:             let mut near = false;
 694:             for dz in -1i32..=2 {
 695:                 for dx in -1i32..=2 {
 696:                     let (fx, fz) = (x as i32 * 2 + dx, z as i32 * 2 + dz);
 697:                     if fx >= 0
 698:                         && fz >= 0
 699:                         && (fx as usize) < fine.width()
 700:                         && (fz as usize) < fine.depth()
 701:                         && solid(&fine, fx as usize, fz as usize)
 702:                     {
 703:                         near = true;
 704:                     }
 705:                 }
 706:             }
 707:             if near {
 708:                 matches += 1;
 709:             }
 710:         }
 711:     }
 712:     assert!(total > 0, "coarse chunk has no walls at all");
 713:     assert!(
 714:         matches * 10 >= total * 9,
 715:         "coarse walls stray from fine walls: {matches}/{total}"
 716:     );
 717: }

 719: /// The player spawns *on the main corridor*: open floor along the
 720: /// centerline, a lit fixture within a light-strip period, and — for the
 721: /// readable opening sequence — solid edge walls on both sides.
 722: #[test]
 723: fn spawn_is_a_readable_walled_corridor() {
 724:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 725:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 726:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 727:     let sp = crate::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(42);
 728: 
 729:     let plans =
 730:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 731:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 732:     let spine = &plan.corridors[0];
 733:     assert!(
 734:         spine.distance(sp.x, sp.z) < 0.3,
 735:         "spawn ({}, {}) is not on the main corridor centerline",
 736:         sp.x,
 737:         sp.z
 738:     );
 739: 
 740:     // The corridor around spawn is open along the centerline, lit, and
 741:     // predominantly walled on both sides. Framed entrances and branch
 742:     // tees may pierce the run, but the edge must *read* as a wall — no
 743:     // dissolution into open fabric inside the readable radius.
 744:     let half = spine.width * 0.5;
 745:     let mut lit = false;
 746:     let mut solid_edges = [0usize; 2];
 747:     const STEPS: usize = 16;
 748:     for step in 0..STEPS {
 749:         let wx = sp.x + step as f32;
 750:         let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, sp.z);
 751:         assert!(!c.solid, "main corridor blocked at ({wx}, {})", sp.z);
 752:         lit |= c.light;
 753:         for (i, side) in [-1.0, 1.0f32].iter().enumerate() {
 754:             let wz = sp.z + side * (half + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5);
 755:             if BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz).solid {
 756:                 solid_edges[i] += 1;
 757:             }
 758:         }
 759:     }
 760:     assert!(lit, "no lit fixture along the first {STEPS} u of corridor");
 761:     for (i, solid) in solid_edges.iter().enumerate() {
 762:         assert!(
 763:             solid * 10 >= STEPS * 6,
 764:             "start corridor side {i} is mostly open ({solid}/{STEPS}): \
 765:              the opening sequence must read as a walled corridor"
 766:         );
 767:     }
 768: }
 769: 
 770: /// The fabric connectivity invariant: every warren cell opens through
 771: /// its west or its north wall (doorway, dropped wall, or an override by
 772: /// corridor/assembly/expanse), so the labyrinth is globally connected
 773: /// by induction — no chunk ever needs to see its neighbors to prove it.
 774: #[test]
 775: fn every_fabric_cell_opens_west_or_north() {
 776:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 777:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 778:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 779:     let mut cells_checked = 0usize;
 780:     for cell_x in -40i64..40 {
 781:         for cell_z in -40i64..40 {
 782:             let x0 = cell_x as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
 783:             let z0 = cell_z as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
 784:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 785:                 Position::new(x0, z0),
 786:                 FABRIC_CELL,
 787:                 42,
 788:                 &config,
 789:                 &noise,
 790:             );
 791:             let plan_for = |wx: f32, wz: f32| {
 792:                 let key = (region_index(wx), region_index(wz));
 793:                 &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == key).unwrap().1
 794:             };
 795:             // The invariant belongs to *pure* fabric. Cells clipped by a
 796:             // corridor edge or an assembly take their connectivity from
 797:             // those systems instead (tested separately), so skip them.
 798:             let (cx0, cz0) = (x0 - PLAN_WALL_T, z0 - PLAN_WALL_T);
 799:             let (cx1, cz1) = (x0 + FABRIC_CELL, z0 + FABRIC_CELL);
 800:             let clipped = plans.iter().any(|(_, p)| {
 801:                 p.corridors.iter().any(|s| {
 802:                     let m = s.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
 803:                     [
 804:                         (cx0, cz0),
 805:                         (cx1, cz0),
 806:                         (cx0, cz1),
 807:                         (cx1, cz1),
 808:                         ((cx0 + cx1) * 0.5, (cz0 + cz1) * 0.5),
 809:                     ]
 810:                     .iter()
 811:                     .any(|&(px, pz)| s.distance(px, pz) <= m + FABRIC_CELL)
 812:                 }) || p.assemblies.iter().any(|a| {
 813:                     let b = a.footprint.bounds();
 814:                     cx0 < b.2 + PLAN_WALL_T
 815:                         && b.0 - PLAN_WALL_T < cx1
 816:                         && cz0 < b.3 + PLAN_WALL_T
 817:                         && b.1 - PLAN_WALL_T < cz1
 818:                 }) || p.anomalies.iter().any(|an| {
 819:                     // Anomaly interiors own their connectivity rules
 820:                     // (entrances, skeleton lanes, arch openings) and are
 821:                     // tested by their own family invariants.
 822:                     an.footprint
 823:                         .bounds()
 824:                         .expanded(PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1)
 825:                         .intersects(WorldBounds::new(cx0, cz0, cx1, cz1))
 826:                 })
 827:             });
 828:             if clipped {
 829:                 continue;
 830:             }
 831:             let mut open = false;
 832:             let mut probe = |wx: f32, wz: f32| {
 833:                 let c =
 834:                     BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan_for(wx, wz), &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz);
 835:                 if !c.solid {
 836:                     open = true;
 837:                 }
 838:             };
 839:             // Sample along the west and north wall bands of the cell.
 840:             let mut a = PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
 841:             while a < FABRIC_CELL - PLAN_WALL_T {
 842:                 probe(x0 + 0.2, z0 + a);
 843:                 probe(x0 + a, z0 + 0.2);
 844:                 a += 0.2;
 845:             }
 846:             assert!(
 847:                 open,
 848:                 "fabric cell ({cell_x},{cell_z}) is sealed on both its \
 849:                  west and north walls"
 850:             );
 851:             cells_checked += 1;
 852:         }
 853:     }
 854:     assert!(cells_checked > 1000, "sample too small: {cells_checked}");
 855: }
 856: 
 857: /// Red identity is owned by whole rooms: some region must contain a red
 858: /// room whose fixtures voxelize as red lights, and crimson/peeled wall
 859: /// voxels may appear only inside a red-room footprint (plus its wall
 860: /// band) — the approach stain is telegraphy, never leakage into fabric.
 861: #[test]
 862: fn red_rooms_are_lit_red_but_never_built_red() {
 863:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL};
 864:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 865:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 866:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 867: 
 868:     let mut red_room_seen = false;
 869:     'search: for rx in -4i64..=4 {
 870:         for rz in -4i64..=4 {
 871:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 872:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 873:                 1.0,
 874:                 42,
 875:                 &config,
 876:                 &noise,
 877:             );
 878:             let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (rx, rz)).unwrap().1;
 879:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
 880:                 if !a.corruption.red_room {
 881:                     continue;
 882:                 }
 883:                 assert!(!a.corruption.abandoned, "a red room must be occupied");
 884:                 // Its lit fixtures plan red lights.
 885:                 let f = a.fixtures.iter().find(|f| f.lit).expect("lit fixture");
 886:                 let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, f.at.x, f.at.z);
 887:                 if c.light {
 888:                     assert!(c.red_light, "red-room fixture plans a warm light");
 889:                     red_room_seen = true;
 890:                     break 'search;
 891:                 }
 892:             }
 893:         }
 894:     }
 895:     assert!(red_room_seen, "no red room found within 81 regions");
 896: 
 897:     // Red walls stay contained: any crimson voxel must sit inside some
 898:     // red-room footprint (plus wall band), and red lights appear only as
 899:     // ceiling lights.
 900:     for (ox, oz) in [(0.0, 0.0), (30.0, 10.0), (-40.0, 70.0), (150.0, -90.0)] {
 901:         let grid = generate(ox, oz);
 902:         let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 903:         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 904:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
 905:                 for y in 0..grid.height() {
 906:                     if grid.get(x, y, z) == VOXEL_RED_WALL {
 907:                         panic!(
 908:                             "VOXEL_RED_WALL should never be voxelized at {wx}, {y}, {wz}",
 909:                             wx = ox + (x as f32 + 0.5) * scale,
 910:                             wz = oz + (z as f32 + 0.5) * scale
 911:                         );
 912:                     }
 913:                 }
 914:                 // Red lights sit at ceiling height, never at floor level.
 915:                 assert_ne!(grid.get(x, 1, z), VOXEL_RED_LIGHT);
 916:             }
 917:         }
 918:     }
 919: }

 921: fn find_macro_anomaly(kind: AnomalyKind) -> (GeneratorConfig, AnomalyInstance) {
 922:     let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 923:     config.anomalies.frequency = 4.0;
 924:     config.anomalies.pillar_expanses = (kind == AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse) as u8 as f32;
 925:     config.anomalies.blackouts = (kind == AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse) as u8 as f32;
 926:     config.anomalies.pit_lattices = (kind == AnomalyKind::PitLattice) as u8 as f32;
 927:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 928:     for rz in 3i64..24 {
 929:         for rx in 3i64..24 {
 930:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 931:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 932:                 1.0,
 933:                 42,
 934:                 &config,
 935:                 &noise,
 936:             );
 937:             if let Some(instance) = plans
 938:                 .iter()
 939:                 .flat_map(|(_, p)| &p.anomalies)
 940:                 .find(|a| a.kind == kind)
 941:             {
 942:                 return (config, instance.clone());
 943:             }
 944:         }
 945:     }
 946:     panic!("no {kind:?} fixture found");
 947: }

 949: #[test]
 950: fn pillar_epoch_changes_only_committed_wake_and_preserves_bearing_lane() {
 951:     use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyStateStamp, AxisDirection};
 952:     let (mut config, instance) = find_macro_anomaly(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
 953:     config.anomalies.remap_intensity = 4.0;
 954:     let gate = instance.gates[instance.gates.len() / 2];
 955:     let reality = RealitySnapshot::new(vec![AnomalyStateStamp::new(
 956:         instance.id,
 957:         1,
 958:         gate.plane,
 959:         gate.axis,
 960:         AxisDirection::Positive,
 961:         crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RedRoomPhase::Outside,
 962:         0,
 963:         0,
 964:     )]);
 965:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
 966:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 967:     let mut changed = 0usize;
 968:     let mut unchanged_forward = 0usize;
 969:     let mut lz = -instance.footprint.half_z + 1.0;
 970:     while lz < instance.footprint.half_z - 1.0 {
 971:         let mut lx = -instance.footprint.half_x + 1.0;
 972:         while lx < instance.footprint.half_x - 1.0 {
 973:             let p = instance.world_coords(lx, lz);
 974:             let a = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
 975:             let b = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &reality, p.x, p.z);
 976:             let in_wake =
 977:                 reality.stamps()[0].point_is_in_wake(p.x, p.z, config.anomalies.remap_distance);
 978:             if a.solid != b.solid {
 979:                 assert!(in_wake, "geometry changed ahead of the crossed gate");
 980:                 assert!(lz.abs() > instance.skeleton_half_width);
 981:                 changed += 1;
 982:             } else if !in_wake {
 983:                 unchanged_forward += 1;
 984:             }
 985:             if lz.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width {
 986:                 assert!(!a.solid && !b.solid, "bearing lane was blocked");
 987:             }
 988:             lx += 0.4;
 989:         }
 990:         lz += 0.4;
 991:     }
 992:     assert!(changed > 0, "pillar epoch produced no changed wake infill");
 993:     assert!(unchanged_forward > 100);
 994: }

1058:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();

1129:     let ring = sample_red_room(
1130:         &red,

1137:     assert!(!ring.solid, "closed red room has no traversable loop");
1138:     assert_eq!(

1184: /// Arch rooms are the stable contrast: pale walls, deep wet carpet, no
1185: /// gates, and geometry provably identical under any encounter state —
1186: /// even a fabricated stamp for their own instance id changes nothing.
1187: #[test]
1188: fn archway_rooms_are_stable_pale_anchors() {
1189:     use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, AxisDirection};
1190:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_PALE_WALL};
1191:     let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
1192:     config.anomalies.frequency = 4.0;
1193:     config.anomalies.pillar_expanses = 0.0;
1194:     config.anomalies.blackouts = 0.0;
1195:     config.anomalies.pit_lattices = 0.0;
1196:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1197:     let mut found = None;
1198:     'search: for rz in 3i64..24 {
1199:         for rx in 3i64..24 {
1200:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
1201:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
1202:                 1.0,
1203:                 42,
1204:                 &config,
1205:                 &noise,
1206:             );
1207:             if let Some(instance) = plans
1208:                 .iter()
1209:                 .flat_map(|(_, p)| &p.anomalies)
1210:                 .find(|a| a.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom)
1211:             {
1212:                 found = Some(instance.clone());
1213:                 break 'search;
1214:             }
1215:         }
1216:     }
1217:     let instance = found.expect("no archway fixture found");
1218:     assert!(instance.gates.is_empty(), "arch rooms must carry no gates");
1219:     assert!(instance.arch.is_some());
1220: 
1221:     let forged = RealitySnapshot::new(vec![AnomalyStateStamp::new(
1222:         instance.id,
1223:         7,
1224:         0.0,
1225:         Axis2::X,
1226:         AxisDirection::Positive,
1227:         crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RedRoomPhase::Outside,
1228:         0,
1229:         0,
1230:     )]);
1231:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1232:     let mut pale_seen = false;
1233:     let mut carpet_seen = false;
1234:     let mut lz = -instance.footprint.half_z + 0.2;
1235:     while lz < instance.footprint.half_z {
1236:         let mut lx = -instance.footprint.half_x + 0.2;
1237:         while lx < instance.footprint.half_x {
1238:             let p = instance.world_coords(lx, lz);
1239:             let a = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1240:             let b = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &forged, p.x, p.z);
1241:             assert_eq!(a, b, "archway geometry moved under a forged epoch");
1242:             if a.solid && a.wall_material == VOXEL_PALE_WALL {
1243:                 pale_seen = true;
1244:             }
1245:             if !a.solid && a.floor_material == VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET {
1246:                 carpet_seen = true;
1247:             }
1248:             lx += 0.4;
1249:         }
1250:         lz += 0.4;
1251:     }
1252:     assert!(pale_seen, "no pale arch wall voxelized");
1253:     assert!(carpet_seen, "no deep wet carpet voxelized");
1254: }

1256: /// Arch rooms are stable — and passable and individual. Every non-blind
1257: /// arch of a transition room is a doorway the player can walk through
1258: /// (open at standing height on both long walls), the dead-end variant keeps
1259: /// its one entrance, and profiles vary between instances so no two arcades
1260: /// present the same rhythm.
1261: #[test]
1262: fn archways_are_walkable_and_no_two_arcades_match() {
1263:     use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::ArchLayout;
1264:     let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
1265:     config.anomalies.frequency = 4.0;
1266:     config.anomalies.pillar_expanses = 0.0;
1267:     config.anomalies.blackouts = 0.0;
1268:     config.anomalies.pit_lattices = 0.0;
1269:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1270:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1271: 
1272:     let mut instances = Vec::new();
1273:     'scan: for rz in 3i64..40 {
1274:         for rx in 3i64..40 {
1275:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
1276:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
1277:                 1.0,
1278:                 42,
1279:                 &config,
1280:                 &noise,
1281:             );
1282:             for instance in plans.iter().flat_map(|(_, p)| &p.anomalies) {
1283:                 if instance.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
1284:                     && !instances.iter().any(|a: &AnomalyInstance| a.id == instance.id)
1285:                 {
1286:                     instances.push(instance.clone());
1287:                     if instances.len() >= 8 {
1288:                         break 'scan;
1289:                     }
1290:                 }
1291:             }
1292:         }
1293:     }
1294:     assert!(instances.len() >= 4, "only {} arch rooms found", instances.len());
1295: 
1296:     let mut profiles = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
1297:     let mut openings_walked = 0usize;
1298:     for instance in &instances {
1299:         let arch = instance.arch.expect("arch profile");
1300:         profiles.insert((
1301:             (arch.bay * 10.0) as i64,
1302:             (arch.opening * 10.0) as i64,
1303:             arch.blind_every,
1304:             (arch.spring_units * 10.0) as i64,
1305:             arch.layout == ArchLayout::Transition,
1306:         ));
1307:         let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
1308:         let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
1309:         match arch.layout {
1310:             ArchLayout::Transition => {
1311:                 // Every non-blind bay center on both long walls is an open,
1312:                 // walkable doorway with standing headroom.
1313:                 let mut bay_index = 0i64;
1314:                 loop {
1315:                     let center = arch.bay * (bay_index as f32 + 0.5);
1316:                     if center + arch.opening * 0.5 >= 2.0 * half_x {
1317:                         break;
1318:                     }
1319:                     let blind =
1320:                         bay_index.rem_euclid(arch.blind_every as i64) == arch.blind_every as i64 - 1;
1321:                     if !blind && center - arch.opening * 0.5 > 0.0 {
1322:                         for side in [-1.0f32, 1.0] {
1323:                             let p = instance
1324:                                 .world_coords(center - half_x, side * (half_z - 0.1));
1325:                             let plan =
1326:                                 sample_anomaly(instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1327:                             assert!(
1328:                                 !plan.solid,
1329:                                 "arch opening walled shut in {:x} bay {bay_index}",
1330:                                 instance.id
1331:                             );
1332:                             let head = plan.lintel_from_units.expect("arch head");
1333:                             assert!(
1334:                                 head >= 2.0,
1335:                                 "arch head {head} too low to walk through in {:x}",
1336:                                 instance.id
1337:                             );
1338:                             openings_walked += 1;
1339:                         }
1340:                     }
1341:                     bay_index += 1;
1342:                 }
1343:             }
1344:             ArchLayout::DeadEnd => {
1345:                 let p = instance.world_coords(-(half_x - 0.1), 0.0);
1346:                 let plan = sample_anomaly(instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1347:                 assert!(!plan.solid, "dead-end entrance sealed in {:x}", instance.id);
1348:                 assert!(plan.lintel_from_units.unwrap_or(0.0) >= 2.0);
1349:             }
1350:         }
1351:     }
1352:     assert!(openings_walked >= 8, "only {openings_walked} openings verified");
1353:     assert!(
1354:         profiles.len() >= instances.len() - 1,
1355:         "arcades repeat themselves: {} profiles for {} rooms",
1356:         profiles.len(),
1357:         instances.len()
1358:     );
1359: }

1361: /// Pillar expanses read calmer than ordinary Level 0 (dry shallow
1362: /// carpet) and the protected bearing lane carries an unbroken light
1363: /// rhythm — the route is architecture, not an invisible collision lane.
1364: #[test]
1365: fn pillar_expanse_is_dry_and_its_bearing_lane_is_lit_in_rhythm() {
1366:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_DRY_CARPET;
1367:     let (config, instance) = find_macro_anomaly(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
1368:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1369:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1370:     let interior = instance.world_coords(1.0, 1.0);
1371:     let plan = sample_anomaly(
1372:         &instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, interior.x, interior.z,
1373:     );
1374:     assert_eq!(plan.floor_material, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET);
1375: 
1376:     // Every 4.8u lane module inside the footprint carries a panel.
1377:     let mut modules = 0usize;
1378:     let mut lit = 0usize;
1379:     let mut lx = (-instance.footprint.half_x / 4.8).ceil() * 4.8 + 2.4;
1380:     while lx < instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band {
1381:         if lx.abs() < instance.footprint.half_x - instance.entry_band {
1382:             let p = instance.world_coords(lx, 0.0);
1383:             let c = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1384:             modules += 1;
1385:             if c.light {
1386:                 lit += 1;
1387:             }
1388:         }
1389:         lx += 4.8;
1390:     }
1391:     assert!(modules >= 8, "sample too small: {modules}");
1392:     assert!(
1393:         lit * 10 >= modules * 8,
1394:         "bearing lane rhythm is broken: {lit}/{modules} modules lit"
1395:     );
1396: }

1398: /// Blackout cues are semantic: skeleton fixtures voxelize as cool
1399: /// glimmers, the approach keeps warm office light, and committed-depth
1400: /// floors pool recessed fluid somewhere.
1401: #[test]
1402: fn blackout_cues_are_glimmers_and_floors_pool_fluid() {
1403:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER};
1404:     let (config, instance) = find_macro_anomaly(AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse);
1405:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1406:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1407: 
1408:     let mut glimmer_seen = false;
1409:     let mut lx = (-instance.footprint.half_x / 28.0).ceil() * 28.0 + 0.2;
1410:     while lx < instance.footprint.half_x {
1411:         let p = instance.world_coords(lx, 0.0);
1412:         let c = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1413:         if c.light {
1414:             assert_eq!(
1415:                 c.light_material, VOXEL_GLIMMER,
1416:                 "skeleton cue is not a glimmer"
1417:             );
1418:             glimmer_seen = true;
1419:         }
1420:         lx += 28.0;
1421:     }
1422:     assert!(glimmer_seen, "no glimmer found on the recovery skeleton");
1423: 
1424:     let mut fluid_seen = false;
1425:     let mut lz = -instance.footprint.half_z * 0.5;
1426:     while lz < instance.footprint.half_z * 0.5 && !fluid_seen {
1427:         let mut sx = -instance.footprint.half_x * 0.5;
1428:         while sx < instance.footprint.half_x * 0.5 {
1429:             let p = instance.world_coords(sx, lz);
1430:             let c = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1431:             if !c.solid && c.floor_material == VOXEL_FLUID {
1432:                 fluid_seen = true;
1433:                 break;
1434:             }
1435:             sx += 0.8;
1436:         }
1437:         lz += 0.8;
1438:     }
1439:     assert!(fluid_seen, "no recessed fluid basin in the blackout core");
1440: }
1441: 
1442: /// A reality in which every fabric drift cell of a world window has
1443: /// rearranged, with epochs deliberately mixed so cell boundaries between
1444: /// different epochs are exercised.
1445: fn drifted_reality(min_cell: i64, max_cell: i64) -> RealitySnapshot {
1446:     let mut reality = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1447:     for cz in min_cell..=max_cell {
1448:         for cx in min_cell..=max_cell {
1449:             for _ in 0..=((cx + cz).rem_euclid(3) as u32) {
1450:                 reality = reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cx, cz);
1451:             }
1452:         }
1453:     }
1454:     reality
1455: }
1456: 
1457: /// The Peripheral Shift: after territory drifts, ordinary fabric has
1458: /// genuinely rearranged — but every planned system (corridors, assemblies
1459: /// and their thresholds, the spawn opening sequence) is byte-identical.
1460: /// "Days of traveled hallways" never replay; the navigation skeleton does.
1461: #[test]
1462: fn peripheral_shift_rearranges_fabric_but_never_the_plan() {
1463:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1464:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
1465:     let plans =
1466:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), REGION_SIZE, 42, &config, &noise);
1467:     let plan_for = |wx: f32, wz: f32| {
1468:         &plans
1469:             .iter()
1470:             .find(|(k, _)| *k == (region_index(wx), region_index(wz)))
1471:             .unwrap()
1472:             .1
1473:     };
1474:     // Drift cells 0..=1 on each axis (world 0..80); leave the rest pristine.
1475:     let reality = drifted_reality(0, 1);
1476:     let sp = crate::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(42);
1477: 
1478:     let mut fabric_changed = 0usize;
1479:     let mut fabric_compared = 0usize;
1480:     for sz in 0..200 {
1481:         for sx in 0..200 {
1482:             let (wx, wz) = (sx as f32 * 0.6 + 0.3, sz as f32 * 0.6 + 0.3);
1483:             let plan = plan_for(wx, wz);
1484:             let before = BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
1485:                 plan,
1486:                 &noise,
1487:                 42,
1488:                 &config,
1489:                 &RealitySnapshot::empty(),
1490:                 wx,
1491:                 wz,
1492:             );
1493:             let after =
1494:                 BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(plan, &noise, 42, &config, &reality, wx, wz);
1495: 
1496:             // Corridor interiors never drift. Their edge band is
1497:             // indeterminate here: where the edge opens, the band is fabric
1498:             // and may lawfully drift, so the band is asserted neither way.
1499:             let corridor_interior = plan
1500:                 .corridors
1501:                 .iter()
1502:                 .any(|s| s.distance(wx, wz) <= s.width * 0.5);
1503:             let corridor_band = !corridor_interior
1504:                 && plan
1505:                     .corridors
1506:                     .iter()
1507:                     .any(|s| s.distance(wx, wz) <= s.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T);
1508:             if corridor_band {
1509:                 continue;
1510:             }
1511:             let planned = corridor_interior
1512:                 || plan.assemblies.iter().any(|a| {
1513:                     let b = a.footprint.bounds();
1514:                     let m = PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05;
1515:                     wx >= b.0 - m && wx <= b.2 + m && wz >= b.1 - m && wz <= b.3 + m
1516:                 })
1517:                 || plan
1518:                     .anomalies
1519:                     .iter()
1520:                     .any(|a| a.footprint.bounds().expanded(3.2 + 0.1).contains(wx, wz));
1521:             let near_spawn = (wx - sp.x).powi(2) + (wz - sp.z).powi(2) < 26.0 * 26.0;
1522:             // Fabric decisions anchor at their own lattice cell's center, so
1523:             // a column within one fabric cell of the drifted area may share
1524:             // a decision with it. Only columns clear of that band must be
1525:             // untouched; columns inside the band are asserted neither way.
1526:             let drift_edge = 2.0 * 40.0;
1527:             let outside_drift = wx > drift_edge + FABRIC_CELL || wz > drift_edge + FABRIC_CELL;
1528:             let boundary_band = !outside_drift && (wx > drift_edge || wz > drift_edge);
1529:             if boundary_band {
1530:                 continue;
1531:             }
1532: 
1533:             if planned || near_spawn || outside_drift {
1534:                 assert_eq!(
1535:                     before, after,
1536:                     "Peripheral Shift touched protected space at ({wx}, {wz})"
1537:                 );
1538:             } else {
1539:                 fabric_compared += 1;
1540:                 if before != after {
1541:                     fabric_changed += 1;
1542:                 }
1543:             }
1544:         }
1545:     }
1546:     assert!(fabric_compared > 2000, "sample too small: {fabric_compared}");
1547:     // Walls are 0.4 u bands on a 7.2 u lattice, so even a full re-deal
1548:     // moves only a few percent of *columns* — what matters is that many
1549:     // whole walls and doorways moved, not that the map inverted.
1550:     assert!(
1551:         fabric_changed * 50 >= fabric_compared,
1552:         "drift barely rearranged the fabric: {fabric_changed}/{fabric_compared}"
1553:     );
1554: }
1555: 
1556: /// The binary-tree connectivity rule holds per fabric cell at *any* epoch,
1557: /// including across boundaries between differently drifted cells: every
1558: /// warren cell still opens through its west or its north wall.
1559: #[test]
1560: fn fabric_stays_connected_through_mixed_drift_epochs() {
1561:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1562:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
1563:     let reality = drifted_reality(-4, 4);
1564:     let mut cells_checked = 0usize;
1565:     for cell_x in -20i64..20 {
1566:         for cell_z in -20i64..20 {
1567:             let x0 = cell_x as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
1568:             let z0 = cell_z as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
1569:             let mut open = false;
1570:             let mut a = PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
1571:             while a < FABRIC_CELL - PLAN_WALL_T {
1572:                 for (wx, wz) in [(x0 + 0.2, z0 + a), (x0 + a, z0 + 0.2)] {
1573:                     if !BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
1574:                         &noise, 42, &tuning, &reality, wx, wz,
1575:                     )
1576:                     .solid
1577:                     {
1578:                         open = true;
1579:                     }
1580:                 }
1581:                 a += 0.2;
1582:             }
1583:             assert!(
1584:                 open,
1585:                 "drifted fabric cell ({cell_x},{cell_z}) sealed both its west and north walls"
1586:             );
1587:             cells_checked += 1;
1588:         }
1589:     }
1590:     assert!(cells_checked > 1000, "sample too small: {cells_checked}");
1591: }
1592: 
1593: /// Strain is the price of mismanaged provisions: at delirium tier 3 the
1594: /// binary-tree doorway guarantee itself erodes, and a meaningful share of
1595: /// warren cells seal both their west and north walls into dead-end
1596: /// pockets. A provisioned wanderer (tier 0) keeps the full guarantee.
1597: #[test]
1598: fn deep_strain_seals_doorways_into_dead_end_pockets() {
1599:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1600:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
1601:     let sealed_cells = |reality: &RealitySnapshot| {
1602:         let mut sealed = 0usize;
1603:         for cell_x in -20i64..20 {
1604:             for cell_z in -20i64..20 {
1605:                 let x0 = cell_x as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
1606:                 let z0 = cell_z as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
1607:                 let mut open = false;
1608:                 let mut a = PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
1609:                 while a < FABRIC_CELL - PLAN_WALL_T {
1610:                     for (wx, wz) in [(x0 + 0.2, z0 + a), (x0 + a, z0 + 0.2)] {
1611:                         if !BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
1612:                             &noise, 42, &tuning, reality, wx, wz,
1613:                         )
1614:                         .solid
1615:                         {
1616:                             open = true;
1617:                         }
1618:                     }
1619:                     a += 0.2;
1620:                 }
1621:                 sealed += usize::from(!open);
1622:             }
1623:         }
1624:         sealed
1625:     };
1626:     assert_eq!(
1627:         sealed_cells(&RealitySnapshot::empty()),
1628:         0,
1629:         "an unstrained fabric must keep the binary-tree guarantee"
1630:     );
1631:     let strained = sealed_cells(&RealitySnapshot::empty().with_delirium(3));
1632:     assert!(
1633:         strained >= 40,
1634:         "deep strain grew too few dead-end pockets: {strained}"
1635:     );
1636:     let mild = sealed_cells(&RealitySnapshot::empty().with_delirium(1));
1637:     assert!(
1638:         mild < strained,
1639:         "strain must escalate: tier 1 sealed {mild}, tier 3 sealed {strained}"
1640:     );
1641: }
