````rust
1643: /// Deep strain hides slips: sub-door-width slots in walls that offer no
1644: /// doorway at all. Doors are never narrower than 1.4 u, so any open span
1645: /// under ~1.1 u in a surviving wall is a slip — and none may exist while
1646: /// the wanderer is provisioned.
1647: #[test]
1648: fn deep_strain_hides_narrow_slips_in_solid_walls() {
1649:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1650:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
1651:     let slip_spans = |reality: &RealitySnapshot| {
1652:         let mut slips = 0usize;
1653:         for cell_x in -20i64..20 {
1654:             for cell_z in -20i64..20 {
1655:                 // Walk this cell's west wall band and measure contiguous
1656:                 // open runs between the junction posts.
1657:                 let wx = cell_x as f32 * FABRIC_CELL + 0.2;
1658:                 let z0 = cell_z as f32 * FABRIC_CELL;
1659:                 let mut run = 0usize;
1660:                 let mut step = 0usize;
1661:                 while step <= (FABRIC_CELL * 10.0) as usize {
1662:                     let wz = z0 + step as f32 * 0.1;
1663:                     let solid = BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
1664:                         &noise, 42, &tuning, reality, wx, wz,
1665:                     )
1666:                     .solid;
1667:                     if !solid {
1668:                         run += 1;
1669:                     } else {
1670:                         if (3..=11).contains(&run) {
1671:                             slips += 1;
1672:                         }
1673:                         run = 0;
1674:                     }
1675:                     step += 1;
1676:                 }
1677:             }
1678:         }
1679:         slips
1680:     };
1681:     // A handful of sub-door spans occur naturally where the expanse
1682:     // boundary clips the tail of a wall run; the strained fabric must grow
1683:     // far more of them — the deliberate slips.
1684:     let calm = slip_spans(&RealitySnapshot::empty());
1685:     let strained = slip_spans(&RealitySnapshot::empty().with_delirium(3));
1686:     assert!(
1687:         strained >= calm + 20,
1688:         "deep strain hid too few secret slips: {strained} vs a calm {calm}"
1689:     );
1690: }

1692: /// The corridor's mouths onto the fabric are Peripheral Shift territory:
1693: /// the drift epoch re-deals their width and phase, and deep strain narrows
1694: /// the survivors and seals whole sections — while the spawn opening
1695: /// sequence keeps its walls in every reality.
1696: #[test]
1697: fn corridor_mouths_drift_with_epochs_and_seal_under_strain() {
1698:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::CirculationSpine;
1699:     use crate::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point;
1700: 
1701:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1702:     let spine = CirculationSpine {
1703:         id: 7,
1704:         spine_kind: SpaceProgram::MainCorridor,
1705:         path: vec![Position::new(-640.0, 2000.0), Position::new(640.0, 2000.0)],
1706:         width: 5.6,
1707:     };
1708:     let wz = 2002.0;
1709:     let calm = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1710:     let parched = calm.with_delirium(3);
1711:     let mut shifted = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1712:     for cx in -17..=17 {
1713:         shifted = shifted.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cx, (wz / 40.0) as i64);
1714:     }
1715: 
1716:     let mouth_open = |reality: &RealitySnapshot, wx: f32| {
1717:         BackroomsLevel::corridor_edge_opens(&spine, &noise, 42, reality, wx, true, wx, wz)
1718:     };
1719:     let (mut calm_open, mut parched_open, mut moved) = (0usize, 0usize, 0usize);
1720:     let mut samples = 0usize;
1721:     let mut wx = -640.0f32;
1722:     while wx < 640.0 {
1723:         let open_now = mouth_open(&calm, wx);
1724:         calm_open += usize::from(open_now);
1725:         parched_open += usize::from(mouth_open(&parched, wx));
1726:         moved += usize::from(open_now != mouth_open(&shifted, wx));
1727:         samples += 1;
1728:         wx += 0.4;
1729:     }
1730:     assert!(samples > 3000 && calm_open > 300, "sample too small");
1731:     assert!(
1732:         moved > 0,
1733:         "a drift epoch must re-deal at least one corridor mouth"
1734:     );
1735:     assert!(
1736:         parched_open * 10 < calm_open * 9,
1737:         "deep strain barely closed the mouths: {parched_open}/{calm_open}"
1738:     );
1739: 
1740:     // The spawn opening sequence stays sacred through drift and strain.
1741:     let sp = spawn_point(42);
1742:     let home = CirculationSpine {
1743:         id: 7,
1744:         spine_kind: SpaceProgram::MainCorridor,
1745:         path: vec![
1746:             Position::new(sp.x - 100.0, sp.z),
1747:             Position::new(sp.x + 100.0, sp.z),
1748:         ],
1749:         width: 5.6,
1750:     };
1751:     for reality in [&calm, &parched, &shifted] {
1752:         assert!(
1753:             !BackroomsLevel::corridor_edge_opens(
1754:                 &home, &noise, 42, reality, sp.x, true, sp.x, sp.z
1755:             ),
1756:             "spawn-readable corridor walls must hold in every reality"
1757:         );
1758:     }
1759: }

1761: /// A strained reality is stingier: each tier lowers the supply-cell
1762: /// acceptance threshold under the *same* hash, so deep strain withholds
1763: /// bottles the calm world offered instead of shuffling them elsewhere.
1764: #[test]
1765: fn deep_strain_withholds_supply_cells_the_calm_world_offered() {
1766:     use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
1767: 
1768:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1769:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
1770:     let calm = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1771:     let parched = calm.with_delirium(3);
1772:     // Default tuning: cell chance is 0.72 calm and 0.72 * 0.55 strained, so
1773:     // a cell whose roll lands between them is offered only to the calm
1774:     // world. Hunt one whose candidate spot actually stamps (open floor).
1775:     let mut verified = false;
1776:     'cells: for cz in 5i64..60 {
1777:         for cx in 5i64..60 {
1778:             let roll = hash(42, 0x0A1A_09D0_57A7_0000, cx, cz);
1779:             if !(0.45..0.65).contains(&unit(roll)) {
1780:                 continue;
1781:             }
1782:             let probe = hash(42, 0x0A1A_09D0_0000_0000, cx, cz);
1783:             let px = (cx as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe)) * 40.0;
1784:             let pz = (cz as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe.rotate_left(23))) * 40.0;
1785:             let chunk = Position::new(
1786:                 (px / config.chunk_size).floor() * config.chunk_size,
1787:                 (pz / config.chunk_size).floor() * config.chunk_size,
1788:             );
1789:             let id = roll | 1;
1790:             let offered = BackroomsLevel
1791:                 .generate_with_reality(chunk, 42, config, &noise, &calm)
1792:                 .supply_items
1793:                 .iter()
1794:                 .any(|item| item.id == id);
1795:             if !offered {
1796:                 // The spot rolled onto solid or anomalous ground; keep
1797:                 // hunting — the assertion needs a supply that really exists.
1798:                 continue;
1799:             }
1800:             let strained = BackroomsLevel
1801:                 .generate_with_reality(chunk, 42, config, &noise, &parched)
1802:                 .supply_items
1803:                 .iter()
1804:                 .any(|item| item.id == id);
1805:             assert!(
1806:                 !strained,
1807:                 "cell ({cx},{cz}) must be withheld from a strained reality"
1808:             );
1809:             verified = true;
1810:             break 'cells;
1811:         }
1812:     }
1813:     assert!(verified, "no in-band supply cell stamped; widen the hunt");
1814: }

1816: /// Geometry priority is not presentation priority: the main corridor stays
1817: /// carved open through a blackout (you can always walk it), but past the
1818: /// approach band the blackout owns the dark — the corridor's light strips
1819: /// die like every other fixture, so circulation never reads as a lit
1820: /// tunnel through the anomaly.
1821: #[test]
1822: fn a_blackout_owns_the_dark_even_over_the_main_corridor() {
1823:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{CirculationSpine, RegionPlan};
1824:     let (config, instance) = find_macro_anomaly(AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse);
1825:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1826:     let center = instance.footprint.center;
1827:     let start_x = center.x - 300.0;
1828:     let plan = RegionPlan {
1829:         origin_world: Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
1830:         size_world: 80.0,
1831:         architects: Vec::new(),
1832:         assemblies: Vec::new(),
1833:         corridors: vec![CirculationSpine {
1834:             id: 0,
1835:             spine_kind: SpaceProgram::MainCorridor,
1836:             path: vec![
1837:                 Position::new(start_x, center.z),
1838:                 Position::new(center.x + 300.0, center.z),
1839:             ],
1840:             width: 5.6,
1841:         }],
1842:         anomalies: vec![instance.clone()],
1843:     };
1844:     let reality = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1845: 
1846:     let mut dark_deep_modules = 0usize;
1847:     let mut lit_outside_modules = 0usize;
1848:     let first_module = (start_x / 4.0).ceil() * 4.0;
1849:     for k in 0..150i64 {
1850:         // Strip modules follow the corridor in *world* space: light where
1851:         // the absolute coordinate along the run satisfies along % 4 < 1.
1852:         let wx = first_module + 4.0 * k as f32 + 0.5;
1853:         let wz = center.z;
1854:         let column =
1855:             BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(&plan, &noise, 42, &config, &reality, wx, wz);
1856:         assert!(!column.solid, "main corridor blocked at ({wx}, {wz})");
1857:         if instance.contains(wx, wz) && instance.normalized_depth(wx, wz) > 0.25 {
1858:             assert!(
1859:                 !column.light,
1860:                 "corridor light strip survives deep blackout at ({wx}, {wz})"
1861:             );
1862:             dark_deep_modules += 1;
1863:         } else if !instance.contains(wx, wz) {
1864:             lit_outside_modules += usize::from(column.light);
1865:         }
1866:     }
1867:     assert!(
1868:         dark_deep_modules >= 5,
1869:         "corridor barely crossed the dark core ({dark_deep_modules} modules)"
1870:     );
1871:     assert!(
1872:         lit_outside_modules >= 10,
1873:         "corridor strips outside the blackout must stay lit ({lit_outside_modules})"
1874:     );
1875: }
1876: 
1877: /// Inside a blackout the same drift stamps rearrange the substrate — the
1878: /// space changes behind the player in real time — while the recovery
1879: /// skeleton stays open in every epoch, so the way out is architecture,
1880: /// never luck.
1881: #[test]
1882: fn blackout_substrate_drifts_but_its_recovery_skeleton_never_does() {
1883:     let (config, instance) = find_macro_anomaly(AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse);
1884:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1885:     let empty = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1886:     let bounds = instance.footprint.bounds();
1887:     let min_cx = (bounds.min_x / 40.0).floor() as i64 - 1;
1888:     let max_cx = (bounds.max_x / 40.0).floor() as i64 + 1;
1889:     let min_cz = (bounds.min_z / 40.0).floor() as i64 - 1;
1890:     let max_cz = (bounds.max_z / 40.0).floor() as i64 + 1;
1891:     let mut reality = RealitySnapshot::empty();
1892:     for cz in min_cz..=max_cz {
1893:         for cx in min_cx..=max_cx {
1894:             reality = reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cx, cz);
1895:         }
1896:     }
1897: 
1898:     // Step 0.4 u: the fabric's wall bands are 0.4 u wide on a 7.2 u
1899:     // lattice, and a coarser stride can cycle past every band forever.
1900:     let mut changed = 0usize;
1901:     let half_span = instance.footprint.half_x.min(40.0);
1902:     let mut lz = -instance.footprint.half_z + 1.0;
1903:     while lz < instance.footprint.half_z - 1.0 {
1904:         let mut lx = -half_span;
1905:         while lx < half_span {
1906:             let p = instance.world_coords(lx, lz);
1907:             let before = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &empty, p.x, p.z);
1908:             let after = sample_anomaly(&instance, &noise, 42, &config, &reality, p.x, p.z);
1909:             if lz.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width {
1910:                 assert!(!before.solid && !after.solid, "recovery skeleton blocked");
1911:             } else if before.solid != after.solid {

1916:         lz += 0.4;
1917:     }
1918:     assert!(
1919:         changed > 40,
1920:         "blackout interior barely drifted ({changed} columns changed)"
1921:     );

1932:     let mut young = (0usize, 0usize); // (alive, sites)
1933:     let mut old = (0usize, 0usize);

1937:             let wx = 1.4 + kx as f32 * 2.8 + 0.2;
1938:             let wz = 1.4 + kz as f32 * 2.8 + 0.2;
1939:             if BackroomsLevel::in_expanse(&noise, 42, wx, wz) {

1941:             }
1942:             let column = BackroomsLevel::column_plan(&noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz);
1943:             if column.solid {
1944:                 continue;
1945:             }
1946:             let age = institution_age_at(&noise, 42, wx, wz);
1947:             let bucket = if age < 0.35 {
1948:                 &mut young
1949:             } else if age > 0.65 {
1950:                 &mut old
1951:             } else {
1952:                 continue;
1953:             };
1954:             bucket.0 += usize::from(column.light);

1972:     // The whole of region (0,0) at 0.5 u per character.

1975:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
1976:     let mut map = String::new();
1977:     for sz in 0..160 {
1978:         for sx in 0..160 {
1979:             let wx = sx as f32 * 0.5 + 0.25;
1980:             let wz = sz as f32 * 0.5 + 0.25;
1981:             let col = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz);
1982:             if col.solid {
1983:                 map.push('#');
````

````rust
  2: //! indexed mesh payload. Geometry stays chunk-local and fixed-point so WebGL
  3: //! uploads are small and camera precision does not degrade far from origin.

 17: 
 18: /// Builds a seam-safe surface payload from a grid that includes a one-voxel
 19: /// X/Z halo. The mapper consults that halo before emitting boundary faces.
 20: pub fn build_surface_mesh(
 21:     halo_grid: &VoxelGrid,
 22:     voxel_scale: f32,
 23:     lod: u8,
 24:     lateral_padding: usize,
 25:     halo_world_origin: [f32; 3],
 26: ) -> SurfaceMeshPayload {
 27:     let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(voxel_scale);
 28:     let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid_with_padding(halo_grid, lateral_padding);
 29:     let width = halo_grid.width() - lateral_padding * 2;
 30:     let depth = halo_grid.depth() - lateral_padding * 2;
 31:     let bounds = Aabb::new(
 32:         [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 33:         [
 34:             width as f32 * voxel_scale,
 35:             halo_grid.height() as f32 * voxel_scale,
 36:             depth as f32 * voxel_scale,
 37:         ],
 38:     );
 39:     let lights =
 40:         collect_emissive_lights(halo_grid, voxel_scale, halo_world_origin, lateral_padding);
 41: 
 42:     let mut mesh = SurfaceMeshPayload {
 43:         vertices: Vec::with_capacity(quads.len() * 4),
 44:         indices: Vec::with_capacity(quads.len() * 6),
 45:         bounds,
 46:         lod,
 47:         light_volume: Vec::with_capacity(
 48:             halo_grid.width() * halo_grid.height() * halo_grid.depth() * 3,
 49:         ),
 50:         light_volume_size: [
 51:             halo_grid.width() as u32,
 52:             halo_grid.height() as u32,
 53:             halo_grid.depth() as u32,
 54:         ],
 55:         light_volume_padding: lateral_padding.min(u8::MAX as usize) as u8,
 56:         lights,
 57:         faces: crate::adapters::face_instances::build_face_instances(&quads, voxel_scale),
 58:         voxel_scale,
 59:     };
 60:     for z in 0..halo_grid.depth() {
 61:         for y in 0..halo_grid.height() {
 62:             for x in 0..halo_grid.width() {
 63:                 let [r, g, b] = halo_grid.get_light_rgb(x, y, z);
 64:                 // The grid light is 0-15, WebGL expects 0-255 for gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE RGB textures.
 65:                 mesh.light_volume.push(r * 17);
 66:                 mesh.light_volume.push(g * 17);
 67:                 mesh.light_volume.push(b * 17);
 68:             }
 69:         }
 70:     }
 71:     for quad in &quads {
 72:         append_quad(&mut mesh, quad, voxel_scale);
 73:     }
 74:     mesh
 75: }
 76: 
 77: fn append_quad(mesh: &mut SurfaceMeshPayload, quad: &MergedQuad, voxel_scale: f32) {
 78:     let x0 = quad.x;
 79:     let x1 = quad.x + quad.w;
 80:     let y0 = quad.y;
 81:     let y1 = quad.y + quad.h;
 82:     let z0 = quad.z;
 83:     let z1_horizontal = quad.z + quad.h;
 84:     let z1_x_face = quad.z + quad.w;
 85: 
 86:     // `w` and `h` span different local axes per face. Move the positive
 87:     // faces to the far voxel plane so the indexed mesh is a closed shell.
 88:     let points = match quad.dir {
 89:         FaceDirection::Up => {
 90:             let y = quad.y + voxel_scale;
 91:             [
 92:                 [x0, y, z0],
 93:                 [x0, y, z1_horizontal],
 94:                 [x1, y, z1_horizontal],
 95:                 [x1, y, z0],
 96:             ]
 97:         }
 98:         FaceDirection::Down => [
 99:             [x0, y0, z0],
100:             [x1, y0, z0],
101:             [x1, y0, z1_horizontal],
102:             [x0, y0, z1_horizontal],
103:         ],
104:         FaceDirection::North => [
105:             [x0, y0, quad.z],
106:             [x0, y1, quad.z],
107:             [x1, y1, quad.z],
108:             [x1, y0, quad.z],
109:         ],
110:         FaceDirection::South => {
111:             let z = quad.z + voxel_scale;
112:             [[x0, y0, z], [x1, y0, z], [x1, y1, z], [x0, y1, z]]
113:         }
114:         FaceDirection::East => {
115:             let x = quad.x + voxel_scale;
116:             [
117:                 [x, y0, z0],
118:                 [x, y1, z0],
119:                 [x, y1, z1_x_face],
120:                 [x, y0, z1_x_face],
121:             ]
122:         }
123:         FaceDirection::West => [
124:             [quad.x, y0, z0],
125:             [quad.x, y0, z1_x_face],
126:             [quad.x, y1, z1_x_face],
127:             [quad.x, y1, z0],
128:         ],
129:     };
130: 
131:     let base = mesh.vertices.len() as u32;
132:     let normal_axis = normal_axis(quad.dir);
133:     let material = material_id(quad.v_type);
134:     for position in points {
135:         mesh.vertices.push(PackedVertex {
136:             position: position.map(pack_position),
137:             normal_axis,
138:             material,
139:             static_indirect: quad.light,
140:             ao: quad.ao,
141:         });
142:     }
143:     mesh.indices
144:         .extend_from_slice(&[base, base + 1, base + 2, base, base + 2, base + 3]);
145: }
146: 
147: fn pack_position(value: f32) -> u16 {
148:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE)
149:         .round()
150:         .clamp(0.0, u16::MAX as f32) as u16
151: }
152: 
153: fn normal_axis(dir: FaceDirection) -> u8 {
154:     match dir {
155:         FaceDirection::Up => 0,
156:         FaceDirection::Down => 1,
157:         FaceDirection::North => 2,
158:         FaceDirection::South => 3,
159:         FaceDirection::East => 4,
160:         FaceDirection::West => 5,
161:     }
162: }
163:

175:         VoxelType::PaleWall => VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
176:         VoxelType::DamagedWall => VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
177:         VoxelType::DryCarpet => VOXEL_DRY_CARPET,
178:         VoxelType::DeepCarpet => VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET,
179:         VoxelType::StickyCarpet => VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET,
180:         VoxelType::Fluid => VOXEL_FLUID,
181:         VoxelType::Glimmer => VOXEL_GLIMMER,
182:         VoxelType::ConcreteWall => VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL,
183:         VoxelType::TileFloor => VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR,
````

````rust
  1: //! Native reference implementation of the GPU fragment shader's SVO
  2: //! ray-marcher (`shaders.rs::raymarchSVO`), marched through a real merged
  3: //! multi-chunk atlas and validated against ground-truth SVO queries.
  4: //!
  5: //! Purpose: the GPU path cannot be unit-tested, so this test ports the GLSL
  6: //! traversal 1:1 and asserts that every reported hit corresponds to an
  7: //! actually-solid voxel in the source octree. Phantom hits (the "random
  8: //! floating squares" artifact) fail the test with a diagnostic dump.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
 11: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 12: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 13: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 14: 
 15: use wasm_frontend::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
 16: use wasm_frontend::application::atlas::{AtlasPool, payload_rows};
 17: use wasm_frontend::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, ChunkSourcePort};
 18: use wasm_frontend::application::streaming::{LoadedChunk, chunk_key};
 19: 
 20: struct AtlasBuild {
 21:     texels: Vec<u32>,
 22:     draws: Vec<ChunkDraw>,
 23: }
 24: 
 25: /// Merges chunks through the engine's pooled atlas, exactly like
 26: /// `Engine::stream_chunks` does on a relayout.
 27: fn build_atlas(chunks: &[LoadedChunk]) -> AtlasBuild {
 28:     let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
 29:     let rows = chunks
 30:         .iter()
 31:         .map(|c| payload_rows(&c.payload))
 32:         .max()
 33:         .unwrap_or(1)
 34:         .max(1);
 35:     pool.ensure_layout(chunks.len(), rows);
 36: 
 37:     let mut draws = Vec::new();
 38:     for c in chunks {
 39:         let key = chunk_key(c.origin.0, c.origin.1);
 40:         pool.assign(key).expect("pool sized for all chunks");
 41:         let offset = pool.node_offset_of(key).unwrap();
 42:         draws.push(ChunkDraw {
 43:             origin: [c.origin.0, 0.0, c.origin.1],
 44:             root_index: (offset + c.payload.root as usize) as i32,
 45:             world_size: c.payload.world_size,
 46:             voxel_size: c.payload.voxel_size,
 47:             svo_depth: c.payload.svo_depth,
 48:         });
 49:     }
 50:     let texels = pool.full_texels(|k| {
 51:         chunks
 52:             .iter()
 53:             .find(|c| chunk_key(c.origin.0, c.origin.1) == k)
 54:             .map(|c| &c.payload)
 55:     });
 56:     AtlasBuild { texels, draws }
 57: }
 58: 
 59: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 60: #[allow(dead_code)] // `t`/`voxel_type` exist for the Debug dump on failure
 61: struct Hit {
 62:     chunk: usize,
 63:     t: f32,
 64:     /// Leaf box in chunk-local space.
 65:     box_min: [f32; 3],
 66:     box_max: [f32; 3],
 67:     voxel_type: u32,
 68: }
 69: 
 70: /// 1:1 Rust port of the GLSL `raymarchSVO` (same constants, same epsilons).
 71: fn raymarch_svo(
 72:     atlas: &[u32],
 73:     ro: [f32; 3],
 74:     rd: [f32; 3],
 75:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
 76:     t_entry: f32,
 77:     world_size: f32,
 78: ) -> Option<(f32, [f32; 3], [f32; 3], u32)> {
 79:     let mut t = t_entry;
 80:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
 81: 
 82:     let mut stack: Vec<(usize, [f32; 3], [f32; 3])> = Vec::new();
 83:     let mut current_node = chunk_root_idx;
 84:     let mut cmin = [0.0f32; 3];
 85:     let mut cmax = [world_size; 3];
 86: 
 87:     for _ in 0..160 {
 88:         let tx = current_node * 4;
 89:         let (is_leaf, a, b) = (atlas[tx] == 1, atlas[tx + 1], atlas[tx + 2]);
 90: 
 91:         if is_leaf {
 92:             if a != 0 {
 93:                 return Some((t, cmin, cmax, a));
 94:             }
 95:             // Empty-space skip to this leaf's exit plane.
 96:             let exit = |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
 97:             let tx = exit(cmin[0], cmax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
 98:             let ty = exit(cmin[1], cmax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
 99:             let tz = exit(cmin[2], cmax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
100:             let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
101:             t = t_exit;
102:             p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
103:             // Snap every tied axis past its exit plane (a ray exactly
104:             // through a corner advances diagonally; leaving an axis ON its
105:             // plane stalls the march instead).
106:             if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
107:                 p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { cmax[0] } else { cmin[0] })
108:                     + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
109:             }
110:             if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
111:                 p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { cmax[1] } else { cmin[1] })
112:                     + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
113:             }
114:             if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
115:                 p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { cmax[2] } else { cmin[2] })
116:                     + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
117:             }
118:             // Multi-level pop, mirroring the shader: the skip may cross
119:             // boundaries shared by several ancestor boxes at once.
120:             while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
121:                 let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
122:                 current_node = f.0;
123:                 cmin = f.1;
124:                 cmax = f.2;
125:             }
126:         } else {
127:             let center = [
128:                 (cmin[0] + cmax[0]) * 0.5,
129:                 (cmin[1] + cmax[1]) * 0.5,
130:                 (cmin[2] + cmax[2]) * 0.5,
131:             ];
132:             let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
133:             let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
134:             let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
135:             let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
136: 
137:             if b & (1 << child_idx) != 0 {
138:                 if stack.len() < 8 {
139:                     stack.push((current_node, cmin, cmax));
140:                 }
141:                 if ox == 1 {
142:                     cmin[0] = center[0]
143:                 } else {
144:                     cmax[0] = center[0]
145:                 }
146:                 if oy == 1 {
147:                     cmin[1] = center[1]
148:                 } else {
149:                     cmax[1] = center[1]
150:                 }
151:                 if oz == 1 {
152:                     cmin[2] = center[2]
153:                 } else {
154:                     cmax[2] = center[2]
155:                 }
156:                 current_node = a as usize + child_idx;
157:             } else {
158:                 let omin = [
159:                     if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cmin[0] },
160:                     if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cmin[1] },
161:                     if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cmin[2] },
162:                 ];
163:                 let omax = [
164:                     if ox == 1 { cmax[0] } else { center[0] },
165:                     if oy == 1 { cmax[1] } else { center[1] },
166:                     if oz == 1 { cmax[2] } else { center[2] },
167:                 ];
168:                 let exit =
169:                     |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
170:                 let tx = exit(omin[0], omax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
171:                 let ty = exit(omin[1], omax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
172:                 let tz = exit(omin[2], omax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
173:                 let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
174:                 t = t_exit;
175:                 p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
176:                 if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
177:                     p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { omax[0] } else { omin[0] })
178:                         + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
179:                 }
180:                 if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
181:                     p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { omax[1] } else { omin[1] })
182:                         + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
183:                 }
184:                 if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
185:                     p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { omax[2] } else { omin[2] })
186:                         + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
187:                 }
188:                 while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
189:                     let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
190:                     current_node = f.0;
191:                     cmin = f.1;
192:                     cmax = f.2;
193:                 }
194:             }
195:         }
196:     }
197:     None
198: }
199: 
200: fn outside(p: [f32; 3], min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
201:     p[0] < min[0]
202:         || p[0] > max[0]
203:         || p[1] < min[1]
204:         || p[1] > max[1]
205:         || p[2] < min[2]
206:         || p[2] > max[2]
207: }
208: 
209: /// Mirrors the shader's `main()`: slab-test all chunks, sort by entry, march
210: /// nearest first, return the first hit.
211: fn march_scene(
212:     atlas: &[u32],
213:     draws: &[wasm_frontend::application::ports::ChunkDraw],
214:     ro: [f32; 3],
215:     rd: [f32; 3],
216: ) -> Option<Hit> {
217:     let safe = |v: f32| {
218:         if v.abs() < 1e-4 {
219:             1e-4f32.copysign(v)
220:         } else {
221:             v
222:         }
223:     };
224:     // The shader passes safe_rd (not raw rd) into raymarchSVO too.
225:     let rd = [safe(rd[0]), safe(rd[1]), safe(rd[2])];
226:     let inv = [1.0 / rd[0], 1.0 / rd[1], 1.0 / rd[2]];
227: 
228:     let mut hits: Vec<(usize, f32)> = Vec::new();
229:     for (i, d) in draws.iter().enumerate() {
230:         let lro = [
231:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
232:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
233:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
234:         ];
235:         let mut t_entry = f32::MIN;
236:         let mut t_exit = f32::MAX;
237:         for a in 0..3 {
238:             let t1 = (0.0 - lro[a]) * inv[a];
239:             let t2 = (d.world_size - lro[a]) * inv[a];
240:             t_entry = t_entry.max(t1.min(t2));
241:             t_exit = t_exit.min(t1.max(t2));
242:         }
243:         if t_entry < t_exit && t_exit > 0.0 {
244:             hits.push((i, t_entry.max(0.0)));
245:         }
246:     }
247:     hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1));
248: 
249:     for (i, t_min) in hits {
250:         let d = &draws[i];
251:         let lro = [
252:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
253:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
254:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
255:         ];
256:         if let Some((t, bmin, bmax, vt)) =
257:             raymarch_svo(atlas, lro, rd, d.root_index as usize, t_min, d.world_size)
258:         {
259:             return Some(Hit {
260:                 chunk: i,
261:                 t,
262:                 box_min: bmin,
263:                 box_max: bmax,
264:                 voxel_type: vt,
265:             });
266:         }
267:     }
268:     None
269: }
270: 
271: /// Every hit the reference ray-marcher reports must be a genuinely solid
272: /// region of the source octree — otherwise the renderer shows phantom boxes.
273: #[test]
274: fn multi_chunk_raymarch_reports_no_phantom_geometry() {
275:     let seed = 42;
276:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
277:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
278:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
279: 
280:     // 3x3 resident set around spawn, same as the engine with radius 1.
281:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
282:     // Level 0 now has vaulted regions up to 5.4 u, so a steep ray starting
283:     // near the edge of the spawn chunk can travel farther laterally before
284:     // reaching its ceiling. Keep enough loaded world around the sweep to
285:     // test traversal, not an artificial streaming boundary.
286:     for dz in -2..=2 {
287:         for dx in -2..=2 {
288:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
289:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
290:                 (ox, oz),
291:                 0,
292:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
293:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
294:             ));
295:         }
296:     }
297:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
298: 
299:     // Ground truth: rebuild each chunk's SVO exactly like LocalChunkSource.
300:     let svos: Vec<_> = chunks
301:         .iter()
302:         .map(|c| {
303:             let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
304:             let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(c.origin.0, c.origin.1), seed, config);
305:             BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, config.svo_depth(), config.svo_world_size())
306:         })
307:         .collect();
308: 
309:     let ro = [5.0f32, 1.7, 5.0]; // spawn eye position
310:     let mut phantoms = Vec::new();
311:     let mut hit_count = 0usize;
312: 
313:     // Dense direction sweep: 64 yaw steps x 17 pitch steps.
314:     for yi in 0..64 {
315:         for pi in -8..=8i32 {
316:             let yaw = yi as f32 / 64.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
317:             let pitch = pi as f32 / 8.0 * 1.2;
318:             let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
319:             let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
320:             let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
321: 
322:             let Some(hit) = march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd) else {
323:                 continue;
324:             };
325:             hit_count += 1;
326: 
327:             // The leaf box center, in voxel coordinates of the owning chunk.
328:             let scale = config.voxel_scale;
329:             let c = [
330:                 (hit.box_min[0] + hit.box_max[0]) * 0.5,
331:                 (hit.box_min[1] + hit.box_max[1]) * 0.5,
332:                 (hit.box_min[2] + hit.box_max[2]) * 0.5,
333:             ];
334:             let (vx, vy, vz) = (
335:                 (c[0] / scale) as u32,
336:                 (c[1] / scale) as u32,
337:                 (c[2] / scale) as u32,
338:             );
339:             let truth = svos[hit.chunk].get(vx, vy, vz);
340:             let solid = truth.map(|(vt, _, _, _)| vt != 0).unwrap_or(false);
341:             if !solid {
342:                 phantoms.push((yaw, pitch, hit));
343:             }
344:         }
345:     }
346: 
347:     assert!(
348:         hit_count > 200,
349:         "sanity: the sweep must actually hit walls, got {hit_count}"
350:     );
351:     assert!(
352:         phantoms.is_empty(),
353:         "{} phantom hits out of {}; first 5: {:#?}",
354:         phantoms.len(),
355:         hit_count,
356:         &phantoms[..phantoms.len().min(5)]
357:     );
358: }
359: 
360: /// The world is a closed slab (floor everywhere at y=0, ceiling at the top),
361: /// so every ray with meaningful up/down pitch MUST hit something. A miss is
362: /// a traversal crack — the "black bars in walls" artifact caused by popping
363: /// only one stack level when a skip crosses several octree levels at once.
364: #[test]
365: fn pitched_rays_never_escape_through_cracks() {
366:     let seed = 42;
367:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
368:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
369: 
370:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
371:     for dz in -1..=1 {
372:         for dx in -1..=1 {
373:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
374:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
375:                 (ox, oz),
376:                 0,
377:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
378:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
379:             ));
380:         }
381:     }
382:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
383: 
384:     let mut misses = 0usize;
385:     let mut total = 0usize;
386:     for px in 0..8 {
387:         for pz in 0..8 {
388:             let ro = [1.0137 + px as f32 * 1.11, 1.7, 0.9713 + pz as f32 * 1.19];
389:             for yi in 0..128 {
390:                 for pi in [-40i32, -25, 25, 40] {
391:                     let yaw = (yi as f32 + 0.173) / 128.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
392:                     let pitch = pi as f32 / 60.0 * 1.2;
393:                     let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
394:                     let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
395:                     let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
396:                     total += 1;
397:                     if march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd).is_none() {
398:                         misses += 1;
399:                     }
400:                 }
401:             }
402:         }
403:     }
404:     assert_eq!(
405:         misses, 0,
406:         "{misses} of {total} pitched rays escaped through cracks"
407:     );
408: }
````

````toml
 1: # wasm_frontend — the browser front end of the voxel engine.
 2: #
 3: # Clean Architecture placement:
 4: #   application/  Use-case layer for the interactive client (player physics,
 5: #                 chunk streaming policy, frame orchestration). Pure Rust,
 6: #                 unit-tested natively. Defines the ports (RendererPort,
 7: #                 ChunkSourcePort) that outer layers implement.
 8: #   adapters/     Interface adapters: input mapping, SVO atlas assembly, and
 9: #                 the local chunk source that drives the `vackrooms` core
10: #                 use cases (generation -> SVO -> GPU serialization).
11: #   drivers/      Frameworks & Drivers: WebGL2 renderer, browser event/rAF
12: #                 plumbing, HUD. Only this layer touches web-sys, and it is
13: #                 compiled exclusively for wasm32.
14: [package]
15: name = "wasm_frontend"

17: edition = "2024"
````

## File: src/use_cases/anomalies/geometry.rs
````rust
  1: //! Column geometry for immutable, non-Red-Room anomaly families.
  2: //!
  3: //! The region planner decides *where* an anomaly exists. This module decides
  4: //! what one world-space column inside that immutable plan looks like. Red Rooms
  5: //! remain a separate encounter feature because their geometry is coupled to a
  6: //! dedicated phase machine and recursive Level 0 destination.
  7: 
  8: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  9:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, ArchBehavior, ArchLayout, RealitySnapshot,
 10: };
 11: use crate::domain::entities::environment::{EnvironmentProfile, FloorState};
 12: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT};
 13: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan};
 14: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 15: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 16: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 17: 
 18: const LIGHT_PERIOD: f32 = 2.8;
 19: 
 20: /// Mutable anomaly infill uses a stable content tile for its seam guard. The
 21: /// tile is a world-generation constant, never the size of an output request.
 22: const GENERATION_TILE_UNITS: f32 = 10.0;
 23: 
 24: struct SampleContext<'a> {
 25:     instance: &'a AnomalyInstance,
 26:     noise: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 27:     seed: u32,
 28:     config: &'a GeneratorConfig,
 29:     reality: &'a RealitySnapshot,
 30:     world_x: f32,
 31:     world_z: f32,
 32:     local_x: f32,
 33:     local_z: f32,
 34:     boundary: f32,
 35:     perimeter: bool,
 36:     skeleton: bool,
 37:     away_from_seam: bool,
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /// Sample one immutable macro anomaly or stable archway anchor.
 41: ///
 42: /// Corridors have already won composition priority before this function is
 43: /// called, so every family may assume its protected bearing route is the only
 44: /// remaining cross-cutting circulation concern. Blackout expanses delegate
 45: /// their substrate to the ordinary Level 0 fabric sampler before applying the
 46: /// anomaly profile.
 47: pub(crate) fn sample_anomaly(
 48:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 49:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 50:     seed: u32,
 51:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 52:     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 53:     world_x: f32,
 54:     world_z: f32,
 55: ) -> ColumnPlan {
 56:     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
 57:     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
 58:     let seam_x = world_x.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
 59:     let seam_z = world_z.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
 60:     let context = SampleContext {
 61:         instance,
 62:         noise,
 63:         seed,
 64:         config,
 65:         reality,
 66:         world_x,
 67:         world_z,
 68:         local_x,
 69:         local_z,
 70:         boundary,
 71:         perimeter: boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T,
 72:         skeleton: local_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width,
 73:         away_from_seam: seam_x > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 74:             && seam_x < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 75:             && seam_z > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 76:             && seam_z < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0,
 77:     };
 78: 
 79:     match instance.kind {
 80:         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => sample_pillar_expanse(&context),
 81:         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => sample_blackout_expanse(&context),
 82:         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => sample_pit_lattice(&context),
 83:         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => sample_archway_anchor(&context),
 84:         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms have a dedicated geometry sampler"),
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: 
 88: /// Dehydration multiplies mutable-infill probability: tier 3 nearly
 89: /// doubles how much anomalous mass a re-dealt space grows.
 90: fn delirium_gain(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> f32 {
 91:     1.0 + 0.3 * reality.delirium() as f32
 92: }
 93: 
 94: fn anomaly_hash(instance: &AnomalyInstance, epoch: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> f32 {
 95:     let mut hash = instance.id
 96:         ^ salt
 97:         ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(19)
 98:         ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
 99:         ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(37);
100:     hash ^= hash >> 30;
101:     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
102:     hash ^= hash >> 27;
103:     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
104:     hash ^= hash >> 31;
105:     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
106: }
107: 
108: fn remap_epoch(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
109:     let state = context.instance.state(context.reality)?;
110:     (state.epoch > 0
111:         && context.boundary > context.instance.entry_band
112:         && state.point_is_in_wake(
113:             context.world_x,
114:             context.world_z,
115:             context.config.anomalies.remap_distance,
116:         ))
117:     .then_some(state.epoch)
118: }
119: 
120: fn sample_pillar_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
121:     let instance = context.instance;
122:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
123:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
124:     let lattice = instance.pillar_lattice.expect("pillar instance lattice");
125:     let cell_x = ((local_x - lattice.phase_x) / lattice.bay_x).floor() as i64;
126:     let cell_z = ((local_z - lattice.phase_z) / lattice.bay_z).floor() as i64;
127:     let mut within_x = (local_x - lattice.phase_x).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
128:     let within_z = (local_z - lattice.phase_z).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_z);
129:     let mut side = instance.pillar_size(cell_x, cell_z).unwrap_or(1.2);
130: 
131:     // Distortion grows only after the entry has taught the player a regular
132:     // grid. The route and entry band therefore remain a reliable baseline.
133:     let budget = ((context.boundary - instance.entry_band) / (instance.entry_band.max(8.0) * 2.5))
134:         .clamp(0.0, 1.0);
135:     let immutable_zone = context.skeleton || budget <= 0.0;
136:     let mut dropped = false;
137:     if !immutable_zone {
138:         dropped = anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D0, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.10 * budget;
139:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D1, cell_z, 0) < 0.30 * budget {
140:             within_x = (within_x + lattice.bay_x * 0.5).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
141:         }
142:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D2, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.08 * budget {
143:             side += 0.4;
144:         }
145:     }
146: 
147:     // A committed wake may change relationships between bays, but never at a
148:     // stable content-tile seam where resident reality cohorts meet.
149:     let wake_epoch = (!immutable_zone && context.away_from_seam)
150:         .then(|| remap_epoch(context))
151:         .flatten();
152:     if let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
153:         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F4, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.25 {
154:             side += 0.4;
155:         }
156:         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F5, cell_z, cell_x) < 0.35 {
157:             within_x = (within_x + 0.4).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
158:         }
159:     }
160: 
161:     let dx = within_x.min(lattice.bay_x - within_x);
162:     let dz = within_z.min(lattice.bay_z - within_z);
163:     let mut solid = context.perimeter || (!dropped && dx < side * 0.5 && dz < side * 0.5);
164:     if !solid && let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
165:         let edge_x = within_x < PLAN_WALL_T || lattice.bay_x - within_x < PLAN_WALL_T;
166:         let edge_z = within_z < PLAN_WALL_T || lattice.bay_z - within_z < PLAN_WALL_T;
167:         let threshold = (0.12
168:             * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity
169:             * delirium_gain(context.reality))
170:         .clamp(0.0, 0.48);
171:         solid = (edge_x && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F1, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold)
172:             || (edge_z && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F2, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold);
173:     }
174:     if context.skeleton {
175:         solid = false;
176:     }
177: 
178:     let lane_light =
179:         local_z.abs() < 0.45 && (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
180:     let field_light = (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
181:         && (local_z + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
182:         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11A7, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.62 * tuning.lights;
183:     let ceiling_units = if !immutable_zone
184:         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D3, cell_x / 2, cell_z / 2) < 0.35 * budget
185:     {
186:         4.0
187:     } else {
188:         4.2
189:     };
190:     ColumnPlan {
191:         light: !solid && (lane_light || field_light),
192:         solid,
193:         ceiling_units,
194:         floor_material: EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel(),
195:         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
196:     }
197: }
198: 
199: fn sample_blackout_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
200:     let instance = context.instance;
201:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
202:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
203:     // The blackout substrate is ordinary fabric under the profile — and it
204:     // drifts under the same Peripheral Shift stamps as ordinary fabric. In
205:     // here the engine also advances drift *behind the player in real time*
206:     // (the darkness hides the swap), so a blackout rearranges more cruelly
207:     // than the level outside it: turning around is never a way back.
208:     let mut plan = BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
209:         context.noise,
210:         context.seed ^ instance.id as u32,
211:         tuning,
212:         context.reality,
213:         context.world_x,
214:         context.world_z,
215:     );
216:     let depth = instance.normalized_depth(context.world_x, context.world_z);
217:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::blackout(depth);
218:     plan.wall_material = profile.wall_voxel();
219:     plan.light_material = profile.light_voxel();
220: 
221:     // Ordinary fixtures thin through the approach instead of cutting directly
222:     // to black, so the darkness is spatially earned.
223:     if depth <= 0.22 {
224:         let cell_x = (context.world_x / LIGHT_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
225:         let cell_z = (context.world_z / LIGHT_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
226:         let keep = 1.0 - depth / 0.22;
227:         plan.light = plan.light && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xFADE, cell_x, cell_z) < keep;
228:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_LIGHT;
229:     } else {
230:         plan.light = false;
231:     }
232:     plan.red_light = false;
233:     plan.ceiling_units = if depth > 0.68 {
234:         2.6
235:     } else if depth > 0.35 {
236:         3.0
237:     } else {
238:         3.4
239:     };
240: 
241:     if profile.floor == FloorState::RecessedFluid && !plan.solid && !context.skeleton {
242:         let cell = 7.2;
243:         let basin_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
244:         let basin_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
245:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xF10D, basin_x, basin_z) < 0.22
246:             && local_x.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
247:             && local_z.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
248:         {
249:             plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
250:         }
251:     }
252: 
253:     plan.solid |= context.perimeter;
254:     if context.skeleton {
255:         plan.solid = false;
256:         plan.light = local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
257:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
258:         return plan;
259:     }
260: 
261:     // Deception is nearly unbounded on purpose: blackouts are meant to be
262:     // almost impossible to walk out of, so decoy glimmers may heavily
263:     // outnumber the honest skeleton — and a delirious wanderer sees more
264:     // liars still.
265:     let decoys = (context.config.anomalies.blackout_decoys
266:         + 0.03 * context.reality.delirium() as f32)
267:         .clamp(0.0, 0.95);
268:     let off_lane = (local_z.abs() - (instance.skeleton_half_width + 7.2)).abs() < 0.45;
269:     if off_lane
270:         && depth > 0.3
271:         && local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45
272:         && tuning.lights > 0.0
273:         && anomaly_hash(
274:             instance,
275:             0,
276:             0xDEC0,
277:             (local_x / 28.0).floor() as i64,
278:             local_z.is_sign_negative() as i64,
279:         ) < decoys
280:     {
281:         plan.light = true;
282:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
283:     }
284: 
285:     if context.away_from_seam
286:         && let Some(epoch) = remap_epoch(context)
287:     {
288:         let cell = 7.2;
289:         let cell_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
290:         let cell_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
291:         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(cell);
292:         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(cell);
293:         let edge = within_x < PLAN_WALL_T || within_z < PLAN_WALL_T;
294:         let threshold = (0.20
295:             * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity
296:             * delirium_gain(context.reality))
297:         .clamp(0.0, 0.65);
298:         if edge && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0xB1AC, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold {
299:             plan.solid = true;
300:             plan.light = false;
301:         }
302:     }
303: 
304:     // The dark owns a structural layer the Peripheral Shift re-deals: past
305:     // the approach band, room-scale partitions stand on the instance's own
306:     // lattice. Their epoch comes from the fabric drift stamps, so the
307:     // engine's rear shift does not merely nudge 0.4 u fabric bands — it
308:     // rearranges *rooms* behind the player. Every drawn partition is
309:     // pierced by its own doorway, so no shift can seal space it creates,
310:     // and the recovery skeleton stays exempt below.
311:     if depth > 0.25 && !context.skeleton && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
312:         const PARTITION_CELL: f32 = 9.6;
313:         let cell_x = (local_x / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
314:         let cell_z = (local_z / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
315:         let anchor = instance.world_coords(
316:             (cell_x as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
317:             (cell_z as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
318:         );
319:         let epoch = context.reality.fabric_drift_epoch(anchor.x, anchor.z);
320:         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
321:         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
322:         for (in_band, along, wall_salt, door_salt) in [
323:             (within_x < PLAN_WALL_T, within_z, 0xB1D0u64, 0xB1D1u64),
324:             (within_z < PLAN_WALL_T, within_x, 0xB1D2u64, 0xB1D3u64),
325:         ] {
326:             if !in_band {
327:                 continue;
328:             }
329:             if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, wall_salt, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.5 {
330:                 let gap = anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, door_salt, cell_x, cell_z);
331:                 let gap_pos = 0.8 + (PARTITION_CELL - 3.2) * gap;
332:                 if along < gap_pos || along >= gap_pos + 1.6 {
333:                     plan.solid = true;
334:                     plan.light = false;
335:                 }
336:             }
337:         }
338:     }
339:     plan
340: }
341: 
342: fn sample_pit_lattice(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
343:     let lattice = context.instance.pit_lattice.expect("pit instance lattice");
344:     let within_x = (context.local_x - lattice.phase_x).rem_euclid(lattice.spacing_x);
345:     let within_z = (context.local_z - lattice.phase_z).rem_euclid(lattice.spacing_z);
346:     let dx = within_x.min(lattice.spacing_x - within_x);
347:     let dz = within_z.min(lattice.spacing_z - within_z);
348:     let pit = !context.skeleton
349:         && context.boundary > lattice.side
350:         && dx < lattice.side * 0.5
351:         && dz < lattice.side * 0.5;
352:     ColumnPlan {
353:         floor: !pit,
354:         solid: context.perimeter,
355:         light: !context.perimeter
356:             && context.local_x.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
357:             && context.local_z.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
358:             && context.config.tuning.lights > 0.0,
359:         ..ColumnPlan::open(3.8)
360:     }
361: }
362: 
363: /// Stable pale arch rooms never inspect `RealitySnapshot`, which keeps them a
364: /// fixed landmark against every mutable anomaly family.
365: ///
366: /// A `Transition` room is a *graph connector*: its `ArchBehavior` decides
367: /// what its far half (local `z > 0`) belongs to. The seam is expressed only
368: /// through legal architectural vocabulary — ceiling regime, floor finish,
369: /// lintel height, fixture rhythm — never through impossible collision or a
370: /// repainted wall, so the crossing is felt before it is understood.
371: fn sample_archway_anchor(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
372:     let instance = context.instance;
373:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
374:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
375:     let arch = instance.arch.expect("arch instance profile");
376:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::archway_room();
377:     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
378:     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
379: 
380:     // The far half of a seam room disagrees with the near half.
381:     let far_side = local_z > 0.0;
382:     let (ceiling_units, floor_material) = match arch.behavior {
383:         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => {
384:             (3.0, EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel())
385:         }
386:         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => (4.4, profile.floor_voxel()),
387:         _ => (3.6, profile.floor_voxel()),
388:     };
389:     let mut plan = ColumnPlan {
390:         wall_material: profile.wall_voxel(),
391:         floor_material,
392:         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
393:     };
394: 
395:     let bay_index = ((local_x + half_x) / arch.bay).floor() as i64;
396:     let along = (local_x + half_x).rem_euclid(arch.bay);
397:     // The far arcade of a scale breach broadens its openings; a culture
398:     // seam presses its lintels lower. Both stay on the shared bay rhythm so
399:     // the two walls visibly disagree about the same structure.
400:     let effective_opening = match arch.behavior {
401:         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => arch.opening * 1.5,
402:         _ => arch.opening,
403:     };
404:     let head_drop = match arch.behavior {
405:         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => 0.4,
406:         _ => 0.0,
407:     };
408:     let across_opening = (along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() < effective_opening * 0.5;
409:     let blind = bay_index.rem_euclid(arch.blind_every as i64) == arch.blind_every as i64 - 1;
410:     let arch_head = {
411:         let t = ((along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() / (effective_opening * 0.5)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
412:         (((arch.spring_units - head_drop) + 0.6 * (1.0 - t)) / 0.2).round() * 0.2
413:     };
414: 
415:     if context.perimeter {
416:         plan.solid = tuning.walls > 0.0;
417:         let on_long_wall = half_z - local_z.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T;
418:         match arch.layout {
419:             ArchLayout::Transition => {
420:                 if on_long_wall && across_opening && !blind {
421:                     plan.solid = false;
422:                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(arch_head);
423:                 }
424:             }
425:             ArchLayout::DeadEnd => {
426:                 let on_entrance_wall = half_x - local_x.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T && local_x < 0.0;
427:                 if on_entrance_wall && local_z.abs() < 1.0 {
428:                     plan.solid = false;
429:                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(
430:                         ((arch.spring_units + 0.6 * (1.0 - local_z.abs())) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
431:                     );
432:                 }
433:             }
434:         }
435:         return plan;
436:     }
437: 
438:     if arch.layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
439:         let arcade_plane = half_z - 1.2 - PLAN_WALL_T;
440:         let in_arcade = (local_z.abs() - arcade_plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5;
441:         let in_alcove = local_z.abs() > arcade_plane;
442:         if in_arcade && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
443:             if across_opening && !blind {
444:                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(arch_head);
445:             } else {
446:                 plan.solid = true;
447:             }
448:         } else if in_alcove {
449:             plan.ceiling_units = 3.0;
450:             if ((local_x * 2.5).sin() * (local_z * 1.7).cos()).abs() < 0.3 {
451:                 plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
452:             }
453:         }
454:     }
455: 
456:     plan.light = local_z.abs() < 0.45
457:         && (local_x + half_x - arch.bay * 0.5).rem_euclid(arch.bay * 2.0) < 0.45
458:         && tuning.lights > 0.0;
459:     let _ = context.boundary;
460:     plan
461: }
462: 
463: #[cfg(test)]
````

````rust
  1: //! Pooled SVO node atlas: stable, fixed-size chunk slots inside one shared
  2: //! RGBA32UI texture.
  3: //!
  4: //! This is the raymarcher's analog of "vertex pooling" in mesh-based voxel
  5: //! engines. The naive approach (concatenate every resident chunk's node
  6: //! array and re-upload the whole texture on any change) makes every chunk
  7: //! load cost O(world) in CPU copies and texture bandwidth. The pool instead
  8: //! gives each chunk a fixed row-aligned slot: loading a chunk rebases and
  9: //! uploads *only that slot's rows*, and evicting a chunk is free (its slot is
 10: //! simply reused later; stale texels are never referenced by the draw table).
 11: //!
 12: //! Every chunk's node array is row-padded to whole 1024-texel rows by the
 13: //! core `OctreeGpuSerializer`, so slots stay row-aligned by construction.
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::ports::ChunkPayload;
 16: use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
 17: 
 18: /// The shader's fixed per-frame chunk table size (uniform array length).
 19: pub const MAX_CHUNKS: usize = 25;
 20: 
 21: /// Texels (= SVO nodes) per atlas row. Must match the shader's `decodeNode`
 22: /// constant and the core serializer's row padding.
 23: pub const ROW_TEXELS: usize = 1024;
 24: 
 25: /// One air-leaf texel (type flag 1, voxel type 0): what free space decodes to.
 26: const AIR_LEAF: [u32; 4] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
 27: 
 28: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 29: pub struct AtlasPool {
 30:     /// Rows per slot. Grows (forcing a relayout) when a chunk won't fit.
 31:     slot_rows: usize,
 32:     /// Slot occupancy; index is the slot number.
 33:     slots: Vec<Option<ChunkKey>>,
 34: }
 35: 
 36: impl AtlasPool {
 37:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 38:         Self::default()
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     /// Nodes (texels) per slot.
 42:     pub fn slot_nodes(&self) -> usize {
 43:         self.slot_rows * ROW_TEXELS
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     /// Total rows in the pooled texture.
 47:     pub fn total_rows(&self) -> usize {
 48:         self.slot_rows * self.slots.len()
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     /// Ensures the pool holds at least `num_slots` slots of at least `rows`
 52:     /// rows each. Returns `true` when the layout changed — every slot
 53:     /// assignment is then dropped and the caller must reassign all resident
 54:     /// chunks and re-upload the whole pool.
 55:     pub fn ensure_layout(&mut self, num_slots: usize, rows: usize) -> bool {
 56:         let changed = rows > self.slot_rows || num_slots > self.slots.len();
 57:         if changed {
 58:             self.slot_rows = self.slot_rows.max(rows);
 59:             let len = self.slots.len().max(num_slots);
 60:             self.slots.clear();
 61:             self.slots.resize(len, None);
 62:         }
 63:         changed
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     /// Assigns (or finds) the slot for `key`. Returns `None` when the pool
 67:     /// is full — the caller sized it for the streaming radius, so that is a
 68:     /// logic error handled by falling back to a full relayout.
 69:     pub fn assign(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 70:         if let Some(i) = self.slots.iter().position(|s| *s == Some(key)) {
 71:             return Some(i);
 72:         }
 73:         let free = self.slots.iter().position(|s| s.is_none())?;
 74:         self.slots[free] = Some(key);
 75:         Some(free)
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     pub fn release(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) {
 79:         for slot in &mut self.slots {
 80:             if *slot == Some(key) {
 81:                 *slot = None;
 82:             }
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     /// First texture row of a slot.
 87:     pub fn slot_first_row(&self, slot: usize) -> usize {
 88:         slot * self.slot_rows
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /// Node offset of `key`'s slot within the pooled atlas.
 92:     pub fn node_offset_of(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 93:         self.slots
 94:             .iter()
 95:             .position(|s| *s == Some(key))
 96:             .map(|i| i * self.slot_nodes())
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     /// Whether `payload` fits in the current slot size.
100:     pub fn fits(&self, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> bool {
101:         payload.nodes.len() / 4 <= self.slot_nodes()
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// The slot-sized texel block for one chunk: child pointers rebased to
105:     /// the slot's node offset, tail padded with air leaves.
106:     pub fn rebased_block(&self, slot: usize, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u32> {
107:         let node_offset = (slot * self.slot_nodes()) as u32;
108:         let mut block = Vec::with_capacity(self.slot_nodes() * 4);
109:         block.extend_from_slice(&payload.nodes);
110:         // Internal nodes (type flag 0) store child indices local to the
111:         // chunk; shift them into pool space.
112:         for i in 0..(payload.nodes.len() / 4) {
113:             if block[i * 4] == 0 {
114:                 block[i * 4 + 1] += node_offset;
115:             }
116:         }
117:         while block.len() < self.slot_nodes() * 4 {
118:             block.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
119:         }
120:         block
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// The whole pool as one texel stream (initial upload, relayouts, and
124:     /// back ends without partial-update support). `lookup` resolves a slot's
125:     /// chunk key to its payload.
126:     pub fn full_texels<'a>(
127:         &self,
128:         lookup: impl Fn(ChunkKey) -> Option<&'a ChunkPayload>,
129:     ) -> Vec<u32> {
130:         let mut texels = Vec::with_capacity(self.total_rows() * ROW_TEXELS * 4);
131:         for (slot, occupant) in self.slots.iter().enumerate() {
132:             match occupant.and_then(&lookup) {
133:                 Some(payload) => texels.extend_from_slice(&self.rebased_block(slot, payload)),
134:                 None => {
135:                     for _ in 0..self.slot_nodes() {
136:                         texels.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
137:                     }
138:                 }
139:             }
140:         }
141:         texels
142:     }
143: }
144: 
145: /// Rows needed to hold a payload's node array.
146: pub fn payload_rows(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> usize {
147:     (payload.nodes.len() / 4).div_ceil(ROW_TEXELS)
148: }
149: 
150: #[cfg(test)]
151: mod tests {
152:     use super::*;
153:     use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
154: 
155:     fn payload(root: u32, node_count: usize) -> ChunkPayload {
156:         ChunkPayload {
157:             root,
158:             nodes: vec![0; node_count * 4],
159:             world_size: 12.8,
160:             voxel_size: 0.2,
161:             svo_depth: 6,
162:             surface: crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload::empty(0),
163:             collision: vec![],
164:             traversal_gates: vec![],
165:             pit_hazards: vec![],
166:             supply_items: vec![],
167:             level_exits: vec![],
168:         }
169:     }
170: 
171:     #[test]
172:     fn slots_are_stable_across_unrelated_evictions() {
173:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
174:         pool.ensure_layout(4, 2);
175:         let (a, b, c) = (
176:             chunk_key(0.0, 0.0),
177:             chunk_key(10.0, 0.0),
178:             chunk_key(20.0, 0.0),
179:         );
180:         let slot_a = pool.assign(a).unwrap();
181:         let slot_b = pool.assign(b).unwrap();
182:         pool.release(a);
183:         let slot_c = pool.assign(c).unwrap();
184:         // b never moved; c reused a's freed slot.
185:         assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(b), Some(slot_b * pool.slot_nodes()));
186:         assert_eq!(slot_c, slot_a);
187:     }
188: 
189:     #[test]
190:     fn rebased_block_shifts_internal_child_pointers_only() {
191:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
192:         pool.ensure_layout(2, 1);
193: 
194:         let mut p = payload(0, 2);
195:         // node 0: internal, child_base 8; node 1: leaf, voxel_type 42.
196:         p.nodes[0] = 0;
197:         p.nodes[1] = 8;
198:         p.nodes[4] = 1;
199:         p.nodes[5] = 42;
200: 
201:         let block = pool.rebased_block(1, &p);
202:         assert_eq!(block.len(), pool.slot_nodes() * 4);
203:         assert_eq!(block[1], 8 + pool.slot_nodes() as u32);
204:         assert_eq!(block[4], 1, "leaf type flag untouched");
205:         assert_eq!(block[5], 42, "leaf payload untouched");
206:         // Padding decodes as air leaves.
207:         assert_eq!(&block[8..12], &AIR_LEAF);
208:     }
209: 
210:     #[test]
211:     fn growing_the_layout_invalidates_assignments() {
212:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
213:         assert!(pool.ensure_layout(2, 1));
214:         let key = chunk_key(0.0, 0.0);
215:         pool.assign(key).unwrap();
216:         assert!(!pool.ensure_layout(2, 1), "same layout is a no-op");
217:         assert!(pool.ensure_layout(2, 3), "bigger slots relayout");
218:         assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(key), None);
219:     }
220: 
221:     #[test]
222:     fn full_texels_covers_every_slot() {
223:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
224:         pool.ensure_layout(3, 1);
225:         let key = chunk_key(0.0, 0.0);
226:         let slot = pool.assign(key).unwrap();
227:         let p = payload(0, 4);
228:         let texels = pool.full_texels(|k| (k == key).then_some(&p));
229:         assert_eq!(texels.len(), 3 * pool.slot_nodes() * 4);
230:         // Unassigned slots are air.
231:         let other_slot = (slot + 1) % 3;
232:         let base = other_slot * pool.slot_nodes() * 4;
233:         assert_eq!(&texels[base..base + 4], &AIR_LEAF);
234:     }
235: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/streaming.rs
````rust
  1: //! Chunk streaming policy and the in-memory chunk store.
  2: //!
  3: //! The world is an infinite plane of square chunks. Each frame the policy
  4: //! computes the set of chunk origins that should be resident around the
  5: //! player; the engine loads missing ones (budgeted, to avoid frame hitches —
  6: //! wasm has no threads, so time-slicing replaces the background meshing
  7: //! thread a native engine would use) and evicts the rest.
  8: 
  9: use std::collections::HashMap;
 10: 
 11: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 12: use crate::application::ports::ChunkPayload;
 13: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{LevelExit, PitHazard, TraversalGate};
 15: use vackrooms::domain::entities::supplies::SupplyItem;
 16: 
 17: /// Integer key for a chunk, quantized from its world origin.
 18: /// Origins are always integer multiples of `chunk_size`, so rounding to
 19: /// millimetres gives a stable, hashable key.
 20: pub type ChunkKey = (i64, i64);
 21: 
 22: pub fn chunk_key(origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32) -> ChunkKey {
 23:     (
 24:         (origin_x * 1000.0).round() as i64,
 25:         (origin_z * 1000.0).round() as i64,
 26:     )
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Decides which chunks should be resident for a given player position.
 30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 31: pub struct StreamingPolicy {
 32:     /// World-space side length of a chunk.
 33:     pub chunk_size: f32,
 34:     /// Chebyshev radius in chunks: 1 -> 3x3 resident set, 2 -> 5x5.
 35:     pub radius: i32,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl StreamingPolicy {
 39:     /// Returns the desired chunk origins, sorted nearest-first so the load
 40:     /// budget is always spent on the most urgent chunk.
 41:     pub fn desired_origins(&self, player_x: f32, player_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32)> {
 42:         let px = if player_x.is_finite() { player_x } else { 0.0 };
 43:         let pz = if player_z.is_finite() { player_z } else { 0.0 };
 44:         let base_x = (px / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 45:         let base_z = (pz / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 46: 
 47:         let mut origins = Vec::with_capacity(((2 * self.radius + 1).pow(2)) as usize);
 48:         for dz in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 49:             for dx in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 50:                 origins.push((
 51:                     base_x + dx as f32 * self.chunk_size,
 52:                     base_z + dz as f32 * self.chunk_size,
 53:                 ));
 54:             }
 55:         }
 56:         origins.sort_by(|a, b| {
 57:             let da = (a.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 58:                 + (a.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 59:             let db = (b.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 60:                 + (b.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 61:             da.total_cmp(&db)
 62:         });
 63:         origins
 64:     }
 65: }
 66: 
 67: /// A resident chunk: payload plus its world origin and current level of
 68: /// detail (0 = full resolution; higher = coarser, see `ChunkSourcePort`).
 69: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 70: pub struct LoadedChunk {
 71:     pub origin: (f32, f32),
 72:     pub lod: u8,
 73:     /// Exact immutable encounter state from which every payload view
 74:     /// (collision, SVO, mesh and lighting) was derived.
 75:     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
 76:     /// Cached identity for diagnostics and fast rejection paths. Exact
 77:     /// equality still uses `reality`, so a hash collision cannot mix worlds.
 78:     pub reality_fingerprint: u64,
 79:     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
 80: }
 81: 
 82: impl LoadedChunk {
 83:     pub fn new(
 84:         origin: (f32, f32),
 85:         lod: u8,
 86:         reality: RealitySnapshot,
 87:         payload: ChunkPayload,
 88:     ) -> Self {
 89:         let reality_fingerprint = reality.fingerprint();
 90:         Self {
 91:             origin,
 92:             lod,
 93:             reality,
 94:             reality_fingerprint,
 95:             payload,
 96:         }
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     pub fn is_in_reality(&self, reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> bool {
100:         self.reality_fingerprint == reality.fingerprint() && &self.reality == reality
101:     }
102: }
103: 
104: /// Keyed store of resident chunks. Iteration order is the insertion order of
105: /// keys (tracked separately) so atlas offsets stay deterministic.
106: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
107: pub struct ChunkStore {
108:     chunks: HashMap<ChunkKey, LoadedChunk>,
109:     order: Vec<ChunkKey>,
110: }
111: 
112: impl ChunkStore {
113:     pub fn new() -> Self {
114:         Self {
115:             chunks: HashMap::new(),
116:             order: Vec::new(),
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
121:         self.order.len()
122:     }
123: 
124:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
125:         self.order.is_empty()
126:     }
127: 
128:     pub fn contains(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> bool {
129:         self.chunks.contains_key(&key)
130:     }
131: 
132:     pub fn get(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<&LoadedChunk> {
133:         self.chunks.get(&key)
134:     }
135: 
136:     pub fn insert(&mut self, key: ChunkKey, chunk: LoadedChunk) {
137:         if self.chunks.insert(key, chunk).is_none() {
138:             self.order.push(key);
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Removes every chunk whose key is not in `keep`, returning whether
143:     /// anything changed.
144:     pub fn retain_keys(&mut self, keep: &[ChunkKey]) -> bool {
145:         let before = self.order.len();
146:         self.order.retain(|k| keep.contains(k));
147:         self.chunks.retain(|k, _| keep.contains(k));
148:         before != self.order.len()
149:     }
150: 
151:     /// Chunks in deterministic (insertion) order.
152:     pub fn iter_ordered(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LoadedChunk> {
153:         self.order.iter().filter_map(|k| self.chunks.get(k))
154:     }
155: 
156:     /// All collision boxes of all resident chunks.
157:     pub fn all_collision_boxes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Aabb> {
158:         self.iter_ordered().flat_map(|c| c.payload.collision.iter())
159:     }
160: 
161:     pub fn all_traversal_gates(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &TraversalGate> {
162:         self.iter_ordered()
163:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.traversal_gates.iter())
164:     }
165: 
166:     pub fn all_supply_items(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &SupplyItem> {
167:         self.iter_ordered()
168:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.supply_items.iter())
169:     }
170: 
171:     pub fn all_level_exits(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LevelExit> {
172:         self.iter_ordered()
173:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.level_exits.iter())
174:     }
175: 
176:     pub fn all_pit_hazards(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &PitHazard> {
177:         self.iter_ordered()
178:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.pit_hazards.iter())
179:     }
180: }
181: 
182: #[cfg(test)]
183: mod tests {
184:     use super::*;
185: 
186:     #[test]
187:     fn desired_origins_covers_square_around_player() {
188:         let policy = StreamingPolicy {
189:             chunk_size: 10.0,
190:             radius: 1,
191:         };
192:         let origins = policy.desired_origins(5.0, 5.0);
193:         assert_eq!(origins.len(), 9);
194:         // Nearest-first: the chunk containing the player comes first.
195:         assert_eq!(origins[0], (0.0, 0.0));
196:         assert!(origins.contains(&(-10.0, -10.0)));
197:         assert!(origins.contains(&(10.0, 10.0)));
198:     }
199: 
200:     #[test]
201:     fn desired_origins_handles_negative_coordinates() {
202:         let policy = StreamingPolicy {
203:             chunk_size: 10.0,
204:             radius: 1,
205:         };
206:         let origins = policy.desired_origins(-0.1, -0.1);
207:         assert_eq!(origins[0], (-10.0, -10.0));
208:     }
209: 
210:     #[test]
211:     fn store_eviction_reports_change() {
212:         let mut store = ChunkStore::new();
213:         let payload = ChunkPayload {
214:             root: 0,
215:             nodes: vec![],
216:             world_size: 10.0,
217:             voxel_size: 0.2,
218:             svo_depth: 6,
219:             surface: crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload::empty(0),
220:             collision: vec![],
221:             traversal_gates: vec![],
222:             pit_hazards: vec![],
223:             supply_items: vec![],
224:             level_exits: vec![],
225:         };
226:         store.insert(
227:             chunk_key(0.0, 0.0),
228:             LoadedChunk::new((0.0, 0.0), 0, RealitySnapshot::default(), payload.clone()),
229:         );
230:         store.insert(
231:             chunk_key(10.0, 0.0),
232:             LoadedChunk::new((10.0, 0.0), 0, RealitySnapshot::default(), payload),
233:         );
234:         assert_eq!(store.len(), 2);
235:         assert!(store.retain_keys(&[chunk_key(0.0, 0.0)]));
236:         assert_eq!(store.len(), 1);
237:         assert!(!store.retain_keys(&[chunk_key(0.0, 0.0)]));
238:     }
239: }
````
