## File: README.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine in Rust, structured with documented Clean
  4: Architecture and compiled to WebAssembly. Procedural "backrooms" world
  5: generation, finite-range voxel irradiance, sparse voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk
  6: streaming and sliding player collision all run inside one wasm
  7: module — built to hold up on low-spec hardware. Rendering is pluggable:
  8: a greedy-meshed WebGL2 rasterizer by default, with an instanced face-splat
  9: path, a retained SVO raymarcher, and a CPU-only software fallback all
 10: selectable at runtime (see [Renderer backends](#renderer-backends)).
 11: 
 12: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design (layer map, ports,
 13: data flow, texel encodings, streaming and rendering pipeline).
 14: 
 15: ## How it works
 16: 
 17: Each chunk goes through the same pipeline, on the main thread or in a
 18: generation worker:
 19: 
 20: 1. **Procedural generation** (`src/use_cases/generate_chunk.rs` +
 21:    `*_level.rs`) — a `LevelGenerator` fills a `VoxelGrid` deterministically
 22:    from `(chunk position, seed, config)`. Level 0 is the office backrooms;
 23:    level 34 is an open grassland. Both tile seamlessly because geometry is
 24:    derived from world-space coordinates, never chunk-local ones.
 25: 2. **Lighting preparation** — exposed emissive faces seed an air-only,
 26:    finite-range RGB diffuse field; solids receive it but never propagate it.
 27:    Runtime panels are separately derived from exposed emissive undersides and
 28:    remain analytic area lights in both GPU renderers.
 29: 3. **SVO build + serialize** — the lit grid is packed into a sparse voxel
 30:    octree and serialized into the GPU texel encoding the renderer expects
 31:    (`src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`).
 32: 4. **Streaming** (`wasm_frontend/src/application/streaming.rs`) — chunks
 33:    around the player are requested, LOD'd by distance, and evicted as the
 34:    player moves; a coarse-first pass keeps distant chunks cheap.
 35: 5. **Collision** — player movement is axis-separated (X and Z tested and
 36:    moved independently against a `CollisionWorld`), so hitting a wall
 37:    diagonally slides along it instead of stopping dead.
 38: 6. **Render** — one of four interchangeable `RendererPort` implementations
 39:    draws the resident chunks (see below).
 40: 
 41: A standing gameplay quirk: leaning into a wall for a few seconds has a
 42: chance to "noclip" the player between level 0 (backrooms) and level 34
 43: (grassland) — see `update_noclip` in
 44: `wasm_frontend/src/application/engine.rs`.
 45: 
 46: ### Renderer backends
 47: 
 48: Chosen with `?renderer=` (see [Usage](#usage)):
 49: 
 50: | Value | Backend | Notes |
 51: |---|---|---|
 52: | *(default)* | `SurfaceRenderer` | Indexed greedy meshes, WebGL2 fixed-function depth. The SVO is kept for collision/debug only — no fragment shader walks it. |
 53: | `splat` | `SplatRenderer` | Instanced face-splat "microvoxel" path: one instance per visible surface rectangle, lit once in the vertex shader. |
 54: | `raymarch` | `WebGl2Renderer` | The retained hybrid SVO raymarcher: per-fragment octree walk against an RGBA32UI node-atlas texture. |
 55: | `cpu` | `CpuCanvasRenderer` | Software rasterizer blitted via `ImageData`; no WebGL context at all. |
 56: 
 57: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` fall back automatically (to CPU, or to
 58: surfaces) if WebGL2 or the requested backend is unavailable.
 59: 
 60: ## Build & run
 61: 
 62: Prerequisites: Rust (with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target) and
 63: [`wasm-pack`](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/).
 64: The page imports wasm-bindgen's native ES-module output directly; there is no
 65: webpack build stage in this repository.
 66: 
 67: ```sh
 68: # 1. Build the wasm front end into static/pkg/
 69: wasm-pack build wasm_frontend --target web --release --no-typescript --out-dir ../static/pkg
 70: 
 71: # 2. Run the dev server
 72: cargo run
 73: 
 74: # 3. Open http://localhost:3000
 75: ```
 76: 
 77: ## Usage
 78: 
 79: Click to capture the mouse; WASD to move, ESC to release.
 80: 
 81: - `http://localhost:3000/` — wasm engine (low-spec profile: 3×3 chunk
 82:   streaming, 0.2 u voxels, adaptive resolution)
 83: - `http://localhost:3000/?spec=high` — high-spec profile (5×5 chunks,
 84:   0.1 u voxels)
 85: - `http://localhost:3000/legacy` — the preserved original Three.js/JS client,
 86:   which fetches chunks from the server's `/maze` and `/octree` endpoints
 87:   instead of generating them in the browser
 88: 
 89: Worlds are shareable by URL — every query parameter below is optional and
 90: combinable:
 91: 
 92: | Parameter | Values | Effect |
 93: |---|---|---|
 94: | `spec` | `high` | Switches to the high-spec profile (finer voxels, wider streaming radius). Default is low-spec. |
 95: | `voxel_size` | `0.4`, `0.2`, `0.1`, `0.05` | Overrides scene voxel size after seam, progressive-LOD, SVO-depth, and dense-memory validation. `0.4` is high-profile-only; `0.05` is standard-profile-only. |
 96: | `seed` | number or text | World seed. Non-numeric text is hashed (FNV-1a) so words work too. |
 97: | `pillars` | `0`–`4` | Structural column density multiplier (`0` = none). Default `1`. |
 98: | `walls` | `0`–`4` | Office wall density multiplier (`0` = open plan). Default `1`. |
 99: | `atria` | `0`–`4` | How much of the world vaults into tall atria. Default `1`. |
100: | `lights` | `0`–`4` | Ceiling light panel density. Default `1`. |
101: | `renderer` | `splat`, `raymarch`, `cpu` | Picks a non-default renderer backend (see above). |
102: | `cpu_preset` | `performance`, `balanced`, `quality`, `maximum`, `custom` | Typed CPU workload profile. Presets render at 12.5%–50% backing resolution per axis and present the complete image over the full page; `balanced` is the default. |
103: | `cpu_scale` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom CPU backing scale relative to the 25%-viewport baseline; CSS presentation always remains full-page. |
104: | `cpu_lod_px` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom projected-radius MIP cutoff; lower preserves finer distant geometry. |
105: | `cpu_splat_radius_px` | `1`–`16` | Custom maximum splat radius; lower values virtually split large leaves for finer surfaces. |
106: | `cpu_virtual_depth` | `3`–`8` | Custom cap on virtual solid-leaf subdivision. |
107: | `cpu_mip_occupancy` | `0`–`0.5` | Custom sparse-LOD rejection threshold; lower retains sparser distant detail. |
108: | `cpu_range` | `16`–`256` | CPU draw distance in world units. |
109: | `cpu_shadows` | `off`, `hero`, `full` | CPU fixture visibility: unshadowed, one cached hero-fixture approximation, or the expensive reference that traces every point/Gauss-sample endpoint. |
110: | `workers` | `auto`, `0`, `1`–`4` | Chunk-generation/streaming concurrency. `auto` reserves the main thread and uses at most four workers; explicit counts clamp to reported hardware. `0` uses the synchronous main-thread fallback. This does not parallelize rendering. |
111: | `level` | `0`, `34` | Debug: boots straight into a level (34 = the grassland) instead of waiting on a noclip roll. |
112: | `force_anomaly` | `pillars`, `blackout`, `pits`, `archway`, `redroom` | Debug: guarantees one anomaly of that family near spawn, bypassing organic frequency and the spawn keep-out. |
113: | `rt_hiz` | `0`, `1` | CPU hierarchical-Z rejection. |
114: | `rt_f2b` | `0`, `1` | CPU/raymarch near-to-far traversal. |
115: | `rt_skip` | `0`, `1` | Raymarch empty-SVO-leaf skipping; `0` selects finest-cell diagnostic DDA. |
116: | `rt_mips` | `0`, `1` | CPU projected-size MIP/LOD collapse. |
117: | `rt_beam_occlusion` | `0`, `1` | CPU cone-light occlusion rays. |
118: | `rt_deferred` | `0`, `1` | CPU exact fine-depth rejection before hidden-splat shading. Off shades first and depth-tests later; pixels are identical. |
119: | `rt_ao` | `0`, `1` | CPU sibling-count ambient-occlusion approximation. Off selects unit ambient visibility for the reference path. |
120: | `rt_shadows` | `0`, `1` | GPU direct-light visibility: per-emitter-sample SVO segments in raymarch; a highest-priority-fixture shadow map on surface/splat. |
121: | `rt_cells` | `0`, `1` | GPU splat cell-range culling. |
122: | `rt_budget` | `0`, `1` | GPU splat far-chunk face budget. |
123: | `rt_cull` | `0`, `1` | CPU and raster-GPU chunk visibility culling. |
124: | `rt_dither` | `0`, `1` | GPU dither/grain effects. |
125: | `rt_bake` | `0`, `1` | Optional approximate surface-renderer voxel diffuse fill. Analytic panel lights remain enabled; default `0`. |
126: | `rt_timer` | `0`, `1` | Asynchronous GPU timing queries. |
127: 
128: The top-right HUD names the section you are in (level, zone, region), and
129: **F3** (or Settings → Debug) toggles the anomaly debug overlay: reality
130: epochs, resident traversal gates and pit hazards, and streaming counters.
131: 
132: The in-page settings menu (gear icon) also exposes mouse sensitivity, invert
133: Y, render scale, FOV, control scheme, typed CPU quality presets/custom detail,
134: and every renderer optimization switch. CPU quality scalars do not silently
135: change optimization switches: hierarchical Z, MIP collapse, traversal order,
136: chunk culling, hidden-splat rejection, ambient occlusion, and flashlight scene-visibility rays remain independently
137: diagnosable. Older `cpuScale`, `cpuSplatPx`, `cpuRange`, and `cpuShadows` links
138: are still accepted; the formerly ambiguous `cpuSplatPx` is interpreted as a
139: radius.
140: Live preferences are saved to `localStorage`; Apply & Reload writes disabled
141: optimizations into the URL so a regression setup can be shared exactly.
142: 
143: ## GitHub Pages
144: 
145: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds `wasm_frontend` in release mode and
146: deploys `static/` on every push to `master` (or via manual dispatch). The
147: main engine (`/`, low- and high-spec profiles) generates chunks entirely in
148: the browser, so it needs nothing but static files and runs unmodified from a
149: Pages project URL (`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) — the worker pool
150: resolves `worker.js` relative to the page, not from the domain root.
151: 
152: The `/legacy` client and the `/maze`/`/octree` endpoints depend on
153: `src/main.rs`'s native HTTP server and cannot run on Pages; only the wasm
154: engine is served there.
155: 
156: One-time setup: in the repo's Settings → Pages, set Source to "GitHub
157: Actions".
158: 
159: ## Tests
160: 
161: ```sh
162: cargo test --workspace
163: npm run test:visual
164: ```
165: 
166: The application layers are browser-free by construction, so player physics,
167: collision, streaming, atlas assembly and input mapping are all covered by
168: native unit tests. The visual command first rebuilds `static/pkg` with
169: `wasm-pack`, then boots every renderer in Chromium and runs the approved
170: surface screenshot regression; it cannot pass against a stale WASM bundle.
171: 
172: ## Workspace layout
173: 
174: | Path | What it is |
175: |---|---|
176: | `src/` | `vackrooms` core: entities, use cases, adapters + native dev server |
177: | `wasm_frontend/` | Browser client: application / adapters / drivers (wasm-only) |
178: | `static/` | Thin HTML shell, wasm bundle output (`pkg/`), legacy client |
179: | `wasm_raycaster/` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (reference only) |
180: 
181: ## Modifying the engine
182: 
183: Ports (traits) sit at the boundary of each layer; implement the trait rather
184: than reaching into a concrete type:
185: 
186: - **New procedural level** — implement `LevelGenerator`
187:   (`src/use_cases/level_generator.rs`) alongside `backrooms_level.rs` /
188:   `grassland_level.rs`, register a level id, and give it a native unit test
189:   (generation must be deterministic and seamless at chunk borders — see the
190:   contract documented on the trait).
191: - **New renderer backend** — implement `RendererPort`
192:   (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`) under `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/`
193:   and wire a `?renderer=` value into `create_renderer` in
194:   `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/browser.rs`.
195: - **New chunk source** (e.g. a different streaming/caching strategy) —
196:   implement `ChunkSourcePort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`); see
197:   `LocalChunkSource` and `WorkerChunkSource` for the synchronous and
198:   worker-pool implementations.
199: - **Player/physics tuning** — `wasm_frontend/src/application/player.rs` and
200:   `engine.rs`; both are plain Rust, unit-tested natively without a browser.
201: 
202: After changing anything under `src/` or `wasm_frontend/src/`, run
203: `cargo test --workspace` (native, browser-free) before rebuilding the wasm
204: bundle with the command in [Build & run](#build--run). See
205: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layer map and data flow.
````

````rust
  1: /// Represents a dense 3D grid of voxels.
  2: /// This is the foundation for our "smaller voxels" requirement.
  3: pub struct VoxelGrid {
  4:     width: usize,
  5:     height: usize,
  6:     depth: usize,
  7:     data: Vec<u8>,
  8:     /// Scalar light level 0-15 (the max of the RGB channels), kept for
  9:     /// presenters and bakes that only need brightness.
 10:     light_data: Vec<u8>,
 11:     /// Colored flood-fill light, 0-15 per channel.
 12:     light_rgb: Vec<[u8; 3]>,
 13:     pub runtime_lights: Vec<crate::domain::entities::architecture::RuntimeLight>,
 14:     /// Semantic threshold planes emitted by the same architectural pass as
 15:     /// geometry. The application consumes them to advance deterministic
 16:     /// anomaly epochs; render/collision never invent a separate reality.
 17:     pub traversal_gates: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGate>,
 18:     /// Real floor openings that relocate the player when entered.
 19:     pub pit_hazards: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::PitHazard>,
 20:     /// Consumable pickups placed by the same generation pass as their
 21:     /// marker voxels. Consumption is reality state, not grid state.
 22:     pub supply_items: Vec<crate::domain::entities::supplies::SupplyItem>,
 23:     /// Physical doorways between Backrooms levels. The application flushes
 24:     /// and re-streams the world when the player steps through one.
 25:     pub level_exits: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::LevelExit>,
 26:     /// Six neighbor-occupancy bits prepared by the geometry source. A set bit
 27:     /// means that face touches solid matter; clearing it means the face is
 28:     /// exposed to air. Streaming generation computes this from its halo, so
 29:     /// chunk-boundary answers do not depend on which neighbor is resident.
 30:     face_occlusion: Vec<u8>,
 31: }
 32: 
 33: /// Neighbor-occupancy encoding shared by meshing, SVO serialization, and CPU
 34: /// surface reconstruction. The order intentionally matches the historical
 35: /// `FaceDirection::occlusion_bit` contract.
 36: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X: u8 = 1;
 37: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X: u8 = 2;
 38: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y: u8 = 4;
 39: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y: u8 = 8;
 40: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z: u8 = 16;
 41: pub const FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z: u8 = 32;
 42: pub const FACE_OCCLUSION_MASK: u8 = 0x3f;
 43: 
 44: pub const VOXEL_AIR: u8 = 0;
 45: pub const VOXEL_WALL: u8 = 1;
 46: pub const VOXEL_FLOOR: u8 = 2;
 47: pub const VOXEL_CEILING: u8 = 3;
 48: pub const VOXEL_LIGHT: u8 = 4;
 49: pub const VOXEL_RED_WALL: u8 = 5;
 50: /// Walkable ground cover (grassland level). Visual-only, like FLOOR.
 51: pub const VOXEL_GRASS: u8 = 6;
 52: /// Walkable shallow water (grassland lakes). Visual-only, like FLOOR.
 53: pub const VOXEL_WATER: u8 = 7;
 54: /// Tree trunk (grassland). Solid: blocks the player like WALL.
 55: pub const VOXEL_TREE: u8 = 8;
 56: pub const VOXEL_RED_LIGHT: u8 = 9;
 57: /// Pale bone-tinted arch-room wall. Solid like WALL.
 58: pub const VOXEL_PALE_WALL: u8 = 10;
 59: /// Rough, damaged blackout-expanse wall. Solid like WALL.
 60: pub const VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL: u8 = 11;
 61: /// Shallow, dry, desaturated pillar-expanse carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 62: pub const VOXEL_DRY_CARPET: u8 = 12;
 63: /// Deep, wet arch-room carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 64: pub const VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET: u8 = 13;
 65: /// Thick, sticky, discolored red-room carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 66: pub const VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET: u8 = 14;
 67: /// Recessed basin holding dark ankle-deep fluid. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 68: pub const VOXEL_FLUID: u8 = 15;
 69: /// Tiny cool emergency glimmer fixture (blackout recovery skeleton).
 70: /// Emissive like LIGHT, far dimmer and colder.
 71: pub const VOXEL_GLIMMER: u8 = 16;
 72: /// Bare structural concrete (Level 1 walls and pillars). Solid like WALL.
 73: pub const VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL: u8 = 17;
 74: /// Institutional tile floor (Level 1). Walkable, like FLOOR.
 75: pub const VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR: u8 = 18;
 76: /// Poured concrete slab floor (Level 1 parking sectors). Walkable.
 77: pub const VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR: u8 = 19;
 78: /// Wooden supply crate (Level 1 Gild sector). Solid: blocks like WALL.
 79: pub const VOXEL_CRATE: u8 = 20;
 80: /// Exposed ceiling pipe / rebar (Level 1). Solid, but authored overhead
 81: /// or as thin obstructions the player walks around.
 82: pub const VOXEL_PIPE: u8 = 21;
 83: /// Metal fire-exit door panel. Non-solid: crossing it is a level transit,
 84: /// so the panel must admit the player who pushes into it.
 85: pub const VOXEL_METAL_DOOR: u8 = 22;
 86: /// Almond water bottle marker. Non-solid, faintly emissive so bottles
 87: /// glint in dim fabric; the pickup itself is the exported `SupplyItem`.
 88: pub const VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER: u8 = 23;
 89: 
 90: /// Number of voxel material ids (the palette table length).
 91: pub const VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT: usize = 24;
 92: 
 93: /// The one authoritative material palette, `0xRRGGBB` per voxel id. Every
 94: /// consumer — octree bake, greedy-mesh debug colors, CPU splatter, and the
 95: /// generated GLSL tables — derives from this table so a new material can
 96: /// never render differently across paths.
 97: pub const MATERIAL_COLORS: [u32; VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT] = [
 98:     0x000000, // 0 air (never drawn)
 99:     0xDDCC66, // 1 yellow wallpaper wall
100:     0x998811, // 2 office carpet floor
101:     0xCCCCCC, // 3 dropped ceiling
102:     0xFFF8D6, // 4 fluorescent panel
103:     0x880000, // 5 crimson / peeled red wall
104:     0x4F9A3D, // 6 grass
105:     0x3A6FB8, // 7 water
106:     0x6B4A2F, // 8 tree / dark pillar
107:     0xFF4433, // 9 red light
108:     0xD8D2C0, // 10 pale arch wall
109:     0x8A7F5C, // 11 rough damaged wall
110:     0xC2B76B, // 12 dry shallow carpet
111:     0x6B5E22, // 13 deep wet carpet
112:     0x7A4A26, // 14 sticky red-room carpet
113:     0x2E2A22, // 15 dark pooled fluid
114:     0x9FC4E8, // 16 cool emergency glimmer
115:     0x8F8D88, // 17 bare structural concrete
116:     0xBDBBB0, // 18 institutional tile floor
117:     0x6E6C66, // 19 poured concrete slab
118:     0x9C7B4A, // 20 wooden supply crate
119:     0x3E4348, // 21 exposed pipe / rebar
120:     0x4A5A6A, // 22 metal fire-exit door
121:     0xEDE6D0, // 23 almond water bottle
122: ];
123: 
124: /// Palette lookup as normalized linear-ish RGB for shader tables.
125: pub fn material_color_f32(voxel: u8) -> [f32; 3] {
126:     let c = MATERIAL_COLORS
127:         .get(voxel as usize)
128:         .copied()
129:         .unwrap_or(0x000000);
130:     [
131:         ((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
132:         ((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
133:         (c & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
134:     ]
135: }
136: 
137: /// Materials that block the player and produce collision boxes. Everything
138: /// else is walkable or decorative.
139: pub const SOLID_MATERIALS: [u8; 8] = [
140:     VOXEL_WALL,
141:     VOXEL_TREE,
142:     VOXEL_RED_WALL,
143:     VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
144:     VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
145:     VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL,
146:     VOXEL_CRATE,
147:     VOXEL_PIPE,
148: ];
149: 
150: /// Materials that emit light in the baked flood fill and render emissive.
151: pub const EMISSIVE_MATERIALS: [u8; 4] = [
152:     VOXEL_LIGHT,
153:     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
154:     VOXEL_GLIMMER,
155:     VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER,
156: ];
157: 
158: /// Authored emitted-radiance scale shared by fixture extraction and every
159: /// renderer's visible-emission path.
160: pub const fn material_emission_strength(material: u8) -> Option<f32> {
161:     match material {
162:         VOXEL_LIGHT => Some(10.0),
163:         VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => Some(8.0),
164:         VOXEL_GLIMMER => Some(0.9),
165:         // A bottle is a glint, not a lamp: just enough to catch the eye.
166:         VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER => Some(0.35),
167:         _ => None,
168:     }
169: }
170: 
171: impl VoxelGrid {
172:     pub fn new(width: usize, height: usize, depth: usize) -> Self {
173:         let size = width * height * depth;
174:         Self {
175:             width,
176:             height,
177:             depth,
178:             data: vec![VOXEL_AIR; size],
179:             light_data: vec![0; size],
180:             light_rgb: vec![[0; 3]; size],
181:             runtime_lights: Vec::new(),
182:             traversal_gates: Vec::new(),
183:             pit_hazards: Vec::new(),
184:             supply_items: Vec::new(),
185:             level_exits: Vec::new(),
186:             face_occlusion: vec![0; size],
187:         }
188:     }
189: 
190:     pub fn width(&self) -> usize {
191:         self.width
192:     }
193:     pub fn height(&self) -> usize {
194:         self.height
195:     }
196:     pub fn depth(&self) -> usize {
197:         self.depth
198:     }
199: 
200:     fn index(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> Option<usize> {
201:         if x < self.width && y < self.height && z < self.depth {
202:             Some(y * (self.width * self.depth) + z * self.width + x)
203:         } else {
204:             None
205:         }
206:     }
207: 
208:     pub fn set(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, voxel_type: u8) {
209:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
210:             self.data[idx] = voxel_type;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:     pub fn get(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
215:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
216:             self.data[idx]
217:         } else {
218:             VOXEL_AIR
219:         }
220:     }
221: 
222:     /// Sets a neutral (white) light level: all three channels get `level`.
223:     pub fn set_light(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, level: u8) {
224:         self.set_light_rgb(x, y, z, [level; 3]);
225:     }
226: 
227:     pub fn get_light(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
228:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
229:             self.light_data[idx]
230:         } else {
231:             0
232:         }
233:     }
234: 
235:     /// Sets colored light (0-15 per channel); the scalar level becomes the
236:     /// max of the channels.
237:     pub fn set_light_rgb(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, rgb: [u8; 3]) {
238:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
239:             self.light_rgb[idx] = rgb;
240:             self.light_data[idx] = rgb[0].max(rgb[1]).max(rgb[2]);
241:         }
242:     }
243: 
244:     pub fn get_light_rgb(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> [u8; 3] {
245:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
246:             self.light_rgb[idx]
247:         } else {
248:             [0; 3]
249:         }
250:     }
251: 
252:     /// Stores the six-bit neighbor-occupancy mask for one voxel.
253:     pub fn set_face_occlusion(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, mask: u8) {
254:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
255:             self.face_occlusion[idx] = mask & FACE_OCCLUSION_MASK;
256:         }
257:     }
258: 
259:     pub fn get_face_occlusion(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
260:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
261:             self.face_occlusion[idx]
262:         } else {
263:             0
264:         }
265:     }
266: }

  1: //! In-wasm chunk source: implements the application's [`ChunkSourcePort`] by
  2: //! driving the core engine use cases directly. There is no server round-trip;
  3: //! the entire pipeline — procedural generation, voxel diffuse bake, SVO build, GPU
  4: //! serialization, collision extraction — runs inside the wasm module.
  5: //!
  6: //! Pipeline per chunk:
  7: //!   GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase  (VoxelGrid, lighting included)
  8: //!     -> BuildOctreeUseCase           (SparseVoxelOctree)
  9: //!     -> OctreeGpuSerializer          (row-padded RGBA32UI texel stream)
 10: //!     -> collision walk               (solid leaves -> world-space AABBs)
 11: 
 12: use vackrooms::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
 13: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
 15: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 16:     FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z,
 17:     FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z, VOXEL_AIR,
 18:     VoxelGrid,
 19: };
 20: use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
 21: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 22: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 23: use vackrooms::use_cases::ports::{NULL_TELEMETRY, NoiseProvider, TelemetryPort};
 24: 
 25: use crate::adapters::surface_mesh::build_surface_mesh;
 26: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 27: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkPayload, ChunkSourcePort};
 28: 
 29: /// Voxel types that block the player. FLOOR/CEILING/LIGHT/GRASS/WATER and
 30: /// the carpet/fluid classes are visual-only: including them would make the
 31: /// player collide with the floor they stand on. Shared with the core so a
 32: /// new wall class can never render solid but collide hollow.
 33: const SOLID_TYPES: [u8; 8] = vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::SOLID_MATERIALS;
 34: 
 35: pub struct LocalChunkSource<N: NoiseProvider> {
 36:     noise: N,
 37:     telemetry: &'static dyn TelemetryPort,
 38:     seed: u32,
 39:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: impl<N: NoiseProvider> LocalChunkSource<N> {
 43:     pub fn new(noise: N, seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> Self {
 44:         Self {
 45:             noise,
 46:             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
 47:             seed,
 48:             config,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     pub fn with_telemetry(
 53:         noise: N,
 54:         seed: u32,
 55:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 56:         telemetry: &'static dyn TelemetryPort,
 57:     ) -> Self {
 58:         Self {
 59:             noise,
 60:             telemetry,
 61:             seed,
 62:             config,
 63:         }
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     fn generate_payload(
 67:         &self,
 68:         origin_x: f32,
 69:         origin_z: f32,
 70:         level: u32,
 71:         lod: u8,
 72:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 73:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
 74:         let config = self.config.with_level(level).at_lod(lod);
 75:         let generator =
 76:             GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&self.noise, self.telemetry);
 77: 
 78:         // Generate one extra voxel around the X/Z perimeter, then crop the
 79:         // authoritative interior for SVO/collision. The greedy mesher reads
 80:         // the halo while deciding boundary faces, so it never invents a face
 81:         // merely because the adjacent streamed chunk has not uploaded yet.
 82:         let halo_config = GeneratorConfig {
 83:             chunk_size: config.chunk_size + config.voxel_scale * 2.0,
 84:             ..config
 85:         };
 86:         let halo_world_origin = [
 87:             origin_x - config.voxel_scale,
 88:             0.0,
 89:             origin_z - config.voxel_scale,
 90:         ];
 91:         let halo_grid = generator.execute_with_reality(
 92:             Position::new(halo_world_origin[0], halo_world_origin[2]),
 93:             self.seed,
 94:             halo_config,
 95:             reality,
 96:         );
 97:         let grid = crop_lateral_halo(&halo_grid, 1);
 98:         let surface = build_surface_mesh(&halo_grid, config.voxel_scale, lod, 1, halo_world_origin);
 99: 
100:         let svo_depth = config.svo_depth();
101:         let svo = BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, svo_depth, config.svo_world_size());
102: 
103:         let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
104:         let collision = extract_collision_boxes(&svo, origin_x, origin_z, config.voxel_scale);
105: 
106:         ChunkPayload {
107:             root: svo.root as u32,
108:             nodes: gpu.texel_data,
109:             world_size: config.svo_world_size(),
110:             voxel_size: config.voxel_scale,
111:             svo_depth: svo_depth as u8,
112:             surface,
113:             collision,
114:             traversal_gates: halo_grid.traversal_gates.clone(),
115:             pit_hazards: halo_grid.pit_hazards.clone(),
116:             supply_items: halo_grid.supply_items.clone(),
117:             level_exits: halo_grid.level_exits.clone(),
118:         }
119:     }
120: }
121: 
122: impl<N: NoiseProvider> ChunkSourcePort for LocalChunkSource<N> {
123:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
124:         self.generate_payload(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, &RealitySnapshot::default())
125:     }
126: 
127:     fn load_with_reality(
128:         &self,
129:         origin_x: f32,
130:         origin_z: f32,
131:         level: u32,
132:         lod: u8,
133:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
134:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
135:         self.generate_payload(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
136:     }
137: }
138: 
139: /// Copies the actual chunk interior out of a generated X/Z halo while
140: /// retaining voxel type and colored baked lighting, then deriving exact
141: /// six-direction neighbor occupancy while the halo is still available.
142: fn crop_lateral_halo(halo: &VoxelGrid, padding: usize) -> VoxelGrid {
143:     assert!(halo.width() > padding * 2 && halo.depth() > padding * 2);
144:     let mut inner = VoxelGrid::new(
145:         halo.width() - padding * 2,
146:         halo.height(),
147:         halo.depth() - padding * 2,
148:     );
149:     for z in 0..inner.depth() {
150:         for y in 0..inner.height() {
151:             for x in 0..inner.width() {
152:                 let hx = x + padding;
153:                 let hz = z + padding;
154:                 inner.set(x, y, z, halo.get(hx, y, hz));
155:                 inner.set_light_rgb(x, y, z, halo.get_light_rgb(hx, y, hz));
156:                 inner.set_face_occlusion(x, y, z, neighbor_occlusion_mask(halo, hx, y, hz));
157:             }
158:         }
159:     }
160:     inner
161: }
162: 
163: /// Exact face closure for one generated voxel, including the lateral halo.
164: ///
165: /// The returned bits travel unchanged through BuildOctree and the GPU atlas.
166: /// Computing them before the crop is what makes a streamed chunk boundary
167: /// authoritative even while its adjacent chunk is unloaded or represented by
168: /// an overlapping power-of-two padded SVO root.
169: fn neighbor_occlusion_mask(grid: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
170:     if grid.get(x, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
171:         return 0;
172:     }
173: 
174:     let occupied = |x: isize, y: isize, z: isize| {
175:         x >= 0
176:             && y >= 0
177:             && z >= 0
178:             && (x as usize) < grid.width()
179:             && (y as usize) < grid.height()
180:             && (z as usize) < grid.depth()
181:             && grid.get(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize) != VOXEL_AIR
182:     };
183:     let x = x as isize;
184:     let y = y as isize;
185:     let z = z as isize;
186:     let mut mask = 0;
187:     if occupied(x + 1, y, z) {
188:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X;
189:     }
190:     if occupied(x - 1, y, z) {
191:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X;
192:     }
193:     if occupied(x, y + 1, z) {
194:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y;
195:     }
196:     if occupied(x, y - 1, z) {
197:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y;
198:     }
199:     if occupied(x, y, z + 1) {
200:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z;
201:     }
202:     if occupied(x, y, z - 1) {
203:         mask |= FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z;
204:     }
205:     mask
206: }
207: 
208: /// Walks the SVO and emits one world-space AABB per solid leaf region.
209: /// Uniform subtrees collapsed by the SVO become single large boxes for free,
210: /// which keeps the collision set small.
211: pub fn extract_collision_boxes(
212:     svo: &SparseVoxelOctree,
213:     origin_x: f32,
214:     origin_z: f32,
215:     voxel_scale: f32,
216: ) -> Vec<Aabb> {
217:     let mut boxes = Vec::new();
218:     let size = 1u32 << svo.depth;
219:     walk(
220:         svo,
221:         svo.root,
222:         0,
223:         0,
224:         0,
225:         size,
226:         origin_x,
227:         origin_z,
228:         voxel_scale,
229:         &mut boxes,
230:     );
231:     boxes
232: }
233: 
234: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
235: fn walk(
236:     svo: &SparseVoxelOctree,
237:     node_idx: usize,
238:     x: u32,
239:     y: u32,
240:     z: u32,
241:     size: u32,
242:     origin_x: f32,
243:     origin_z: f32,
244:     voxel_scale: f32,
245:     out: &mut Vec<Aabb>,
246: ) {
247:     match svo.nodes[node_idx] {
248:         SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
249:             if SOLID_TYPES.contains(&voxel_type) {
250:                 let min = [
251:                     origin_x + x as f32 * voxel_scale,
252:                     y as f32 * voxel_scale,
253:                     origin_z + z as f32 * voxel_scale,
254:                 ];
255:                 let extent = size as f32 * voxel_scale;
256:                 out.push(Aabb::new(
257:                     min,
258:                     [min[0] + extent, min[1] + extent, min[2] + extent],
259:                 ));
260:             }
261:         }
262:         SvoNode::Internal {
263:             child_base_index,
264:             child_mask,
265:         } => {
266:             let half = size / 2;
267:             for child in 0..8u32 {
268:                 if child_mask & (1 << child) != 0 {
269:                     walk(
270:                         svo,
271:                         child_base_index as usize + child as usize,
272:                         x + (child & 1) * half,
273:                         y + ((child >> 1) & 1) * half,
274:                         z + ((child >> 2) & 1) * half,
275:                         half,
276:                         origin_x,
277:                         origin_z,
278:                         voxel_scale,
279:                         out,
280:                     );
281:                 }
282:             }
283:         }
284:     }
285: }
286: 
287: #[cfg(test)]
288: mod tests {

````rust
  1: //! URL query → generation settings. Lets players share worlds by URL:
  2: //!
  3: //! `?seed=1234&voxel_size=0.1&pillars=0.5&walls=1.2&anomalies=0.8`
  4: //!
  5: //! * `seed`    — world seed (u32; any text is hashed so words work too).
  6: //! * `pillars` — structural column density multiplier (0 = none).
  7: //! * `walls`   — office wall density multiplier (0 = open plan).
  8: //! * `atria`   — how much of the world vaults into tall atria.
  9: //! * `lights`  — ceiling light panel density.
 10: //! * `voxel_size` — optional scene resolution in world units. The selected
 11: //!   profile remains in force when the value violates generator limits.
 12: //! * `anomalies`, `anomaly_size` and the per-family knobs control Level 0
 13: //!   phenomena without changing ordinary fabric density.
 14: //! * `remap_intensity`, `remap_distance` and `anomaly_safe_radius` control
 15: //!   deterministic traversal-epoch transformations.
 16: //!
 17: //! Multipliers default to 1.0 and are clamped to 0..=4; physical distances
 18: //! use narrower documented ranges. Kept free of
 19: //! web-sys so it is natively unit-tested; the browser driver only hands in
 20: //! `window.location.search`.
 21: 
 22: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 23: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{AnomalyTuning, GeneratorConfig, LevelTuning};
 24: 
 25: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 26: pub struct GenerationParams {
 27:     pub seed: u32,
 28:     pub voxel_size: Option<f32>,
 29:     pub tuning: LevelTuning,
 30:     pub anomalies: AnomalyTuning,
 31: }
 32: 
 33: /// Exact-key lookup in a location search string (`?a=1&b=2`, leading `?`
 34: /// optional). Every query consumer must go through this (or an equivalent
 35: /// `split('&')` loop): raw `str::find("key=")` substring probes have caused
 36: /// settings to apply that nobody asked for — `?spawn_yaw=2` silently
 37: /// matching `yaw=`, values containing `capture=1`, and the like.
 38: pub fn query_param<'a>(query: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
 39:     query
 40:         .trim_start_matches('?')
 41:         .split('&')
 42:         .find_map(|pair| match pair.split_once('=') {
 43:             Some((k, v)) if k == key => Some(v),
 44:             _ => None,
 45:         })
 46: }
 47: 
 48: /// True when the query holds exactly `key=1`.
 49: pub fn query_flag(query: &str, key: &str) -> bool {
 50:     query_param(query, key) == Some("1")
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Parses `window.location.search` (with or without the leading `?`).
 54: /// Unknown keys are ignored; malformed values fall back to defaults.
 55: pub fn parse_generation_params(query: &str, default_seed: u32) -> GenerationParams {
 56:     let mut params = GenerationParams {
 57:         seed: default_seed,
 58:         voxel_size: None,
 59:         tuning: LevelTuning::default(),
 60:         anomalies: AnomalyTuning::default(),
 61:     };
 62: 
 63:     for pair in query.trim_start_matches('?').split('&') {
 64:         let Some((key, value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
 65:             continue;
 66:         };
 67:         let knob = |t: &mut f32| {
 68:             if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<f32>() {
 69:                 if v.is_finite() {
 70:                     *t = v.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
 71:                 }
 72:             }
 73:         };
 74:         let ranged = |t: &mut f32, min: f32, max: f32| {
 75:             if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<f32>() {
 76:                 if v.is_finite() {
 77:                     *t = v.clamp(min, max);
 78:                 }
 79:             }
 80:         };
 81:         match key {
 82:             "seed" => {
 83:                 params.seed = value.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(|_| hash_seed(value));
 84:             }
 85:             "voxel_size" => {
 86:                 params.voxel_size = value.parse::<f32>().ok().filter(|v| v.is_finite());
 87:             }
 88:             "pillars" => knob(&mut params.tuning.pillars),
 89:             "walls" => knob(&mut params.tuning.walls),
 90:             "atria" => knob(&mut params.tuning.atria),
 91:             "lights" => knob(&mut params.tuning.lights),
 92:             // World provisioning: drink, food, and level-door frequency.
 93:             // 0 removes that class of content entirely.
 94:             "almond_water" => knob(&mut params.tuning.almond_water),
 95:             "rations" => knob(&mut params.tuning.rations),
 96:             "level_doors" => knob(&mut params.tuning.level_doors),
 97:             "anomalies" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.frequency),
 98:             "anomaly_size" => ranged(&mut params.anomalies.size, 0.5, 2.0),
 99:             "pillar_expanses" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.pillar_expanses),
100:             "blackouts" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.blackouts),
101:             "red_rooms" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.red_rooms),
102:             "pit_lattices" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.pit_lattices),
103:             "remap_intensity" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.remap_intensity),
104:             "remap_distance" => ranged(&mut params.anomalies.remap_distance, 4.0, 64.0),
105:             "anomaly_safe_radius" => ranged(&mut params.anomalies.safe_radius, 4.0, 32.0),
106:             // Gameplay tuning: the probability per closed-loop epoch that a
107:             // red room hashes a single far-side escape breach. 0 seals every
108:             // loop, 1 guarantees a breach; it is never the entrance.
109:             "red_escape_bias" => ranged(&mut params.anomalies.red_escape_bias, 0.0, 1.0),
110:             "archways" => knob(&mut params.anomalies.archways),
111:             // Deception: the fraction of blackout glimmers placed one
112:             // segment off the recovery skeleton. The default is high on
113:             // purpose — most glimmers lie.
114:             "blackout_decoys" => ranged(&mut params.anomalies.blackout_decoys, 0.0, 0.9),
115:             // Debug: guarantee one anomaly of this family on the spawn's
116:             // macro cell (settings menu "Spawn anomaly"). Unknown values
117:             // leave the world untouched.
118:             "force_anomaly" => {
119:                 params.anomalies.forced_kind = match value {
120:                     "pillars" => Some(AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse),
121:                     "blackout" => Some(AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse),
122:                     "pits" => Some(AnomalyKind::PitLattice),
123:                     "archway" => Some(AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom),
124:                     "redroom" => Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom),
125:                     _ => None,
126:                 };
127:             }
128:             _ => {}
129:         }
130:     }
131:     params
132: }
133: 
134: /// Seed + generator configuration derived from the URL query. The main
135: /// thread and every generation worker call this with the same query string,
136: /// so all of them voxelize the identical world by construction.
137: pub fn generator_setup_from_query(query: &str, default_seed: u32) -> (u32, GeneratorConfig) {
138:     let params = parse_generation_params(query, default_seed);
139:     let base = if has_exact_pair(query, "spec", "high") {
140:         GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
141:     } else {
142:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
143:     };
144:     let configured = base
145:         .with_tuning(params.tuning)
146:         .with_anomalies(params.anomalies);
147:     let configured = params
148:         .voxel_size
149:         .and_then(|voxel_size| configured.try_with_voxel_size(voxel_size).ok())
150:         .unwrap_or(configured);
151:     (params.seed, configured)
152: }
153: 
154: fn has_exact_pair(query: &str, expected_key: &str, expected_value: &str) -> bool {
155:     query
156:         .trim_start_matches('?')
157:         .split('&')
158:         .filter_map(|pair| pair.split_once('='))
159:         .any(|(key, value)| key == expected_key && value == expected_value)
160: }
161: 
162: /// Non-numeric seeds ("?seed=kitten") hash to a stable u32 (FNV-1a).
163: fn hash_seed(text: &str) -> u32 {
164:     let mut h: u32 = 0x811C_9DC5;
165:     for b in text.bytes() {
166:         h ^= b as u32;
167:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
168:     }
169:     h
170: }

   1: //! # wasm_frontend — browser client for the vackrooms voxel engine
   2: //!
   3: //! This crate is the *outer rings* of the engine's Clean Architecture when it
   4: //! runs in a browser. The dependency rule points strictly inward:
   5: //!
   6: //! ```text
   7: //! drivers (web-sys, WebGL2, DOM)        <- wasm32 only
   8: //!    |
   9: //! adapters (input mapping, SVO atlas, local chunk source)
  10: //!    |
  11: //! application (player physics, streaming policy, frame orchestration, ports)
  12: //!    |
  13: //! vackrooms core (entities + use cases: VoxelGrid, SVO, generation, lighting)
  14: //! ```
  15: //!
  16: //! * `application` and `adapters` are platform-agnostic and unit-tested with
  17: //!   plain `cargo test` on the host.
  18: //! * `drivers` is the only module that talks to the browser, and it is only
  19: //!   compiled for `wasm32`.
  20: //! * The `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` entry point below is the composition root:
  21: //!   it wires concrete drivers into the application's ports.
  22: 
  23: pub mod adapters;
  24: pub mod application;
  25: pub mod core;
  26: 
  27: pub mod drivers;
  28: 
  29: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  30: use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, Ordering};
  31: 
  32: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  33: pub static DOOM_CONTROLS: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
  34: 
  35: /// Mouse look inversion (Y axis).
  36: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  37: pub static INVERT_Y: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
  38: 
  39: /// Mouse sensitivity multiplier, stored as f32 bits. 1.0 = default.
  40: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  41: pub static MOUSE_SENSITIVITY_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x3F80_0000); // 1.0f32
  42: 
  43: /// Manual internal-resolution override as f32 bits; 0.0 = automatic
  44: /// (adaptive governor).
  45: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  46: pub static RENDER_SCALE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
  47: 
  48: /// Anomaly debug overlay visibility (settings switch and the F3 key).
  49: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  50: pub static ANOMALY_DEBUG: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

  52: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  53: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
  54: pub fn set_anomaly_debug(enabled: bool) {
  55:     ANOMALY_DEBUG.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
  56: }

  58: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  59: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
  60: pub fn set_doom_controls(enabled: bool) {
  61:     DOOM_CONTROLS.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
  62: }
  63: 
  64: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  65: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
  66: pub fn set_invert_y(enabled: bool) {

  70: /// Mouse/touch look sensitivity multiplier (clamped to 0.1–5.0).
  71: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  72: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
  73: pub fn set_mouse_sensitivity(multiplier: f32) {
  74:     let m = if multiplier.is_finite() {
  75:         multiplier.clamp(0.1, 5.0)
  76:     } else {
  77:         1.0
  78:     };
  79:     MOUSE_SENSITIVITY_BITS.store(m.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
  80: }
  81: 
  82: /// Forces the internal render resolution scale (0.25–1.0), or restores the
  83: /// adaptive governor when `scale` is 0.
  84: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  85: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
  86: pub fn set_render_scale(scale: f32) {
  87:     let s = if scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0 {
  88:         scale.clamp(0.25, 1.0)
  89:     } else {
  90:         0.0
  91:     };
  92:     RENDER_SCALE_BITS.store(s.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
  93: }

  95: /// CPU render settings are atomics only at the browser boundary. Every
  96: /// public setter rebuilds and validates a typed `CpuRenderSettings` snapshot;
  97: /// the splatter itself never reads these globals.
  98: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
  99: pub static CPU_SCALE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x3F80_0000); // 1.0f32
 100: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 101: pub static CPU_LOD_CUTOFF_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x3F80_0000); // 1.0f32
 102: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 103: pub static CPU_MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x4100_0000); // 8.0f32
 104: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 105: pub static CPU_MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(5);
 106: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 107: pub static CPU_MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x3E80_0000); // 0.25f32
 108: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 109: pub static CPU_MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x42C0_0000); // 96.0f32
 110: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 111: pub static CPU_SHADOWS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
 112:

 118:     use crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuQualityPreset;
 119:     store_cpu_settings(CpuQualityPreset::from_id(preset_id).settings());
 120: }
