 176: /// Renderer optimization toggles as a bitfield — see
 177: /// [`application::render_settings::RenderToggles`]. Initialized from the URL
 178: /// query at boot; the settings menu flips individual switches afterwards.
 179: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 180: pub static RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(u32::MAX);
 181: 
 182: /// Flips one renderer optimization switch by name (`"hiz"`, `"f2b"`,
 183: /// `"skip"`, `"mips"`, `"beam_occlusion"`, `"shadows"`, `"cells"`,
 184: /// `"deferred"`, `"ao"`, `"cull"`, `"budget"`, `"dither"`, `"bake"`,
 185: /// `"timer"`). Unknown names
 186: /// are ignored.
 187: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 188: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 189: pub fn set_render_toggle(name: &str, enabled: bool) {
 190:     let mut toggles = get_render_toggles();
 191:     toggles.set(name, enabled);
 192:     RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.store(toggles.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 193: }
 194: 
 195: /// Returns one renderer switch by its short URL name. This small diagnostic
 196: /// export lets the settings UI and browser smoke tests verify the effective
 197: /// state after URL and local-preference overrides have been composed.
 198: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 199: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 200: pub fn render_toggle_enabled(name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
 201:     get_render_toggles().enabled(name)
 202: }
 203: 
 204: /// Snapshot of the toggle switchboard, taken once per frame by each driver
 205: /// and passed by value into the platform-free render code.
 206: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 207: pub fn get_render_toggles() -> crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles {
 208:     let bits = RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
 209:     if bits == u32::MAX {
 210:         crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles::default()
 211:     } else {
 212:         crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles::from_bits(bits)
 213:     }
 214: }
 215: 
 216: /// Boot-time initialization from the URL query (`?rt_<name>=0|1`).
 217: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 218: pub fn init_render_toggles(query: &str) {
 219:     let toggles = crate::application::render_settings::parse_render_toggles(query);
 220:     RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.store(toggles.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 221: }
 222: 
 223: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 224: pub fn get_cpu_settings() -> crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings {
 225:     let scale = f32::from_bits(CPU_SCALE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 226:     let lod_cutoff = f32::from_bits(CPU_LOD_CUTOFF_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 227:     let max_splat_radius = f32::from_bits(CPU_MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 228:     let max_virtual_depth = CPU_MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as u8;
 229:     let min_mip_occupancy =
 230:         f32::from_bits(CPU_MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 231:     let max_draw_dist = f32::from_bits(CPU_MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 232:     let shadow_mode = CPU_SHADOWS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
 233: 
 234:     crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings {
 235:         internal_scale: scale,
 236:         lod_cutoff_px: lod_cutoff,
 237:         max_splat_radius_px: max_splat_radius,
 238:         max_virtual_depth,
 239:         min_mip_occupancy,
 240:         max_draw_distance: max_draw_dist,
 241:         shadows: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuShadowMode::from_id(shadow_mode),
 242:         ..crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings::default()
 243:     }
 244:     .validated()
 245: }
 246: 
 247: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 248: fn update_cpu_settings(update: impl FnOnce(&mut crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings)) {
 249:     let mut settings = get_cpu_settings();
 250:     update(&mut settings);
 251:     store_cpu_settings(settings);
 252: }
 253: 
 254: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 255: fn store_cpu_settings(settings: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings) {
 256:     let settings = settings.validated();
 257:     CPU_SCALE_BITS.store(settings.internal_scale.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 258:     CPU_LOD_CUTOFF_BITS.store(settings.lod_cutoff_px.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 259:     CPU_MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_BITS.store(settings.max_splat_radius_px.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 260:     CPU_MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.store(settings.max_virtual_depth as u32, Ordering::Relaxed);
 261:     CPU_MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY_BITS.store(settings.min_mip_occupancy.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 262:     CPU_MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE_BITS.store(settings.max_draw_distance.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 263:     CPU_SHADOWS.store(settings.shadows.id(), Ordering::Relaxed);
 264: }
 265: 
 266: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 267: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 268: pub fn get_blueprint_svg(seed: u32, rx: i32, rz: i32, voxel_scale: f32, size_world: f32) -> String {
 269:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 270:     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 271:         seed,
 272:         vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(rx as f32 * size_world, rz as f32 * size_world),
 273:         size_world,
 274:         &vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
 275:         &noise,
 276:     );
 277:     let chunk_size = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 { 20.0 } else { 10.0 };
 278:     let mut chunk_bounds = Vec::new();
 279:     let steps = (size_world / chunk_size).round() as i32;
 280:     for i in 0..steps {
 281:         for j in 0..steps {
 282:             let min_x = rx as f32 * size_world + i as f32 * chunk_size;
 283:             let min_z = rz as f32 * size_world + j as f32 * chunk_size;
 284:             let chunk_coord_x = (min_x / chunk_size).round() as i64;
 285:             let chunk_coord_z = (min_z / chunk_size).round() as i64;
 286:             chunk_bounds.push(vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::ChunkBounds {
 287:                 min_x,
 288:                 min_z,
 289:                 max_x: min_x + chunk_size,
 290:                 max_z: min_z + chunk_size,
 291:                 label: format!("[{}, {}]", chunk_coord_x, chunk_coord_z),
 292:             });
 293:         }
 294:     }
 295: 
 296:     let options = vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintOptions {
 297:         pixels_per_unit: 10.0,
 298:         show_chunk_grid: true,
 299:         show_fixtures: true,
 300:         show_structure: true,
 301:         seed,
 302:         level: 0,
 303:         voxel_scale,
 304:     };
 305:     vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::render_region_blueprint_svg(
 306:         &plan,
 307:         &chunk_bounds,
 308:         options,
 309:     )
 310: }
 311: 
 312: /// Compact geometry feed for the canvas debug map. This deliberately returns
 313: /// planning primitives rather than SVG so the page can redraw cheaply while
 314: /// panning, zooming, or changing overlays.
 315: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 316: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 317: pub fn get_debug_region_json(seed: u32, region_x: i32, region_z: i32) -> String {
 318:     use std::fmt::Write;
 319:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::SpaceProgram;
 320: 
 321:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 322:     let size = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 323:     let origin =
 324:         vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(region_x as f32 * size, region_z as f32 * size);
 325:     let config = vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 326:     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 327:         seed, origin, size, &config, &noise,
 328:     );
 329:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(8192);
 330:     write!(
 331:         out,
 332:         "{{\"origin\":[{:.1},{:.1}],\"size\":{:.1},\"walls\":[",
 333:         origin.x, origin.z, size
 334:     )
 335:     .unwrap();
 336:     let mut first = true;
 337:     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 338:         let vertices = &assembly.footprint.vertices;
 339:         for pair in vertices
 340:             .iter()
 341:             .zip(vertices.iter().cycle().skip(1))
 342:             .take(vertices.len())
 343:         {
 344:             if !first {
 345:                 out.push(',');
 346:             }
 347:             first = false;
 348:             write!(
 349:                 out,
 350:                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1}]",
 351:                 pair.0.0, pair.0.1, pair.1.0, pair.1.1
 352:             )
 353:             .unwrap();
 354:         }
 355:     }
 356:     out.push_str("],\"corridors\":[");
 357:     first = true;
 358:     for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 359:         for pair in corridor.path.windows(2) {
 360:             if !first {
 361:                 out.push(',');
 362:             }
 363:             first = false;
 364:             write!(
 365:                 out,
 366:                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1}]",
 367:                 pair[0].x, pair[0].z, pair[1].x, pair[1].z, corridor.width
 368:             )
 369:             .unwrap();
 370:         }
 371:     }
 372:     out.push_str("],\"lights\":[");
 373:     first = true;
 374:     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 375:         for fixture in &assembly.fixtures {
 376:             if !first {
 377:                 out.push(',');
 378:             }
 379:             first = false;
 380:             write!(
 381:                 out,
 382:                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{}]",
 383:                 fixture.at.x, fixture.at.z, fixture.half_x, fixture.half_z, fixture.lit
 384:             )
 385:             .unwrap();
 386:         }
 387:     }
 388:     out.push_str("],\"rooms\":[");
 389:     first = true;
 390:     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 391:         let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 392:         if !first {
 393:             out.push(',');
 394:         }
 395:         first = false;
 396:         let kind = match assembly.program {
 397:             SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => "corridor",
 398:             SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "abandoned",
 399:             _ => "room",
 400:         };
 401:         write!(
 402:             out,
 403:             "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},\"{}\"]",
 404:             b.0, b.1, b.2, b.3, kind
 405:         )
 406:         .unwrap();
 407:     }
 408:     out.push_str("],\"anomalies\":[");
 409:     first = true;
 410:     for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 411:         if !first {
 412:             out.push(',');
 413:         }
 414:         first = false;
 415:         let b = anomaly.footprint.bounds();
 416:         write!(
 417:             out,
 418:             "[\"{:?}\",\"{:016x}\",{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{}]",
 419:             anomaly.kind,
 420:             anomaly.id,
 421:             b.min_x,
 422:             b.min_z,
 423:             b.max_x,
 424:             b.max_z,
 425:             anomaly.gates.len(),
 426:         )
 427:         .unwrap();
 428:     }
 429:     out.push_str("]}");
 430:     out
 431: }
 432: 
 433: /// Debug payload for one generated chunk: a compact material slice plus the
 434: /// plan objects that explain why those voxels were placed.
 435: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 436: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 437: pub fn get_debug_chunk_json(seed: u32, chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32, voxel_scale: f32) -> String {
 438:     use std::fmt::Write;
 439:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::SpaceProgram;
 440:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 441:         VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR,
 442:         VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_PALE_WALL, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
 443:         VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_WATER,
 444:     };
 445: 
 446:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 447:     let config = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 {
 448:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 449:     } else {
 450:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 451:     };
 452:     let chunk_origin = vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z);
 453:     let generator =
 454:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 455:     let grid = generator.execute(chunk_origin, seed, config.clone());
 456:     let region_size = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 457:     let region_origin = vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(
 458:         (chunk_x / region_size).floor() * region_size,
 459:         (chunk_z / region_size).floor() * region_size,
 460:     );
 461:     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 462:         seed,
 463:         region_origin,
 464:         region_size,
 465:         &config,
 466:         &noise,
 467:     );
 468:     let width = grid.width().saturating_sub(2);
 469:     let depth = grid.depth().saturating_sub(2);
 470:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(width * depth + 4096);
 471:     write!(
 472:         out,
 473:         "{{\"origin\":[{:.1},{:.1}],\"scale\":{:.3},\"width\":{},\"depth\":{},\"cells\":\"",
 474:         chunk_x, chunk_z, voxel_scale, width, depth
 475:     )
 476:     .unwrap();
 477:     // One top-down material per column. Priority keeps red lights and walls
 478:     // visible while still exposing floor/ceiling coverage in the same slice.
 479:     for z in 0..depth {
 480:         for x in 0..width {
 481:             let mut material = b'.';
 482:             for y in 0..grid.height() {
 483:                 material = match grid.get(x + 1, y, z + 1) {
 484:                     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => b'R',
 485:                     VOXEL_LIGHT => b'L',
 486:                     VOXEL_GLIMMER => b'g',
 487:                     VOXEL_RED_WALL => b'X',
 488:                     VOXEL_WALL | VOXEL_TREE => b'#',
 489:                     VOXEL_PALE_WALL => b'P',
 490:                     VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL => b'D',
 491:                     VOXEL_CEILING => {
 492:                         if material == b'.' {
 493:                             b'^'
 494:                         } else {
 495:                             material
 496:                         }
 497:                     }
 498:                     VOXEL_FLOOR | VOXEL_GRASS | VOXEL_WATER => {
 499:                         if material == b'.' {
 500:                             b'_'
 501:                         } else {
 502:                             material
 503:                         }
 504:                     }
 505:                     VOXEL_DRY_CARPET => {
 506:                         if material == b'.' {
 507:                             b','
 508:                         } else {
 509:                             material
 510:                         }
 511:                     }
 512:                     VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET | VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET => {
 513:                         if material == b'.' {
 514:                             b'~'
 515:                         } else {
 516:                             material
 517:                         }
 518:                     }
 519:                     VOXEL_FLUID => {
 520:                         if material == b'.' {
 521:                             b'w'
 522:                         } else {
 523:                             material
 524:                         }
 525:                     }
 526:                     _ => material,
 527:                 };
 528:             }
 529:             out.push(material as char);
 530:         }
 531:     }
 532:     out.push_str("\",\"corridors\":[");
 533:     let mut first = true;
 534:     for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 535:         for pair in corridor.path.windows(2) {
 536:             if !first {
 537:                 out.push(',');
 538:             }
 539:             first = false;
 540:             write!(
 541:                 out,
 542:                 "[{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{}]",
 543:                 (pair[0].x - chunk_x) / voxel_scale,
 544:                 (pair[0].z - chunk_z) / voxel_scale,
 545:                 (pair[1].x - chunk_x) / voxel_scale,
 546:                 (pair[1].z - chunk_z) / voxel_scale,
 547:                 corridor.width / voxel_scale,
 548:                 if corridor.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor {
 549:                     0
 550:                 } else {
 551:                     1
 552:                 }
 553:             )
 554:             .unwrap();
 555:         }
 556:     }
 557:     out.push_str("],\"boxes\":[");
 558:     first = true;
 559:     let mut box_out = |kind: &str, label: &str, bounds: (f32, f32, f32, f32), color: u8| {
 560:         if !first {
 561:             out.push(',');
 562:         }
 563:         first = false;
 564:         write!(
 565:             out,
 566:             "[\"{}\",\"{}\",{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{}]",
 567:             kind,
 568:             label,
 569:             (bounds.0 - chunk_x) / voxel_scale,
 570:             (bounds.1 - chunk_z) / voxel_scale,
 571:             (bounds.2 - bounds.0) / voxel_scale,
 572:             (bounds.3 - bounds.1) / voxel_scale,
 573:             color
 574:         )
 575:         .unwrap();
 576:     };
 577:     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 578:         let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 579:         let label = match assembly.program {
 580:             SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "ABANDONED",
 581:             _ => "ASSEMBLY",
 582:         };
 583:         box_out("assembly", label, b, 0);
 584:         for space in &assembly.spaces {
 585:             box_out("space", "SUB-ROOM", space.footprint.bounds(), 0);
 586:         }
 587:         for ceiling in &assembly.ceiling_zones {
 588:             box_out("ceiling", "CEILING ZONE", ceiling.area.bounds(), 0);
 589:         }
 590:         let s = &assembly.structure;
 591:         let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 592:         box_out(
 593:             "structure",
 594:             "COLUMN GRID",
 595:             (b.0 + s.phase.0, b.1 + s.phase.1, b.2, b.3),
 596:             0,
 597:         );
 598:         for opening in &assembly.entrances {
 599:             let half = opening.width * 0.5;
 600:             let b = if opening.through_x_wall {
 601:                 (
 602:                     opening.center.x - half,
 603:                     opening.center.z - 0.12,
 604:                     opening.center.x + half,
 605:                     opening.center.z + 0.12,
 606:                 )
 607:             } else {
 608:                 (
 609:                     opening.center.x - 0.12,
 610:                     opening.center.z - half,
 611:                     opening.center.x + 0.12,
 612:                     opening.center.z + half,
 613:                 )
 614:             };
 615:             box_out("portal", "PORTAL", b, 0);
 616:         }
 617:     }
 618:     for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 619:         let b = anomaly.footprint.bounds();
 620:         let label = match anomaly.kind {
 621:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => "PILLAR EXPANSE",
 622:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => "BLACKOUT",
 623:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PitLattice => "PIT LATTICE",
 624:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::RedRoom => "RED LOOP",
 625:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => "ARCH ANCHOR",
 626:         };
 627:         box_out("anomaly", label, (b.min_x, b.min_z, b.max_x, b.max_z), 1);
 628:         // Anomaly-aware developer visibility: gates (threshold planes) and
 629:         // the immutable skeleton lane, keyed by instance id in the label.
 630:         for gate in anomaly.traversal_gates() {
 631:             let gb = match gate.axis {
 632:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::X => {
 633:                     (gate.plane - 0.1, gate.span_min, gate.plane + 0.1, gate.span_max)
 634:                 }
 635:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::Z => {
 636:                     (gate.span_min, gate.plane - 0.1, gate.span_max, gate.plane + 0.1)
 637:                 }
 638:             };
 639:             let glabel = format!(
 640:                 "{} {:08X}",
 641:                 match gate.kind {
 642:                     vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGateKind::Remap => "GATE",
 643:                     vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold =>
 644:                         "THRESHOLD",
 645:                     vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGateKind::RedLoop => "RED LOOP",
 646:                     vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGateKind::RedEscape => "ESCAPE",
 647:                 },
 648:                 (gate.instance_id & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32
 649:             );
 650:             box_out("gate", &glabel, gb, 1);
 651:         }
 652:         if anomaly.kind != vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::RedRoom
 653:             && anomaly.kind != vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
 654:         {
 655:             let lane_a = anomaly.world_coords(-anomaly.footprint.half_x, 0.0);
 656:             let lane_b = anomaly.world_coords(anomaly.footprint.half_x, 0.0);
 657:             let hw = anomaly.skeleton_half_width;
 658:             let lane = (
 659:                 lane_a.x.min(lane_b.x) - hw,
 660:                 lane_a.z.min(lane_b.z) - hw,
 661:                 lane_a.x.max(lane_b.x) + hw,
 662:                 lane_a.z.max(lane_b.z) + hw,
 663:             );
 664:             box_out("skeleton", "PROTECTED ROUTE", lane, 1);
 665:         }
 666:     }
 667:     out.push_str("],\"fixtures\":[");
 668:     first = true;
 669:     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 670:         for fixture in &assembly.fixtures {
 671:             if !first {
 672:                 out.push(',');
 673:             }
 674:             first = false;
 675:             write!(
 676:                 out,
 677:                 "[{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{:.2},{}]",
 678:                 (fixture.at.x - chunk_x) / voxel_scale,
 679:                 (fixture.at.z - chunk_z) / voxel_scale,
 680:                 fixture.half_x / voxel_scale,
 681:                 fixture.half_z / voxel_scale,
 682:                 fixture.lit
 683:             )
 684:             .unwrap();
 685:         }
 686:     }
 687:     out.push_str("]}");
 688:     out
 689: }
 690: 
 691: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 692: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 693: pub fn get_chunk_blueprint_svg(
 694:     seed: u32,
 695:     chunk_x: f32,
 696:     chunk_z: f32,
 697:     voxel_scale: f32,
 698:     layer: String,
 699: ) -> String {
 700:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 701:     let chunk_pos = vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z);
 702: 
 703:     let config = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 {
 704:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 705:     } else {
 706:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 707:     };
 708: 
 709:     let generator =
 710:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 711:     let grid = generator.execute(chunk_pos, seed, config);
 712: 
 713:     let region_size = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 714:     let rx = (chunk_x / region_size).floor() * region_size;
 715:     let rz = (chunk_z / region_size).floor() * region_size;
 716:     let semantics = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 717:         seed,
 718:         vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(rx, rz),
 719:         region_size,
 720:         &config,
 721:         &noise,
 722:     );
 723: 
 724:     let slice = match layer.as_str() {
 725:         "floor" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::FloorPlan,
 726:         "wall" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::WallPlan,
 727:         "ceiling" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::CeilingPlan,
 728:         _ => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::Composite,
 729:     };
 730: 
 731:     vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::render_voxel_chunk_svg(
 732:         &grid,
 733:         chunk_pos,
 734:         &config,
 735:         slice,
 736:         Some(&semantics),
 737:     )
 738: }
 739: 
 740: /// Fast single-chunk voxel blueprint with semantic overlays.
 741: ///
 742: /// Why fast? This renders only one 50×50 (or 200×200 for high-spec) voxel
 743: /// grid instead of stitching N×N chunks, so it completes in < 5 ms inside
 744: /// WASM.  The browser can call this on every keypress without delay.
 745: ///
 746: /// Arguments (all passed from JavaScript):
 747: /// * `seed`          – World seed.
 748: /// * `chunk_x`       – Chunk origin X in world units (chunk_index * chunk_size).
 749: /// * `chunk_z`       – Chunk origin Z in world units.
 750: /// * `voxel_scale`   – Metres per voxel (0.2 default, 0.1 high-spec).
 751: /// * `pixels_per_voxel` – SVG pixels per cell (8–12 is comfortable).
 752: /// * `show_grid`     – Draw hairline grid lines.
 753: /// * `show_semantics`– Draw corridor / room / door overlays.
 754: /// * `show_ceiling`  – Include ceiling and light voxels.
 755: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 756: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 757: pub fn get_chunk_voxel_blueprint_svg(
 758:     seed: u32,
 759:     chunk_x: f32,
 760:     chunk_z: f32,
 761:     voxel_scale: f32,
 762:     pixels_per_voxel: f32,
 763:     show_grid: bool,
 764:     show_semantics: bool,
 765:     show_ceiling: bool,
 766: ) -> String {
 767:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 768:     let chunk_pos = vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z);
 769: 
 770:     let config = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 {
 771:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 772:     } else {
 773:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 774:     };
 775: 
 776:     // Generate the voxel grid for this single chunk.
 777:     let generator =
 778:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 779:     let grid = generator.execute(chunk_pos, seed, config.clone());
 780: 
 781:     // Generate the region plan covering this chunk (for semantic overlays).
 782:     let region_size = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 783:     let rx = (chunk_x / region_size).floor() * region_size;
 784:     let rz = (chunk_z / region_size).floor() * region_size;
 785:     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 786:         seed,
 787:         vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(rx, rz),
 788:         region_size,
 789:         &config,
 790:         &noise,
 791:     );
 792: 
 793:     let options = vackrooms::adapters::chunk_voxel_renderer::VoxelBlueprintOptions {
 794:         pixels_per_voxel: pixels_per_voxel.max(4.0).min(20.0),
 795:         show_grid,
 796:         show_voxels: true,
 797:         show_semantics,
 798:         show_labels: show_semantics, // labels only make sense when boxes are visible
 799:         show_ceiling,
 800:     };
 801: 
 802:     vackrooms::adapters::chunk_voxel_renderer::render_chunk_voxel_blueprint_svg(
 803:         &grid,
 804:         &plan,
 805:         chunk_pos,
 806:         voxel_scale,
 807:         options,
 808:     )
 809: }
 810: 
 811: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 812: #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 813: pub fn get_large_voxel_blueprint_svg(
 814:     seed: u32,
 815:     rx_val: i32,
 816:     rz_val: i32,
 817:     voxel_scale: f32,
 818:     size_world: f32,
 819:     layer: String,
 820: ) -> String {
 821:     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 822: 
 823:     let config = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 {
 824:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 825:     } else {
 826:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 827:     };
 828: 
 829:     let chunk_size = config.chunk_size;
 830:     let steps = (size_world / chunk_size).round() as i32;
 831: 
 832:     // Generate the region plan
 833:     let rx_origin = rx_val as f32 * size_world;
 834:     let rz_origin = rz_val as f32 * size_world;
 835:     let semantics = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 836:         seed,
 837:         vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(rx_origin, rz_origin),
 838:         size_world,
 839:         &config,
 840:         &noise,
 841:     );
 842: 
 843:     // Generate all chunks and combine them
 844:     let generator =
 845:         vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 846: 
 847:     let chunk_w = (chunk_size / voxel_scale).round() as usize;
 848:     let chunk_d = (chunk_size / voxel_scale).round() as usize;
 849: 
 850:     let total_w = steps as usize * chunk_w;
 851:     let total_d = steps as usize * chunk_d;
 852: 
 853:     let mut combined_cells = vec![0u8; total_w * total_d];
 854: 
 855:     let slice = match layer.as_str() {
 856:         "floor" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::FloorPlan,
 857:         "wall" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::WallPlan,
 858:         "ceiling" => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::CeilingPlan,
 859:         _ => vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::Composite,
 860:     };
 861: 
 862:     for i in 0..steps {
 863:         for j in 0..steps {
 864:             let chunk_x = rx_origin + i as f32 * chunk_size;
 865:             let chunk_z = rz_origin + j as f32 * chunk_size;
 866:             let grid = generator.execute(
 867:                 vackrooms::entities::models::Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z),
 868:                 seed,
 869:                 config.clone(),
 870:             );
 871: 
 872:             // Copy chunk voxels to combined grid
 873:             for cz in 0..chunk_d {
 874:                 for cx in 0..chunk_w {
 875:                     let vx = cx + 1;
 876:                     let vz = cz + 1;
 877: 
 878:                     let mut has_wall = false;
 879:                     let mut has_red_wall = false;
 880:                     let mut has_light = false;
 881:                     let mut has_red_light = false;
 882:                     let mut has_floor = false;
 883:                     let mut has_ceiling = false;
 884:                     let mut has_tree = false;
 885:                     let mut has_grass = false;
 886:                     let mut has_water = false;
 887: 
 888:                     for y in 0..grid.height() {
 889:                         match grid.get(vx, y, vz) {
 890:                             1 => has_wall = true,
 891:                             5 => has_red_wall = true,
 892:                             4 => has_light = true,
 893:                             9 => has_red_light = true,
 894:                             2 => has_floor = true,
 895:                             3 => has_ceiling = true,
 896:                             8 => has_tree = true,
 897:                             6 => has_grass = true,
 898:                             7 => has_water = true,
 899:                             _ => {}
 900:                         }
 901:                     }
 902: 
 903:                     let cell_type = match slice {
 904:                         vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::FloorPlan => {
 905:                             if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
 906:                                 if has_red_wall { 2 } else { 1 }
 907:                             } else if has_floor || has_grass || has_water {
 908:                                 if has_water {
 909:                                     7
 910:                                 } else if has_grass {
 911:                                     6
 912:                                 } else {
 913:                                     5
 914:                                 }
 915:                             } else {
 916:                                 0
 917:                             }
 918:                         }
 919:                         vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::WallPlan => {
 920:                             if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
 921:                                 if has_red_wall { 2 } else { 1 }
 922:                             } else {
 923:                                 0
 924:                             }
 925:                         }
 926:                         vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::CeilingPlan => {
 927:                             if has_light || has_red_light {
 928:                                 if has_red_light { 4 } else { 3 }
 929:                             } else if has_ceiling {
 930:                                 9
 931:                             } else {
 932:                                 0
 933:                             }
 934:                         }
 935:                         vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintSlice::Composite => {
 936:                             if has_wall || has_red_wall || has_tree {
 937:                                 if has_red_wall { 2 } else { 1 }
 938:                             } else if has_light || has_red_light {
 939:                                 if has_red_light { 4 } else { 3 }
 940:                             } else if has_floor || has_grass || has_water {
 941:                                 if has_water {
 942:                                     7
 943:                                 } else if has_grass {
 944:                                     6
 945:                                 } else {
 946:                                     5
 947:                                 }
 948:                             } else {
 949:                                 0
 950:                             }
 951:                         }
 952:                     };
 953: 
 954:                     let target_x = i as usize * chunk_w + cx;
 955:                     let target_z = j as usize * chunk_d + cz;
 956:                     let idx = target_z * total_w + target_x;
 957:                     combined_cells[idx] = cell_type;
 958:                 }
 959:             }
 960:         }
 961:     }
 962: 
 963:     vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::render_large_voxel_blueprint_svg(
 964:         &combined_cells,
 965:         total_w,
 966:         total_d,
 967:         rx_origin,
 968:         rz_origin,
 969:         voxel_scale,
 970:         size_world,
 971:         slice,
 972:         Some(&semantics),
 973:         false,
 974:     )
 975: }
 976: 
 977: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 978: mod entry {
 979:     use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
 980: 
 981:     /// Composition root. Runs automatically when the wasm module is
 982:     /// instantiated by `static/index.html`.
 983:     ///
 984:     /// `static/worker.js` instantiates this same module inside a Web Worker
 985:     /// with `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` skipped (`init` is passed
 986:     /// `{ skip_start: true }` is not available for start fns, so instead the
 987:     /// worker checks for a missing DOM and bails out here).
 988:     #[wasm_bindgen(start)]
 989:     pub fn start() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
 990:         console_error_panic_hook::set_once();
 991:         // Inside a Web Worker there is no `window`/DOM: this module was
 992:         // loaded as the generation worker, which drives itself through
 993:         // `worker_init`/`worker_generate` instead of `boot`.
 994:         if web_sys::window().is_none() {
 995:             return Ok(());
 996:         }
 997:         crate::drivers::browser::boot()
 998:     }
 999: }
1000: 
1001: /// Generation-worker entry points. A worker is a second instance of this
1002: /// same wasm module: `worker_init` builds a chunk source from the *same*
1003: /// URL query the main thread used (identical world by construction), and
1004: /// `worker_generate` runs the full chunk pipeline — architectural
1005: /// generation, voxel diffuse bake, greedy mesh + face instances, SVO build and
1006: /// serialization, collision extraction — returning one transferable byte
1007: /// buffer (see `adapters::chunk_codec`).
1008: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
1009: mod worker_entry {
1010:     use std::cell::RefCell;
1011: 
1012:     use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
1013: 
1014:     use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::encode_chunk_payload;
1015:     use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
1016:     use crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query;
1017:     use crate::application::ports::ChunkSourcePort;
1018:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
1019:     use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
1020: 
1021:     thread_local! {
1022:         static SOURCE: RefCell<Option<LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>>> =
1023:             const { RefCell::new(None) };
1024:     }
1025: 
1026:     /// `default_seed` must match the main thread's `WORLD_SEED`.
1027:     #[wasm_bindgen]
1028:     pub fn worker_init(query: &str, default_seed: u32) {
1029:         let (seed, config) = generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
1030:         SOURCE.with(|s| {
1031:             *s.borrow_mut() = Some(LocalChunkSource::new(
1032:                 SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
1033:                 seed,
1034:                 config,
1035:             ));
1036:         });
1037:     }
1038: 
1039:     #[wasm_bindgen]
1040:     pub fn worker_generate(
1041:         _request_id: u32,
1042:         origin_x: f32,
1043:         origin_z: f32,
1044:         level: u32,
1045:         lod: u8,
1046:         reality_words: Vec<u32>,
1047:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
1048:         let reality = RealitySnapshot::from_words(&reality_words)
1049:             .expect("worker_generate received an invalid reality snapshot");
1050:         SOURCE.with(|s| {
1051:             let source = s.borrow();
1052:             let source = source
1053:                 .as_ref()
1054:                 .expect("worker_generate called before worker_init");
1055:             encode_chunk_payload(
1056:                 &source.load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, &reality),
1057:             )
1058:         })
1059:     }
1060: }
````

## File: ARCHITECTURE.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms — Architecture
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine built on **Clean Architecture**, targeting
  4: low-spec hardware. The whole engine — procedural generation, lighting, sparse
  5: voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, player physics, and
  6: rendering — compiles to a single WebAssembly module. The browser
  7: runs it; a zero-dependency native HTTP server merely serves the files (or, on
  8: GitHub Pages, static files alone — the wasm engine generates chunks entirely
  9: client-side and needs no server).
 10: 
 11: ## Rendering family
 12: 
 13: `RendererPort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`) has four
 14: implementations, selected at runtime by `create_renderer`
 15: (`wasm_frontend/src/drivers/browser.rs`) from the `?renderer=` query param:
 16: 
 17: | `?renderer=` | Driver | Approach |
 18: |---|---|---|
 19: | *(default)* | `surface_webgl::SurfaceRenderer` | Indexed greedy meshes, WebGL2 fixed-function depth. The SVO is retained per chunk for collision/debug only — no fragment shader walks it. |
 20: | `splat` | `splat_webgl::SplatRenderer` | Instanced face-splat "microvoxel" path: one GPU instance per visible surface rectangle, lit once in the vertex shader; the retained mesh is drawn only into the shadow map. |
 21: | `raymarch` | `webgl::WebGl2Renderer` | The hybrid SVO raymarcher described below — a per-fragment octree walk. |
 22: | `cpu` | `cpu_canvas::CpuCanvasRenderer` | Software rasterizer (`adapters::cpu_splatter`) blitted via `ImageData`; no WebGL context at all. |
 23: 
 24: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` fall back (to CPU, or to surfaces)
 25: if WebGL2 or the requested backend fails to initialize.
 26: 
 27: Renderer code is organized by lifetime and responsibility rather than by one
 28: backend-sized class:
 29: 
 30: | Module | Responsibility |
 31: |---|---|
 32: | `drivers/surface_webgl/` | `draw_lit_world_surfaces`, `upload_world_surface_chunks`, and renderer composition |
 33: | `drivers/splat_webgl/{mod,resources,draw}.rs` | splat composition, instance/shadow resources, staged frame pipeline |
 34: | `drivers/webgl/` | `draw_voxel_scene`, `upload_voxel_atlas`, and raymarch composition |
 35: | `adapters/cpu_splatter/` | atlas decode, camera, cone light, ray queries, shading, raster traversal, tests |
 36: | `adapters/cpu_splatter/settings/` | typed CPU quality presets, one validated scalar model, and explicit flashlight/fixture visibility policies |
 37: | `drivers/gl/` | context/program setup, matrices, light selection, shadow targets, timers, visibility |
 38: | `drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/` | reconstruct surfaces → sample optional diffuse field → shade visible surface |
 39: | `drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/` | decode atlas → intersect voxel scene → shade nearest hit |
 40: | `drivers/shaders/{evaluate_scene_lighting,apply_distance_fog,encode_display_color}.rs` | shared linear-light, Beer–Lambert, and display equations |
 41: 
 42: Optional shortcuts are plain data in `application::render_settings::RenderToggles`.
 43: Each driver snapshots that switchboard once per frame; inner algorithms never
 44: read browser globals. The same switches are available live in Settings →
 45: Optimize and as shareable `?rt_<name>=0|1` query parameters.
 46: 
 47: The CPU composition root separately snapshots `CpuRenderSettings`. Its named
 48: presets change only bounded workload/quality scalars (resolution, distant LOD,
 49: splat radius, virtual depth, sparse-MIP threshold, range, and fixture-shadow
 50: policy). They do not mutate `RenderToggles`. The CPU canvas resolution factor
 51: is applied before both the canvas and software framebuffer are resized, so a
 52: reduced render always covers the full CSS viewport instead of filling only a
 53: corner of a larger backing store.
 54: 
 55: CPU fixture visibility is an explicit three-level policy. `off` is the fast
 56: unoccluded diagnostic, `hero` amortizes one real fixture-center segment, and
 57: `full` is the radiometric reference: every point endpoint and every one of a
 58: rectangle's four Gauss endpoints traces a finite SVO segment. CPU MIPs average
 59: linear albedo and colored bake values; ordinary LOD never collapses a subtree
 60: containing emission, while the hard work-cap fallback retains aggregate
 61: emissive coverage/radiance instead of deleting the panel.
 62: 
 63: The `raymarch` backend is a correctness-first SVO ray caster with two explicit
 64: stepping policies over the same stateless point lookup and hit record:
 65: 
 66: 1. **Chunk intervals** — robust parallel-safe slabs produce entry/exit
 67:    intervals. Near-to-far traversal may stop only when every remaining AABB
 68:    starts beyond the nearest solid hit; padded chunk cubes may overlap.
 69: 2. **Reference traversal (`rt_skip=0`)** — exact finest-cell 3-D DDA. Voxel
 70:    size and SVO depth come from each payload; neither is inferred from its
 71:    power-of-two padded world size.
 72: 3. **Empty-leaf traversal (`rt_skip=1`)** — restart from the root for each
 73:    sample, then jump to the exact exit of a masked octant or empty leaf. No
 74:    mutable descent stack survives a jump.
 75: 4. **Shading** — sRGB material values are decoded to linear RGB, ceiling
 76:    panels use a downward one-sided rectangular-emitter integral. The
 77:    raymarcher intentionally rejects the bake's face-independent leaf value;
 78:    when `rt_shadows=1`, each of the rectangle integral's four samples traces
 79:    an SVO visibility segment through every resident chunk. Beer–Lambert fog
 80:    is composed in linear space before one shared tone-map/sRGB conversion.
 81: 
 82: The default surface renderer evaluates the same analytic fixture list. Static
 83: fixtures and runtime flares use separate uniform arrays, so dropping a flare
 84: cannot evict a ceiling panel. `rt_bake` defaults off and never removes analytic
 85: lights; on the surface renderer it enables the deliberately approximate,
 86: quantized diffuse-fill field. Surface visibility is also an explicit raster
 87: approximation: `rt_shadows=1` provides one shadow map for the highest-priority
 88: fixture. The raymarcher is the strict all-fixture visibility reference.
 89: 
 90: There is no global fixture budget in either rewritten GPU path. The complete,
 91: deduplicated fixture list lives in an RGBA32F texture; a conservative
 92: finite-support intersection builds contiguous per-surface or per-chunk
 93: clusters. Clustering changes only which provably zero-contribution lights are
 94: skipped, not the lighting equation or the set of contributing fixtures.
 95: 
 96: Low-spec strategy: the raymarcher uses one fullscreen pass, the surface path
 97: uses the hardware depth buffer, neither requests MSAA, SVO data stays in
 98: nearest-filtered integer textures, and an **adaptive internal-resolution
 99: governor** (0.5×–1.0× backing store, hysteresis + cooldown) replaces temporal
100: checkerboarding.
101: 
102: ## The dependency rule
103: 
104: Source dependencies point inward only. No inner layer names a browser, GPU,
105: socket, or clock.
106: 
107: ```
108: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
109: │ FRAMEWORKS & DRIVERS                                               │
110: │   wasm_frontend/drivers   WebGL2, DOM events, rAF, HUD, console    │
111: │   src/main.rs             native HTTP server (std::net only)      │
112: │   src/frameworks_drivers  SimpleNoiseProvider, StdTelemetry        │
113: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
114: │  │ INTERFACE ADAPTERS                                           │  │
115: │  │   src/adapters            OctreeGpuSerializer, VoxelMapper,  │  │
116: │  │                           JsonPresenter                      │  │
117: │  │   src/interface_adapters  WebRendererAdapter (presenters)    │  │
118: │  │   wasm_frontend/adapters  InputCollector, LocalChunkSource   │  │
119: │  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
120: │  │  │ USE CASES (application business rules)                 │  │  │
121: │  │  │   src/use_cases           GenerateChunk + ports        │  │  │
122: │  │  │   src/domain/use_cases    BuildOctree, lighting, maze  │  │  │
123: │  │  │   wasm_frontend/application  Engine (frame loop),      │  │  │
124: │  │  │      Player, CollisionWorld, StreamingPolicy, atlas    │  │  │
125: │  │  │      + ports (RendererPort, ChunkSourcePort)           │  │  │
126: │  │  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │  │
127: │  │  │  │ ENTITIES (enterprise business rules)             │  │  │  │
128: │  │  │  │   VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree, Position, Grid   │  │  │  │
129: │  │  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │  │
130: │  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
131: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
132: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
133: ```
134: 
135: ### Crates
136: 
137: | Crate | Role | Targets |
138: |---|---|---|
139: | `vackrooms` (root) | Entities + use cases + adapters; native dev-server binary | native **and** wasm32 |
140: | `wasm_frontend` | Browser client: application/adapters (portable) + drivers (wasm-only) | wasm32 (pure layers test natively) |
141: | `wasm_raycaster` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment | kept for reference |
142: 
143: The split inside `wasm_frontend` is enforced mechanically: `web-sys`,
144: `js-sys` and `wasm-bindgen` are `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")']`
145: dependencies, and `drivers/` is `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`. A native
146: `cargo test` therefore cannot even *see* browser types — the compiler is the
147: architecture cop.
148: 
149: ### Ports (dependency inversion boundaries)
150: 
151: | Port | Defined in (inner) | Implemented by (outer) |
152: |---|---|---|
153: | `NoiseProvider` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `SimpleNoiseProvider` |
154: | `TelemetryPort` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `StdTelemetry` (native stdout), `ConsoleTelemetry` (browser console), `NullTelemetry` (tests) |
155: | `RendererPort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `SurfaceRenderer` (default), `SplatRenderer`, `WebGl2Renderer` (raymarch), `CpuCanvasRenderer`, recording fakes (tests) |
156: | `ChunkSourcePort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `LocalChunkSource` (synchronous, in-wasm generation), `WorkerChunkSource` (pooled Web Worker generation, default); an HTTP-fetching implementation would slot in without touching the engine |
157: 
158: ## Data flow: from noise to pixel
159: 
160: The SVO atlas path below feeds the `raymarch` backend directly; the default
161: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` consume the same lit `VoxelGrid` but
162: greedy-mesh or face-splat it instead of walking the octree per fragment (the
163: SVO they receive is used for collision only).
164: 
165: ```
166: SimpleNoiseProvider (driver)
167:       │ NoiseProvider port
168:       ▼
169: GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase ──► VoxelGrid (dense u8 grid + light grid)
170:       │                                   │
171:       │                          bake_voxel_lighting (world-unit air paths)
172:       ▼                                   ▼
173: BuildOctreeUseCase ──────────────► SparseVoxelOctree
174:       │                              (arena Vec<SvoNode>, uniform-collapsed)
175:       ▼
176: OctreeGpuSerializer ─────────────► RGBA32UI texel stream, rows of 1024,
177:       │                              row-padded per chunk
178:       ▼
179: application::atlas::build_atlas ─► merged atlas + per-chunk rebased roots
180:       │ RendererPort port
181:       ▼
182: WebGl2Renderer ──────────────────► RGBA32UI texture + uniform chunk table
183:       ▼
184: fragment shader (drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/) — fullscreen quad,
185: robust chunk intervals, DDA or empty-leaf stepping ──► pixels
186: ```
187: 
188: Collision geometry is derived **from the same SVO** (solid WALL/RED_WALL
189: leaves → world-space AABBs in `local_chunk_source::extract_collision_boxes`),
190: so physics and visuals can never drift apart. Uniform subtrees collapsed by
191: the SVO become single large collision boxes for free.
192: 
193: ### SVO node texel encoding (RGBA32UI, one node per texel)
194: 
195: | Channel | Internal node (`R == 0`) | Leaf node (`R == 1`) |
196: |---|---|---|
197: | R | 0 | 1 |
198: | G | `child_base_index` (children contiguous at +0..+7) | `voxel_type` |
199: | B | `child_mask` (bit *i* set = child *i* non-empty) | 24-bit `0xRRGGBB` color |
200: | A | 0 | scalar light 0–15, face-occlusion bits, and RGB light 0–15/channel |
201: 
202: The same layout is documented at its source of truth,
203: `src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`, and decoded in
204: `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/decode_voxel_atlas.rs`.
205: 
206: ## Level 0: architecture first
207: 
208: Level 0 is a **world-planning system**, not a random room generator. Math
209: selects architectural *intentions*; it never substitutes for them. Planning
210: descends a strict scale hierarchy, each level constraining the next:
211: 
212: ```
213: world seed
214:   -> MacroFields         multi-octave parameter fields (world_topology)
215:     -> MacroCell graph   160 u cells: nodes, portals, red-room events,
216:                          vertical links (use_cases/world_topology.rs)
217:       -> RegionPlan      80 u architectural plan (use_cases/region_plan/)
218:         -> ColumnPlan    one voxel column (use_cases/level_zero/)
219:           -> VoxelGrid   resolution-dependent output (level_zero/voxelize.rs)
220: ```
221: 
222: **Fractal math's one job.** `world_topology::sample_fields` sums three
223: noise octaves per parameter (`F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ·N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`) into `[0, 1]`
224: fields — `openness`, `vertical_pressure`, `institution_age`,
225: `anomaly_pressure`, `redroom_pressure`, `style_blend`. Fields only bias
226: probabilities and style choices (where the building's rules change); a
227: planner still decides every corridor, room, stair, and threshold. This is
228: what makes billions of areas *differ* without ever placing a wall by noise.
229: 
230: **The macro graph.** `plan_macro_cell(seed, cell, red_room_scale, noise)`
231: is a pure function returning one 160 u `MacroCell`: a `WorldNode` per
232: region (classified `Warren` / `OpenPlate` / `Atrium` / `Stairwell` /
233: `RedRoomEncounter`), shared-edge `Portal`s (both neighbors of an edge
234: derive the identical crossing — the infinite-corridor contract),
235: `VerticalLink` stair reservations, and at most one `RedRoomEvent`. A 5×5
236: graph snapshot test pins the exact topology of seed 42: an unintentional
237: world change fails the build.
238: 
239: **Red rooms are graph events, not a biome.** Events are planned on the
240: macro lattice by a deterministic local tournament: a candidate cell fires
241: only if no candidate within the separation radius beats its score, so any
242: two encounters keep a cooldown distance (≥ 3 regions), clustered where
243: `redroom_pressure` runs high. The region planner merely *realizes* an event
244: that targets its region by promoting one occupied, reachable assembly.
245: 
246: **Vertical circulation.** `vertical_link_for_region` reserves stairwells
247: where `vertical_pressure` is high: `OrdinaryStair` and `EndlessAscent`
248: links are realized by `use_cases/vertical_circulation.rs` as compact Stair
249: assemblies beside the main spine — a lit vestibule, a monotonic flight of
250: 0.2 u treads (raised floor voxelizes as solid, so it collides), and either
251: a landing or an endless climb into an unlit 5.4 u shaft. Elevation is an
252: integer story index on `WorldNode`; `EndlessDescent` / `ServiceShaft`
253: links stay graph reservations until the engine can stream below elevation
254: 0 and the player gains vertical physics (see roadmap).
255: 
256: **Archways are topological connectors.** A `Transition` arch room carries
257: an `ArchBehavior`: most are plain `Anchor`s, but a `CultureSeam`'s far
258: half changes ceiling regime, floor grammar, and lintel height, and a
259: `ScaleBreach`'s far half repeats the same grammar larger. The seam is
260: expressed only through legal architectural vocabulary — never impossible
261: collision or repainted walls.
262: 
263: Both stages are split by intent, one module per planning concern:
264: `use_cases/region_plan/` (genome, circulation, suites, corruption, debug)
265: and `use_cases/level_zero/` (fabric, circulation_sampler, assembly_sampler,
266: compose_column, generate, column_field, voxelize). Within one region, the
267: planner works as follows:
268: 
269: 1. **Region plans.** The world tiles into fixed 80 u regions. A pure function
270:    of `(seed, region)` derives 1–3 `ArchitectGenome`s (circulation style,
271:    structural system, proportions, threshold/ceiling/lighting languages,
272:    renovation history), routes one dominant 4.8–7.2 u primary spine between
273:    shared edge portals (so it chains across regions forever), then adds at
274:    most two 3.6–5.0 u interior branches. It attaches incomplete, 12–24 u
275:    `AssemblyInstance` masses beside that circulation rather than tiling the
276:    region with rooms. Thresholds are selected per assembly: narrow lintelled
277:    doors are rare; most fronts use a broad or unframed portal.
278: 2. **Corruption.** A final pass makes the sane plan Backrooms: suites repeat
279:    with misaligned copies, one assembly becomes an unlit
280:    `AbandonedExpansion` shell, renovations overlay contradictory column
281:    grids.
282: 3. **Voxelization.** `BackroomsLevel` samples the plan per voxel column with
283:    priority *corridor → assembly → fabric*: corridors carve open under
284:    3.4–4.2 u (primary) or 3.0–3.6 u (secondary) ceilings; assemblies retain
285:    long perimeter runs and sparse partitions; everything between is a sparse
286:    18 u wall fabric that dissolves into open space. A broad ceiling field
287:    holds the visual baseline at 3.2–3.6 u, with 3.8–4.4 u expanses, 4.5–5.4 u
288:    vaults, and rare 2.5–2.8 u compression zones. This keeps cheap office
289:    finishes at an implausible scale instead of producing a low office maze.
290: 
291: **The Peripheral Shift.** "Whenever not directly observed, the layout can
292: warp, stretch, or rearrange itself." `RealitySnapshot` (RTY v3) carries one
293: drift epoch per 40 u fabric cell. The epoch re-salts only the fabric's
294: cosmetic and porosity decisions — wall dropout, doorway
295: direction/position/framing, dead lights — read at each deciding lattice
296: cell's own anchor, so walls rebuild whole and the binary-tree doorway rule
297: (hence global connectivity) holds at any epoch mix. Corridors, portals,
298: assemblies, anomaly identities, arch-anchor surroundings, and the spawn
299: opening sequence never drift: navigation survives; hallway memory does not.
300: The engine advances epochs two ways: territory abandoned beyond the
301: streaming footprint (plus hysteresis) drifts on departure, and *inside a
302: blackout* the shift runs in real time — cells wholly behind the player's
303: facing, beyond any light's reach, and fully inside the blackout advance on
304: a slow cadence and force-rebuild in place, hidden by the dark.
305: 
306: **Fixture decay and flicker.** The `institution_age` field steers the
307: fabric's dead-light ratio (young wings ~1.15x survival, ancient wings
308: ~0.6x). A deterministic share of warm panels carries a `flicker_mode`
309: authored at light collection (tired-ballast shimmer, dying tubes); the
310: engine pre-flickers intensity CPU-side once per frame, like flares, so all
311: renderers agree and no shader needs a clock.
312: 
313: All plan geometry snaps to a 0.4 u lattice (one coarse voxel) so every LOD
314: of a chunk voxelizes the same architecture. Debug hook:
315: `cargo run --example dump_plan` prints region plans as ASCII;
316: `debug_region_ascii` renders any plan.
317: 
318: ### Infinite generation and anomalies
319: 
320: The generation code is organized by the language of Level 0, rather than by
321: delivery mechanism:
322: 
323: ```
324: world_topology (macro fields, graph events, portals, vertical links)
325:         │
326: InfiniteRegionWindow ──► RegionPlan(s) ──► architectural ColumnPlan
327:                                                 │
328: anomalies/{planning,geometry} ──────────────────┤
329: red_rooms/{planning,geometry,recursive_level} ──┤
330: vertical_circulation (stair profiles) ──────────┘
331:                                                 │
332:                                       ColumnField (1-column halo)
333:                                                 │
334:                                       voxelize_columns ──► VoxelGrid
335: ```
336: 
337: - `domain/entities/anomaly/` contains only domain language: rectilinear
338:   geometry, immutable anomaly instances, traversal semantics, and canonical
339:   reality snapshots. The public `anomaly` namespace remains stable.
340:   `domain/entities/world_topology.rs` holds the macro-graph language
341:   (`MacroCell`, `WorldNode`, `Portal`, `VerticalLink`, `MacroFields`).
342: - `use_cases/anomalies/` plans and samples macro anomaly families on the
343:   same 160 u lattice as the world graph; per-anchor chance is weighted by
344:   the `anomaly_pressure` field, so anomalies arrive in loose
345:   constellations, never a uniform sprinkle.
346:   `use_cases/red_rooms/` owns the assembly-derived encounter and its recursive
347:   Level 0 address. The old `anomaly_plan` module is only a compatibility
348:   facade. The pre-planning `?level=1` generator lives untouched in
349:   `use_cases/legacy_blueprint.rs`, consulted by nothing in Level 0.
350: - `InfiniteRegionWindow` is the finite query cache for an infinite region
351:   lattice. A missing plan is an error instead of silently falling back to an
352:   unrelated region.
353: - A committed Red Room derives its branch seed and region-aligned translation
354:   with integer hashes over the full 64-bit anomaly id. Planning and sampling
355:   use that same address, so worker order, chunk boundaries, and floating-point
356:   id precision cannot select different worlds.
357: - `ColumnField` and `voxelize_columns` are resolution-dependent output stages.
358:   World planning never reads the requested output extent; generating one 20 u
359:   area or four 10 u areas produces the same voxels at matching coordinates.
360: 
361: Reality is part of chunk identity. Entering a Red Room changes the active
362: infinite Level 0 address, so all resident chunks are atomically scheduled for
363: replacement; partially repainting only the vestibule would splice two worlds
364: at a streaming boundary.
365: 
366: ### Generation invariants (enforced by tests)
367: 
368: Massive procedural worlds only work when randomness is constrained. These
369: contracts are non-negotiable and each is asserted natively:
370: 
371: - The same seed, coordinates, LOD, and reality always produce identical
372:   geometry; the 5×5 macro-graph snapshot digest pins seed 42's topology.
373: - Neighboring regions independently compute the same shared portals, and
374:   the primary route crosses every region boundary (corridors chain forever).
375: - Every assembly entrance opens onto a corridor; sealed masses are
376:   intentional (`AbandonedExpansion`), never accidents.
377: - Stair flights rise monotonically from a flat entrance, keep ≥ 2.2 u of
378:   headroom over every tread, and reach their declared landing.
379: - Red-room events keep a minimum separation radius; a red room never
380:   produces red masonry — only red light over ordinary architecture.
381: - World planning never reads the requested output extent: one 20 u query
382:   and four 10 u queries produce the same voxels at matching coordinates.
383: 
384: ## Chunk streaming
385: 
386: Chunk generation runs on a pool of Web Workers (`WorkerChunkSource`,
387: `static/worker.js` — each a second instance of the same wasm module). The
388: pure `GenerationWorkerPreference` policy accepts `?workers=auto|0|1..4`:
389: `auto` reserves one reported hardware thread and caps the pool at four,
390: explicit counts are clamped to reported hardware and the four-worker product
391: cap, while `0` selects the synchronous in-thread `LocalChunkSource`. That
392: local source is also the automatic fallback if worker startup fails. These workers parallelize chunk
393: generation, lighting, meshes, SVO serialization, and collision extraction;
394: they do **not** parallelize any renderer, including the CPU splatter. Either
395: way, the resident set
396: itself is **time-sliced** and **progressive**: `StreamingPolicy` produces the
397: desired resident set (nearest-first) each frame, and the `Engine` spends a
398: per-tick cost budget on it in two phases:
399: 
400: 1. **Availability** — every missing chunk first loads at a *coarse LOD*
401:    (voxels 2× the size, ~1/8 the generation/lighting/SVO cost, ~1 budget
402:    unit), so the whole footprint renders after roughly one tick instead of
403:    trickling in chunk by chunk.
404: 2. **Refinement** — leftover budget reloads the nearest coarse chunk *within
405:    `fine_distance`* at full resolution, replacing it in place (same atlas
406:    slot, partial row upload). Chunks beyond `fine_distance` stay coarse: at
407:    that range a coarse voxel projects to about the same pixels as a fine one
408:    — a screen-space-error LOD. Refinement is monotonic while resident, so
409:    the LOD choice never flaps.
410: 
411: Every LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`GeneratorConfig::at_lod`
412: halves the SVO depth as it doubles `voxel_scale`), and cell borders/door
413: positions derive from world space, so a coarse chunk is a faithful low-res
414: proxy of its fine version and payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
415: The atlas texture and collision world are rebuilt only on a resident-set
416: change — steady-state frames upload nothing (asserted by
417: `steady_state_does_not_reupload_atlas`).
418: 
419: Profiles (selected by URL, `?spec=high`):
420: 
421: | | chunk size | radius | voxels (fine/coarse) | SVO depth | fine ring |
422: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
423: | low (default) | 10 u | 1 (3×3) | 0.2 / 0.4 u | 6 / 5 | 15 u (all 9) |
424: | high | 20 u | 2 (5×5) | 0.1 / 0.2 u | 8 / 7 | 25 u (~9 of 25) |
425: 
426: `?voxel_size=` overrides the fine voxel edge independently of the streaming
427: profile. `GeneratorConfig::try_with_voxel_size` is the single validator used
428: by the browser and every worker: the value must be finite and positive, tile
429: the chunk edge at both fine and progressive half-resolution LOD, fit the
430: renderer-wide depth-eight SVO contract, and remain
431: inside the measured dense-grid budget including the lateral halo. The UI
432: offers 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, and 0.05 u. The 10 u profile rejects 0.4 u because its
433: 25-cell axis cannot be halved exactly; the 20 u profile rejects 0.05 u because
434: it would require depth nine. Every chunk payload transports its exact voxel size
435: and depth, so neither renderer reverse-engineers them from padded bounds.
436: 
437: The shader's chunk table is fixed at 25 entries — exactly the 5×5 high-spec
438: worst case (`application::atlas::MAX_CHUNKS`).
439: 
440: ## Player simulation
441: 
442: `application::player` ports the original client's tuning 1:1: exponential
443: friction (8 s⁻¹), acceleration 4 u/s² (terminal 0.5 u/s), mouse sensitivity
444: 0.002 rad/px, pitch clamped short of ±90°. Collision is **axis-separated
445: sliding**: X and Z are moved and tested independently against the
446: `CollisionWorld`, so hitting a wall diagonally slides along it. `dt` is
447: clamped to 100 ms so a background-tab hitch cannot teleport the player
448: through a wall.
449: 
450: ## Testing strategy
451: 
452: Ports make the interesting logic natively testable — no browser, no GPU:
453: 
454: - `cargo test --workspace` covers entities, generation (including the
455:   macro-graph snapshot, red-room separation, stair-flight, and arch-seam
456:   invariants), lighting equations and bake invariants, octree build/serialize,
457:   plus the front end's player physics, sliding collision, streaming policy,
458:   atlas rebasing, input mapping, and the resolution governor.
459: - Renderer/chunk-source **test doubles** verify the engine's contract with
460:   its ports (upload counts, draw-table sizes) rather than pixels.
461: - Playwright GPU references require visible panel emission and lit room
462:   geometry, exercise exact raymarched occlusion, and compare every decoded
463:   pixel when correctness-preserving traversal/culling optimizations are
464:   toggled live over the same resident scene.
465: 
466: ## Native dev server
467: 
468: `src/main.rs` is a zero-dependency HTTP server used for local development:
469: static files with correct MIME types (`application/wasm` is mandatory for
470: streaming instantiation), plus the legacy JSON/binary chunk endpoints
471: (`/maze`, `/octree`) that the preserved Three.js client (`/legacy`) still
472: consumes. The wasm client needs no data endpoints at all.
473: 
474: ## Roadmap (documented non-goals of this iteration)
475: 
476: - **Vertical streaming**: chunks keyed by `(x, z, elevation)` so
477:   `EndlessDescent` / `ServiceShaft` links can voxelize real destinations;
478:   player step-up and Y physics so planned flights become climbable. The
479:   topology contracts (`VerticalLink`, integer `elevation`) already exist —
480:   the endless variants should re-address the world at each landing, never
481:   mesh a literal infinite staircase.
482: - Arch seams as *portal transforms*: a `CultureSeam` crossing re-seeding
483:   the architect genome on the far side, `LoopBreach` returning near the
484:   origin under a shifted reality epoch (gate machinery exists; the arch
485:   kinds need their own `TraversalGate` semantics).
486: - Red-room progression: foreshadowing (warming/flickering fixtures across
487:   the one or two assemblies adjacent to a planned event, driven by the
488:   existing event lookup).
489: - Temporal reprojection / checkerboarding to complement adaptive resolution.
490: - Per-chunk AABB *rasterization* (BackSide boxes + `gl_FragDepth` writeback)
491:   to replace the fullscreen quad once chunk counts grow beyond 25 (`raymarch`
492:   backend only).
493: - LOD: shallower SVO mip levels for distant chunks.
````

 480:                     <option value="0">0 — synchronous fallback</option>
 481:                     <option value="1">1 generation worker</option>
 482:                     <option value="2">2 generation workers</option>
 483:                     <option value="3">3 generation workers</option>
 484:                     <option value="4">4 generation workers</option>
 485:                 </select>
 486:             </div>
 487:             <p class="hint">Workers generate and stream world chunks. They do not parallelize the CPU splat renderer; explicit counts are clamped to available hardware.</p>
 488:             <div class="setting-row">
 489:                 <label for="setting-scale">Render scale</label>
 490:                 <select id="setting-scale">
 491:                     <option value="0">Auto (adaptive)</option>
 492:                     <option value="0.5">50% — fastest</option>
 493:                     <option value="0.65">65%</option>
 494:                     <option value="0.8">80%</option>
 495:                     <option value="1">100% — sharpest</option>
 496:                 </select>
 497:             </div>
 498:             <div class="setting-row">
 499:                 <label for="setting-fov">Field of view <span class="value" id="fov-value">75&deg;</span></label>
 500:                 <input type="range" id="setting-fov" min="55" max="100" step="1" value="75">
 501:             </div>

 504:         <!-- Renderer Optimizations Tab -->
 505:         <div id="tab-optimizations" class="tab-content" style="display: none;">
 506:             <p class="hint">Each switch has a correct fallback path. Disable one at a time to isolate image or performance regressions; changes apply immediately.</p>
 507:             <div class="settings-group">
 508:                 <h3>CPU splatter</h3>
 509:                 <div class="setting-row inline-switch">

 558:                 </div>

 609:                 </div>
