````html
 619:             <p class="hint">All World rows require Apply &amp; Reload. 0 removes that content class; the guaranteed Level 1 door only vanishes at Level doors = 0.</p>
 620:         </div>
 621: 
 622:         <!-- CPU Renderer Tab -->
 623:         <div id="tab-cpu" class="tab-content" style="display: none;">
 624:             <p class="hint">The CPU canvas always fills the page. Resolution percentages control its backing pixels per axis; every traversal optimization and flashlight visibility ray remains independently switchable under Optimize.</p>
 625:             <div class="setting-row">
 626:                 <label for="setting-cpu-preset">CPU quality preset</label>
 627:                 <select id="setting-cpu-preset">
 628:                     <option value="performance">Performance — 12.5% backing</option>
 629:                     <option value="balanced">Balanced — 25% backing</option>
 630:                     <option value="quality">Quality — 37.5% backing</option>
 631:                     <option value="maximum">Maximum — 50% backing</option>
 632:                     <option value="custom">Custom</option>
 633:                 </select>
 634:             </div>
 635:             <div class="setting-row">
 636:                 <label for="setting-cpu-scale">CPU backing resolution <span class="value" id="cpu-scale-value">25%</span></label>
 637:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-scale" min="0.25" max="2.0" step="0.05" value="1.0">
 638:             </div>
 639:             <div class="setting-row">
 640:                 <label for="setting-cpu-lod">Distant LOD cutoff (px) <span class="value" id="cpu-lod-value">1.00</span></label>
 641:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-lod" min="0.25" max="2.0" step="0.05" value="1.00">
 642:             </div>
 643:             <div class="setting-row">
 644:                 <label for="setting-cpu-splat">Maximum splat radius (px) <span class="value" id="cpu-splat-value">8.0</span></label>
 645:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-splat" min="1.0" max="16.0" step="0.5" value="8.0">
 646:             </div>
 647:             <div class="setting-row">
 648:                 <label for="setting-cpu-depth">Virtual split depth <span class="value" id="cpu-depth-value">5</span></label>
 649:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-depth" min="3" max="8" step="1" value="5">
 650:             </div>
 651:             <div class="setting-row">
 652:                 <label for="setting-cpu-mip-occupancy">Sparse LOD threshold <span class="value" id="cpu-mip-occupancy-value">25%</span></label>
 653:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-mip-occupancy" min="0" max="0.5" step="0.01" value="0.25">
 654:             </div>
 655:             <div class="setting-row">
 656:                 <label for="setting-cpu-dist">Draw distance (world units) <span class="value" id="cpu-dist-value">96</span></label>
 657:                 <input type="range" id="setting-cpu-dist" min="16" max="256" step="8" value="96">
 658:             </div>
 659:             <div class="setting-row">
 660:                 <label for="setting-cpu-shadows">Fixture shadow policy</label>
 661:                 <select id="setting-cpu-shadows">
 662:                     <option value="off">Off — unshadowed direct light (fast)</option>
 663:                     <option value="hero">Hero fixture — one visibility ray</option>
 664:                     <option value="full">Full reference — every fixture sample (slow)</option>
 665:                 </select>
 666:             </div>
 667:             <p class="hint">Lower LOD cutoff and splat radius preserve finer geometry but visit more nodes. “Hero fixture” is an explicit one-light approximation. “Full reference” traces every point endpoint and all four samples of every rectangular fixture.</p>
 668:         </div>
 669: 
 670:         <!-- Debug Tab -->
 671:         <div id="tab-debug" class="tab-content" style="display: none;">
 672:             <div class="setting-row inline-switch">
 673:                 <label for="setting-anomaly-debug">Anomaly debug overlay (F3)</label>
 674:                 <input type="checkbox" id="setting-anomaly-debug">
 675:             </div>
 676:             <div class="setting-row">
 677:                 <label for="setting-force-anomaly">Spawn anomaly at spawn point <span class="value">reload</span></label>
 678:                 <select id="setting-force-anomaly">
 679:                     <option value="">None (organic only)</option>
 680:                     <option value="pillars">Pillar expanse</option>
 681:                     <option value="blackout">Blackout expanse</option>
 682:                     <option value="pits">Pit lattice</option>
 683:                     <option value="archway">Archway anchor room</option>
 684:                     <option value="redroom">Red room</option>
 685:                 </select>
 686:             </div>
 687:             <p class="hint">The forced anomaly is placed deterministically on the spawn's macro cell so every worker generates the same world. The overlay lists reality epochs, traversal gates and pit hazards near you.</p>
 688:         </div>
 689: 
 690:         <p class="hint">Controls and unmarked Graphics/CPU settings apply instantly. Rows marked “reload” require Apply &amp; Reload.</p>
 691: 
 692:         <div class="settings-actions">
 693:             <button id="fullscreen-btn">Fullscreen</button>
 694:             <button id="close-settings-btn">Close</button>
 695:             <button id="apply-settings-btn">Apply &amp; Reload</button>
 696:         </div>
 697:     </div>
 698: 
 699:     <script type="module">
 700:         import init, {
 701:             set_doom_controls,
 702:             set_mouse_sensitivity,
 703:             set_invert_y,
 704:             set_render_scale,
 705:             set_fov,
 706:             set_cpu_quality_preset,
 707:             set_cpu_scale,
 708:             set_cpu_lod_cutoff,
 709:             set_cpu_max_splat_radius,
 710:             set_cpu_virtual_depth,
 711:             set_cpu_mip_occupancy,
 712:             set_cpu_max_draw_distance,
 713:             set_cpu_shadows,
 714:             set_anomaly_debug,
 715:             set_render_toggle,
 716:         } from './pkg/wasm_frontend.js';
 717: 
 718:         const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
 719:         const overlay = $('overlay');
 720:         const settingsMenu = $('settings-menu');
 721: 
 722:         // ---- Persistence -------------------------------------------------
 723:         // Live preferences (applied instantly, saved per device).
 724:         const PREFS_KEY = 'vackrooms_prefs';
 725:         const defaultRenderToggles = {
 726:             hiz: true,
 727:             f2b: true,
 728:             skip: true,
 729:             mips: true,
 730:             beam_occlusion: true,
 731:             deferred: true,
 732:             ao: true,
 733:             shadows: true,
 734:             cells: true,
 735:             budget: true,
 736:             cull: true,
 737:             dither: true,
 738:             bake: false,
 739:             timer: true,
 740:         };
 741:         const CPU_PRESETS = Object.freeze({
 742:             performance: Object.freeze({ id: 0, scale: 0.5, lod: 1.5, splatRadius: 14.0, virtualDepth: 4, mipOccupancy: 0.35, distance: 72, shadows: 'off' }),
 743:             balanced: Object.freeze({ id: 1, scale: 1.0, lod: 1.0, splatRadius: 8.0, virtualDepth: 5, mipOccupancy: 0.25, distance: 96, shadows: 'off' }),
 744:             quality: Object.freeze({ id: 2, scale: 1.5, lod: 0.65, splatRadius: 4.0, virtualDepth: 6, mipOccupancy: 0.12, distance: 128, shadows: 'hero' }),
 745:             maximum: Object.freeze({ id: 3, scale: 2.0, lod: 0.35, splatRadius: 2.0, virtualDepth: 8, mipOccupancy: 0.05, distance: 160, shadows: 'full' }),
 746:         });
 747:         const normalizeGenerationWorkers = (value) => {
 748:             const text = String(value ?? 'auto');
 749:             if (text === 'auto' || text === '0') return text;
 750:             const requested = Number(text);
 751:             return Number.isInteger(requested) && requested > 0
 752:                 ? String(Math.min(4, requested))
 753:                 : 'auto';
 754:         };
 755:         const clampFinite = (value, min, max, fallback) => {
 756:             const number = Number(value);
 757:             return Number.isFinite(number) ? Math.min(max, Math.max(min, number)) : fallback;
 758:         };
 759:         const copyCpuPreset = (target, name) => {
 760:             const preset = CPU_PRESETS[name];
 761:             if (!preset) return false;
 762:             target.cpuPreset = name;
 763:             target.cpuScale = preset.scale;
 764:             target.cpuLod = preset.lod;
 765:             target.cpuSplat = preset.splatRadius;
 766:             target.cpuVirtualDepth = preset.virtualDepth;
 767:             target.cpuMipOccupancy = preset.mipOccupancy;
 768:             target.cpuDist = preset.distance;
 769:             target.cpuShadows = preset.shadows;
 770:             return true;
 771:         };
 772:         const sanitizeCpuPrefs = (target) => {
 773:             if (target.cpuPreset !== 'custom' && copyCpuPreset(target, target.cpuPreset)) return;
 774:             target.cpuPreset = 'custom';
 775:             target.cpuScale = clampFinite(target.cpuScale, 0.25, 2.0, 1.0);
 776:             target.cpuLod = clampFinite(target.cpuLod, 0.25, 2.0, 1.0);
 777:             target.cpuSplat = clampFinite(target.cpuSplat, 1.0, 16.0, 8.0);
 778:             target.cpuVirtualDepth = Math.round(clampFinite(target.cpuVirtualDepth, 3, 8, 5));
 779:             target.cpuMipOccupancy = clampFinite(target.cpuMipOccupancy, 0, 0.5, 0.25);
 780:             target.cpuDist = Math.round(clampFinite(target.cpuDist, 16, 256, 96) / 8) * 8;
 781:             target.cpuShadows = ['off', 'hero', 'full'].includes(target.cpuShadows)
 782:                 ? target.cpuShadows
 783:                 : 'off';
 784:         };
 785:         const defaults = {
 786:             scheme: 'modern',
 787:             sensitivity: 1.0,
 788:             invertY: false,
 789:             scale: 0,
 790:             fov: 75,
 791:             generationWorkers: 'auto',
 792:             cpuPreset: 'balanced',
 793:             cpuScale: 1.0,
 794:             cpuLod: 1.0,
 795:             cpuSplat: 8.0,
 796:             cpuVirtualDepth: 5,
 797:             cpuMipOccupancy: 0.25,
 798:             cpuDist: 96.0,
 799:             cpuShadows: 'off',
 800:             anomalyDebug: false,
 801:             renderToggles: { ...defaultRenderToggles },
 802:         };
 803:         let savedPrefs = {};
 804:         try { savedPrefs = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(PREFS_KEY) || '{}') || {}; } catch (_) {}
 805:         let prefs = { ...defaults, ...savedPrefs };
 806:         prefs.generationWorkers = normalizeGenerationWorkers(prefs.generationWorkers);
 807:         const owns = (object, key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(object, key);
 808:         // Preferences written by the former UI had scalar CPU controls but
 809:         // no preset name. Preserve those values as a custom profile.
 810:         if (!owns(savedPrefs, 'cpuPreset') && [
 811:             'cpuScale', 'cpuLod', 'cpuSplat', 'cpuDist', 'cpuShadows',
 812:         ].some((key) => owns(savedPrefs, key))) {
 813:             prefs.cpuPreset = 'custom';
 814:         }
 815:         sanitizeCpuPrefs(prefs);
 816:         // Preferences are shallow-merged above. Rebuild the nested catalog
 817:         // from the known names so new switches default on and stale/corrupt
 818:         // keys can never point at a non-existent settings control.
 819:         const savedRenderToggles = prefs.renderToggles || {};
 820:         prefs.renderToggles = Object.fromEntries(
 821:             Object.entries(defaultRenderToggles).map(([name, fallback]) => [
 822:                 name,
 823:                 typeof savedRenderToggles[name] === 'boolean'
 824:                     ? savedRenderToggles[name]
 825:                     : fallback,
 826:             ]),
 827:         );
 828:         // Migrate the old single-key scheme store.
 829:         const legacyScheme = localStorage.getItem('vackrooms_controls');
 830:         if (legacyScheme) { prefs.scheme = legacyScheme; localStorage.removeItem('vackrooms_controls'); }
 831: 
 832:         const savePrefs = () => localStorage.setItem(PREFS_KEY, JSON.stringify(prefs));
 833: 
 834:         // World/graphics-profile settings travel in the URL so worlds stay
 835:         // shareable by link.
 836:         const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
 837:         const activeGenerationWorkers = urlParams.has('workers')
 838:             ? normalizeGenerationWorkers(urlParams.get('workers'))
 839:             : prefs.generationWorkers;
 840:         if (!urlParams.has('workers') && activeGenerationWorkers !== 'auto') {
 841:             // Saved reload-required preferences must reach the Rust
 842:             // composition root before `init()` reads location.search.
 843:             urlParams.set('workers', activeGenerationWorkers);
 844:             const query = urlParams.toString();
 845:             history.replaceState(
 846:                 null,
 847:                 '',
 848:                 `${window.location.pathname}${query ? `?${query}` : ''}${window.location.hash}`,
 849:             );
 850:         }
 851:         const parseToggle = (value, fallback) => {
 852:             if (['0', 'false', 'off'].includes(value)) return false;
 853:             if (['1', 'true', 'on'].includes(value)) return true;
 854:             return fallback;
 855:         };
 856:         // Active state is deliberately separate from persisted device
 857:         // preferences: opening somebody else's diagnostic link must not make
 858:         // its overrides permanent after an unrelated settings change.
 859:         const activeRenderToggles = { ...prefs.renderToggles };
 860:         for (const name of Object.keys(defaultRenderToggles)) {
 861:             const key = `rt_${name}`;
 862:             if (urlParams.has(key)) {
 863:                 activeRenderToggles[name] = parseToggle(
 864:                     urlParams.get(key),
 865:                     activeRenderToggles[name],
 866:                 );
 867:             }
 868:         }
 869:         // URL CPU settings are active-session overrides, just like renderer
 870:         // toggles. They must not leak into device preferences when an
 871:         // unrelated live setting is saved later.
 872:         const activeCpu = { ...prefs };
 873:         const CPU_PREF_FIELDS = [
 874:             'cpuPreset', 'cpuScale', 'cpuLod', 'cpuSplat',
 875:             'cpuVirtualDepth', 'cpuMipOccupancy', 'cpuDist', 'cpuShadows',
 876:         ];
 877:         const persistActiveCpu = () => {
 878:             for (const field of CPU_PREF_FIELDS) prefs[field] = activeCpu[field];
 879:             savePrefs();
 880:         };
 881:         const cpuShadowId = (mode) => ({ off: 0, hero: 1, full: 2 })[mode] ?? 0;
 882: 
 883:         // ---- Populate the menu from current state -------------------------
 884:         $('control-scheme').value = prefs.scheme;
 885:         $('setting-sensitivity').value = prefs.sensitivity;
 886:         $('sensitivity-value').textContent = Number(prefs.sensitivity).toFixed(1);
 887:         $('setting-invert-y').checked = !!prefs.invertY;
 888:         $('setting-scale').value = String(prefs.scale);
 889:         $('setting-fov').value = prefs.fov;
 890:         $('fov-value').textContent = `${prefs.fov}°`;
 891:         $('setting-generation-workers').value = activeGenerationWorkers;
 892:         for (const [name, enabled] of Object.entries(activeRenderToggles)) {
 893:             $(`setting-rt-${name}`).checked = !!enabled;
 894:         }
 895: 
 896:         const refreshCpuControls = () => {
 897:             $('setting-cpu-preset').value = activeCpu.cpuPreset;
 898:             $('setting-cpu-scale').value = activeCpu.cpuScale;
 899:             $('cpu-scale-value').textContent = `${Math.round(activeCpu.cpuScale * 25)}%`;
 900:             $('setting-cpu-lod').value = activeCpu.cpuLod;
 901:             $('cpu-lod-value').textContent = Number(activeCpu.cpuLod).toFixed(2);
 902:             $('setting-cpu-splat').value = activeCpu.cpuSplat;
 903:             $('cpu-splat-value').textContent = Number(activeCpu.cpuSplat).toFixed(1);
 904:             $('setting-cpu-depth').value = activeCpu.cpuVirtualDepth;
 905:             $('cpu-depth-value').textContent = String(activeCpu.cpuVirtualDepth);
 906:             $('setting-cpu-mip-occupancy').value = activeCpu.cpuMipOccupancy;
 907:             $('cpu-mip-occupancy-value').textContent = `${Math.round(activeCpu.cpuMipOccupancy * 100)}%`;
 908:             $('setting-cpu-dist').value = activeCpu.cpuDist;
 909:             $('cpu-dist-value').textContent = activeCpu.cpuDist;
````

````rust
435:     pub collision: Vec<Aabb>,

437:     /// the voxel grid. The engine folds crossings into the next reality.
438:     pub traversal_gates: Vec<TraversalGate>,
439:     /// Authored floor openings with deterministic recovery destinations.
440:     pub pit_hazards: Vec<PitHazard>,
441:     /// Consumable pickups exported beside the geometry.

447: /// One background chunk-load order, echoed back verbatim with its result so
448: /// the engine can reject stale work (wrong level, chunk no longer desired,
449: /// or already refined past this LOD).
450: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
451: pub struct ChunkRequest {
452:     /// Monotonic identity assigned by the engine. A completion may only
453:     /// clear the pending entry carrying this exact id; this prevents a late
454:     /// result from an evicted/re-requested chunk from cancelling newer work.
455:     pub request_id: u32,
456:     pub origin_x: f32,
457:     pub origin_z: f32,
458:     pub level: u32,
459:     pub lod: u8,
460:     /// Immutable encounter state used to generate this chunk. It is part of
461:     /// request identity, not ambient worker state.
462:     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
463: }
464: 
465: impl ChunkRequest {
466:     /// Exact identity check for asynchronous completion validation. Origins
467:     /// compare by bits so this remains an identity operation rather than an
468:     /// approximate spatial comparison.
469:     pub fn is_same_request(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
470:         self.request_id == other.request_id
471:             && self.origin_x.to_bits() == other.origin_x.to_bits()
472:             && self.origin_z.to_bits() == other.origin_z.to_bits()
473:             && self.level == other.level
474:             && self.lod == other.lod
475:             && self.reality == other.reality
476:     }
477: }
478: 
479: /// A finished background load.
480: #[derive(Debug)]
481: pub struct CompletedChunk {
482:     pub request: ChunkRequest,
483:     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
484: }
485: 
486: /// Abstraction over where chunks come from. The browser build implements
487: /// this with in-wasm procedural generation (`adapters::local_chunk_source`)
488: /// or a Web Worker pool (`drivers::worker_source`); a networked build could
489: /// implement it with HTTP fetches instead.
490: pub trait ChunkSourcePort {
491:     /// Loads the chunk at `origin` for the given Backrooms level
492:     /// (0 = backrooms, 34 = grassland; see the core's `level_generator`).
493:     ///
494:     /// `lod` selects the level of detail: 0 is full resolution and each
495:     /// step doubles the voxel size, costing ~1/8 as much to produce. Any
496:     /// LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`world_size` invariant),
497:     /// so payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
498:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload;
499: 
500:     /// Loads against an explicit immutable reality snapshot. Stateless
501:     /// sources retain source compatibility through the default implementation;
502:     /// procedural sources override this and route the snapshot into generation.
503:     fn load_with_reality(
504:         &self,
505:         origin_x: f32,
506:         origin_z: f32,
507:         level: u32,
508:         lod: u8,
509:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
510:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
511:         let _ = reality;
512:         self.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
513:     }
514: 
515:     /// True when the source generates in the background. The engine then
516:     /// drives it with [`Self::request`]/[`Self::poll_completed`] instead of
517:     /// the blocking [`Self::load`], keeping the frame loop responsive.
518:     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
519:         false
520:     }
521: 
522:     /// Queues a background load. Deduplication is the caller's concern.
523:     fn request(&mut self, _request: ChunkRequest) {}
524: 
525:     /// Takes every finished background load. Results may arrive in any
526:     /// order and may be stale; the caller validates against its own state.
527:     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
528:         Vec::new()
529:     }
530: 
531:     /// Takes requests which the asynchronous transport definitively could
532:     /// not complete. The engine validates the full request identity before
533:     /// clearing pending state, then issues a fresh request on the same tick.
534:     /// Synchronous sources and infallible test doubles need not override it.
535:     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
536:         Vec::new()
537:     }
538: }
````

````rust
 19: /// chunk seam after rounding.

 39: /// Why a requested scene voxel size cannot be used by a generator profile.

 43:     NotPositive,

 45:     /// independently generated neighbors disagree at their shared seam.
 46:     DoesNotTileChunk {
 47:         chunk_size: f32,
 48:         voxel_size: f32,
 49:     },
 50:     DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
 51:         fine_axis_voxels: u32,
 52:         divisor: u32,
 53:     },
 54:     SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
 55:         required: u32,
 56:         maximum: u32,
 57:     },
 58:     DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
 59:         required_columns: u64,
 60:         maximum_columns: u64,
 61:     },

 72:             Self::NotPositive => write!(f, "voxel size must be greater than zero"),
 73:             Self::DoesNotTileChunk {
 74:                 chunk_size,

202:     /// Applies a user-selected scene voxel size after checking every
203:     /// invariant relied upon by chunk generation and GPU traversal.
204:     ///
205:     /// The override must be finite, positive, tile this profile's chunk edge
206:     /// with a whole number of cells, fit the renderer's SVO-depth limit, and
207:     /// stay inside the dense pre-compression memory budget. Callers should
208:     /// keep the original profile when this returns an error.
209:     pub fn try_with_voxel_size(mut self, voxel_size: f32) -> Result<Self, VoxelSizeError> {
210:         if !voxel_size.is_finite() {
211:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotFinite);
212:         }
213:         if voxel_size <= 0.0 {
214:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotPositive);
215:         }
216: 
217:         let ratio = f64::from(self.chunk_size) / f64::from(voxel_size);
218:         let axis_voxels = ratio.round();
219:         let reconstructed_chunk = axis_voxels * f64::from(voxel_size);
220:         let seam_tolerance = f64::from(self.chunk_size).abs().mul_add(1.0e-6, 1.0e-6);
221:         if axis_voxels < 1.0
222:             || !ratio.is_finite()
223:             || (reconstructed_chunk - f64::from(self.chunk_size)).abs() > seam_tolerance
224:         {
225:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileChunk {
226:                 chunk_size: self.chunk_size,
227:                 voxel_size,
228:             });
229:         }
230: 
231:         let axis_voxels = axis_voxels as u32;
232:         if axis_voxels % PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR != 0 {
233:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
234:                 fine_axis_voxels: axis_voxels,
235:                 divisor: PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR,
236:             });
237:         }
238:         let required_depth = axis_voxels
239:             .checked_next_power_of_two()
240:             .map(u32::trailing_zeros)
241:             .unwrap_or(u32::BITS);
242:         if required_depth > MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH {
243:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
244:                 required: required_depth,
245:                 maximum: MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH,
246:             });
247:         }
248: 
249:         // LocalChunkSource generates one lateral cell on each side for seam
250:         // visibility and boundary light-volume samples. Validate the real
251:         // dense allocation rather than only the cropped payload.
252:         let allocated_axis = u64::from(axis_voxels) + 2;
253:         let required_columns = allocated_axis * allocated_axis;
254:         if required_columns > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS {
255:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
256:                 required_columns,
257:                 maximum_columns: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS,
258:             });
259:         }
260: 
261:         let height_voxels =
262:             (MAX_GENERATED_HEIGHT_WORLD_UNITS / f64::from(voxel_size)).ceil() as u64 + 2;
263:         let required_voxels = required_columns
264:             .checked_mul(height_voxels)
265:             .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
266:         if required_voxels > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS {
267:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
268:                 required_voxels,
269:                 maximum_voxels: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS,
270:             });
271:         }
272: 
273:         self.voxel_scale = voxel_size;
274:         Ok(self)
275:     }
276: 
277:     /// The same chunk at a coarser level of detail: voxels double per LOD
278:     /// step, so lod 1 costs ~1/8 of lod 0 to generate, light, and serialize.
279:     /// `svo_world_size()` is invariant across LODs (half the voxels at twice
280:     /// the scale), so payloads of any LOD are interchangeable to the renderer.
281:     pub fn at_lod(mut self, lod: u8) -> Self {
282:         self.voxel_scale *= (1u32 << lod.min(4)) as f32;
283:         self
284:     }
285: 
286:     pub fn svo_depth(&self) -> u32 {
287:         let voxels = (self.chunk_size / self.voxel_scale).round().max(1.0) as u32;
288:         voxels.next_power_of_two().trailing_zeros()
289:     }
290: 
291:     pub fn svo_world_size(&self) -> f32 {
292:         let size = 1 << self.svo_depth();
293:         size as f32 * self.voxel_scale
294:     }
295: }
296: 
297: pub struct GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
298:     noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
299:     telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
300: }
301: 
302: impl<'a> GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
303:     /// Constructs the use case with silent telemetry (tests, wasm default).
304:     pub fn new(noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider) -> Self {
305:         Self {
306:             noise_provider,
307:             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
308:         }
309:     }
310: 
311:     /// Constructs the use case with an injected telemetry sink (native server,
312:     /// browser console, ...). Keeps the Dependency Rule intact: the use case
313:     /// only knows the TelemetryPort trait.
314:     pub fn with_telemetry(
315:         noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
316:         telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
317:     ) -> Self {
318:         Self {
319:             noise_provider,
320:             telemetry,
321:         }
322:     }
323: 
324:     pub fn execute(&self, chunk_pos: Position, seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> VoxelGrid {
325:         self.execute_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, &RealitySnapshot::default())
326:     }
327: 
328:     /// Generates a chunk against an immutable encounter-state snapshot.
329:     /// The snapshot is part of the request identity in the browser pipeline;
330:     /// generation itself remains pure and replayable.
331:     pub fn execute_with_reality(
332:         &self,
333:         chunk_pos: Position,
334:         seed: u32,
335:         config: GeneratorConfig,
336:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
337:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
338:         // Pluggable levels: everything except the legacy office blueprint
339:         // (level 90, kept inline below) goes through the LevelGenerator port.
340:         // Level 0 is the architecturally *planned* Backrooms: region plans
341:         // (circulation -> assemblies -> corruption) drive the voxelization.
342:         if config.level == 0 || config.level == 1 || config.level == 34 {
343:             use crate::use_cases::grassland_level::GrasslandLevel;
344:             use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
345:             use crate::use_cases::level_one::HabitableLevel;
346:             use crate::use_cases::level_zero::BackroomsLevel;
347: 
348:             let start_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros();
349:             let generator: &dyn LevelGenerator = match config.level {
350:                 0 => &BackroomsLevel,
351:                 1 => &HabitableLevel,
352:                 _ => &GrasslandLevel,
353:             };
354:             let mut grid = generator.generate_with_reality(
355:                 chunk_pos,
356:                 seed,
357:                 config,
358:                 self.noise_provider,
359:                 reality,
360:             );
361:             let lighting =
362:                 crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
363:                     config.voxel_scale,
364:                 )
365:                 .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
366:             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
367: 
368:             let elapsed_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros().saturating_sub(start_micros);
369:             self.telemetry.log(&format!(
370:                 "[TELEMETRY] level {} chunk generated. Duration={}us, Grid={}x{}x{}",
371:                 config.level,
372:                 elapsed_micros,
373:                 grid.width(),
374:                 grid.height(),
375:                 grid.depth()
376:             ));
377:             return grid;
378:         }
379: 
380:         legacy_blueprint::generate_legacy_blueprint(
381:             self.noise_provider,
382:             self.telemetry,
383:             chunk_pos,
384:             seed,
385:             config,
386:         )
387:     }
388: }

516:     #[test]
517:     fn coarse_chunk_generates_the_same_layout_smaller() {
518:         let noise = MockNoiseProvider { value: 0.0 };
519:         let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
520:         let fine = generator.execute(
521:             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
522:             42,
523:             GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES),
524:         );
525:         let coarse = generator.execute(
526:             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
527:             42,
528:             GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES).at_lod(1),
529:         );
530:         assert_eq!(coarse.width() * 2, fine.width());
531:         assert_eq!(coarse.depth() * 2, fine.depth());
532:         // Same maze at half resolution. Cell sizes truncate differently per
533:         // scale (5.0/0.4 = 12 voxels vs 25 at fine), so wall planes may land
534:         // one fine voxel off; an LOD proxy only needs walls to line up to
535:         // within that tolerance.
536:         let wall = crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
537:         let mut wall_match = 0usize;
538:         let mut wall_total = 0usize;
539:         for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
540:             for x in 0..coarse.width() {
541:                 if coarse.get(x, 1, z) != wall {
542:                     continue;
543:                 }
544:                 wall_total += 1;
545:                 let (fx, fz) = (x * 2, z * 2);
546:                 let mut near = false;
547:                 for dz in -1i32..=2 {
548:                     for dx in -1i32..=2 {
549:                         let (sx, sz) = (fx as i32 + dx, fz as i32 + dz);
550:                         if sx >= 0
551:                             && sz >= 0
552:                             && (sx as usize) < fine.width()
553:                             && (sz as usize) < fine.depth()
554:                             && fine.get(sx as usize, 1, sz as usize) == wall
555:                         {
556:                             near = true;
557:                         }
558:                     }
559:                 }
560:                 if near {
561:                     wall_match += 1;
562:                 }
563:             }
564:         }
565:         assert!(wall_total > 0, "coarse chunk must still contain walls");
566:         assert!(
567:             wall_match * 10 >= wall_total * 9,
568:             "coarse walls should lie within one fine voxel of fine walls: {wall_match}/{wall_total}"
569:         );
570:     }

709:     #[test]
710:     fn test_microbiome_zones_generation_and_contiguous() {
711:         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
712:         use crate::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
713: 
714:         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
715:         let config = GeneratorConfig::high_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES);
716:         let chunk_size = config.chunk_size;
717:         let mut zones = std::collections::HashSet::new();
718: 
719:         let seed = 42;
720:         let mut grid_zones = vec![MicrobiomeZone::Standard; 100];
721: 
722:         for cz in 0..10 {
723:             for cx in 0..10 {
724:                 let wx = 10.0 * chunk_size + (cx as f32) * 5.0;
725:                 let wz = 10.0 * chunk_size + (cz as f32) * 5.0;
726:                 let n = noise.evaluate_2d(
727:                     seed ^ 0x2b8f_a43c,
728:                     crate::entities::models::Position::new(wx * 0.05, wz * 0.05),
729:                 );
730: 
731:                 let zone = if n < -0.7 {
732:                     MicrobiomeZone::Blackout
733:                 } else if n < -0.4 {
734:                     MicrobiomeZone::Holes
735:                 } else if n > 0.85 - (config.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1) {
736:                     MicrobiomeZone::Atrium
737:                 } else if n > 0.6 {
738:                     MicrobiomeZone::PillarField
739:                 } else if n > 0.4 {
740:                     MicrobiomeZone::Arch
741:                 } else if n > 0.2 && n < 0.25 {
742:                     MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom
743:                 } else {
744:                     MicrobiomeZone::Standard
745:                 };
746: 
747:                 zones.insert(zone);
748:                 grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx] = zone;
749:             }
750:         }
751: 
752:         assert!(zones.len() >= 2, "Expected at least 2 distinct zones");
753: 
754:         let mut same_neighbor_count = 0;
755:         let mut total_neighbors = 0;
756:         for cz in 1..9 {
757:             for cx in 1..9 {
758:                 let z = grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx];
759:                 total_neighbors += 4;
760:                 if grid_zones[(cz - 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
761:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
762:                 }
763:                 if grid_zones[(cz + 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
764:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
765:                 }
766:                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx - 1] == z {
767:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
768:                 }
769:                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx + 1] == z {
770:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
771:                 }
772:             }
773:         }
774: 
775:         assert!(
776:             same_neighbor_count as f32 / total_neighbors as f32 > 0.6,
777:             "Expected zones to be highly contiguous"
778:         );
779:     }

813:     #[test]
814:     fn test_atria_tuning_knob() {
815:         let n = 0.8; // Edge case
816: 
817:         let mut config_zero = GeneratorConfig::high_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES);
818:         config_zero.tuning.atria = 0.0;
819:         let threshold_zero = 0.85 - (config_zero.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1);

822:         let mut config_high = GeneratorConfig::high_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES);
````

````rust
 64:     /// Internal-resolution multiplier (further scaled by the adaptive
 65:     /// governor). The CPU quality model owns its bounded fraction so the
 66:     /// canvas and software framebuffer always have identical dimensions;
 67:     /// CSS then presents that complete image over the viewport.
 68:     fn resolution_factor(&self) -> f64 {
 69:         match self {
 70:             DriverRenderer::Surface(_) | DriverRenderer::Splat(_) | DriverRenderer::Raymarch(_) => {
 71:                 1.0
 72:             }
 73:             DriverRenderer::Cpu(_) => crate::get_cpu_settings().canvas_resolution_factor(),
 74:         }
 75:     }

 87: /// Complete backing-store scale after the global governor/override and the
 88: /// selected renderer's own bounded workload factor are composed.
 89: fn effective_resolution_scale(renderer: &DriverRenderer, governor_scale: f32) -> f64 {
 90:     let forced =
 91:         f32::from_bits(crate::RENDER_SCALE_BITS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed));
 92:     let global_scale = if forced > 0.0 {
 93:         forced as f64
 94:     } else {
 95:         governor_scale as f64
 96:     };
 97:     global_scale * renderer.resolution_factor()
 98: }

237: /// Renderer selection: surfaces by default, `?renderer=splat` for the
238: /// instanced face-splat path (default candidate once parity/perf is
239: /// confirmed), `?renderer=raymarch` for the retained SVO debug path,
240: /// `?renderer=cpu` for software fallback.
241: fn create_renderer(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement, query: &str) -> Result<DriverRenderer, JsValue> {
242:     let renderer_choice = query_param(query, "renderer");
243:     if renderer_choice == Some("cpu") {
244:         return Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?));
245:     }
246:     if renderer_choice == Some("raymarch") {
247:         return WebGl2Renderer::new(canvas).map(DriverRenderer::Raymarch);
248:     }
249:     if renderer_choice == Some("splat") {
250:         let profile = if query_param(query, "spec") == Some("high") {
251:             SplatProfile::high()
252:         } else {
253:             SplatProfile::low()
254:         };
255:         match SplatRenderer::new(canvas, profile) {
256:             Ok(gpu) => return Ok(DriverRenderer::Splat(gpu)),
257:             Err(err) => {
258:                 web_sys::console::warn_2(
259:                     &JsValue::from_str(
260:                         "splat renderer unavailable, falling back to surface meshes:",
261:                     ),
262:                     &err,
263:                 );
264:             }
265:         }
266:     }
267:     match SurfaceRenderer::new(canvas) {
268:         Ok(gpu) => Ok(DriverRenderer::Surface(gpu)),
269:         Err(err) => {
270:             web_sys::console::warn_2(
271:                 &JsValue::from_str(
272:                     "WebGL2 surface renderer unavailable, falling back to CPU splatting:",
273:                 ),
274:                 &err,
275:             );
276:             Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?))
277:         }
278:     }
279: }

281: pub fn boot() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
282:     let window = web_sys::window().ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no window"))?;
283:     let document = window
284:         .document()
285:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no document"))?;
286: 
287:     let canvas: HtmlCanvasElement =
288:         element(&document, "view").or_else(|_| element(&document, "game-canvas"))?;
289:     let overlay: HtmlElement = element(&document, "overlay")?;
290:     let status_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "status-msg")?;
291:     let play_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "play-msg")?;
292: 
293:     // ?spec=high -> 20u chunks, 5x5 streaming radius, 0.1u voxels.
294:     // Default is the low-spec profile: 10u chunks, 3x3 radius, 0.2u voxels.
295:     // Generation controls: ?seed=… (number or any text) plus the density
296:     // knobs ?pillars= ?walls= ?atria= ?lights= (multipliers, default 1).
297:     let query = window.location().search().unwrap_or_default();
298:     web_sys::console::log_1(&format!("BOOTING ENGINE: query={}", query).into());
299:     // Renderer optimization switchboard (?rt_<name>=0|1); see
300:     // application::render_settings for the catalog of switches.
301:     crate::init_render_toggles(&query);
302:     // This resolver is also called inside every worker. Keeping the actual
303:     // GeneratorConfig behind one adapter prevents a rejected voxel override
304:     // from producing different worlds on the main and worker threads.
305:     let (resolved_seed, generator_config) = generator_setup_from_query(&query, WORLD_SEED);
306:     let high_spec = generator_config.chunk_size == GeneratorConfig::high_spec().chunk_size;
307:     // Spawn on the main corridor of region (0,0), looking east down its
308:     // west leg: the first frame is a lit, walled corridor receding into
309:     // fog — the player knows immediately that this is the Backrooms.
310:     let spawn_at = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(resolved_seed);
311:     let spawn = [spawn_at.x, 1.7, spawn_at.z];
312:     // Face east along +X.
313:     let spawn_yaw = -std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
314:     // ?level=34 boots straight into the grassland (debugging any level in
315:     // any renderer without waiting on a noclip roll).
316:     let initial_level = query_param(&query, "level")
317:         .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok())
318:         .unwrap_or(0);
319:     let engine_config = if high_spec {
320:         EngineConfig {
321:             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
322:             chunk_radius: 2,
323:             seed: resolved_seed,
324:             spawn,
325:             spawn_yaw,
326:             // 5x5 footprint: the outer ring (>= 20 units away) stays at
327:             // the coarse LOD, so high spec pays for ~9 fine chunks, not 25.
328:             fine_distance: 25.0,
329:             initial_level,
330:             ..EngineConfig::default()
331:         }
332:     } else {
333:         EngineConfig {
334:             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
335:             seed: resolved_seed,
336:             spawn,
337:             spawn_yaw,
338:             initial_level,
339:             ..EngineConfig::default()
340:         }
341:     };
342: 
343:     let renderer = Rc::new(RefCell::new(create_renderer(&canvas, &query)?));
344:     if let Some((label_rgba, label_w, label_h)) = build_label_atlas() {
345:         renderer
346:             .borrow_mut()
347:             .upload_label_atlas(&label_rgba, label_w, label_h);
348:     }
349:     if let Ok(hud_renderer) = element::<HtmlElement>(&document, "hud-renderer") {
350:         hud_renderer.set_text_content(Some(renderer.borrow().label()));
351:     }
352:     // Names the section the player is standing in (top-right HUD). The
353:     // locator re-derives the deterministic region plan, cached per region.
354:     let locator = Rc::new(RefCell::new(SectionLocator::new(
355:         resolved_seed,
356:         generator_config,
357:     )));
358:     // This pool parallelizes chunk generation/lighting/SVO construction,
359:     // never the renderer. The pure policy reserves the main thread and
360:     // clamps explicit requests to reported hardware. Zero selects the
361:     // synchronous source, which is also the worker-startup fallback.
362:     let worker_preference = parse_generation_worker_preference(&query);
363:     let hardware_concurrency = window.navigator().hardware_concurrency();
364:     let generation_worker_count = worker_preference.resolve(hardware_concurrency);
365:     let source: Box<dyn crate::application::ports::ChunkSourcePort> =
366:         if generation_worker_count == 0 {
367:             web_sys::console::log_1(&"chunk generation: synchronous main thread".into());
368:             Box::new(LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
369:                 SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
370:                 resolved_seed,
371:                 generator_config,
372:                 &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
373:             ))
374:         } else {
375:             match crate::drivers::worker_source::WorkerChunkSource::new(
376:                 &query,
377:                 WORLD_SEED,
378:                 generation_worker_count,
379:             ) {
380:                 Ok(pool) => {
381:                     web_sys::console::log_1(
382:                         &format!("chunk generation: {} worker threads", pool.pool_size()).into(),
383:                     );
384:                     Box::new(pool)
385:                 }
386:                 Err(err) => {
387:                     web_sys::console::warn_2(
388:                         &JsValue::from_str(
389:                             "worker pool unavailable, falling back to in-thread generation:",
390:                         ),
391:                         &err,
392:                     );
393:                     Box::new(LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
394:                         SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
395:                         resolved_seed,
396:                         generator_config,
397:                         &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
398:                     ))
399:                 }
400:             }
401:         };
402:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new(
403:         engine_config,
404:         Box::new(SharedRenderer(renderer.clone())),
405:         source,
406:     )));
407:     let input = Rc::new(RefCell::new(InputCollector::new()));
408:     let touch = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TouchState::default()));
409: 
410:     let is_capture = query_flag(&query, "capture");
411:     if is_capture {
412:         let mut cam_pos = spawn;
413:         if let Some(parts) = query_param(&query, "camera").map(|v| v.split(',').collect::<Vec<_>>())
414:             && parts.len() == 3
415:             && let (Ok(x), Ok(y), Ok(z)) = (
416:                 parts[0].parse::<f32>(),
417:                 parts[1].parse::<f32>(),
418:                 parts[2].parse::<f32>(),
419:             )
420:         {
421:             cam_pos = [x, y, z];
422:         }
423:         let yaw_val = query_param(&query, "yaw")
424:             .and_then(|v| v.parse::<f32>().ok())
425:             .unwrap_or(1.5708);
426:         let pitch_val = query_param(&query, "pitch")
427:             .and_then(|v| v.parse::<f32>().ok())
428:             .unwrap_or(-0.05);
429:         engine
430:             .borrow_mut()
431:             .teleport_player(cam_pos, yaw_val, pitch_val);
432:     }
433: 
434:     if !is_capture {
435:         attach_input_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
436:         attach_touch_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
437:     }
438:     run_frame_loop(
439:         window, document, canvas, overlay, status_msg, play_msg, renderer, engine, input, locator,
440:     )
441: }
442: 
443: fn element<T: JsCast>(document: &Document, id: &str) -> Result<T, JsValue> {
444:     document
445:         .get_element_by_id(id)
446:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str(&format!("missing #{id} element")))?
447:         .dyn_into::<T>()
448:         .map_err(|_| JsValue::from_str(&format!("#{id} has unexpected element type")))
449: }
450: 
451: fn attach_input_listeners(
452:     document: &Document,
453:     canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement,
454:     overlay: &HtmlElement,
455:     input: &Rc<RefCell<InputCollector>>,
456:     touch: &Rc<RefCell<TouchState>>,
457: ) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
458:     // Keyboard: KeyboardEvent.code -> MoveIntent, mapped by the input adapter.
459:     for (event, pressed) in [("keydown", true), ("keyup", false)] {
460:         let input = input.clone();
461:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(KeyboardEvent)>::new(move |e: KeyboardEvent| {
462:             // F3 toggles the anomaly debug overlay (and never reaches the
463:             // browser's own F3 find shortcut).
464:             if pressed && e.code() == "F3" {
465:                 e.prevent_default();
466:                 if !e.repeat() {
467:                     let on = crate::ANOMALY_DEBUG.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
468:                     crate::ANOMALY_DEBUG.store(!on, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
469:                 }
470:                 return;
471:             }
472:             if !e.repeat() {
473:                 input.borrow_mut().key_event(&e.code(), pressed);
474:             }
475:         });
476:         document.add_event_listener_with_callback(event, closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
477:         closure.forget();
478:     }
479: 
480:     // Mouse look (deltas are ignored by the adapter unless pointer-locked).
481:     {
482:         let input = input.clone();
483:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MouseEvent)>::new(move |e: MouseEvent| {
484:             input
485:                 .borrow_mut()
486:                 .mouse_delta(e.movement_x() as f32, e.movement_y() as f32);
487:         });
488:         document.add_event_listener_with_callback("mousemove", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
489:         closure.forget();
490:     }
491: 
492:     // Click-to-play: the overlay requests pointer lock on the render canvas.
493:     {
494:         let canvas = canvas.clone();
495:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut()>::new(move || {
496:             canvas.request_pointer_lock();
497:         });
498:         overlay.add_event_listener_with_callback("click", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
499:         closure.forget();
500:     }
501: 
502:     // Pointer-lock state drives both the input adapter and overlay
503:     // visibility — unless a touch session owns them.
504:     {
505:         let input = input.clone();
506:         let touch = touch.clone();
507:         let doc_for_closure = document.clone();
508:         let overlay = overlay.clone();
509:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut()>::new(move || {
510:             if touch.borrow().active {
511:                 return;
512:             }
513:             let locked = doc_for_closure.pointer_lock_element().is_some();
514:             input.borrow_mut().set_locked(locked);
515:             let _ = overlay
516:                 .style()
517:                 .set_property("display", if locked { "none" } else { "flex" });
518:         });
519:         document.add_event_listener_with_callback(
520:             "pointerlockchange",
521:             closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref(),
522:         )?;
523:         closure.forget();
524:     }
525: 
526:     Ok(())
527: }
528: 
529: /// Wires the touch controls: overlay tap-to-play, split-screen virtual
530: /// joystick + look surface on the canvas, and the on-screen flashlight and
531: /// menu buttons (`#btn-flashlight`, `#btn-menu`, inside `#touch-ui`).
532: fn attach_touch_listeners(
533:     document: &Document,
534:     canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement,
535:     overlay: &HtmlElement,
536:     input: &Rc<RefCell<InputCollector>>,
537:     touch: &Rc<RefCell<TouchState>>,
538: ) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
539:     let touch_ui: Option<HtmlElement> = element(document, "touch-ui").ok();
540: 
541:     let set_touch_play = {
542:         let input = input.clone();
543:         let touch = touch.clone();
544:         let overlay = overlay.clone();
545:         let touch_ui = touch_ui.clone();
546:         Rc::new(move |on: bool| {
547:             touch.borrow_mut().active = on;
548:             let mut input = input.borrow_mut();
549:             input.set_locked(on);
550:             if !on {
551:                 input.set_move_axes(0.0, 0.0);
552:             }
553:             let _ = overlay
554:                 .style()
555:                 .set_property("display", if on { "none" } else { "flex" });
556:             if let Some(ui) = &touch_ui {
557:                 let _ = ui
558:                     .style()
559:                     .set_property("display", if on { "flex" } else { "none" });
560:             }
561:         })
562:     };
563: 
564:     // Tap the overlay -> enter touch play (the desktop path uses `click` +
565:     // pointer lock instead). prevent_default suppresses the synthetic click
566:     // that would otherwise also request pointer lock.
567:     {
568:         let enter = set_touch_play.clone();
569:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(TouchEvent)>::new(move |e: TouchEvent| {
570:             e.prevent_default();
571:             enter(true);
572:         });
573:         overlay.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchend", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
574:         closure.forget();
575:     }
576: 
577:     // Canvas touches: left 45% of the screen is the movement joystick,
578:     // the rest is the look surface.
579:     {
580:         let touch = touch.clone();
581:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(TouchEvent)>::new(move |e: TouchEvent| {
582:             let mut st = touch.borrow_mut();
583:             if !st.active {
584:                 return;
585:             }
586:             e.prevent_default();
587:             let move_split = web_sys::window()
588:                 .and_then(|w| w.inner_width().ok())
589:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
590:                 .unwrap_or(800.0)
591:                 * 0.45;
592:             let changed = e.changed_touches();
593:             for i in 0..changed.length() {
594:                 let Some(t) = changed.item(i) else { continue };
595:                 let (x, y) = (t.client_x() as f64, t.client_y() as f64);
596:                 if x < move_split && st.move_id.is_none() {
597:                     st.move_id = Some(t.identifier());
598:                     st.move_origin = (x, y);
599:                 } else if st.look_id.is_none() {
600:                     st.look_id = Some(t.identifier());
601:                     st.look_last = (x, y);
602:                 }
603:             }
604:         });
605:         canvas.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchstart", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
606:         closure.forget();
607:     }
608: 
609:     {
610:         let input = input.clone();
611:         let touch = touch.clone();
612:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(TouchEvent)>::new(move |e: TouchEvent| {
613:             let mut st = touch.borrow_mut();
614:             if !st.active {
615:                 return;
616:             }
617:             e.prevent_default();
618:             let changed = e.changed_touches();
619:             for i in 0..changed.length() {
620:                 let Some(t) = changed.item(i) else { continue };
621:                 let (x, y) = (t.client_x() as f64, t.client_y() as f64);
622:                 if st.move_id == Some(t.identifier()) {
623:                     let dx = ((x - st.move_origin.0) / JOYSTICK_RADIUS).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
624:                     let dy = ((y - st.move_origin.1) / JOYSTICK_RADIUS).clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
625:                     // Screen-space up (negative dy) walks forward.
626:                     input.borrow_mut().set_move_axes(dx as f32, -dy as f32);
627:                 } else if st.look_id == Some(t.identifier()) {
628:                     let (lx, ly) = st.look_last;
629:                     st.look_last = (x, y);
630:                     input.borrow_mut().mouse_delta(
631:                         (x - lx) as f32 * TOUCH_LOOK_SCALE,
632:                         (y - ly) as f32 * TOUCH_LOOK_SCALE,
633:                     );
634:                 }
635:             }
636:         });
637:         canvas.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchmove", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
638:         closure.forget();
639:     }
640: 
641:     for event in ["touchend", "touchcancel"] {
642:         let input = input.clone();
643:         let touch = touch.clone();
644:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(TouchEvent)>::new(move |e: TouchEvent| {
645:             let mut st = touch.borrow_mut();
646:             if !st.active {
647:                 return;
648:             }
649:             e.prevent_default();
650:             let changed = e.changed_touches();
651:             for i in 0..changed.length() {
652:                 let Some(t) = changed.item(i) else { continue };
653:                 if st.move_id == Some(t.identifier()) {
654:                     st.move_id = None;
655:                     input.borrow_mut().set_move_axes(0.0, 0.0);
656:                 } else if st.look_id == Some(t.identifier()) {
657:                     st.look_id = None;
658:                 }
659:             }
660:         });
661:         canvas.add_event_listener_with_callback(event, closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
662:         closure.forget();
663:     }
664: 
665:     // On-screen buttons (optional elements; the page may omit them).
666:     if let Ok(btn) = element::<HtmlElement>(document, "btn-flare") {
667:         let input = input.clone();
668:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |e: web_sys::Event| {
669:             e.prevent_default();
670:             e.stop_propagation();
671:             input.borrow_mut().queue_flare();
672:         });
673:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchend", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
674:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("click", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
675:         closure.forget();
676:     }
677:     if let Ok(btn) = element::<HtmlElement>(document, "btn-flashlight") {
678:         let input = input.clone();
679:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |e: web_sys::Event| {
680:             e.prevent_default();
681:             e.stop_propagation();
682:             input.borrow_mut().toggle_flashlight();
683:         });
684:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchend", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
685:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("click", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
686:         closure.forget();
687:     }
688:     if let Ok(btn) = element::<HtmlElement>(document, "btn-menu") {
689:         let exit = set_touch_play.clone();
690:         let closure = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |e: web_sys::Event| {
691:             e.prevent_default();
692:             e.stop_propagation();
693:             exit(false);
694:         });
695:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("touchend", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
696:         btn.add_event_listener_with_callback("click", closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
697:         closure.forget();
698:     }
699: 
700:     Ok(())
701: }
702: 
703: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
704: fn run_frame_loop(
705:     window: Window,
706:     _document: Document,
707:     canvas: HtmlCanvasElement,
708:     _overlay: HtmlElement,
709:     status_msg: HtmlElement,
710:     play_msg: HtmlElement,
711:     renderer: Rc<RefCell<DriverRenderer>>,
712:     engine: Rc<RefCell<Engine>>,
713:     input: Rc<RefCell<InputCollector>>,
714:     locator: Rc<RefCell<SectionLocator>>,
715: ) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
716:     let hud_fps: HtmlElement = element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-fps")?;
717:     let hud_chunks: HtmlElement = element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-chunks")?;
718:     let hud_nodes: HtmlElement = element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-nodes")?;
719:     let hud_scale: HtmlElement = element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-scale")?;
720:     let hud_gpu: HtmlElement = element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-gpu")?;
721:     let hud_dist: Option<HtmlElement> =
722:         element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-dist").ok();
723:     let last_dist_text = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
724:     // Top-right section readout and the anomaly debug overlay; both are
725:     // optional page elements so older/embedded shells keep working.
726:     let hud_section: Option<HtmlElement> =
727:         element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "hud-section").ok();
728:     let last_section_text = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
729:     let debug_overlay: Option<HtmlElement> =
730:         element(window.document().as_ref().unwrap(), "debug-overlay").ok();
731:     let debug_overlay_visible = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
732: 
733:     // Survival vitals panel; optional so embedded shells keep working.
734:     let document = window.document().unwrap();
735:     let vitals_thirst: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-thirst-fill").ok();
736:     let vitals_hunger: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-hunger-fill").ok();
737:     let vitals_cond: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-cond-fill").ok();
738:     let vitals_thirst_bar: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-thirst").ok();
739:     let vitals_hunger_bar: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-hunger").ok();
740:     let vitals_inv: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "vitals-inv").ok();
741:     let death_overlay: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "death-overlay").ok();
742:     let last_deaths = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32));
743:     let death_shown_at = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
744: 
745:     let query = window.location().search().unwrap_or_default();
746:     let is_capture = query_flag(&query, "capture");
747:     // Visual baselines get fifteen settled frames; renderer smoke tests only
748:     // need proof that a loaded scene completed a couple of real draws. The
749:     // shorter path keeps deliberately unoptimized reference renderers usable
750:     // under software WebGL in CI without weakening screenshot baselines.
751:     let capture_settle_frames = if query_flag(&query, "smoke") { 2 } else { 15 };
752:     let capture_frame_counter = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32));
753: 
754:     let last_time = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
755:     let frame_count = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32));
756:     let hud_window_start = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
757:     let was_ready = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
758: 
759:     // Standard self-referential rAF closure pattern.
760:     let raf_handle: Rc<RefCell<Option<Closure<dyn FnMut(f64)>>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(None));
761:     let raf_handle_clone = raf_handle.clone();
762: 
763:     let loop_window = window.clone();
764:     *raf_handle.borrow_mut() = Some(Closure::new(move |time_ms: f64| {
765:         let dt = if is_capture {
766:             0.0
767:         } else if last_time.get() > 0.0 {
768:             ((time_ms - last_time.get()) / 1000.0) as f32
769:         } else {
770:             1.0 / 60.0
771:         };
772:         last_time.set(time_ms);
773: 
774:         // Adaptive resolution: size the backing store to
775:         // window * governor scale * renderer base factor. A non-zero
776:         // user override (settings menu) replaces the governor scale.
777:         {
778:             let scale = effective_resolution_scale(
779:                 &renderer.borrow(),
780:                 engine.borrow().stats().resolution_scale,
781:             );
782:             let target_w = (loop_window
783:                 .inner_width()
784:                 .ok()
785:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
786:                 .unwrap_or(800.0)
787:                 * scale)
788:                 .max(1.0) as u32;
789:             let target_h = (loop_window
790:                 .inner_height()
791:                 .ok()
792:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
793:                 .unwrap_or(600.0)
794:                 * scale)
795:                 .max(1.0) as u32;
796: 
797:             if canvas.width() != target_w || canvas.height() != target_h {
798:                 canvas.set_width(target_w);
799:                 canvas.set_height(target_h);
800:                 renderer.borrow_mut().resize(target_w, target_h);
801:             }
802:         }
803: 
804:         let frame_input = input.borrow_mut().take_frame();
805:         engine.borrow_mut().tick(dt, &frame_input);
806: 
807:         // Loading overlay: flip to "click to play" once the spawn chunk is in.
808:         let stats = engine.borrow().stats();
809:         if stats.ready && !was_ready.get() {
810:             was_ready.set(true);
811:             let _ = status_msg.style().set_property("display", "none");
812:             let _ = play_msg.style().set_property("display", "block");
813:         }
814: 
815:         // HUD refresh at a fixed frame cadence.
816:         frame_count.set(frame_count.get() + 1);
817:         if frame_count.get() % HUD_INTERVAL == 0 {
818:             let elapsed = (time_ms - hud_window_start.get()) / 1000.0;
819:             if elapsed > 0.0 {
820:                 let fps = (HUD_INTERVAL as f64 / elapsed).round();
821:                 hud_fps.set_text_content(Some(&fps.to_string()));
822:             }
823:             hud_window_start.set(time_ms);
824:             hud_chunks.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
825:                 "{}/{}",
826:                 stats.fine_chunks, stats.resident_chunks
827:             )));
828:             hud_nodes.set_text_content(Some(&stats.atlas_nodes.to_string()));
829:             let effective_scale =
830:                 effective_resolution_scale(&renderer.borrow(), stats.resolution_scale);
831:             hud_scale.set_text_content(Some(&format!("{:.0}%", effective_scale * 100.0)));
832:             if let Some(hud_dist) = &hud_dist {
833:                 // Restrained rounding, and only touch the DOM on change.
834:                 let text = format!("{:.0} m", stats.distance_m);
835:                 let mut last = last_dist_text.borrow_mut();
836:                 if *last != text {
837:                     hud_dist.set_text_content(Some(&text));
838:                     *last = text;
839:                 }
840:             }
841:             let gpu = renderer.borrow().gpu_frame_ms();
842:             let cpu_telemetry = renderer.borrow().cpu_telemetry_string();
843:             if let Some(text) = cpu_telemetry {
844:                 hud_gpu.set_text_content(Some(&text));
845:             } else {
846:                 hud_gpu.set_text_content(Some(
847:                     &gpu.map(|ms| format!("{ms:.1} ms"))
848:                         .unwrap_or_else(|| "n/a".to_string()),
849:                 ));
850:             }
851: 
852:             // Top-right section readout ("LEVEL 0 · MAIN CORRIDOR · ...").
853:             // The locator caches its region plan, so this is cheap except on
854:             // a region crossing; only touch the DOM when the text changes.
855:             if let Some(hud_section) = &hud_section {
856:                 let (level, pos) = {
857:                     let engine_ref = engine.borrow();
858:                     (engine_ref.level(), engine_ref.player().position)
859:                 };
860:                 let text = locator.borrow_mut().describe(level, pos[0], pos[2]);
861:                 let mut last = last_section_text.borrow_mut();
862:                 if *last != text {
863:                     hud_section.set_text_content(Some(&text));
864:                     *last = text;
865:                 }
866:             }
867: 
868:             // Survival vitals: bar widths + inventory/temperature line.
869:             if let Some(fill) = &vitals_thirst {
870:                 let _ = fill
871:                     .style()
872:                     .set_property("width", &format!("{:.0}%", stats.hydration * 100.0));
873:             }
874:             if let Some(fill) = &vitals_hunger {
875:                 let _ = fill
876:                     .style()
877:                     .set_property("width", &format!("{:.0}%", stats.satiety * 100.0));
878:             }
879:             if let Some(fill) = &vitals_cond {
880:                 let _ = fill
881:                     .style()
882:                     .set_property("width", &format!("{:.0}%", stats.condition * 100.0));
883:             }
884:             if let Some(bar) = &vitals_thirst_bar {
885:                 let _ = bar.set_class_name(if stats.hydration < 0.25 { "bar low" } else { "bar" });
886:             }
887:             if let Some(bar) = &vitals_hunger_bar {
888:                 let _ = bar.set_class_name(if stats.satiety < 0.25 { "bar low" } else { "bar" });
889:             }
890:             if let Some(inv) = &vitals_inv {
891:                 inv.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
892:                     "🥛 {} · 🥫 {} · {:.0}°C",
893:                     stats.almond_bottles, stats.rations, stats.ambient_c
894:                 )));
895:             }
896:             // Death flash: appears on each new death, fades after ~2.5 s.
897:             if let Some(overlay) = &death_overlay {
898:                 if stats.deaths > last_deaths.get() {
899:                     last_deaths.set(stats.deaths);
900:                     death_shown_at.set(time_ms);
901:                     let _ = overlay.set_class_name("shown");
902:                 } else if time_ms - death_shown_at.get() > 2500.0
903:                     && !overlay.class_name().is_empty()
904:                 {
905:                     let _ = overlay.set_class_name("");
906:                 }
907:             }
908: 
909:             // Anomaly debug overlay (F3 or the settings switch).
910:             if let Some(overlay_el) = &debug_overlay {
911:                 let on = crate::ANOMALY_DEBUG.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
912:                 if on {
913:                     overlay_el.set_text_content(Some(&engine.borrow().anomaly_debug_text()));
914:                 }
915:                 if on != debug_overlay_visible.get() {
916:                     debug_overlay_visible.set(on);
917:                     let _ = overlay_el
918:                         .style()
919:                         .set_property("display", if on { "block" } else { "none" });
920:                 }
921:             }
922:         }
923: 
924:         // In capture mode, wait until the camera chunk is loaded, then allow
925:         // the requested number of frames to settle before exposing readiness.
926:         if is_capture {
927:             let engine_ref = engine.borrow();
928:             let pos = engine_ref.player().position;
929:             let cs = engine_ref.chunk_size();
930:             let cam_chunk = crate::application::streaming::chunk_key(
931:                 (pos[0] / cs).floor() * cs,
932:                 (pos[2] / cs).floor() * cs,
933:             );
934:             if frame_count.get() % 30 == 0 {
935:                 web_sys::console::log_1(
936:                     &format!(
937:                         "[DEBUG CAPTURE] player pos: {:?}, cs: {}, cam_chunk: {:?}, resident: {}, ready: {}",
938:                         pos,
939:                         cs,
940:                         cam_chunk,
941:                         engine_ref.is_chunk_resident(cam_chunk),
942:                         engine_ref.stats().ready
943:                     )
944:                     .into(),
945:                 );
946:             }
947:             if engine_ref.is_chunk_resident(cam_chunk) {
948:                 let frames = capture_frame_counter.get();
949:                 if frames < capture_settle_frames {
950:                     capture_frame_counter.set(frames + 1);
951:                 } else {
952:                     if let Some(w) = web_sys::window() {
953:                         let _ = js_sys::Reflect::set(
954:                             &w,
955:                             &JsValue::from_str("__sceneReady"),
956:                             &JsValue::from_bool(true),
957:                         );
958:                     }
959:                 }
960:             }
961:         }
962: 
963:         // Schedule next frame.
964:         if let Some(closure) = raf_handle_clone.borrow().as_ref() {
965:             let _ = loop_window.request_animation_frame(closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref());
966:         }
967:     }));
968: 
969:     if let Some(closure) = raf_handle.borrow().as_ref() {
970:         window.request_animation_frame(closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
971:     }
972:     // Keep the closure (and everything it captures) alive forever.
973:     std::mem::forget(raf_handle);
974:     Ok(())
975: }
````

````rust
 119: /// Adaptive internal-resolution governor. Low-spec machines get fewer rays
 120: /// per frame by rendering at a reduced backing-store resolution; the driver
 121: /// applies the scale to the canvas. Hysteresis + cooldown prevent flapping.
 122: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 123: pub struct PerfGovernor {
 124:     ema_frame_ms: f32,
 125:     scale: f32,
 126:     cooldown_frames: u32,
 127:     /// Frames since the last scale-up attempt (saturating).
 128:     frames_since_raise: u32,
 129:     /// While positive, scale-ups are locked out because a recent raise
 130:     /// immediately overloaded the GPU and had to be reverted (anti-flap).
 131:     raise_lockout_frames: u32,
 132: }
 133: 
 134: impl PerfGovernor {
 135:     const SCALES: [f32; 4] = [0.5, 0.65, 0.8, 1.0];
 136:     /// A drop this soon after a raise counts as a failed raise.
 137:     const RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES: u32 = 600;
 138:     /// How long a failed raise blocks further raise attempts (~1 min).
 139:     const RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES: u32 = 3600;
 140: 
 141:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 142:         Self {
 143:             ema_frame_ms: 16.0,
 144:             scale: 0.8,
 145:             cooldown_frames: 0,
 146:             frames_since_raise: u32::MAX,
 147:             raise_lockout_frames: 0,
 148:         }
 149:     }
 150: 
 151:     pub fn scale(&self) -> f32 {
 152:         self.scale
 153:     }
 154: 
 155:     pub fn update(&mut self, frame_ms: f32) {
 156:         self.ema_frame_ms = self.ema_frame_ms * 0.95 + frame_ms.clamp(0.0, 100.0) * 0.05;
 157:         self.frames_since_raise = self.frames_since_raise.saturating_add(1);
 158:         self.raise_lockout_frames = self.raise_lockout_frames.saturating_sub(1);
 159:         if self.cooldown_frames > 0 {
 160:             self.cooldown_frames -= 1;
 161:             return;
 162:         }
 163:         let idx = Self::SCALES
 164:             .iter()
 165:             .position(|&s| s == self.scale)
 166:             .unwrap_or(2);
 167:         if self.ema_frame_ms > 33.0 && idx > 0 {
 168:             // Sustained under ~30 fps: drop one resolution step. If this
 169:             // happens right after a raise, the raise failed — lock raises
 170:             // out for a while so the scale doesn't oscillate.
 171:             if self.frames_since_raise < Self::RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES {
 172:                 self.raise_lockout_frames = Self::RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES;
 173:             }
 174:             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx - 1];
 175:             self.cooldown_frames = 120;
 176:         } else if self.ema_frame_ms < 17.5
 177:             && idx + 1 < Self::SCALES.len()
 178:             && self.raise_lockout_frames == 0
 179:         {
 180:             // Holding 60Hz vsync (rAF EMA floors at ~16.7 ms, so a lower
 181:             // threshold would never fire): probe one resolution step up.
 182:             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx + 1];
 183:             self.cooldown_frames = 240;
 184:             self.frames_since_raise = 0;
 185:         }
 186:     }
 187: }

 241: /// Per-frame intensity gain of one fixture's authored flicker mode.
 242: /// Deterministic in (id, time): every machine shows the same buzz.
 243: /// Mode 1 is a tired ballast — a fast shallow shimmer with slow beats.
 244: /// Mode 2 is a dying tube — mostly lit, with hard sputtering dropouts.
 245: fn fixture_flicker_gain(id: u64, mode: u8, time: f32) -> f32 {
 246:     let phase = (id % 977) as f32 * 0.61;
 247:     match mode {
 248:         1 => {
 249:             let t = time * 47.0 + phase;
 250:             (0.86 + 0.10 * t.sin() * (t * 0.093).cos() + 0.04 * (time * 3.1 + phase).sin())
 251:                 .clamp(0.7, 1.0)
 252:         }
 253:         2 => {
 254:             // Coarse deterministic gate: ~9 decisions per second per tube.
 255:             let step = (time * 9.0 + phase) as u64;
 256:             let mut h = id ^ step.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
 257:             h ^= h >> 31;
 258:             h = h.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
 259:             if (h >> 40) % 100 < 24 {
 260:                 0.06
 261:             } else {
 262:                 0.92
 263:             }
 264:         }
 265:         _ => 1.0,
 266:     }
 267: }
````
